data.biography:
On 28 May 2024, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front spokesperson Major Gwahram Baloch stated that, on 26 May 2024, at six o’clock in the evening, BLF freedom fighters from the Qurban unit surrounded the Pakistani military camp in Nondada, Jhao, from all sides and launched a massive attack using heavy weapons. A team of BLF sniper shooters was also involved in the operation.

The attack resulted in the deaths of many enemy personnel and injuries to several others. Five outposts and the main camp’s front positions were destroyed. The fighters approached the camp, throwing grenades and inflicting significant casualties and damage on the enemy.

Meanwhile, many enemy personnel fled their outposts and the main camp out of fear. The battle continued for four hours. However, the day after the attack, on 27 May, the defeated enemy forces attacked the civilian population, as usual. At several locations, the forces blocked roads and began taunting and harassing people.

During this attack, Sarmachar Second Lieutenant Ashraf, alias Rehan Nokap, son of Murad Bakhsh and a resident of Kundadi, was martyred by a mortar shell fired by the enemy in retaliation.

Ashraf Baloch was an extremely hardworking and courageous Sarmachar who was devoted to the freedom struggle. He continued to demonstrate his bravery and fighting skills by participating in operations against the occupying Pakistani army on various fronts in Awaran.

It should be noted that Shaheed Ashraf Jan served as an active fighter in the BLF and was injured twice in two battles with the enemy. However, on both occasions, after recovering from his injuries, he returned to the front lines with even greater determination and enthusiasm.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Allah Noor Jamaldini, alias Rokein, and his brother Asif Jamaldini, alias Zubair, sons of Peer Bakhsh Jamaldini, were residents of the Qazi Abad area of Noshki. They joined the Baloch liberation movement in March 2023 and October 2024. They became part of the BLA Frontline in July 2024 and 2025, subsequently joining the Majeed Brigade in August 2024 and the Fateh Squad. Both brothers were martyred in Operation Herof on the Noshki Front.
The rugged valleys and scorching deserts of Balochistan are not merely witnesses to deprivation; they are cradles of resistant thought, where the dream of liberation is nurtured across generations. The life story of these two brothers from Qazi Abad, Noshki - Allah Noor and Asif Jamaldini - is not just a tale of familial sacrifice. It represents the pinnacle of a political and philosophical revolution that has permeated the very soul of modern Baloch youth.
Allah Noor Jamaldini, known in the resistance ranks as "Rokein," possessed intellectual and political foresight far removed from superficial emotionalism. He formally joined the Baloch national movement in March 2023. When he took to the mountain front in July 2024, it was the practical manifestation of a thinker on the battlefield. Allah Noor understood that in the struggle for national survival, the fear of death is dwarfed by the reality of a life in bondage. Driven by this conviction, he joined the Majeed Brigade in August 2024.

On September 12, 2025, the enemy Pakistani army attempted to advance by deploying commandos via helicopters following a drone attack in the Dasht area of Mastung. During this operation, clashes broke out between Pakistani forces and fighters of the Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS). While resisting the enemy’s advance, BRAS fighters eliminated three Pakistani army personnel, while two freedom fighters, Abu Bakar alias Majeed and Abdul Had alias Usman, attained martyrdom.

Martyr Abu Bakar Kurd, alias Majeed, son of Fateh Muhammad, belonged to the Dasht area of Mastung. He had been associated with the Balochistan Liberation Front for the past year and was serving on the Mastung and Quetta fronts.

Martyr Abdul Hadd Mengal, alias Usman, son of Haji Mussa, belonged to the Johan area of Kalat. He had been associated with the Baloch Liberation Army for the past year and was serving on the Mastung front in the struggle against national subjugation.
Hammal Baloch was killed by the Pakistani Frontier Corps on 1 December 2010 during a raid on Ayub Gichki’s house in Turbat, Balochistan.
Nimroz Baloch, was a resident of the Mand area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 4 July 2011 in Balochistan.

On 23 January 2011, at approximately 4:15 pm, in the Chitkan area of Panjgur district in Balochistan, Pakistani intelligence agencies, the Frontier Corps, and other genocidal forces raided the house of Nasir Dagarzai. During the raid, they abducted Nasir Dagarzai, Abid Saleem, Mehrab Omar, and Abid Rasool Bakhsh while they were sitting in the guest room (Betak) drinking tea.
Before taking him away, Pakistani forces also shot Nasir Dagarzai three times, leaving him wounded at the scene. The forces then took Nasir to a hospital, after which he was transferred to detention and torture cells, where he was subjected to severe torture. His hands were ground with a grinder and his body was burned with fire.
Approximately five days later, on 27 January 2011, Pakistani forces again shot Nasir Dagarzai and Abid Rasool Bakhsh. At around 1:00 am, they took them to the forests of Gowargo in the Panjgur area and dumped them there. Abid Rasool Bakhsh succumbed to his wounds and died there. However, by chance, Nasir Dagarzai, although badly injured, was found by a person who informed the Levies. He was then transferred to Quetta for medical treatment. After receiving treatment, he was brought back to Panjgur, and due to the gunshot wounds, doctors inserted a rod in his leg.
On 11 March 2011, Nasir Dagarzai gave an interview to Samandar Askani on Radio Gwank in which he described the details of these events.
Later, on 23 May 2011, when Nasir was traveling with his brother Mohammad Gull Dagarzai to Quetta for medical treatment, Pakistani forces abducted him again at the Lak Pass area near Quetta and forcibly disappeared him. On 16 July 2011, he was killed and his mutilated body was dumped. The body was recovered from Lak Pass near Quetta on 17 July 2011.
Similarly, in the same incident, the mutilated bodies of Abid Saleem, son of Mohammad Saleem Baloch, and Mehrab Baloch, son of Haji Mohammad Umar, who had also been abducted and forcibly disappeared, were later recovered on 24 May 2011 from the Margap area of Turbat district in Balochistan.
The short film “The Line of Freedom,” written and directed by the British director David Whitney and produced by Nooruddin Mengal, Mir Bhawal Mengal, and David Whitney, was released in 2013 and was inspired by Nasir Dagarzai.
Nasir Dagarzai’s son, Zameer Dagarzai, was abducted by Pakistani forces and Pakistan-backed death squads on 3 March 2026 from the Chitkan Taar office in Panjgur district, Balochistan. On 11 March 2026, his tortured body was found under the Washaap Bridge in the Panjgur district of Balochistan.
Misk Ali Bugti, was a resident of the Dera Bugti area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 1 February 2017 in Balochistan.

Martyr Kambar Baloch, alias Sagaar Baloch was born in house of Mohammad Kareem Baloch and in Shahrak area of Kech, Balochistan. He became part of Baloch liberation movement in platform of Balochistan Liberation Front BLF in 2014. He newly joined in Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) before same days of his martyrdom. He embraced martyrdom along with eight comrades, Jalil Sher Baloch, Samad Baloch, Dad Shah, Samad Baloch, Shoaib Baloch, Rahmdil Baloch, Haris Baloch and Nawaz Baloch  in a drone attack of Pakistan Army  on Nov 29, 2022 in Jath, Kolwa area of Kech, Balochistan.

On 9 September 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of ten fighters belonging to the organization. He paid tribute to the Sarmachars who were martyred while defending national liberation and their homeland, Balochistan.
- The statement identified the following fighters:
1-  Akhtar Dawood, alias Ali Sher, son of Asad Sajidi.
2- Khalil Ahmad, alias Ustad Awais, son of Sher Ahmad.
3-  Imran, alias Aajo, son of Saifullah.
4-  Hasil, alias Munir Ahmad, son of Sher Mohammad.
5- Inayatullah, alias Sher Zaman, son of Manzoor Ahmad.
6- Asad Rahim, son of Rahim Baksh.
7- Mujeeb Ur Rehman, alias Shay Mureed, son of Saeed Ahmad.
8- Sahil, alias Arman, son of Peeral.
9- Javed, alias Murshid.
10- Mohammad Younis, alias Taleb, son of Mohammad Omar.

Inayatullah, alias Sher Zaman, son of Manzoor Ahmed, resident of Sabri, Dhadar, joined the organization in 2026. He was a brave and hardworking fighter. In this short period, he first carried out urban duties and then, by organizational decision, moved to the mountain front. In this brief time, he took part in important combat operations, inflicting losses of life and resources on the enemy. He rendered valuable service on the fronts of Bolan, Kaabu, Maran, and Dasht. He was martyred on 22 July 2026 in a clash with the enemy on the Mastung front, becoming immortalized forever in Baloch national history.
On 2 February 2026, the Pakistani military carried out a drone strike in Killi Jamaldini, an area of Noshki district in Balochistan and killed a three year old child, Deedag Baloch.

On 24 May 2026, a statement issued by the spokesperson of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), Jeeyand Baloch, stated that the Majeed Brigade, the fidayee unit of the organization, carried out a fidayee attack this morning targeting a military shuttle train transporting soldiers of the occupying Pakistani army at the Chaman Phatak area in Quetta, inflicting heavy casualties on the enemy.
This fidayee mission was carried out by Majeed Brigade fidayee and organizational commander Bilal Shahwani, alias Saeen. The 25-year-old fidayee Bilal Shahwani, son of Chief Abdul Ghani Shahwani, was a resident of Killi Sarde, Sariab, in Shal (Quetta). He joined the Baloch resistance movement for independence in 2020. Due to his outstanding performance in the military field and organizational discipline, the martyred Bilal was included in the fidayee unit of the Majeed Brigade in 2022 upon his voluntary request. He remained active on the critical fronts of Nagaho, Dasht Kombela, Quetta, and Kalat, and rose to the rank of commander because of his natural military capabilities.
Commander Bilal Shahwani, alias Saeen, was an active and strategic military mind within the BLA network. Over the past six months, the direct command of all major attacks and guerrilla operations against the occupying military across the entire combat front of Dasht Kombela had been in the hands of the martyred fidayee Bilal Shahwani. Prior to this, during the organization’s historic military offensive, “Operation Herof 1,” he led the vanguard units against the enemy on the Kalat front, while during “Operation Herof 2,” he commanded the fidayee units in the highly sensitive Red Zone area of Quetta, breaching the enemy’s security perimeter.
The transfer of Pakistani military personnel, at the exact moment of their clandestine movement from Quetta Cantonment to the Jaffer Express via the shuttle train, was presented as clear evidence of the deep penetration of the BLA’s intelligence wing, “ZIRAB,” and the combat expertise of Commander Bilal Shahwani.
The BLA paid its highest revolutionary tribute to its fidayee commander, Bilal Shahwani, alias Saeen, for his organizational services and ultimate sacrifice. An active field commander offering himself for a fidayee mission was described as clear evidence of the BLA’s institutional evolution and ideological superiority. According to the statement, this decision demonstrates that the Baloch national resistance has progressed beyond traditional guerrilla methods into a modern military structure in which organizational commanders prioritize collective national goals over individual material roles. Bilal Shahwani’s actions, the statement said, will be preserved in history as a fundamental principle of the political and military struggle of occupied nations, proving that the modern material network of an occupying state can only be countered through a sustainable balance of deep ideological discipline, intelligence access, sacrifice, and strategic resolve. The statement concluded by saying that their war would continue until the complete independence and establishment of absolute sovereignty on the soil of Balochistan.
The BLA claimed that the attack killed 82 Pakistani soldiers and injured 121 others in the Majeed Brigade’s fidayee attack, but according to open sources, the number was much higher.

Muzammil Baloch, also known as Rauf, son of Mahmood Baloch, was a resident of Khudabadan, Panjgur district, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2022 and served in the Intelligence Wing, ZIRAB. His educational qualification was a BS in Economics from the University of Balochistan, Quetta. He was martyred during Operation Herof Phase II on the Quetta front.
Recognizing his intelligence, courage, and dedication, Muzammil Baloch was inducted into the organization’s intelligence wing, ZIRAB, where he worked with great diligence, responsibility, and strict adherence to the principles of secrecy. Work in the field of intelligence requires deep insight, patience, and precise analytical ability, all of which Rauf possessed. His intellectual understanding and practical performance placed him among those individuals who, while working behind the scenes, played a crucial role in the movement.
During Operation Herof Phase II, he was present on the Quetta front alongside his fellow Sarmachars. During a prolonged clash with enemy forces in the Wali Jet area of Saryab, he embraced martyrdom, thereby inscribing his name in the pages of the struggle for freedom.

Shujahat Allah Baloch was abducted from his farm in Darmakol, Pidark, Turbat district of Balochistan on January 31, 2015, by a Pakistani state patronized death squad. This particular death squad is headed by Sardar Abdul Aziz Bizenjo and operated by his son Mufti Shahmeer Aziz.
Shujahat Allah Baloch was born on February 2, 1992, to Naimat Allah Baloch. He was born and raised in Pidark, a small town 40 km from Turbat city. After completing his matriculation, he joined his father in farming their land. Shujahat Allah’s uncle, Kamal Kohdahi, is a renowned Balochi poet and a staunch supporter of an independent Balochistan. Kamal Kohdahi was the elder of the Kohdahi family.
To weaken the Baloch independence struggle in Makuran, the Kohdahi family was attacked on March 22, 2014, in Pidark by the joint forces of the Pakistani army and the death squad of Sardar Aziz Bizenjo, in which Kamal Kohdahi, along with four relatives - his brother-in-law Murad Hasil, two nephews, Islam Baloch and Ikram Baloch, and a close relative, Sameer Baloch - were extrajudicially murdered. Since 2015, more than 25 male members of the Kohdahi family have been killed by the Pakistani state and its death squad.
Shujahat Allah Baloch was killed on the same day that he was abducted; his mutilated body was dumped at Githan-e-Dann on the main road from Pidark to Turbat. Every part of his body bore witness to the savage and brutal mentality of Sardar Abdul Aziz Bizenjo and the hatred of the Pakistani state toward Baloch people. All of his teeth were broken, and his facial skeleton was completely crushed; his entire body bore scars and bruises of torture. On his forehead, from ear to ear, were many small cuts made by a sharp object. The bones of his arms and legs were broken in many places. His neck had a deep wound made by a sharp object. After torturing him in the most inhumane way, they executed him in a mafia-style killing with three bullets.

On 4 March 2026, a statement issued by the spokesperson of the Balochistan Liberation Front, Major Gwahram Baloch, stated that on 3 February 2026, fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front launched a coordinated operation at four different locations in Hoshap against Pakistani forces. In this organized operation, various BLF units simultaneously targeted the enemy army at four different locations in Hoshap.
In the initial phase of the operation, one unit of fighters surrounded the police station located in Hoshap Bazaar and took control of the station, holding the personnel hostage. While this unit was seizing government weapons, ammunition, and other equipment, an enemy military convoy consisting of four vehicles approached the area, resulting in an intense face-to-face clash between BLF fighters and enemy forces. During the clash, the fighters targeted and destroyed two enemy vehicles, killing several Pakistani military personnel on board.
Meanwhile, a second unit of fighters positioned at another location attacked two armored enemy vehicles with heavy weapons. Several military personnel were killed or wounded in the clash. Witnessing the defeat and retreat of their ground forces, the enemy resorted to gunship helicopters and advanced drone technology to halt the BLF fighters’ advance.
In this prolonged clash, seven BLF fighters - Shaneed Baloch (alias Shohaz Baloch), Zabad Baloch (alias Deedag), Atta Baloch (alias Obaid), Ghaffar Baloch (alias Noroz), Abdul Samad Baloch (alias Muheem Jan), Zaheer Baloch (alias Istaal), and Nadeem (alias Sahil) - fought valiantly until their last bullet and last breath and embraced martyrdom while courageously defending their motherland.
Zabad Baloch, alias Deedag Son of Ghulam Mohammad Baloch, resident of Syed Abad Kelkour, Panjgur. Zabad Baloch participated in armed struggle in 2019 under the BLF platform, while prior to that he had been active in the student organization since 2015. He was a fearless and hardworking fighter who, despite difficult circumstances and atrocities inflicted upon his family, maintained his active and conscious connection with the movement. He participated in operations on various fronts and inflicted heavy losses on the enemy. Even tactics such as torture and enforced disappearance could not shake his resolve.
Anwar Baloch was a resident of the Mashkai area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 5 October 2016 in Balochistan.
Javed Jan, alias Zubair, was a resident of the Kaleero, Dasht area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 11 July 2020 in Balochistan.
Sikandar Baloch was a resident of the Mehi, Mashkai area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 18 September 2020 in Balochistan.

Ibrahim Baloch was born in 1978 into the Saleh family in the Seerag area of Mand. He completed his matriculation from Mand Bullow High School. As a young man, he supported political groups that worked to prepare the masses for the freedom of Balochistan. When the armed struggle began, he stood alongside freedom fighters by assisting with funding and logistics.
Because of his activities, and due to being a cousin and brother-in-law of Wahid Qambar and Shaheed Dr. Khalid Baloch, he became a marked man. On 28 November 2005, he was abducted by Pakistani agencies from Maripur, Karachi. After ten months of extensive torture, he resurfaced on 21 September in Khuzdar, Balochistan.
After his release, he did not slow down his activities. He used to say, “Why are people so concerned about their personal interests? Why don’t they unite and think about the national interest of the Baloch?”
On the night of 28 June 2009, he was traveling from Turbat to Tump with his friend. At around 10 pm, he was ambushed in Malikabad by Pakistani forces dressed in civilian clothes. Their car was stopped, and its tyres were shot. Once an informer confirmed Ibrahim’s identity, he was shot on the spot. His friend was also injured.
By dawn, around 5 am on 29 June 2009, he succumbed to his injuries while being taken to Turbat. He was laid to rest in his family graveyard in Mand Bullow.

data.martyrdomPlace: Gawak, Tehsil Mand, District Turbat, Balochistan
data.biography: On 18 November 2025, Pakistani forces opened fire on people who were on their way to a picnic in the Gawak area of Tehsil Mand in the Turbat district of Balochistan, killing Ismail Baloch, son of Jalal Khan, and injuring his friend Noman Baloch, son of Haider. Noman was later taken into custody while wounded and forcibly disappeared.

Najuma Baloch was a woman originally from Tasp, Panjgur, in Eastern Balochistan. She had relocated to Sham-E-Sar (Haqqabad), Sistan and Balochistan, where she was martyred in the missile strike. Her family was reportedly a target of ongoing military operations in the region.

Mohammad Ismail Kubdani, son of Lashkari Khan Kubdani and a resident of Kharan, was shot dead on March 9, 2026, during the holy month of Ramzan by a state-backed death squad. The attackers opened fire on Ismail at approximately 8:15 AM while he was working as a labourer in a tailor’s shop.
Mohammad Ismail had previously been subjected to enforced disappearance in June 2025. After spending months in custody, he was reportedly released in January 2026. Despite attempting to return to a normal civilian life and earn a livelihood through daily labour, he was targeted and killed in broad daylight.
Zahoor Ahmad, alias Ishaq, was a resident of the Gowash, Awaran area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 27 August 2020 in Balochistan.

Faraz Ahmed, alias Dostain, son of Muneer Ahmad, was a resident of Gichk in the Panjgur district of Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2025 and became a member of the Fateh Squad. He served on the Kharan and Kalat fronts and was martyred during Operation Herof Phase 2 on the Kharan front.
Faraz Ahmed, alias Dostain, belonged to the Gichk area of Panjgur. He was among those young individuals who accepted the struggle for national freedom not merely as an idea but as a practical responsibility. After joining the BLA, he quickly established himself through his seriousness, discipline, and combat capabilities, which led to his inclusion in the organization’s Fateh Squad. Becoming part of this unit indicated that Dostain possessed advanced combat skills and the ability to play a role in critical operations. On the Kharan and Kalat fronts, he carried out his duties according to these principles and demonstrated discipline, strategy, and steadfastness in every engagement.
During Operation Herof Phase II, the Sarmachars confronted the enemy on the Kharan front with organized strategy and extraordinary courage. In this battle, Faraz stood on the front line alongside his fellow Sarmachar (freedom fighters) and fought until the final moments, giving practical expression to the philosophy of sacrifice upon which movements for freedom are built.

data.martyrdomPlace: Dambani Syahgesi, Zamuran, Turbat district, Balochistan
data.biography:
Abdullah Baloch, son of Peer Muhammad, a 25-year-old driver from the Dambani Syahgesi area of Zamuran, Kech, was forcibly disappeared on 2 May 2026 at around 4:30 AM from his home. FC personnel raided his house, assaulted his family, and took Abdullah along with his father, Peer Muhammad, into custody.
Five hours later, the bodies of Abdullah Baloch and his father, Peer Muhammad, were found dumped near an FC camp.

Named after the legendary Baloch hero Mir Dad Shah, he was known among his peers for his resilience. He was a seasoned guerrilla fighter who had survived multiple previous skirmishes in the difficult terrain of Balochistan before his martyrdom in Diz area of Paroom in Panjgur.
data.birthPlace: Daki Bazar Absar, Turbat, Occupied Baluchistan

data.biography:
Abdul Qudoos Qambarani, alias Sikandar, son of Abdullah Qambrani, was a resident of the Mohalla Khel area of Kalat, Balochistan. He held a Doctor of Veterinary Medicine degree from LUAWMS University. He joined the BLA on 15 August 2025 and served on the Nagaho, Kalat, and Khuzdar fronts. He was killed on 10 July 2026 in Zaidi, Khuzdar.
Abdul Quddus, alias Sikandar, was among the brave and courageous Sarmachars of the BLA who possessed military training and the capability to infiltrate deep inside enemy camps and destroy them. He was killed in face-to-face combat during an operation to take control of a key strategic area in Khuzdar. On 15 August 2025, driven by national consciousness and ideological conviction, he made the conscious decision to devote his educational skills and abilities to the Baloch Liberation Army. He joined the ranks of the BLA and was deployed to the Nagaho front. His decision was based on his understanding of the realities on the ground and his conviction that, under conditions of occupation and the subjugation of one’s homeland, defending the motherland becomes the foremost responsibility of every conscious individual.
After completing his military training, Sikandar carried out his responsibilities in different areas in accordance with the organization’s decisions. Wherever he served, he established himself as a steadfast, brave, fearless, and self-sacrificing Sarmachar. As soon as he entered the battlefield, he developed into a disciplined and professional fighter and soon emerged as a highly skilled combatant. Within a short period, keeping in view the requirements of the battlefield, he received advanced training in the use of various weapons and employed them effectively in major operations against the enemy. He was one of the Ghazis of the BLA’s historic Operation Herof II and remained active as a frontline fighter in various major attacks. Earlier this year, he also played a role as a frontline fighter in a major attack carried out against the enemy in Jhal Magsi. His message to the enemy was always clear.
Sikandar was one of the brave and prominent Sarmachars associated with the BLA’s war doctrine, and he put its warfighting skills and capabilities into practice until the very end of his life. He was killed while protecting his fellow Sarmachars during a deadly attack on the enemy in Zaidi, Khuzdar. In doing so, he became one of the figures remembered in Baloch history and honored by his supporters.
Shahnawaz Baloch, a leader of the Baloch National Movement, was murdered on 23 November 2010 in Ormara Town, Balochistan.

data.fullName: Saleh Mohammad Jatak, alias Gwahram Khan
data.biography:
Saleh Mohammad Jatak, alias Guwahram Khan, son of Abdullah Jatak, joined the BLA on 12 June 2025. He served on the Nagaho and Kark fronts and was martyred on 10 July 2026 in Zaidi, Khuzdar, at the age of 35.
Realizing what he regarded as Pakistan's brutality and illegitimate occupation, Martyr Saleh Mohammad joined the revolutionary and national ranks of the Baloch Liberation Army last year and began his armed resistance against the enemy through the organization's ranks. Seeking to counter the enemy's ambitions, he took up a position on the Nagaho front, where he received basic military training. After completing his training, he joined the organization's patrol units and took part in multiple battles. He believed in offensive military strategies against the enemy and remained on the front line in implementing such organizational policies.
Saleh Mohammad was aware of the fact that, in his view, this war had not been imposed on the Punjabis by the Baloch; rather, the Punjabis had imposed it on the Baloch. Through occupation and exploitation, he believed they sought to erase Baloch identity, culture, and civilization while forcibly taking Baloch land and denying the Baloch their right to live freely. Because of this, he regarded the struggle as not only a war to restore and defend statehood but also as the only option for the survival and protection of Baloch national identity. He was one of those Sarmachars who could adapt to changing circumstances on the battlefield while remaining steadfast and consistent in his actions. He possessed the ability to carry out major and significant responsibilities with composure. Through his actions and character, he was portrayed as a persistent threat to the enemy.
He sought to demonstrate through his actions that the Baloch had become capable of challenging the enemy through their own strength and capabilities. With this offensive mindset, he took part in an important organizational operation in the Zaidi region against the enemy. While contributing to the operation's success, he helped push back the enemy's advance and inflicted significant losses before being killed on the battlefield. His supporters believe that his death secured his place in the pages of Baloch history forever.
Abdullah, son of Haji Dad Muhammad, a 23 year old driver by profession from Reesh Pesh Paroom, Panjgur, was targeted and killed in the Panjgur area on March 20, 2026.

Adil Baloch, son of Assa Baloch, was a resident of Balgatar, Kech. He was abducted along with his brother Shah Jan and six other close relatives from different areas on August 22, 2023. After four months, on November 20, 2023, he was killed, along with his brother Shah Jan and relative Nabi Dad, son of Lewari Baloch, by a Pakistan military-backed death squad in Balgatar, Kech.

Mohammad Riaz Nichari, alias Kaka Zaheer, son of Faqeer Mohammad Nichari, was a resident of the Kabo area of Mastung. He joined the BLA in May 2023 and moved to the mountain front in January 2024. He served on the Mastung and Kalat fronts, was promoted to the rank of Patrol Commander, and was martyred on 6 June 2026 in Iskaalko, Kalat.
Mohammad Riaz Nichari, known among his fellow Sarmachars as Kaka Zaheer, was regarded as one of the dedicated and hardworking members of the BLA who viewed national defense and freedom as the fundamental pillars of a Baloch state. Driven by his ideological commitment to the Baloch national movement, he endured six years of inhumane torture and hardship in the enemy’s prisons. Yet, despite these brutal atrocities, he remained steadfast in his convictions and unwavering in his commitment to the national cause.
Rather than breaking his resolve, the enemy’s repression further strengthened his political consciousness and ideological resilience. In 2023, he chose the path of armed struggle, joined the BLA, and was deployed to the Kalat front.
Transforming his ideological conviction into practical action on the battlefield, he served as an active combatant and a responsible Sarmachar in the Kalat region. Commitment to duty, ideological steadfastness, tireless hard work, and the ability to confront the enemy with courage, discipline, and determination in combat were among the defining characteristics of his personality. In recognition of these qualities and capabilities, he was entrusted with patrol command responsibilities in the Mastung region. He carried out these responsibilities with professionalism, dedication, and a strong sense of duty, fulfilling his mission with unwavering commitment until his last breath.
He was not merely a responsible cadre by virtue of rank or position; through his conduct and actions, he embodied the qualities of a dedicated and responsible Sarmachar. Until his final days, he carried out his duties with unwavering commitment, contributing to the defense of areas under the organization’s control and influence while helping to halt enemy advances along the defensive front. Remaining steadfast in the defense of these positions, he fought courageously in direct combat against enemy forces and ultimately embraced martyrdom on the Iskalko front.
data.fullName: Mohammad Riaz Nichari, alias Kaka Zaheer

data.biography:
On 11 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch announced the martyrdom of 14 fighters of the organization who attained martyrdom in confrontations with the Pakistani army and in airstrikes while defending their homeland, Balochistan, and fighting for national liberation and the right to self-determination.

On 13 August 2026, Pakistani Air Force fighter jets bombarded the Pandran area of Kalat District in Balochistan, resulting in the martyrdom of four members of the organization: Waseem Baloch, alias Farhan; Obaidullah Baloch, alias Shaheen; Nawaz Ali Baloch, alias Dilshad; and Mohammad Hassan, alias Ahmad.

On 25 August 2026, during an organizational mission in the Kech area of Balochistan, Sher Jan, alias Jamal, was shot from behind by a traitor, resulting in his martyrdom.

On 3 September 2026, while patrolling in the Mastung area of Balochistan, the organization’s brave fighters, Mohammad Younis, alias Salal; Sameer Ahmad, alias Zemal; Aziz Ahmad, alias Janan; and Sikandar Baloch, confronted Pakistani forces, targeted several enemy personnel, and embraced martyrdom.

On 14 September 2026, while engaging Pakistani forces and defending his fellow fighters in the Machani Kor Paroom area of Panjgur District, Babar Baloch, alias Kambar, embraced martyrdom.

On 18 September 2026, during a confrontation with Pakistani forces in the Chagi area of Balochistan, fighters of the organization, Riaz Baloch, alias Sabir; Taimoor Shah, alias Shaheen; Zia Ul Haq, alias Ziaullah; and Jumma Baloch, alias Commando, embraced martyrdom.

Mohammad Hassan, alias Ahmad, son of Sahib Khan, resident of Kuddi, Kalat, joined the armed struggle for Baloch national liberation through the BLF platform at the beginning of 2026. After receiving military training and ideological maturity, he moved to the mountain front in Kalat. He was an extremely sincere, hardworking and disciplined sarmachar. On the morning of 13 August, he was martyred in the bombing by enemy jets in the Pandran area of Kalat.

On July 12th, 1927, Akbar Bugti was born in Barkhan, Balochistan at the home of Nawab Behram Khan Bugti. Since childhood, Akbar Bugti was destined to be a great and brave man.  He eagerly perused education and was dedicated to his studies.  In addition to his early education at Aitcheson College, Lahore, Akbar Khan Bugti also attended Oxford University in London England.  After the death of his father in 1939, the thirteen year old Akbar Khan Bugti was appointed as chief of his tribe.

Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti went on to pay an important role in Balochistan politics.  He began his political career when elected to the National Assembly of Pakistan in 1958, serving as Interior Minister.  In October of the same year, President Iskandar Mirza declared martial law and dismissed the cabinet.  In the early 1960’s, Akbar Khan Bugti supported the National Awami Party candidate for the National Assembly from Quetta division and he was elected with a great number of votes.  The defeated Field Marshal Ayub Khan was offended by the young Khan’s public endorsement of his political opponents and ordered the detention of Akbar. Akbar Khan Bugti remained imprisoned until his release in the mid 1960’s after a lengthy hunger strike.

In the early 1970’s, the Federal Government appointed Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti as Governor of Balochistan.  Soon after Akbar Khan Bugti was appointed Governor, the Pakistani military began a ruthless crackdown in Balochistan.  When the Federal Government refused to cease military aggression towards Baloch citizens, Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti resigned from his post as Governor.
During the Military Operations in the early 1970’s, the Pakistani Army deployed over 100,000 soldiers in Balochistan.  In addition to the ground troops, the Iranian Shah sent F-14 fighter jets and AH-1 Gunship helicopters to help Pakistan commit genocide.  More than 4000 Baloch civilians were massacred by Pakistani and Iranian Forces during the crack-down.

In 1988, Akbar Khan Bugti joined the Balochistan National Alliance and was soon thereafter elected as Chief Minister.  He soon resigned from the position after the provincial assembly was dissolved in 1990 by Gen. Muhammad Musa Khan.  Several years later, Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti formed a new political party, the Jamhoori Watan Party (JWP).  The JWP was wildly popular in Balochistan and Akbar Khan Bugti was elected to the new provincial assembly.  Three years later, Akbar was elected to the National Assembly of Pakistan, representing JWP in the Parliament.  In 1997, Akbar Khan Bugti was re-elected to the National Assembly.
In 2005, a Sindhi female doctor was violently raped by an officer of the Pakistani Army at a Military Base near Sui.  Dera Bugti Chieftain Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti demanded justice for the rape victim, but former President Musharraf refused to pursue a case against the implicated officer.  Instead, Musharraf launched a full scale military assault on July 17th, 2005.  Twenty innocent Bugti villagers were killed in the massacre and many of them were women and children.
After the 2005 massacre in Dera Bugti, the then 87 year old Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti decided to go to the mountains and for over a year, Nawab Akbhar Khan Bugti and his brave comrades fought with the forces. On August 26th, 2006 in the Tatany Mountains, forces launched a fierce military operation against Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti.  Gunship helicopters and Fighter Jets bombarded the mountain range with chemical weapons.  Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti and 32 of his comrades were martyred that day.
Although Musharraf thought the death of Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti would be the end of Baloch Nationalism but it was only the beginning.  Shaheed Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti inspired the entire Baloch Nation to resist for the protection of Baloch land.  For everyone from young teenagers to senior citizens, Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti became a source of Baloch pride and a symbol of conviction.
The former Pakistani President General Pervez Musharraf seemed mighty during his presidency but his true significance has become apparent as he leads the shameful life of a criminal behind bars.  Musharraf forced himself into the seat of power of an already faltering state and when he inevitably was unable to meet the needs of the people, he was quickly deposed.
Despite controversy and hardship, Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti will always be remembered as a hero of the Baloch nation and is considered the greatest leader of the Baloch Nation. He is still alive in our hearts as a candle in a dark dungeon. People commemorate his death with utmost respect and love. For all time, his lovers and admirers hold rallies in demonstration of his remembrance. This only shows that in a war between right and wrong, the person with the righteous aims always wins.

On the morning of January 8, 2026, at around 10 AM in the Zamuran area of Buleda, the Pakistani military carried out a drone attack on the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) camp, resulting in the martyrdom of four BLF fighters. The martyrs include Hussain, alias Kamal Baloch; Akbar, alias Tahir Baloch; Waseem, alias Mero Baloch; and Huzaifa, alias Nodan Baloch.
Huzaifa, alias Nodan Baloch, son of Noor Hamid and resident of Mand, joined the BLF on September 10, 2025. Before relocating to the camp, he maintained contact with the organization. Huzaifa, alias Nodan, was a hardworking and duty-conscious sarmachar. He set an example for every comrade through his dedication, courage, and eagerness to learn. He observed everything carefully and sought to improve with every new opportunity. His sincerity and hard work served as a guiding light for fighters, and his contributions to strengthening the organizational mission were significant.

Martyr Rasool Baksh Baloch alias Kalo Baloch, son of  Doshamby Baloch and was a resident of Keelkoar, area of Panjgur, Balochistan. He affiliated with Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) since 2014. He embraced martyrdom in a clash with Pakistan Army on Feb 24, 2023 in Keelkor area of  Panjgur Balochistan. His elder brother Bahr Baloch was killed by Pakistan Army in 2022 who affiliated with Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA).

Iqbal Baloch, a resident of Khuzdar district in Balochistan, was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces from Hub in May 2021. On 16 March 2022, his mutilated body was found dumped in Awaran.

On 5 November 2024, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that on 4 November 2024, BLA fighters ambushed a convoy of the occupying Pakistani army in the Qadirabad area of Nushki, resulting in at least 10 enemy personnel of the occupying force being eliminated on the spot. In the ongoing extended battle, two veteran BLA fighters fought valiantly and accepted martyrdom.
During the prolonged fight, two comrades of the Baloch Liberation Army, fighters Adnan Baloch (alias Safar Khan) and Yasir Baloch (alias Master Safar Khan), defended the motherland with courage and bravery, embracing martyrdom.
Adnan Baloch, alias Safar Khan, despite being injured by an enemy bullet, did not abandon his position and continued fighting for over an hour, allowing his unit a secure retreat before sacrificing his life.
In this battle, another esteemed BLA comrade, Yasir Baloch, alias Master Safar Khan, was also wounded in an extended clash with the enemy. He managed to hold his ground, but due to excessive blood loss, he too attained the noble status of martyrdom.
Adnan Baloch, alias Safar Khan, son of Wazir Ahmed, hailed from Kili Mengal in Nushki. A BS student in International Relations, Adnan joined the Baloch Liberation Army in early 2023, serving as an urban guerrilla for national liberation. During his time with the organisation, he displayed exceptional skill in operations across Nushki city and its surroundings, dealing significant blows to the enemy. His courageous actions, unwavering bravery, and commitment led to numerous victories, ultimately culminating in his heroic martyrdom.

On 31 January 2012 in Karachi, Zamur Domki (née Bugti, aged 34) sister of Brahamdagh Bugti, sister-in-law of Mehran Baluch and granddaughter of Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti, together with her 13 year old daughter Janna Domki, were visiting the house of Zamur’s maternal uncle after attending a cousin’s wedding at the Carlton Hotel in Defence Housing Authority (DHA), Karachi. They were travelling in a black Toyota sedan (registration: ANR-353) bearing a Balochistan MPA number plate, accompanied by their driver, Barkat Baloch, and a 12-year-old daughter of the household helper.
Between 1:00 and 1:30 AM on 31 January 2012 shortly after leaving the uncle’s house, a black car intercepted their vehicle near Gizri Bridge in Clifton. A man dressed in a black shalwar kameez, believed to belong to Pakistan’s intelligence agencies (ISI and MI), jumped out and opened fire on the driver, Barkat Baloch, as the car attempted to escape. Barkat Baloch was killed instantly by multiple gunshot wounds to the head.
The assailant then opened the rear door. At that moment, two motorcycles arrived and positioned themselves on either side of the car. Zamur Bugti pleaded with the gunman to spare her daughter and offered her own life instead. Ignoring her pleas, the killer moved to the front passenger seat and fired several shots into Janna Domki’s chest and neck.
Zamur Bugti was forced to watch her daughter being murdered. She was then shot more than a dozen times in the head, face, and neck at point-blank range and left dying in a pool of blood. Throughout the attack, police personnel reportedly watched from a distance without intervening.
Zamur Bugti was the daughter of the late Rehan Bugti, the elder sister of Baloch Republican Party leader Brahamdagh Bugti, and the wife of Bakhtiar Domki, a former Member of the Provincial Assembly (MPA) of Balochistan who was then part of the opposition in the provincial assembly. Bakhtiar Domki is also a maternal grandson of Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti.
Bakhtiar Domki has directly accused state intelligence agencies of carrying out the targeted killings.
Zamur Bugti had received death threats prior to the incident. Several other Baloch women related to prominent Baloch nationalist leaders have also received similar threats in the past.

In the early hours of 27th May 2025, the Pakistani military once again demonstrated its unrelenting brutality through a heinous and unlawful operation in the Malaar Machhi area of Awaran, Balochistan. The attack resulted in the extrajudicial execution of two Baloch individuals and the critical wounding of a third, an elderly woman, all belonging to a single Baloch family that has already endured years of state persecution.
Naeem Baloch, son of Sanjar Baloch, and his aunt Hoori, daughter of Qasim, were shot dead by Pakistani forces after security personnel stormed their home around 1 AM and opened indiscriminate fire. Naeem’s mother, Dadi Baloch, was critically injured and left without medical assistance until the following morning, her condition deteriorating due to state-imposed neglect. This massacre marks the fourth such incident in Awaran within a single week, part of an intensifying campaign of systematic violence.
This was not the first time this family had suffered at the hands of the state. In 2015, seven of their relatives, including another aunt, Gohar, were killed in an aerial bombardment. In 2023, Naeem himself was forcibly disappeared. His mother, now critically injured, had previously been detained in 2015.

On 2 February 2022, sixteen members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayeen unit, the Majeed Brigade, carried out simultaneous attacks, nine in Noshki and seven on the Frontier Corps headquarters in Panjgur. The organization named this action "Operation Ganjal". 90 Pakistani security personnel were killed in Noshki and 105 in Panjgur.
In the BLA’s operation on the Noshki FC headquarters, 9 fidayeen participated. On 2 February 2022, Meerain Jamaldini (alias Zagrain) drove an VBEID into the camp’s main gate. Following this, Badil Baloch (alias Riyasat), Murad Aajo (alias Baba), Aneel Baloch (alias Balach), Yasir Noor (alias Saif), Aziz Zehri (alias Barag), Ibraheem Baloch (alias Kabeer), Deedag Bahar (alias Rauf) and Bilal Baloch (alias Wahid) entered the camp. As a result, 90 military personnel, including one officer, were killed, and a portion of the camp was destroyed.
The operation continued throughout the night. In the early morning of 3 February 2022, after their ammunition was exhausted, the remaining eight fidayeen took their own lives by firing their weapons.

On 25 August 2024 Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch announced the launch of a "Fidayeen Operation" named "Herof" across Balochistan. As part of this operation, fidayeen from the BLA's elite unit, Majeed Brigade, have attacked the main camp of the Pakistani forces in Bela and have successfully infiltrated it. Meanwhile, other BLA fighters have taken full control of all major highways across Balochistan, blocking them completely.
During Operation “Herof,” 44 attacks were carried out simultaneously at 40 locations across 13 districts of Balochistan. As a result, 130 Pakistani army personnel were killed and 55 were injured. In addition, gas pipelines were destroyed at 2 locations, railway tracks at 7 locations, and 2 bridges were blown up.
During the operation, 13 vehicles transporting minerals were set on fire. Blockades were also established at 14 locations across Balochistan, and 3 members of a “death squad” were killed.
As part of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayee (suicide) operation “Herof,” the BLA’s Majeed Brigade carried out an attack on the Pakistani army’s Bela camp. The Majeed Brigade maintained control of the camp for twenty hours, during which 68 enemy personnel were killed.
Nine fidayeen (self-sacrificing fighters) of the Majeed Brigade at Bela camp - Ghaus Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Talib), Mahal Baloch (alias Zilan Kurd), Rizwan Baloch (alias Hammal), Mohammad Baloch (alias Meerak), Fazal Gul Zehri (alias Shawaiz), Tayyab Baloch (alias Lala), Junaid Zehri (alias Kami), Mohammad Asif Nechari (alias Naveed), and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Khalid) - along with Shafqat (alias Dayar) of the Fateh Squad in Mastung, were martyred in the operation.
Ghaus Baksh Sumalani, alias Talib, and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani, alias Khalid, were brothers. They took part in the same operation and were martyred while defending their motherland.

On 15 April 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said that between April 3 and April 14, 2026, fighters of the BLA killed 29 personnel of the occupying Pakistani army and injured several others in fourteen different operations across various areas of Balochistan, including Surab, Kharan, Washuk, Mastung, Uthal, Jhal Magsi, and Panjgur. During these operations, full control was established over various highways and checkposts of the occupying forces, where blockades were set up, and 13 Levies and police personnel were taken into custody. In these attacks, the occupying army’s supply lines were also targeted and destroyed at two locations. In intense clashes in the Surab area of Balochistan with the occupying army, three BLA fighters - Saleem Jattak, alias Qazi Naveed; Ali Dost, alias Mulla Zakir; and Samiullah Shahwani, alias Hakkal - attained martyrdom while fighting gallantly.
Ali Dost, alias Mullah Zakir, son of Rasool Bakhsh, was a resident of the Ghulam Paranz area of Mastung District, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2023 and moved to the mountain front in 2024. He served on the Mastung, Kalat, and Surab fronts and was martyred on April 6, 2026, in Surab.
Ali Dost, known as Mullah Zakir, was a prominent figure within the Baloch Liberation Army. He was distinguished by his strong revolutionary consciousness and intellectual clarity, and he stood as a guiding presence among his comrades. A deep awareness of national responsibility and a firm resolve to confront the enemy were integral to his character.
Upon developing a clear sense of national consciousness, he carried out his responsibilities with discipline and dedication, inflicting considerable losses on enemy forces. Following the completion of his civic responsibilities, he advanced to the mountain front, where he assumed further duties. In a short period, he earned a reputation as a reliable and trustworthy comrade.
He actively served on the fronts of Mastung, Kalat, and Surab, contributing both militarily and ideologically. For committed youth like Ali Dost, the armed front was seen as a decisive means of resistance, and through his actions, he demonstrated that revolutionary thought must be translated into practical struggle.
His steadfastness at every stage of the movement stands as an enduring example for others. His sacrifice has secured him a place among those revolutionaries who, rejecting a life under oppression, chose instead a path of resistance, dignity, and legacy.

Zakir Hussain alias Sami Baloch, son of Abdul Khaliq Rodeni, a resident of Damb, Sorab, was martyred on April 13, 2025, when operatives of a death squad, backed by the Pakistani military, opened fire on him in Sorab. Zakir Hussain began his journey as a freedom fighter in 2018 when he joined the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) to fight for the freedom and dignity of his nation. He was a true and brave fighter, firmly believing that the Baloch deserve to live in a free and sovereign homeland. Despite the brutal oppression of the state, neither his resolve weakened nor did his steps falter in the struggle. Despite facing numerous threats and challenges from the occupying state, Zakir Hussain remained steadfast in his commitment to the Baloch national cause. In 2020, Zakir Hussain was forcibly disappeared by the occupying state's intelligence agencies - a common tactic used to silence Baloch activists and resistance members. He endured unimaginable torture and abuse for eight months in the state’s prisons. Yet, even behind bars, Zakir Hussain’s spirit and determination remained unbroken. The state’s attempt to crush his resolve for freedom failed. Upon his release, he rejoined the struggle with renewed passion and continued to play an active role in various operations against the enemy while remaining part of the BLF’s urban network. His bravery and sacrifices will serve as a guiding light for future generations in the Baloch freedom movement. The sacrifice of fighter Zakir Hussain, alias Sami Baloch, will not be in vain. His role and actions will continue to inspire and lead us in the struggle for Baloch liberation.

On 22 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch stated that BLF fighters had formally launched Operation Almas with a large-scale, coordinated attack on the main camp of the Pakistani army’s Frontier Works Organization (FWO) at Gwadar Zero Point. Fighters from the BLF’s special Saddo Operational Battalion, alongside members of other units, are participating in this major military engagement. The battle continued into the following day, 23 October 2026, with loud explosions and intense gunfire heard from the location. On 23 October 2026, a statement issued by the BLF spokesperson announced the completion of Operation Almas. The statement claimed that dozens of military and intelligence personnel had been killed, the hub of colonial projects had been destroyed, and army and Frontier Corps posts had been wiped out. It declared that the historic Operation Almas had concluded after achieving all its intended objectives. Operation Almas was carried out in Gwadar and the surrounding areas. It has formally concluded after reportedly achieving all its planned strategic, military, and economic objectives following prolonged and intense clashes. During this wide-ranging operation, the occupying Pakistani army and intelligence network suffered what the statement described as irreparable human and material losses. The BLF’s self-sacrificing fighters targeted the Frontier Works Organization’s (FWO) main camp, destroying a key centre for the implementation of colonial projects, particularly in Gwadar and across Makuran. This, the statement asserted, demonstrated to the world that, without the will and consent of the Baloch nation, colonial projects in Balochistan would never be safe. The offices and camps of Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) and Military Intelligence (MI) inside the FWO’s main camp were also targeted by the organisation’s fighters. Several soldiers, including senior officers, were reportedly killed in the attacks. Throughout Operation Almas, the Jind-Nadr Sarmachars not only thwarted every counterattack by the occupying army, every attempt by armoured vehicles to advance, and every reinforcement convoy, but also forced them to retreat, maintaining control of the camp for twenty hours. As a result of the actions of the Saddo Operational Battalion’s fighters during Operation Almas, Military Intelligence (MI) officers, Special Services Group (SSG) personnel, and dozens of regular army personnel were reportedly killed. In addition, the enemy’s main camp, posts, internal barracks, and administrative offices were reportedly destroyed in explosions and attacks. A number of the occupying army’s armoured vehicles, along with surveillance drones and quadcopters, were also reportedly destroyed during the operation. After repeatedly inflicting defeats on the occupying enemy during Operation Almas, the Jind-Nadr Sarmachars of the Saddo Operational Battalion, adhering to the philosophy of the last bullet, sacrificed their lives in the struggle for freedom, adding a new chapter of bravery to Baloch national history. The following Jind-Nadr Sarmachars played key roles in the operation: Khalid, alias Zamur; Bilqees Didag, alias Almas; Hamidullah, alias Badil; Shakeel, alias Sohrab; Majeed Zaib, alias Aftab; Nasir Ali, alias Nodan; Mujahid Mehr, alias Sagar Zamurani; and Barat, alias Safar Jan. All eight were reported to have embraced martyrdom during this historic operation. On 27 October 2026, the spokesperson issued another detailed statement, announcing that BLF special units had carried out a comprehensive, coordinated, organized, and effective attack on the centres of the occupying Pakistani army, the colonial intelligence network, and exploitative institutions in Gwadar. The statement claimed that more than 80 military and intelligence personnel had been killed; several armoured vehicles, the main army barracks, and intelligence offices had been destroyed; four quadcopters and two surveillance drones had been shot down; and a police station had been seized. It also reported that operations had been conducted at Gabd and Rimdan 250. Following these deadly blows to the state's exploitative structures, Operation Almas was declared successfully concluded. The spokesperson stated that the BLF was formally presenting to the nation, subjugated peoples, and the international community a comprehensive account of the far-reaching military and political achievements of Operation Almas. The historic, organized, effective, coordinated, and comprehensive operation was launched at 4:00 p.m. on 22 October 2026 against the occupying Pakistani state apparatus in Gwadar and the adjoining coastal region. The operation was described as the most organized, coordinated, and far-reaching attack to date against the occupying Pakistani state, its usurping army, intelligence network, exploitative economic institutions, and local puppet administration. It was presented as an expression of the organization's resolve and capabilities. The revolutionary participation of fearless Baloch women, standing shoulder to shoulder with men in the struggle for Baloch national freedom, national survival, and the defence of the coast and its resources, was portrayed as heralding the end of the usurping colonizer. This historic operation was named after the BLF's fearless and courageous guerrilla commander, Almas Baloch. For the past eight years, Commander Almas had been actively involved in the armed national struggle under the BLF banner, driven by her ideological convictions. Bilqees Didag, alias Almas, daughter of Allah Bakhsh Didag, resident of Dasht Kumbel, is a shining chapter of courage, steadfastness and revolutionary sacrifice. She spent her early life in ordinary circumstances and received regular education up to the eighth grade. She was married and has a beloved daughter, but rising above herself and her family circle, she made the cause of the motherland's freedom her whole life. In 2018 she formally joined the armed struggle for national freedom through BLF's revolutionary platform. After joining the organization, she served for four years as a volunteer in the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB), rendering highly valuable and arduous service. For the past eight years Shaheed Almas had been fully active and ideologically committed in the armed defense struggle through the BLF platform. During her organizational life she served as a very active and fearless member of the intelligence wing in sensitive and difficult areas such as Dasht, Turbat and Gwadar. She kept herself in motion day and night to deliver vital intelligence about the enemy to the organization in time. During military fronts and operations, she always carried out, with courage and steadfastness, the very difficult and dangerous responsibility of delivering supplies, weapons and logistics to the sarmachars across Dasht's harsh and rugged mountain ranges. On the path of her revolutionary struggle, the occupying Pakistani army and operatives of the state's death squads made every effort to obstruct her. The occupying army repeatedly attempted to abduct her, hold her in illegal detention and break her mentally and physically, and on one occasion state personnel subjected her to severe torture that left her badly injured. But this tactic of state oppression, taunting and torture could not shake her steadfastness. She faced every hardship with a smile and always stood firm like a rock on the armed front, keeping the flag of freedom high. Even in these grave conditions under state oppression, the wise and courageous way she carried out organizational responsibilities while hiding in various areas is eloquent proof of her high military insight and ideological maturity. Shaheed Bilqees Didag alias Almas put into practice the idea that on the difficult path of national freedom, all hardships, troubles and sacrifices are acceptable, but national slavery and state domination are not acceptable under any circumstances. To realize this idea, she made the final decision to sacrifice herself for the motherland. Shaheed Almas carried out her duties with great devotion in various military detachments and units of the BLF, and from the time the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB) was founded she was its active founder and core member.

Yasir Baloch, alias Sabzo, son of Habibullah, was a resident of Killi Pasond Khan in the Gurgina area of Mastung. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Nushki and Chagi fronts. He was martyred on August 31, 2026, in the Nokcha area of Chagi District, Balochistan.
Hailing from Mastung, Yasir Baloch, alias Sabzo, decided this year to join the Baloch Liberation Army, recognizing the importance of armed resistance against national slavery and embracing it as a goal for national and state formation. He was transferred to the Shor front. After completing basic military courses through hard work and rigorous training, he joined a patrol unit, where he took part in various military operations against the enemy and, together with his comrades, carried out significant actions against the enemy’s looting-based policies. In a short time on the battlefield, he proved himself to be a revolutionary, brave, and fearless fighter.
Martyr Yasir was aware of the historical truth that without state sovereignty, national prosperity and freedom are in no way possible, and it was this realization that mobilized him on the platform of armed resistance, where he took part in numerous military operations against the occupying forces and inflicted heavy losses on them. During a prolonged clash with the enemy, he and his comrades inflicted heavy casualties on the enemy, and he attained the supreme rank of martyrdom. Martyr Yasir chose the struggle for national liberation over a life of humiliating slavery and sacrificed himself for that cause. History will remember him as a great revolutionary fighter.

On 21 October 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 18 October 2026, during prolonged clashes with Pakistani forces in Chaghi Dognan, Balochistan, 10 personnel of the occupying Pakistani army who had arrived to conduct an operation against the BLA were killed, while two BLA fighters, Javed Baloch, alias Malang, and Kamal Khan, alias Saddam, sacrificed their lives for the Baloch motherland.

According to the statement, the occupying Pakistani army attacked BLA positions at 6:00 AM on 18 October 2026. In retaliation, the BLA adopted a tactical approach and assumed defensive positions against the enemy. While defending their fellow fighters and the local Baloch population, BLA combatants launched a counter-offensive against the enemy's ground forces using both light and heavy weaponry. Despite possessing superior manpower and advanced weaponry, the enemy suffered casualties and material losses at the hands of the BLA. Following its defeat on the ground, the occupying Pakistani army requested aerial reinforcements. The forces were also supported by long-range mortar fire and artillery; however, our sarmachars stood like an impenetrable wall against the enemy. During the engagement, enemy drones also arrived in the area to target our fighters. The occupying Pakistani army further subjected the local civilian population to indiscriminate shelling.

In this battle, which lasted from 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM, two of BLA brave sarmachars were martyred. Fighting with exceptional valour, both sons of the soil defended their fellow fighters and the base until the very last drop of their blood. Among these fearless and noble sarmachars, Javed Baloch, alias Malang, was martyred after being struck by a drone.

He joined the BLA in 2025. He hailed from Dalbandin and had inflicted heavy losses on the occupying Pakistani army in several skirmishes.

Kamal Khan, alias Saddam, from Narmuk, fought valiantly alongside Javed Baloch, alias Malang, helping ensure the safety of their fellow fighters. During this prolonged battle, their ammunition ran out. Adhering to the philosophy of the “last bullet,” he chose martyrdom with pride rather than surrendering to the enemy.

Kamal Khan had been actively involved in the struggle under the banner of the BLA since 2022. He served the national cause across various regions of Balochistan, including Bolan, Nagahau, Suran, Narmuk, Mangochar, and Kalat. He was a brave and courageous sarmachar (freedom fighter) who possessed exceptional combat skills.

Shahnawaz, son of Faiz Mohammad, was born on 11th January 1991 in Gichk, District Panjgur. He was a resident of Kark-e-Dal, Gechk, District Panjgur. He received his early education in his hometown and was an F.A. student at Degree College Panjgur.
He joined the Baloch Students Organization at a very young age and continued his struggle for national liberation until his martyrdom. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising peaceful political expression. He was a senior member of the Baloch Students Organization Azad.
He was abducted on 23rd April 2015 by Frontier Corps and intelligence agency personnel from his residence in Gichk, District Panjgur, Balochistan, on the night of his wedding, along with two others. His dead body was handed over to the local Levies Force, a policing agency, on 23rd April 2015 in Gichk, District Panjgur, Balochistan.
He was targeted under the state’s kill-and-dump policy in Balochistan, which

Basit Nadeem, son of Lal Baksh and a resident of Gwarjak, Mashkai, was a political activist. During his wedding ceremony, the Pakistan Army raided his house and arrested him along with his two cousins, Aftab Baloch and Ijaz Baloch, as well a relative, Shah Nawaz Baloch. On the same day, 15 April 2015, they were allegedly killed in a fake encounter in Mashkai. Basit had been newly married.

Sajid Baloch, son of Karim Baksh and a resident of Jimmuri in Gwadar district, was a political activist. He was forcibly disappeared by the Pakistan Army on March 6, 2011, and was later extrajudicially killed while in their custody. His mutilated body was found on August 19, 2011, in the Belar area of Kulanch.

On 11 August 2025, the umbrella alliance of Baloch armed organizations in Balochistan, Baloch Raji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS), launched coordinated operations during which several government installations were destroyed and dozens of Pakistani military personnel were killed. A large quantity of military equipment was also reportedly seized. Images showing the bodies of the deceased Pakistani soldiers, destroyed vehicles, and military uniforms hanging at various locations subsequently went viral on social media.
Even after the coordinated attacks had ended, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), a member of the BRAS alliance, maintained control of the Zehri area and successfully repelled multiple attempts by Pakistani forces to advance into the region.
After holding control of the area for several days, the BLA eventually withdrew. Following its withdrawal, the Pakistani military entered Zehri with gunship helicopters, battle tanks, and a large contingent of troops. According to reports, the forces spread fear and panic through looting and other actions in the area. Since then, Zehri and its surrounding regions have remained under military operations and repression.
Following their defeat at the hands of the armed groups, Pakistani forces allegedly targeted civilians in retaliation. As a result of this repression, 11 Baloch individuals were reportedly killed.
On 16 April 2026, several people from Zehri and its surrounding areas - including Wadera Mohammad Dayaan, Imam Bakhsh, Manzoor Ahmad Miraji, Munir Hayat Dayaan, Izzatullah Pandrani, Habibullah, Mohammad Sharif, Mohammad Ramzan, and three unidentified individuals - were reportedly extrajudicially executed by Pakistani forces while traveling along roads in the Sohinda area. One individual, Abdul Salam, survived with serious injuries.
During the ongoing military operation in the area, these individuals were allegedly detained by Pakistani forces from various locations and transferred to the Sohinda Rest House, approximately five kilometres from Noorgama. There, their hands and feet were allegedly bound, they were blindfolded, and they were subsequently shot dead.
The incident occurred one day after the BLA claimed that two of its fighters had been killed during clashes in the Sohinda area.
In its statement, the BLA said that, on 15 April 2026, its fighters targeted advancing Pakistani military units with a remote-controlled explosive device. Following the explosion, they allegedly carried out an ambush on a military convoy moving toward the area.
The organization claimed that ten Pakistani military personnel were killed in the two attacks, while two of its own fighters, Tanveer Mengal and Saadullah, were also killed.
