data.biography:
Kegad Baloch, a resident of Gomazi, Tump, was a political activist. She was always engaged in mobilizing people about the Baloch national struggle and the importance of participating in this ongoing fight for independence. Pakistani forces tried to force her to stop her activities, but she responded with these words: “We sacrifice ourselves for freedom, but never surrender before the occupier.”
Pakistani forces carried out a military raid on the house of Kegad Baloch and her relatives. During the raid, they tortured women and children. Due to the extreme torture, Kegad was martyred on July 24, 2021.

Muneer Ahmad, son of Sharif, aged 32, was a resident of Istakhali, Naal, Balochistan, and worked as a driver. On 2 October 2026, at approximately 9:00 PM, he was abducted from his home by a death squad. His family was left without any information about his whereabouts, marking the beginning of a month-long period of uncertainty and anguish.

On 2 November 2026, exactly one month after his disappearance, Muneer Ahmad was killed, and his body was dumped in Nal Laghorzard, Balochistan.

Mir Dost, son of Ubaid Ullah and a resident of Kosh Kalat, Tump, Kech, was found dead in the Ginnah area of Turbat, Kech, on November 10, 2025. His body showed clear signs of severe torture as well as multiple bullet wounds.

According to his family, Mir Dost was forcibly disappeared from his home on February 13, 2025, by personnel of the Pakistani security forces. For nearly nine months, his family endured anguish, unaware of his fate despite repeatedly appealing to the authorities. After months of silence, his tortured and bullet-riddled body was recovered, confirming that he had been extrajudicially executed while in the custody of state forces.

On 13 January 2026, in the Washbud area of Panjgur district, members of a death squad operating under the patronage of Pakistani forces, riding in a white Toyota vehicle, attacked the Municipal Committee office and opened fire, injuring the gatekeeper, Mohammad Alam. During the attack, Zohaib Ahmed, son of Mohammad Azam, who had come to the office for an interview, was dragged out from inside the building, abducted and taken away by the attackers. The following day, on 14 January 2026 his tortured and bullet riddled body was recovered from the Bonistan area of Panjgur district. Zohaib Ahmed was a graduate and worked as a shopkeeper by profession.

Babar Majeed Baloch, known by his alias Fareed Baloch, was a dedicated activist from Khuzdar, Balochistan. He committed himself to the Baloch liberation movement by joining the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in 2012.

Babar Majeed was a multifaceted member of the BLA, serving for years as a vital component of the organization's media team. His commitment to the cause went beyond communication, as he was also counted among the courageous, self-sacrificing members of the BLA's elite unit, the Majeed Brigade.

His ultimate act of bravery and loyalty occurred on December 25, 2018. During an attack targeting General Aslam Baloch, Shaheed Babar Majeed exhibited immense selflessness by embracing the General to shield him from the blast, prioritizing the life of his leader over his own.

He embraced martyrdom in this heroic act, falling alongside General Aslam Baloch, Kareem Baloch, Akhtar Baloch, Taj Muhammad Baloch, and Aman Ullah Baloch. Babar Majeed Baloch's life is eternally honored as a testament to profound loyalty, media service, and the highest degree of self sacrifice.
data.fullName: Babar Majeed Baloch alias Fareed Baloch

data.biography:
On 8 August 2016, terrorists attacked the Government Hospital in Quetta, Balochistan, in a suicide bombing and shooting. More than 70 people were killed, mainly lawyers, and more than 130 others were injured.
The majority of those killed were lawyers who had gathered at the hospital after the body of Advocate Bilal Anwar Kasi, president of the Balochistan Bar Association, was brought there. Kasi had been shot dead by a gunman near Mengal Chowk on Manno Jan Road in Quetta while he was leaving his home for his office.
Responsibility for the attack was claimed by various Islamist groups, including Jamaat-ul-Ahrar and the Islamic State Khorasan Province. However, nationalist groups have alleged that these extremist organisations are backed by the Pakistani state and its military to counter the nationalist movement in the region and exploit its natural resources.
Estimates of the death toll ranged between 70 people, while more than 120 were injured. Of those killed, 54 were lawyers. Among them, 15 were Baloch by ethnicity, while the majority were Pashtuns by ethnicity.

The Baloch advocates or lawyers who were killed are identified as follows:

01 Ghulam Farooq Badini, son of Haji Abdul Ghani.
02 Bashir Ahmed Qazi, son of Qazi Ahmed Jan.
03 Bashir Ahmad Zehri, son Haji Mir Ahmed Zehri.
04 Naseer Ahmed Langove, son Abdul Rahim.
05 Chakar Khan Rind, son of Mehmood.
06 Abdul Rashid, son of Abdul Latif.
07 Nooruddin Rakshani, son Haji Naseeruddin.
08 Muhammad Imran, son Ghulam Farooq.
09 Muneer Ahmed Mengal, son Ghulam Murtaza.
10 Sangat Jehan Jamaldini, son of Dr. Jahanzaib.
11 Mohammad Ali Satakzai, son of Taj Mohammad Khan.
12 Mehmood Ahmed Lehri, son Haji Abdul Hameed.
13 Jamil Ur Rehman, son of Qazi Abdul Hameed.
14 Amanullah Langove, son of Haji Dad Karim.
15 Sabir Ali, son of Abdul Rasheed.

Mir Mehmood Ahmed Lehri was a graduate of Law College, Quetta and also held a Masters degree in international relations.
Advocate Lehri was 43 years old.

On 24th August 2011 Pakistani forces raided the hotel of Mulla Haneef & Asghar in Gayab Mand, District Turbat, Balochistan. 19 people were taken into custody & forcibly disappeared, including Gwahram Khalid & Khayham Mohammad Umer, the forces removed the abductees’ shirts, blindfolded them & claimed they belonged to the Baloch Musallah Difa Tanzeem, a notorious death squad.

The abductees were taken to the Mand military camp & forced to chant pro-Pakistan slogans, the next morning, they were shifted to Turbat military camp, lined up & ordered to introduce themselves, when Khayam spoke, a soldier kicked him from behind, knocking him unconscious, an elderly man who protested was also beaten.

The abductees were divided into groups of five & kept in small rooms, it was Ramzan & most were fasting, yet they were given only one glass of water for the entire day.

All abductees were released within a week except Gwahram Khalid & Khayam Mohammad Umer.

On 3rd November 2011, their bodies were found stuffed in flour sacks in Turbat. Khayam showed signs of severe torture; his hand, three fingers & backbone were broken.

Faqeer Jan, son of Ghulam Jan Shambizai, was abducted on the night of October 18, 2025, by a state-backed death squad in Gwaash, Panjgur. Witnesses reported that the abductors arrived in a Surf vehicle and forcibly took him away, and on October 20, 2025 his tortured and bullet-riddled body was found dumped in an open area.
Khuda-e-Raheem Bangulzai was a government employee. He was abducted on 10 December 2010 and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. A week later, on 18 December 2010, his body was found and dumped.

data.organization: Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) / Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS)
data.biography:
At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Zahoor Baloch, also known as Pulli, son of Shah Mohammad, was a resident of Spelinji, Mastung, Balochistan. He was a medical student who joined the BLA and served in the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). He was martyred during Operation Herof Phase II on the Quetta front.
Zahoor Baloch was among those Sarmachars whose lives became symbols of determination, sacrifice, and relentless resistance. Despite being a medical student, he chose the path of the national war of liberation over a comfortable life. He carried within him a deep conviction for the freedom of his homeland—a belief that gave him the courage to face every danger.
On the Quetta front, fighting shoulder to shoulder with his fellow Sarmachars, he proved that the true strength of a revolutionary fighter lies in his resolve and his ideology. In pursuit of the goal of liberating his homeland, he fought until his last breath against enemy forces in the Wali Jet area of Saryab during Operation Herof Phase II, where he sacrificed his life. Through his sacrifice, he left behind the message that those who remain steadfast on the path of freedom live forever in history.
Mir Rustam Marri was a social activist. He was murdered on 23 June 2011 in Dera Allah Yar, Balochistan.

Naik Mohammad son of Adam and resident of Kulli Awaran, was martyred on February 18, 2022, by elements associated with the enemy’s spy network. Due to certain important reasons and sensitive matters, the organization chose to keep the news of his martyrdom confidential.
In late 2012, Naik Mohammad also known as Wahag, joined the struggle for Baloch national liberation through the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF), and remained committed to this national cause until the last moments of his life.
He participated in several battles under the banner of the BLF and fought bravely against the occupying enemy forces.
In 2015, the occupying Pakistani forces demolished his house with dynamite and forcibly displaced his family, pushing them into a life of severe displacement and hardship. Despite these challenges, Naik Mohammad never bowed before the enemy. Instead, he stood firm and remained loyal to the organization and the movement for freedom.

On 30 September 2024, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that they pay tribute to their six comrades - Shafo Sumalani alias Tadain, Samad Khan Chalgari Marri alias Dostain, Mohammad Gul Marri alias Waheed Baloch, Ghulam Qadir Marri alias Anjeer Baloch, Obaid Baloch alias Fida, and Taj Mohammad Chalgari Marri alias Babul - who were martyred in a bombing by jet fighters of the Pakistani Air Force in Harnai, Balochistan. On 12 September, at 4 AM, jet fighters of the Pakistani Air Force dropped several heavy and deadly bombs on BLA fighters, with the support of drone surveillance, in the Ali Khan Thal area of Harnai, Balochistan. As a result of the bombing, six fighters were martyred. After the attack, the morally bankrupt enemy desecrated the bodies of the martyred fighters and took their body parts using gunship helicopters.

Taj Mohammad Chalgari Marri alias Babul hailed from Bolan Pul Kodi and had been serving on the Bolan front for the past three years. His family has been exiled due to the oppression of the occupying state. His brother, Shaheed Commander Nadir Marri alias Gwando, and Shaheed Lal Muhammad Chalgari were also martyrs from his household, which counts nine martyrs under one roof. The organization deeply values the sacrifices made by him and his family.
data.fullName: Taj Mohammad Chalgari Marri, alias Babul

data.biography:
Yahya, the son of Wahid Marri, was a 23-year-old who had recently moved to Hub Chowki in search of work so that he could earn a living and support his family. On 5 July 2026, his life was shattered when he was forcibly disappeared from Hub Chowki by the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD). For two months and 14 days, his family was left in anguish, deprived of any information about his whereabouts and denied the basic right to know whether he was alive. On 19 September 2026, his body was found dumped in Manghopir, Karachi, following what was presented as a fake encounter. Hilal Syed, who had also left Tump and moved to Hub Chowki to work and earn a living, was killed in the same manner.
Yahya and Hilal had left their hometowns with the simple hope of building ordinary lives through honest work. They were seeking nothing more than safety, dignity, and the ability to earn enough to put two meals on the table each day. Instead, their search for a livelihood ended in disappearance and death.
Muneer Baloch, was a resident of the Khuzdar area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 13 November 2013 in Balochistan.

Lateef Baloch, son of Mohammad Noor and Dur Bibi Baloch, was a resident of Murmasi in the Mashkay area of Awaran, Balochistan. He was affiliated with a pro-independence armed organization, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF). He embraced martyrdom during a military clash with the Pakistan Army on October 10, 2019.

On 16 October 2026, a statement issued by the Baloch Republican Guards (BRG) stated that, on the night of 30 September 2026, occupying Pakistani forces arrived in the Sunni area of Kachhi district, Balochistan, to conduct an operation. A sudden confrontation took place between the occupying forces and the freedom fighters, who launched a deadly attack against the enemy. As a result, the occupying army suffered significant casualties and material losses.

During the clashes, five devoted BRG freedom fighters - Bafa Jan Jatoi, son of Lal Jan Jatoi, a resident of Sunni, Kachhi; Fareed Jan Jatoi, alias Zahri, son of Ghulam Jan, a resident of Sunni, Kachhi; Obaidullah Jan Jatoi, son of Sajjar Khan, a resident of Sunni, Kachhi; Imam Din Jatoi, alias Mumtaz, son of Nihal Khan, a resident of Sunni, Kachhi; and Ayaz Jan Ghola, alias Alim, son of Abdul Sattar, belonging to the Ghola Baloch tribe and a resident of Sunni, Kachhi - embraced martyrdom while defending their homeland and fighting for national independence.

All these freedom fighters were highly dedicated, brave, hardworking, and disciplined comrades. They inflicted various forms of losses on the occupying enemy in several areas of Balochistan, including Kachhi, Dhadar, Sunni, Bolan, and Sibi.

Shafi Baloch, son of Mohammad Alam, was a resident of District Sibi. He was a B.A student at Degree College Sibi and the Central Senior Joint Secretary of BSO Azad. He was also a kidney patient. He was on his way from Quetta to Mastung with some activists of BSO Azad when their vehicle was intercepted by three white vehicles at Lakh Pass, and armed men dragged all the passengers out. They took Shafi Baloch into custody, along with his 14 other friends, on 17th June 2011. After six days of extreme torture and physical violence, his mutilated dead body was found in the Bolan area of Mach on 23rd June 2011, showing signs of severe torture by security agencies.
He was a keen lover of books and spent most of his time studying nationalist literature. He was among the top leadership of the Baloch Students Organization Azad at a time when the organization was under the radar of Pakistani state actions, and its activists were being killed on a daily basis. Shafi’s dumped body was part of the continuing policy of “kill and dump” attributed to the Pakistani army against political activists in Balochistan.
Under this policy, the Pakistani army has allegedly killed hundreds of thousands of Baloch political activists to suppress the nationalist struggle spreading across Balochistan. Spreading organizational aims and objectives and raising mass awareness in the Bolan and Mach areas regarding the ongoing Baloch struggle for the liberation of Baloch land, as well as highlighting state crimes being practiced in Balochistan, were important roles he played in a very short period of time. He was one of the important leaders of the organization. His killing was a blow to the organization, but his commitment to the Baloch movement endured until his martyrdom.

Barkat Baloch, son of Azeem, a 25-year-old farmer from Sohrdap, Gresha, Khuzdar, died after 12 days of suffering from injuries sustained in a death squad attack.
On 17 September 2026, Barkat Azeem was travelling with his friend, Alam Khan, son of Dad Bakhsh, to attend a wedding when death squads opened fire on them in Sohrdap, Gresha. Alam Khan was killed in the attack, while Barkat Azeem was critically injured.
Barkat was rushed to Civil Trauma Hospital in Karachi, where he remained hospitalised for 12 days, fighting for his life and suffering from severe injuries sustained in the attack. On 28 September 2026, he succumbed to his injuries and died.
Two friends were targeted in the same attack. One was killed immediately, while the other survived for 12 days in hospital before ultimately succumbing to his injuries.

Yousaf Raza, son of Raza Mohammad, was a resident of Tump, district Kech. He received his early education in Tump and was a student at High School Tump. He was also a member of the BSO Azad Tump Zone. He held different positions in the organization and was soon elected as a zonal member. He played a key role in mobilizing the Baloch youth of his surroundings to join the Baloch liberation movement. He had a keen interest in revolutionary literature. He stood by the organizational policies and continued his struggle for the liberation of the Baloch homeland until his martyrdom. He was threatened by security agencies to quit BSO Azad, but he remained in the movement until the end.
He was abducted on 13 December 2010 by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agencies from Balgathar, district Panjgur, Balochistan. His bullet-riddled body was found dumped on 18 December 2010 in the Murghap region of district Kech, Balochistan. He was killed for practicing his basic right to do politics. His body bore severe signs of torture. He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a very young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

In 1838, the British sent a force led by Alexander Burnes to reinstate Shah Shuja Durrani as the king of Afghanistan by deposing Amir Dost Mohammad Khan. To reach Afghanistan, they needed passage through Balochistan, particularly the Bolan Pass. However, Khan Mehrab Khan refused to allow the British to use his land to attack a neighboring country. The British sent Lieutenant Leach to negotiate with the Baloch government, but the Khan stood firm. When British forces reached Shaal via Bolan, some patriotic Baloch, without the Khan’s knowledge, attacked British troops out of nationalist sentiment and a desire to protect their homeland.
After toppling Amir Dost Mohammad Khan, the British Governor General of India, Lord Auckland, ordered an attack on Balochistan. In 1839, around 7,000 British troops marched from Shaal to attack the Baloch Meeri (capital). Anticipating an invasion, Khan Mehrab Khan declared war and sent messages to tribal leaders, but many saw the British as allies rather than invaders and chose to collaborate with them rather than defend their land. When Khan Mehrab Khan gathered his resistance fighters, the number of loyal warriors had dwindled to only 700 due to the short sightedness of many tribal chiefs. Nevertheless, Mehrab Khan was determined to fight. At his court, a respected figure, Akhund Muhammad Siddiq, advised him that he was not in a position to wage war at that time. He suggested that the Khan should leave Kalat with his companions, regroup and strengthen his forces, and then launch an attack against the British when the time was right, on 13 November 1839, the British forces launched an attack on Kalat, and a fierce battle ensued. During the fighting, Khan Mehrab Khan Baloch was martyred by a British bullet.

Among those martyred alongside him were:

Diwan Bacha Mal, Minister of Finance

Diwan Khem Chand

Diwan Asardas Mukhi, from the Hindu Panchayat of Kalat

Abdul Karim Raisani, brother of Sardar Asad Khan Raisani

Sardar Wali Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (maternal uncle of Martyr Amir Mehrab Khan)

Mir Taj Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (cousin of Mehrab Khan)

Mir Muhammad Ali Shahizai Mengal

Mir Fazal Muhammad Lehri, brother of Sardar Muhammad Khan Lehri

Sardar Zaman Khan Pandrani

Mir Dad Karim Chandozai Shahwani

Mir Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Mir Badal Khan, brother of Sardar Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Khan Muhammad Dehwaar, Arbab-e-Kalat.

Mir Nabi Bakhsh Jatoi, from the Narmak region of Kalat

Mir Qaiser Khan Bizenjo

Mir Shah Dost Bizenjo

Muhammad Raza Waziri Khel

Noor Muhammad Shahizai, son of Polat Sagaar Sarmastani, in charge of the armory

Taj Muhammad Shagasi

On 20 March 2026, in the Hajika area of Surab, Balochistan, 30 year old Obaidullah, son of Aman Ullah, and a farmer by profession  was returning home when he was shot near Hajika Cross by soldiers of the Pakistani Frontier Corps and labeled him a militant.

Shehak Baloch, alias Sabzo, son of Anwar Baloch, was a resident of Turbat, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2024.
Shehak Baloch, alias Sabzo, belonged to Turbat. After joining the BLA, he quickly distinguished himself through discipline, composure, and commitment. He did not seek visibility, yet his presence on the battlefield carried its own weight and commanded recognition.
During Operation Herof I, he fought on the front lines in direct engagements with enemy forces and was seriously wounded. For many, such an experience would have marked the end of active participation. For Sabzo, it became a point of return. After recovery, he resumed his duties with even greater focus and resolve, demonstrating that his commitment was neither temporary nor emotional, but deliberate and sustained.
In Operation Herof II, he carried out a VBIED attack against a military camp on the Dalbandin front. This was a decision made with full awareness of its consequences and executed with determination. His martyrdom reflects the character of a fighter who understood resistance not as a momentary reaction but as an enduring responsibility.

Yaseen Zehri, son of Abdul Quddos, belonged to Anjeera in Khuzdar. He was shot and martyred by a state-backed death squad led by a local tribal chief in the city of Anjeera, Khuzdar, on 4th August 2011.
He received his primary education at Government Primary School Anjeera and completed his matriculation at Government Model High School Khuzdar. He was martyred shortly after passing his first year.
He began his political career on the platform of the Baloch Students Organization Azad in 2009, when he was studying in the 9th class. As a member of the organization, he carried out his responsibilities diligently, due to which he was soon elected as the Deputy Unit Secretary. After completing his matriculation, he was elected as the Unit Secretary of the Gul Bahar Unit.
He remained active in all organizational activities, which led to an FIR being registered against him by the police. He also participated in the Baloch Culture Day program and the central rally of the organization on 15th January 2010, during which they were attacked by Pakistani agencies.
Alongside his political involvement, he had a passion for cricket and led his college team in matches in his area. He was also a poet, and his poetry was published in local newspapers.

On September 12, 2025, the enemy Pakistani army attempted to advance by deploying commandos via helicopters following a drone attack in the Dasht area of Mastung. During this operation, clashes broke out between Pakistani forces and fighters of the Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS). While resisting the enemy’s advance, BRAS fighters eliminated three Pakistani army personnel, while two freedom fighters, Abu Bakar alias Majeed and Abdul Had alias Usman, attained martyrdom.

Martyr Sangat Abu Bakar Kurd, alias Majeed, son of Fateh Muhammad, belonged to the Dasht area of Mastung. He had been associated with the Balochistan Liberation Front for the past year and was serving on the Mastung and Quetta fronts.

Martyr Sangat Abdul Hadd Mengal, alias Usman, son of Haji Mussa, belonged to the Johan area of Kalat. He had been associated with the Baloch Liberation Army for the past year and was serving on the Mastung front in the struggle against national subjugation.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Shoaib Shah alias Meerak, son of Mohammad Omar Shah was resident of Peer Shar, Zehri area of Khuzdar district of Balochistan, he joined the BLA on August 16, 2025 and served in Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS) unit and martyred in Operation Herof Phase 2, Noshki Front.
Hailing from the historic and resilient land of Zehri, Shoaib Shah, known in the resistance as Meerak, was a devoted traveler of the ideological caravan that sought to extinguish the darkness of subjugation with the light of sacrifice. When he took the oath of armed resistance under the banner of the BLA on August 16, 2025, his objective was not merely combat, but the restoration of a dignified national existence. His exceptional intelligence, military discipline, and endurance earned him a place within the ranks of the organization’s most elite and specialized unit, the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS).
Shoaib Shah played a pivotal role in several strategic encounters against the enemy across the rugged terrains of Nagahu and Kalat. During Operation Herof Phase 2, On the decisive front of Nushki, where the ground was made to shrink beneath the feet of the occupying forces, Meerak demonstrated his prowess as a master tactician of the STOS. Even when the enemy unleashed its full military might, Shoaib Shah’s resolve remained unshaken. He defended the motherland until his final bullet, establishing a legacy of steadfastness that will forever serve as a beacon for Baloch sarmachars. His martyrdom is a renewal of the sacred vow that the price of freedom is paid only in blood.

data.biography:
On 1 November 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson, Gwahram Baloch, issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of eight of the organisation’s fighters: Captain Yahya, alias Ustad Khalid Jan; Aris Baloch, alias Omar Jan; Hafeez Baloch, alias Karwan, son of Dad Mohammad; Javid Baloch, alias Gulab, son of Bori Baloch; Abdul Khaliq, alias Nothak; Sajid Baloch, alias Mehran; Hameed Baloch, alias Buzerg; and Akram Baloch, alias Gwahram.

The statement paid tribute to these brave and ideologically committed members of the organisation, who embraced martyrdom while engaging in clashes with the Pakistani army and its death squads on various fronts across Balochistan.

Martyr Aris Baloch, alias Omar Jan formally joined the armed struggle for Baloch national freedom through the BLF platform in November 2024. He was a very sincere, cheerful, kind, brave, hardworking and dutiful sarmachar who always took a leading part in organizational affairs and guerrilla operations. To strengthen the organizational system in Pasni and activate its military network, BLF trusted his exceptional abilities and gave him important organizational responsibilities, which he carried out very well until his martyrdom.

Martyr Aris played a key role in many important military operations and missions during guerrilla warfare on various difficult fronts in Makuran, including Pidrak, Shadikor, Baduk, the Coastal Highway, Pasni, Shatangi and Nalent. He was a very straightforward, principled and fearless sarmachar, always eager and ready to go to the battlefront. On 18 July, during an organizational mission in Pasni city, he was seriously wounded, but as soon as he recovered he resolutely returned to his front and resumed his national duties.

On 7 October 2026, while on patrol in Rek Pusht, Pasni, he came face to face with operatives of the death squad nurtured by the occupying army. In the close-quarters clash with the death squad, Martyr Aris Baloch, alias Omar Jan fought the enemy with great bravery and courage, embraced martyrdom and became immortal in Baloch national history. 2 death squad members were also wounded in the clash, whom the occupying army evacuated them and sent them to Karachi for further treatment.

On 23 January 2011, at approximately 4:15 pm, in the Chitkan area of Panjgur district in Balochistan, Pakistani intelligence agencies, the Frontier Corps, and other genocidal forces raided the house of Nasir Dagarzai. During the raid, they abducted Nasir Dagarzai, Abid Saleem, Mehrab Omar, and Abid Rasool Bakhsh while they were sitting in the guest room (Betak) drinking tea.
Before taking him away, Pakistani forces also shot Nasir Dagarzai three times, leaving him wounded at the scene. The forces then took Nasir to a hospital, after which he was transferred to detention and torture cells, where he was subjected to severe torture. His hands were ground with a grinder and his body was burned with fire.
Approximately five days later, on 27 January 2011, Pakistani forces again shot Nasir Dagarzai and Abid Rasool Bakhsh. At around 1:00 am, they took them to the forests of Gowargo in the Panjgur area and dumped them there. Abid Rasool Bakhsh succumbed to his wounds and died there. However, by chance, Nasir Dagarzai, although badly injured, was found by a person who informed the Levies. He was then transferred to Quetta for medical treatment. After receiving treatment, he was brought back to Panjgur, and due to the gunshot wounds, doctors inserted a rod in his leg.
On 11 March 2011, Nasir Dagarzai gave an interview to Samandar Askani on Radio Gwank in which he described the details of these events.
Later, on 23 May 2011, when Nasir was traveling with his brother Mohammad Gull Dagarzai to Quetta for medical treatment, Pakistani forces abducted him again at the Lak Pass area near Quetta and forcibly disappeared him. On 16 July 2011, he was killed and his mutilated body was dumped. The body was recovered from Lak Pass near Quetta on 17 July 2011.
Similarly, in the same incident, the mutilated bodies of Abid Saleem, son of Mohammad Saleem Baloch, and Mehrab Baloch, son of Haji Mohammad Umar, who had also been abducted and forcibly disappeared, were later recovered on 24 May 2011 from the Margap area of Turbat district in Balochistan.
The short film “The Line of Freedom,” written and directed by the British director David Whitney and produced by Nooruddin Mengal, Mir Bhawal Mengal, and David Whitney, was released in 2013 and was inspired by Nasir Dagarzai.
Nasir Dagarzai’s son, Zameer Dagarzai, was abducted by Pakistani forces and Pakistan-backed death squads on 3 March 2026 from the Chitkan Taar office in Panjgur district, Balochistan. On 11 March 2026, his tortured body was found under the Washaap Bridge in the Panjgur district of Balochistan.

data.martyrdomPlace: Bolan and Harnai Mountainous area, Balochistan
data.biography:
An armed encounter took place between the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) freedom fighters and the enemy forces at Jantro on Saturday, October 23, 2021 in Bolan and Harnai mountainous area. Several occupying Pakistani army personnel were killed and wounded in the battle. While valiantly defending the motherland, four BLA members also made the ultimate sacrifice. The combat with the Pakistani occupying forces began when a a patrolling party of BLA came face to face with the advancing enemy forces. BLA fighters charged at the enemy and a battle ensued that lasted for more than three hours. The BLA Sarmachars set high examples of bravery by eliminating and injuring several enemy troops and completely halting their advance. During the battle, four brave comrades, Tariq Marri alias Nasir, Mohammed Hussain Marri alias Jabal, Bakhtiar Sumalani alias Yusuf and Saifullah Zehri alias Sohrab embraced martyrdom. Deprived of moral values, the enemy army also killed two unarmed Baloch farmers named Juma Khan son of Ali Murad and Mahmood son of Shahu from nearby areas, and threw their dead bodies in the said area to portray them as BLA fighters. 
The martyred comrades Bakhtiar Khan Sumalani alias Yusuf son of Mittha Khan of Shahrag and fellow sarmachar, Saifullah Zehri alias Sohrab son of Saleh Muhammad of Yakbozi Zehri had been defending the Baloch motherland through the ranks of Baloch Liberation Army for the last one year. Both colleagues managed to gain a prominent position in the organization in a short span of time.

On January 14, 2026, members of armed groups working under Pakistani forces, locally known as death squads, abducted Mulla Razaq, son of Dad Mohammad, from his home in Zamuran Newano, Turbat district, Balochistan and forcibly disappeared him. His tortured body was recovered the following day, on January 15, 2026.

Qadeer Baloch, alias Saud Dost, pen name Saud Sobain, son of Abdul Rashid, was a resident of Tump, Gomazi, Balochistan. He worked as an auto-parts shopkeeper and joined the armed struggle in 2013. He joined the BLA in August 2023 and served on the Kulbar, Mazanband, and Zamuran fronts. He held the rank of Camp Commander and was killed on 28 July 2026 in Turbat, Balochistan.
Martyr Qadeer Baloch, alias Saud Dost, had been associated with the Baloch Liberation Army for the past three years, while remaining active in the Baloch armed resistance for a total of 13 years. During this period, he gained extensive experience of difficult and challenging circumstances. He was a sarmachar (guerrilla fighter) who neither became disheartened by the difficulties encountered on the battlefield nor grew complacent following success. Rather, he remained constantly active, advancing, engaging the enemy with determination, and preparing himself for every new challenge that arose. His thirteen-year journey of resistance and his steadfastness throughout that period were defining features of his character and conduct.
Martyr Qadeer did not believe in remaining confined to past circumstances or methods, nor in maintaining a fixed or static approach. For this reason, he continuously adapted to changing conditions, adjusted to the intensification of the conflict and its evolving requirements, and took an active role in organizing and carrying out operations against the enemy. It was on account of these capabilities and qualities that he was chosen as the organization’s Camp Commander, a responsibility he held until his death. Drawing on his extensive experience as well as newer tactics and methods, he participated in numerous engagements and inflicted serious losses on the opposing side. His battlefield experience also served as an important source of learning for newly recruited comrades, who benefited from his knowledge and experience.
Martyr Qadeer’s long association with the armed resistance and the national movement, together with his steadfastness until the very end, represents a significant achievement in his years of struggle. His long and unwavering commitment to national freedom, his continued participation in the armed resistance, and ultimately his sacrifice of his life for his homeland will ensure that he is remembered in Baloch national history as a dedicated freedom fighter.

Mohsin Ali, alias Chiragh, son of Mohammad Ali, was a resident of the Nagor area of Panjgur district in Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2023 and became part of the Majeed Brigade in 2024.
Mohsin Ali, alias Chiragh, was among the fighters who took part in both phases of Operation Herof. His consistent participation reflected his unwavering commitment and practical experience. data.fullName: Yasir Zehri Baloch, alias Master Safar Khan
data.biography:
On 5 November 2024, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that on 4 November 2024, BLA fighters ambushed a convoy of the occupying Pakistani army in the Qadirabad area of Nushki, resulting in at least 10 enemy personnel of the occupying force being eliminated on the spot. In the ongoing extended battle, two veteran BLA fighters fought valiantly and accepted martyrdom.
During the prolonged fight, two comrades of the Baloch Liberation Army, fighters Adnan Baloch (alias Safar Khan) and Yasir Baloch (alias Master Safar Khan), defended the motherland with courage and bravery, embracing martyrdom.
Adnan Baloch, alias Safar Khan, despite being injured by an enemy bullet, did not abandon his position and continued fighting for over an hour, allowing his unit a secure retreat before sacrificing his life.
In this battle, another esteemed BLA comrade, Yasir Baloch, alias Master Safar Khan, was also wounded in an extended clash with the enemy. He managed to hold his ground, but due to excessive blood loss, he too attained the noble status of martyrdom
Yasir Zehri Baloch, alias Master Safar Khan, son of Lal Jan Zehri, belonged to the Mulla area of Khuzdar. At 27 years old, Yasir, a mechanical engineer, joined the BLA in 2018, serving on both urban and mountainous fronts against the forces of occupation. Yasir fought in significant battles across Bolan, Nagaho, and Shorparud (Kalat), playing a vital role in defeating the enemy. His dedication, sincerity, and tenacity in the pursuit of Baloch freedom were unparalleled. A true warrior, Yasir’s courage and intelligence marked him as an exemplary BLA soldier.

On 20 October 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that Sarmachars (freedom fighters) of the BLA had carried out 34 high-intensity military operations over 12 days across various regions of Balochistan between 9 and 20 October 2026. In these attacks, 14 personnel of the occupying army and nine operatives of Military Intelligence and death squads were killed, while operational control and snap-checking on key highways continued successfully under the organisational policy of an “economic blockade.”

During these operations, the freedom fighters also captured a serving soldier of the Pakistani army. In face-to-face clashes with occupying forces on various fronts, six BLA fighters fought courageously and attained the highest status of martyrdom.

Amanullah Mengal, alias Meerak, who was severely injured in a quadcopter attack by the occupying army at Ziarat Cross, succumbed to his injuries and was martyred on 8 August 2026.

On 18 September 2026, intense clashes took place between the occupying Pakistani army and BLA fighters at Siah Chang in Chagai, resulting in the deaths and injuries of several occupying army personnel, while the brave BLA fighter Ishaq Shokat Baloch, alias Meeran Baloch, attained martyrdom while fighting courageously.

On 19 September 2026, a prolonged and bloody confrontation took place between the occupying Pakistani army and BLA fighters at Paroom in Panjgur. During these clashes, four personnel of the occupying army were killed, several were injured, and one military vehicle was destroyed. In this battle, four BLA fighters - Ali Baloch, alias Salman Baloch; Ikhtiyar Baloch, alias Fareed Baloch; Sanaullah Baloch, alias Shay Mureed; and Sohail Baloch, alias Haji Absar - fought heroically and attained the highest status of martyrdom.

Ali Baloch, alias Salman Baloch, son of Rozi Khan, was a resident of Dambuk, Buleda. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served in Paroom, Panjgur, Balochistan. He was martyred on 19 September 2026, in Paroom, Panjgur, Balochistan.

Ali Baloch, alias Salman Baloch, made the conscious, intellectual, and historic decision to join the ranks of the Baloch Liberation Army this year in defense of Baloch land, sovereignty, and freedom, becoming part of the ongoing national liberation struggle against the occupying force. He took up his position on the Paroom front under the guidance of his command and, by demonstrating excellent performance in basic training courses, proved himself ready to fight on the front lines. Sangat Ali, a native of Buleda, established himself in a short period on the battlefield as a revolutionary, ideologically committed sangat capable of confronting harsh conditions.

He took part with great bravery and courage in various military engagements and operations against the enemy, inflicting losses on the occupying force. He remained firmly and courageously committed to the ideological and intellectual convictions with which he had decided to take part in this great national struggle and never hesitated to make sacrifices. On 19 September 2026, he attained martyrdom alongside some of his comrades during an operation against the enemy, bringing honor to his nation and homeland. His spirit of sacrifice and the blood he shed in the cause of national liberation will serve as a guiding light for other young people, inspiring them to become part of this great struggle.

Taimoor, son of Imam Bakhsh, a 26 year old farmer from Surab, was abducted and forcibly disappeared by the Pakistani Frontier Corps on February 9, 2026. After several days in custody, his body was found dumped in the Surab area of Balochistan on February 20, 2026. His body showed clear signs of severe torture.

On 25 August 2024 Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch announced the launch of a "Fidayeen Operation" named "Herof" across Balochistan. As part of this operation, fidayeen from the BLA's elite unit, Majeed Brigade, have attacked the main camp of the Pakistani forces in Bela and have successfully infiltrated it. Meanwhile, other BLA fighters have taken full control of all major highways across Balochistan, blocking them completely.
During Operation “Herof,” 44 attacks were carried out simultaneously at 40 locations across 13 districts of Balochistan. As a result, 130 Pakistani army personnel were killed and 55 were injured. In addition, gas pipelines were destroyed at 2 locations, railway tracks at 7 locations, and 2 bridges were blown up.
During the operation, 13 vehicles transporting minerals were set on fire. Blockades were also established at 14 locations across Balochistan, and 3 members of a “death squad” were killed.
As part of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayee (suicide) operation “Herof,” the BLA’s Majeed Brigade carried out an attack on the Pakistani army’s Bela camp. The Majeed Brigade maintained control of the camp for twenty hours, during which 68 enemy personnel were killed.
Nine fidayeen (self-sacrificing fighters) of the Majeed Brigade at Bela camp - Ghaus Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Talib), Mahal Baloch (alias Zilan Kurd), Rizwan Baloch (alias Hammal), Mohammad Baloch (alias Meerak), Fazal Gul Zehri (alias Shawaiz), Tayyab Baloch (alias Lala), Junaid Zehri (alias Kami), Mohammad Asif Nechari (alias Naveed), and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Khalid) - along with Shafqat (alias Dayar) of the Fateh Squad in Mastung, were martyred in the operation.
Ghaus Baksh Sumalani, alias Talib, and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani, alias Khalid, were brothers. They took part in the same operation and were martyred while defending their motherland.

Abid Rahman, alias Rahman, son of Aziz-ur-Rahman, was a resident of Alandor, Buleda, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2024 and moved to the mountain front in 2026, where he served in the media unit. He was martyred on 29 July 2026 in Zamuran.
For the last two years, Abid Rahman had been an active participant in the organization’s national and revolutionary program of armed resistance and was involved in organizational activities in various capacities. Along with participating in different military activities on the urban front, he completed various media courses under the organization’s policies and developed his abilities in the relevant field.
In accordance with organizational orders, he joined the organization’s camp on the Zamuran front this year. There, he participated in various physical and training courses and completed them successfully. During the training, he demonstrated considerable hard work, dedication, and enthusiasm for learning, which drew the attention and admiration of his comrades.
Abid Rahman was a supporter of modern and rapid forms of warfare rather than traditional methods. He possessed broad revolutionary thinking and an ability to observe and understand situations, qualities that were consistently reflected in his practical activities.
During his national and wartime service, in addition to participating in armed resistance and fulfilling his responsibilities, he played an active role in the media unit in the field, where he demonstrated his abilities to the fullest. He worked with great dedication to bring firsthand footage from the battlefield to the public and the wider world. He fulfilled every responsibility assigned to him by the organization with professionalism and commitment.
His ability to observe the circumstances and events arising in the field and to understand them correctly was one of his prominent qualities. Organizational discipline, responsibility, and seriousness were fundamental aspects of his work. Through these qualities, he established a strong example in a short period.
He fulfilled the responsibilities entrusted to him until the end. While resisting an opposing force during an operation, he was killed on 29 July 2026 in Zamuran. His sacrifices will be remembered in the pages of history.

Mehran Baloch, son of Haji Akbar and a resident of Minaz, Buleda, was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 16 November 2025, when Pakistani security forces raided his home and transferred him to a military camp. His whereabouts remained unknown until his body was discovered in Sohlo Kour, Buleda, Kech District, on 21 October 2026, alongside the body of Yasir Baloch, son of Baloch Khan, who had also been a victim of enforced disappearance by Pakistani forces.

On 2 June 2025 in the Mach area of Bolan, Pakistani forces and fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) came face to face when the fighters were travelling for organizational activities. At a location called Goni Para, clashes broke out between the BLA fighters and the Pakistani forces. During the confrontation, the forces deployed commandos using helicopters. In the clashes that continued for several hours, at least eight personnel of the opposing forces were killed, while five BLA fighters - Washdal, alias Mashmar; Samiullah, alias Sameer; Shehryar Shahwani, alias Chairman; Sajawal, alias Cheeda; and Nadir, alias Chiragh - achieved martyrdom.
Washdil, alias Mashmar, son of Lal Khan Sumalani, belonged to Sanjawal in the Bolan region. 22 old Washdal joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2024 and at a young age, took up arms with the resolve to fulfill what he saw as his national responsibility. He played an important role on many occasions on the Bolan front and ultimately embraced martyrdom after inflicting significant losses on the enemy.
Samiullah, alias Sameer, son of Muhammad Akram; the Shehryar, alias Chairman, son of Mehrab Khan Shahwani; and the Sajawal, alias Cheeda, son of Bawal Khan Shahwani - all belonged to Parangabad in Mastung. These three companions joined the BLA a year ago and as urban guerrillas, participated in several successful operations. Always active in striking the enemy and fulfilling organizational duties, they were present on every front. Their lives, devoted to the cause of national freedom, have become a guiding light for Baloch youth.
Nadir, alias Chiragh, son of Mazar Khan Lehri, was originally from Narmuk in the Kalat region but was residing in Quetta. In his guerrilla role, he was highly organized, vigilant, and steadfast, confronting the enemy with courage. Constantly engaged in organizational work, he remained firm in his responsibilities until his final breath.
Shahnawaz Zehri, was a resident of the Mashkai area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 11 July 2016 in Balochistan.
Ali Nawaz Gohar was a resident of the Mehi, Mashaki area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 4 August 2015 in Balochistan.

Martyr Siraj was a resident of Geshkaor, in the Kolwa area of Awaran, Balochistan. He had been affiliated with the pro-independence organization Baloch Republican Army (BRA) for several years. Along with his two comrades, Razzaq Baloch and Bahoot Baloch, he embraced martyrdom during a clash with the Pakistan Army in the Rekachai area between Mahra and Kolwa in Awaran on October 16, 2015.

data.biography:
Rahmdil, son of Muhammad Bakhsh, a 24-year-old labourer and resident of Singabad Tajaban, was forcibly disappeared in January 2026. He had been summoned by Pakistani forces to the Hoshap camp. After being told that he was free to leave, he and his elder brother were intercepted a short distance away near Guwand Sarin by state security personnel and state-sponsored death squads. His elder brother was beaten and released, while Rahmdil was taken away, and his whereabouts remained unknown.
For months, his family demanded his safe return. On 20 January 2026, family members blocked the CPEC Road at Tajaban in protest, calling for Rahmdil’s recovery. The protest was later called off after authorities assured the family that efforts would be made to secure his release. However, those assurances never materialized. Instead, after months of anguish, Rahmdil’s mutilated body was found dumped near Banuk-e-Chadai in the Kech area on the morning of 20 June 2026.

On 13th April 2026, in the Barkhan area of Balochistan, Pakistani forces shelled and bombed civilian populations, killing twelve innocent Baloch civilians, including women and children, and seriously injuring three others.

The martyrs are:

- Ali, son of Sultan Umair, aged 40
- Babul, daughter of Gulzar, aged 30
- Mir Jan, son of Ali, aged 2
- Somri, daughter of Bhangan, aged 35
- Balach, son of Sabzo, aged 70
- Shari, aged 22
- Rehman, son of Balach, aged 18
- Naikho, daughter of Jamalan, aged 17
- Allah Bakhsh, son of Balach, aged 6
- Saddo, daughter of Balach, aged 13
- Hapo, daughter of Balach, aged 8
- Mahrang, daughter of Balach, aged 2

The injured are:

- Zarbibi, daughter of Sher, aged 55
- Hazar Khan, son of Balach, aged 9
- Israr, daughter of Balach, aged 15

This is not the first time that Pakistani forces have bombed civilians in Balochistan, targeting unarmed and innocent women and children as a form of collective punishment. Nor can this be considered “collateral damage.” Rather, the Pakistani state and its forces are deliberately targeting the Baloch people to maintain an atmosphere of fear in the region, suppress internal dissent, exploit Baloch coastal resources, and continue policies of genocide against the Baloch nation.

Fazul Baloch S/O Mohammad Umar, alias Gwahram Baloch, was born on 1st March 1994, in Mand Gayab, Balochistan. He received his primary education at Gayab Primary School & completed matriculation at High School Mand Soroo. Fazul Baloch was intelligent, well-mannered & talented, with a particular passion for football, excelling as a goalkeeper.

He began his political career in 2008. Through tireless work, love for his homeland, and active political engagement, he studied political circles, Balochi literature & history while organizing local political activities. At that time, political activism in Mand was very limited.

Balochistan was unsafe for politics, with activists frequently abducted by the Pakistani military & their bodies mutilated recovered. Peaceful gatherings were often attacked. Observing this, Fazul Baloch connected with armed Baloch groups & joined the Baloch Republican Army (BRA). In 2010, after completing two months of guerrilla training at the BRA camp in Mangochar (Mastung), he returned to Mand to continue armed activities.

Later, he left BRA & joined the Baloch Liberation Front (BLF). After his close associate Martyr Zubair Baloch was abducted & killed in 2011, Fazul Baloch temporarily went abroad to fulfill organizational duties. During this time, his brother Khayam Baloch & cousin Gwahram Baloch were abducted & killed. Abroad, Fazul Baloch took a well-paying job, but after completing his responsibilities, he returned to Balochistan.

He personally purchased a cruiser pickup, two motorcycles & a sniper rifle for his organization. On the battlefield, he worked tirelessly alongside his companions & was appointed Deputy Commander of the Mand network. He was also the driving force behind a rehabilitation center for youth affected by drugs, managing both treatment & essential needs.

Due to military operations & state oppression, many Baloch were forced to migrate. Fazul Baloch’s family had relocated to western Balochistan for safety. On January 5, 2018, he visited relatives there. On the night of January 8-9, while returning home, he was shot, severely wounded & captured by Iranian border forces. Admitted to a local hospital after intervention by relatives, he succumbed to his injuries on 13th January 2018 attaining martyrdom.

Shakoor Baloch was born on 23rd August 1988 in the fertile land of Mastung. He belonged to the Dehwar tribe of the Baloch nation. Shakoor Baloch completed his primary and secondary education in his native town. After completing his intermediate studies, he decided to pursue higher education in Quetta, where he joined BSO Azad.
Shakoor Baloch was so deeply devoted to the national cause that, at a very young age, he embraced martyrdom for his motherland. In the initial phases of his political career, he was elected as Deputy and Unit Secretary of the University of Balochistan (UOB) unit. After gaining political maturity and understanding, he was elected as a Central Committee Member of BSO Azad in the 2012 council session.
Moreover, Shakoor was a dedicated and committed activist of the organization. Besides his educational career, he devoted his entire life to political activities. To cover his educational expenses, he worked as a part-time teacher at a language centre while continuing both his studies and political work simultaneously. He was a promising learner, and his personality remained inspiring and influential among Baloch students.
Shakoor was a very simple person with a gentle demeanor, modest nature, and humane character. His way of communicating with friends and people around him was widely appreciated, and he was a keen observer. Behind his humble nature, he carried a deep vision for the future of the Baloch nation.
Shakoor was martyred by the forces of Pakistan on 18th August 2013 on Sariab Road near Balochistan University, in front of Barma Hotel. This was a huge loss for the entire Baloch nation, and particularly for the organization in which he served as a committed Central Committee Member. Unfortunately, his mother and father were also tortured and beaten by Pakistani agencies on the same day when they went to receive the body of their devoted son, a great son of the Baloch soil.

On February 23, 2022 the occupying forces of Pakistan stroke the Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) guerrilla camp in Satak Kor mountain range of Hoshab, district Kech and fired three missiles loaded with chemicals that wreaked havoc over a large area, destroying palm groves and other plants at the site. After the drone missile attacks, the infantry team of the occupying forces surrounded the area, and with the help of more than eight state helicopters entered the camp. Five Sarmachaars including two commanders of the organization Master Asif Baloch and Siraj Baloch were martyred in this attack. While the other five Sarmachaars - Shoaib, Munir, Arif Jan, Diljan, Kamal, Kamash Malang, Jangi Khan, and Daolat - were martyred in the defense of the homeland, fighting the enemy for over an hour and killing several commandos of the occupying forces.
The martyred son of the motherland, Commander Master Asif alias Mukesh Jan son of Muhammad Raza, was the operational commander of Shapuk area of Hoshap region and a member of the organization's Central Advisory Committee. He was a teacher who started his career as a teacher in 2002. Under his national responsibility, he taught his students about national slavery and national liberation instead of teaching the false curriculum of Pakistan. He was working as a political activist for the national liberation until 2015, and then he joined the armed resistance. After the martyrdom of Jamil Jan alias Kia along with four of his associates in Pasni Shadi Kaur in 2017.
Master Asif was appointed as the Operational Commander of Hoshab region of the organization who fulfilled his responsibilities till the martyrdom. He was a great teacher and a warrior.
data.martyrdomPlace: Satak Kor, Hoshap, Turbat district, Balochistan

data.biography: Anwar Kethran was a journalist who was assassinated by state-backed goons on the evening of 23 July 2020 as he rode his motorbike home in the town of Barkhan. He was killed for informing the public about alleged corrupt practices by Pakistani officials and for writing about state brutality in Balochistan.

data.familyDetails:
On October 16, 2025, Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) freedom fighters took control of a Levies Force outpost at Mill Shahurai in Surab and seized the personnel’s weapons. The outpost had been involved in extortion, prompting the operation. Meanwhile, another squad blocked the Quetta–Karachi highway for over an hour and conducted snap checks.

During the blockade, a police vehicle arrived. The fighters asked the personnel to surrender their weapons with a guarantee of safety. All complied, but one personnel opened fire, resulting in the martyrdom of Maqbool Baloch, alias Bali, and serious injuries to Kamran Baloch, alias Sahrot, who later succumbed to his wounds on the way. The personnel who opened fire was neutralized in retaliation.

Martyr Maqbool Mohammad Hassni, alias Bali, son of Mola Bakhsh Muhammad Hassni, belonged to Ahmedwal, Noshki. Known for bravery and sincerity, he joined the BLA earlier this year and quickly earned respect due to his hard work and fighting skills. He served on the fronts of Shoor Parod, Noshki, and Kharan.

Martyr Kamran Sumalani, alias Sahrot, son of Martyr Jalaluddin, also from Ahmedwal, Noshki, joined the BLA in March this year. He served on the fronts of Shoor Parod, Noshki, and Kharan, dedicating his days and nights to the cause of national liberation until his last breath.

data.biography:
Ameer Baloch, alias Kamran, son of Master Babo, was a resident of Konshkalat, Tump. He joined the armed struggle in 2023 and became a member of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in January 2026. During his service, he was deployed on the Dasht and Kulbar fronts. He was martyred on 6 May 2026 in Konshkalat, Tump, Balochistan.
Ameer Baloch, alias Kamran, decided to join the Baloch Liberation Army in early 2026, after which he was deployed to the Kulbar front. He had come to believe that the Baloch nation could never achieve a prosperous and bright future under Pakistan's rule. He believed that, in order to achieve this objective, the Baloch people would have to restore their right to sovereignty over their own homeland.
He was a committed soldier of the BLA's offensive military strategy and the national defense against the occupying Pakistani state. He actively participated in military operations against the enemy on both the Kulbar and Dasht fronts. Among his comrades, he was known for fighting on the frontlines and confronting the enemy with courage and determination. Alongside his fellow Sarmachars, he inflicted numerous blows upon the enemy on the battlefield.
Rather than spending his life in silence under the shadow of subjugation, Martyr Ameer Baloch chose the path of revolutionary and active struggle. He remained steadfast in this cause and ideology until his final breath and ultimately attained martyrdom. His sacrifices stand as a clear message to the enemy: the Baloch people will never accept the occupation of their homeland, and sooner or later, sovereignty will be restored to Baloch soil.
Mahzaib Asghar was identified as one of the young female children (reportedly 4 years old) killed in the missile strike in Sistan and Balochistan.

Gazzain Naseer Qambarani, 24 years old, was the youngest among his seven siblings. He received his early education in Quetta city, Balochistan, where he was residing with his family. He was an active political worker and had served as the President of the Baloch Students Organization’s Islamabad Zone in 2014. He played an important role in organizing activities in a place like Islamabad, where only a few Baloch students were residing for their educational purposes. He wished to complete his education, but the security forces did not allow that to happen.
In the early hours of Tuesday, 7 July 2015, the Frontier Corps (F.C.) raided Kili Qambarani at around 07:00 a.m., Pakistan Standard Time. After a house-to-house search, the forces took Gazzain Qambarani with them. On 13 August 2016, security forces handed over three dead bodies to Civil Hospital Quetta, Balochistan. The security forces bluntly lied and claimed that he was killed in an encounter, while he had been in their custody for a long time. Since then, fake encounters of Baloch youth have continued by the Pakistani security forces. His family has also repeatedly been targeted by security agencies due to their political affiliation with a Baloch political organization.

Najeeb Ullah, son of Lal Bakhsh, aged 31, a resident of Meri-a-Kallag in Kech, Balochistan, and employed as a Naib Qasid (junior staff member) at a government school, was tragically killed by state-sponsored militias, locally known as death squads, on October 30, 2025. The incident occurred at approximately 7:15 a.m. near Meri Link Road, close to Mehran Shop, when assailants in a white Toyota Corolla opened fire on him.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Balach Shah, alias Meeras Mehr, son of Shahbaz, resident of Bostan, Tump, Turbat district of Balochistan, joined the BLA in August 2023 and the Majeed Brigade in October 2023. He was active in Kahan and the entire Koh-e-Suleman region.
Balach Shah hailed from Bostan in Tump, a region where resistance is not merely a political stance but part of the collective social consciousness. After joining the BLA in August 2023, he distinguished himself in a short period through discipline, composure, and operational reliability. His induction into the Majeed Brigade in October 2023 reflected both his military preparedness and ideological commitment.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, he was appointed as Operation Commander on the Dalbandin front. On this sensitive front, he was responsible not only for operational planning and field coordination but also for maintaining frontline leadership. He ultimately attained martyrdom while fulfilling these responsibilities.

On November 12, 2024, in the Balgatar area, during an organizational mission, the comrades of the organization were martyred while bravely fighting the enemy. The martyrs include Second Lieutenant Azum, alias Qasim, son of Muhammad Rahim, a resident of Teertej Awaran; Second Lieutenant Anwar, alias Sana, son of Hussain, a resident of Red Tok Balgatar; Arab Nawaz, alias Jahanzaib, a resident of Gresha; and Zaheer, alias Azad, son of Fazal, a resident of Biront Keelkor. They all sacrificed their lives in defense of their motherland.

A press statement issued by the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) on 16 October 2024 stated that on Friday, 11 October 2024, two of the organization’s fighters were travelling to Pirandar Sorak Kor in Awaran for organizational work when they were ambushed by agents of a death squad formed by the Pakistani state. As soon as the agents spotted the comrades, they opened indiscriminate fire and attempted to surround them. Both Captain Talib Baloch and Adil Baloch embraced martyrdom as a result of the gunfire.
Captain Talib Baloch, known as Modi, son of Mir Muhammad and a resident of Draski, Awaran, had been associated with the Balochistan Liberation Front since 2012 and had dedicated his life to the cause of Balochistan’s national freedom. He participated in numerous significant battles, inflicting heavy losses on the enemy in terms of both lives and resources. His important role was evident in successful operations across various regions, including Basima, Rakhshan, Balgatar, Washuk, Mashkay, Awaran, Kech, Ormara, Gichk, and Panjgur.
Martyr Talib Baloch was compassionate and kind to his comrades and remained steadfast, committed, and active with unwavering determination.
In an attempt to weaken their resolve and force them to abandon the national struggle, state forces subjected his family to collective punishment: family members were forcibly disappeared, their property was set on fire, and they were forced to flee their homes. Yet, despite all these atrocities, the martyr’s determination remained unshaken. Even under severe hardship and oppression by state forces, Martyr Talib Baloch never wavered from his commitment to national freedom. His courage and sacrifice are proof that no obstacle in the path of the struggle could defeat him. His twelve-year struggle stands as a living testament to the philosophy of sacrifice, and in the end, he joined the caravan of martyrs.
Martyr comrade Adil, known as Nasir, son of Nawab and a resident of Ziarat Dan, had been associated with the Balochistan Liberation Front for the past year and was part of the organization’s urban network. He was a determined, educated, and courageous comrade who sacrificed his life for the freedom of his homeland. The enemy’s intelligence agencies forcibly disappeared him twice, but despite all the difficulties, they failed to break his resolve.
data.martyrdomPlace: Pirandar Sorak Kor, Awaran District, Balochistan

data.biography:
On 31 May 2021, Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) fighters attacked the Pakistani military’s “Awais” camp (Ghazaband Scouts’ 129 Wing) in Marwaar, Bolan. The three-hour assault completely destroyed the camp. BLA fighters killed 24 Pakistani soldiers on the spot and captured Lance Naik Bilal from Dera Ismail Khan. He was later tried by a Baloch national court and executed.
Following a coordinated plan, the fighters surrounded the camp, cut through barbed wire, and stormed inside. After intense fighting lasting over three hours, they overran the base, killed 24 enemy personnel, seized a large quantity of arms and ammunition, and took one prisoner. As usual, the Pakistani military downplayed its losses.
Three BLA fighters embraced martyrdom in the operation: Hangal Marri (alias Laila), Aftab Jattak (alias Washain), and Shahwez Zehri (alias Saraang). They were buried in Bolan with full military honours.
The three belonged to the elite Fateh Squad, formed in 2018 and named after Martyr Fateh Qambrani (alias Chairman), who single-handedly enabled the capture of an enemy camp in Meshdari, Shahrag, the same year. Fateh Squad members are selected for exceptional bravery and close-combat skills.
In the Marwaar attack, these three charged the enemy lines, breached the perimeter, and created openings that allowed the BLA to capture the camp entirely.
Hangal Marri (alias Laila) joined the BLA in 2006 and served with distinction on the Kahan and Bolan fronts for 15 years.
Aftab Yousuf Jattak (alias Washain), a highly educated economics graduate from Zehri, joined in 2019 and quickly earned a place in the Fateh Squad due to his skill and courage.
Shahwez Zehri (alias Saraang) joined in 2017, served in urban units, then volunteered for the Bolan front and the Fateh Squad, where he fought bravely until his martyrdom.

data.fullName: Waqar Ahmad Lehri, alias Chakar Josh
data.biography:
Waqar Ahmad Lehri, alias Chakar Josh, son of Sanaullah Lehri, was a resident of the Balochi Street area of Quetta, Balochistan. He joined as an urban guerrilla in 2022 and later moved to the mountain front in August 2025. He served on the Quetta and Noshki fronts and was martyred on 13 September 2026 in the Sultan Shar area of Qila Abdullah, Balochistan.
Waqar Ahmad Lehri, alias Chakar Josh, joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2022. During the initial period, he carried out responsibilities on the urban front and, due to his discipline, secrecy, consistency, and ability to understand circumstances, established himself as a reliable urban guerrilla. Rather than making emotional decisions, he was accustomed to acting with patience and caution, and he was known for not stepping back from his responsibilities even in difficult circumstances. His transition from civilian life to an armed resistance role was not merely a physical transformation, but also reflected a form of mental training in which discipline, patience, and commitment to his cause were given fundamental importance.
On August 1, 2025, Waqar Ahmed Lehri moved from the urban front to the mountain front. The harsh conditions of mountain life, long distances, difficult terrain, and continuous physical exertion tested his abilities at a new level, but due to his strong physical endurance and exceptional perseverance, he gradually adapted to this environment. According to his comrades, he stood out in physical contests and rigorous training and maintained his morale even in difficult circumstances. After remaining associated with the fronts in Quetta and Noshki, his physical life came to an end on September 13, 2026, in Sultan Shar, Qila Abdullah. His story presents the figure of a young man who faced changing fronts at different stages of his life and remained committed to the path he had chosen until the end.

data.fullName: Rashid Ahmad Zehri, alias Jamal Khan
data.biography:
On 21 October 2025, a statement was issued by Baloch Khan, the spokesperson of the Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS), an umbrella alliance of Baloch armed organizations. The statement said that, in defence of the Baloch population in Zehri, Khuzdar, Balochistan, BRAS forces eliminated dozens of enemy personnel, while six freedom fighters embraced martyrdom. Among them was Martyr Fiaz Jattak, alias Shahwaiz.

The statement added that the occupying Pakistani army attempted to advance for aggressive purposes in the Zehri area of Khuzdar, which is under the control of the Baloch Raaji Ajoi Sangar (BRAS), resulting in fierce clashes. Dozens of occupying army personnel were eliminated in these clashes, while six freedom fighters of the Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar were martyred in defence of the motherland.

Among the martyrs, Abdul Aziz Baloch and Hafiz Muhammad Umar Baloch were martyred on 26 September, while Sanaullah Baloch, Abdul Aziz Baloch, Rashid Ahmed Zehri, and Fiaz Jattak were martyred on 30 September.

Martyr Rashid Ahmad Zehri alias Jamal Khan, son of Mohammad Ashraf Zehri, belonged to Norgama Zehri. At the age of just nineteen, he chose the path of liberation and joined ranks of Baloch Liberation Army three months ago. Despite his young age, he proved with his courage, determination that the yearning for freedom is a sign of faith.

On 7 October 2023, the so-called Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) of the Pakistani genocidal forces killed two Baloch men in staged encounters. Both victims had previously been forcibly disappeared. They were identified as Mohammad Shafi, who was abducted and forcibly disappeared from Quetta on 7 October 2023, and Yousuf Nichari, who was abducted and forcibly disappeared from Nichari Abad, Kali Badu, on 26 August 2023.

On May 17, 2025, during an urban mission, senior members of the organization - Amjid Basham alias Shams Sahir and Sabrullah Baloch alias Wahag Jan, launched an attack on the Pakistani army headquarters "Asghar Gate" in the central city of Turbat, Kech, at 7:00 AM. They used grenade launchers, which hit the target precisely, resulting in the death of one enemy personnel and woundings to two others.
Following the operation, both comrades attempted to withdraw, but the state forces deployed surveillance drones to track them. The enemy forces blocked the escape route, which led to an armed confrontation. In a clash that lasted for about ten minutes, two enemy personnel were eliminated and one was wounded. However, Captain Amjid Basham and Lieutenant Sabrullah embraced martyrdom during the firefight.
Amjid Basham Baloch held the rank of Captain, and Martyr Sabrullah Baloch was a Lieutenant.
Amjid Basham Baloch was a talented, politically mature, and deeply conscious young man. He possessed a rare and dignified blend of leadership, vision, and devotion to national service. With his academic excellence and traditional as well as professional education, he could have easily chosen a comfortable and secure life. But Amjid rejected ease and chose the difficult path of resistance for the freedom and dignity of the homeland.
