Even during his student life, Amjid displayed firm ideological thinking and leadership qualities, which earned him popularity among students and the public in Turbat. In 2017, he formally joined the armed struggle and became actively involved in resistance operations against the enemy. On January 27, 2017, Pakistani forces forcibly disappeared him along with his brother, Barkat Basham. During the 18 months of disappearance, Amjid endured severe physical and mental torture. Yet, his spirit remained unbroken. When he was released on July 29, 2018, his body bore the marks of brutality, but his heart was free from fear. Without hesitation, he rejoined the freedom movement and resumed his role on the ground. After his release, he continued organizing resistance activities in the city. In May 2022, during a mission, he was surrounded by state forces. But with bravery, military skill, and fearlessness, he broke the siege and successfully escaped. He was in the final semester of his BS in Computer Science at Turbat University and also taught English and computer skills at a private academy. His life was a complete chapter of awareness, national service, sacrifice, and courage.

On 14 June 2025, Riaz Baloch, also known as Aman, was killed in a landmine explosion during an organizational mission in the Sahiji mountain range of Dasht (Kech). Aman, active in the armed resistance since 2016, played a key role in previous operations, including “Assrich,” carried out under the BRAS coalition.

Advocate Ameer Bakhsh Langove was born on April 6, 1966, in Quetta, Balochistan. His father’s name was Khan Mohammad. He received his early education at Jamia High School, Quetta. After completing his matriculation, he obtained a diploma from the Polytechnic Institute. He later earned an M.A. in Geology from the University of Balochistan (UOB) and completed his LL.B. at Law College, Quetta.
For a short time, he worked in the Labour Department, but due to his revolutionary activities, he resigned from his position.
His political training was shaped by his brother, Martyr Majeed, who played an important role as an ideological cadre member of the Baloch Students Organization (BSO). Majeed still had much to accomplish, but when the motherland calls her devoted sons, they respond like the Majeed The First, sacrificing their lives in her name.
After the martyrdom of Majeed the First, a remarkable transformation was seen in Ameer Bakhsh. Although Majeed was physically separated from him, he began to regard every Baloch as his own brother.
He regularly studied Marxist and resistance literature. Whenever he met a comrade, he would either give him a book to read or recommend one, insisting that it was essential reading.
When Nawab Khair Bakhsh Marri returned from exile in Afghanistan, Ameer Bakhsh actively participated in the Haq Tawar study circles.
During his time in the BSO, he enthusiastically and skillfully constructed barricades.
Balach Gorgej was his favorite personality. He frequently cited examples from Balach Gorgej, and he carried within him a similar spirit of vengeance and resistance.
He owned an old Yamaha motorcycle, which he mostly used while carrying out organizational duties.
His personality was deeply impressive. Anyone who met him wished to meet him again. He had a strong aversion to narcotics and used to say, “If a person addicted to drugs cannot help himself, how can anyone expect him to help others?”
He was counted among the leading figures of the Baloch Liberation Army and was skilled in guerrilla warfare. In a short period of time, he accomplished feats that, according to Shaheed Babu Ali Sher Kurd, many considered impossible. He used to say that a guerrilla must be at least fifty percent technical. He regarded secrecy as the soul of guerrilla warfare - and few could serve as a better example of secrecy than he did. He remained discreet in every aspect of his life. He rose to the rank of commander, yet very few knew. While living underground, he worked as a farmer in a region of Balochistan, and no one knew his true identity. For ten years, he kept the enemy in a constant state of unrest.
He was severely injured during the Baloch-Pashtun conflict on October 10, 1992, but by what was believed to be the blessing of the motherland, he survived.
He would occasionally recall isolated mistakes made by fellow activists and appear saddened. He often said that if a comrade faced a technical issue, he should ask a thousand times if necessary, because there was no room for error - the first mistake could be the last. Only those comrades about whom he had complete knowledge were included in his command. It was often said that very few activists could endure walking the path he chose, as it was so difficult that many found it beyond their capacity. He detested personal fame and self-promotion.
He was constantly engaged in struggle. He would say that for a slave, there is nothing but the dark night of slavery, and that this night can only be transformed into a bright morning through continuous struggle.
Now, who will give us courage? You used to say that much work still remained. Had secrecy not bound you, you would have guided us on what to do. If you were walking beside us, this journey would feel easier. We do not possess your strength of decision-making. We had read about Dr. Che Guevara in books, but in you we saw a Che Guevara with our own eyes. You were always active, cautious in your work, and you taught your comrades the same. When surrounded by the enemy, you would break through the siege and escape. You took care of your own health and were attentive to the well-being of your comrades. Wherever there was a problem affecting a Baloch, you would personally look into it. When newspapers reported the issue of Baloch women allegedly being buried alive, you appeared deeply disturbed. In your honesty, bravery, and determination, we were reminded of the revolutionary martyr Che Guevara. The motherland is calling you - return to us. Ameer Bakhsh Lango was martyred on January 27, 2010, at around 10 p.m., in a traffic accident on the RCD Highway near Mastung while carrying out organizational duties. After taking his body into custody, BLA informed newspaper offices by telephone on January 28, 2010, of his martyrdom. On January 29, 2010, news of his martyrdom was published in newspapers with headline prominence.
The spokesperson of the Baloch Liberation Army, Meerak Baloch, said regarding his martyrdom:
Mahikan Asghar was identified as one of the young female children (reportedly 7 years old) martyred in the missile strike in Sistan and Baluchistan.

Dolat Baloch, a 24-year-old student and son of Charshamby, was shot and killed in broad daylight by members of a state-backed death squad in Hoshap Bazar, Balochistan. The killing took place as Dolat had gone to accompany his mother, who was collecting financial assistance through the Benazir Income Support Programme.
According to eyewitness, a white Toyota Corolla intercepted them in the marketplace. Without warning or confrontation, Dolat was shot in front of his family. As the gunmen fled toward a nearby military camp, his mother chased after his bloodied body, crying in agony.
This was not the first time Dolat’s family had been subjected to harassment and intimidation by armed actors operating with the protection of Pakistan’s security forces.

Mujahid Baloch, son of Habib, a 22-year-old driver and resident of Kaleri Paroom, Panjgur, was forcibly disappeared on the night of 7 June 2026 from the CPEC Road area of Sarsand, Panjgur. Following his disappearance, his family had no information about his whereabouts.
On 18 June 2026, his bullet-riddled body was recovered near Chakul, Panjgur.

On 13 October 2026, Pakistani genocidal forces killed six Baloch men who had previously been subjected to enforced disappearance and dumped their bodies in the Sui area of Dera Bugti district, Balochistan.
The incident was also confirmed by Sher Mohammad Bugti, the Central Spokesperson of the Baloch Republican Party.

The victims have been identified as follows:
- Mohammad Khan Bugti, son of Yar Mohammad Bugti
- Lalu Bugti, son of Taj Mohammad Bugti
- Shahmeer Bugti, son of Shahal Bugi
- Waheed Bugti, son of Habib Bugti
- Ghulam Din Bugti, son of Kurri Bugti
- Akram Khan, son of Wadera Mazar Khan Bugti

Salman Baloch and Abdul Waheed Baloch were friends who longed for a Balochistan free from occupation and tyranny. Both were students at Degree College Khuzdar. Salman Baloch was the son of Sher Mohammad Baloch, while Abdul Waheed was the son of Ghaus Baksh Mohammad Shahi, a veteran of the 1970s uprising against the Bhutto regime, from the town of Kathan.
Abdul Waheed was no stranger to the brutality of the occupying forces. His father suffered a severe head injury from a gunshot wound in the 1970s, and his brother, Abdul Kabeer, was abducted on March 27, 2009.
The two youths were specifically targeted and shot dead on February 29, 2012, in Khuzdar by local death squad leader Shafiq Mengal, who led Tehreek Nifaz-e-Amn, an organization allied with the Pakistani state and its forces.
Abdul Waheed once famously declared, “Death is unavoidable; if we overcome the fear of it, then nobody in this world can keep our motherland enslaved.”

Inayatullah, son of Khair Muhammad and a resident of Tehsil Paroom, district Panjgur, was forcibly disappeared by state backed death squads on December 1st, 2024. According to family members, he was enforcedly disappeared from his home during an illegal raid by state operatives in early December 2024.

For nearly eight months, his whereabouts remained unknown. On August 03, 2025, his mutilated body was recovered from a remote area of Panjgur.

Operation Dara-e-Bolan, which began on 29 January 2024 continued for two days until 31 January 2024 and was successfully concluded after achieving its intended objectives. A total of 385 Sarmachars from four different units of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) participated in Operation Dara-e-Bolan. Among them were 12 Fidayeen from the BLA’s Majeed Brigade. The other participating units included the Fateh Squad, the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS) and the Intelligence Wing.
Operation Dara-e-Bolan commenced on the evening of 29 January 2024 at 9:00 pm local time and continued for two days. After achieving the desired results, the BLA’s Senior Command Council announced the conclusion of Operation Dara-e-Bolan on 31 January 2024 at 7:00 pm and issued instructions to all units to vacate their positions and report back to their base camps.
During the operation, BLA Sarmachars took complete control of an area within a 70 kilometre radius, including Mach city and the strategically important National Highway N-65. Over the course of Operation Dara-e-Bolan, a total of 78 enemy personnel were killed. These included 45 Frontier Corps (FC) personnel who were killed within the first three hours of the operation in Mach city; 10 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on an army camp at the Pir Ghaib Bolan location; 4 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on a military convoy at the Gokurt Mach location; 12 regular army personnel who were killed on 30 January when Majeed Brigade Fidayeen eliminated them and entered the FC headquarters; and at least 5 SSG commandos who were targeted and killed by the Fidayeen on 31 January 2024. In addition, two police personnel were also killed, including one Station House Officer (SHO).
A large number of Levies and police personnel were captured by the BLA during the operation; however, as they were Baloch, they were released. During Operation Dara-e-Bolan, 13 brave fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army attained martyrdom. Of these, 12 martyred Sarmachars belonged to the Majeed Brigade Fidayeen, while one martyred Sarmachar was from the BLA’s Fateh Squad.
The martyred Sarmachars were: Qasim Baloch, Saddam Hussain, Salal Baloch, Farooq Baloch, Atta Baloch, Hammal Momin, Zeeshan Zehri, Nadir Bangulzai, Nizam Baloch, Zeeshan Baloch, Jamal Baloch, Wadood Satakzai, and Kashif Shahwani.
Salal Baloch, alias Shay Mureed, son of Noor Bibi, joined the armed struggle for Baloch national liberation in 2019. Salal ibn Noor Bibi belonged to the Parom area of Panjgur and had previously been living a prosperous life abroad. However, possessing strong national consciousness, he decided to abandon his life abroad and return to Balochistan. In 2021, he offered his services to the BLA - Majeed Brigade. He was a politically aware and educated young man, and as a guerrilla fighter, he was extremely brave and strategically minded.

On 13th April 2026, in the Barkhan area of Balochistan, Pakistani forces shelled and bombed civilian populations, killing twelve innocent Baloch civilians, including women and children, and seriously injuring three others.

The martyrs are:

- Ali, son of Sultan Umair, aged 40
- Babul, daughter of Gulzar, aged 30
- Mir Jan, son of Ali, aged 2
- Somri, daughter of Bhangan, aged 35
- Balach, son of Sabzo, aged 70
- Shari, aged 22
- Rehman, son of Balach, aged 18
- Naikho, daughter of Jamalan, aged 17
- Allah Bakhsh, son of Balach, aged 6
- Saddo, daughter of Balach, aged 13
- Hapo, daughter of Balach, aged 8
- Mahrang, daughter of Balach, aged 2

The injured are:

- Zarbibi, daughter of Sher, aged 55
- Hazar Khan, son of Balach, aged 9
- Israr, daughter of Balach, aged 15

This is not the first time that Pakistani forces have bombed civilians in Balochistan, targeting unarmed and innocent women and children as a form of collective punishment. Nor can this be considered “collateral damage.” Rather, the Pakistani state and its forces are deliberately targeting the Baloch people to maintain an atmosphere of fear in the region, suppress internal dissent, exploit Baloch coastal resources, and continue policies of genocide against the Baloch nation.
Dur Khan Baloch, was a resident of the Kalat area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 15 May 2015 in Balochistan.

In continuation of the Fidayee (self-sacrificing) operation carried out on 8 July 2026 in Khuzdar city, Balochistan, against the compound of state asset and national traitor Shafiq Mengal, alias Shafiq Laghor (the coward) which resulted in the deaths of 34 members of Shafiq's death squad and the martyrdom of five members of the BLA. According to the organization, this operation, marking the commencement of the first phase of 'Operation Marg-e-Ghadaran' manifests the BLA's growing operational and intelligence capabilities against the colonial system and the criminal networks nurtured under it.

The five Fidayeen involved in this complex battle successfully breached the enemy's siege and retreated safely, while five other freedom fighters sacrificed their lives during various stages of this organized action to complete this crucial operation.
The operation commenced with the breaching of the outer security perimeter of Shafiq Laghor’s house, a responsibility undertaken by a talented Fidayee of the Majeed Brigade, Beebarg alias Pulliya Osama. The 22 year old Fidayee Beebarg hailed from the Tindilan area of Mastung and belonged to the Bangulzai tribe of the Baloch, formally joining the BLA and the Majeed Brigade in 2025. Following his enlistment into the organization's ranks, he remained active on the challenging military fronts of Khuzdar and Dasht, Quetta. Prior to this operation, he had demonstrated outstanding performance during 'Operation Herof 2' in the attack on the Frontier Corps central camp established at the Agriculture Office in Quetta. During the Khuzdar operation, he commanded the explosive laden vehicle, skillfully ramming it into the main gate of Shafiq Laghor's compound. Consequently, the outer defensive lines and checkpoints were reduced to rubble within seconds, instantly killing a large number of the enemy's armed guards stationed there and thereby clearing the path for the inner advance.
Immediately after the severe chaos caused by the explosion at the main gate, the next operational objective was to breach the security network of the compound's inner building, a task completed with utmost dedication and bravery by another valiant Fidayee of the Majeed Brigade, Zia Ur Rahman alias Imran. Hailing from Khadkocha, the 19-year-old Fidayee Zia Ur Rahman belonged to the Shahwani tribe and became a part of the BLA and the Majeed Brigade in 2025. Due to his exceptional combat skills, he quickly rose to the forefront of organizational activities on rigorous fronts such as Khuzdar and Koh-e-Maran. He had also been part of the frontline against the enemy on the Hazarganji front during 'Operation Herof 2.' In this battle of Khuzdar, right after Beebarg’s Fidayee strike, he courageously braved enemy fire to gain entry into the inner building of the compound and detonated the Fidayee jacket strapped to his body. As a result, the inner defensive line was completely destroyed, and the enemy's internal command-and-control system was paralyzed, providing the remaining Fidayeen with the opportunity to secure internal positions.
As soon as the inner security line collapsed, the remaining Fidayeen entered the compound and assumed various positions, where Fidayee Mohammad Ramzan Zehri, alias Shaban, took a stand at the main gate and its surrounding vital sectors to confront the enemy on the frontline. The 25-year-old Fidayee Mohammad Ramzan hailed from the Yakboozi area of Zehri, was the son of Chakar Khan, and belonged to the Zehri tribe. He joined the BLA in 2020 and became part of the Majeed Brigade in 2025 after extensive operational service. He was part of the guerrilla war for a long time across vast and highly sensitive fronts such as Bolan, Harboi, Nagaho, Zehri and Khuzdar and played a key role in the sensitive attack on the Quetta Red Zone during 'Operation Herof 2.' During the Khuzdar operation, he stood firm against the enemy's private death squad and uniformed collaborators at the central gate, fighting a close quarter battle and embracing martyrdom on the frontline while inflicting heavy casualties on the enemy.
The phase of maintaining resistance inside this enemy stronghold until the final moments and penetrating Shafiq Laghor’s residential block to clear all sides was carried out by two Fidayeen comrades of the Majeed Brigade, Shahzaib Baloch alias Sagaar and Shahzain Baloch alias Chedag. A resident of Manguchar, the son of Khalil Ahmed and belonging to the Nichari tribe of the Baloch, Fidayee Shahzaib Baloch began his journey in the organization as an urban guerrilla in December 2024, after which he transitioned to the regular mountain front in March 2025 and became part of the Majeed Brigade in June 2025. He was active on the Nagaho and Shoor fronts and had put up prolonged resistance against the enemy's heavy military strength under the direct command of the martyred Comrade Sameer during the battle at the Noshki main camp in 'Operation Herof 2.' Alongside him was Fidayee Shahzain Baloch alia

On 7 April 2026, a statement issued by the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson, Gwahram Baloch, stated that on the morning of 6 April at 7 AM, fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front, under an extraordinary and well-organized military strategy, killed multiple Pakistani soldiers during an extensive military blockade and control operation on the Quetta-Taftan Highway in Operation Kardigap. Quadcopters were destroyed, and the state defense system was paralyzed. One Sarmachar was martyred.
In this battle, a brave and capable Sarmachar of the BLF, Ikhlaq Ahmad Mengal, alias Nazeer, a resident of Wadh, District Khuzdar, made history with his bravery in face-to-face combat with the enemy and embraced martyrdom. Ikhlaq Ahmed was not only an excellent guerrilla commander but also a revolutionary poet.
He served the movement on difficult fronts in Wadh, Bolan, Mastung, and Kalat, and also served as a camp commander in the Mehlabi area of Kalat. At the time of his martyrdom, he was leading a patrol unit in Kardigap and Garginah.

data.martyrdomPlace: Tadukor, Jhal Jhao, Awaran District, Balochistan
data.biography:
On 9 August 2024 freedom fighter Second Lieutenant Shambein, alias Sheikh Jan, was martyred while bravely fighting a local death squad in the Tadukor area of Jhal Jhao.
Shaheed Shambein, alias Sheikh Jan, son of Noor Mohammad, belonged to Sod Hero Goth in the Jhao tehsil of Awaran district. Before formally joining the BLF, he lived in the city for two years and worked as a supporter of the movement. After two years of tireless dedication and hard work, he officially joined the organization on 15 August 2019.
Because of his hard work, ability, and perseverance, he rose to a high position in a very short period. Shaheed Sheikh Jan served the cause of national liberation through the BLF on several fronts. He played a significant role in inflicting heavy losses on the enemy in key battles in Jhao, Awaran, Kolwah, Keelkore, and Ormara.
Due to his commitment to the national struggle and his contributions, the martyr’s family was continuously subjected to oppression by the Pakistani army. As part of this persecution, Shaheed Sheikh’s brother was forcibly disappeared in an attempt to pressure him into abandoning his stance. Yet he remained steadfast, making it clear to the enemy that the enslavement of the Baloch nation is a plague, and that every son of the Baloch nation will sacrifice even his life to continue the struggle for freedom.

Kaleem Baloch was a resident of Mastung district. He received his primary education in his home district and soon after joined the Baloch Students Organization, becoming a member of the BSO Azad Mastung Zone. He was a sincere and dedicated comrade of the organization and stood for the national cause in times of difficulty, at a time when the state launched a crackdown against members of BSO Azad and killed several of its members.
He was threatened by security agencies to leave the organization or face death, but he remained committed and did not abandon his lawful political activism under the banner of the Baloch Students Organization Azad. He had a passion for studying revolutionary literature of oppressed nations around the world.
He was abducted from Satellite Town, Quetta, by Pakistan’s secret agencies on August 25, 2011. His bullet-ridden body was found in Mastung district on September 11, 2011. His body showed severe signs of torture.
He was one of the committed members of the organization who continued his struggle during difficult times. In Baloch history, he is always remembered in golden words.

Naeem Shay, son of Shay Mohammad, 29 year-old, a resident of Tehsil Grisha of district Khuzdar, was shot dead by state-backed death squads in the small town of Grisha area in Nadagi on August 22nd, 2025. 

At the morning of August 22nd, when Naeem with his cousin (Iqbal Hakeem), were going to their relatives home. On their way, they were approached by state-backed death squads and they had been both killed on spot in area of Grisha Nadagi, district Khuzdar. 

On the year of 2022, Naeem was enforcedly detained by Pakistani armed personnel and intelligence agencies along with his father, brother and three other relatives. After few months of captivity, they were all safely released. Yet the fate of Naeem was not changed, and he was tragically martyred by the same state operatives in the town.

Faisal Baloch was born on July 8, 1976, in Quetta. During his schooling, he was a brilliant student. He later became a position holder in his M.A. in History and completed his Master of Philosophy at the University of Balochistan. His articles were regularly published in Daily Asaap, a Balochistan-based newspaper that was later forcibly shut down by Pakistan’s military. He worked at the U.S. Consulate in Karachi and later joined the German NGO Hanns Seidel Foundation (HSF). He was an intellectual who never used social media to impose his opinions on others. Faisal loved discussing and listening to diverse viewpoints within the Baloch political struggle. His political maturity and his efforts to build broader unity became a threat to the Pakistani occupiers of Baloch lands. A Baloch rights activist was killed on the very day the world was celebrating Human Rights Day. Faisal Mengal, a young Baloch intellectual and social activist, was chased and gunned down by Pakistani security forces in broad daylight in Karachi on December 10, 2011.

On 4 March 2026, a statement issued by the spokesperson of the Balochistan Liberation Front, Major Gwahram Baloch, stated that on 3 February 2026, fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front launched a coordinated operation at four different locations in Hoshap against Pakistani forces. In this organized operation, various BLF units simultaneously targeted the enemy army at four different locations in Hoshap.
In the initial phase of the operation, one unit of fighters surrounded the police station located in Hoshap Bazaar and took control of the station, holding the personnel hostage. While this unit was seizing government weapons, ammunition, and other equipment, an enemy military convoy consisting of four vehicles approached the area, resulting in an intense face-to-face clash between BLF fighters and enemy forces. During the clash, the fighters targeted and destroyed two enemy vehicles, killing several Pakistani military personnel on board.
Meanwhile, a second unit of fighters positioned at another location attacked two armored enemy vehicles with heavy weapons. Several military personnel were killed or wounded in the clash. Witnessing the defeat and retreat of their ground forces, the enemy resorted to gunship helicopters and advanced drone technology to halt the BLF fighters’ advance.
In this prolonged clash, seven BLF fighters - Shaneed Baloch (alias Shohaz Baloch), Zabad Baloch (alias Deedag), Atta Baloch (alias Obaid), Ghaffar Baloch (alias Noroz), Abdul Samad Baloch (alias Muheem Jan), Zaheer Baloch (alias Istaal), and Nadeem (alias Sahil) - fought valiantly until their last bullet and last breath and embraced martyrdom while courageously defending their motherland.
Ghaffar Baloch, alias Noroz Son of Aziz, resident of Jatt Kolwah, joined the armed struggle under the BLF platform in 2023 and quickly established himself as a brave and hardworking fighter. In the battle of Hoshap, he carried out the difficult responsibility of carrying rocket launcher attacks, striking devastating blows against the enemy from various positions. His combat skills and love for the homeland are testified by his martyrdom.

Lateef Baloch, son of Jan Mohammad, was a resident of Mastung district, Balochistan. He was a student and a member of BSO Azad. He received his early education in his hometown, Mastung. He mobilized hundreds of youths to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of the Baloch homeland.
Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by security forces. He was threatened by Pakistani agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he remained with the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom. He was an example of bravery and commitment. He joined the organization at an early age and stood by his national ideology until the end.
He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising peaceful political expression. He was abducted on 11 August 2011 from Mastung, Balochistan, by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agencies. His bullet-riddled body was found on 18 August 2011 in Dasht, Mastung district, Balochistan. His body showed extreme signs of torture.
He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a young age will be remembered in the golden chapters of Baloch history.

On 21 December 2010, journalist, human rights defender, and member of the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) Siddique Eido, along with Yousuf Nazar, a member of the Baloch Student Organisation (Azad) (BSO-Azad), went to the District and Sessions Court of Gwadar, a port city in Balochistan. They were returning home to the sub-district of Pasni under the security of five policemen, including one Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) and four police constables.
As they reached the Frontier Corps (FC) check post in the Karwat area on the coastal highway, they were stopped by the officials of the Pakistani Frontier Corps. Siddique Eido and Yousuf Nazar were dragged into a van. The accompanying policemen tried to protect them but were severely beaten by the Frontier Corps and held in custody for several hours. Meanwhile, Siddique Eido and Yousuf Nazar were forcibly disappeared.
On 28 April 2011, the bodies of Siddique Eido and Yousuf Nazar were found in Ormara, Balochistan. Both showed visible signs of torture, and both men had been shot in the head. Their families have continued to receive threats not to pursue the cases.
After Naeem Sabir, who was killed on 1 March 2011, Siddique Eido became the second member of the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) to be killed in 2011.

Imran Taj, son of Mohammad Taj, aged 26, from Sarikallag, Gowarkop, was a bright student at the University of Turbat, enrolled in the IBLC department. On June 27, 2025, after his classes, he was traveling from the university to his home in Mohledy Reik, Absar. At around 2:30 PM, he was forcibly taken from the road by ISI and FC personnel.
After nine months of enforced disappearance, on February 27, 2026, his body was found in Kech Kour, (Kech River) Turbat, bearing clear signs of torture. This tragic loss has left a deep void in his family and the entire Baloch Nation.

Fida Baloch, son of Arz Mohammad, was a resident of Mandeel, Mashkai, District Awaran, Balochistan. He received his early education in his hometown of Mashkai and was a student of Engineering at the University of Information Technology, Quetta. He was also a member of BSO Azad, Shaal Zone. He was one of the best friends of Qambar Chakar.
He mobilized hundreds of youths to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of the Baloch homeland. Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by the security forces. He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and BSO Azad, but he remained with the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom.
He had a keen interest in reading revolutionary literature about oppressed nations. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising peaceful political expression.
He was abducted on 23 March 2014 from Quetta by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agencies. His bullet-riddled body was found on 19 October 2015 in Gajjar, Mashkai, District Awaran, Balochistan.
His sacrifices in the liberation movement and struggle for the freedom of the Baloch homeland will always be remembered in golden words in the history of Balochistan.

Kareem Jan, son of Azeem and a resident of Mashkay, Awaran, was extrajudicially killed while in the custody of Pakistani forces. On February 22, 2025, he was summoned by personnel of the Frontier Corps (FC) and the Pakistan Army to a local military headquarters. He was subsequently forcibly disappeared. For five months, his whereabouts remained unknown to his family.
On July 12, 2025, military officials notified his relatives that Kareem Jan had died in custody and instructed them to collect his body from the camp. His remains bore clear signs of severe torture, indicating he had been subjected to months of inhumane treatment.
This was not the first time Kareem Jan had been targeted. In 2023, he was previously disappeared and held incommunicado for eight months before being released—physically weakened and bearing visible signs of brutal torture.

On 26 April 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said that fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army carried out twenty-seven operations across Balochistan between 15 April and 25 April. These operations included IED blasts, drone strikes, and ambushes targeting the Pakistani military. In these attacks, 42 personnel of the forces were killed and numerous others were injured, while one soldier was taken into custody alive. BLA fighters seized control of multiple security posts and confiscated weapons. During clashes at various locations, Sangat Shah Karam Mullazai (alias Sachan), Asim Shahwani (alias Rodain), and Gwahram Baloch (alias Qambar) embraced martyrdom.
Mohammad Asim Shahwani, alias Rodain, son of Khadim Hussain Shahwani, was a resident of Killi Hasni, Tera Mil, in the Dasht area of Mastung District, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in April 2025 as an urban guerrilla, serving on the Quetta front. In November 2025, he moved to the mountain front and continued his service on the Quetta and Mastung fronts. He was martyred on 19 April 2026 in Kambela, Dasht, Mastung.
Mohammad Asim Shahwani, alias Rodain, who attained martyrdom during a battle with enemy forces in Mastung, was a Sarmachar of the Baloch Liberation Army. He was well-versed in modern warfare concepts and applied them effectively in practice. During Operation Herof, he stood firm on the front lines against the enemy, inflicting significant losses. He adhered to a school of thought that prioritized frontline engagement, confronting the enemy directly during the most intense phases of conflict.
For seven months, he remained active on the urban front, participating in key operations against the enemy. After fulfilling his responsibilities there, he was assigned to the mountain front, where he made the mountains his base. On the Mastung front, he played a significant role in the organization’s recent advances across key routes and urban areas.
He was a fighter marked by courage and determination, willing to go to any extent to achieve his military objectives. Refusing to live under subjugation, he continued his journey guided by a collective vision of resistance aimed at achieving lasting freedom and prosperity. With this conviction, he secured a permanent place in Baloch history - one that will continue to be remembered by future generations of such brave inheritors.

On 11 May 2011, on the bank of the Rakhshan River at Damb, Panjgur, some labourers spotted a body in a shallow ditch. When the residents of the area searched, they found two more mutilated bodies. They were later identified by their relatives as Agha Abid Shah, Abdul Sattar Baloch, and Safeer Baloch.
Abdul Sattar Baloch was born on 15 December 1968 to Sufi Dad Mohammed at Diz Paroom, Panjgur. He completed his master’s in Balochi literature from Balochistan University and later took up teaching as his profession.
Agha Abid Shah, Abdul Sattar Baloch, and Safeer Baloch were abducted by state agencies on 15 August 2010 from the vicinity of the District Headquarters Hospital, Panjgur. Panjgur erupted in protest; for a week, the entire district was shut down, and both male and female protesters besieged the office of the Deputy Commissioner to oppose this travesty of justice and the enforced disappearance of these three Baloch political workers. The Frontier Corps (FC) used excessive force to crush the protest and, on 17 August 2010, fired upon the protesters, killing one protester, Hussain Baloch.

Naseem Qadir Baksh, son of Qadir Baksh and a resident of the Hoshab Parkotag area of Turbat district, Balochistan, came from a poor household and worked locally, often using his father’s motorcycle to earn a living. On the night of 8 November 2025, death-squad operatives forcibly abducted him from his home. He was subsequently killed with extreme brutality, and parts of his body were mutilated or removed. His family reported hearing gunfire that night but were unaware at the time that their loved one had been killed.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Faheem Mengal, alias Cobra, son of retired Subedar Mohammad Bakhsh Mengal, was a resident of Zor Abad, Noshki District, Balochistan. He joined the BLA on June 11, 2025, and was martyred on the Noshki front during Operation Herof Phase 2.
Faheem Mengal, who earned the distinctive identity of “Cobra” within the guerrilla ranks, was a metaphor for Noshki’s rugged horizon—one who chose resistance as his way of life over compromise. Cobra’s combat skills and the swiftness of his strikes were a true reflection of his name; he was known for his expertise in approaching a target silently and delivering a decisive blow. During Operation Herof, when the scent of gunpowder permeated every corner of Balochistan, Faheem Mengal stood like a wall against the enemy’s advance on the Noshki front, his ancestral land. Paying the debt of his soil with his blood, he fought until his final breath and embraced martyrdom.

On 22 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch stated that BLF fighters had formally launched Operation Almas with a large-scale, coordinated attack on the main camp of the Pakistani army’s Frontier Works Organization (FWO) at Gwadar Zero Point. Fighters from the BLF’s special Saddo Operational Battalion, alongside members of other units, are participating in this major military engagement. The battle continued into the following day, 23 October 2026, with loud explosions and intense gunfire heard from the location. On 23 October 2026, a statement issued by the BLF spokesperson announced the completion of Operation Almas. The statement claimed that dozens of military and intelligence personnel had been killed, the hub of colonial projects had been destroyed, and army and Frontier Corps posts had been wiped out. It declared that the historic Operation Almas had concluded after achieving all its intended objectives. Operation Almas was carried out in Gwadar and the surrounding areas. It has formally concluded after reportedly achieving all its planned strategic, military, and economic objectives following prolonged and intense clashes. During this wide-ranging operation, the occupying Pakistani army and intelligence network suffered what the statement described as irreparable human and material losses. The BLF’s self-sacrificing fighters targeted the Frontier Works Organization’s (FWO) main camp, destroying a key centre for the implementation of colonial projects, particularly in Gwadar and across Makuran. This, the statement asserted, demonstrated to the world that, without the will and consent of the Baloch nation, colonial projects in Balochistan would never be safe. The offices and camps of Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) and Military Intelligence (MI) inside the FWO’s main camp were also targeted by the organisation’s fighters. Several soldiers, including senior officers, were reportedly killed in the attacks. Throughout Operation Almas, the Jind-Nadr Sarmachars not only thwarted every counterattack by the occupying army, every attempt by armoured vehicles to advance, and every reinforcement convoy, but also forced them to retreat, maintaining control of the camp for twenty hours. As a result of the actions of the Saddo Operational Battalion’s fighters during Operation Almas, Military Intelligence (MI) officers, Special Services Group (SSG) personnel, and dozens of regular army personnel were reportedly killed. In addition, the enemy’s main camp, posts, internal barracks, and administrative offices were reportedly destroyed in explosions and attacks. A number of the occupying army’s armoured vehicles, along with surveillance drones and quadcopters, were also reportedly destroyed during the operation. After repeatedly inflicting defeats on the occupying enemy during Operation Almas, the Jind-Nadr Sarmachars of the Saddo Operational Battalion, adhering to the philosophy of the last bullet, sacrificed their lives in the struggle for freedom, adding a new chapter of bravery to Baloch national history. The following Jind-Nadr Sarmachars played key roles in the operation: Khalid, alias Zamur; Bilqees Didag, alias Almas; Hamidullah, alias Badil; Shakeel, alias Sohrab; Majeed Zaib, alias Aftab; Nasir Ali, alias Nodan; Mujahid Mehr, alias Sagar Zamurani; and Barat, alias Safar Jan. All eight were reported to have embraced martyrdom during this historic operation. On 27 October 2026, the spokesperson issued another detailed statement, announcing that BLF special units had carried out a comprehensive, coordinated, organized, and effective attack on the centres of the occupying Pakistani army, the colonial intelligence network, and exploitative institutions in Gwadar. The statement claimed that more than 80 military and intelligence personnel had been killed; several armoured vehicles, the main army barracks, and intelligence offices had been destroyed; four quadcopters and two surveillance drones had been shot down; and a police station had been seized. It also reported that operations had been conducted at Gabd and Rimdan 250. Following these deadly blows to the state's exploitative structures, Operation Almas was declared successfully concluded. The spokesperson stated that the BLF was formally presenting to the nation, subjugated peoples, and the international community a comprehensive account of the far-reaching military and political achievements of Operation Almas. The historic, organized, effective, coordinated, and comprehensive operation was launched at 4:00 p.m. on 22 October 2026 against the occupying Pakistani state apparatus in Gwadar and the adjoining coastal region. The operation was described as the most organized, coordinated, and far-reaching attack to date against the occupying Pakistani state, its usurping army, intelligence network, exploitative economic institutions, and local puppet administration. It was presented as an expression of the organization's resolve and capabilities. The revolutionary participation of fearless Baloch women, standing shoulder to shoulder with men in the struggle for Baloch national freedom, national survival, and the defence of the coast and its resources, was portrayed as heralding the end of the usurping colonizer. This historic operation was named after the BLF's fearless and courageous guerrilla commander, Almas Baloch. For the past eight years, Commander Almas had been actively involved in the armed national struggle under the BLF banner, driven by her ideological convictions. Bilqees Didag, alias Almas, daughter of Allah Bakhsh Didag, resident of Dasht Kumbel, is a shining chapter of courage, steadfastness and revolutionary sacrifice. She spent her early life in ordinary circumstances and received regular education up to the eighth grade. She was married and has a beloved daughter, but rising above herself and her family circle, she made the cause of the motherland's freedom her whole life. In 2018 she formally joined the armed struggle for national freedom through BLF's revolutionary platform. After joining the organization, she served for four years as a volunteer in the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB), rendering highly valuable and arduous service. For the past eight years Shaheed Almas had been fully active and ideologically committed in the armed defense struggle through the BLF platform. During her organizational life she served as a very active and fearless member of the intelligence wing in sensitive and difficult areas such as Dasht, Turbat and Gwadar. She kept herself in motion day and night to deliver vital intelligence about the enemy to the organization in time. During military fronts and operations, she always carried out, with courage and steadfastness, the very difficult and dangerous responsibility of delivering supplies, weapons and logistics to the sarmachars across Dasht's harsh and rugged mountain ranges. On the path of her revolutionary struggle, the occupying Pakistani army and operatives of the state's death squads made every effort to obstruct her. The occupying army repeatedly attempted to abduct her, hold her in illegal detention and break her mentally and physically, and on one occasion state personnel subjected her to severe torture that left her badly injured. But this tactic of state oppression, taunting and torture could not shake her steadfastness. She faced every hardship with a smile and always stood firm like a rock on the armed front, keeping the flag of freedom high. Even in these grave conditions under state oppression, the wise and courageous way she carried out organizational responsibilities while hiding in various areas is eloquent proof of her high military insight and ideological maturity. Shaheed Bilqees Didag alias Almas put into practice the idea that on the difficult path of national freedom, all hardships, troubles and sacrifices are acceptable, but national slavery and state domination are not acceptable under any circumstances. To realize this idea, she made the final decision to sacrifice herself for the motherland. Shaheed Almas carried out her duties with great devotion in various military detachments and units of the BLF, and from the time the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB) was founded she was its active founder and core member.

Martyr Talib Baloch Alias Kamanchar Baloch, son of Yaseen Baloch and was a resident of Maheer, Mand area of Kech. He became part of the Baloch liberation movement in platform of Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in 2008. He was at rank of Lieutenant for years.
He embraced martyrdom in a drone attack of Pakistan’s military along with his seven comrades, Kareem Baloch, Mullah Bakhsh, Hazza Baloch, Asif Baloch, Shezad Baloch, Jalal Baloch, and Manzoor Baloch on Feb 23, 2023 in Mazanband area of Kech, Balochistan.

On 13th February 2009 Jalil Ahmed Reki, the Central Information Secretary of the Balochistan Republican Party (BRP) & S/O Abdul Qadeer Baloch (Vice Chairman, VBMP), was abducted by Pakistani forces in the presence of several witnesses from Saryab Road, Quetta, while he was walking home from Friday prayers. 

Meanwhile, Mohammad Younis Baloch, a central leader of the Baloch National Movement (BNM) & S/O Faqir Mohammad from Panjgur, was arrested by Iranian intelligence agencies from Sarawan on 22 May 2011. He was later handed over to Pakistani authorities on 16th August 2011.

Their bullet-riddled bodies were found on 22 November 2011 in Mand near the Sheraz mountains. A gun & an abandoned motorcycle had been placed near their bodies by their executioners. They were identified by their relatives on 23rd November 2011 when the bodies were shifted to Turbat Civil Hospital.

In a statement issued by Jeeyand Baloch, the spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), it was said that on Friday night, June 6, 2025, the occupying Pakistani forces advanced in the Splinji, Maru and Phull areas of Mastung. As a result, clashes broke out between the Baloch Liberation Army fighters and the occupying forces. The clashes continued until morning, during which at least seven enemy personnel were killed and several others injured, while two of our fighters, Zafran alias Khalil and Sana alias Angle, were martyred.
Zafran alias Khalil, son of Ismail SUmalani, belonged to Pir Ismail Marwar in the Bolan region. He had been part of the national liberation struggle since 2014 and, as a member of the Baloch Liberation Army, remained active on the frontlines against the enemy. On the Negaho front, he took part in numerous battles, defeated the enemy, and ultimately embraced martyrdom there as a commander. Martyr Zafran was a symbol of unwavering struggle, perseverance, revolutionary discipline and sincerity. For eleven years, in all seasons and all circumstances, he stood against the enemy and rendered unforgettable services.
Sana alias Angle, son of Inayatullah Satakzai, belonged to the Phull Maru area of Splinji. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army one year ago and, in a short time, proved through his dedication, revolutionary discipline, and spirit that courage and sacrifice are not dependent on age. He fulfilled his responsibilities on the Nagaho front with commitment and attained the honored status of martyrdom.

On 29 November 2022, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 26 November 2022, at 6:00 am, the Pakistani army fired hundreds of missiles from Iranian kamikaze drones in and around the Siakoh area of Kahan, Kohlu district of Balochistan. Out of these, two missiles fell within the premises of a BLA camp located in Siakoh. As a result, eight freedom fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army embraced martyrdom.
Afterward, the enemy launched a large scale ground and air operation in Kahan and adjoining areas. The spokesperson stated that for a long time Pakistan and Iran have maintained joint military cooperation against the Baloch national cause, including intelligence coordination. They also exchange advanced and lethal weapons.
In the first phase of the operation, following the drone attacks, several special forces commandos were dropped from around a dozen Pakistan Army combat helicopters, and shelling began from the air. Subsequently, military troops from Kohlu, Dera Bugti, and nearby areas - consisting of more than 400 personnel - participated in the operation using several armored and other military vehicles.
As soon as the Pakistani army initiated the operation, nearby BLA camps in the area began countering the enemy’s advance from different fronts by adopting a joint defense strategy.
The combat between the enemy forces and the freedom fighters continued intermittently until the evening. As a result, the freedom fighters inflicted heavy casualties on the Pakistani forces from all sides. Breaking the army’s land and air siege through skilled combat tactics, they carried their injured comrades, along with weapons and other sensitive equipment, to safe locations.
During the conflict, after several hours of fierce resistance by the fighters, the army turned its guns toward the local population in Nissau, Siakoh, Drehis, Parhki, Jantali, and adjoining areas. The enemy set fire to many houses and severely tortured residents. Meanwhile, troops stopped two innocent Baloch pedestrians and killed them.
The organization’s fighters who embraced martyrdom were - Gahmar Khan alias Garra, Thal Khan alias Thallu, Hameed Baloch alias Sado
Shadi Khan alias Kooda, Abu Bakr Baloch alias Rehan, Jameel alias Naadi
Kareem Khan alias Jamal, Muhammad Nusrat alias Asif - The organization also rejected reports claiming that BLA fighters had been arrested during the operation. Through the media, it challenged ISPR to substantiate its narrative with concrete evidence.
Jameel alias Naadi joined the BLA in 2019 and remained dedicated to national service with utmost hard work and devotion until his last breath. He fought in many battles across different areas of Bolan and Kahan.
Haneef Baloch, was a resident of the Panjgur area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 3 July 2018 in Balochistan.

On 13th April 2026, in the Barkhan area of Balochistan, Pakistani forces shelled and bombed civilian populations, killing twelve innocent Baloch civilians, including women and children, and seriously injuring three others.

The martyrs are:

- Ali, son of Sultan Umair, aged 40
- Babul, daughter of Gulzar, aged 30
- Mir Jan, son of Ali, aged 2
- Somri, daughter of Bhangan, aged 35
- Balach, son of Sabzo, aged 70
- Shari, aged 22
- Rehman, son of Balach, aged 18
- Naikho, daughter of Jamalan, aged 17
- Allah Bakhsh, son of Balach, aged 6
- Saddo, daughter of Balach, aged 13
- Hapo, daughter of Balach, aged 8
- Mahrang, daughter of Balach, aged 2

The injured are:

- Zarbibi, daughter of Sher, aged 55
- Hazar Khan, son of Balach, aged 9
- Israr, daughter of Balach, aged 15

This is not the first time that Pakistani forces have bombed civilians in Balochistan, targeting unarmed and innocent women and children as a form of collective punishment. Nor can this be considered “collateral damage.” Rather, the Pakistani state and its forces are deliberately targeting the Baloch people to maintain an atmosphere of fear in the region, suppress internal dissent, exploit Baloch coastal resources, and continue policies of genocide against the Baloch nation.

Mujahid, son of Khair Jan and a resident of Kharan, was fatally shot by members of state-backed death squad in a crowded market area of Kharan on July 17, 2025. He sustained critical gunshot wounds during the daylight attack and was immediately shifted to Sheikh Zayed Hospital in Kharan, where he later succumbed to his injuries.
Eyewitnesses confirm that the assailants, affiliated with death squads operated and sponsored by the Pakistani forces, opened fire on Mujahid.

On March 8, 2023, Pakistani drones fired three missiles at a Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) guerrilla camp in the mountain range between Hoshap and Pasni. Following the strike, Pakistani forces began landing commandos around the camp from helicopters. In the missile attack, the camp commander, Hasil Baloch, along with four other fighters, was martyred. The remaining Sarmachars fought bravely in close combat, killing several commandos of the occupying forces before they themselves were martyred in the great cause of freedom for their homeland.
The Sarmachars who were martyred are:
Hasil (alias Doda), Wasdil (alias Jami), Nizam (alias Noshad), Waqas (alias Miras), Khalid (alias Kiyya), Shah Fahad (alias Aslam), and Ilyas Baloch (alias Rahmdil).
Martyr Nizam (alias Noshad), son of Pir Bakhsh and resident of Shapak, joined the armed struggle in 2018. Shaheed Nizam was a true son of Balochistan and an extremely dedicated comrade. He took part in several operations against the enemy in Panjgur, Kech, and Pasni.
Zakariya Baloch, was a resident of the Anjira, Khuzdar area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 15 January 2011 in Balochistan.

On 11 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch announced the martyrdom of 14 fighters of the organization who attained martyrdom in confrontations with the Pakistani army and in airstrikes while defending their homeland, Balochistan, and fighting for national liberation and the right to self-determination.

On 13 August 2026, Pakistani Air Force fighter jets bombarded the Pandran area of Kalat District in Balochistan, resulting in the martyrdom of four members of the organization: Waseem Baloch, alias Farhan; Obaidullah Baloch, alias Shaheen; Nawaz Ali Baloch, alias Dilshad; and Mohammad Hassan, alias Ahmad.

On 25 August 2026, during an organizational mission in the Kech area of Balochistan, Sher Jan, alias Jamal, was shot from behind by a traitor, resulting in his martyrdom.

On 3 September 2026, while patrolling in the Mastung area of Balochistan, the organization’s brave fighters, Mohammad Younis, alias Salal; Sameer Ahmad, alias Zemal; Aziz Ahmad, alias Janan; and Sikandar Baloch, confronted Pakistani forces, targeted several enemy personnel, and embraced martyrdom.

On 14 September 2026, while engaging Pakistani forces and defending his fellow fighters in the Machani Kor Paroom area of Panjgur District, Babar Baloch, alias Kambar, embraced martyrdom.

On 18 September 2026, during a confrontation with Pakistani forces in the Chagi area of Balochistan, fighters of the organization, Riaz Baloch, alias Sabir; Taimoor Shah, alias Shaheen; Zia Ul Haq, alias Ziaullah; and Jumma Baloch, alias Commando, embraced martyrdom.

Riaz Baloch, alias Sabir, son of Ghulam Nabi, resident of Manguchar, Kalat, joined the BLF in 2026. After performing national duties on the harsh fronts of Chagi, on 18 September 2026 at Aminabad he resisted the enemy's advance and, along with other fighters, attained martyrdom.

Abdul Sattar, son of Khalid, a resident of Dasht Sholeeg, district Gwadar, a young photographer and intermediate student, was enforcedly disappeared by Pakistani forces on November 12, 2024.

Following his enforced disappearance, his family held a press conference demanding his safe release and highlighting his abduction, yet their calls went unanswered.

On September 19, 2025, Pakistani forces killed him in a fake encounter. His body bore clear signs of severe physical torture followed by bullet wounds. His remains, along with three other Baloch victims, were transferred to Civil Hospital Turbat by FC personnel.

Operation Dara-e-Bolan, which began on 29 January 2024 continued for two days until 31 January 2024 and was successfully concluded after achieving its intended objectives. A total of 385 Sarmachars from four different units of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) participated in Operation Dara-e-Bolan. Among them were 12 Fidayeen from the BLA’s Majeed Brigade. The other participating units included the Fateh Squad, the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS) and the Intelligence Wing.
Operation Dara-e-Bolan commenced on the evening of 29 January 2024 at 9:00 pm local time and continued for two days. After achieving the desired results, the BLA’s Senior Command Council announced the conclusion of Operation Dara-e-Bolan on 31 January 2024 at 7:00 pm and issued instructions to all units to vacate their positions and report back to their base camps.
During the operation, BLA Sarmachars took complete control of an area within a 70 kilometre radius, including Mach city and the strategically important National Highway N-65. Over the course of Operation Dara-e-Bolan, a total of 78 enemy personnel were killed. These included 45 Frontier Corps (FC) personnel who were killed within the first three hours of the operation in Mach city; 10 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on an army camp at the Pir Ghaib Bolan location; 4 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on a military convoy at the Gokurt Mach location; 12 regular army personnel who were killed on 30 January when Majeed Brigade Fidayeen eliminated them and entered the FC headquarters; and at least 5 SSG commandos who were targeted and killed by the Fidayeen on 31 January 2024. In addition, two police personnel were also killed, including one Station House Officer (SHO).
A large number of Levies and police personnel were captured by the BLA during the operation; however, as they were Baloch, they were released. During Operation Dara-e-Bolan, 13 brave fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army attained martyrdom. Of these, 12 martyred Sarmachars belonged to the Majeed Brigade Fidayeen, while one martyred Sarmachar was from the BLA’s Fateh Squad.
The martyred Sarmachars were: Qasim Baloch, Saddam Hussain, Salal Baloch, Farooq Baloch, Atta Baloch, Hammal Momin, Zeeshan Zehri, Nadir Bangulzai, Nizam Baloch, Zeeshan Baloch, Jamal Baloch, Wadood Satakzai, and Kashif Shahwani.
Zeeshan Rind, alias Aftab, son of Habibullah Rind, belonged to Nawabshah, Sindh. Despite residing in Sindh, he was deeply aware of the suffering of the Baloch people and Balochistan. Recognizing his national responsibilities, he decided to join the armed struggle one and a half years prior and became part of the BLA. Six months later, he offered his services to the BLA Majeed Brigade and played a key role in the successful execution of Operation Dara-e-Bolan, ultimately sacrificing his life for the homeland. He succeeded in killing more than ten enemy soldiers single handedly.

On 3 November 2024, Pakistan's Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) extrajudicially killed three Baloch - Mohammad Nawaz Buzdar, Ghulam Buzdar, and Jaffar Marri - in a staged encounter in the Rarasham area of Musakhel District. All three had previously been abducted and forcibly disappeared by the so called Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) of the Pakistani genocidal forces from Rarasham.

Mohammad Nawaz Buzdar, a resident of Rarasham Barg Posht, was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 10 September 2024, from Rarasham, Musakhel District.

Ghulam Buzdar, a resident of Rarasham, was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 21 September 2024, from Rarasham, Musakhel District.

Jaffar Marri was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 2 October 2024, from Rarasham, Musakhel District.

Sajid Baloch, alias Kaka Rahmat, son of Abdullah, a resident of Gomazi, embraced martyrdom for the national cause. On the organizational front, on December 1, 2025, Shaheed Sajid Baloch was bitten by venomous insects and succumbed to his injuries. The BLF pays homage to him for his invaluable services to the Baloch nation.
Shaheed Sajid Baloch joined the national liberation struggle and became affiliated with the BLF in 2013. He remained active on the urban front for one year before moving to the mountain camps in 2014. He carried out organizational responsibilities with exemplary hard work, dedication, and perseverance, and played major roles on several important fronts.
Alongside his comrades, Shaheed Sajid Baloch participated in successful battles on various war fronts. He took part in organizational activities in several areas, including Tump, Mand, Turbat, Gwadar, Zamuran, and Dasht. In his circles, he was known as “Tik Teer” (Perfect Shooter) due to his outstanding combat skills and capabilities.

On July 10, 2025, in a statement issued by Jeeyand Baloch, spokesman for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), it was announced that BLA fighters had successfully attacked the main camp of the occupying Pakistani army in the Gadar area of Surab, gaining full control over two sections of the camp. During the operation, the fighters also shot down an enemy quadcopter. Reinforcing convoys sent by the army were heavily targeted and ambushed.
In total, 18 Pakistani military personnel were killed. During the clashes, one fighter from the BLA’s elite Fateh Squad, Haroon Baloch alias Dostain, was martyred.
The attack began around 11 a.m. when BLA fighters assaulted the Pakistani army’s main camp in Gadar, Surab, from two directions. After more than an hour of intense fighting, the fighters succeeded in capturing two sections of the camp. While attempting to seize the third section, fighter Haroon Baloch alias Dostain embraced martyrdom.
Martyr Haroon Baloch alias Dostain, son of Ali Bakhsh Balghani, hailed from the Kishangi Balghani area of Noshki. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2022 and initially participated in urban guerrilla operations. Later, he moved to the mountainous front, where, due to his exceptional military skills, he was inducted into the BLA’s elite Fateh Squad.
Martyr Haroon Baloch led several significant operations on the Kalat (Shor Parod), Noshki, and Kharan fronts.
Haroon Baloch was a childhood friend of martyr Yasin alias Rauf, and both belonged to the same area. Together, they carried the cause of freedom from the towns to the rugged mountains and ultimately attained the highest rank of martyrdom with the same conviction.

Sardil Sherkhan, a resident of Shadi-Kaur in Pasni, was forcibly disappeared by Pakistan’s Military Intelligence (MI) on 22 November 2025. He remained missing for approximately six months, during which his family received no information about his whereabouts and continued to wait for his return.
On 30 May 2026, Sardil’s family received the devastating news that his body had been found dumped in Pasni. After six months of uncertainty and waiting, the family was left to mourn the loss of their loved one, whose life had been taken, while many questions surrounding his disappearance and death remain unanswered.

Miraj Baloch, son of Martyr Rahmat, was born in 1999 in the Karki area of Gajjar, Mashkai. He received his primary education in his birthplace, Karki, and later attended Gajjar Higher Secondary School for further studies. While he was in the 10th grade in 2013, an earthquake struck the entire area, and his school building was destroyed. Subsequently, the Pakistan Army took control of Gajjar and occupied the schools. His family moved to Zung, Mashkai.
Miraj became a member of BSO Azad. His entire family was associated with the freedom movement; his father and elder brother were killed in separate clashes with Pakistani forces. He was assassinated on 19 May 2015.

Noor Ahmad Notezai, alias Shaden, son of Abdul Rab Notezai, was a resident of Dalbandin. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Chagi front. He was martyred on 31 August 2026 in the Nokcha area of Chagi District, Balochistan.
Noor Ahmad Notezai, alias Shaden, from Dalbandin, after understanding the national, ideological, political, and conscious program of the Baloch armed resistance, joined the war on the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army this year and became active on the ground in Shor. After graduating from basic military courses and proving himself to be a hardworking, capable, fearless, and brave fighter, he, under command guidance, began practical combat operations against the enemy from the Chagai front. He inflicted severe financial losses on the enemy in accordance with the organizational economic blockade policy enforced in the relevant area and remained active in the region under the organizational program until the very end.
Noor Ahmad Notezai took an active part in various activities, including establishing organizational dominance in the area and conducting armed operations against the enemy. He was a sarmachar who understood the realities and conditions of the battlefield and possessed the ability to strike the enemy hard. In an encounter with the enemy, after killing several enemy personnel along with his comrades, he sacrificed himself for the protection and freedom of his homeland. With his martyrdom, he conveyed the same message that other comrades had already conveyed: the Baloch nation is prepared to go to any lengths against the enemy to secure its homeland’s freedom and the restoration of its state. His sacrifices will be remembered forever in history, and its reward will be an independent Balochistan.

data.biography:
On February 23, 2022 the occupying forces of Pakistan struck the Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) guerrilla camp in the Satak Kor mountain range of Hoshab, district Kech, and fired three chemical-laden missiles that wreaked havoc over a large area, destroying palm groves and other vegetation at the site. Following the drone missile attacks, the infantry team of the occupying forces surrounded the area and, with the support of more than eight state helicopters, entered the camp. Five Sarmachaars, including two commanders of the organization, Master Asif Baloch and Siraj Baloch, were martyred in this attack. Meanwhile, five other Sarmachaars - Shoaib, Munir, Arif Jan, Diljan, Kamal, Kamash Malang, Jangi Khan, and Daolat - were martyred defending their homeland, fighting the enemy for over an hour and killing several commandos of the occupying forces.
Arif Jan, alias Mir Khan, son of Faqir, resident of the Aapsar area of Turbat, joined the armed struggle in 2020. He was a skilled and courageous fighter.

On 1 November 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson, Gwahram Baloch, issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of eight of the organisation’s fighters: Captain Yahya, alias Ustad Khalid Jan; Aris Baloch, alias Omar Jan; Hafeez Baloch, alias Karwan, son of Dad Mohammad; Javid Baloch, alias Gulab, son of Bori Baloch; Abdul Khaliq, alias Nothak; Sajid Baloch, alias Mehran; Hameed Baloch, alias Buzerg; and Akram Baloch, alias Gwahram.

The statement paid tribute to these brave and ideologically committed members of the organisation, who embraced martyrdom while engaging in clashes with the Pakistani army and its death squads on various fronts across Balochistan.

Captain Yahya Baloch, alias Ustad Khalid Jan. From a young age, Captain Yahya began taking an active part in political gatherings and national activities alongside the Baloch national leader Martyr Dr. Manan Jan. After gaining political awareness and intellectual maturity, he formally joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in 2011. In the early years he worked with the urban network, carrying out organizational duties with great secrecy, courage and skill, and he also took command of covert organizational operations in the cities.

Yahya Baloch was a sarmachar of strict organizational discipline, ideological conviction, immense endurance and hard work. He was an expert instructor in explosives, mining and heavy weapons. To bring Baloch guerrilla warfare in line with the demands of the modern era, he constantly introduced new military techniques and made full use of them in operations. Whenever and wherever the organization needed him, he took part in organizational activities from the front ranks.

On organizational instruction he left for the Kharan front in 2015, and played a key role in several successful engagements against the enemy in Kharan, Shor, Nushki, Khuzdar and Kalat. In the same year, 2015, his elder brother, Shaheed Hafiz Sarfaraz Baloch, was abducted from a madrisa in Karachi by the Pakistani army and intelligence agencies as collective punishment. In 2016 he was martyred along with four other abducted Baloch in a staged encounter in Mashkay, and their bodies were dumped. These inhuman and brutal tactics could not shake his resolve. His family background holds a long and illustrious list of martyrs, including Shaheed Nurul Haq, Shaheed Dr. Manan, Shaheed Abdul Rahim son of Ata Muhammad alias Zamindar, Shaheed Sajid Umar and Shaheed Majid Umar. He absorbed all these shocks and pains and continued his fight against the enemy like a revolutionary warrior.

Martyr Captain Yahya took part in battles against the enemy on the difficult and rugged fronts across Balochistan, including Mashkay, Awaran, Kolwah, Jhao, Gresha, Naal, Awaran, Khuzdar, Zehri, Zamuran, Buleida, Kharan, Shor, Nushki, Rakhshan, Washuk, Surab and Kalat. He also played a key and courageous role in the BLF's historic Naal city operation. Among friends he was always cheerful, kind and gentle. In any engagement that needed heavy weapons, he carried them on his own shoulders and attacked the enemy from the front line.

On 7 October 2026, fighting the enemy in Gidar, Surab, in his last battle as a captain, he kept up this tradition, personally taking charge of the 82 mm rocket launcher and heavy weapons and attacking the enemy. During the battle, an accidental explosion of an 82 mm rocket shell martyred him.
