On 22 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch stated that BLF fighters had formally launched Operation Almas with a large-scale, coordinated attack on the main camp of the Pakistani army’s Frontier Works Organization (FWO) at Gwadar Zero Point. Fighters from the BLF’s special Saddo Operational Battalion, alongside members of other units, are participating in this major military engagement. The battle continued into the following day, 23 October 2026, with loud explosions and intense gunfire heard from the location.

On 23 October 2026, a statement issued by the BLF spokesperson announced the completion of Operation Almas. The statement claimed that dozens of military and intelligence personnel had been killed, the hub of colonial projects had been destroyed, and army and Frontier Corps posts had been wiped out. It declared that the historic Operation Almas had concluded after achieving all its intended objectives.

Operation Almas was carried out in Gwadar and the surrounding areas. It has formally concluded after reportedly achieving all its planned strategic, military, and economic objectives following prolonged and intense clashes. During this wide-ranging operation, the occupying Pakistani army and intelligence network suffered what the statement described as irreparable human and material losses.

The BLF’s self-sacrificing fighters targeted the Frontier Works Organization’s (FWO) main camp, destroying a key centre for the implementation of colonial projects, particularly in Gwadar and across Makuran. This, the statement asserted, demonstrated to the world that, without the will and consent of the Baloch nation, colonial projects in Balochistan would never be safe.

The offices and camps of Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) and Military Intelligence (MI) inside the FWO’s main camp were also targeted by the organisation’s fighters. Several soldiers, including senior officers, were reportedly killed in the attacks. Throughout Operation Almas, the Jind-Nadr Sarmachars not only thwarted every counterattack by the occupying army, every attempt by armoured vehicles to advance, and every reinforcement convoy, but also forced them to retreat, maintaining control of the camp for twenty hours.

As a result of the actions of the Saddo Operational Battalion’s fighters during Operation Almas, Military Intelligence (MI) officers, Special Services Group (SSG) personnel, and dozens of regular army personnel were reportedly killed. In addition, the enemy’s main camp, posts, internal barracks, and administrative offices were reportedly destroyed in explosions and attacks. A number of the occupying army’s armoured vehicles, along with surveillance drones and quadcopters, were also reportedly destroyed during the operation.

After repeatedly inflicting defeats on the occupying enemy during Operation Almas, the Jind-Nadr Sarmachars of the Saddo Operational Battalion, adhering to the philosophy of the last bullet, sacrificed their lives in the struggle for freedom, adding a new chapter of bravery to Baloch national history.

The following Jind-Nadr Sarmachars played key roles in the operation: Khalid, alias Zamur; Bilqees Didag, alias Almas; Hamidullah, alias Badil; Shakeel, alias Sohrab; Majeed Zaib, alias Aftab; Nasir Ali, alias Nodan; Mujahid Mehr, alias Sagar Zamurani; and Barat, alias Safar Jan. All eight were reported to have embraced martyrdom during this historic operation.

On 27 October 2026, the spokesperson issued another detailed statement, announcing that BLF special units had carried out a comprehensive, coordinated, organized, and effective attack on the centres of the occupying Pakistani army, the colonial intelligence network, and exploitative institutions in Gwadar.

The statement claimed that more than 80 military and intelligence personnel had been killed; several armoured vehicles, the main army barracks, and intelligence offices had been destroyed; four quadcopters and two surveillance drones had been shot down; and a police station had been seized. It also reported that operations had been conducted at Gabd and Rimdan 250. Following these deadly blows to the state's exploitative structures, Operation Almas was declared successfully concluded.

The spokesperson stated that the BLF was formally presenting to the nation, subjugated peoples, and the international community a comprehensive account of the far-reaching military and political achievements of Operation Almas. The historic, organized, effective, coordinated, and comprehensive operation was launched at 4:00 p.m. on 22 October 2026 against the occupying Pakistani state apparatus in Gwadar and the adjoining coastal region.

The operation was described as the most organized, coordinated, and far-reaching attack to date against the occupying Pakistani state, its usurping army, intelligence network, exploitative economic institutions, and local puppet administration. It was presented as an expression of the organization's resolve and capabilities. The revolutionary participation of fearless Baloch women, standing shoulder to shoulder with men in the struggle for Baloch national freedom, national survival, and the defence of the coast and its resources, was portrayed as heralding the end of the usurping colonizer.

This historic operation was named after the BLF's fearless and courageous guerrilla commander, Almas Baloch. For the past eight years, Commander Almas had been actively involved in the armed national struggle under the BLF banner, driven by her ideological convictions.

Bilqees Didag, alias Almas, daughter of Allah Bakhsh Didag, resident of Dasht Kumbel, is a shining chapter of courage, steadfastness and revolutionary sacrifice. She spent her early life in ordinary circumstances and received regular education up to the eighth grade. She was married and has a beloved daughter, but rising above herself and her family circle, she made the cause of the motherland's freedom her whole life. In 2018 she formally joined the armed struggle for national freedom through BLF's revolutionary platform. After joining the organization, she served for four years as a volunteer in the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB), rendering highly valuable and arduous service.

For the past eight years Shaheed Almas had been fully active and ideologically committed in the armed defense struggle through the BLF platform. During her organizational life she served as a very active and fearless member of the intelligence wing in sensitive and difficult areas such as Dasht, Turbat and Gwadar. She kept herself in motion day and night to deliver vital intelligence about the enemy to the organization in time. During military fronts and operations, she always carried out, with courage and steadfastness, the very difficult and dangerous responsibility of delivering supplies, weapons and logistics to the sarmachars across Dasht's harsh and rugged mountain ranges.

On the path of her revolutionary struggle, the occupying Pakistani army and operatives of the state's death squads made every effort to obstruct her. The occupying army repeatedly attempted to abduct her, hold her in illegal detention and break her mentally and physically, and on one occasion state personnel subjected her to severe torture that left her badly injured. But this tactic of state oppression, taunting and torture could not shake her steadfastness. She faced every hardship with a smile and always stood firm like a rock on the armed front, keeping the flag of freedom high. Even in these grave conditions under state oppression, the wise and courageous way she carried out organizational responsibilities while hiding in various areas is eloquent proof of her high military insight and ideological maturity.

Shaheed Bilqees Didag alias Almas put into practice the idea that on the difficult path of national freedom, all hardships, troubles and sacrifices are acceptable, but national slavery and state domination are not acceptable under any circumstances. To realize this idea, she made the final decision to sacrifice herself for the motherland. Shaheed Almas carried out her duties with great devotion in various military detachments and units of the BLF, and from the time the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB) was founded she was its active founder and core member.

On 11 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch announced the martyrdom of 14 fighters of the organization who attained martyrdom in confrontations with the Pakistani army and in airstrikes while defending their homeland, Balochistan, and fighting for national liberation and the right to self-determination.

On 13 August 2026, Pakistani Air Force fighter jets bombarded the Pandran area of Kalat District in Balochistan, resulting in the martyrdom of four members of the organization: Waseem Baloch, alias Farhan; Obaidullah Baloch, alias Shaheen; Nawaz Ali Baloch, alias Dilshad; and Mohammad Hassan, alias Ahmad.

On 25 August 2026, during an organizational mission in the Kech area of Balochistan, Sher Jan, alias Jamal, was shot from behind by a traitor, resulting in his martyrdom.

On 3 September 2026, while patrolling in the Mastung area of Balochistan, the organization’s brave fighters, Mohammad Younis, alias Salal; Sameer Ahmad, alias Zemal; Aziz Ahmad, alias Janan; and Sikandar Baloch, confronted Pakistani forces, targeted several enemy personnel, and embraced martyrdom.

On 14 September 2026, while engaging Pakistani forces and defending his fellow fighters in the Machani Kor Paroom area of Panjgur District, Babar Baloch, alias Kambar, embraced martyrdom.

On 18 September 2026, during a confrontation with Pakistani forces in the Chagi area of Balochistan, fighters of the organization, Riaz Baloch, alias Sabir; Taimoor Shah, alias Shaheen; Zia Ul Haq, alias Ziaullah; and Jumma Baloch, alias Commando, embraced martyrdom.

Obaidullah Baloch, alias Shaheen, son of Abdullah, resident of Surab, began his formal revolutionary journey through the BLF platform in 2026. After military training, he was moved to the difficult front in Kalat. On the morning of 13 August 2026, during the bombing by enemy jets in Pandran, Kalat, he stood his ground bravely on the field and offered his life for the freedom of the homeland.

Zakir Baloch, son of Abdin, was a 20 year old driver by profession and a resident of Sabzal Bazar, Parom, Panjgur district of Balochistan. He earned his livelihood through driving and was known in the area as a hardworking young man striving to support his family.
Zakir Baloch was killed on March 5, 2026, in the Kaleri area of Parom, Panjgur. Armed men of a death squad operating under the command of Pakistani forces opened fire on him, leaving him critically wounded. He later succumbed to his injuries.
The son of Dosta Mahmood Baloch and Shazia Baloch. He was identified as a young child (reportedly 5 years old) who was martyred during the missile attack in Sistan and Balochistan.

Arafat Ibrahim was a minor and a student, he studied up to Grade 7 at Government High School Mand Soroo & then left for further studies in Quetta, the capital of Balochistan. On his way to Quetta, Pakistan’s secret service officials abducted him & later his bullet riddled body was found in Murghap. On 23 Oct 2011 while travelling from Turbat to Quetta on a passenger bus, seven military and two civilian vehicles stopped the bus near Shadi Kaur. Officials checked passengers’ names, ordered Arafat off the bus, sent the driver away, beat Arafat in front of everyone, blindfolded him & took him to Turbat, on 6 Nov 2011 VSH News reported that two mutilated bodies had been found in Murgaap. The bodies of Arafat Baloch & Karim Jan were taken to Civil Hospital Turbat, where their families identified them. Arafat’s body bore signs of severe torture: cigarette burns, a broken nose, three fingers cut off, a broken hand, & two bullet wounds, one to the head and one to the chest, two weeks later, Pakistani security forces raided Arafat’s home again, harassed his family & broke his gravestone, when the family attempted to file a complaint, the police threatened them with worse consequences.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Mohammad Deen Marri, alias Waheed Marri, son of Qaim Khan Marri, was a resident of Badrah Laki. He joined the BLA in 2023 in Sangan, Sibi, and served in Bolan, Quetta, and Mastung. He was martyred during Operation Herof Phase II on the Mastung front. He was the brother of Fiday Azal, alias Dada, and Martyr Mohammad Hussain, alias Jabal.
Martyr Mohammad Deen Marri was a soldier of the liberation war whose family itself stands as a living symbol of sacrifice and bravery. His two brothers, Fidayi Azal, alias Dada, and Martyr Muhammad Hussain, alias Jabal, had already embraced martyrdom on the path of freedom before him. Thus, three members of the same family sacrificed their lives for the homeland. This great legacy did not weaken his resolve; rather, it strengthened it, and he remained determined to uphold this responsibility until his last breath.
Martyr Mohammad Deen Marri was an expert on the battlefield, intimately familiar with the mountains, and seasoned by harsh conditions. The rugged mountains of Balochistan served as both his refuge and training ground, where he mastered the arts of endurance, patience, and steadfastness. Due to his combat skills, silent maneuvering, and ability to deliver decisive blows to the enemy, he became part of the “Fateh Squad” within a very short period after joining the organization.
He played a pivotal role on the fronts of Bolan, Quetta, and Mastung, fighting on the front lines in every battle. His morale never wavered on the battlefield, and he fought until his final moment, setting a brilliant example of perseverance, courage, and determination.
Martyr Mohammad Deen Marri was present on the Mastung front during “Operation Herof II,” where he embraced martyrdom while fighting on the front line.
data.fullName: Mohammad Deen Marri, alias Waheed Marri

data.biography: Jalil Baloch was a resident of the Nizarabad, Kech area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 16 June 2016 in Balochistan.

On 16 February 2022, the ground forces of the Pakistani state, accompanied by air support, attacked a camp of the Baloch Nationalist Army in the early hours of the morning in the mountainous area of Kulbar, Tump. A prolonged skirmish ensued, beginning at 6:00 AM and continuing until 5:00 PM, during which the Baloch Sarmachars killed several enemy commandos and partially damaged two enemy helicopters.
In this clash, Noor Salam Noor alias Istaal, son of Bahar Baloch and a resident of Dashtuk Zamuran; Zubair Akram alias Asadjan, son of Akram Baloch and a resident of Hotabad Zamuran Bazaar; Kambar Baloch alias Mehrwan, son of Tariq and a resident of Kolaho; Sageer Baloch alias Tariq, son of Noorbakhsh and a resident of Basima; Rasool Jan alias Chirag, son of Ali Jan and a resident of Sarankan; and Hafiz Faraz alias Mullah Darwish, son of Abdul Ghani and a resident of Sarankan, were martyred.

Aziz Baloch, also known as Chakar Baloch, was born to Master Abdullah Baloch and Safia Baloch in the Malikabad area of Tump, Balochistan. He joined the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in 2013. He was both a poet and a warrior. Through his words and poetry, he expressed national aspirations and inspired his nation and comrades. He embraced martyrdom along with his two comrades, Mukhtar Baloch (alias Ustad Noor Baloch) and Sajid Baloch (alias Asumi Baloch), on December 7, 2020, in the Dashtuk area of Zamuran, Kech, Balochistan.

Adeel Baloch, son of Abdul Qayyum and a resident of Kohad, Tump, was taken into custody during a raid in Kohad Bazaar by Pakistani security forces and death squads. Three other young men were detained alongside him and transferred to undisclosed locations.

For three days, Adeel remained missing. On 23 October 2026, his body was recovered from Sernkin, Kech.
Sahib Khan Baloch, was a resident of the Anjira, Khuzdar area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 3 February 2016 in Balochistan.

Saddam Hussain, 28, son of Mehrab Ali, was a mechanic by profession and a resident of Shapuk, an area of Turbat. On 21 July 2025, at approximately 3:00 p.m., he was allegedly abducted by Pakistani security agencies, including the Frontier Corps (FC) and Military Intelligence (MI), from the Singani Sar area of Turbat and subsequently forcibly disappeared.
On 12 June 2026, the body of Saddam Hussain was recovered from the D. Baloch area of Turbat district in Balochistan.

Zubair Zahid, son of Zahid Baloch, was born in 1995 in Pasni. He was a student of FSc at Government Inter College Pasni and a member of BSO Azad Pasni Zone. He received his early education in his native area, Pasni.
He actively led organizational programs and was always engaged in mobilizing youth to become part of the Baloch struggle for an independent homeland. Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by security forces. He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he remained with the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom. He was an example of bravery and commitment.
He joined the organization at an early age and remained committed to his national ideology until the end. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising peaceful political expression.
He was abducted on 08 September 2011 from Zero Point in Gwadar District, Balochistan, by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agencies. His bullet-riddled body was found dumped on 03 October 2011 in Gwadar District, Balochistan. His body showed severe signs of torture.
He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a very young age will be remembered in the golden pages of Baloch history.

Imran Sarparah, alias Asim, son of Mhammad Hussain Sarparah, was a resident of the Sariab area of Quetta, Balochistan. He joined the BLA as an urban guerrilla in December 2024 and moved to the mountain front in January 2026. He served on the Quetta, Nagaho, and Noshki fronts and was killed on 13 September 2026 in the Sultan Shar area of Qila Abdullah, Balochistan.
Imran Sarparah, alias Asim, belonged to Sariab, the heart of Shal. In December 2024, he joined the Baloch Liberation Army as an urban guerrilla. With this decision at a young age, that period of his personal life was left behind in which a young person builds a separate path for his home, his personal desires, and his future. Imran decided to connect his personal life with the concept of a national responsibility. This choice was not merely an ordinary change, but along with it, he also had to give up many of his personal comforts, relationships, and possibilities for the future.
In January 2026, he became associated with the mountain front and later remained in the areas of Quetta, Nagaho, and Nushki. By this stage, his life had moved quite far from its previous direction. The city life in which personal priorities and everyday routines had their own place had now become a memory left behind for him. He devoted a major part of his life to a collective purpose and considered the difficulties and hardships that came along this path to be part of his responsibility.
On September 13, 2026, during a clash in Sultan Shar, Qila Abdullah, Imran Sarparah, alias Asim, attained martyrdom. The final period of his life was a great fulfillment of the decision he had made nearly two years earlier. His journey, which had begun in Sariab, physically came to a stop in Sultan Shar, but the most prominent aspect of his personality remained that, at a young age, he made a collective responsibility his priority instead of his personal life.

On 13th April 2026, in the Barkhan area of Balochistan, Pakistani forces shelled and bombed civilian populations, killing twelve innocent Baloch civilians, including women and children, and seriously injuring three others.

The martyrs are:

- Ali, son of Sultan Umair, aged 40
- Babul, daughter of Gulzar, aged 30
- Mir Jan, son of Ali, aged 2
- Somri, daughter of Bhangan, aged 35
- Balach, son of Sabzo, aged 70
- Shari, aged 22
- Rehman, son of Balach, aged 18
- Naikho, daughter of Jamalan, aged 17
- Allah Bakhsh, son of Balach, aged 6
- Saddo, daughter of Balach, aged 13
- Hapo, daughter of Balach, aged 8
- Mahrang, daughter of Balach, aged 2

The injured are:

- Zarbibi, daughter of Sher, aged 55
- Hazar Khan, son of Balach, aged 9
- Israr, daughter of Balach, aged 15

This is not the first time that Pakistani forces have bombed civilians in Balochistan, targeting unarmed and innocent women and children as a form of collective punishment. Nor can this be considered “collateral damage.” Rather, the Pakistani state and its forces are deliberately targeting the Baloch people to maintain an atmosphere of fear in the region, suppress internal dissent, exploit Baloch coastal resources, and continue policies of genocide against the Baloch nation.

Bibi Mahtab Raisani, the proud mother of Mir Abdul Wadood Raisani, a leader of the Baloch Republican Party (BRP), who was kidnapped by Pakistan’s notorious agencies, took it upon herself, despite her old age, to become his silenced voice. She joined the Voice of Baloch Missing Persons (VOBMP), an organization devoted to raising awareness and taking action on the cases of disappeared Baloch activists abducted by the state of Pakistan. In a very short time, she not only became a leading figure of the organization but also the voice of the entire Baloch nation.
She took it upon herself to bear the sorrows of the families of Baloch missing persons and became their source of courage. She never missed an activity, even the Long March organized to raise the voice of the Baloch people. She urged everyone not to lose hope in their struggle. In a speech in Malir, Karachi, she said, “Balochistan is ours, and it belongs to our children; we will fight until Balochistan is free.”
When Abdul Majeed Junior was martyred in Quetta by the Pakistan army, they refused to return his body to his family for burial. The Baloch people, under her leadership, gathered at the hospital, reclaimed his body, and set off on his final journey to rest in peace in the motherland’s kind lap.
On May 21, 2010, Bibi Mahtab Raisani was traveling with other leaders of VOBMP from Quetta to appear before the judicial commission in Karachi, which had been formed to trace missing persons. Their vehicle was targeted by Pakistan’s agencies in Kalat, 160 km from Quetta. In the blast, both rear tires of the vehicle were flattened, causing it to go out of control and spin four times before crashing violently. The 82-year-old Madar-e-Baloch (mother of the Baloch nation) died at the scene, while other VOBMP leaders were injured. She was buried with the full honor of a martyr at the Baloch Martyrs’ graveyard in Kalat.

Peerjan Baloch, son of Kachkul, was 23 years old and belonged to the Rahi Nigur area of Panjgur. He was a driver by profession and came from a poor family.

At around 3:00 PM on 9 June 2026, the CTD forcibly disappeared Peerjan. For 66 days, his family waited for his release, holding on to the hope that he would return home. Instead, on 10 August 2026, he was killed in a fake encounter in Chedagi, Panjgur.

For 66 days, Peerjan’s family was left without answers. They were never informed of any crime he had allegedly committed. No warrant or FIR was presented to the family before he was taken away. They waited for their son to return home alive, but instead received his dead body.

In 1909, the British government arrested Shakir Khan and his son, Meer Nooruddin. Subsequently, in 1910, Noora Mengal and his tribespeople launched a guerrilla war against the British government. He continued his resistance and did not surrender.
Similarly, in 1917, Meer Shadi Khan Nosherwani was given money by the British government to arrest Noora Mengal Baloch. However, he failed to capture him and instead arrested three of Noora Mengal’s companions.
Furthermore, Noora Mengal continued to fight against the British army. However, during a battle in 1919, he was unable to continue fighting due to a shortage of weapons and ammunition.
Afterward, he moved from Jhalawan to Kharan and sought refuge at the home of Meer Habibullah Nosherwani. He requested Meer Habibullah to provide him with weapons so he could resume his fight against the imperialist regime. Alternatively, he asked for assistance in reaching Afghanistan, where he could obtain weapons.
However, Meer Habibullah Nosherwani betrayed Noora. While promising to supply him with weapons within a few days, he secretly informed the British authorities of Noora’s presence so they could arrest him at his residence. The British arrested Noora and imprisoned him.
Noora Mengal, a brave fighter of the Baloch nation and a defender of his land, died in a British jail on August 30, 1921, in Hyderabad, Sindh.

In 1838, the British sent a force led by Alexander Burnes to reinstate Shah Shuja Durrani as the king of Afghanistan by deposing Amir Dost Mohammad Khan. To reach Afghanistan, they needed passage through Balochistan, particularly the Bolan Pass. However, Khan Mehrab Khan refused to allow the British to use his land to attack a neighboring country. The British sent Lieutenant Leach to negotiate with the Baloch government, but the Khan stood firm. When British forces reached Shaal via Bolan, some patriotic Baloch, without the Khan’s knowledge, attacked British troops out of nationalist sentiment and a desire to protect their homeland.
After toppling Amir Dost Mohammad Khan, the British Governor General of India, Lord Auckland, ordered an attack on Balochistan. In 1839, around 7,000 British troops marched from Shaal to attack the Baloch Meeri (capital). Anticipating an invasion, Khan Mehrab Khan declared war and sent messages to tribal leaders, but many saw the British as allies rather than invaders and chose to collaborate with them rather than defend their land. When Khan Mehrab Khan gathered his resistance fighters, the number of loyal warriors had dwindled to only 700 due to the short sightedness of many tribal chiefs. Nevertheless, Mehrab Khan was determined to fight. At his court, a respected figure, Akhund Muhammad Siddiq, advised him that he was not in a position to wage war at that time. He suggested that the Khan should leave Kalat with his companions, regroup and strengthen his forces, and then launch an attack against the British when the time was right, on 13 November 1839, the British forces launched an attack on Kalat, and a fierce battle ensued. During the fighting, Khan Mehrab Khan Baloch was martyred by a British bullet.

Among those martyred alongside him were:

Diwan Bacha Mal, Minister of Finance

Diwan Khem Chand

Diwan Asardas Mukhi, from the Hindu Panchayat of Kalat

Abdul Karim Raisani, brother of Sardar Asad Khan Raisani

Sardar Wali Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (maternal uncle of Martyr Amir Mehrab Khan)

Mir Taj Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (cousin of Mehrab Khan)

Mir Muhammad Ali Shahizai Mengal

Mir Fazal Muhammad Lehri, brother of Sardar Muhammad Khan Lehri

Sardar Zaman Khan Pandrani

Mir Dad Karim Chandozai Shahwani

Mir Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Mir Badal Khan, brother of Sardar Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Khan Muhammad Dehwaar, Arbab-e-Kalat.

Mir Nabi Bakhsh Jatoi, from the Narmak region of Kalat

Mir Qaiser Khan Bizenjo

Mir Shah Dost Bizenjo

Muhammad Raza Waziri Khel

Noor Muhammad Shahizai, son of Polat Sagaar Sarmastani, in charge of the armory

Taj Muhammad Shagasi
On February 3, 2026, in the Qaziabad area of Nushki district, Balochistan, Pakistani forces brutally shot and killed 60 year old, Babu Atta Mohammad Badini.

Zubair Nawab, son of Nawab, worked as a border labourer.
On 25 September 2026, he went on a picnic with his friends in the Lutham area of Balicha, Tump District. They informed the Pakistani army of their presence at the location. They were subsequently targeted by a rocket fired from a drone operated by Pakistani forces. The attack killed Zubair Nawab and three of his friends: Yasir, son of Mohammad Karim; Sameer Baloch, son of Abdul Khaliq; and Didag Baloch, son of Mohammad Omar. Two other people were also injured in the incident.

Balach Baloch, son of Mola Baksh and Fazila Baloch, was a resident of Absar, Turbat. He was the youngest among his eight siblings.
He completed his matriculation from Absar School and worked at a tailor’s shop in Star Plus Market, Turbat. He was 24 years old.
He was abducted by Pakistani forces on October 29, 2023, from his home in Absar, Turbat, Kech. After twenty-six days, on November 22, 2023, he was killed by the CTD in a fake encounter, along with three others—Saif Baloch, Shakoor, and Wadood Baloch—in Banuk Chadahi, Turbat, Kech, Balochistan.
His sister, Najman Baloch, and other family members, along with prominent figures like Dr. Shalee Baloch and Gulzar Dost, held a seven-day sit-in at Fida Chowk, the main bazaar of Turbat, Kech, to protest fake encounters in Balochistan. On the seventh day, his body was buried in the presence of thousands of people, including women, at Koh-e-Murad, Turbat, on November 29, 2023.
After his burial, the sit-in continued and was reorganized by leaders of the Baloch Yakjehti Committee, including Sabiha Baloch, Sammi Baloch, Seema Baloch, and others. The protest then transformed into a convoy called the historic “March Against Baloch Genocide,” which moved from Turbat to Quetta. Upon arrival in Quetta, Baloch leader Dr. Mahrang Baloch took command. After several days of protest in Quetta, the march convoy continued to Pakistan’s capital, Islamabad, where it made a lasting impact.

On January 12, 2026 Pakistani army carried out a drone attack on a temporary patrol camp of Baloch Liberation Army in the Shurparood area of Kalat, in which four veteran freedom fighters of BLA - Sangat Zohair alias Haq Nawaz, Sangat Manzoor Kurd alias Bakhtiar Cheeta, Sangat Samiullah alias Javed Phalia and Sangat Naseer Ahmed alias Meerak - attained martyrdom.
Zohair alias Haq Nawaz Baloch, son of Mohammad Afzal Faqirzai, belonged to Ahmad Wal area of Noshki. He joined Baloch Liberation Army in 2023 and took over responsibilities as a trainer for a year due to his abilities. Sangat Zohair served on the Mastung, Kalat and Noshki fronts. Zohair was known within the organization for his discipline and military skills. He paid special attention to the ideological training of new fighters.

Zahoor Ahmad Langove, alias Shikari, son of Abdul Majeed Langove, was a resident of the Zehri area of Khuzdar District. He joined the BLA in 2023 and served on the Bolan, Shor, Parod, and Surab fronts. He was martyred on 30 August 2026 in the Jori area of Surab.
Martyr Zahoor Ahmad Langove, who proved to be a scourge to the enemy and was skilled in warfare across various battlefronts of Balochistan, from Bolan to Shor and Parod, and then from Parod to Surab, chose the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army and became part of the caravan of national liberation in 2023. During these three years, he took part in important and historic battles and continued to leave his revolutionary impact wherever he went. He remained committed until his last breath to the cause for which he had chosen armed resistance and sacrificed his life for the greatness and freedom of his homeland.
He was a realist on the battlefield who understood the realities of war and had the ability and skills to adapt to every situation, environment, front, and demand of warfare, which consistently distinguished him among his comrades. He remained active on the battlefield for three years, during which he took part in highly important and historic battles that pushed the enemy back and struck their important defensive positions with such force that these battles will remain part of the enemy’s historical failures, while they will be remembered as great victories in the struggle for the Baloch homeland and freedom. He was highly intelligent in combat, and this combat intelligence proved important in organizational strategy, planning, and pushing the enemy back.
The revolutionary and national services that Martyr Zahoor Langove rendered throughout his life will be remembered as great achievements in the struggle for national liberation. His role in Baloch history will always be remembered as that of a revolutionary who, instead of accepting slavery and focusing on an individual life, adopted the philosophy of sacrifice for his homeland and its freedom. His sacrifices will always remain an example in the Baloch national liberation struggle, as he demonstrated extraordinary courage, bravery, and revolutionary commitment.

Niyamatullah Baloch was a resident of Khuzdar. He was a student and a member of BSO Azad Khuzdar Zone. He received his primary education in his native area, Khuzdar. He mobilized many youths to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of the Baloch homeland.
Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by the security forces. He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he remained with the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom. He was an example of bravery and commitment. He joined the organization at an early age and stood by his national ideology until the end.
He believed in political struggle and was targeted for his peaceful political expression. He was abducted by Pakistan’s secret agencies from Basima, District Washuk, on February 17, 2013. His bullet-riddled body was found in Khuzdar in February 2013. His body bore severe signs of torture.
He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle in difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a young age will be remembered in the history of Balochistan.

On May 3, 2026, United Baloch Army (UBA) spokesperson Mazar Baloch issued a statement confirming that Shadi Gull Marri, alias Propag, had been a member of the armed pro-independence organization for several years. He was active in the Kohistan Marri and Harnai areas, where he performed various duties. According to the statement, he dedicated his entire life to the Baloch independence struggle.
The UBA added that after arresting state informant Durrain Marri, son of Sohbat Khan Marri, they learned that on April 1, 2026, in Harnai, Balochistan, Durrain had lured Shadi Gul Marri under the pretext of an assignment. He allegedly mixed sedatives into his tea, rendering him unconscious. Shadi Gul Marri was then brutally killed, and his body was buried with the help of accomplices at an undisclosed location. The organization later executed Durrain Marri.

data.fullName: Shahbaz Khan Marri, alias Peer Jan
data.biography:
In a statement issued on 19 November 2025 by Mazaar Baloch, spokesperson of the Baloch United Army (UBA), it was said that on 4 November at 7:30 in the morning, the Pakistan Air Force carried out a drone strike using guided missiles in the mountain range of Koh-e-Nagai in the Kalat region. As a result, four Sarmachars were martyred, including a fighter from the brother organization, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF). The organization pays tribute to them.

The fire that broke out after the drone attack severely burned the surrounding land, while unusual marks were also found on nearby rocks and stones, indicating that the weapons used contained chemical elements. The attack not only caused serious damage to the local environment but also left deep effects on the area’s natural balance.

Those who attained martyrdom in the drone attack include Dr. Mudasir Shahwani, alias Sarbuland Baloch; Shahbaz Khan Budani Marri, alias Peer Jan; Shakir Jatoi Baloch, alias Rudin Baloch and Haris Muhammad Shahi Baloch, alias Aftab Baloch.

Shahbaz Khan Marri joined the United Baloch Army in 2019 and from the beginning he demonstrated responsibility and unwavering commitment. His guerrilla tactics on the battlefield were admirable. His tireless efforts and serious role on different fronts earned the trust of his comrades, and he established himself within the organization as a determined fighter. He remained continuously active on the harsh and complex fronts of Koh-e-Nagai, Mach and Bolan, where his steadfastness and ability to assess situations and make decisions stood out.

Naveed Baloch, son of Abdul Haq, a Levies Sepoy in the Balochistan Levies Force and a resident of Gajjar, tehsil Mashkay, Awaran district, was summoned to a Pakistani military camp in Mashkay on September 7, 2025. He was subsequently enforcedly disappeared then for three days.

On September 10, 2025, his bullet-riddled body was discovered in Besima, Washuk district.

Jumma Khan Jatak, alias Borjan, son of Zarak Khan Jatak, was a resident of Mola, Khuzdar, Balochistan. His educational background was in religious studies. He joined the BLA on 20 July 2025 and served on the Nagaho and Kark fronts. He was martyred in Zaidi on 10 July 2026 at the age of 26.
Jumma Khan Jatak, considering national freedom to be the essence of human dignity and equating the occupation of Balochistan by what he regarded as a terrorist and uncivilized state like Pakistan with the humiliation of humanity, began armed resistance for the freedom of Balochistan through the Baloch Liberation Army last year. On the organization’s directive, he took up a position in the Nagaho region and, after completing basic military training, began fulfilling his organizational responsibilities with discipline and professionalism. He was one of those Sarmachars who was very clear about his objectives and targets and possessed the ability to confront the enemy and fight with great bravery.
Jumma Khan Jatak was not only aware of national consciousness, but also had a deep understanding of and knowledge about Islam. He was convinced, in light of Islamic teachings, that armed resistance against the occupying Punjabi forces was the only way forward through which a state could be established that would, in practice, protect the rights and freedom of the people of Balochistan. Martyr Borjan was also convinced that Pakistan, in the name of Islam, posed a danger to humanity and sought to preserve its existence through looting, occupation, and inhumane and non-Islamic practices, and that its destruction was necessary for the protection of the region and the greater good of humanity. He joined the battlefield and, through his dedicated service, left a message for the nation that participation in the freedom struggle of Balochistan was the duty of every person, regardless of class.
He remained committed to the path he had consciously chosen until the very end. He played a significant individual role in inflicting heavy losses on the enemy and taking control of the area in Zaidi. During active combat, while ensuring the safety of his fellow Sarmachars, he was killed. His sacrifices will remain in the pages of Baloch national history forever.

On 8 April 2025, Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) fighters were on patrol in the Kapudi area of Dukki when they came face to face with enemy forces. The clashes continued for hours. During the fighting, the BLA fighters managed to kill 9 enemy personnel and injure several others. In this battle, three BLA fighters - Abdul Wahab alias Deedag, Rahim Khan Marri alias Sarang, and Zahid Ali alias Washdil - were martyred.
Abdul Wahab alias Deedag, son of Mohammad Azam Zehri, belonged to Khakhoi, Zehri. He joined the BLA in 2022, and soon became a unit commander, serving in the special “Fateh Squad.” He led several operations on the Bolan and Dukki fronts. Even when wounded, he continued fighting and embraced martyrdom while resisting the enemy until his last bullet. His discipline, sense of timing, and skill in making battlefield decisions played a key role in many national victories.
Yahya Baloch was a resident of the Zamuran area in Kech District, Balochistan. He was a teacher by profession and was martyred on 7 November 2005.

On the night of May 11, 2025, Tariq Baloch, son of Ibrahim Kalmati and a renowned car racer from Jewani, Gwadar District, was forcibly abducted from his guesthouse by law enforcement agencies (LEAs) in a white Toyota Corolla. Less than 24 hours later, in the early morning of May 12, his lifeless body was found dumped in Palliri, Jewani, Balochistan.
Tariq was a widely admired sports figure, known across Pakistan and Iran for his motor racing accomplishments. His abduction and extrajudicial killing highlight the brutal reality in Balochistan: no profession, reputation, or apolitical status offers protection from the state’s ongoing campaign of violence.
This was not Tariq’s first encounter with illegal detention. On February 22, 2023, he and his brother Salman were forcibly disappeared by Pakistan’s Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD). Both were eventually released when no charges or evidence could justify their arrest. This time, however, Tariq did not return alive.

Shafiq Baloch, alias Zagrain, son of Dad Mohammad Baloch, was a resident of the Rahenegur area of Panjgur, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in September 2025 and served on the Paroom, Panjgur, and Gwargo fronts. He was promoted to the rank of Patrol Commander and was martyred on 17 September 2026 in the Gwargo area of Panjgur, Balochistan.
Shafiq Baloch, who was recognized and respected among his sarmachars for his indomitable combat prowess and skills, rejected the humiliating communal life of national servitude and, last year, made the historic decision to commit himself to national liberation, launching an armed resistance from the Panjgur front under the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army. Upon joining the front lines, Shafiq embraced the organization’s revolutionary, ethical, and disciplined culture and actively participated in training courses, where he excelled within a short period—an achievement he later demonstrated on the battlefield.
While remaining mobile and active on the front lines and utilizing his administrative, revolutionary, and combat skills, he took part in a major military operation against the enemy on the Panjgur front, inflicting significant losses on the enemy. Owing to his administrative, revolutionary, and military abilities, he was entrusted with mobile command responsibilities in the area, which he carried out with dedication until his final breath, employing robust strategies to restrict the enemy’s movement in the region while expanding organizational activities. During a bloody clash with the enemy, he led his sangats, fought until his last breath, and was martyred.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Siraj Baloch, alias Nabeel, son of Wahid Baksh Baloch, was born in 2003 and was a resident of Zamuran, Buleda district of Balochistan.
Siraj Baloch joined the Baloch Liberation Army in June 2025 and became part of the Majeed Brigade in August 2025. Prior to his formal induction, he remained connected with the BLA for three years as a committed supporter. On 31 January, he carried out a VBIED attack targeting the main army camp in Pull Abad, Tump.
His path was shaped not by immediacy but by years of conscious alignment and preparation. Long before his final act, his commitment had already taken form through patience, clarity, and ideological resolve. When the moment arrived, he stepped forward with certainty, carrying a decision refined over time and executed with unwavering determination.

On 12 March 2026, a statement issued by the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson, Gwahram Baloch, stated that two fighters of the organization, Waheed Baloch (alias Waleed) and Sameer Baloch (alias Meraan), were martyred in a clash with a death squad in the Gresha area of Naal.
The spokesperson further stated that a unit of BLF fighters was on a routine patrol in the Gresha area of Naal on 13 February 2026 when, at around 2:00 PM, agents of a state-sponsored death squad, who had pre-positioned themselves in an ambush at the location of Nadgi, attacked them. The fighters immediately took up positions and counter-attacked the enemy, after which a prolonged clash began between the fighters and the operatives of the state-backed armed group.
During this clash, which lasted more than two hours, another unit of fighters struck the death squad from a different direction, causing them to become disoriented. The fighters’ timely tactical maneuver forced the enemy to retreat. The enemy was compelled to flee the scene, carrying their killed and wounded personnel.
In the initial phase of the clash, one fighter was martyred and another was critically wounded by enemy fire. Amid intense gunfire, a unit of fighters evacuated the wounded sarmachar and the body of the martyred fighter from the scene to a safe location. However, the second wounded fighter later succumbed to his injuries and attained martyrdom.

Sameer Baloch, alias Meraan
In this clash with the enemy, Sameer Baloch, son of Khaliq Dad and a resident of Badrang Gresha, was martyred. He joined the mountain guerrilla front under the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front in March 2024. He was a hardworking, sociable, and exceptionally brave fighter. Martyr Sameer Baloch held a special place among his fellows due to his character and sincerity. He served on various fronts in Awaran, Kolwah, Jhao, Soorgar, Ornach, Naal, and Gresha. The BLF pays tribute to him for this great sacrifice.

Waheed Baloch, alias Waleed
The other fighter martyred in this battle with the enemy was Waheed Baloch, son of Khaliq Dad and a resident of Goni Gresha. He joined the Balochistan Liberation Front as an urban guerrilla in 2024. After successfully carrying out missions for one year, he was transferred to the mountain front in 2025 pursuant to an organizational decision. He was an expert in geographical affairs. Despite being wounded in his final battle, his morale remained high. He continued guiding his comrades to safety from the enemy's encirclement until his last breath. The organization pays tribute to him for this great sacrifice.

Shadi Khan Marri, son of Jamal Khan Marri, a 70 year old tribal elder and resident of Uthal in Lasbela District, Balochistan, was abducted by Pakistani forces on 23 September 2010 and forcibly disappeared. On 26 December 2010, he was extrajudicially killed, and his body was dumped on the Quetta-Sibi Road in the Dasht area of Mastung District.

data.birthPlace: Nizarabad, Turbat, Kech district, Occupied Baluchistan
data.biography:
Shari Baloch ( 1991 – 26 April 2022) was a Baloch educator, mother, and fidayee member of the Baloch Liberation Army’s Majeed Brigade.
Born in Nizarabad, Turbat, Kech district, Balochistan, Shari was the daughter of Hayat Baloch. Raised in a highly educated and well-established family, she earned her Bachelor of Education (B.Ed) in 2014 and Master of Education (M.Ed) in 2018. She held a master’s degree in Zoology from the University of Balochistan and was pursuing further postgraduate studies at the Allama Iqbal Open University, Turbat campus.
A committed secondary school science teacher in Turbat, Shari was married to a dentist and was a devoted mother to her eight year old daughter Mahrosh and five year old son Ishaq.
During her university years she was an active member of the Baloch Students Organization Azad (BSO-Azad), though she maintained no public affiliation with nationalist political movements afterward.
In 2020, she voluntarily joined the Majeed Brigade, the BLA’s elite unit for high risk self sacrificial operations. On 26 April 2022, at the age of thirty one, Shari Baloch carried out a suicide attack on a van carrying Chinese staff of the Confucius Institute  near the University of Karachi. She became the first woman in the Majeed Brigade to successfully execute such an operation and attained martyrdom in the blast.
Rafeeq Baloch, was a resident of the Dasht, Kech area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 24 February 2017 in Balochistan.

On 2 February 2022, sixteen members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayeen unit, the Majeed Brigade, carried out simultaneous attacks, nine in Noshki and seven on the Frontier Corps headquarters in Panjgur. The organization named this action "Operation Ganjal". 90 Pakistani security personnel were killed in Noshki and 105 in Panjgur.
In the BLA’s operation on the Noshki FC headquarters, 9 fidayeen participated. On 2 February 2022, Meerain Jamaldini (alias Zagrain) drove an VBEID into the camp’s main gate. Following this, Badil Baloch (alias Riyasat), Murad Aajo (alias Baba), Aneel Baloch (alias Balach), Yasir Noor (alias Saif), Aziz Zehri (alias Barag), Ibraheem Baloch (alias Kabeer), Deedag Bahar (alias Rauf) and Bilal Baloch (alias Wahid) entered the camp. As a result, 90 military personnel, including one officer, were killed, and a portion of the camp was destroyed.
The operation continued throughout the night. In the early morning of 3 February 2022, after their ammunition was exhausted, the remaining eight fidayeen took their own lives by firing their weapons.

On 9 November 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Republican Guards spokesperson Dostain Baloch announced the martyrdom of five members of the organisation and paid red salutes to them.

The spokesperson said: “We pay heartfelt tribute and offer red salutes to the sincere, brave, and ideologically committed fighters of the Baloch Republican Guards: Commander Habibullah Jan Jatoi, alias Laghari; Sharif Jatoi, alias Commando; Saeed Jan Jatoi, alias Nana; Hazrat Jatoi, alias Bolani; and Umeed Ali Jatoi, alias Nadir. They embraced martyrdom while bravely fighting against the occupying Pakistani army in the Sanni area of Kachhi for the freedom and right to self-determination of Balochistan."

On 1 November 2026, in the Sanni area of Kachhi, Commander Habibullah Jan and his revolutionary comrades launched an ambush against a convoy of the occupying Pakistani army.
Commander Habibullah Jan and his brave fighters fiercely engaged the enemy on the front lines, inflicting significant human and material losses on the occupying forces.
During the clash, an enemy drone suddenly launched an attack, seriously injuring Commander Habibullah Jan, Saeed, Hazrat, and Umeed. Despite their injuries, they continued to face the consequences of the attack. However, unable to survive their severe injuries, Habibullah Jan and his comrades later embraced martyrdom. All five members were residents of the Sanni area of Kachhi.

Rasheed Lasi, son of Jalil Ahmed, was a 19 year old shepherd from Sukhan, area of Uthal. He belonged to a poor family and worked as a shepherd to support his family. On September 22, 2026, Rasheed was targeted and killed by Frontier Corps soldiers of the Pakistani forces in Gajeri, Sukhan, Uthal, Balochistan.

During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Fahad Baloch, alias Diyar, son of Attaullah Badini, was a resident of the Qazi Abad area of Noshki District in Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2025 and served on the Shor Parod front. He was martyred in Noshki during Operation Herof Phase 2.
Fahad Baloch, alias Diyar, grew up in the environment of Noshki, where the question of national freedom quietly takes shape in the minds of the younger generation. Fahad did not view the conditions around him merely as an everyday reality; rather, he sought to understand them as part of a broader historical narrative. This awakening of consciousness led him to a point where an individual rises beyond personal limits and becomes connected to the question of a nation’s collective destiny. His association with the armed resistance movement was the result of this intellectual journey, in which the idea of freedom evolved from a mere desire into a firm ideological conviction.
Fahad Baloch served on the Shor Parod front and was present on the Noshki front during Operation Herof Phase 2. There, during the historic six-day battle, he delivered decisive blows to the enemy with courage and strategic resolve, and on that very front he sacrificed his life, becoming immortal in the history of the war of freedom.

On 11 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch announced the martyrdom of 14 fighters of the organization who attained martyrdom in confrontations with the Pakistani army and in airstrikes while defending their homeland, Balochistan, and fighting for national liberation and the right to self-determination.

On 13 August 2026, Pakistani Air Force fighter jets bombarded the Pandran area of Kalat District in Balochistan, resulting in the martyrdom of four members of the organization: Waseem Baloch, alias Farhan; Obaidullah Baloch, alias Shaheen; Nawaz Ali Baloch, alias Dilshad; and Mohammad Hassan, alias Ahmad.

On 25 August 2026, during an organizational mission in the Kech area of Balochistan, Sher Jan, alias Jamal, was shot from behind by a traitor, resulting in his martyrdom.

On 3 September 2026, while patrolling in the Mastung area of Balochistan, the organization’s brave fighters, Mohammad Younis, alias Salal; Sameer Ahmad, alias Zemal; Aziz Ahmad, alias Janan; and Sikandar Baloch, confronted Pakistani forces, targeted several enemy personnel, and embraced martyrdom.

On 14 September 2026, while engaging Pakistani forces and defending his fellow fighters in the Machani Kor Paroom area of Panjgur District, Babar Baloch, alias Kambar, embraced martyrdom.

On 18 September 2026, during a confrontation with Pakistani forces in the Chagi area of Balochistan, fighters of the organization, Riaz Baloch, alias Sabir; Taimoor Shah, alias Shaheen; Zia Ul Haq, alias Ziaullah; and Jumma Baloch, alias Commando, embraced martyrdom.

Sikandar Baloch, son of Rahim Dad, resident of Dasht Pangu, joined the BLF on 25 June 2025. He spent most of his time on the Nagahu front. After being moved to the Mastung front under an organizational decision, on 3 September 2026 he bravely fought the army during a patrol and was martyred along with his fellow sarmachars.

data.fullName: Yasir Baloch, alias Master Safar Khan

data.biography:
Haroon Rasheed, son of Abdul Rasheed, was a resident of Quetta. He was an intermediate (F.Sc) student at Science College, Quetta, and a member of the Science College unit of BSO Azad, Shaal Zone. He received his early education in Quetta.
He mobilized hundreds of youth to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of their homeland. Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by security forces. He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and BSO Azad, but he remained steadfast with the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom.
He was an example of bravery and commitment. He joined the organization at an early age and stood by his national ideology until the end. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising his peaceful political expression.
He was killed by Pakistani police forces on Double Road, Quetta, on January 22, 2009. He was among the most committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad.
His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

Nako Nabi Bakhsh, a Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) fighter, was martyred on November 8, 2021 in an attack by the enemy. He was attacked by the ISI agents when he was travelling in Tagran area of Tump, district Turbat, Balochistan.
Nabi Bakhsh alias Nako son of Rehmat belonged to Tump Koharh. He had been associated with the BLA since 2014, during this period, Nako Nabi Bakhsh courageously served the national movement.  Not only himself was devoted to the national cause, but his entire family also has never hesitated to make sacrifices in this regard.
Nako Nabi Bakhsh's house was attacked several times by the occupying forces and his house was set on fire but he and his family did not back down from the ideology of independent Balochistan.

In Gwadar, nine Fidayeen of the BLA Majeed Brigade were divided into two units and took part in the operation. The first unit, which included Fidayeen Hawa Baloch (alias Droshum), Yahya Lal (alias Lashari), Adnan Arman (alias Changaiz), and Yousif Baloch (alias Yagi), attacked the compound of the occupying Pakistani intelligence agencies, resulting in the elimination of 12 personnel. Women and children in residential quarters near the compound were provided safe passage; however, the occupying army later martyred these same civilians by opening fire.
About forty minutes later, occupying forces advanced toward the compound, leading to clashes that continued until the evening. In these clashes, more than 24 personnel were eliminated, and three military vehicles, including an armored vehicle, were destroyed.
The second squad, which included Fidayeen Kambar Ismail (alias Sarbaz), Khurshid KB (alias Arman), Waseem Baloch (alias Kareem), Shoaib Baloch (alias Shehzad), and Yasir, took up strong positions in Port Bazaar near Gwadar Port. After announcements were made in mosques, freedom fighters went to the bazaar, met the public, and held political discussions. After repelling the advance of occupying forces in the city, the freedom fighters later advanced toward the port and fired several rockets that hit their targets. Clashes continued until the next day, eliminating more than 19 personnel.
Hawa Baloch, alias Droshum, daughter of Shaheed Nabi Baksh, was a resident of the Kohad Tump area of Turbat district in Balochistan. She was born on 13 September 2006. Her father, Nabi Baksh, was martyred on 8 November 2021. During Operation Herof Phase Two at the Gwadar front, Fidayee Hawa Baloch fought selflessly, standing shoulder to shoulder with fellow fidayeen in demanding combat conditions. Her conduct reflected composure, commitment, and an unshaken sense of responsibility in the face of danger. Carrying forward the legacy of sacrifice, she transformed conviction into action and left a powerful mark through her presence, resolve, and solidarity on the battlefield.

On February 23, 2022 the occupying forces of Pakistan stroke the Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) guerrilla camp in Satak Kor mountain range of Hoshab, district Kech and fired three missiles loaded with chemicals that wreaked havoc over a large area, destroying palm groves and other plants at the site. After the drone missile attacks, the infantry team of the occupying forces surrounded the area, and with the help of more than eight state helicopters entered the camp. Five Sarmachaars including two commanders of the organization Master Asif Baloch and Siraj Baloch were martyred in this attack. While the other five Sarmachaars - Shoaib, Munir, Arif Jan, Diljan, Kamal, Kamash Malang, Jangi Khan, and Dolat - were martyred in the defense of the homeland, fighting the enemy for over an hour and killing several commandos of the occupying forces.
Jangi Khan Baloch, alias Essa son of Master Asa resident of Shapuk joined Student politics at a very young age. He joined the armed struggle in 2014. He was the only son of his parents. Jangi Khan was one of the best fighters who was recently appointed as the Second Commander of Siraj Zahir Field Camp.
