data.biography: Hakeem Baloch, was a resident of the Gebun, Kech area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 5 December 2012 in Balochistan.

Early Life and Professional Background

Dr. Mannan Baloch was born in the Mashkay area of Awaran, Balochistan. A medical doctor by profession, he served as a Medical Officer in the health department of Balochistan. Despite a stable professional career, his deep seated concern for the socio-political conditions of his people led him to pivot from medicine to full time political activism.

Political Leadership and Vision

Dr. Baloch was a cornerstone of modern Baloch nationalist politics. He is widely credited with playing a dual role in the revitalization of the Baloch National Movement (BNM) and providing the ideological and organizational groundwork for the formation of BSO Azad.

As the Secretary General of the BNM, he was recognized as a sophisticated political strategist. His expertise in international politics and his ability to forecast geopolitical shifts allowed him to elevate the Baloch cause on the global stage. He was a staunch advocate for institutionalism, believing that the strength of a movement lay in its organizational discipline rather than individual personalities.

Mobilization and Activism

Known for his tireless grassroots work, Dr. Mannan traveled extensively throughout the difficult terrains of Balochistan. He focused on:

Political Education: Organizing circles to educate the youth on national rights and international law.

Unity: Bridging gaps between various factions to create a cohesive front for the Baloch national cause.

Awareness: Documenting and speaking out against human rights violations and socioeconomic injustices.

Martyrdom

On January 30, 2016, Dr. Mannan Baloch was martyred during a military operation in Mastung, Balochistan. He was martyred alongside four of his comrades, including Ashraf Baloch and Hanif Baloch. His death was mourned across the region, and he remains a symbol of intellectual resistance and dedication within the Baloch liberation movement.

On 21 September 2024, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Major Gwahram Baloch issued a statement paying tribute to Lieutenant Akhtar Baloch, alias Ali.

The spokesperson stated that Lieutenant Akhtar Baloch, alias Ali, son of Haji Mohammad, was a resident of Gomazi, Tump, and a dedicated BLF fighter. He was martyred on 28 August 2024 by mercenaries of the occupying Pakistani forces.

The spokesperson said that the BLF paid tribute to Lieutenant Akhtar Baloch for his great sacrifice. He added that the search for those responsible for his killing was ongoing. Those responsible for Akhtar Baloch's death had committed a national crime, and the organization was determined to identify them and bring them to justice. Such elements were a curse upon any nation, and eliminating them was essential for national survival, freedom, and progress.

Akhtar Baloch was a selfless participant in the freedom movement. He had been working in Gulf countries but returned to his homeland in 2009 to join the BLF and fight for the national cause. He received military training in Mashkay and participated in various battles against the enemy, achieving significant victories.

Recognizing his leadership skills, the organization appointed him commander of its urban network. Serving as a lieutenant, he led armed activities in urban areas using guerrilla tactics. In 2012, after coming under the enemy's radar, he moved to the mountains and participated in BLF military operations in Siyahji, Mazanband, Kulbar, Zamuran, Buleda, and Balgatar.

On 3 August 2016, Akhtar Baloch and his fellow fighter, Aman, alias Kinar, were wounded during an operation against the enemy. Despite his injuries, Akhtar Baloch continued fighting and successfully led his comrades to safety. However, Aman was killed while defending the homeland. After recovering from his injuries, Akhtar Baloch returned to the front lines to fulfil his national duties.

For the two years preceding his death, Akhtar Baloch had been living in hiding in urban areas under the organization's directives. He was eventually killed by agents of Pakistani intelligence services.

Matric student Jangiyan Baloch, son of Abdullah Rashed from Panjgur district, Balochistan, was reportedly subjected to enforced disappearance on May 26, 2025, from Jaeen Paroom. According to his family, he was allegedly taken by a death squad along with soldiers of the Frontier Corps (FC).
On February 15, 2026, his body was reportedly found dumped in the Shapatan area of Panjgur.

Rafiullah Gorgnari, alias Tanveer, son of Saifullah Gorgnari, was a resident of the Killi Kari Sor area of Mastung, Balochistan. He joined the BLA as an urban guerrilla in October 2024 and moved to the mountain front in October 2025, where he served on the Mastung front. He was martyred on 6 September 2026 in the Khadkocha area of Mastung, Balochistan.
Rafiullah Gorgnari, who carried out his activities with lightning speed on the ground and created difficult situations for the enemy from the urban front to the war front, made the final decision in 2024 to resist the usurping occupier through armed resistance while establishing an ideological and intellectual connection with the great cause of Baloch national liberation. Under organizational orders, he began his national and guerrilla activities on the urban front, where he monitored the enemy, provided crucial information, and delivered real-time intelligence for military operations. On the urban front, he remained active against the enemy for a full year, continuously fulfilling his national and organizational responsibilities. 
After one year, on organizational orders, he moved from the urban front to the mountain front, completed his training, and became part of the combat lines. For the following year, he played a key role in participating in organized military operations against the enemy from Mastung, as well as in expanding the organization’s sphere of influence in the region. At Khadkocha, he joined his fellow fighters in several major and historic assaults against the enemy and played a full role in inflicting a defeat on the occupiers. It was while fulfilling these national and revolutionary responsibilities that he was martyred fighting the enemy for the freedom of his homeland, inscribing his name in history alongside the national martyrs.

data.fullName: Saddam Hussain Siyah Paad, alias KD
data.biography:
Operation Dara-e-Bolan, which began on 29 January 2024 continued for two days until 31 January 2024 and was successfully concluded after achieving its intended objectives. A total of 385 Sarmachars from four different units of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) participated in Operation Dara-e-Bolan. Among them were 12 Fidayeen from the BLA’s Majeed Brigade. The other participating units included the Fateh Squad, the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS) and the Intelligence Wing.
Operation Dara-e-Bolan commenced on the evening of 29 January 2024 at 9:00 pm local time and continued for two days. After achieving the desired results, the BLA’s Senior Command Council announced the conclusion of Operation Dara-e-Bolan on 31 January 2024 at 7:00 pm and issued instructions to all units to vacate their positions and report back to their base camps.
During the operation, BLA Sarmachars took complete control of an area within a 70 kilometre radius, including Mach city and the strategically important National Highway N-65. Over the course of Operation Dara-e-Bolan, a total of 78 enemy personnel were killed. These included 45 Frontier Corps (FC) personnel who were killed within the first three hours of the operation in Mach city; 10 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on an army camp at the Pir Ghaib Bolan location; 4 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on a military convoy at the Gokurt Mach location; 12 regular army personnel who were killed on 30 January when Majeed Brigade Fidayeen eliminated them and entered the FC headquarters; and at least 5 SSG commandos who were targeted and killed by the Fidayeen on 31 January 2024. In addition, two police personnel were also killed, including one Station House Officer (SHO).
A large number of Levies and police personnel were captured by the BLA during the operation; however, as they were Baloch, they were released. During Operation Dara-e-Bolan, 13 brave fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army attained martyrdom. Of these, 12 martyred Sarmachars belonged to the Majeed Brigade Fidayeen, while one martyred Sarmachar was from the BLA’s Fateh Squad.
The martyred Sarmachars were: Qasim Baloch, Saddam Hussain, Salal Baloch, Farooq Baloch, Atta Baloch, Hammal Momin, Zeeshan Zehri, Nadir Bangulzai, Nizam Baloch, Zeeshan Baloch, Jamal Baloch, Wadood Satakzai, and Kashif Shahwani.
Saddam Hussain Siyah Paad, alias KD, son of Aziz Mohammad Siyah Paad, belonged to the Eri Kalag area of Kharan. The 29 year old Saddam Hussain was a graduate of Tando Jam University in Sindh. He had been associated with the armed struggle for the previous eight years. In 2016, he was forcibly disappeared by the occupying forces and subjected to severe torture, yet he did not renounce his stance on national liberation. After his release from captivity, he concluded that there was no remaining space for peaceful politics in Balochistan and therefore chose the armed path of struggle. Alongside being a mature and perceptive political activist, he was also a hardworking and resilient guerrilla fighter. Two years prior, he offered his services to the BLA - Majeed Brigade.

Ali Mohammad, son of Hakeem Baloch and a resident of Mashkai Khandri, was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani genocidal forces on February 1, 2025. After more than four months of incommunicado detention, he was extrajudicially executed. On June 11, 2025, his body visible signs of custodial torture was found dumped at a local hospital in Mashkai.

Ijaz Baloch, son of Fazal Baloch, born on 01 March 1992 in Gowarjak, Mashkai, was a resident of Gowarjak, Mashkai, District Awaran, Balochistan. He received his early education in Mashkai and was an FSc student at Inter College Mashkai and a member of BSO Azad Mashkai Zone.
He mobilized hundreds of youths to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of the Baloch homeland. Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by the security forces. He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he remained with the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom. He was an example of bravery and commitment.
He joined the organization at an early age and remained committed to his national ideology until the end. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising peaceful political expression. He was abducted from his home on 21 April 2015 by Pakistani military forces in Gowarjak, Mashkai. His bullet-riddled body was found dumped on the same day in Gajjar, Mashkai, District Awaran, Balochistan. His body bore severe signs of torture.
He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

On 12 August 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahran Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of nine fighters of the organization: 1. Zubair Baloch, alias Shahvez; 2. Shahnawaz Baloch, alias Rahchar; 3. Rahim Baloch, alias Ajiz Baloch; 4. Musharaf Baloch, alias Basham; 5. Munir Baloch, alias Khalid Baloch; 6. Mohammad Zaman, alias Yahya; 7. Jasim Baloch, alias Babar; 8. Gaji Khan Baloch, alias Aftab; and 9. Abdullah Baloch, alias Usman, and paid tribute to all the martyred comrades who sacrificed their lives for the freedom of the motherland, Balochistan.

Abdullah Baloch, alias Usman, son of Ustad Murad Bakhsh and a resident of Raghe Baloch Abad, began his struggle through the platform of the BLF in 2024. While carrying out his organizational responsibilities, he performed his duties with great honesty and dedication in the cause of freedom. While defending his position, he became involved in an intense clash with the occupying forces. He demonstrated courage and determination throughout the confrontation and was killed while fighting for his homeland.

Ghulam Nabi Baloch, alias Bolani, son of Haji Noor Mohammad Satakzai, was a resident of the Dagari area of Quetta. He joined the BLA in 2024 and served on the Mastung, Bolan, and Quetta fronts. He was promoted to the rank of Patrol Commander and was martyred on 25 September 2026 in the Dagari area of Quetta, Balochistan.
Ghulam Nabi Baloch, alias Bolani, possessed the ability to fight effectively on the battlefield and the courage to turn harsh conditions to his advantage. He understood the importance of the fundamental human right to Baloch national sovereignty and freedom and, in 2024, made the historic decision to join the Baloch Liberation Army and took up a position on the rugged Bolan front, where he became active. After completing basic training courses, he moved into the combat lines and took part in battles against the enemy, inflicting heavy blows on them. He possessed formidable combat skills in confronting and defeating the enemy, which he demonstrated on every front during his national service.
After serving in Bolan, he was deployed to the Mastung and then the Quetta fronts. He carried out his military and professional duties on every front with full dedication. After proving himself on various fronts to be a brave, selfless, and administratively capable leader, he was entrusted by the organization with patrol command responsibilities, which he carried out with great diligence and dedication until his final days. While carrying out a coordinated and organized operation against the enemy in the Dagari area of Quetta, he led his team with excellence. Fighting the enemy on the front lines, he attained martyrdom for the great national cause and freedom and was immortalized forever in the pages of national history.

Shahjan, son of Murad Baloch and a resident of district Panjgur, was forcibly disappeared on July 29, 2025, from the main Chitkan Bazar in Panjgur by state-backed death squads.

Just two days before his abduction, Shah Jan had gotten married. Family members reported that he was transferred to the main Frontier Constabulary (FC) camp in Panjgur shortly after his enforced disappearance.

After four days of illegal detention, on August 04, 2025, his mutilated body was found in Panjgur.

Ali Mohammed Mengal stood firm and brave in his fight against the oppressors of the Baloch nation.
Under the leadership of Shaheed Noroz Khan, he pointed his rifle toward the tyrant Ayub Khan and his regime. Later, Ali Mohammed Mengal once again answered the call of duty and rose up for the Baloch cause against the so-called democratic government of Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto. With his band of brothers, he bravely defended his people and his nation.
However, on 10 August 1973, in the area of Jhalawan, the Pakistani Army ambushed Ali Mohammed Mengal and his band of brothers. Like a true sarmachar, he fought to his last breath, until his blood washed the soil of his beloved land.
Shaheed Ali Mohammed Mengal and the other martyrs do not die. They live on in the hearts and souls of today’s sarmachars, motivating them, energizing them, and reminding them of the difficult path toward the independence of Balochistan.

Abdul Khaliq, son of Ibrahim, was a 28-year-old government employee (JVT teacher) and a resident of the Gowani area of Gresha, Khuzdar. In the late hours of the night on 21 September 2026, armed, state-sponsored personnel assaulted him at his home while he was peacefully sleeping inside the premises of his house.
Abdul Khaliq was an educator who served in the field of education for the betterment of his community, where schools are either without teachers or have been transformed into army barracks. Instead of providing support, the government failed to protect him, and he was indiscriminately targeted and killed by a state-backed death squad that reportedly operated under the Pakistani Army and Frontier Corps (FC) in the area.
When the family members followed the attackers, they fled the scene and entered the premises of local state-backed death squad members.
Abdul Khaliq was an educated man who was deeply concerned about his students and taught at a school in the remote areas of his village.

On 4 March 2026, a statement issued by the spokesperson of the Balochistan Liberation Front, Major Gwahram Baloch, stated that on 3 February 2026, fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front launched a coordinated operation at four different locations in Hoshap against Pakistani forces. In this organized operation, various BLF units simultaneously targeted the enemy army at four different locations in Hoshap.
In the initial phase of the operation, one unit of fighters surrounded the police station located in Hoshap Bazaar and took control of the station, holding the personnel hostage. While this unit was seizing government weapons, ammunition, and other equipment, an enemy military convoy consisting of four vehicles approached the area, resulting in an intense face-to-face clash between BLF fighters and enemy forces. During the clash, the fighters targeted and destroyed two enemy vehicles, killing several Pakistani military personnel on board.
Meanwhile, a second unit of fighters positioned at another location attacked two armored enemy vehicles with heavy weapons. Several military personnel were killed or wounded in the clash. Witnessing the defeat and retreat of their ground forces, the enemy resorted to gunship helicopters and advanced drone technology to halt the BLF fighters’ advance.
In this prolonged clash, seven BLF fighters - Shaneed Baloch (alias Shohaz Baloch), Zabad Baloch (alias Deedag), Atta Baloch (alias Obaid), Ghaffar Baloch (alias Noroz), Abdul Samad Baloch (alias Muheem Jan), Zaheer Baloch (alias Istaal), and Nadeem (alias Sahil) - fought valiantly until their last bullet and last breath and embraced martyrdom while courageously defending their motherland.
Shaneed Baloch, alias Shohaz Baloch Son of Mohammad Rafiq, resident of Sahaki Kelkour, joined the armed struggle in 2016 under the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front. Prior to this, he had been involved in student politics since 2012. He was an exceptionally brave, hardworking, and politically conscious fighter. He struck devastating blows against the enemy on various fronts with his extraordinary combat abilities and remained on the front line in every difficult mission. His family has long endured the hardships of state oppression and displacement.

Ali Baig Bugti, son of Pahi Bugti and a resident of Siah Aaf, Dera Bugti, was forcibly disappeared by personnel of Pakistani secret agencies on October 18, 2024, from Dera Bugti city. His family was suffering for months with no information about his whereabouts or condition.
After nearly eight months of illegal detention, Ali Baig was extrajudicially killed. On June 12, 2025, his severely mutilated body was found dumped in Piara Colony, located in Sui, District Dera Bugti.
data.martyrdomPlace: Piara Colony, Sui, Dera Bugti, Balochistan

data.biography:
Shoaib Umrani, alias Gurk (Gorgein), son of Ali Bakhsh Umrani, was 21 years old and a resident of Baghbana, Khuzdar, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2025 and served on the Kalat and Khuzdar fronts. He was martyred on 10 July 2026 in Zaidi, Khuzdar, Balochistan.
Registering his name in the history of the war on the fronts of Khuzdar and Kalat, Sarmachar Shoaib Umrani rejected Punjabi dominance. Instead of accepting a humiliating life of slavery, he chose to become part of the struggle for national freedom and enlisted in the ranks of the BLA in 2025. After completing his basic military training courses, he decided to provide his services in the war zone and became active on the Khuzdar and Kalat fronts. With strong ideological and mental conviction, Shoaib Umrani quickly mastered the art and strategies of warfare and began inflicting heavy blows on the enemy.
He carried out his responsibilities on the battlefield as an agile, disciplined, courageous, dignified, and resolute fighter. Whenever he confronted the enemy, he fought with great professionalism, bravery, and a spirit of sacrifice, demonstrating unwavering and exceptional resolve.
He did not fight the enemy with weapons alone but confronted it with strong revolutionary determination. It was this revolutionary consciousness that gave him strength throughout this period, and he stood his ground steadfastly as a Sarmachar against the enemy. He inflicted heavy damage on the enemy many times on the battlefield and made great efforts to support his fellow Sangats in maintaining organizational superiority in the region.
He maintained this ideological and conscious conviction until the end and continued to fight the enemy. On 10 July 2026, in Zaidi, he sacrificed himself for the freedom and glory of the motherland and joined the ranks of those great martyrs of Baloch history who have preserved and protected Baloch identity and survival.

The massacre of Baloch by the Muttahida Qaumi Movement (MQM) in Karachi on January 7, 2010, sparked a series of protests all over Balochistan. Baloch people marched in support of their brothers in Karachi in every major city and town. The Baloch Student Organization (BSO-Azaad) called for a peaceful demonstration in Khuzdar to express their anger against Pakistan’s planned genocide of Baloch living in Karachi. On January 15, 2010, students gathered at Degree College Khuzdar. Activists of the Baloch National Front (BNF) also came and joined them to show their solidarity. As the protest rally departed from the college, within a few minutes it came under fire from all sides. The Pakistani army’s assault on the unprovoked peaceful rally was so brutal and severe that it left many dead and injured.
Baloch activists rushed their fallen comrades to the hospital. Two Baloch youths, Ali Dost Baloch, who worked in the municipal office, and Saddam Hussain Baloch, a member of BSO-Azad and a student of Residential College Khuzdar, succumbed to their injuries and joined the martyrs of the Baloch heroic struggle for the liberation of their motherland. Liaqat Ali Baloch, Zafar Baloch, Inayat Baloch, Ghulam Fareed Baloch, and Nazeer Baloch were severely injured. The wounded were later shifted to Karachi due to the lack of medical facilities in Balochistan. Doctors in Karachi amputated Liaqat Ali Baloch’s leg from the knee to save his life.

On June 27, 2025, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) issued a statement saying that on June 22, 2025, its fighters were on an organizational patrol in the Gresha area when they encountered operatives of a state-sponsored death squad near the Badrang region. A fierce clash ensued, during which three BLF fighters embraced martyrdom, while one enemy operative was killed and several others were wounded.
The martyrs of this encounter were Second Lieutenant Maqbool Baloch (alias Qandeel Baloch), Siraj Baloch (alias Zubair Baloch) and Khalid Baloch (alias Safar Baloch).
Shaheed Siraj Baloch (alias Zubair) son of Daulat Baloch, was a resident of Bahri, Gresha. He too was forcibly disappeared in 2020, but even after his release, his ideological commitment remained steadfast. A year before his martyrdom, he joined the Balochistan Liberation Front and, within a short time, played a vital role in several sensitive missions.

He started as an active student in BSO Azad, driven by love for his homeland. With time, he left student life behind and went to the mountains, joining the armed struggle. In the region, people knew him as a brave frontline fighter who never stepped back from his cause. In 2018, he fought with all his heart and gave his life, remembered for sacrificing his last drop of blood for what he believed in.

Hasnain Shahwani, alias Maqbool, son of Ibrahim Shahwani, was a resident of Killi Kark, Mastung. He joined the BLA on 22 October 2022 and was later promoted to the rank of Camp Commander in the Fateh Squad. He served on the Kalat and Mastung fronts and was killed on 1 June 2026 in the Kirdagap area of Mastung, Balochistan.
Hasnain Shahwani, alias Maqbool, was regarded by his associates as a capable, people-friendly, and militarily skilled member of the BLA. He was considered a reliable leader for his comrades, compassionate toward the local population, and an effective fighter against opposing forces. Owing to these qualities, he was selected as a camp commander, where he carried out his responsibilities effectively and remained steadfast in his conduct and character until his final days.
His notable qualities included military capability, endurance in prolonged combat, and tactical skill and alertness during engagements. Because of these qualities, he was given command responsibilities within the Fateh Squad, where he led members of elite units in multiple battles. He played a key role in organizational military activities in Mastung, Kalat, and surrounding areas, particularly in maintaining control over towns and highways.
During Operations Herof I and Herof II, he served as a frontline fighter and leader. During Herof II, he led members of the organization’s elite unit, the Fateh Squad, on the Mastung front and played an important role in the operation in the area. Within his area of responsibility, he expanded the organization’s presence and systematically implemented its offensive strategy.
In accordance with the organization’s policy, he maintained defensive positions in areas under its control and, on several occasions, succeeded in halting enemy advances. During the organization’s incursions into urban areas, he remained active as a frontline leader. Remaining committed to his responsibilities until his final days, he continued to resist enemy advances in the Kirdagap area of Mastung and was killed in combat on 1 June 2026.

On 2 February 2022, sixteen members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayeen unit, the Majeed Brigade, carried out simultaneous attacks, nine in Noshki and seven on the Frontier Corps headquarters in Panjgur. The organization named this action "Operation Ganjal". 90 Pakistani security personnel were killed in Noshki and 105 in Panjgur.
In the BLA’s operation on the Noshki FC headquarters, 9 fidayeen participated. On 2 February 2022, Meerain Jamaldini (alias Zagrain) drove an VBEID into the camp’s main gate. Following this, Badil Baloch (alias Riyasat), Murad Aajo (alias Baba), Aneel Baloch (alias Balach), Yasir Noor (alias Saif), Aziz Zehri (alias Barag), Ibraheem Baloch (alias Kabeer), Deedag Bahar (alias Rauf) and Bilal Baloch (alias Wahid) entered the camp. As a result, 90 military personnel, including one officer, were killed, and a portion of the camp was destroyed.
The operation continued throughout the night. In the early morning of 3 February 2022, after their ammunition was exhausted, the remaining eight fidayeen took their own lives by firing their weapons.

Saadat Marri, also known as Sado Marri, was born in 1927 in the Harnai area of Sibi, Balochistan. He took part in the Baloch resistance movements of 1964 and in the 1972 war for the independence of Balochistan. In 1977, when a number of Baloch migrated to Afghanistan, Saadat Baloch also migrated with his family. In 1992, he returned to Balochistan along with many other Baloch and settled near the mountains of Hazar Ghanji. On 17 March 2003, under the command of the Baloch Liberation Army, Saadat Marri and a group of guerrilla fighters established their first guerrilla camp in the Tump area of Turbat District, Balochistan, where the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) was formed. In 2004, they began their attacks from Gwadar. Despite his old age, he remained active on the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF). His commitment to the Baloch cause made him immortal in the hearts of his people. On December 3, 2007, the freedom fighters under his leadership attacked a Frontier Corps (FC) post in Kech. This became his final mission, which he completed for his motherland. After overrunning the post, he continued to engage the remaining enemy soldiers so that his comrades could withdraw safely. He fought until he embraced martyrdom. His martyrdom came only months after the martyrdom of his son, Gulzar Baloch, who was killed on August 14, 2007. His unwavering commitment and the true philosophy of Baloch nationalism reached every part of Balochistan.

Hasil Baloch, son of Master Arz Muhammad, was born on January 2, 1995, in Mandeel, Mashkai, District Awaran. He was an intermediate student at Inter College Awaran and served as the president of BSO Azad Mashkai Zone.
He played an important role in organizing the political activities of the organization in the Mashkai region. He was a devoted worker of the organization and had a keen interest in reading revolutionary literature.
During his presidency, the organization managed to continue its struggle in Mashkai despite a brutal crackdown by security agencies. The actions of the state did not allow him to continue his education, as Pakistani security forces pursued him due to his peaceful political activities under the banner of BSO Azad.
He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising his right to peaceful political expression. He was killed by the Pakistan Army in a military operation in Kolwah, District Awaran, on October 5, 2016.
His sacrifice will be remembered in golden words in the history of BSO Azad and the Baloch liberation movement.
Majid Baloch was killed by Pakistani Frontier Corps forces on 1 December 2010 in Turbat during a raid on Ayub Gichki's house.
Murad Baloch was murdered on 1 December 2010 by the Pakistani Frontier Corps during a raid on Ayub Gichki’s house in Turbat, Balochistan.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Barat Baloch, alias Aslam, son of Murad Bakhsh, aged 24, was a resident of Askani Bazaar in the Absar area of Turbat district, Balochistan. He joined the BLA on 28 January 2023 and became part of the Majeed Brigade in August 2023. During his time in the organization, he served on the Panjgur, Kolwa, Keelkor, and Gichk fronts.
Barat Baloch belonged to Turbat, Kech. The land of Turbat has always been a shining symbol of courage, political awareness, and sacrifice. It is a soil whose people have never hesitated to make every kind of sacrifice for national liberation. From this dignified land was born a fearless Sarmachar (freedom fighter) like Barat, a young man who was intellectually and consciously prepared to make every sacrifice for the freedom of his homeland. From childhood, Barat Baloch grew up hearing stories of sacrifice and resistance around him, and this very spirit and consciousness led him to the battlefield in pursuit of national liberation.
Barat Baloch was present on the Gwadar front during Operation Herof II. On the Gwadar front, Barat and his companions fought an organized and determined battle, the effects of which will become clear in the coming days in the Baloch war of independence and in the geopolitical situation of the entire region.
Barat wrote history in the battle for freedom with his blood and proved that Baloch Fidayee Sarmachars remain on the battlefield until their last breath, continuously delivering decisive blows to the enemy.

Martyr Dad Shah Baloch, alias Waheed Baloch was born in house of Hasil Baloch and Jameela Baloch in Dandal, Shapuk area of Kech, Balochistan. He became part of Baloch liberation movement in platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in 2013 and for years, he joined in Baloch Republican Army (BRA). He newly joined in Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) before same days of his martyrdom. He embraced martyrdom along with eight comrades, Jalil Sher Baloch, Samad Baloch, Dad Shah, Kambar Baloch, Shoaib, Rahmdil, Haris Baloch and Nawaz Baloch  in a drone attack of Pakistan Army  on Nov 29, 2022 in Jath, Kolwa area of Kech, Balochistan.
data.fullName: Dad Shah Baloch, alias Waheed Baloch

data.biography:
In 1838, the British sent a force led by Alexander Burnes to reinstate Shah Shuja Durrani as the king of Afghanistan by deposing Amir Dost Mohammad Khan. To reach Afghanistan, they needed passage through Balochistan, particularly the Bolan Pass. However, Khan Mehrab Khan refused to allow the British to use his land to attack a neighboring country. The British sent Lieutenant Leach to negotiate with the Baloch government, but the Khan stood firm. When British forces reached Shaal via Bolan, some patriotic Baloch, without the Khan’s knowledge, attacked British troops out of nationalist sentiment and a desire to protect their homeland.
After toppling Amir Dost Mohammad Khan, the British Governor General of India, Lord Auckland, ordered an attack on Balochistan. In 1839, around 7,000 British troops marched from Shaal to attack the Baloch Meeri (capital). Anticipating an invasion, Khan Mehrab Khan declared war and sent messages to tribal leaders, but many saw the British as allies rather than invaders and chose to collaborate with them rather than defend their land. When Khan Mehrab Khan gathered his resistance fighters, the number of loyal warriors had dwindled to only 700 due to the short sightedness of many tribal chiefs. Nevertheless, Mehrab Khan was determined to fight. At his court, a respected figure, Akhund Muhammad Siddiq, advised him that he was not in a position to wage war at that time. He suggested that the Khan should leave Kalat with his companions, regroup and strengthen his forces, and then launch an attack against the British when the time was right, on 13 November 1839, the British forces launched an attack on Kalat, and a fierce battle ensued. During the fighting, Khan Mehrab Khan Baloch was martyred by a British bullet.

Among those martyred alongside him were:

Diwan Bacha Mal, Minister of Finance

Diwan Khem Chand

Diwan Asardas Mukhi, from the Hindu Panchayat of Kalat

Abdul Karim Raisani, brother of Sardar Asad Khan Raisani

Sardar Wali Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (maternal uncle of Martyr Amir Mehrab Khan)

Mir Taj Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (cousin of Mehrab Khan)

Mir Muhammad Ali Shahizai Mengal

Mir Fazal Muhammad Lehri, brother of Sardar Muhammad Khan Lehri

Sardar Zaman Khan Pandrani

Mir Dad Karim Chandozai Shahwani

Mir Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Mir Badal Khan, brother of Sardar Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Khan Muhammad Dehwaar, Arbab-e-Kalat.

Mir Nabi Bakhsh Jatoi, from the Narmak region of Kalat

Mir Qaiser Khan Bizenjo

Mir Shah Dost Bizenjo

Muhammad Raza Waziri Khel

Noor Muhammad Shahizai, son of Polat Sagaar Sarmastani, in charge of the armory

Taj Muhammad Shagasi

Sadiq Noor, son of Noor Ullah, 17 years old student from Gelli Bahot Bazar, Buleda, Turbat district, Balochistan.
On September 7, 2025, he was abducted and forcibly disappeared from his home in Absar, Turbat at 1:30 PM by Frontier Corps and Military Intelligence of the Pakistani forces in broad daylight.
After 4 months and 28 days On April 10, 2026, his lifeless body was dumped in Kech kour (Kech River), Turbat district.

data.birthPlace: Gido Sing area of Gichk, Panjgur,  Occupied Baluchistan
data.biography: Inayat Baloch was a dedicated member of the BNA unit based in Panjgur. He was recognized by the organization for his bravery during ground combat in the Paroom mountains. He was one of the five BNA members who refused to surrender during the encirclement by the SSG.

On 30 December 2023 Pakistani forces carried out a drone attack and attempted to surround a camp of BRAS in Gurandi Zeera Kaur area of Mashkay by dropping commandos through helicopters. Following professional military tactics, Baloch freedom fighters formed multiple teams to foil enemy aggression and carried several successful attacks against the advancing enemy troops. At least 7 enemy commandos were eliminated in two separate attacks, whereas, three Baloch freedom fighters, identified as Sarwar alias Duruk, Azam alias Basit and Abdul Sattar alias Maraij made ultimate sacrifices. Two freedom fighters of BRAS, Kenagi alias Muslim and Ali alias Atta, while forestalling enemy advances for hours and providing a safe route for Baloch freedom fighters, also embraced martyrdom. Both valiant fighters fought the enemy troops until their last bullets, and made the ultimate sacrifices at their own hands after running out of ammunition. The fallen comrades were affiliated with the allied organisations of BRAS. Kenagi alias Muslim, son of Martyr Shehak, a resident of Mehi, Mashkay joined BLF in 2021. He was known for his expertise in IED making. His father and more than 30 members of his family have embraced martyrdom while serving for the Baloch national struggle for freedom.

Abdul Rauf, son of Barkat, was a private school teacher and a resident of Dasht. He was killed after being accused of blasphemy by religious extremists backed Pakistani forces. A few days earlier, Abdul Rauf was accused by his students of writing insulting notes during class. Subsequently, a religious jirga was convened at a madrassa in the Malikabad area of Turbat on Saturday, ostensibly to investigate the allegations and examine Abdul Rauf’s faith, and he was summoned to appear before it. On Saturday, 5 August 2023 around 11 a.m., Abdul Rauf, along with some of his friends, was on his way to appear before the jirga to testify to his faith when he was killed by unknown armed men en route to the jirga.

On November 12, 2024, in the Balgatar area, during an organizational mission, the comrades of the organization were martyred while bravely fighting the enemy. The martyrs include Second Lieutenant Azum, alias Qasim, son of Muhammad Rahim, a resident of Teertej Awaran; Second Lieutenant Anwar, alias Sana, son of Hussain, a resident of Red Tok Balgatar; Arab Nawaz, alias Jahanzaib, a resident of Gresha; and Zaheer, alias Azad, son of Fazal, a resident of Biront Keelkor. They all sacrificed their lives in defense of their motherland.
Hayat Bewas Baloch, was a resident of the Dasht, Kech area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 13 April 2015 in Balochistan.

Jasim Baloch, alias Meraj, son of Abdullah and a resident of the Sabzap area of Panjgur District, Balochistan, joined the BLA in 2026. He served in Panjgur and Chedagi and was martyred on 10 August 2026 in the Chedagi area of Panjgur.
Martyr Jasim, alias Meraj, became part of the caravan of independence through the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army this year, with the aim of ending Pakistani occupation of Baloch land and restoring Balochistan’s independent statehood. After joining the organization, he was sent to the Panjgur front, where he successfully completed basic military courses with great interest, courage, and revolutionary spirit and became active against the enemy. After his training, he was assigned to organizational patrols, where he fully supported his fellow sangat in monitoring the enemy’s movements in the area and maintaining organizational superiority there.
Jasim served the organization for a short period, but during this time, he confronted the enemy with great courage, steadfastness, and revolutionary thought and consciousness. While remaining within the framework of the organization’s program, policies, and discipline, he inflicted considerable losses on the enemy. He was a Sarmachar who possessed the ability to fight with presence of mind on the battlefield and respond quickly in emergency situations, and he always remained mentally prepared to face all kinds of circumstances. Because of these abilities, he was assigned to important organizational patrols by the command, where he fulfilled his national and organizational responsibilities until his final moments. When enemy personnel advanced with the aim of targeting Baloch-populated areas, he, along with his fellow Sarmachars, became a shield to protect the civilian population, launched attacks against the enemy, and forced them to retreat.
Martyr Jasim, while defending the motherland and the civilian population and halting the enemy’s advance, shed his blood and sacrificed himself for the motherland. By standing firm against the enemy until his martyrdom and confronting it, he demonstrated that the sons of the Baloch homeland and its brave youth possess the capability to defend their land and national freedom and that, sooner or later, they will eliminate the enemy’s presence from Balochistan and restore their autonomy and statehood.

On January 3, 2026, in Turbat district, Balochistan, plainclothes operatives of the Pakistani intelligence agency ISI abducted 35 year old Kareem Jan, son of Malang, from Star Plus Market. He was kept in enforced disappearance for nearly a month, and on February 1, 2026, his mutilated body was dumped in the Balgatar area of Panjgur.

On 29 November 2022, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 26 November 2022, at 6:00 am, the Pakistani army fired hundreds of missiles from Iranian kamikaze drones in and around the Siakoh area of Kahan, Kohlu district of Balochistan. Out of these, two missiles fell within the premises of a BLA camp located in Siakoh. As a result, eight freedom fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army embraced martyrdom.
Afterward, the enemy launched a large scale ground and air operation in Kahan and adjoining areas. The spokesperson stated that for a long time Pakistan and Iran have maintained joint military cooperation against the Baloch national cause, including intelligence coordination. They also exchange advanced and lethal weapons.
In the first phase of the operation, following the drone attacks, several special forces commandos were dropped from around a dozen Pakistan Army combat helicopters, and shelling began from the air. Subsequently, military troops from Kohlu, Dera Bugti, and nearby areas - consisting of more than 400 personnel - participated in the operation using several armored and other military vehicles.
As soon as the Pakistani army initiated the operation, nearby BLA camps in the area began countering the enemy’s advance from different fronts by adopting a joint defense strategy.
The combat between the enemy forces and the freedom fighters continued intermittently until the evening. As a result, the freedom fighters inflicted heavy casualties on the Pakistani forces from all sides. Breaking the army’s land and air siege through skilled combat tactics, they carried their injured comrades, along with weapons and other sensitive equipment, to safe locations.
During the conflict, after several hours of fierce resistance by the fighters, the army turned its guns toward the local population in Nissau, Siakoh, Drehis, Parhki, Jantali, and adjoining areas. The enemy set fire to many houses and severely tortured residents. Meanwhile, troops stopped two innocent Baloch pedestrians and killed them.
The organization’s fighters who embraced martyrdom were - Gahmar Khan alias Garra, Thal Khan alias Thallu, Hameed Baloch alias Sado
Shadi Khan alias Kooda, Abu Bakr Baloch alias Rehan, Jameel alias Naadi
Kareem Khan alias Jamal, Muhammad Nusrat alias Asif - The organization also rejected reports claiming that BLA fighters had been arrested during the operation. Through the media, it challenged ISPR to substantiate its narrative with concrete evidence.
Hameed alias Sado joined the BLA two years ago. For the past year, he had been serving on the armed front with great bravery and devotion in Bolan, Nissau, and Kahan.

On 17 November 2024, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Army spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 25 February 2024, three members of the BLA - Mohammad Deen alias Chakar Bolani, Shoaib Shahwani alias Riaz Baloch, and Asim Kurd alias Nazir Baloch - were killed in an attack by death squads in Kahan, district Kohlu, Balochistan.
The three comrades were returning to their frontlines after completing a special organizational mission in Kahan when operatives of a death squad, lying in ambush, opened fire on them. As a result, all three members of the organization were killed.
Shoaib Shahwani alias Riaz Baloch, son of Ahmad Ali Shahwani, was a resident of Saryab Chak Shahwani Shaheed Chowk in Quetta.

data.fullName: Ghulam Qadir Marri, alias Anjeer Baloch
data.biography:
On 30 September 2024, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that they pay tribute to their six comrades - Shafo Sumalani alias Tadain, Samad Khan Chalgari Marri alias Dostain, Mohammad Gul Marri alias Waheed Baloch, Ghulam Qadir Marri alias Anjeer Baloch, Obaid Baloch alias Fida, and Taj Mohammad Chalgari Marri alias Babul - who were martyred in a bombing by jet fighters of the Pakistani Air Force in Harnai, Balochistan. On 12 September 2024, at 4 AM, jet fighters of the Pakistani Air Force dropped several heavy and deadly bombs on BLA fighters, with the support of drone surveillance, in the Ali Khan Thal area of Harnai, Balochistan. As a result of the bombing, six fighters were martyred. After the attack, the morally bankrupt enemy desecrated the bodies of the martyred fighters and took their body parts using gunship helicopters.

Ghulam Qadir Marri alias Anjeer Baloch hailed from the Nisau Jabhar area. He joined the organization in 2014 and served in Kahan, Bambur, and adjacent areas for seven years before fighting on the Bolan front for the past three years. The fighters martyred in the bombing in Harnai were on patrol under his command. His family has sacrificed for the Baloch national movement for generations; before him, three of his brothers - Shaheed Nadi Jameel Marri, Shaheed Kowda Shadi Khan Marri, and Shaheed Saubat Khan Marri - were martyred for the national cause through the platform of BLA.

On 21 February 1987, in the coastal town of Jiwani, Balochistan, Pakistani forces opened indiscriminate fire on a peaceful protest rally organized by local Baloch residents over water shortages and the demand for clean drinking water. A two year old girl, Yasmeen Baloch, along with Azgul Baloch and Ghulam Nabi Baloch, were killed, and several other demonstrators were injured.

Nasir Baloch, alias Sofi Baloch was born in the house of Master Elahi Bakhsh and Saeeda Baloch in Washbod area of Panjgur Balochistan. He affiliated with Baloch Liberation Front (BLF) since 2013. He was a 2nd lieutenant in his organization. He embraced martyrdom along with his comrade Kambar Baloch in a military clash with Pakistan Army in mountain area of Chahi Chagl, Washoob, Panjgur on Oct 22, 2021.

data.martyrdomPlace: Sorap Dam, Buleda, Turbat district, Balochistan
data.biography:
Nizar Arz Muhammad, son of Arz Muhammad, and a resident of Jahin Tehsil Paroom, Panjgur, was forcibly disappeared from Alandhoor in Buleda, Kech, On 30 September 2025, along with three other by State-Backed death squads. 

On October 1st, he has been tragically killed and his bullet-riddled body was discovered from the Sorap Dam area in Tehsil Buleda. He was a driver and engaged in cross-border trade alike many other common Baloch oil-traders. 

His enforced disappearance was reported by Baloch Yakjehti Committee (BYC) social media platforms on the early night of October 1st, 2025.
Mayar Baloch, was a resident of the Dasht, Kech area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 21 November 2017 in Balochistan.

On June 6, 2025 at around 7 AM, a large contingent of operatives from the puppet militia (Bugti Peace Force) operating under the patronage of the occupying Pakistani army and intelligence agencies, and led by the puppet Chief Minister of Balochistan, Sarfraz Bugti, launched an attack on a patrol team’s camp of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in the mountainous region of Koh Jandar, Rakhni, Barkhan.
The Sarmachars (freedom fighters) immediately adopted a defensive strategy and, after an intense battle lasting approximately three hours, successfully thwarted the enemy’s advance and encirclement attempts, managing to withdraw safely. During this clash, two members of the death squad were killed.
However, the battle did not end with this initial phase. The enemy pursued the Sarmachars and implemented a strategy to block their escape routes. A few kilometres from the site of the initial clash, the Sarmachars encountered fresh reinforcements of the occupying Pakistani army, leading to another intense confrontation. This fierce battle continued for seven hours. In this prolonged combat, four fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front embraced martyrdom and etched their names in the pages of history, while two soldiers of the occupying Pakistani army were killed and several others were severely injured.
Among the martyrs who laid down their lives in the clash with the occupying forces at Koh Jandar, Rakhni, were Rasaan Qadir (alias Rehan), Mustafa Noor (alias Diljan), Samiullah (alias Meeran), and Shahzaib (alias Shahshan).
Sarmachar Rasaan Qadir (alias Rehan), son of Qadir Bakhsh, was a resident of Dansar Labach, Awaran. Shaheed Rasaan Qadir Baloch joined the BLF in April 2023. Initially, he was assigned responsibilities in the organisation’s urban intelligence wing. An educated and experienced fighter, he efficiently fulfilled his duties within the urban network. After being exposed to enemy surveillance, the organisation transferred him to the Barkhan front in February 2025, where he quickly displayed exceptional skills in military affairs, guerrilla warfare, and frontline discipline.

On April 15, 2025, a statement issued by Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS) claimed that BRAS freedom fighters killed 22 personnel of the occupying Pakistani Army in attacks in Noshki and Barkhan (Chamalang). During these operations, the freedom fighters captured the main camp of the occupying army. In the ensuing clashes, the enemy forces were forced to retreat, and five BRAS freedom fighters were martyred while fighting the Pakistani Army.
On April 14, 2025, Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar targeted the main camp of the occupying Pakistani Army in the Galangor area of Noshki. The fighters first eliminated enemy personnel stationed at security posts in a sniper attack before launching a full-scale assault. The operation began at 9:30 p.m. and continued until 1:00 a.m., during which the freedom fighters took control of a large part of the camp.
A total of 17 personnel of the occupying Pakistani Army were killed and several others injured in the attack, while the fighters seized weapons and ammunition belonging to the enemy forces. During the final clearance of the main camp, two BRAS freedom fighters, Sangat Nazar Jan and Sangat Rauf, were martyred in clashes with the enemy army.
Martyr Sangat Yaseen, alias Rauf, son of Rahim Bakhsh, belonged to the Keshangi area of Noshki. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2022 to fight against national oppression. For a year, he dealt heavy blows to the enemy army in Noshki city and its surrounding areas as an urban guerrilla. Later, in 2023, he was transferred to the mountain front, where he used his skills on the fronts of Shoor Parod, Noshki, and Kharan, inflicting significant losses on the enemy army.
Due to his exceptional combat skills, Sangat Yaseen was appointed patrol commander. He dedicated his days and nights to striking the enemy.

On 25 October 2010, Shaheed Lala Hameed Baloch, a member of Baloch National Movement (BNM), was abducted by Pakistani forces, and on 18 November 2010 his tortured body was found in Hironk with a note reading “An Eid gift for the Baloch nation.” He was laid to rest in Gwadar, where thousands came to honor him.

On 9th December 2025, a statement issued by the Baloch Liberation Army stated that freedom fighters had targeted the Pakistani Army in three separate attacks in Mastung, Mand, and Quetta. In these operations, eleven enemy personnel were killed, and one was captured alive. During the operations, three BLA freedom fighters — Qasum Arman Baloch alias Almas, Dad Khuda Marri alias Rehan, and Uzaifa Baloch alias Ganjal — embraced martyrdom.
BLA freedom fighters ambushed enemy personnel at Zahri Ghat in the Dasht area of Mastung on 7th December 2025, when the troops were attempting to advance toward a local settlement. In this operation, eight occupying army personnel were killed on the spot, and several others were wounded. The freedom fighters also succeeded in capturing one enemy soldier, Sepoy Zafarullah, son of Jhanda Khan. During the operation, the enemy used helicopters, quadcopters, and surveillance cameras, but the fighters shot down two quadcopters and a surveillance camera through an effective strategy. The clash continued for more than two hours, during which fighter Dad Khuda Marri alias Rehan was seriously injured. Comrades tried their best to move him to a safe place, but he succumbed to his injuries.

On February 9, 2026, at approximately 5:00 PM, Murtaza, son of Yahya, a 31 year old farmer from Marap, Surab, was taken by the Frontier Corps at Mall FC Chowki on the Main RCD Road, Surab. He was forcibly disappeared without any judicial order, without being informed of any charges against him, and without being produced before any court or legal authority. From that moment, his family received no information regarding his location or condition. He entered a state of total incommunicado detention, invisible to the law, inaccessible to his family, and unaccounted for by any official institution.
Prior to the recovery of his body, the Baloch Yakjehti Committee formally submitted Murtaza’s case to the United Nations Working Group on Enforced or Involuntary Disappearances (WGEID) while he remained forcibly disappeared, urging the Working Group to communicate with the Government of Pakistan and press for the immediate disclosure of his fate and whereabouts.
On February 20, 2026, eleven days after he was taken, Murtaza’s body was recovered. His body bore visible marks of severe physical abuse, consistent with the treatment documented in numerous other cases of enforced disappearance in Balochistan, where victims are returned bearing evidence of what was done to them while in custody by Pakistani forces.

Mohammad Karim Baloch was an activist of the Baloch Students Organization - Azad (BSO-AZAD). On 14 February 2011, he was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. On 17 February 2011, his body was dumped in Quetta, Balochistan.

On May 27, 2025, Darman Baloch, son of Rahim Bakhsh, was summoned to a Frontier Corps (FC) camp in Awaran, Balochistan. He was detained, briefly released, and then forcibly disappeared shortly afterward. On the night of May 30, 2025, his mutilated body was discovered in the Kohro area of Awaran district.
Darman Baloch was the primary breadwinner for his family. He was killed by personnel of the Pakistani Frontier Corps in Jaho, Awaran.

Shakir Rahman Sasoli, alias Ashraf, son of Abdul Rasheed Sasoli, was a resident of the Killi Datto area of Mastung, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Kalat front. He was martyred on 15 July 2026 in the Naghar area of Surab, Balochistan.
Martyr Shakir, recognizing in 2026 the enemy’s onslaught and its vile designs to plunder Balochistan and maintain its dominion over the region, decided to take part in the national resistance. He joined the armed resistance of the Baloch Liberation Army and, under organizational orders, was transferred to the Kalat front. He completed the organization’s rigorous, professional, and physically demanding training, participating with full spirit and determination. Having acquired the basic qualities required for active service on the battlefield, he joined its armed operations. Within a short period, he made his mark through highly effective military actions.
He possessed a keen interest in learning combat skills and strategies and in proving himself in the field. He displayed the same revolutionary spirit and determination in combat. He remained free from hesitation on the battlefield and avoided unmilitary habits such as impatience. He was a sarmachar who possessed essential military qualities: constant movement, excellent coordination with his comrades, the ability to adapt to changing circumstances, the capacity for quick decision-making, and the ability to maintain mental composure under the harshest and most difficult conditions. He maintained these qualities until his final engagement and, working continuously alongside his comrades, countered the enemy’s military strategies, advances, and other efforts. Even during his final military engagement, he displayed great courage and valor and attained martyrdom after inflicting severe losses on the enemy.
Martyr Shakir remained faithful to his revolutionary oath and pledge, serving the homeland until the very end and fulfilling both his individual and national responsibilities to the fullest in his efforts to drive the enemy from Baloch soil. He showed the entire nation this path: rather than accepting the enemy’s occupation, one must pursue armed resistance against it in order to bring it to an end - a course he regarded as indispensable for collective survival and protection. His sacrifices will be remembered in the golden pages of national history.

Mohammad Shakir Shahwani, alias Asmatullah, son of Allah Dana, was a resident of the Killi Sarawan Pada area of Mastung. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Chagi Front. He was martyred on 31 August 2026 in the Nokcha area of Chagi District, Balochistan.
Like other young people, Mohammad Shakir Shahwani, upon becoming aware of the national reality that without an independent state, the Baloch cannot live a developed and prosperous life in any way, joined the ranks of the Baloch Liberation Army on the Shor front in 2026 as a result of this realization and became active in the field of armed resistance against the enemy. He passed the organization’s rigorous physical, mental, and psychological courses with outstanding skill and ability, quickly establishing himself as a capable and worthy fighter. After completing his training, he was deployed to the front lines, where he carried out his duties to the highest standard until the end.
Shakir Shahwani took part in numerous military operations against the enemy and inflicted heavy losses on them. There was a seriousness in his demeanor and a profound maturity in his thinking, which he always proved through his actions and conduct. His inherent combat skills always set him apart. He sacrificed himself in the cause of national freedom, joining the ranks of those great freedom fighters who gave their lives for the liberation of the homeland, the prosperity of the Baloch people, and the restoration of the independent status of the State of Balochistan, and emerged victorious in history.

Yahya Baloch was a Baloch Students Organization - Azad (BSO-Azad) activist who was brutally murdered by Pakistani Frontier Corps forces during a raid on his house in the Tootak area of Khuzdar district, Balochistan, on 18 February 2011.
Rasheed Baloch was a resident of the Buleda area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 11 December 2015 in Balochistan.

On June 4, 2025, at around 2 PM, in the area of Killi Safar Ali Jungle in Dukki, Balochistan, the Pakistani forces’ agency, the Counter Terrorism Department, raided a house and took into custody 20 year old Mohammad Fareed Baloch, son of Mohammad Anwar, forcibly disappearing him. After being illegally held in enforced disappearance for eight months, he was extrajudicially killed on February 6, 2026, and his mutilated body was dumped.

data.biography:
Rehan Baloch (15 June 1998 – 11 August 2018) was a Baloch fidayee of the Majeed Brigade, Baloch Liberation Army, and the son of the organization’s founding commander in chief, Martyr General Aslam Baloch.
Born in Quetta (Shaal), Rehan belonged to one of Balochistan’s most prominent revolutionary families, with several relatives holding key positions in pro independence organizations. His father, General Aslam Baloch, led the BLA until his martyrdom in December 2018.
Rehan left formal education while in 8th grade and, at the age of thirteen, formally joined the Baloch Liberation Army on 1 January 2012. He later volunteered for the Majeed Brigade, the BLA’s elite unit for self sacrificial operations.
On 11 August 2018, at the age of twenty, Rehan Baloch carried out a suicide attack targeting a bus carrying Chinese engineers at Dalbandin, Chagai district, Balochistan. He attained martyrdom in the operation, becoming one of the youngest fidayeen of the Majeed Brigade.

Munir Ahmad, alias Abdul Baseer, was a resident of Zehri. He joined the BLA in 2025, served on the Washuk front, and was martyred on 7 August 2026 in the Washuk area of Balochistan. Martyr Maulana Munir Ahmad had become well-versed in his national and religious duties, and it was this thought and ideology that convinced him to embrace the struggle for national liberation. Last year, he made the historic decision to join the revolutionary and operational ranks of the Baloch Liberation Army and became active on the battlefield. After completing basic training and programmes, he stepped into the harsh practical arena of war and took part in various combat operations against the enemy. He proved himself on the battlefield to be a steadfast, courageous and powerful fighter. He faced the battlefield and the trials of war head-on, displayed high morale in every engagement, and left a heroic impact on the enemy. He also took part in the historic battle of Operation Herof II in the Baloch national liberation war against the enemy, where, alongside his fellow fighters, he inflicted a historic defeat on the enemy, the effects of which will remain for years to come. Throughout his entire period of warfare, he proved himself to be a guerrilla fighter of the highest calibre, demonstrating exceptional steadfastness at every turn and continuing to cause destruction to the enemy. He was fully aware of the art of making the best use of resources on the battlefield, and his strategy was aimed at inflicting maximum damage on the enemy with limited resources. During his two-year period of warfare, Martyr Maulana Munir Ahmad joined the ranks of those great revolutionaries who remained steadfast in the struggle for the freedom of their homeland and nation until their final breath. His sacrifices demand that people from every class and school of thought should become part of this great struggle, which symbolises service to humanity and a better future. His sacrifices will be written in golden letters in the pages of history.

Inayatullah Bangulzai, alias Bawal, son of Rahmatullah Bangulzai, was a resident of the Sarkhin area of Kalat, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in May 2025 and served on the Nagaho and Kalat fronts. He was martyred on 18 August 2026 in the Hajikeh area of Surab, Balochistan.
Martyr Inayatullah Bangulzai made the national and ideological decision to join the Baloch Liberation Army last year and was transferred to the Nagaho front. After completing basic military courses, he took part in numerous military operations and played an outstanding individual role in blockades and in establishing organizational dominance in the relevant areas against the enemy. He was a Sarmachar who displayed exceptional organizational discipline during patrols, combining the qualities of a guerrilla fighter with professional military conduct. These abilities stayed with him to the very end, always setting him apart.
He took part in various combat operations and in each one fully demonstrated his military prowess, delivering heavy blows to the enemy on multiple occasions. His combat skills proved a lesson to the enemy on several occasions. He was not only a strong soldier on the battlefield but also a comrade imbued with revolutionary zeal and thought. He maintained strong and revolutionary ties with his fellow revolutionaries, was always ready to assist his comrade fighters, and upheld the highest ethical and professional conduct toward the people. He was one of those Sarmachar who carried out every responsibility of the organization, large or small, with the utmost sincerity and in a timely manner.
Remaining loyal to the cause of national liberation until the very end, he embraced martyrdom during an encounter with the occupying forces at Surab and became immortal in history. The sacrifice of Martyr Inayatullah Bangulzai is a continuation of the sacrifices of those martyrs which will continue until the establishment of a free and sovereign state of Balochistan.

Faqeer Mohammad Ajiz Shahwani, a 30 year old poet, son of Abdul Qadir, was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 22 September 2010. His body was later dumped on 22 October 2010 in the Ghanja Dori area of Mastung.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, the BLA’s Majeed Brigade Fidayeen targeted the main camp and the Coast Guard camp of the Pakistan Navy in the coastal city of Pasni, Balochistan. The operation was initiated by Fazal, alias Miraan, who rammed a vehicle loaded with explosives into the main entrance gate of the Navy camp. The explosion instantly killed at least seven personnel stationed at the gate.
Immediately after this initial attack, six Fidayeen - Yasma Baloch, alias Zareena; Waseem Baloch, alias Zirbaar; Zaid Zamurani, alias Abram; Sabzal Baloch, alias Kohsar; Diljan Baloch, alias Ameer Ajoo; and Operation Commander Shabeer Baloch, alias Kiya - entered the camp and took up positions. Fierce clashes with the occupying Navy and Navy special units inside the camp continued for more than five hours, during which at least 33 Pakistani personnel were killed. This operation not only inflicted significant casualties on the enemy but also dealt a severe blow to the defense structure of the Navy camp.
Yasma Baloch aka Zareena, and Waseem Baloch aka Zirbar, were husband and wife from Alandoor, Buleda, and Kallahdar, Zamuran.
Yasma Baloch, born on 14 February 1997 in Alandoor, Buleda, joined the Baloch Liberation Army’s Majeed Brigade in 2022.
Waseem Baloch, born on 27 April 1992 in Kallahdar, Zamuran, became active in the movement in 2014 and joined the Majeed Brigade in 2022.
They shared a marriage before they shared a final stand. Yasma Baloch and Waseem Baloch, husband and wife, sacrificed their lives together while attacking the occupying forces' camp in Pasni. Their story is not only about death, but about how private life and national duty fully converged, turning a partnership into a symbol of shared commitment and resistance. Two individuals bound by partnership and a shared decision to give everything for what they believed the freedom of their motherland demanded.

Ghulam Jan Baloch, son of Sheehy Baloch and a resident of Tejaban, Kech, was a shepherd from a poor family. He was abducted by Pakistani forces on July 29, 2021, and the following day, on July 30, his body was returned to his family.

Obaid Baloch, alias Sanjar / Baam, son of Pervaiz Baloch, was born in 2005. He was a resident of Chah Sar, Turbat District, Balochistan.
Obaid Baloch joined the Baloch Liberation Army in June 2025 and became part of the Majeed Brigade in November 2025. On 31 January 2026, during Operation Herof, he carried out a VBIED fidayee attack on the army camp located in Tump Rodban.
In a short span of time, his path came to reflect not momentary passion but steadfast resolve and conscious commitment. He took every step with full awareness of its consequences and with a deep sense of responsibility. In the end, he did not dedicate a single act, but his entire life to a cause he chose with clarity and upheld with quiet conviction.

Najeeb Baloch, son of Karam Dad and a resident of the Badai area of Zamuran in Turbat district, Balochistan, was abducted on 26 September 2015 from Kech by Frontier Corps (FC) and Pakistani state intelligence agencies in front of many people.
His body was found the next day, on 27 September 2015, in the Kaisaak area of Turbat. He was a signboard painter by profession.

Qamber Aslam, a 12-year-old boy and son of Aslam Baloch, was shot in the chest and killed by personnel of the Federal Constabulary (FC) while working in his family’s farmland in Kolwah, Aashal Dandar, district Awaran.
The incident took place on the morning of July 18, 2025, as Qamber was sowing onion seeds near his home. A patrolling unit of the FC opened direct fire, fatally striking the child.

data.biography:
On 28 June 2026, the spokesperson for the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) issued a statement announcing that five fighters of the organisation - Shoaib Zehri, alias Farooq; Zakariya Zehri, alias Ustad Zoreen Baloch; Kifayatullah Badini, alias Badil Baloch; Captain Hashum Baloch, alias Kambar; and Abdul Rahim, alias Ustad Imran - had embraced martyrdom. The statement said that the blood of the martyrs guarantees Baloch national survival and sovereignty.

Kifayatullah Badini was martyred on May 14, 2026, in the Abbad area of Nushki when he was targeted in a drone strike by the occupying army.
Kifayatullah Badini began his struggle in April 2024 under the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front. Before formally transferring to the mountain front, he received basic training in organizational and political discipline, as well as military principles. After completing this ideological training, he formally joined the mountain front.
He was an extremely resilient and sincere fighter with deep knowledge of military principles and battlefield tactics. He carried out guerrilla operations on the difficult fronts around Nushki and Shaal and diligently fulfilled his organizational duties. Through his tireless efforts, organizational discipline, and high political consciousness, he earned a respected and dignified position within the organization's ranks.
On May 14, the fighters' unit was on patrol in the Abbad area of Nushki as part of an organizational duty when the occupying army launched a drone strike on them. As a result, Kifayatullah Badini, alias Badil Baloch, son of Habibullah Badini and a resident of Saryab Road, Quetta, was martyred.

On 9 May 2026, the spokesperson for the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) Gwahram Baloch issued a statement saying that on 4 May 2026, fighters of the organization were conducting a routine patrol in Washuk when they suddenly came face to face with the occupying Pakistani army. The fighters immediately adopted effective guerrilla warfare tactics, swiftly dividing into different units and launching attacks on the enemy. As a result of this strategy, three enemy personnel were killed and several others were wounded.

During the clash, a BLF fighter was injured, yet he continued to confront the enemy with steadfastness. Two fighters, Captain Mukhtiyar Baloch, alias Peerak Baloch, and Gareeb Shah, alias Irfan Baloch, held their positions and kept enemy units engaged, blocking their advance so that their fellow fighters could safely withdraw from the area. Due to their courageous strategy, all other fighters successfully reached their safe bases. Both fighters continued fighting until their last bullet and breath, ultimately embracing martyrdom.

Gareeb Shah, alias Irfan Baloch, son of Nasir Baloch, was a resident of Mashkay Gazzi. He joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in May 2024 for the survival of the Baloch nation and the liberation of the homeland. In a short period, through his dedication, hard work, and sense of duty, he proved himself to be an exceptional fighter. He fought on the frontlines in various battles in Mashkay and Jhao, and fulfilled his organizational responsibilities at camp with exemplary conduct. On 4 May 2026, in the area of Washuk, while bravely fighting enemy forces alongside his fellow commander, Captain Peerak Baloch, he also embraced martyrdom.

Hassan Baloch, the 16-year-old son of Jumma Baloch and a resident of Rekbazar, Mand, was subjected to enforced disappearance by the Frontier Corps (FC) while travelling from Mand to Tump. He was taken away in broad daylight in the afternoon near the Aziyaan area.

After 41 days of disappearance, Hassan’s body was found dumped in Mukahndar, Mand, Kech, on 14 October 2026. Hassan was a young shepherd who lived a simple life and worked hard to make a living.
