Nadir Bangulzai, alias Shay Mureed, son of Nawab Khan Bangulzai, was a resident of Spilenji. He joined the BLA in 2025 and later became part of the Majeed Brigade. He served on the Nagaho front and was martyred in Mastung.
After joining the organization, Nadir Bangulzai, alias Shay Mureed, was transferred to the Nagaho front. There, Shay Mureed carried forward the tradition of resistance and remained steadfast in the struggle against the enemy. His personality reflected determination, fearlessness, and a deep commitment to his nation. Inspired by this national consciousness, he decided to join the Majeed Brigade. This decision was not merely the choice of a path, but a pledge to his homeland and his people.
During Operation Herof Phase II, Fidayee Nadir Baloch sacrificed his life while fighting on the Mastung front for the great cause of freedom. In doing so, he inscribed his name into the tradition of sacrifice that forms the very essence of Baloch resistance history.

Martyr Masood Baloch, alias Balach son of Mohammad Usman Baloch and was a resident of Kohn Zangi area of Panjgur, Balochistan. According organizational statement;  He became part of Baloch liberation movement in the platform of Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in 2022.  He embraced martyrdom in Panjgur during an unfortunate incident. On 8th October, Masood alias Balach was preparing an IED for an operation when he embraced martyrdom due to a premature explosion. He was a hardworking and committed fighter, and his absence will be felt forever.

Younus Sabzal, alias Malguzar, son of Sabzal Bizenjo, was a resident of the Sahib Dad Bazaar area of Dasht, Dade, Kech. He joined the BLA on 5 February 2025 and served on the Seyahji, Kulbar, and Zamuran fronts. He was martyred on 1 September 2026 in the Dasht area of Kech District, Balochistan.
Younus Sabzal, an active Sarmachar on the Seyahji, Kulbar, and Zamuran fronts for the past two years, was an extremely capable, brave, and fearless fighter, who withstood the intense hardships of war with revolutionary zeal over the past year and constantly troubled the enemy on the front lines with his actions, combat skills, and abilities. He had participated in numerous military operations and actions against the enemy, where he inflicted heavy losses on them. He was wounded in the historic Operation Herhof II, and after recovering from his injuries he rejoined the front. 
These combat skills of Younus Sabzal were used against the enemy with the same intensity until the very end. He served on various fronts in Makuran, and on every front, he fulfilled his responsibilities admirably. He actively participated in organizational activities in various areas of Kech and attained the great rank of martyrdom during a bloody clash with the enemy on September 1. Throughout this period, Younus Sabzal remained bound by organizational discipline and made invaluable sacrifices for national freedom. His sacrifices will always be remembered in Baloch national history, and in the pages of history he will be remembered as a brave fighter who gave his life for the freedom of his homeland.

data.biography: Early Life and Education Imdad Bojair was born on December 1, 1982, in the village of Kehken, Turbat (Kech), into the home of Bojair Baloch. As the eldest of six siblings, he grew up with a strong sense of responsibility. He received his primary education at the Government Primary School in Kehken and completed his matriculation at the Government High School in Shahrak, Turbat, in 1997. He pursued higher studies at the Atta Shad Degree College in Turbat, earning his FA degree in 1999 and a Bachelor of Arts (BA) in 2005. In 2000, his family relocated from Kehken to Daki Bazar, Absar, which would later become the site of his political and intellectual activities. Intellectual and Literary Contributions Imdad Bojair was a dedicated intellectual who believed in the power of education and literature to raise national consciousness. Writings: Using the pen name "Bahad Baloch," he was a prolific writer, contributing articles to the daily newspaper Daily Tawar and Asaap magazine. His work focused on organizational literature and the socio-political conditions of his people. Warna Library: In a commitment to promoting literacy, he established the "Warna Library" in his own home. This library became a community hub where local youth gathered daily for study and intellectual discussion. Political Career Imdad Bojair began his formal political journey in 2009 when he joined the Baloch National Movement (BNM), a nationalist mass party. He served the organization in various capacities within the Turbat Zone. Known for his organizational skills and dedication, he eventually rose to become a region leader and organizer for the Kech region, a position he held until his death. Martyrdom On August 14, 2013, Frontier Corps (FC) and security agencies conducted a raid on his residence in Absar. During this operation, Imdad Bojair was assassinated alongside Raza Jahangeer Baloch, the Central General Secretary of BSO-Azad. His martyrdom is commemorated by his supporters as a significant loss to both the intellectual and political wings of the Baloch movement. Personal Life Imdad Bojair married his cousin, Banul Baloch, on August 17, 2003. He is survived by his three children: two daughters, Fatima and Mahnaz, and a son, Mehroz Baloch.

Yasir Baloch, son of Baloch Khan, was a 19 year old student from Minaz, Buleda. On 2 March 2026, Frontier Corps soldiers of the Pakistani forces abducted him from his home in Buleda, and he was forcibly disappeared. After 7 months and 18 days, his body was found dumped alongside body of Mehran Baloch in Sohlo Kour, Buleda, Balochistan.

Abubakr Baloch, alias Durra, son of Ismail Baloch, was a resident of Sand-e-Sar, Isai, Panjgur district of Balochistan. He joined the BLA in March 2022, was deployed to the mountain fronts in November 2023, and joined the Majeed Brigade in September 2024. He was educated as a software engineer at Iqra University, Karachi.
Abubakr Baloch, known by his alias Durra, belonged to a generation that chose its path not out of impulse but out of conscious conviction. Trained as a software engineer, he understood the intersection between modern technology, organizational structure, and resistance strategy. After joining the BLA in March 2022, he committed himself to the organization in a disciplined and methodical manner. His role was not confined to military training alone; he also became part of the BLA’s media wing, Hakkal, where he contributed to media operations. His involvement in writing, communication, and narrative development reflected his understanding that the struggle is not limited to the battlefield but extends equally to intellectual and informational fronts.
In November 2023, he was deployed to the mountain front, serving on the Bolan front under some of the most demanding operational conditions. He was among those fighters who carried responsibilities quietly yet emerged at the forefront during decisive moments. His participation in Operation Dara-e-Bolan 1 and Operation Herof 1, followed by his joining the Majeed Brigade in September 2024 and his presence on the front line during the Jaffar Express hijacking, were all part of a progression in which his responsibilities steadily increased.
During Operation Herof II, he fought on the Dalbandin front and embraced martyrdom during clashes at the military camp. Durra’s life represents the image of a young man who carried both intellect and arms with equal responsibility, integrating knowledge, organization, and action into a single, coherent commitment.

On the night of 29 June 2025, Pakistani military personnel, along with its backed death squad, raided the village of Khandari in Mashkay and abducted an Elderly man Qadir Bakhsh, son of Arzi. Just hours after his abduction, his bullet-riddled body bearing signs of torture was discovered dumped nearby.

Yasir Nasir, son of Haji Nasir Ababagr, was born in 1992 in Mand, district Kech, Balochistan. He was a resident of district Gwadar, Balochistan. He received his early education from his hometown and was a student of FSc at Atta Shad Degree College, Turbat, and a member of BSO Azad.
He believed in political struggle and was targeted for his peaceful political expression. He played a key role in mobilizing Baloch youth to join the Baloch liberation struggle for the independence of their homeland. He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he remained with the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom.
He had a keen interest in reading revolutionary literature of oppressed nations. He was abducted on 16 October 2010 by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agencies from Sur Bandan, Gwadar, and his case was registered at the Gwadar police station. His bullet-riddled body was found dumped on 8 April 2011 alongside the body of Qambar Chakar in Murghap, district Kech, Balochistan. His body bore extreme signs of torture.
He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a very young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

Saeed Mohammad, the 49-year-old son of Shahoo Baloch and a shopkeeper from Panwan, Jiwani, was abducted from his home on 9 December 2025 at around 3:00 AM and forcibly disappeared. From that night onward, his family was denied any information about his whereabouts. He was never brought before a court, never given the right to defend himself, and his family was left in endless uncertainty.
On 3 May 2026, after 145 days, his dead body was found dumped in the Nalent area of Balochistan.

Manzoor Baloch, son of Nabi Dad, was only 17 years old - a child and an eighth-grade student at the Boys High School in Kolwahi Bazaar, Absar. On July 8, 2025, at around 1:00 a.m., he was forcibly taken from his home. A minor was made to disappear in the darkness of the night.
For nine months, his family searched for him. His father visited the DC office again and again, begging for justice: “If my son has committed any crime, bring him before a court. He is just a child.” No evidence was presented. No court hearing was held. There was only silence.
On February 26, 2026, his body was found dumped in Kech Kor, Turbat. Instead of justice, his parents were handed his lifeless body during the sacred month of Ramadan.
Abdul Baqi Baloch was killed by Pakistani forces in Bolan, Balochistan, on 3 March 2009.

Sumaiya Qalandarani Baloch (1998 – 24 June 2023) was a Baloch journalist, media strategist, and fidayee (self sacrificing fighter) of the Baloch Liberation Army’s elite Majeed Brigade.
Born in Tootak, Khuzdar district, Balochistan, Sumaiya was the daughter of Ubaid Qalandrani and granddaughter in law of General Aslam Baloch, the founding leader of the BLA. Her family suffered heavily under state repression: on 18 February 2011, her grandfather, several uncles, and cousins were among those forcibly disappeared from Tootak, an incident that profoundly shaped her path.
At the age of eighteen, in 2016, Sumaiya joined the Baloch Liberation Army. For the first five years she served in the organisation’s media wing, where her education and intellect helped significantly strengthen its outreach and effectiveness. In 2019, she voluntarily transferred to the Majeed Brigade, the BLA’s special unit for high risk self sacrificing operations. Over the next four years she underwent intensive training while being repeatedly offered the opportunity to reconsider her decision and ensure it was free of any external pressure or emotional impulse. She remained resolute.
On 24 June 2023, at the age of twenty-five, Sumaiya Qalandarani Baloch, known within the organisation as Sumaiya Baloch, carried out a successful fidayee attack and attained martyrdom. She was engaged to fellow Majeed Brigade fidayee Rehan Baloch at the time of her death.
Remembered as a highly educated, determined, and selfless fighter, Sumaiya is immortalised in Baloch resistance history as one of the few women to undertake a Majeed Brigade operation.

Azmat Rind, son of Ameer Bakhsh Rind and a resident of Dera Murad Jamali, was forcibly disappeared on June 5, 2025, in broad daylight near Sabzi Mandi, Naseerabad. On July 9, his family was informed by Pakistani military forces that he had succumbed to injuries sustained in custody.
Azmat was reportedly subjected to severe torture and extrajudicially killed while in illegal detention. In a further act of inhumanity, his body was clandestinely buried by the forces in a deserted area of Chatar, Naseerabad—denying his family the right to a proper religious and cultural burial.

Swearing upon the Qur’an as a solemn guarantee, the state of Pakistan sent a jirga to negotiate with Nawab Noroz Khan. Trusting the sanctity of the Qur’an as a binding assurance, Nawab Noroz Khan descended from the mountains along with his son, Battay Khan, and his companions. However, rather than engaging in meaningful negotiations or addressing their legitimate demands, the state - consistent with its pattern of duplicity - arrested them.
Nawab Noroz Khan was sentenced to life imprisonment, while his son and several of his companions were condemned to death and executed in the prisons of Sukkur and Hyderabad in Sindh.
When the armed fighters came down from the mountains, they kissed the Qur’an and declared, 'We offer ourselves in its name, but we will not surrender our weapons.' The official delegation repeatedly invoked the Qur’an to reassure them that the government would honor its commitments, insisting that no greater guarantee could exist than the Holy Book itself. Yet once they had descended, those promises were broken, and they were taken into custody. They were confined in harsh prison cells dating back to the British colonial period.
Four companions of Nawab Noroz Khan - Bhawal Khan, Masti Khan, Jamal Khan, and Wali Mohammad - were hanged in Hyderabad Jail, Sindh on 15 July 1960. Their bodies were received by Mir Rasool Bakhsh, the paternal uncle of Mir Mohammad Ali Talpur. After the funeral rites were performed, the martyrs were transported to their ancestral homeland for burial.
Nawab Noroz Khan’s son, Mir Battay Khan, along with Sabzal Khan and Ghulam Rasool, was executed in Sukkur Jail, Sindh on 15 July 1960.
Nawab Nauroz Khan himself passed away on 25 December 1965 at Civil Hospital Hyderabad, Sindh, while in custody. His body was received by Mir Rafique Ahmed. Following the funeral rites, Mir Rasool Bakhsh arranged for his body to be transported to his ancestral place.
His youngest son, Jalal Khan, remained imprisoned until 1970. He was spared execution because he was a minor at the time of his arrest.
Nawab Noroz Khan and the seven martyrs were laid to rest in the Chashma area of Kalat District, a few kilometres from Kalat Bazaar in Balochistan.
Bhawal Khan Musiyni was born in 1930 in the Bulbul Zehri area of Khuzdar district. He joined the Khan of Kalat National Militia, which remained his first and only job. He was executed at the age of 30.

On 15 May 2026, a press statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that the Sarmachars (freedom fighters) of the Baloch Liberation Army carried out eighteen successful operations against the enemy across Balochistan between 4 May 2026 and 14 May 2026, resulting in the deaths of 31 personnel of the occupying Pakistani army, including a Major-rank officer, while several others were seriously injured. These attacks included seven powerful IED strikes. Additionally, the Sarmachars seized control of main highways for hours at various locations, targeting vehicles belonging to exploitative companies and occupying forces, and detaining individuals associated with these companies. In these coordinated operations, seven personnel and operatives of the state-backed “Death Squads” and Military Intelligence (MI) were also killed.
During intense clashes with the occupying forces at various locations, five BLA fighters - Ali Jan Siahpad alias Sudais, Ehsanullah alias Master Maran, Nasrullah alias Mama Zagreen, Tanveer Mengal alias Murad Khan, and Saadullah Baloch alias Wajid - embraced martyrdom while fighting valiantly against the enemy.
Ehsanullah Nichari, alias Master Mahran, son of Haji Ali Ahmed, was a resident of the Mangochar area of Kalat District, Balochistan. He graduated in Political Science from Minhaj University Lahore and joined the Balochistan Liberation Army in November 2025. He served on the Shoorparod and Kalat fronts and was martyred on 10 May 2026 in the Chapar area of Kalat.
Ehsanullah Nichari, alias Master Mahran, was an intelligent and capable student of Political Science. He had a deep understanding of international and regional politics and global complexities, and this intellectual awareness led him toward armed struggle for Baloch national interests and demands. He understood the regional and global situation and recognized the importance of armed struggle in establishing Baloch national power. He was aware that failure to achieve and establish national power could expose the nation’s existence to serious threats amid future regional and international conflicts.
With a deep understanding of armed struggle and the importance of military strength, he chose the Shoorparod front, where he completed rigorous and professional military training and later participated in several armed clashes on the ground. He did not limit his understanding of power to ideology alone, but also took practical steps toward building Baloch national strength.
His martyrdom is presented as a manifestation of this conscious ideology: that without national power, collective survival and existence cannot be safeguarded under any circumstances. He was martyred on 10 May at the Kalat front while fighting the enemy in defence of the homeland and for freedom.

Ismail Baloch, son of Elahi Bakhsh, a 25 year old labourer by profession and a resident of Baghbana, Khuzdar, was abducted and forcibly disappeared on November 18, 2025, by a Pakistani forces backed death squad from the main RCD Road in Surab. Armed men of the death squad stopped Ismail on the roadside, abducted him and took him to an unknown location. After his enforced disappearance, no information was provided about his condition or whereabouts, leaving his family in anguish. On November 19, 2025, Ismail’s body was recovered from the Baghbana area of Khuzdar. The body bore multiple bullet wounds, confirming that he had been extrajudicially killed while in custody.
Maqbool Baloch, was a resident of the Anjira, Khuzdar area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 3 February 2016 in Balochistan.

The first unit, which included Fidayeen Hawa Baloch (alias Droshum), Yahya Lal (alias Lashari), Adnan Arman (alias Changaiz), and Yousif Baloch (alias Yagi), attacked the compound of the occupying Pakistani intelligence agencies, resulting in the elimination of 12 personnel. Women and children in residential quarters near the compound were provided safe passage; however, the occupying army later martyred these same civilians by opening fire.
About forty minutes later, occupying forces advanced toward the compound, leading to clashes that continued until the evening. In these clashes, more than 24 personnel were eliminated, and three military vehicles, including an armored vehicle, were destroyed.
The second squad, which included Fidayeen Kambar Ismail (alias Sarbaz), Khurshid KB (alias Arman), Waseem Baloch (alias Kareem), Shoaib Baloch (alias Shehzad), and Yasir, took up strong positions in Port Bazaar near Gwadar Port. After announcements were made in mosques, freedom fighters went to the bazaar, met the public, and held political discussions. After repelling the advance of occupying forces in the city, the freedom fighters later advanced toward the port and fired several rockets that hit their targets. Clashes continued until the next day, eliminating more than 19 personnel.
Yousif Baloch, alias Yagi, son of Ishaq, was a 21 year old known for his steadfastness and deep commitment to his cause. He maintained morale even under the most difficult circumstances and consistently stood shoulder to shoulder with his fellow Sarmachars. His personality was defined by discipline, resilience, and the ability to make timely decisions in accordance with changing battlefield conditions. These qualities distinguished him as a responsible and dependable presence in combat.
He remained actively engaged on the Parom and Panjgur fronts, where he participated in multiple combat engagements against the occupying Pakistani forces and carried out his organizational responsibilities with dedication and consistency. Yousif also took part in Operation Heirof II on the Gwadar front. In Gwadar, alongside his fellow fighters, he fought a prolonged and coordinated battle. His participation and courageous rol

On September 13, 2025, clashes broke out between Baloch Raaji Ajoi Sangar (BRAS) freedom fighters and the Pakistani army in the Kotan area of Zamuran while the freedom fighters were on patrol. In these clashes, four enemy army personnel were killed and several others were injured, while two freedom fighters, Sudeer alias Bramsh and Islam alias Sagaar, were martyred.

Martyr Sangat Islam alias Sagaar, son of Atta Muhammad, belonged to the Tanak area of Maskay. Islam alias Sagaar, who studied at LUAWMS University Uthal, joined the Baloch Liberation Army earlier this year and was active on the Panjgur front.

Martyr Sangat Sudeer Baloch alias Barmash, son of Pir Jan, was a resident of the Sri Kahan area of Tump, though he originally belonged to Zamuran. He joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in November last year and served on the Zamuran, Mand, and Tump fronts.
Abdul Ghaffar, was a resident of the Anjira, Khuzdar area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 26 March 2013 in Balochistan.

Javed Akhtar, son of Master Akhtar Baloch, was born in December 1983 in Buleda, District Kech. He was a student of Intermediate and later completed his B.A. at Atta Shad Degree College, Turbat. He also served as the president of BSO Azad, Buleda Zone.
Javed Akhtar believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising his right to peaceful political expression. He was shot by the Pakistan Army during a public gathering in Buleda on August 27, 2011. The gathering had been organized by BSO Azad activists and other Baloch youth in response to the killing of the Baloch leader Nawab Akbar Bugti.
He was attacked by security forces in front of hundreds of people and was later shifted to Karachi for medical treatment, but he did not survive.
He was a hardworking member of the organization and played an important role in organizing Baloch youth under the banner of BSO Azad in his area. At a young age, he joined BSO Azad and actively participated in its activities.
He was killed for the ‘crime’ of being a Baloch youth who spoke out for the lawful demand for freedom for his motherland and for being a member of the Baloch Students Organization Azad.

On 22 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch stated that BLF fighters had formally launched Operation Almas with a large-scale, coordinated attack on the main camp of the Pakistani army’s Frontier Works Organization (FWO) at Gwadar Zero Point. Fighters from the BLF’s special Saddo Operational Battalion, alongside members of other units, are participating in this major military engagement. The battle continued into the following day, 23 October 2026, with loud explosions and intense gunfire heard from the location. On 23 October 2026, a statement issued by the BLF spokesperson announced the completion of Operation Almas. The statement claimed that dozens of military and intelligence personnel had been killed, the hub of colonial projects had been destroyed, and army and Frontier Corps posts had been wiped out. It declared that the historic Operation Almas had concluded after achieving all its intended objectives. Operation Almas was carried out in Gwadar and the surrounding areas. It has formally concluded after reportedly achieving all its planned strategic, military, and economic objectives following prolonged and intense clashes. During this wide-ranging operation, the occupying Pakistani army and intelligence network suffered what the statement described as irreparable human and material losses. The BLF’s self-sacrificing fighters targeted the Frontier Works Organization’s (FWO) main camp, destroying a key centre for the implementation of colonial projects, particularly in Gwadar and across Makuran. This, the statement asserted, demonstrated to the world that, without the will and consent of the Baloch nation, colonial projects in Balochistan would never be safe. The offices and camps of Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) and Military Intelligence (MI) inside the FWO’s main camp were also targeted by the organisation’s fighters. Several soldiers, including senior officers, were reportedly killed in the attacks. Throughout Operation Almas, the Jind-Nadr Sarmachars not only thwarted every counterattack by the occupying army, every attempt by armoured vehicles to advance, and every reinforcement convoy, but also forced them to retreat, maintaining control of the camp for twenty hours. As a result of the actions of the Saddo Operational Battalion’s fighters during Operation Almas, Military Intelligence (MI) officers, Special Services Group (SSG) personnel, and dozens of regular army personnel were reportedly killed. In addition, the enemy’s main camp, posts, internal barracks, and administrative offices were reportedly destroyed in explosions and attacks. A number of the occupying army’s armoured vehicles, along with surveillance drones and quadcopters, were also reportedly destroyed during the operation. After repeatedly inflicting defeats on the occupying enemy during Operation Almas, the Jind-Nadr Sarmachars of the Saddo Operational Battalion, adhering to the philosophy of the last bullet, sacrificed their lives in the struggle for freedom, adding a new chapter of bravery to Baloch national history. The following Jind-Nadr Sarmachars played key roles in the operation: Khalid, alias Zamur; Bilqees Didag, alias Almas; Hamidullah, alias Badil; Shakeel, alias Sohrab; Majeed Zaib, alias Aftab; Nasir Ali, alias Nodan; Mujahid Mehr, alias Sagar Zamurani; and Barat, alias Safar Jan. All eight were reported to have embraced martyrdom during this historic operation. On 27 October 2026, the spokesperson issued another detailed statement, announcing that BLF special units had carried out a comprehensive, coordinated, organized, and effective attack on the centres of the occupying Pakistani army, the colonial intelligence network, and exploitative institutions in Gwadar. The statement claimed that more than 80 military and intelligence personnel had been killed; several armoured vehicles, the main army barracks, and intelligence offices had been destroyed; four quadcopters and two surveillance drones had been shot down; and a police station had been seized. It also reported that operations had been conducted at Gabd and Rimdan 250. Following these deadly blows to the state's exploitative structures, Operation Almas was declared successfully concluded. The spokesperson stated that the BLF was formally presenting to the nation, subjugated peoples, and the international community a comprehensive account of the far-reaching military and political achievements of Operation Almas. The historic, organized, effective, coordinated, and comprehensive operation was launched at 4:00 p.m. on 22 October 2026 against the occupying Pakistani state apparatus in Gwadar and the adjoining coastal region. The operation was described as the most organized, coordinated, and far-reaching attack to date against the occupying Pakistani state, its usurping army, intelligence network, exploitative economic institutions, and local puppet administration. It was presented as an expression of the organization's resolve and capabilities. The revolutionary participation of fearless Baloch women, standing shoulder to shoulder with men in the struggle for Baloch national freedom, national survival, and the defence of the coast and its resources, was portrayed as heralding the end of the usurping colonizer. This historic operation was named after the BLF's fearless and courageous guerrilla commander, Almas Baloch. For the past eight years, Commander Almas had been actively involved in the armed national struggle under the BLF banner, driven by her ideological convictions. Bilqees Didag, alias Almas, daughter of Allah Bakhsh Didag, resident of Dasht Kumbel, is a shining chapter of courage, steadfastness and revolutionary sacrifice. She spent her early life in ordinary circumstances and received regular education up to the eighth grade. She was married and has a beloved daughter, but rising above herself and her family circle, she made the cause of the motherland's freedom her whole life. In 2018 she formally joined the armed struggle for national freedom through BLF's revolutionary platform. After joining the organization, she served for four years as a volunteer in the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB), rendering highly valuable and arduous service. For the past eight years Shaheed Almas had been fully active and ideologically committed in the armed defense struggle through the BLF platform. During her organizational life she served as a very active and fearless member of the intelligence wing in sensitive and difficult areas such as Dasht, Turbat and Gwadar. She kept herself in motion day and night to deliver vital intelligence about the enemy to the organization in time. During military fronts and operations, she always carried out, with courage and steadfastness, the very difficult and dangerous responsibility of delivering supplies, weapons and logistics to the sarmachars across Dasht's harsh and rugged mountain ranges. On the path of her revolutionary struggle, the occupying Pakistani army and operatives of the state's death squads made every effort to obstruct her. The occupying army repeatedly attempted to abduct her, hold her in illegal detention and break her mentally and physically, and on one occasion state personnel subjected her to severe torture that left her badly injured. But this tactic of state oppression, taunting and torture could not shake her steadfastness. She faced every hardship with a smile and always stood firm like a rock on the armed front, keeping the flag of freedom high. Even in these grave conditions under state oppression, the wise and courageous way she carried out organizational responsibilities while hiding in various areas is eloquent proof of her high military insight and ideological maturity. Shaheed Bilqees Didag alias Almas put into practice the idea that on the difficult path of national freedom, all hardships, troubles and sacrifices are acceptable, but national slavery and state domination are not acceptable under any circumstances. To realize this idea, she made the final decision to sacrifice herself for the motherland. Shaheed Almas carried out her duties with great devotion in various military detachments and units of the BLF, and from the time the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB) was founded she was its active founder and core member.

On 12 August 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahran Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of nine fighters of the organization: 1. Zubair Baloch, alias Shahvez; 2. Shahnawaz Baloch, alias Rahchar; 3. Rahim Baloch, alias Ajiz Baloch; 4. Musharaf Baloch, alias Basham; 5. Munir Baloch, alias Khalid Baloch; 6. Mohammad Zaman, alias Yahya; 7. Jasim Baloch, alias Babar; 8. Gaji Khan Baloch, alias Aftab; and 9. Abdullah Baloch, alias Usman, and paid tribute to all the martyred comrades who sacrificed their lives for the freedom of the motherland, Balochistan.

Musharraf Baloch, alias Basham, son of Naseer and a resident of Mashkay Tank, also made the ultimate sacrifice for the national cause of freedom. In 2022, he formally joined the armed struggle of the Baloch movement through the platform of the BLF. Initially, he played a highly active role in military affairs on the urban guerrilla front. Later, in 2025, he was transferred to the mountainous warfare front in accordance with an organizational decision. During guerrilla operations, he engaged in armed confrontations with the occupying forces. During one of these clashes, he was martyred while bravely fighting against the enemy forces.

Mitha Khan, son of Nawab Khan and a student at Bolan Medical College, was forcibly disappeared from Mach along with his brother, Hafiz Muhammad Waqas. Both brothers were taken by the CTD and killed on the same day. Their bodies were found on 24 August 2026.

On the evening of June 7th, 2024, at six o'clock, in the Kalatuk Marmar Cross area of Turbat, Balochistan Sarmachars were en route to conduct organizational work when they encountered a confrontation with operatives of a death squad formed by the Pakistani army. The death squad operatives surrounded the Sarmachars, resulting in the martyrdom of Sarmachar Mahmood alias Mehrwan. His comrade managed to evade the encirclement using guerrilla tactics, carrying the arms and equipment of the fallen Sarmachar. Martyred veteran comrade Mahmood alias Mehrwan son of Major Molabakhsh resident of Hassadig Dasht was associated with Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) since 2012 to achieve national independence. HE stood by his comrades in many important battles and set a high example of courage. Martyr Mahmood Jan, also known as Mehrwan, was a close relative of martyrs Sarmachar Nako Issa alias Nako Sheera, Sameer alias Sowgath, Sana alias Sowgath, and Jaffar alias Sana. The martyr Mahmood alias Mehrwan, was a compassionate, determined, and passionate individual. Prior to engaging in armed struggle, he was actively involved in the political struggle for the independence of Balochistan. In 2012, he participated in urban guerrilla warfare with the BLF. Since that time, until his martyrdom, he remained dedicated to the cause, immortalizing himself by joining the ranks of the esteemed comrades of the Balochistan Liberation Front and other martyrs.

Qadeer Baloch, son of Haji Elahi Bakhsh, born in November 1987, was a resident of Ginnah district, Kech, Balochistan. He received his early education from his hometown and was a student of Information Technology at the Balochistan University of Information Technology, Engineering and Management Sciences, Quetta. He was a member of BSO Azad, Shaal Zone.
To be part of the organization, he was threatened by Pakistani agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he stood with the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom. He used to read revolutionary literature of oppressed nations and was always engaged in the struggle to mobilize hundreds of youths to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of the Baloch homeland. Because of this, many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by security forces. Since they believed in political struggle, they were targeted for exercising peaceful political expression.
Qadeer was allegedly killed by state forces on 26 June 2010 on Airport Road, Turbat, Kech district, Balochistan. He was among the committed members of the organization who continued their struggle in difficult times. His highly effective activism inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.
Muneer Baloch, was a resident of the Sunny Soran, Bolan area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 14 June 2019 in Balochistan.

Zubair Ahmad Sarparah, son of Sardar Ghulam Rabbani, was a 35 year old member of the Baloch Students Organization - Azad (BSO-Azad). He was abducted on 1 October 2010 and forcibly disappeared. On 26 December 2010, his body was dumped on Qambarani Road, Quetta, Balochistan.

In a face to face battle with the Pakistani military and its agents in the mountainous regions of Noshki and Kharan on 24 September 2021, more than a dozen enemy personnel were killed, whereas six freedom fighters, including five members of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), also embraced martyrdom.
The battle commenced early Friday morning in Siyah Lop, near Baddo Dor, when enemy forces attempted to encircle a patrolling party of Baloch freedom fighters. In the face-to-face battle that lasted for more than four hours, scores of enemy personnel were killed and injured. Five freedom fighters of the BLA and one freedom fighter of the United Baloch Army (UBA), while evacuating their comrades from the battle zone, embraced martyrdom.
The fallen comrades include Commander Ganjal alias Comrade Mazar, Nazeer alias Sangar, Faisal alias Yasir, Kaleem alias Bolani, and Rehan alias Mehrwaan, all members of the Baloch Liberation Army. A member of the United Baloch Army, Nodaan alias Hammal, bravely fought alongside BLA comrades and embraced martyrdom.
Nodaan alias Hammal, son of Comrade Hameed Baloch, was a lawyer by profession and had been a member of the UBA for more than a year. Nodaan, who was also from Noshki town, fought until his last breath alongside the comrades of the BLA.
data.martyrdomPlace: Noshki and Kharan mountainous area, Balochistan

data.biography:
In continuation of the Fidayee (self-sacrificing) operation carried out on 8 July 2026 in Khuzdar city, Balochistan, against the compound of state asset and national traitor Shafiq Mengal, alias Shafiq Laghor (the coward) which resulted in the deaths of 34 members of Shafiq's death squad and the martyrdom of five members of the BLA. According to the organization, this operation, marking the commencement of the first phase of 'Operation Marg-e-Ghadaran' manifests the BLA's growing operational and intelligence capabilities against the colonial system and the criminal networks nurtured under it.

The five Fidayeen involved in this complex battle successfully breached the enemy's siege and retreated safely, while five other freedom fighters sacrificed their lives during various stages of this organized action to complete this crucial operation.
The operation commenced with the breaching of the outer security perimeter of Shafiq Laghor’s house, a responsibility undertaken by a talented Fidayee of the Majeed Brigade, Beebarg alias Pulliya Osama. The 22 year old Fidayee Beebarg hailed from the Tindilan area of Mastung and belonged to the Bangulzai tribe of the Baloch, formally joining the BLA and the Majeed Brigade in 2025. Following his enlistment into the organization's ranks, he remained active on the challenging military fronts of Khuzdar and Dasht, Quetta. Prior to this operation, he had demonstrated outstanding performance during 'Operation Herof 2' in the attack on the Frontier Corps central camp established at the Agriculture Office in Quetta. During the Khuzdar operation, he commanded the explosive laden vehicle, skillfully ramming it into the main gate of Shafiq Laghor's compound. Consequently, the outer defensive lines and checkpoints were reduced to rubble within seconds, instantly killing a large number of the enemy's armed guards stationed there and thereby clearing the path for the inner advance.
Immediately after the severe chaos caused by the explosion at the main gate, the next operational objective was to breach the security network of the compound's inner building, a task completed with utmost dedication and bravery by another valiant Fidayee of the Majeed Brigade, Zia Ur Rahman alias Imran. Hailing from Khadkocha, the 19-year-old Fidayee Zia Ur Rahman belonged to the Shahwani tribe and became a part of the BLA and the Majeed Brigade in 2025. Due to his exceptional combat skills, he quickly rose to the forefront of organizational activities on rigorous fronts such as Khuzdar and Koh-e-Maran. He had also been part of the frontline against the enemy on the Hazarganji front during 'Operation Herof 2.' In this battle of Khuzdar, right after Beebarg’s Fidayee strike, he courageously braved enemy fire to gain entry into the inner building of the compound and detonated the Fidayee jacket strapped to his body. As a result, the inner defensive line was completely destroyed, and the enemy's internal command-and-control system was paralyzed, providing the remaining Fidayeen with the opportunity to secure internal positions.
As soon as the inner security line collapsed, the remaining Fidayeen entered the compound and assumed various positions, where Fidayee Mohammad Ramzan Zehri, alias Shaban, took a stand at the main gate and its surrounding vital sectors to confront the enemy on the frontline. The 25-year-old Fidayee Mohammad Ramzan hailed from the Yakboozi area of Zehri, was the son of Chakar Khan, and belonged to the Zehri tribe. He joined the BLA in 2020 and became part of the Majeed Brigade in 2025 after extensive operational service. He was part of the guerrilla war for a long time across vast and highly sensitive fronts such as Bolan, Harboi, Nagaho, Zehri and Khuzdar and played a key role in the sensitive attack on the Quetta Red Zone during 'Operation Herof 2.' During the Khuzdar operation, he stood firm against the enemy's private death squad and uniformed collaborators at the central gate, fighting a close quarter battle and embracing martyrdom on the frontline while inflicting heavy casualties on the enemy.
The phase of maintaining resistance inside this enemy stronghold until the final moments and penetrating Shafiq Laghor’s residential block to clear all sides was carried out by two Fidayeen comrades of the Majeed Brigade, Shahzaib Baloch alias Sagaar and Shahzain Baloch alias Chedag. A resident of Manguchar, the son of Khalil Ahmed and belonging to the Nichari tribe of the Baloch, Fidayee Shahzaib Baloch began his journey in the organization as an urban guerrilla in December 2024, after which he transitioned to the regular mountain front in March 2025 and became part of the Majeed Brigade in June 2025. He was active on the Nagaho and Shoor fronts and had put up prolonged resistance against the enemy's heavy military strength under the direct command of the martyred Comrade Sameer during the battle at the Noshki main camp in 'Operation Herof 2.' Alongside him was Fidayee Shahzain Baloch alia

Adeel, son of Master Iqbal and a resident of Absar, Turbat in Kech district, was extrajudicially killed on 23 June 2025 at 11:00 AM by state-backed death squad near Park Hotel in Turbat.
Adeel was a former victim of enforced disappearance, abducted by Pakistani security forces on 8 March 2023. His disappearance sparked a prolonged sit-in protest by his family at D-Baloch in Turbat, lasting over 20 days. Later, they joined the sit-in organized by the Baloch Yakjehti Committee (BYC) at Fida Chowk, following the extrajudicial killing of Balaach Mola Bakhsh by the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD).

On 3 July 2026, a loud explosion was heard in the Panwan area of Jiwani, Balochistan. Later, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that, under Operation Zirpahazag (Protection of the Sea) Phase Six, a Fedayee attack was carried out on the Coast Guards camp in Jiwani. More than 30 enemy personnel were killed, dozens of others were severely injured and the camp was completely destroyed.
The statement further stated that at 6:32 PM Attaullah Baloch, alias Ajmal, a Fedayee sarmachar of the organization's elite unit, the Majeed Brigade, successfully drove an explosive laden Mazda vehicle into the Coast Guards camp at Panwan in the Jiwani area and detonated it. As a result of the powerful blast, the fortified colonial camp of the Coast Guards was completely turned into a heap of rubble.
Immediately after the attack, the organization's vanguard unit, the Fateh Squad, advanced rapidly and in an organized manner, launching an assault on the destroyed camp from all sides. The sarmachars of the Fateh Squad targeted the remaining personnel near the camp who had survived the blast and were suffering from extreme fear and panic in close-quarters combat, and shot them dead.
Given the critical condition of the injured personnel and those trapped under the rubble, a further increase in the enemy's casualties is highly likely.
The targeted military center was established at Panwan, approximately 10 kilometers from Jiwani city, for espionage and strict surveillance of the coastal belt, serving as a highly sensitive stronghold of the occupying state. In this joint camp, more than 20 regular military personnel from the 3rd Battalion of the Pakistan Coast Guards and the 32nd Unit of the Punjab Regiment, along with key operatives from the occupying army's intelligence agencies, Military Intelligence (MI) and the ISI, were permanently deployed. From there, the colonial operations of blockading the Baloch coast and plundering its resources were controlled.
The brave Fedayee of the BLA Majeed Brigade who made this operation successful, Attaullah Baloch, alias Ajmal, son of Mohammad Azeem, was a resident of Negindap, Rakhshan, Panjgur. The 20 year old Fedayee was educated and equipped with a high level of political and revolutionary consciousness. He formally joined the BLA on 29 August 2024 and rendered invaluable services against the enemy on the difficult military fronts of Panjgur, Kelkor, Paroom, and Washuk. Later, he voluntarily joined the Majeed Brigade for the sacred cause of the motherland's independence and delivered this historic blow to the enemy.

data.martyrdomPlace: Yar Mohammad Bazar, kallag Kor, Parom, Panjgur district, Balochistan
data.biography:
On the night between Saturday and Sunday, at 3:00 AM on April 25, 2020, Pakistani forces, along with local death squads, surrounded Baloch fighters (Sarmachaars) in Yar Mohammad Bazaar, located in the Parom Kallag Kor area of Panjgur district. A clash broke out between the forces and the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) fighters, which continued for twelve hours.
The fighting lasted until 2:30 PM on April 26, 2020. After the Pakistani ground forces retreated, military helicopters shelled the fighters, resulting in the killing of four Sarmachaars - Major Noora, son of Sher Dil, alias Peerak; Lieutenant Nawaz, son of Haji Ghulam Hussain; Abdul Malik, son of Haji Ghulam Hussain; Momin, son of Mohammad Azeem - During this prolonged twelve hour clash, several soldiers of the Pakistani army and associated death squads were killed and injured.

Major Noora, alias Peerak, son of Sher Dil, was born in 1992 in Parom, Panjgur, Balochistan. He had been associated with the Baloch national liberation movement and armed struggle for over a decade. He was a highly intelligent and capable fighter. He not only served in various roles across different regions of Balochistan, providing significant military contributions, but also played an important role in organizing the Balochistan Liberation Front through his abilities.

Lieutenant Nawaz, alias Gulab, son of Ghulam Hussain, was born in Parom. He had been associated with the BLF and the armed struggle for ten years and, due to his dedication and capabilities, attained the rank of Lieutenant.

Abdul Malik, son of Ghulam Hussain, was also born in Parom and had been associated with the armed organization BLF for two years.

Momin Baloch, son of Muhammad Azeem, was born in Buleda Salo and had been actively engaged in the armed struggle for two years.

On January 12, 2026 Pakistani army carried out a drone attack on a temporary patrol camp of Baloch Liberation Army in the Shurparood area of Kalat, in which four veteran freedom fighters of BLA - Sangat Zohair alias Haq Nawaz, Sangat Manzoor Kurd alias Bakhtiar Cheeta, Sangat Samiullah alias Javed Phalia and Sangat Naseer Ahmed alias Meerak - attained martyrdom.
Naseer Sumalani alias Meerak, son of Nabi Bakhsh Sumalani, belonged to Shahrag. He joined Baloch Liberation Army two years ago and served on Bolan and Kalat fronts. Sangat Meerak was considered an example of frontal discipline and responsibility. One of his brothers, Sangat Khair Bakhsh Sumalani alias Fareed was martyred in November 2022 while following the “philosophy of the last bullet” during prolonged clashes with enemy forces on Bolan front.

On 29 April 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson, Gwahram Baloch, announced the martyrdom of six fighters of the organization, paid tribute to them, and stated that the organization’s fighters were martyred in the national war of liberation. The martyrs include Ikram Baloch (alias Hameed), Shaibaz Shohaz (alias Kiyya), Masood Baloch (alias Bharag), Salman Waheeda (alias Chirag), Izzat Baloch (alias Jummi), and Hamza Baloch (alias Waheed).
The spokesperson further stated that the martyred fighters fulfilled their oath and national duty of defending the nation and homeland to the last drop of their blood, sacrificing their lives and achieving immortality. The martyrs proved through their great sacrifices that Baloch sarmachars do not hesitate to make any sacrifice in the defense of the nation and homeland.
Lieutenant Salman Waheeda, alias Shikari Chirag, son of Waheeda, a resident of Zamuran, Turbat district, Balochistan, joined the national liberation struggle through the platform of the BLF in 2023. During this brief period, he rendered invaluable national services with bravery and sincerity on the war fronts of Zamuran, Kulbar, Mazan-Band, Buleda, Paroom, and Mand against the occupying enemy. Salman Waheeda, alias Chirag played a pivotal role in the operation in the Darya Cham area of Mand to capture an enemy camp last year, in which eleven enemy soldiers were killed. He was a hardworking, responsible, and skilled expert marksman, and a member of the Sniper Tactical Team. Despite being uneducated, he possessed a remarkable ability to learn and grasp things quickly. Salman Waheeda, alias Chirag was martyred on April 16, 2026, in an enemy aerial strike in the Dashtuk area of Zamuran.

Sher Zaman Kurd was a 22 year old ambitious political worker of the Baloch Republican Party (BRP) and a resident of Mach, Bolan. On 12 February 2011, he was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. A month later, on 12 March 2011, his body was dumped on Sariab Road in Quetta.

Lal Baloch, alias Adnan, son of Mohammad Hayat Mohammad Hassni, was a resident of Bagli Chatar, Chagi, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Chagai front. He was martyred on 31 August 2026 in the Nokcha area of Chagi District, Balochistan.
Lal Baloch, alias Adnan, from Chagi, decided to join the Baloch Liberation Army in 2026 and was transferred to the Shor front. After graduating from the organization’s basic military training, he joined organizational patrols and took an active part in several operations against the enemy. He made the historic decision to resist rather than remain silent against the occupier’s policies because he understood that this war against the enemy was a fight for our identity and survival, which is vital to our collective life. This conscious awareness kept him steadfast on the path of resistance until the end.
Martyr Lal Balich took an active part in military operations and other organizational activities against the enemy in the relevant area and, together with his comrades, dealt heavy blows to the enemy. He provided his sangat with full individual support in implementing the policy of organizational economic blockade and fully demonstrated his abilities on the battlefield. He remained active against the enemy as a dynamic and effective fighter until the very end. In a prolonged clash with the enemy, he was martyred at Dalbandin and inscribed his name among the great freedom fighters of history who will forever be part of Baloch national history. The fruits of his sacrifices will manifest in the establishment of an independent Baloch state.

Sami Baloch, son of Hafiz Abdul Qadir, was born on 15 March 1991 in Kattan, Khuzdar, and was a resident of Khuzdar District. He received his early education in his native hometown. Sami Baloch was a student at the University of Engineering and Technology, Khuzdar, and a member of BSO Azad, Khuzdar Zone. He joined the Baloch Students Organization Azad during his university studies and soon became active in every activity of the organization.
He was one of the first people in the area to spread the ideology of Baloch nationalism among the youth, inspiring hundreds of young people from his hometown to join the organization. He played an important role in raising awareness about the Baloch liberation movement among the youth. He also had a keen interest in reading revolutionary literature from around the world.
He was abducted on 1 September 2011 from Khuzdar District by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agencies. After two months of extreme torture and detention, his bullet-riddled body was found dumped on 17 November 2011 in the Ferozabad area of Khuzdar District, Balochistan.
His sacrifices for the Baloch land will be remembered in the history of Balochistan in golden words.

On 4 March 2026, a statement issued by the spokesperson of the Balochistan Liberation Front, Major Gwahram Baloch, stated that on 3 February 2026, fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front launched a coordinated operation at four different locations in Hoshap against Pakistani forces. In this organized operation, various BLF units simultaneously targeted the enemy army at four different locations in Hoshap.
In the initial phase of the operation, one unit of fighters surrounded the police station located in Hoshap Bazaar and took control of the station, holding the personnel hostage. While this unit was seizing government weapons, ammunition, and other equipment, an enemy military convoy consisting of four vehicles approached the area, resulting in an intense face-to-face clash between BLF fighters and enemy forces. During the clash, the fighters targeted and destroyed two enemy vehicles, killing several Pakistani military personnel on board.
Meanwhile, a second unit of fighters positioned at another location attacked two armored enemy vehicles with heavy weapons. Several military personnel were killed or wounded in the clash. Witnessing the defeat and retreat of their ground forces, the enemy resorted to gunship helicopters and advanced drone technology to halt the BLF fighters’ advance.
In this prolonged clash, seven BLF fighters - Shaneed Baloch (alias Shohaz Baloch), Zabad Baloch (alias Deedag), Atta Baloch (alias Obaid), Ghaffar Baloch (alias Noroz), Abdul Samad Baloch (alias Muheem Jan), Zaheer Baloch (alias Istaal), and Nadeem (alias Sahil) - fought valiantly until their last bullet and last breath and embraced martyrdom while courageously defending their motherland.
Zaheer Baloch, alias Istaal Son of Mayar, resident of Kolwah, began his armed struggle under the Balochistan Liberation Front platform in February 2025 and dedicated himself to the liberation and defense of his homeland. He was an active and hardworking young fighter who demonstrated his military skills on various fronts in an extremely short period of time.

Ajmal Baloch, son of Yaseen, a laborer from Nasirabad, Turbat, Kech, belonged to a poor family and was the sole breadwinner for his family.
On 21 August 2025, he was abducted from Gwadar and forcibly disappeared.
On 3 May 2026, his body was dumped in the Nalent area of Balochistan.

On 11 August 2025, the umbrella alliance of Baloch armed organizations in Balochistan, Baloch Raji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS), launched coordinated operations during which several government installations were destroyed and dozens of Pakistani military personnel were killed. A large quantity of military equipment was also reportedly seized. Images showing the bodies of the deceased Pakistani soldiers, destroyed vehicles, and military uniforms hanging at various locations subsequently went viral on social media.
Even after the coordinated attacks had ended, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), a member of the BRAS alliance, maintained control of the Zehri area and successfully repelled multiple attempts by Pakistani forces to advance into the region.
After holding control of the area for several days, the BLA eventually withdrew. Following its withdrawal, the Pakistani military entered Zehri with gunship helicopters, battle tanks, and a large contingent of troops. According to reports, the forces spread fear and panic through looting and other actions in the area. Since then, Zehri and its surrounding regions have remained under military operations and repression.
Following their defeat at the hands of the armed groups, Pakistani forces allegedly targeted civilians in retaliation. As a result of this repression, 11 Baloch individuals were reportedly killed.
On 16 April 2026, several people from Zehri and its surrounding areas - including Wadera Mohammad Dayaan, Imam Bakhsh, Manzoor Ahmad Miraji, Munir Hayat Dayaan, Izzatullah Pandrani, Habibullah, Mohammad Sharif, Mohammad Ramzan, and three unidentified individuals - were reportedly extrajudicially executed by Pakistani forces while traveling along roads in the Sohinda area. One individual, Abdul Salam, survived with serious injuries.
During the ongoing military operation in the area, these individuals were allegedly detained by Pakistani forces from various locations and transferred to the Sohinda Rest House, approximately five kilometres from Noorgama. There, their hands and feet were allegedly bound, they were blindfolded, and they were subsequently shot dead.
The incident occurred one day after the BLA claimed that two of its fighters had been killed during clashes in the Sohinda area.
In its statement, the BLA said that, on 15 April 2026, its fighters targeted advancing Pakistani military units with a remote-controlled explosive device. Following the explosion, they allegedly carried out an ambush on a military convoy moving toward the area.
The organization claimed that ten Pakistani military personnel were killed in the two attacks, while two of its own fighters, Tanveer Mengal and Saadullah, were also killed.

On 14th February 2026, Faraz, son of Bahadur, a 23 year old resident of Koshkalat, Tump area of Turbat district of Balochistan, was shot dead by a Pakistani state-backed death squad. The squad which is being weaponised by the Pakistani state, giving them the power to crush every voice and youth in Balochistan. The same state won't take a single action against them. They backed them to spread fear and do whatever they want like harassment, blackmailing and threatening families for their own needs too.
Faraz was a young civilian raised under significant hardship by his family. He was an embroidery pattern artist. Like many others in Balochistan, he was striving to build a future and support his family. His life was tragically cut short in an act of violence that has become increasingly common across Balochistan.

On 30 December 2023 Pakistani forces carried out a drone attack and attempted to surround a camp of BRAS in Gurandi Zeera Kaur area of Mashkay by dropping commandos through helicopters. Following professional military tactics, Baloch freedom fighters formed multiple teams to foil enemy aggression and carried several successful attacks against the advancing enemy troops. At least 7 enemy commandos were eliminated in two separate attacks, whereas, three Baloch freedom fighters, identified as Sarwar alias Duruk, Azam alias Basit and Abdul Sattar alias Maraij made ultimate sacrifices. Two freedom fighters of BRAS, Kenagi alias Muslim and Ali alias Atta, while forestalling enemy advances for hours and providing a safe route for Baloch freedom fighters, also embraced martyrdom. Both valiant fighters fought the enemy troops until their last bullets, and made the ultimate sacrifices at their own hands after running out of ammunition. The fallen comrades were affiliated with the allied organisations of BRAS. Ali alias Atta was a resident of Gajali in Mashkay. He had been serving his national duties through the platform of BLF since 2013. He also took part in several operations against the occupying forces and inflicted heavy losses upon the enemy forces.

Javed son of Mazaar, a committed and courageous national fighter of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF), was martyred on April 1, 2025, in an ambush by collaborators of the Pakistani army. Paying tribute to him, BLF vows to bring the enemy’s agents to justice.
Javed Baloch alias Asif son of Mazaar, originally hailed from Jan Muhammad Bazaar in Dasht, district Kech. His family later moved to Gwadar. He joined the BLF in 2011 and remained part of the urban network under the command of Martyr Haleem and Martyr Ghani until 2012, actively participating in organizational operations against the enemy. Gwadar holds strategic importance for the BLF, and the sacrifices of Sarmachars like Shaheed Javed have played a vital role in foiling the exploitative plans of the occupying state. Javed was the cousin of Martyr Ghani.
After 2012, he played a prominent role in military operations on the frontlines of Dasht. In early 2016, following organizational strategy, he shifted from the city to the camp and took part in face-to-face combat missions. Due to his skill, dedication, and exceptional marksmanship, he was assigned as a sniper. He played a key role in attacking Pakistani military camps, including the historic "Battle of Sibdan" on January 25, 2022, in which BLF fighters completely destroyed a heavily fortified enemy post, forcing the adversary to retreat.
Javed remained loyal to the organization until his last breath. On April 1, 2025, during an organizational leave in a secure area, enemy agents ambushed him, and he embraced martyrdom.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Shahid Bangulzai, alias Commando, son of Abdul Wahid Bangulzai, was originally from the Garrani area of Mastung and a resident of Hazarganji, Quetta. He joined the BLA on 17 December 2024 and served in the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS) unit. He was martyred during Operation Herof Phase II on the Quetta front.
Shahid Bangulzai was present on the Quetta front during Operation Herof Phase II. Due to his seriousness, sense of responsibility, and practical capabilities, he was inducted into the organization’s Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). During the operation, he remained active on the Quetta front alongside his fellow Sarmachars, where they challenged the enemy’s military superiority. During a clash with enemy forces in the Wali Jet area of Saryab, he stood his ground with his fellow fighters and was martyred in the battle.
Shahid Bangulzai’s struggle and sacrifice serve as a reminder that Baloch Sarmachars, through their courage, strategic thinking, and endurance, can challenge even the strongest fortresses of the enemy.

data.biography:
On the night of April 29, 2025 in the Dannuk area of Turbat, the Pakistani occupying forces attempted to surround members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s urban guerrilla network. In response, the fighters launched a strong counter-attack. The clashes, which began at 3:30 AM, continued until sunrise. The fighters held their positions for three hours and continued to inflict heavy blows on the enemy. During this time, they also targeted a convoy of the occupying forces, causing significant casualties. Thirteen enemy personnel were killed and several others were injured during the clashes.
Three Baloch Liberation Army fighters were killed in the fighting: Nabeel, alias Ali; Feroz Sarban, alias Nodbandag and Mohammad Umar Zaka, alias Guru.
Nabeel Ahmed, alias Ali, son of Rasool Bakhsh Hoth, belonged to the Gokdan area of Turbat. He had been active as a political worker through the Baloch Students Organization. In 2009, he joined the armed struggle through its affiliated organization. In 2010, during a raid by the occupying army, fighting continued from midnight until eight in the morning. During the clash, he killed and injured several military personnel, but was himself severely wounded and left in a near-dead state by the enemy. His sister was also injured, and his father and cousin were forcibly disappeared. His brother, Sangat Mubashir Hoth alias Shah Dost was martyred in October 2020 in close combat on the Kulbar front.
Nabeel spent five years imprisoned in Mach, Gaddani, and Turbat jails. Despite torture, he did not abandon his path. After his release, he took to the mountains and became active as an urban guerrilla, leading multiple missions. At the time of his death, he was serving as a unit commander. He was known as an exemplary fighter for his discipline, intellectual depth, and steadfast endurance. His life embodied the harsh realities of imprisonment, torture and resistance under an occupying state. Rather than be captured, Nabeel Ahmed followed the “last bullet” philosophy and chose martyrdom by taking his own life with his final bullet.
Salam Mengal, was a resident of the Anjira, Khuzdar area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 9 November 2013 in Balochistan.

In the Gramkan area of Panjgur district, Balochistan, around 10:00 PM on the night of April 6, 2024, clashes erupted between fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) and the occupying Pakistani army when enemy forces attempted to raid a fighters’ hideout. The fighters, Hasrat and Abdi, who were encircled by the enemy, bravely confronted the attacking forces. During the fighting, the occupying army was also reinforced by operatives of local so-called death squads. By 3:00 AM on April 7, 2024, both valiant fighters continued to resist the enemy forces and their collaborators with determination, killing at least eleven enemy personnel and injuring several others. After fighting for five consecutive hours, both like-minded fighter brothers attained martyrdom. Martyr Hasrat, alias Asad, and Martyr Abdi, alias Sawar, son of Ali Mohammad, belonged to the Gramkan area of Panjgur. Both brothers joined the armed struggle for Baloch national liberation in 2019. They remained active on the Panjgur city, Gichk Kilkor, and Kolwah fronts in the pursuit of national freedom. Both fighters were exemplary in sincerity, dedication, and perseverance. From the very first day, the martyred companions, relying on their combat skills, inflicted repeated defeats on the enemy across multiple fronts and remained steadfast in this struggle until their final breath.

On December 27, 2024, the mutilated body of Zareef Baloch was found near his home in Dazin Tump. His body bore horrific evidence of torture, including burn marks, bruises from severe beatings, and signs of electric shocks. His limbs had been tied, and his tongue had been cut, further illustrating the brutality he endured. Just days earlier, on December 26, Frontier Corps (FC) personnel had raided his home and forcibly abducted him in the presence of his family. His father was also killed by the same forces, reflecting the ongoing oppression in the region.

On 11 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch announced the martyrdom of 14 fighters of the organization who attained martyrdom in confrontations with the Pakistani army and in airstrikes while defending their homeland, Balochistan, and fighting for national liberation and the right to self-determination.

On 13 August 2026, Pakistani Air Force fighter jets bombarded the Pandran area of Kalat District in Balochistan, resulting in the martyrdom of four members of the organization: Waseem Baloch, alias Farhan; Obaidullah Baloch, alias Shaheen; Nawaz Ali Baloch, alias Dilshad; and Mohammad Hassan, alias Ahmad.

On 25 August 2026, during an organizational mission in the Kech area of Balochistan, Sher Jan, alias Jamal, was shot from behind by a traitor, resulting in his martyrdom.

On 3 September 2026, while patrolling in the Mastung area of Balochistan, the organization’s brave fighters, Mohammad Younis, alias Salal; Sameer Ahmad, alias Zemal; Aziz Ahmad, alias Janan; and Sikandar Baloch, confronted Pakistani forces, targeted several enemy personnel, and embraced martyrdom.

On 14 September 2026, while engaging Pakistani forces and defending his fellow fighters in the Machani Kor Paroom area of Panjgur District, Babar Baloch, alias Kambar, embraced martyrdom.

On 18 September 2026, during a confrontation with Pakistani forces in the Chagi area of Balochistan, fighters of the organization, Riaz Baloch, alias Sabir; Taimoor Shah, alias Shaheen; Zia Ul Haq, alias Ziaullah; and Jumma Baloch, alias Commando, embraced martyrdom.

Taimoor Shah, alias Shaheen, son of Gul Mohammad, resident of Chagi, joined the BLF at the beginning of the 2026. After military training, he carried out national duties on the difficult fronts of Chagai. On 18 September 2026, in the battle against the enemy's encirclement at Aminabad, Chagi, he was martyred fighting bravely.

Fareed Baloch, son of Haleem Baloch, was born on October 15, 1989, in Panjgur. He was a resident of Civil Colony, Khuzdar. Fareed Baloch was abducted outside a check post of the Frontier Corps (FC) on Saryab Road, Quetta, by security agencies.
On February 9, after 6 PM, while he was travelling with his cousin in a three-wheeler, he was stopped at a checkpoint by FC personnel along with some individuals in plain clothes and was taken away in a jeep bearing no registration number.
He was a student at the Balochistan University of Engineering and Technology, Khuzdar, and served as the zonal president of the Baloch Students Organization Azad.
After 45 days of abduction and torture in an army cell, his bullet-riddled body was found on March 27, 2011 at Ferozabad Nullah in Khuzdar District, Balochistan. Fareed was shot in the head, and his body also bore marks of torture.
He was killed because of his political beliefs and was targeted for exercising his right to peaceful political expression. Fareed had a dream of completing his education and working for a brighter future for his people, but he was killed because of his ideology and political struggle.
He was a mature political leader who led the organization in his zone under very difficult circumstances and had a keen interest in reading books on various topics.

Nawab Noroz Khan Zarakzai (1875 – 25 December 1965), also known among the Baloch as Babu Noroz, was the hereditary leader of the Zarakzai subtribe of the Zehri in the Jhalawan region of Kalat. He commanded an insurgency of several hundred fighters against Pakistani forces from 1958 to 1959 in opposition to the One Unit administrative scheme, which curtailed Baloch regional autonomy, and the prior deposition of the Khan of Kalat.
Born in Zehri tehsil of Khuzdar district to Sardar Pasand Khan Zarakzai, Noroz Khan briefly served as a civil servant under British rule from 1908 to 1910 before resigning to support his brother Nawab Mohammad Khan's revolt against colonial authority. This marked the beginning of his lifelong commitment to tribal independence. Over the following decades, he participated in intermittent anti-British campaigns through the 1930s, enduring imprisonment and escaping from Sukkur Jail in 1925 (or around 1926), which solidified his reputation as a resolute defender of Baloch prerogatives within the princely state of Kalat.
The 1958 uprising was triggered by Islamabad's imposition of the One Unit scheme, which merged Balochistan into a unified West Pakistan province and diminished local governance, as well as the 1955 military action against Kalat's ruler, Mir Ahmad Yar Khan. Noroz Khan mobilized between 150 and 1,000 tribesmen in mountainous terrain, conducting guerrilla operations that challenged army deployments until his surrender in early 1959 under assurances of safe conduct sworn on the Quran by government representatives. Betrayed despite the pledge, he faced a military tribunal that convicted him of treason and sentenced him to life imprisonment. His son Bhatte Khan (also referred to as Batey Khan or Dilawar Khan in some accounts) and six companions—Bhawal Khan Musiyani, Masti Khan Musiyani, Ghulam Rasool Nechari, Sabzal Khan Zehri, Jamal Khan, and Wali Mohammad—were executed by hanging on 15 July 1960, fueling enduring grievances over due process in the conflict.
Noroz Khan died in Hyderabad Central Jail on 25 December 1965 at approximately 90 years old. His death in custody cemented his status as an icon of Baloch defiance against centralization, though Pakistani accounts frame the episode as the suppression of sedition amid post-independence consolidation.
Early Life and Tribal Leadership
Origins and Family Background
Noroz Khan, also known as Nawab Noroz Khan or Babu Noroz, was born in 1875 in Zehri Tehsil of Khuzdar District, Balochistan, as the son of Sardar Pasand Khan Zarakzai. The Zarakzai were a sub-branch of the Zehri tribe, a prominent Brahui-speaking Baloch group in the Jhalawan area of the Kalat Khanate, historically involved in local governance and regional conflicts.
As the son of a sardar (tribal chief), Noroz Khan was born into the tribal aristocracy, where leadership passed through familial lines in a pastoral-nomadic society centered on livestock herding, kinship alliances, and resistance to external authority. His family included his brother Nawab Mohammad Khan, who later led anti-British efforts that Noroz joined in early adulthood. This upbringing instilled a deep commitment to tribal autonomy, shaping his role as Nawab of the Zarakzai.
Rise as Nawab of the Zarakzai Tribe
Noroz Khan ascended to the hereditary title of Nawab in the early 20th century through familial succession amid intra-tribal dynamics and anti-colonial pressures. His brief service as a civil servant under the British (1908–1910) ended when he resigned in solidarity with his brother Nawab Mohammad Khan's armed uprising. British authorities reportedly offered him leadership over the Zehri in place of another brother, Rasool Bakhsh, to divide the tribe, but he refused, prioritizing tribal unity over personal gain. This decision elevated his stature as a unifying figure.
By assuming the Nawab title, he inherited oversight of Zarakzai levies and disputes, building influence through loyalty to kin and tribe during a period when British indirect rule via the Khan of Kalat increasingly eroded local prerogatives. Among Baloch adherents, this era marked his transition to a revered patriarch affectionately called Babu Noroz.
Pre-Partition Resistance
Anti-British Campaigns (1914–1932)
Noroz Khan resigned his civil service position in 1910 to join his brother's revolt against British authority in Balochistan. He participated in this campaign and later led a series of anti-British guerrilla operations from 1914 to 1932, targeting colonial outposts, levies, and policies in Jhalawan, Makran, and Khuzdar. His forces frequently crossed into Afghan territory for sanctuary and regrouping, exploiting the porous Durand Line.
In 1922 (or around that period), British authorities arrested him, convicted him of rebellion, and sentenced him to life imprisonment. He was initially held in Kala Pani jail in Mach and later transferred to Sukkur Central Jail, from which he escaped around 1925–1926 with local aid. Post-esca
