data.biography:
Martyr Mullah Baksh Baloch Alias Gaffar Baloch, son of  Kareem Baloch and was a resident of  Darchko, Dasht area of  Kech, Balochistan. He became part of Baloch liberation movement in 2017 and in 2021, he joined Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF).
He embraced martyrdom in a drone attack of Pakistan’s military along with his seven comrades, Kareem Baloch, Asif Baloch, Hazza Baloch,  Shezad Baloch, Jalal Baloch, Talib Baloch, and Manzoor Baloch on Feb 23, 2023 in Mazanband area of Kech, Balochistan.

Kumar Baloch, son of Mohammad Ishaq, was born on February 5, 1996 in Kohrdo Jhao, District Awaran. He received his early education from Government High School Kohrdo Jao. Due to financial difficulties and his involvement in the national struggle, he was unable to continue his studies at the university level.
After completing his FA, he pursued a private BA, but could not continue his education due to the reasons mentioned above. He was a keen lover of education and a kind-hearted person. Unfortunately, financial difficulties did not allow him to pursue higher education. He remained mostly quiet.
In his free time, Kumar Baloch played cricket in the village, as he was passionate about the sport. He also took part in social activities in the village. He was always available to support anyone in need of help.
Kumar Baloch began his political career on the platform of BSO Azad in 2009 and, until his martyrdom, remained part of the Baloch Students Organization, serving in different positions within the organization. At the time of his martyrdom at the hands of the Pakistani state, he was serving as the organizer of the Jao Zone.
He believed in political struggle and was targeted for his peaceful political expression. He was killed by Pakistani-backed religious extremists in Korak Jhao, Awaran, on October 23, 2016. His sacrifices for the national liberation movement will always be remembered, and he will continue to inspire Baloch youth to join the liberation struggle, which he believed to be the only guarantor of a prosperous Balochistan.

On 12 August 2026, several Baloch people, including women and children, were killed and several others were injured as a result of an aerial bombardment of a civilian population by the Pakistan Air Force, reportedly using American-made F-16 fighter aircraft, in the Gidar Gindan area of Surab District, Balochistan. Following the airstrike, the injured and deceased were transported by police and local residents to DHQ Hospital in Surab, where the injured received medical treatment.

The families of the deceased and local residents subsequently began a protest by placing the bodies at Surab Main Chowk on the Quetta-Karachi National Highway (N-25). As a result, traffic on the highway was disrupted, with long queues of vehicles forming on both sides. Videos and photographs of the protest subsequently circulated widely on social media under the hashtag #SurabMassacre.

Those killed in the airstrike were identified as Shabir Ahmad Sumalani, son of Khudadad Sumalani, a resident of Marap, Surab; Noor Jan Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, a resident of Gindan; Karim Dad Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, a resident of Gandan; Raj Babu, wife of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani; Safia, wife of Noor Jan Mirwani; and Jalal Mirwani, son of Noor Jan Mirwani.

Those injured were identified as Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, son of Jan Muhammad Mirwani; Abdul Karim Mirwani, son of Jan Muhammad Mirwani; Mehrullah Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani; Nadeem Mirwani, son of Abdul Salam Mirwani; Shoaib Mirwani, son of Abdul Karim Mirwani; Sarah, wife of Baseer Ahmed Mirwani; Sabira, wife of Tufail Ahmed Mirwani; Zamra, daughter of Abdul Aziz Mirwani; Hajira, wife of Abdul Fattah Mirwani; Asim, son of Baseer, aged 1; Rahabia, daughter of Abdul Karim, aged 3; Sadia, daughter of Abdul Salam, aged 5; Fatima, daughter of Abdul Karim, aged 7; Zia-ur-Rehman, son of Abdul Karim, aged 2; Amir, son of Abdul Karim, aged 1; and Hasina, daughter of Muhammad Aslam, aged 4.

Sara, wife of Baseer Ahmed Mirwani, was admitted to the hospital on 5 September 2026. She succumbed to her injuries and passed away in the hospital.

Following a detailed technical and scientific analysis of remnants of rocket components recovered from debris at the site of the aerial bombardment, important evidence reportedly emerged indicating that the recovered fragments belonged to an air-launched missile fired from an F-16 fighter aircraft.

Photographs of the recovered debris and the subsequent technical analysis reportedly indicated that the fragment was part of an AIM-120 Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile (AMRAAM), an American-made air-to-air missile.

Key technical evidence and serial numbers

According to the information and serial numbers reportedly engraved on the surface of the debris, the following details were recorded:

Assembly Number: ASSY 872128-1

Serial Number: 09-987138

Date of Manufacture: 09/09 (September 2009)

According to open-source intelligence (OSINT) records, the part number “872128-1” reportedly corresponds to the control section and rocket motor assembly of an AMRAAM missile manufactured by the American defense company Raytheon. Based on this evidence and the reported matching serial numbers, it is claimed that the debris was not part of an aircraft’s internal structure but instead consisted of remnants from an operational missile fired from an F-16 aircraft.

Hidayatullah, son of Sher Mohammad, was born in Basima, Balochistan. He began his political struggle with BSO Azad and became a member of the BSO Azad Basima Zone. Many of his comrades and friends were martyred by security forces for joining the Baloch liberation movement under the banner of BSO Azad, but such threats to his life did not prevent him from participating in the activities of the organization.
He remained committed to the Baloch national cause and the organization until his martyrdom. He believed in a peaceful political struggle. He was martyred on 25 May 2013. He was a dedicated member of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times.
He inspired many young people to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

Jahanzaib Baloch, the son of Roshin and a resident of Babber Shoor, Pasni, district Gwadar, was a labourer. He was forcibly disappeared by Frontier Corps (FC) personnel on September 28, 2025, from his hometown, Babber Shoor, Pasni.

After three days of enforced disappearance, his bullet-riddled body was recovered on October 1, 2025, in Uthal, Balochistan.

Warna Noroz Baloch, son of Aga Moosa Jan, was a resident of District Kalat. He was a student and a member of BSO Azad, Kalat Zone. He received his early education in his native area, Kalat.
He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising his right to peaceful political expression. He mobilized hundreds of youth to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of their homeland. Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by security forces.
He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he remained committed to the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom. He was an example of bravery and dedication. He joined the organization at an early age and stood firm in his national ideology until the end.
He was killed by Pakistan’s secret agencies at a public gathering in Kalat on July 15, 2008. His body bore severe signs of torture. He was among the most committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times.
He inspired many young people to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

data.biography:
On 9 September 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of ten fighters belonging to the organization. He paid tribute to the Sarmachars who were martyred while defending national liberation and their homeland, Balochistan.
- The statement identified the following fighters:
1-  Akhtar Dawood, alias Ali Sher, son of Asad Sajidi.
2- Khalil Ahmad, alias Ustad Awais, son of Sher Ahmad.
3-  Imran, alias Aajo, son of Saifullah.
4-  Hasil, alias Munir Ahmad, son of Sher Mohammad.
5- Inayatullah, alias Sher Zaman, son of Manzoor Ahmad.
6- Asad Rahim, son of Rahim Baksh.
7- Mujeeb Ur Rehman, alias Shay Mureed, son of Saeed Ahmad.
8- Sahil, alias Arman, son of Peeral.
9- Javed, alias Murshid.
10- Mohammad Younis, alias Taleb, son of Mohammad Omar.

Mujeeb Ur Rehman, alias Shay Mureed, son of Saeed Ahmad, joined the organization’s urban network three years ago under the command of martyred Major Mama Chakar. He remained constantly active and ready for organizational tasks. Whether it was logistical needs or military duties, he carried out all his responsibilities faithfully and diligently. By organizational decision, he moved to the mountain front in February 2026. In this short period, he rendered national service on the fronts of KhadKocha, Mastung, Zehri, Shor, Barkhan, Manguchar, and Kalat, inflicting blows upon enemy that will be remembered for history. He was a fighter endowed with leadership ability, and because of this he was also entrusted with responsibility for a camp, which he carried out steadfastly until his martyrdom. He attained the rank of martyrdom in a clash with the enemy on 19 May 2026.

On 1 September 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that, during intense fighting with the occupying forces at Dasht Goran in Chaghi, twenty personnel, including a captain, were killed and several others were wounded. Two BLA fighters were also killed while fighting for their homeland.
He stated that on 31 August 2026, the BLA began a blockade and conducted snap-checking at Nadirabad in Dasht Goran, Chagi, at around 6:00 p.m. During this, a convoy consisting of eight vehicles belonging to Pakistan's forces arrived at the location. They were also assisted by elements of the area's death squads.
Under a wartime strategy, BLA fighters took up positions and launched intense attacks against the enemy. The fighters continued to attack the Pakistani forces. During the fighting, four enemy vehicles came within their encirclement, causing severe damage, and all personnel aboard them were killed. The use of rockets and other modern weapons left the enemy with no opportunity to escape. BLA fighters targeted one of the enemy vehicles with a rocket and completely destroyed it, resulting in further casualties.
The vehicle was later lifted and taken away by a crane. Despite being greater in number, the enemy was unable to withstand the BLA fighters. This effective counter-operation by the BLA delivered a major response to the Pakistani forces. Among the twenty personnel of the occupying Pakistani Army killed in the attack was Captain Ubaid (147/LC, formerly 69/PR, 60/W). It has remained the practice of the Pakistani Army to conceal the actual number of its killed and wounded soldiers and officers. In this battle as well, it concealed the number of its killed and wounded personnel, as well as its logistical losses.
In this battle at Dasht Goran, Chagi, two BLA fighters, Nasir, alias Baba, and Bashir Ahmad, alias Shaukat, sacrificed their lives for Balochistan and made history through their courage and bravery. Despite being surrounded by the enemy, they demonstrated exceptional military skill, strategy, and bravery, inflicting heavy losses on hundreds of personnel of the occupying forces. The battle continued intermittently from 6:30 p.m. until 4:00 a.m., during which the enemy suffered what was described as a historic defeat. The enemy remained engaged until late at night in removing its destroyed vehicles and wounded personnel from the area. Local residents witnessed dozens of ambulances removing the bodies of the dead from the site. During the battle, the occupying Pakistani forces also had the assistance of drones.
Nasir Baloch, alias Baba, belonged to Dasht Goran, Chagi, in the Manguchar area of Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2014. He was an extremely brave and hardworking fighter who possessed exceptional battlefield skills. During his twelve-year struggle, he played a key role in several important and decisive battles in the areas of Shor Parod, Nagaho, Chaghai, and Dalbandin. His name will always be written in golden words for his actions against the enemy.
Bashir Ahmad, alias Shaukat, belonged to Gazg in Kalat District. He began his national responsibilities through the BLA platform in 2015. He also struck heavy blows against the enemy in areas of Balochistan, including Narmak, Nagaho, Chaghai, Saroon, and Shor Parod, among others, and remained a frontline participant in Baloch fighters' operations. His bravery, strategy, and unparalleled spirit of sacrifice for the homeland serve as a guiding light for Baloch youth.

data.biography: On June 4, 2025, in the Balochistan area of Dukki, in the Killi Safar Ali Jangal, Pakistan’s Counter Terrorism Department abducted 44 year old Mohammad Anwar, son of Mohammad Hussain, in broad daylight as he was leaving the mosque after prayers, and forcibly made him disappear. On January 4, 2026, his mutilated body was found. Mohammad Anwar was a farmer by profession and had no connection with any political party or armed group.
Amjid Jan Baloch, was a resident of the Rekchahy, Awaran area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 16 November 2015 in Balochistan.

Mohammad Nawaz Marri was a social worker. On 5 January 2011, he was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. While in illegal custody, he was extrajudicially killed, and on 23 March 2011, his body was dumped in the Lasbela district of Balochistan.

data.organization: Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) / Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB)
data.biography:
The fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front’s special unit, the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB), attacked the Brigade Headquarters in the Nokundi area of Chagai, Balochistan, at around 8:19 PM on the night of November 30, 2025. SOB fighters successfully entered the offices and residential compound of foreign employees of the Saindak and Reko Diq projects, located in the centre of the camp, and managed to take several foreigners present in the compound hostage. The Pakistani army deployed its air force, SSG commandos, and modern heavy weapons against the fighters, but the brave Sarmachars of SOB repelled every attempt and forced them to retreat. During the operation, the Balochistan Liberation Front offered the Pakistani side an opportunity to negotiate on its demands; however, 18 hours after the offer, the Pakistani army chose to use force and began directly targeting the compound with artillery and aerial attacks. This resulted in intense clashes between the occupying forces and the fighters, which continued until the martyrdom of the SOB fighters.
In this special operation by the Saddo Operational Battalion, 76 military personnel, including foreign hostages, were killed, and 6 SOB fighters embraced martyrdom. The Nokundi operation by SOB was a continuation of the BLF’s long-standing armed resistance strategy for the independence of Balochistan and the protection of its natural wealth.
Among the martyrs were:
1 Asif alias Khalid Baloch, son of Mulla Ghulam Jan.
2 Inayat Sahil alias Gwahram Baloch, son of Ishaq Baloch.
3 Zareena Rafiq alias Tranag Maho, daughter of Master Rafiq Ahmed.
4 Nabeel Ahmed alias Ustad Adil Baloch, son of Haji Muhammad Ishaq.
5 Meer Jan Meeral alias Janan Baloch, son of Muhammad Raheem Baloch.
6 Ghulam Jan alias Istaal Baloch, son of Faiz Muhammad.
Asif alias Khalid Baloch, son of Mulla Ghulam Jan, resident of Diz Paroom, commanded the SOB operation. He joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in May 2013 and volunteered for Sado Operational Battalion (SOB) his military services in 2024. Asif Baloch was an expert in combat skills, strategy formulation, and optimal use of weapons. He fought bravely and demonstrated exemplary leadership while leading the operations against the enemy forces for 36 hours, and commanded his team exceptionally until his martyrdom on December 2, 2025.

On the night of June 8, 2025, Baloch Liberation Army fighter Waseem Kashani, also known as Chiragh, was martyred in an explosion during the placement of an IED on an enemy route in the Bonistan area of Panjgur. Sangat Waseem, son of Haji Muhammad Akbar Kashani, was a resident of Bonistan, Panjgur.
Waseem held a master’s degree in Social Work. Despite serving in the state force Levies, he chose the path of national rebellion in 2021 and joined the Baloch Liberation Army. He remained active as an urban guerrilla for five years. He participated in various operations in a covert role against the enemy and maintained strict secrecy regarding his identity and activities.

Baloch Khan was a grassroots activist who transitioned into the armed struggle to defend what he described as his motherland. He was identified as one of the six primary fighters who held the frontline during the July 29 confrontation, ensuring the survival of the larger patrolling group.
data.birthPlace: Kallag Jaki Gorkop, Kech, Occupied Baluchistan

data.biography:
Haleem Baloch, son of Mohammad Sadiq, a 30 year old shopkeeper from Panjgur, was taken by a state backed death squad on February 19, 2026, from Khudabadan Masjid in Panjgur, Balochistan. Haleem was a civilian who earned his livelihood through his shop and supported his family.
The death squad, operating under the command of Pakistani forces, forcibly took Haleem from the mosque area without presenting any legal warrant or explanation. After his abduction, his family continued searching for him and repeatedly tried to obtain information about his whereabouts, but no information was provided.
On March 6, 2026, a body with multiple gunshot wounds was found near the Panjgur Airport. The body was taken to Civil Hospital Panjgur for identification, where family members later confirmed that it was Haleem Baloch.

On February 21, 2025, organizational comrades and freedom fighters Sakhi Bakhsh alias Qandeel and Balach alias Aslam were martyred in a clash with Pakistani forces and their militia (Death Squad) in the Teertej area of Awaran during an organizational mission.
Martyr Balach alias Aslam, son of Ali Bakhsh, a resident of Greshag, Khuzdar, joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in 2024. He actively participated in numerous battles in Awaran and Kolwah. Though he was a student, after gaining ideological awareness of the national freedom struggle, he chose to engage in armed resistance.

Shoaib Baloch, son of Muhammad Ayoub, a shopkeeper and resident of Khudabadan, Panjgur, was forcibly disappeared on 8 February 2023. For more than three years, his family lived in uncertainty, waiting for his return and hoping that he would one day come home.

On 10 August 2026, that wait ended with the devastating news of his brutal killing in a fake encounter by Pakistani forces in the Chedagi area of Panjgur.

Mohammad Iqbal, son of Nawab Khan, was a 28 year old labourer and resident of the area near the Hann River in Barkhan. 
On 26 December 2025, at around 12:00 PM, Military Intelligence personnel of the Pakistani forces abducted him and subjected him to enforced disappearance in front of the Sessions Court in Rakni, Barkhan.
After nine months and 14 days of enforced disappearance, his body was found dumped in Barkhan on 10 October 2026, following a fake encounter.

data.martyrdomPlace: Satak Kor, Hoshap, Turbat district, Balochistan
data.biography:
On February 23, 2022 the occupying forces of Pakistan struck the Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) guerrilla camp in the Satak Kor mountain range of Hoshab, district Kech, and fired three chemical-laden missiles that wreaked havoc over a large area, destroying palm groves and other vegetation at the site. Following the drone missile attacks, the infantry team of the occupying forces surrounded the area and, with the support of more than eight state helicopters, entered the camp. Five Sarmachaars, including two commanders of the organization, Master Asif Baloch and Siraj Baloch, were martyred in this attack. Meanwhile, five other Sarmachaars - Shoaib, Munir, Arif Jan, Diljan, Kamal, Kamash Malang, Jangi Khan, and Daolat - were martyred defending their homeland, fighting the enemy for over an hour and killing several commandos of the occupying forces.
Dil Jan, alias Nazir, son of Meeran, resident of Sangabad Tijaban, had been involved in the armed resistance since 2018. He was an expert fighter and a valiant son of the motherland. In 2021, one of his brothers was martyred in an attack by the State Death Squads, and another brother remains imprisoned in the torture cells of the occupying forces.

Yousuf Baloch was a resident of Basima. He received his early and primary education there. He began his political struggle during his student life and joined the organization at a very early age, remaining with it until his martyrdom.
He joined BSO Azad Basima Zone and embraced martyrdom on 9th October 2013. He was a committed member of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many young people to join the caravan of BSO Azad.
His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

On 13th April 2026, in the Barkhan area of Balochistan, Pakistani forces shelled and bombed civilian populations, killing twelve innocent Baloch civilians, including women and children, and seriously injuring three others.

The martyrs are:

- Ali, son of Sultan Umair, aged 40
- Babul, daughter of Gulzar, aged 30
- Mir Jan, son of Ali, aged 2
- Somri, daughter of Bhangan, aged 35
- Balach, son of Sabzo, aged 70
- Shari, aged 22
- Rehman, son of Balach, aged 18
- Naikho, daughter of Jamalan, aged 17
- Allah Bakhsh, son of Balach, aged 6
- Saddo, daughter of Balach, aged 13
- Hapo, daughter of Balach, aged 8
- Mahrang, daughter of Balach, aged 2

The injured are:

- Zarbibi, daughter of Sher, aged 55
- Hazar Khan, son of Balach, aged 9
- Israr, daughter of Balach, aged 15

This is not the first time that Pakistani forces have bombed civilians in Balochistan, targeting unarmed and innocent women and children as a form of collective punishment. Nor can this be considered “collateral damage.” Rather, the Pakistani state and its forces are deliberately targeting the Baloch people to maintain an atmosphere of fear in the region, suppress internal dissent, exploit Baloch coastal resources, and continue policies of genocide against the Baloch nation.

On 1 November 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson, Gwahram Baloch, issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of eight of the organisation’s fighters: Captain Yahya, alias Ustad Khalid Jan; Aris Baloch, alias Omar Jan; Hafeez Baloch, alias Karwan, son of Dad Mohammad; Javid Baloch, alias Gulab, son of Bori Baloch; Abdul Khaliq, alias Nothak; Sajid Baloch, alias Mehran; Hameed Baloch, alias Buzerg; and Akram Baloch, alias Gwahram.

The statement paid tribute to these brave and ideologically committed members of the organisation, who embraced martyrdom while engaging in clashes with the Pakistani army and its death squads on various fronts across Balochistan.

Martyr Hafeez Baloch, alias Karwan, son of Dad Muhammad, resident of Hoteg Dal Bazaar, Pasni, formally joined the armed and intellectual struggle for Baloch national freedom through the BLF platform on 17 October 2025. He was a highly educated young man who had completed a BS in Education at Gwadar University. Despite his higher education, he chose not to stay within the confines of an outdated education system and instead dedicated his knowledge and awareness to the freedom of the oppressed Baloch nation and the war for national survival. Being educated, he was a sarmachar equipped with deep political thinking, intellectual maturity and ideological awareness. He was counted among those conscious BLF workers who understood the political and intellectual demands of the national movement as well as those of the battlefront. He served on the sensitive strategic fronts of Pasni, Shadikor, Gwarkop, Kulanch and Pidrak with great bravery, organizational discipline and professional skill. He was a very hardworking, diligent and dutiful sarmachar who stepped forward to face the enemy in every difficult engagement. On 18 October 2026, in a clash with the death squad formed by the occupying army in Chakli, Kulanch, he embraced martyrdom and became immortal in history.

On June 9, 2025, Pakistani security forces reportedly raided the Rodakan area of Kolwah, detaining multiple residents and transferring them to the Jirk military camp. While most of those detained were later released, Nawab, son of Noor Bakhsh and a resident of Rodakan, remained in custody.
Nawab’s body was later found in Hoshaab, Kech, bearing clear signs of custodial torture. According to local reports, his body showed extensive burn injuries, likely consistent with the use of electric shocks and other forms of physical abuse.

Asad Baloch alias Major Basit Baloch son of Mohammad and Amina Baloch and was a resident of Kulanch Pasni, Balochistan. According to organizational statement. He become part of Baloch Liberation movement in the platform of Balochistan Liberation Front BLF in 2011. He was a member of the Makran area Council of BLF and held on rank of the Major.

His family members were made victim of collective punishment. His brother Sabir Baloch was forcibly disappeared by the Pakistani army to force Asad Baloch to give up his struggle for independence. When Asad did not come under pressure, the Pakistan Army killed his brother Sabir in military custody on November 2016 and dumped his mutilated body, claiming that he was killed in an encounter. on March 4, 2016, his mother, Bibi Amina, was wounded by forces’ firing. He himself was injured in an attack by Death Squad on January 3, 2016. Similarly, the state of Pakistan and its death squads killed his three uncles, Lal Bakhsh on October 16, 2016, Yousif Baloch on March 31, 2016 and Babu on August 11, 2018. 

Asad Baloch embraced martyrdom along with other his three comrades Pervez Mehr, alias Malok Baloch; Akil Azab, alias Riaz Baloch; and Saki Baksh, alias Mureed Baloch during a clash with Pakistan’s Army in Madag Kaur, area of Kolwa, Kech, Balochistan on Oct 9, 2021.

data.biography: On 17 May 2019, a statement issued by the spokesperson of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) said that two BLA fighters and one fighter of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) were killed in combat with the Pakistan Army and its affiliated death squad, which operates under the supervision of Qambar Khan, in the Kalat area of Balochistan on Thursday, 16 May 2019. Qambar Khan is a local tribal chief in the Parod area of Kalat and the son of a well-known Baloch freedom fighter, the late Lawang Khan, who was killed by the Pakistani Army during the insurgency in Balochistan in the 1970s. According to locals and pro-freedom organizations, Qambar Khan is now working with the Pakistan Army and has formed a death squad in the area to fight against Baloch freedom fighters. Several skirmishes between BLA fighters and Qambar Khan’s death squad have also been reported in the past. The BLA spokesperson said, “Several Pakistani forces personnel and affiliates of Qambar Khan were killed in the combat, during which two BLA fighters, Mama Shams Pirkani Baloch and Doctor Shoaib Baloch alias Gazain, along with a Balochistan Liberation Front fighter, Zafar Mohammed Hasni alias Khuddal, embraced martyrdom.”

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Qaseem Murad, alias Tanveer, son of Murad Ali Siyah Pad, was a resident of Ghazi Road in Kharan district of Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2025 and served on the Noshki and Kharan fronts. He was a member of the BLA Fateh Squad. He was martyred during Operation Herof Phase II on the Kharan front.
Qaseem Murad, alias Tanveer, belonged to Kharan, a land where even the grains of sand seem to breathe stories of resistance. Raised in an atmosphere of resistance, Qaseem joined the BLA and served on the fronts of Noshki and Kharan. For him, these fronts were not merely battlefields but paths where a Sarmachar proves his loyalty, courage, and combat skills. Because of these qualities, he earned a place in the organization’s frontline unit, the Fateh Squad, a formation that always stands at the very front of battle, where only those step forward whose hearts beat not with fear but with determination for national liberation.
During Operation Herof Phase II, Qaseem was present on the Kharan front. In the clashes there, he fought alongside his fellow Sarmachars (freedom fighters) with the determination of someone whose veins carried the dream of freedom like flowing blood. In those confrontations, he ultimately sacrificed his life. His sacrifice continues to echo in the air of Kharan like a lasting story, reminding future generations that when someone fights for their homeland, their life inevitably becomes part of history.

On 28 May 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that the BLA pays tribute to the sacrifice of Bashir Baloch, alias Jalat, who laid down his life for the Baloch homeland in Tump.
The statement further stated that, on behalf of the organization, the BLA pays tribute to the sacrifice of Balochistan freedom fighter Bashir alias Jalat. In 2017, he offered his services through the platform of the BLA for the freedom of Balochistan. As a young asset of the organization, Sarmachar Bashir served for one year in Zamuran as an urban guerrilla fighter. In recognition of his urban warfare skills, the organization deployed him to the sensitive city of Quetta. There, Sangat Bashir alias Jalat inflicted severe blows on the enemy through a series of successful operations.
After serving in Quetta for three and a half years, the organization sent him to the Bolan and Kahan regions. In the rugged mountains of Bolan and Kahan, together with fellow fighters, he participated in many successful battles and confronted the enemy in exemplary attacks. Bashir alias Jalat remained active on the Kahan and Bolan fronts for two and a half years, working diligently alongside Baloch freedom fighters. He was a talented, committed, and dutiful guerrilla fighter.
On the night of 26 May 2026, during a skirmish with the enemy, he sacrificed his life for the Baloch motherland. His experiences, efforts, and selfless services to the Baloch cause are a beacon of guidance for Baloch freedom fighters and the nation. His contributions will be remembered and recorded in history with honor. Like thousands of other Baloch martyrs, he irrigated the Baloch homeland with his precious blood. The organization will not allow his sacrifices to go in vain.

Martyr Yasir Baloch, alias Meeral Baloch , Son of Wahid Baloch and was a resident Gawrag Bag Dasht, area of Kech, Balochistan. He became part of liberation movement in platform of Baloch Republican Army (BRA) in 2020 and he newly joined in a pro-independence organization, Baloch Liberation Army BLA. He embraced martyrdom along with his a comrade, Zahid  during a clash with Pakistan Army  on Nov 17, 2022 in Balor, Kolwa area of Kech, Balochistan.

On 16 February 2022, the ground forces of the Pakistani state, accompanied by air support, attacked a camp of the Baloch Nationalist Army in the early hours of the morning in the mountainous area of Kulbar, Tump. A prolonged skirmish ensued, beginning at 6:00 AM and continuing until 5:00 PM, during which the Baloch Sarmachars killed several enemy commandos and partially damaged two enemy helicopters.
In this clash, Noor Salam Noor alias Istaal, son of Bahar Baloch and a resident of Dashtuk Zamuran; Zubair Akram alias Asadjan, son of Akram Baloch and a resident of Hotabad Zamuran Bazaar; Kambar Baloch alias Mehrwan, son of Tariq and a resident of Kolaho; Sageer Baloch alias Tariq, son of Noorbakhsh and a resident of Basima; Rasool Jan alias Chirag, son of Ali Jan and a resident of Sarankan; and Hafiz Faraz alias Mullah Darwish, son of Abdul Ghani and a resident of Sarankan, were martyred.
The organization’s regional commander, Noor Salam Noor, had been associated with the Baloch armed resistance since 2010. After the martyrdom of the organization’s commander, Aqeel Jan, along with five others in 2014, Noor Salam was appointed commander of Turbat. Subsequently, in 2018, he was appointed operational commander of the entire Makuran region. During this period, he played a vital role in strengthening the organization and continued to perform his duties as an active commander in the historic resistance war against the enemy. He also played an invaluable role in representing the organization in the operations of Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sanger (BRAS) and in keeping BRAS active and operational. Moreover, he was a distinguished poet and the author of a poetry book. Through his revolutionary poetry, he also played an active role in the Baloch resistance.
The other brave sons of the motherland - Zubair, Qambar, Hafiz Faraz, Rasool Jan, and Sageer Jan - had joined the organization last year. All the Sarmachars possessed exemplary character and were true lovers of their land. The organization honors them with the title of “Pasban-e-Watan” in recognition of their bravery and historic role.

Raziq Lateef, son of Abdul Lateef, born in October 1992 in Goburd Mand, was a resident of Mand, district Kech. He received his early education in his native area, Goburd Mand, and was a student at High School in Suro, Mand, Balochistan, and a member of BSO Azad Mand Zone.
He held different positions in the organization and was soon elected as a zonal member. He played a very important role in mobilizing the Baloch youth of his surroundings to join the struggle against slavery. He had a keen interest in reading revolutionary literature. He was a strong comrade and believed in political struggle, for which he was targeted.
He was threatened many times by security agencies to quit BSO Azad, but he remained in the movement until the end. He was abducted on 13 December 2010 by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agencies from Balgatar, district Panjgur, Balochistan. His bullet-riddled body was found dumped on 18 December 2010 in Murghap, district Kech, Balochistan. His body showed extreme signs of torture.
His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in the golden pages of Baloch history.

Noor Khan, son of Amir Bakhsh, was enforcedly disappeared on July 21, 2025, by state-backed death squads from the Jhal Jahoo area of district Awaran. Just hours after his enforced disappearance, his extrajudicially killed body was recovered in the same locality, riddled with bullets.

In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Sabiri Bangulzai, alias Sherzaman, son of Mohammad Hussain Bangulzai, was a resident of Killi Sarde, Quetta, Balochistan. He was 29 years old. He joined the BLA in 2024 and later joined the Majeed Brigade the same year. During Operation Herof Phase 2, his role was Operation Commander in the Mastung Camp attack.
Sabiri Bangulzai, known among his comrades as Sher Zaman, grew up in Quetta, a city where street names may change but the dreams written on its walls endure. He was a quiet guardian of those enduring dreams. His demeanor reflected a thoughtful calmness, shaped not by performance but by depth of understanding. He spoke little, but when he did, his words carried clarity and certainty.
After joining the organization in 2024, Sabiri quickly earned the respect and trust that many spend years trying to achieve. His selection into the Majeed Brigade acknowledged not only his operational ability but also his steady judgment and inner discipline. During the Mastung Camp operation, he served as the field commander. In that role, he was not only a tactical leader but also a source of confidence for those around him. His leadership was defined by precision and the kind of strength that does not waver under pressure.

During a military operation in the Gichk area of Panjgur, Balochistan, on 15 August 2020, Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) Sarmachars (fighters) fought a prolonged battle to halt the advance of the occupying Pakistani army. Several enemy soldiers were killed and wounded in the encounter, while two brave BLA comrades were also martyred.
The two BLA Sarmachars — Asif alias Fida, son of Lal Jan, and Gulab alias Waheed, son of Pahlan — attacked the occupying Pakistani army in the Gichk Salari area to stop its advance. In the hours-long battle, several personnel of the occupying army were killed and wounded, and both Sarmachars bravely embraced martyrdom while defending the motherland.
Sangat Shaheed Asif Baloch and Sangat Shaheed Gulab Baloch had been associated with the Baloch Liberation Army since 2017. Both comrades were exemplary in their ideological maturity, bravery, hard work, and dedication. The martyred comrades rendered invaluable services to the defence of the motherland and the Baloch independence movement.
Since 13 August 2020, the Pakistan Army has launched a large-scale military operation in Panjgur, Gichk, and surrounding areas, which has since extended to the Raghay area of Besima, Sikhan, and most parts of Awaran for the past eight days (as of 20–21 August 2020). The occupying forces are violating the laws of war by targeting civilians with gunship helicopters during the operation. Meanwhile, homes of Baloch civilians are being set on fire, and dozens of women and children have been tortured and forcibly disappeared.

Haroon Zehri, son of Rauf Zehri, was born in the United Arab Emirates and received his early education there. After some time, he, along with his family, moved to their ancestral area of Khattan in Khuzdar. He completed his intermediate studies in Computer Science at Khuzdar Degree College.
After the Council Session of 2006, he joined BSO Azad and began actively participating in the organization’s activities. He was arrested multiple times by the police and law enforcement agencies due to his activism against state barbarism in Balochistan. He was a brave and courageous visionary of his generation.
When Zakir Majeed was abducted by Pakistani security agencies, Haroon, along with his friends, blocked the main highway from Shaal to Karachi, for which he was arrested by the authorities. Multiple false cases were registered against him.
Alongside his political activism, he pursued a B.Com degree from the University of Balochistan. He also had a keen interest in resolving social issues and was known as a kind and friendly person.
Due to his commitment to the Baloch cause, he chose not to pursue a government job and instead joined an NGO to meet his financial needs.
He was killed by Pakistan-backed religious extremists in Khuzdar on October 7, 2012.

Taj Muhammad Baloch, known by his Alias Taju Baloch, was a dedicated son of Mastung, Balochistan. His commitment to the cause of Baloch self determination was rooted deeply in his identity and his region.

His active engagement in the Baloch liberation movement began in 2003, the year he formally joined the ranks of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA). Over the next decade and a half, Taju Baloch distinguished himself through his consistent efforts and resolve, becoming recognized as one of the organization's most active and committed members.

Martyr Taj Muhammad Baloch made the ultimate sacrifice on December 25, 2018. He embraced martyrdom during a significant operation, alongside several key leaders and veterans of the movement, including: General Aslam Baloch, Babar Majeed, Kareem Baloch, Aman Ullah Baloch, and Akhtar Baloch.

His life and death stand as a profound testament to the steadfast resolve and sacrificial spirit demonstrated by those dedicated to the Baloch struggle.

data.biography:
On 6 February 1976 in Karachi, Asad Mengal, son of former Chief Minister of Balochistan Atta Ullah Mengal, and his friend Ahmed Kurd were sitting at the home of Baloch politician Balakh Sher Mazari. They were discussing politics over tea. As they stepped out to leave, shots and sirens suddenly filled the air. The pair were shot and whisked away by Pakistani state forces.
On 5 July 1977, Army Chief Zia-ul-Haq declared martial law and imprisoned Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. Bhutto wrote several books from jail. His last book, titled “Ufwah aur Haqeeqat” (Rumour and Reality), reveals shocking insights in Chapter Three about Asad Mengal’s disappearance. According to the book, Bhutto received a call from Ghulam Mustafa Jatoi, the Chief Minister of Sindh, who informed him about the abduction of Asad Mengal and Ahmed Kurd. After several days of unsuccessful searches for the two men, Bhutto spoke to General Tikka Khan about them. In a sad tone, Tikka Khan informed Prime Minister Bhutto that they had been killed during detention and that their bodies were buried somewhere along the route to Quetta. Nobody ever found them or their bodies.
Asad Mengal and Ahmed Kurd were the first missing persons in Balochistan under Pakistani occupation, and their case was the first high-profile case of its kind. The practice of enforced disappearances began in 1973 when Bhutto dissolved the provincial assembly of Balochistan, which was headed by Chief Minister Ataullah Mengal. Bhutto initiated a military operation, and as a result, thousands of Baloch went into exile, including Marri chieftain Khair Baksh Marri, a powerful and popular Baloch nationalist politician. This led to a militant movement against Bhutto’s regime.
Mir Mohammad Ali Talpur was one of the comrades of Khair Baksh Marri and remembers the beginning of the resistance movement and what led up to it. “Enforced disappearances began during the 1973–77 insurgency. Apart from Asad Mengal and Ahmed Kurd, Shafi Mohammad Marri, Bahar Khan Marri, Ali Dost Marri, and Allah Bakhsh Marri were picked up and never heard from again,” Mir Mohammad Ali Talpur told Lok Sujag about the early days. “There must have been other Marris and Mengals too. These people were picked up on suspicion and were likely tortured to death during interrogation.”
Baloch people from diverse religious and class backgrounds participated in the mid-1970s insurgency. For example, Duleep Dass (Dali), a Christian Marxist from Karachi, was part of Khair Bux Marri’s militant movement. He was picked up in the summer of 1976 along with his friend Sher Ali Marri from Belpat, Balochistan, and was never heard from again.
In a telephonic interview with a Pakistani media channel, conducted in the presence of Akhtar Mengal, former ISI chief General (retd.) Hamid Gul admitted that Asad Mengal and Ahmed Kurd were captured injured but alive during clashes. He stated that they were later tortured and extrajudicially killed, and that their bodies were buried near Thatta in Sindh.

On 16 July 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that the BLA eliminated more than forty personnel of the Pakistani Army and injured several others in forty-eight operations across Balochistan during the previous fifteen days. As part of the economic blockade, vehicles violating the blockade on major highways were targeted and destroyed. Furthermore, four key bridges were destroyed using planted explosive devices. During various clashes with the occupying forces, five BLA fighters - Rahimullah Mohammad Hassni, alias Zafar, son of Lumma Raaj Bibi; Khair Mohammad Khairo, alias Hammal, son of Shahbaz; Kaka Baloch, alias Kaka Rasheed, son of Shahbaz; Masood Baloch, alias Sami, son of Ghulam Jan; and Shah Nazar Baloch, alias Badal, son of Khuda Nazar - embraced martyrdom.

Khair Mohammad Khairo, alias Hammal Baloch, son of Shahbaz, was a resident of the Sangan area of Bolan. He joined the BLA in 2016 and served on the Bolan, Quetta, and Mastung fronts. He was martyred on 7 July 2026 in the Harnai area of Balochistan.
Khair Mohammad was among the brave and fearless fighters of the BLA, guided by the philosophy of sacrifice and selflessness. During the past ten years of struggle, he played a central role in the organization's important operations on the Bolan front, which proved devastating for the enemy. In every battle, he demonstrated bravery, strategic thinking, and selflessness, remaining a front-line fighter in every major military operation of the organization. Together with his brother, Martyr Kaka Baloch, and other fellow fighters, he inflicted such heavy blows on the enemy that they are remembered as significant chapters in Baloch military history.
Khair Mohammad, alias Hammal, did not regard merely taking up arms as the essence of war. Rather, he viewed warfare as a strategy based on strong organization, political consciousness, rigorous physical training, and professionalism. In this regard, he proved himself not only as a capable soldier but also as a comrade who left a lasting influence on his fellow fighters. His role in the historic Battle of Pir Ismail was remarkable, where he confronted the enemy with great determination.
Following this, during Operation Dara-e-Bolan II (Rail Hijacking), an attack described as a historic blow to the enemy, he played an important role as a front-line fighter. Alongside his fellow Sarmachars, he participated in an operation in which hundreds of enemy personnel were reportedly killed. In Operation Dara-e-Bolan I, he again demonstrated bravery and determination, inflicting severe losses on the enemy during the historic offensive. Apart from these major battles, he also fought as a front-line fighter in the battles of Mashdari, Jhalawan, and Katokach.
He continued the legacy of his family's traditions, as his family had joined the Baloch resistance in 1973, and carried forward the ideals of Martyr Ghani and Martyr Rahim. He confronted the enemy during its recent advance on the Harnai and Bolan fronts and embraced martyrdom while fighting with courage. His sacrifices and participation in these historic battles will always be remembered as an enduring example in Baloch military history.

Martyr Zahid Baloch, alias Zubair Baloch , Son of Raees Baloch and was a resident Kolwa area of Kech, Balochistan. He became part of liberation movement in platform of Baloch Republican Army (BRA) in 2021 and he newly joined in a pro-independence organization, Baloch Liberation Army BLA. He embraced martyrdom along with his a comrade, Yasir Baloch during a clash with Pakistan Army  on Nov 17, 2022 in Balor, Kolwa area of Kech, Balochistan.

On February 23, 2026, at around 5:30 PM, Pakistani forces surrounded the Khudabadan area of Panjgur district in Balochistan and raided several houses. They opened unprovoked fire, and Awais Baloch, son of Mohammad Yar and a resident of the Khudabadan area, was seriously injured. Despite his injuries, he was taken into custody by the forces and forcibly disappeared along with three brothers: Bakhtiyar, son of Haji Mohammad Hassan; Irfan, son of Haji Mohammad Hassan; and Bilal, son of Haji Hassan, as well as another young man, Hassan, son of Khalil.
The following day, on February 24, 2026, Awais’s body was dumped at Civil Hospital Panjgur. His body showed clear signs of severe torture.

On 07 February 2026, a press statement issued by the Balochistan Liberation Front stated that three of its fighters - Captain Farooq Baloch alias Sohrab, Adeel Baloch alias Hameed Baloch, and Ahmad Baloch alias Deedar - were martyred in the Tasp area of District Panjgur, Balochistan. A fourth fighter, Hafiz Abdul Wahab Badini, was martyred in Kalat District, Balochistan.
Fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front went to the Tasp area of Panjgur on January 25, 2026, to carry out a covert organizational mission. There, FC personnel attempted to surround them, resulting in an intense face to face clash between the fighters and state forces. During the clash, the BLF fighters demonstrated extraordinary courage, bravery, and steadfastness, and did not retreat even under the most difficult circumstances.
In the clash, several FC personnel were killed or wounded, while three BLF fighters embraced martyrdom while fighting valiantly. The martyred fighters continued to perform their duties until their last breath and set a practical example of determination, discipline, and commitment in the national struggle.
Ahmad Baloch alias Dedaar, son of Muhammad, resident of Chitkan, Panjgur. He joined BLF on February 12, 2024, and continued to fulfill his national responsibilities with discipline and seriousness. He performed his duties with wisdom and dedication at every stage. He participated in military actions on various fronts and stood with full determination for national freedom until his last breath. Ahmad Baloch's dedication and sacrifice constitute a source of pride for the organisation and other sarmachars. His services will always be remembered.

data.biography: Hussain was an ethnic Baloch. He started his journalist career in the Pakistani newspapers, including Daily Times and The News International. In 2012, he wrote a series of reports on "enforced disappearances and human rights violations in Balochistan". Following a police raid, interrogations and alleged death threats, he fled the country, sought political asylum and lived in exile in Sweden since 2017. In 2015, he started the online magazine, the Balochistan Times.

Inayatullah Bangulzai, alias Babar, son of Haji Ghani Bangulzai, was a resident of the Splenji area of Mastung, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in April 2024 and later joined the Majeed Brigade in August 2024.
Fidayee Inayatullah was a capable and skilled fighter. Due to his combat abilities and tactical proficiency, he was appointed as a patrol commander on the Nagao front within a short period. In this role, he played a significant part in the field training of his fellow Sarmachars. Those who served under his command greatly benefited from his operational experience and battlefield leadership.
During Operation Herof II, he was deployed on the Quetta front, regarded as one of the most sensitive theatres of battle. Engaged in frontline combat, he successfully pushed back enemy forces while providing cover for his comrades. His bravery and perseverance bolstered the morale of all those fighting beside him.
Amid intense clashes, he advanced with his fellow fighters toward the railway station near the Red Zone, where the battle raged for several hours. Holding his ground until his final moments, he remained steadfast under extreme pressure. He ultimately sacrificed his life on that front, and his name became etched into the enduring narrative of courage and sacrifice.

In the Gramkan area of Panjgur district, Balochistan, around 10:00 PM on the night of April 6, 2024, clashes erupted between fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) and the occupying Pakistani army when enemy forces attempted to raid a fighters’ hideout. The fighters, Hasrat and Abdi, who were encircled by the enemy, bravely confronted the attacking forces. During the fighting, the occupying army was also reinforced by operatives of local so-called death squads. By 3:00 AM on April 7, 2024, both valiant fighters continued to resist the enemy forces and their collaborators with determination, killing at least eleven enemy personnel and injuring several others. After fighting for five consecutive hours, both like-minded fighter brothers attained martyrdom. Martyr Hasrat, alias Asad, and Martyr Abdi, alias Sawar, son of Ali Mohammad, belonged to the Gramkan area of Panjgur. Both brothers joined the armed struggle for Baloch national liberation in 2019. They remained active on the Panjgur city, Gichk Kilkor, and Kolwah fronts in the pursuit of national freedom. Both fighters were exemplary in sincerity, dedication, and perseverance. From the very first day, the martyred companions, relying on their combat skills, inflicted repeated defeats on the enemy across multiple fronts and remained steadfast in this struggle until their final breath.

On 13th April 2026, in the Barkhan area of Balochistan, Pakistani forces shelled and bombed civilian populations, killing twelve innocent Baloch civilians, including women and children, and seriously injuring three others.

The martyrs are:

- Ali, son of Sultan Umair, aged 40
- Babul, daughter of Gulzar, aged 30
- Mir Jan, son of Ali, aged 2
- Somri, daughter of Bhangan, aged 35
- Balach, son of Sabzo, aged 70
- Shari, aged 22
- Rehman, son of Balach, aged 18
- Naikho, daughter of Jamalan, aged 17
- Allah Bakhsh, son of Balach, aged 6
- Saddo, daughter of Balach, aged 13
- Hapo, daughter of Balach, aged 8
- Mahrang, daughter of Balach, aged 2

The injured are:

- Zarbibi, daughter of Sher, aged 55
- Hazar Khan, son of Balach, aged 9
- Israr, daughter of Balach, aged 15

This is not the first time that Pakistani forces have bombed civilians in Balochistan, targeting unarmed and innocent women and children as a form of collective punishment. Nor can this be considered “collateral damage.” Rather, the Pakistani state and its forces are deliberately targeting the Baloch people to maintain an atmosphere of fear in the region, suppress internal dissent, exploit Baloch coastal resources, and continue policies of genocide against the Baloch nation.

Shehzad Baloch, son of Nazeer, was a 14-year-old student and resident of Paroom, Panjgur. He was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani state-sponsored death squads on 31 May 2025 from Kaeen, Paroom, Panjgur. For more than a year, his family waited in anguish, hoping that he would return home safely. On 25 July 2026, he was killed, and his body was found in Panjgur, Balochistan.

On 3 February 2024, the Pakistani Army’s Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) issued a statement declaring that 24 terrorists had been neutralized in a military operation conducted in the Mach area of Bolan. The operation was launched in response to Operation Darra-e-Bolan, an operation launched by the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), a Baloch pro-independence militant group, in the Mach area of Bolan district. The group reportedly maintained control of the area for three days.

However, subsequent investigations revealed that four of the deceased individuals had previously been reported as victims of enforced disappearances, and some of their cases had been registered with Baloch human rights organizations.

The identities of the deceased individuals were confirmed as follows:

- Bashir Ahmed, son of Haji Khan Marri, a resident of Mashriqi Bypass, Quetta, who was forcibly disappeared on 2 July 2023.

- Arman Marri, son of Nihal Khan Marri, a resident of Mashriqi Bypass, Quetta, who was forcibly disappeared on 2 July 2023.

- Sobadar, son of Gulzar Khan Tengani, a resident of the Main Kor area of Harnai district, who was forcibly disappeared on 9 September 2023.

- Shakil, son of Ramzan, a resident of the Mishk area of Zehri, Khuzdar district.

The family members of Bashir and Arman were also actively participating in a sit-in protest in Islamabad. Organized by the Baloch Yakjehti Committee (BYC), the sit-in was held outside the National Press Club to protest enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings.

The families tirelessly appealed to the government to secure the return of their forcibly disappeared loved ones, but all their pleas fell on deaf ears. Ultimately, they were devastated to receive the mutilated bodies of their young relatives, whom they believed had been victims of a staged encounter.

On 5 February 2024, when the family members went to Civil Hospital Quetta to receive the bodies, they were reportedly coerced into signing an unlawful form falsely stating that the deceased had links to militant groups and labeling them as terrorists. The family members refused to comply. Following a large demonstration, the bodies were eventually handed over to them.

In a statement issued on 19 November 2025 by Mazaar Baloch, spokesperson of the Baloch United Army (UBA), it was said that on 4 November at 7:30 in the morning, the Pakistan Air Force carried out a drone strike using guided missiles in the mountain range of Koh-e-Nagai in the Kalat region. As a result, four Sarmachars were martyred, including a fighter from the brother organization, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF). The organization pays tribute to them.

The fire that broke out after the drone attack severely burned the surrounding land, while unusual marks were also found on nearby rocks and stones, indicating that the weapons used contained chemical elements. The attack not only caused serious damage to the local environment but also left deep effects on the area’s natural balance.

Those who attained martyrdom in the drone attack include Dr. Mudasir Shahwani, alias Sarbuland Baloch; Shahbaz Khan Budani Marri, alias Peer Jan; Shakir Jatoi Baloch, alias Rudin Baloch; and Haris Muhammad Shahi Baloch, alias Aftab Baloch.

Shakir Jatoi joined the organization nine months ago and continued to carry out his responsibilities with great seriousness, honesty, and consistency until his martyrdom. Despite the short period, his hard work, sense of responsibility, and dedication made it clear that he was deeply committed to his ideology and his comrades.
data.fullName: Shakir Jatoi Baloch, alias Rodaan Baloch

data.biography: On September 16, 2025 the Balochistan Liberation Front carried out an ambush on the convoy of the occupying army near Kunchati Cross in Dasht, Kech. The military convoy consisted of several buses and three escort vehicles. As a result of the Sarmachars’ attack, a clash erupted which continued for 45 minutes, during which at least 4 enemy personnel were eliminated and three were wounded. In this clash, BLF comrades Sarmachar Atiq alias Captain Miran and Sarmachar Shehak alias Ashob fought bravely and attained martyrdom.

Wazir Ahmad, alias Zahid, son of Jamal, was a resident of the Gowargo area of Panjgur District, Balochistan. He joined the BLA on 20 November 2025 and served on the Chedagi, Panjgur, and Washuk fronts. He was martyred on 10 August 2026 in the Chedagi area of Panjgur.
Wazir Ahmad, alias Zahid, joined the organization in November last year and became part of the revolutionary caravan committed to the national cause and the national duty of defending the motherland. He successfully completed the organization’s rigorous and demanding physical and mental training phases, demonstrating excellent capabilities and a strong national spirit. During the training, he completed all the arduous exercises and graduated as a capable and skilled cadre. He was counted among those Sarmachar who possessed the ability and courage to face every difficult and challenging circumstance with a composed spirit, which he later demonstrated through his performance and practical activities.
On the battlefield, Martyr Wazir was among those Sangat who were committed to following organizational orders and carrying out the responsibilities assigned by the command to the best of their abilities, while striving to perform every task and activity with seriousness. During various organizational activities, his decision-making, adherence to time, and steadfastness under all kinds of difficult and challenging circumstances were prominent aspects of his character. Within a short period, he adapted himself to the battlefield environment and the realities of life there. In this context, he was made part of various organizational patrols, where he struck the enemy on several occasions and inflicted losses upon them. He possessed the ability to deliver severe blows to the enemy on the battlefield and, on several occasions, confronted the enemy face-to-face and defeated them.
He remained steadfast on the battlefield and continued to confront the enemy until his final moments. The national oath he had pledged to uphold when he joined the organization was fulfilled until his last breath, as he defended the motherland and civilian populations against the enemy’s aggression and, in this very cause, embraced martyrdom. His sacrifices will be remembered in history as those of a brave and great fighter who attained martyrdom in the defense of the motherland and its people.

Naveed Baloch, son of Hameed and a resident of Buleda in district Kech, was extrajudicially killed on 6 December 2024 by the state of Pakistan. His bullet-riddled body was found in a car in Buleda. Naveed’s family has a long history of enforced disappearances and abductions carried out by state forces.
A few months before his killing, his brother and cousin, Muslim Arif, were forcibly abducted, although Muslim Arif was later released. Another cousin, Uzair, son of Umeed, was abducted by armed forces just seven days before Naveed’s murder. Naveed had been trying to secure Uzair’s release, visiting the camp twice without success. On his third attempt, he was taken to the camp, where he was inhumanely killed.
Naveed was a vocal advocate for his brothers and other Baloch individuals who had been forcibly disappeared. He was also active during the Baloch National Gathering, working for the Baloch cause.
