In the intense clashes in Noshki, he scripted a new saga of bravery and embraced martyrdom while defending his birthplace.

Parvez Baloch, son of Mazar Baloch, was a resident of Pidrak, Kech, and worked as a teacher. He was abducted and forcibly disappeared by a death squad backed by the Pakistani state in the early hours of 13 October 2026 from Main Bazar, Pasni, Balochistan.

The following morning, on 14 October 2026, the death squad killed Parvez Baloch and dumped his mutilated body in the Daroband area of Pasni, Balochistan.

On 9 September 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of ten fighters belonging to the organization. He paid tribute to the Sarmachars who were martyred while defending national liberation and their homeland, Balochistan.
- The statement identified the following fighters:
1-  Akhtar Dawood, alias Ali Sher, son of Asad Sajidi.
2- Khalil Ahmad, alias Ustad Awais, son of Sher Ahmad.
3-  Imran, alias Aajo, son of Saifullah.
4-  Hasil, alias Munir Ahmad, son of Sher Mohammad.
5- Inayatullah, alias Sher Zaman, son of Manzoor Ahmad.
6- Asad Rahim, son of Rahim Baksh.
7- Mujeeb Ur Rehman, alias Shay Mureed, son of Saeed Ahmad.
8- Sahil, alias Arman, son of Peeral.
9- Javed, alias Murshid.
10- Mohammad Younis, alias Taleb, son of Mohammad Omar.

Hasil, alias Munir Ahmad, son of Sher Mohammad, resident of Lanjar, began his part in the Baloch national liberation struggle through the BLF platform in 2025. He was an extremely sincere, hardworking, fearless, and disciplined fighter. He carried out various military and organizational duties during guerrilla warfare on the difficult fronts of Jhao, Naal, and Awaran. He carried out every organizational duty with great diligence and, through his character, hard work, and revolutionary spirit, earned a respected place among his fellow fighters in the organization’s ranks. On 9 August 2026, while BLF fighters were on a routine patrol in the Jhao wadhi, they were attacked by local death-squad personnel at Merani Kour. In this clash, Martyr Hasil displayed great bravery, fought with courage, and was martyred. His courage gave the other fighters the chance to take up a stronger position, from which they counterattacked, killing several death-squad personnel and seizing their weapons.

On the morning of May 26, 2025, Ghous Bakhsh Baloch, son of Master Elahi Bakhsh and a resident of Malar Kahn, Awaran District, was summoned by Pakistani military personnel to a nearby camp. Hours later, his body was discovered bearing multiple bullet wounds, in what was clearly an extrajudicial execution carried out with no legal justification or due process.

On 26 January 2018, the Pakistani armed forces launched an attack on a base camp of the Baloch Republican Army (BRA) in the Kolwah area of Balochistan. The operation involved a large number of ground troops, supported by gunship helicopters from the air, in an attempt to seize control of the camp. However, through bravery and effective military strategy, BRA fighters successfully foiled the attempt and forced the forces to retreat.
During the operation, the forces’ attempt to capture the camp led to several hours of direct, face-to-face clashes at different locations with the occupying personnel, resulting in the deaths of several soldiers. In the course of this direct combat, an organization member, Shoaib Baloch, alias Lakmeer, blocked the enemy’s advance in order to secure a safe escape route for his fellow fighters. While resisting the forces for three hours, he ultimately embraced martyrdom.
Martyr Shoaib had been associated with the BRA for a long period. In recognition of his great sacrifice, the organization conferred upon him the title “Kohsar-e-Watan”.

Zohaib Ahmad Rodeni, a 19-year-old son of Salam Rodeni and a member of the Baloch Republican Party (BRP), was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces on 8 August 2010. His body was later found dumped in the Khuzdar district on 14 August 2010.

Martyr Samad Baloch,  son of Mohammad Hussain and was a resident Parag, Kolwa area of Kech, Balochistan. He became part of Baloch liberation movement in platform of the Baloch Republican Army (BRA) in 2013. He newly joined in Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) before same days of his martyrdom. He embraced martyrdom along with eight comrades, Jalil Sher Baloch, Javid Baloch, Dad Shah Baloch, Kambar Baloch, Shoaib Baloch, Rahmdi Baloch, Haris Baloch and Nawaz Baloch  in a drone attack of Pakistan Army  on Nov 29, 2022 in Jath, Kolwa area of Kech, Balochistan.

On the morning of January 8, 2026, at around 10 AM in the Zamuran area of Buleda, the Pakistani military carried out a drone attack on the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) camp, resulting in the martyrdom of four BLF fighters. The martyrs include Hussain, alias Kamal Baloch; Akbar, alias Tahir Baloch; Waseem, alias Mero Baloch; and Huzaifa, alias Nodan Baloch.
Captain Hussain, alias Kamal Baloch, son of Abdul Ghafoor and resident of Buleda Gilli Chairman Bazaar, joined the BLF on February 11, 2021. Hussain, alias Kamal, was a brave and hardworking fighter who played an important role in the organizational leadership as deputy commander of the camp. He oversaw camp discipline, training, and mission planning, demonstrating strategy and perseverance in every decision. His leadership and dedication served as a guiding light for the sarmachars and strengthened the organization. Captain Hussain, alias Kamal’s, sacrifice and service boost the morale of fighters and set an example of bravery, responsibility, and dedication for future generations.

Zaheer Baloch, son of Ramzan and a resident of Gebun, district Kech, was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani law enforcement agencies from his home on April 16, 2025.

Following his enforced disappearance , local media and human rights organizations reported his case and demanded his immediate release. Despite these calls, after seven months of enforced disappearance, Pakistani forces killed him in a fake encounter in Dasht, Kech, on September 20, 2025, along with three other victims.

Naeem Baloch was a Baloch Students Organization - Azad (BSO-Azad) activist who was brutally murdered by Pakistani Frontier Corps forces during a raid on his house in the Tootak area of Khuzdar district, Balochistan, on 18 February 2011.

The freedom fighter of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), Naseer Ahmed, alias Sikandar, was martyred on 23 July 2024 in the area of Gichk after being bitten by a poisonous snake while carrying out his duties in the struggle for Baloch national liberation.
Naseer Ahmed, alias Sikandar, son of Mullah Mohammad Isa, belonged to the Basima Solair area of Washuk. He joined an allied organization in 2015 and began armed resistance against Baloch national subjugation. In 2020, he formally became a member of the Baloch Liberation Army.
Naseer Baloch carried out national duties on the fronts of Panjgur, Washuk, Rakhshan, Goran, Kolwah, Hoshab, and Kilkor. Through his participation in major battles, he played a significant role in inflicting heavy losses on the enemy.
His family was continuously subjected to repression by the Pakistani army, and his home was burned down six times during military operations. Despite these hardships, he did not retreat even an inch from his stance on national freedom. Through his exemplary character and sacrifice, he made it clear to the enemy that the Baloch prioritize national freedom over subjugation and regard martyrdom on this path above all else.

Abdul Haleem Mohammad Shahi, alias Danish, son of Karam Khan Mohammad Shahi, was a resident of the Kohak area of Kalat, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Mastung front. He was martyred on 19 September 2026 in the Shirnaap area of Mastung, Balochistan.
Abdul Haleem Mohammad Shahi, who waged fierce attacks against the enemy and subdued them, made the revolutionary decision this year to join the great collective cause of national liberation and, from the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army, began his national, historical, and revolutionary role. After joining the organization, he was transferred to camp, where he joined a training camp.
He attained the supreme rank of martyrdom while performing his national duty against the enemy at Shirnaap, Mastung, inscribing his name in the annals of history as a great hero.
Qaim Deen Mengal was martyred in a battle with the Pakistani army on 16 May 2008.

Habib Baloch, alias Khalid Baloch, son of Mohammad Saleem, was a resident of Katagri, Panjgur. He joined the BLA in December 2025 and moved to the Mountain Front in April 2026, where he served on the Gwargo and Kilkoor fronts. He was martyred on 17 September 2026 in the Gwargo area of Panjgur, Balochistan.
Habib Baloch was a fighter of military prowess who was relentless in battle against the enemy. He rejected Pakistan’s illegal occupation and, a year before his martyrdom, decided to join the cause of freedom, becoming active on the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army. Under organizational discipline, he first received combat and revolutionary training at a training camp, after which he joined the front lines. He was known among his comrades as a brave fighter who put tremendous effort into every organizational task and activity. He took an active part in operations against the enemy in the areas of Kilkoor and Gwargo.
Based on his hard work and abilities, he was soon made part of a patrol team, where he performed exceptionally well. He was always among the comrades at the forefront of strengthening the organization and expanding its presence in the region, as well as taking military action against the enemy. These military and revolutionary abilities remained with him until the end. He was martyred during an engagement in Gwargo after leading a major attack on the enemy alongside his comrades and subsequently inflicting heavy losses on them while halting their advance in the area. By offering his life as a sacrifice on the path to national liberation, he immortalized himself in history forever.

Israr Baloch, son of Mohammad Anwar, was a 25 year old master tailor and a resident of Qambrani Road, Killi Bangulzai, Quetta. He was taken into custody on 25 March 2026 by Eagle Force personnel from Qambrani Link Road near Keachi Baig Police Station and was later killed in custody.
He was detained without any legal justification, warrant, or formal charge. Following his detention at Keachi Baig Police Station, he was transferred through Hazar Town Police Station and Shaal Kot Police Station in Hazar Ganji before being moved to New Saryab Police Station, where he was brutally killed on 1 April 2026.
The transfer of Israr Baloch across multiple police stations indicates a deliberate effort to conceal his whereabouts, deny his family access to him, and keep him isolated without providing any information to them. He was subjected to custodial physical and psychological torture. His movement through four police stations clearly reflects a system that detains, abuses, and kills without accountability. All departments of the forces, along with the judicial system, are implicated in the Baloch genocide.

Mohammad Kareem Dehwar, son of Shafi Mohammad, a 34 year old student, was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces on 14 February 2011. Two months later, on 17 April 2011, his body was found on the Western Bypass in Quetta, Balochistan.

data.organization: Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) / Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS)
data.biography:
At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Ghulam Jilani, also known as Miran, son of Ghulam Rabbani, was a resident of Faizabad, Dhadar Kachhi, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2024 and served in the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). He was martyred during Operation Herof Phase II on the Quetta front.
Ghulam Jilani, from the land of Dhadar Kachhi, was among those Sarmachars who chose to resist national subjugation rather than accept it as destiny. Through his actions and character, he demonstrated that when a conscious individual makes the freedom of his nation the purpose of his life, his steps do not falter in the face of fear or expediency. Because of these qualities, he was selected for the organization’s Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS).
During Operation Herof Phase II, Miran fought against the enemy alongside his fellow Sarmachars on the Quetta front. In the Saryab area, at Wali Jet, during a prolonged clash with enemy forces, he displayed steadfast courage and ultimately sacrificed his life.
Qadeer Baloch, was a resident of the Dasht, Kech area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 25 May 2016 in Balochistan.

On November 25, 2025, in the Washbud area of Panjgur district in Balochistan, operatives of a Death Squad working under Pakistani forces abducted 32 year old Pazeer Baloch, son of Mohammad Amin, and kept him forcibly disappeared. Several months later, on February 7, 2026, his mutilated body was dumped.

Mir Lawang Khan was born in 1901 at Mir Habib Khan’s house in Killi Mengal, Noshki. He was the second of five brothers and the elder brother of the Balochi national poet, Mir Gul Khan Naseer. His family belonged to the Zagar Mengal sub-tribe of the Mengal tribe.
Mir Lawang Khan received his early education in his native town of Noshki. At that time, Noshki had only a primary school, so Mir Lawang Khan studied only up to the fourth grade.
Mir Lawang Khan settled in Dasht-e-Goran, a small town in Kalat District, after the forced annexation of Balochistan into Pakistan in 1948.
After the NAP government in Balochistan was dismissed on 13 February 1973, the Prime Minister of Pakistan, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, launched a military operation in Balochistan. On 7 August 1973, Pakistani troops entered Dasht-e-Goran to search for weapons and freedom fighters. Mir Lawang Khan chose to fight rather than allow them to enter his village.
A long battle ensued between the Pakistan Army, which was equipped with state-of-the-art weaponry, and a handful of Baloch fighters who had chosen to fight alongside Mir Lawang Khan and were armed with outdated and obsolete rifles. After almost a full day of fighting and the loss of 25 soldiers, the Pakistan Army was able to subdue the 35 Baloch fighters who had taken a stand against them.
At the age of 72, Shaheed Mir Lawang Khan and his 35 companions sacrificed their lives for the honour of the Baloch nation. They chose to die rather than allow the troops to violate the honour of the Baloch people by intruding into the homes of the female members of their village.
Shaheed Mir Lawang Khan left behind a legacy that will not be forgotten by the Baloch nation: that the honour of the nation and the motherland comes before life itself.

Khalid Zehri, a resident of Khuzdar, was forcibly disappeared on 23 March 2025 by Pakistani security forces and the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) from Zaidi town, Khuzdar. He remained in incommunicado detention for over three months before being killed in custody.
On 29 June 2025, his tortured and bullet-riddled body was found dumped—bearing clear signs of severe physical torture and extrajudicial execution.
He was an ordinary civilian earning a livelihood to support his family.

Operation Dara-e-Bolan, which began on 29 January 2024 continued for two days until 31 January 2024 and was successfully concluded after achieving its intended objectives. A total of 385 Sarmachars from four different units of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) participated in Operation Dara-e-Bolan. Among them were 12 Fidayeen from the BLA’s Majeed Brigade. The other participating units included the Fateh Squad, the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS) and the Intelligence Wing.
Operation Dara-e-Bolan commenced on the evening of 29 January 2024 at 9:00 pm local time and continued for two days. After achieving the desired results, the BLA’s Senior Command Council announced the conclusion of Operation Dara-e-Bolan on 31 January 2024 at 7:00 pm and issued instructions to all units to vacate their positions and report back to their base camps.
During the operation, BLA Sarmachars took complete control of an area within a 70 kilometre radius, including Mach city and the strategically important National Highway N-65. Over the course of Operation Dara-e-Bolan, a total of 78 enemy personnel were killed. These included 45 Frontier Corps (FC) personnel who were killed within the first three hours of the operation in Mach city; 10 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on an army camp at the Pir Ghaib Bolan location; 4 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on a military convoy at the Gokurt Mach location; 12 regular army personnel who were killed on 30 January when Majeed Brigade Fidayeen eliminated them and entered the FC headquarters; and at least 5 SSG commandos who were targeted and killed by the Fidayeen on 31 January 2024. In addition, two police personnel were also killed, including one Station House Officer (SHO).
A large number of Levies and police personnel were captured by the BLA during the operation; however, as they were Baloch, they were released. During Operation Dara-e-Bolan, 13 brave fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army attained martyrdom. Of these, 12 martyred Sarmachars belonged to the Majeed Brigade Fidayeen, while one martyred Sarmachar was from the BLA’s Fateh Squad.
The martyred Sarmachars were: Qasim Baloch, Saddam Hussain, Salal Baloch, Farooq Baloch, Atta Baloch, Hammal Momin, Zeeshan Zehri, Nadir Bangulzai, Nizam Baloch, Zeeshan Baloch, Jamal Baloch, Wadood Satakzai, and Kashif Shahwani.
Qasim, alias Tangi Lala, son of Fazal Baloch, belonged to the Heronk area of Turbat. He had been associated with the armed struggle for Baloch national liberation since 2013. For over a decade, he proved himself to be an outstanding guerrilla fighter and inflicted significant losses on enemy forces in several major engagements. In 2018, he voluntarily offered his services to the BLA Majeed Brigade and waited for five years with exceptional patience and secrecy for his mission. When he was finally assigned a special covert mission during Operation Dara-e-Bolan, he sacrificed his life and completed the mission successfully.

Safiullah Baloch, alias Ameer, son of Abdul Wahab, was a resident of the Khudabadan area of Panjgur, Balochistan. He joined the BLA on 19 December 2019 as an urban guerrilla and moved to the Mountain Front on 12 December 2025. He held a B.Sc. degree. He served on the Panjgur front and was martyred on 17 September 2026 in the Gwargo area of Panjgur, Balochistan.
After gaining awareness of national slavery and occupation and awakening his intellectual and ideological consciousness, Martyr Safiullah began his national responsibilities as an urban guerrilla on the Panjgur front in 2019, seven years ago, through the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army for national liberation. For six years, he fulfilled his responsibilities on the urban front as a key asset of the organization. As an educated young man, he quickly grasped the operational needs of the war front and guerrilla activities and served as a dynamic Sangat for the organization on the urban front. In recognition of this trust and his abilities, he was given administrative responsibilities on the urban front, and he also provided the organization with crucial intelligence that contributed to the success of several operations.
He continued to provide the organization with vital intelligence even while living under harsh urban conditions and in the worst combat situations. After six years as an urban guerrilla, he was transferred to the front lines last year under organizational orders and soon joined the combat lines based on his experience and abilities. Over the past year, he took an active part in key economic, military, and organizational policies aimed at securing superiority over the enemy on the Gwargo front, and he proved himself to be a brave and resolute sarmachar. He remained steadfastly committed to that goal until the end, faced the enemy, attained martyrdom, and became immortal in history.

Originally from the Parom area of the Panjgur district in Eastern Balochistan, Dosta Mahmood Baloch was an unarmed political activist who had moved to Sham-E-Sar, Sistan and Balochistan (Western Balochistan), to escape Pakistan's military actions. He was identified by Pakistan as the primary target of the missile strike.

On 25 August 2024 Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch announced the launch of a "Fidayeen Operation" named "Herof" across Balochistan. As part of this operation, fidayeen from the BLA's elite unit, Majeed Brigade, have attacked the main camp of the Pakistani forces in Bela and have successfully infiltrated it. Meanwhile, other BLA fighters have taken full control of all major highways across Balochistan, blocking them completely.
During Operation “Herof,” 44 attacks were carried out simultaneously at 40 locations across 13 districts of Balochistan. As a result, 130 Pakistani army personnel were killed and 55 were injured. In addition, gas pipelines were destroyed at 2 locations, railway tracks at 7 locations, and 2 bridges were blown up.
During the operation, 13 vehicles transporting minerals were set on fire. Blockades were also established at 14 locations across Balochistan, and 3 members of a “death squad” were killed.
As part of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayee (suicide) operation “Herof,” the BLA’s Majeed Brigade carried out an attack on the Pakistani army’s Bela camp. The Majeed Brigade maintained control of the camp for twenty hours, during which 68 enemy personnel were killed.
Nine fidayeen (self-sacrificing fighters) of the Majeed Brigade at Bela camp - Ghaus Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Talib), Mahal Baloch (alias Zilan Kurd), Rizwan Baloch (alias Hammal), Mohammad Baloch (alias Meerak), Fazal Gul Zehri (alias Shawaiz), Tayyab Baloch (alias Lala), Junaid Zehri (alias Kami), Mohammad Asif Nechari (alias Naveed), and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Khalid) - along with Shafqat (alias Dayar) of the Fateh Squad in Mastung, were martyred in the operation.
Ghaus Baksh Sumalani, alias Talib, and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani, alias Khalid, were brothers. They took part in the same operation and were martyred while defending their motherland.

Mohammad Raheem Langove, alias Asfand, son of Jan Mohammad Langove, was a resident of Kalat. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Kalat Front. He was martyred on 15 July 2026 in Nighar, Surab, Balochistan.
Martyr Mohammad Raheem Langove, recognizing the enemy’s aggression, indecency, and barbaric designs that year, decided to become part of the great caravan of national freedom. Joining the revolutionary ranks of the Baloch Liberation Army, he took up a position on the Kalat Front against the enemy forces. Within a short period, having understood the organization’s revolutionary and national program, he sincerely completed his military training in order to prepare himself both physically and mentally. He did not regard the training merely as instruction in the basic use and handling of weapons; rather, he accepted it as the finest and most disciplined preparation for war and carried out even the harshest exercises with full dedication and discipline.
After completing the basic courses, he began taking part in military engagements and demonstrated his combat abilities in every military and organizational operation. He possessed the ability to break through enemy encirclements, turn the course of events on the battlefield in his favor, and gain the upper hand over the enemy at any given moment. He was a comrade well aware of the modern requirements of guerrilla warfare and of Balochistan’s geographical advantages against the enemy’s field units, and he made full use of these geographical advantages on the battlefield. Owing to the scarcity of resources available in guerrilla warfare, he understood the need for and importance of using them effectively and possessed an excellent ability to employ limited resources according to circumstances. A realistic understanding of battlefield conditions was a prominent aspect of his military capabilities.
These military qualities and skills remained with him until the end. Owing to his ability to strike the enemy forcefully, he was an active sarmachar in the organization’s policy of advancement. He attained martyrdom while fighting the enemy face-to-face, keeping alive through his blood the consciousness and conviction upon which he had based his decision to join the struggle. His sacrifices for the preservation of a great historic human civilization and for the restoration of the state will forever remain part of Baloch national memory.

Shah Nawaz Baloch, son of Faiz Mohd and a resident of Gichk, Panjgur, was an active political activist. During his student life, he joined the BSO Azad Panjgur Zone, where he gained political insight and wisdom from Martyr Agha Abid Shah. Agha Abid Shah was abducted and killed by Pakistani forces in 2011.
Shah Nawaz later moved to Karachi and continued his political struggle from there, remaining actively engaged until his martyrdom. During his wedding ceremony, the Pakistan Army raided Gwarjk, Mashkai, and arrested him along with three of his relatives. On the same day, 15 April 2015, they were killed in what was described as a fake encounter.
Karima Baloch, who was the chairperson of BSO Azad at that time, paid tribute to him and stated that “he was one of the younger comrades of the organization.” They had recently been married. Therefore, we titled them the “Grooms of Balochistan.”

Martyr Major Kareem Baloch Alias Mullah Bahram Baloch, son of Haji Shay Muhammad Baloch and was a resident of Goburd, Mand area of Kech, Balochistan. He affiliated with Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) since 2008. He leaded and nurtured the freedom fighters politically and with guerrilla tactics for years as a member of regional council of Makuran region of BLF.  Due to his talent and experience became regional camp commander in 2019.  
He embraced martyrdom in a drone attack of Pakistan’s military along with his seven comrades, Mullah Bakhsh, Manzoor Baloch,  Asif Baloch, Shehzad Baloch, Jalal Baloch,  Talib Baloch and Hazza Baloch on Feb 23, 2023 in Mazanband area of Kech, Balochistan

Haris Mohammad Shahi, alias Aftab Jan
data.biography:
In a statement issued on 19 November 2025 by Mazaar Baloch, spokesperson of the Baloch United Army (UBA), it was said that on 4 November at 7:30 in the morning, the Pakistan Air Force carried out a drone strike using guided missiles in the mountain range of Koh-e-Nagai in the Kalat region. As a result, four Sarmachars were martyred, including a fighter from the brother organization, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF). The organization pays tribute to them.

The fire that broke out after the drone attack severely burned the surrounding land, while unusual marks were also found on nearby rocks and stones, indicating that the weapons used contained chemical elements. The attack not only caused serious damage to the local environment but also left deep effects on the area’s natural balance.

Those who attained martyrdom in the drone attack include Dr. Mudasir Shahwani, alias Sarbuland Baloch; Shahbaz Khan Budani Marri, alias Peer Jan; Shakir Jatoi Baloch, alias Rudin Baloch and Haris Muhammad Shahi Baloch, alias Aftab Baloch.

Haris Muhammad Shahi, alias Aftab Baloch, formally joined the United Baloch Army two years ago. In a short time, he earned distinction due to his exceptional intelligence, strong resolve, and military skill. As an urban guerrilla, he closely monitored enemy movements, operated a strong information network, and played an important role in ground defense. He later played key roles on the challenging fronts of Koh Nagai, Mach, Kolpur and Bibi Nani. Until his final breath, he bravely confronted the enemy for the defense of his homeland and offered an eternal sacrifice that elevated him to the noble rank of martyrdom.

Shah Hussain, son of Shafi Jan, a 26 years young police constable and a resident of Tasp, Panjgur, was enforcedly disappeared on October 29, 2025 by Pakistani forces and later released on November 03, of the same year and was extrajudicial killed by state-backed death squad on May 24, 2026, in the area of Tasp, Panjgur, Balochistan.

On 29 March 2026, a statement issued by the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson, Jeeyand Baloch, stated that between 19 March and 28 March, the Sarmachars of the Baloch Liberation Army carried out 14 separate operations in Washuk, Kharan, Kalat, Mastung, Surab, Khuzdar, Quetta, Turbat, and Barkhan. These actions resulted in the deaths of 18 personnel of the occupying army and left several others injured. The Sarmachars successfully took control of various check posts, detained personnel, and confiscated weapons and military equipment. During these operations, two BLA Sarmachars - Abdullah Rodeni, alias Sarban (19 March 2026), and Yaqoob Baloch, alias Durra (21 March 2026) - attained martyrdom during direct clashes with the occupying forces.
Yaqoob Baloch, alias Durra, son of Gul Sher Baloch and a resident of Dasht, Turbat, joined the BLA in 2024. He served on the fronts of Shoor Parod, Kalat, and Mastung. He attained martyrdom on 21 March 2026 after succumbing to wounds sustained during an intense clash with the occupying army in Gurgina, Mastung.
Wazeer Khan Baloch, was a resident of the Kalat area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 15 May 2015 in Balochistan.

In continuation of the Fidayee (self-sacrificing) operation carried out on 8 July 2026 in Khuzdar city, Balochistan, against the compound of state asset and national traitor Shafiq Mengal, alias Shafiq Laghor (the coward) which resulted in the deaths of 34 members of Shafiq's death squad and the martyrdom of five members of the BLA. According to the organization, this operation, marking the commencement of the first phase of 'Operation Marg-e-Ghadaran' manifests the BLA's growing operational and intelligence capabilities against the colonial system and the criminal networks nurtured under it.

The five Fidayeen involved in this complex battle successfully breached the enemy's siege and retreated safely, while five other freedom fighters sacrificed their lives during various stages of this organized action to complete this crucial operation.
The operation commenced with the breaching of the outer security perimeter of Shafiq Laghor’s house, a responsibility undertaken by a talented Fidayee of the Majeed Brigade, Beebarg alias Pulliya Osama. The 22 year old Fidayee Beebarg hailed from the Tindilan area of Mastung and belonged to the Bangulzai tribe of the Baloch, formally joining the BLA and the Majeed Brigade in 2025. Following his enlistment into the organization's ranks, he remained active on the challenging military fronts of Khuzdar and Dasht, Quetta. Prior to this operation, he had demonstrated outstanding performance during 'Operation Herof 2' in the attack on the Frontier Corps central camp established at the Agriculture Office in Quetta. During the Khuzdar operation, he commanded the explosive laden vehicle, skillfully ramming it into the main gate of Shafiq Laghor's compound. Consequently, the outer defensive lines and checkpoints were reduced to rubble within seconds, instantly killing a large number of the enemy's armed guards stationed there and thereby clearing the path for the inner advance.
Immediately after the severe chaos caused by the explosion at the main gate, the next operational objective was to breach the security network of the compound's inner building, a task completed with utmost dedication and bravery by another valiant Fidayee of the Majeed Brigade, Zia Ur Rahman alias Imran. Hailing from Khadkocha, the 19-year-old Fidayee Zia Ur Rahman belonged to the Shahwani tribe and became a part of the BLA and the Majeed Brigade in 2025. Due to his exceptional combat skills, he quickly rose to the forefront of organizational activities on rigorous fronts such as Khuzdar and Koh-e-Maran. He had also been part of the frontline against the enemy on the Hazarganji front during 'Operation Herof 2.' In this battle of Khuzdar, right after Beebarg’s Fidayee strike, he courageously braved enemy fire to gain entry into the inner building of the compound and detonated the Fidayee jacket strapped to his body. As soon as the inner security line collapsed, the remaining Fidayeen entered the compound and assumed various positions, where Fidayee Mohammad Ramzan Zehri, alias Shaban, took a stand at the main gate and its surrounding vital sectors to confront the enemy on the frontline. The phase of maintaining resistance inside this enemy stronghold until the final moments and penetrating Shafiq Laghor’s residential block to clear all sides was carried out by two Fidayeen comrades of the Majeed Brigade, Shahzaib Baloch alias Sagaar and Shahzain Baloch alias Chedag. Chairman Ghulam Muhammad was born on January 1, 1959, in Mand, the hometown  of the national poet Mulla Fazul, in the house of Muhammad Ayub Baloch. He was born during  the harsh rule of General Ayub Khan, known for his cruelty, at a time when Baloch bloodshed  was common. However, Chairman Ghulam Muhammad was raised by a courageous mother,  Bibi Hairnisa. Initially named Naseer Ahmed Khan, in the honour of Meer Naseer Khan Noori,  but his grandfather called him Ghulam Muhammad. Once, in his childhood, they visited a  hospital, and on the way back, his father showed him two tombs, symbolizing bravery and  courage inherited from their ancestors who fought against the British. He had a deep interest  in listening to stories of Baloch ancestors who fought for freedom. His father often recounted  tales of brave martyrs who sacrificed their lives for their land, sparking's keen interest. From  an early age, he displayed a talent for reciting poetry beautifully. He had a strong interest in  both politics and poet. 
He began his education at Soro (Mand) School in 1965. At the age of eight, in 1967,  when the Baloch Student Organization (BSO) was founded, he actively participated in BSO  circles and other programs, eagerly absorbing knowledge. During the height of BSO's influence  in the Bhutto era, Ghulam Muhammad participated in all political activities under the guidance  of Shaheed Fida Ahmad. 
In 1974, he became the Zonal Secretary of Mand Zone amidst Balochistan's turmoil,  where political workers were being targeted by the state. Despite the adversities, he continued  his work with great enthusiasm and strategic planning, aiming to foster the nation against state  oppression. 
Due to curfews and state atrocities against political workers, he went underground for  some periods. upon returning home, his mother expressed her anguish over the harm he was  facing. However, he reassured her, stating that his actions were for a cause he believed in, one  that would make her proud. He emphasized his commitment to securing the independence of  their land, refusing to let State repression upon Baloch 
During Bhutto's reign, many Baloch families migrated to Afghanistan but he further  strengthened his resolve and ideological vision. He remained focused solely on the  independence of the nation, demonstrating remarkable foresight and determination. 
He sacrificed his personal desires to serve his nation diligently, guided initially by  Shaheed Fida Ahmed, whose mentorship had a profound impact on the Baloch cause. 
The Bhutto era strengthen Baloch political workers ideologically, with suppression only  fuelling their resistance. Those efforts intensified to nationalist ideas in Baloch youth,  emphasizing unity and the struggle for independence. In 1979, upon his return from Qatar, he urged his brother to arrange a meeting with Sheer  Muhammad Marri, a renowned Baloch guerrilla fighter. During their encounter, Marri advised  him against aligning with Ghaus Bakhsh Bezanjo and Attaullah Mengal, considering them  rebellious to the Baloch cause. 
In 1980, he completed his matriculation from Government High School Soro (Mand)  with distinction, followed by further education in Karachi in 1981, where he joined Sindh  Muslim College. Amidst his studies, he actively participated in political activities, forming  connections with fellow activists. 
In 1982, his dedication for Baloch cause led to his appointment as the General Secretary  of the Karachi Zone. His honesty and courage in managing student activities and nurturing  ideological vision were widely appreciated. 
Recognizing the need for Baloch politics in Karachi, he mobilized Baloch youth, successfully  organizing BSO's political program in the area. 
In 1984, under Shaheed Fida Ahmed's leadership, BSO reunited under its original ideology,  with Ghulam Muhammad being appointed as the provisional president of BSO Sindh. 
In 1985, after completing his graduation, he joined the University of Balochistan where  he further continued his political activism. In 1986, during the 8th council session of BSO, he  was selected as the Junior Vice Chairman. His political qualities and insight promoted  organizational unity and adherence to decisions. 
In 1987, amidst challenges from Kahoor Khan and the creation of BSO SOBH, Ghulam  Muhammad played a crucial role unifying BSO once again. Along with Shaheed Fida Ahmed,  they founded the Baloch National Youth Movement (BNYM), aiming to fight for Balochistan's  victory. 
At the first gathering of BNYM, they declared a departure from parliamentary politics,  stating that Baloch issues could not be resolved through parliamentary means. This stance  resonated with many BSO workers, who openly supported BNYM for the Baloch cause. In  1987, BSO and BNYM organized a public gathering in Mand, where the revolutionary spirit  was worth watching, Baloch women and children waving BSO flags and chanting slogans in  support of both organizations. 
Following Shaheed Fida Ahmed's tenure, Waheed Baloch became Chairman, and  Shaheed Ghulam Muhammad became the Secretary-General of BSO. Guided by Shaheed Fida  Ahmed's ideology, Ghulam Muhammad emphasized rejecting parliamentary politics and  focused on the real vision for the Baloch struggle. As the General Secretary of BSO, he met  with the Afghan ambassador, initially denying support for the ANP movement in Quetta, but  eventually gave them aid during their strike. 
In the 1990 Council Session, he was chosen as the Chairman of BSO. In this role, he  reiterated that parliamentary politics did not serve the interests of Baloch youth or the Baloch  cause. In 1991, state violence erupted when members of the organization were martyred during  a conflict at the Agriculture College in Mastung. Following Shaheed Fida Ahmed's death, BNYM split again, leading to the formation  of a new party, (BNM) by Dr. Malik and Dr. Abdul Hai. Ghulam Muhammad joined BNM after  his BSO membership. In 1993, he concluded his first political career with BSO, having served  sincerely from 1973 to 1993, during which he excelled in student politics. 
Transitioning to party politics, Ghulam Muhammad joined BNM in 1993, aiming to  continue Shaheed Fida Ahmed's vision. Despite challenges and rebellious acts by Dr. Abdul  Hai and Dr. Malik, he remained steadfastly connected to the party. He was then appointed as  the Zonal President of Kech. 
During internal conflicts within the party, Ghulam Muhammad remained resolute,  affirming that such rebellions were not sincere in serving the Baloch cause. In 1997-1998, after  the failure of party, Akhtar Mengal, Dr. Hai, and Mahmood Khan Achakzai introduced  PONAM Alliance. Ghulam Muhammad, as the Junior Vice President, clarified that BNM had  no affiliation with PONAM. 
 The 2002 Pakistani Elections, where Dr. Malik and Dr. Hai participated. While chairman  Ghulam Muhammad embarked on a revolutionary journey by establishing a new organizing  body within BNM, standing alongside Lala Muneer, Shaheed Rasool Bakhsh, and Waja  Muhammad Hussain Baloch. 
In the 2004 Council Session of BNM, Shaheed Ghulam Muhammad declared that the  party should support armed struggle for Baloch liberation, for armed organizations, and  complete disengagement from parliamentary politics. Despite state repression, he continued to  lead the party, advocating for national liberation and internationalizing Baloch issues. After all  his struggle and fight for Baloch freedom. State threatened him and his family trying to  suppress his voice for Baloch freedom movement. 
He was illegally abducted on December 3rd, 2006. His abduction resulted in  widespread demonstrations, so he was later released on October 10th, 2007. In the 2008  Council Session, he was re-elected as president, reiterating the party's goals for national  liberation despite State repression. In 3rd April 2009 he again become the victim of illegal  abduction alongside Lala Muneer (then Voice Chairman of BNM) and Sheer Muhammad (then  central committee member of BRP). In 9th April 2009 after a week of his abduction his bullet  riddled body was found in Murgaap along with Lala Muneer and Sher Muhammad.

In 1838, the British sent a force led by Alexander Burnes to reinstate Shah Shuja Durrani as the king of Afghanistan by deposing Amir Dost Mohammad Khan. To reach Afghanistan, they needed passage through Balochistan, particularly the Bolan Pass. However, Khan Mehrab Khan refused to allow the British to use his land to attack a neighboring country. The British sent Lieutenant Leach to negotiate with the Baloch government, but the Khan stood firm. When British forces reached Shaal via Bolan, some patriotic Baloch, without the Khan’s knowledge, attacked British troops out of nationalist sentiment and a desire to protect their homeland.
After toppling Amir Dost Mohammad Khan, the British Governor General of India, Lord Auckland, ordered an attack on Balochistan. In 1839, around 7,000 British troops marched from Shaal to attack the Baloch Meeri (capital). Anticipating an invasion, Khan Mehrab Khan declared war and sent messages to tribal leaders, but many saw the British as allies rather than invaders and chose to collaborate with them rather than defend their land. When Khan Mehrab Khan gathered his resistance fighters, the number of loyal warriors had dwindled to only 700 due to the short sightedness of many tribal chiefs. Nevertheless, Mehrab Khan was determined to fight. At his court, a respected figure, Akhund Muhammad Siddiq, advised him that he was not in a position to wage war at that time. He suggested that the Khan should leave Kalat with his companions, regroup and strengthen his forces, and then launch an attack against the British when the time was right, on 13 November 1839, the British forces launched an attack on Kalat, and a fierce battle ensued. During the fighting, Khan Mehrab Khan Baloch was martyred by a British bullet.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.

On 8 August 2016, terrorists attacked the Government Hospital in Quetta, Balochistan, in a suicide bombing and shooting. More than 70 people were killed, mainly lawyers, and more than 130 others were injured.
The majority of those killed were lawyers who had gathered at the hospital after the body of Advocate Bilal Anwar Kasi, president of the Balochistan Bar Association, was brought there. Kasi had been shot dead by a gunman near Mengal Chowk on Manno Jan Road in Quetta while he was leaving his home for his office.
Responsibility for the attack was claimed by various Islamist groups, including Jamaat-ul-Ahrar and the Islamic State Khorasan Province. Chairman Dost Mohammed was once elected Chairman of Union Council Gomazi. He was affiliated with the Pakistan National Party (PNP) and was a close confidant of Mir Ghaus Bakhsh Bizenjo.
In 2013, his son, Sikandar Baloch, decided to take up arms against Pakistani state subjugation. He went to the mountains and joined the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF).
In early 2017, the Frontier Corps (FC) summoned Chairman Dost Mohammed to its camp in Tump, where he met Colonel Chandio and Major Haider Ali. They told him that although his political and social activities were within the legal framework of Pakistan, they had information suggesting that he was affiliated with Sarmachars (freedom fighters) and that his son, Sikandar, was a member of the BLF. They demanded that he ensure his son surrendered to Pakistan. Dost Mohammed replied that his son was an adult, did not live with him, and was beyond his influence.
Despite this, state authorities continued to harass the family to force Sikandar to surrender. An Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) colonel also summoned Chairman Dost Mohammed to the Turbat FC camp and later visited his home, threatening him with severe consequences if Sikandar did not surrender.
On 15 February 2017, in broad daylight, a local death squad operating under the patronage of the Pakistani state killed Sikandar’s elder brother, Tahir Baloch, in cold blood inside the Gomazi Health Center, where he worked as a male nurse. This made it clear to Chairman Dost Mohammed and his family that the state was pursuing collective punishment, targeting the entire family due to Sikandar’s resistance activities.
On 21 May 2017, the bus in which Chairman Dost Mohammed was traveling from Turbat to Karachi was stopped by Pakistani security agencies at a place called Talar. He was forcibly removed from the vehicle, and this was the last time he was seen alive. It is believed that he was handed over to Military Intelligence (MI), where he was tortured to death in custody. His mutilated body was found on 25 May 2017 in Kunchiti, Balochistan.
On 1 April 2022, the family was informed that their son, Sikandar Baloch, had been martyred while fighting the Pakistani army in the mountains of Mand.

On 2 February 2022, sixteen members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayeen unit, the Majeed Brigade, carried out simultaneous attacks, nine in Noshki and seven on the Frontier Corps headquarters in Panjgur. The organization named this action "Operation Ganjal". 90 Pakistani security personnel were killed in Noshki and 105 in Panjgur.
On 2 February 2022 at 8:00 PM Fidayee Jamal Baloch alias Chacha, son of Rehmatullah, a resident of Turbat, rammed an VBEID into the main gate of the FC camp in Panjgur. As a result, the front portion of the camp was destroyed, and all soldiers deployed for security at the spot were killed instantly. After this, under the leadership of Unit Commander Hamid Raheem alias Zubair, son of Raheem Bakhsh, a resident of Chitkan, Panjgur, the fidayee fighters Sami Sameer alias Shoaib, son of Ustad Ilahi Bakhsh, resident of Gramkan, Panjgur; Ilyas Baloch alias Qadir, son of Aslam, resident of Gramkan, Panjgur; Asad Wahag alias Sabzo, son of Sadiq, resident of Kilkor; Nasir Imam alias Hamal, son of Imam, resident of Parom; and Zameer Baloch alias Faraz, son of Mohammad Hassan, resident of Dandar, Hoshab, entered the camp. They killed the majority of the soldiers present in the camp, while the remaining enemy personnel, instead of confronting the fighters, abandoned the camp and fled. The objective of the Panjgur unit was to seize control of the camp and hold it for as long as possible. After the enemy fled, the fighters took full control of the entire camp. Subsequently, to recapture the camp from the fighters, the enemy called in SSG commandos, the army, and combat helicopters. During this time, with the support of combat helicopters and armored vehicles, the SSG commandos launched five major assaults on the Baloch fighters. In every attack, the fighters inflicted heavy casualties on the enemy and forced them to retreat. The fighters continued to hold control of the camp while fighting the enemy’s elite military units for 72 hours. After failing in ground assaults, on 5 February 2022 in the afternoon, heavy shelling was carried out against the fighters using combat helicopters. As a result, after prolonged resistance, the fighters were martyred.

Abdul Khaliq, son of Ameer Bakhsh, a resident of Dashti Bazar, Kech, Balochistan, and a former employee of the Frontier Corps (FC), was forcibly disappeared on October 28 from Dashti Bazar. Four days later, his tortured and bullet-riddled body was recovered from the Kech River, bearing multiple gunshot wounds and clear signs of severe torture.

Abdul Khaliq had previously served as a soldier in the Frontier Corps. During his service, after being transferred from Mirani Dam to the main FC camp, he was pressured by senior military officials to participate in the torture and killing of Baloch detainees. Khaliq refused to comply with these unlawful and unconstitutional orders. After resigning, he established a small tailoring business in Dashti Bazar to earn a livelihood.

His refusal to partake in such abuses and his decision to live independently made him a target. According to local sources, Abdul Khaliq was subjected to collective punishment and was ultimately abducted and executed by state-backed death squads.
Ramzan Baloch, was a resident of the Mehi, Mashkai area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 30 June 2015 in Balochistan.

Shabeer Ahmad, son of Sabro Khan, was a 19-year-old farmer from Kocha Gresha Naal. He was forcibly disappeared on April 27, 2026. Following his disappearance, his family made continuous efforts to trace his whereabouts but received no information regarding his condition or location.
After remaining missing for more than a month, Shabeer Ahmed was killed, and his bullet-riddled body was dumped on June 8, 2026, in the Basima area of Washuk.
Shabeer was a young farmer who worked to support his family through agriculture.

Mumtaz Kurd, son of Bijjar, was a resident of Mach, district Bolan, Balochistan. Mumtaz Kurd was an FSc student and a member of BSO Azad, Mach Zone. He received his early education from his hometown, Mach. He belonged to a highly educated and political family, which inspired him to join the Baloch Students Organization Azad. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising peaceful political expression.
He was abducted on 12 October 2010 by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agencies along with his cousin Ali Jan Kurd. His cousins Ali Sher Kurd and Sher Zaman Kurd had previously been abducted and killed by security agencies due to their political affiliation. His bullet-riddled body was found dumped on 18 January 2011 in Ganjidori, Mastung district, Balochistan. He was killed for exercising his political views and his right to political participation for his people.
He actively participated in every activity of the organization and played a key role in mobilizing the youth of the area for the movement.
He joined BSO Azad at a very young age and was martyred by the Pakistan Army at a very young age after severe torture. His body bore extreme signs of torture. He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the ranks of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in the golden pages of Baloch history.

On 2 August 2024, in the Noshki area of Balochistan, during a sit-in organised as part of the Baloch National Gathering in Gwadar (a campaign concerning missing persons and enforced disappearances), indiscriminate firing by Pakistan’s Frontier Corps (FC) resulted in one young man being martyred on the spot and two others seriously injured. One of the injured, youth Hikmatullah Baloch, had been critically wounded by a bullet to the neck. He remained in the intensive care unit for forty days. After initial treatment at the Quetta Trauma Centre, he was transferred to Karachi for advanced medical care. On 13 September 2024, he succumbed to his injuries in a Karachi hospital and was martyred.

Haroon Rasheed Buzdar, alias Mubarak (Wahag Buzdar), son of Abdul Rasheed Buzdar, was a resident of Chinala, an area of Dera Ghazi Khan in the Koh-e-Sulaiman region. He held a B.S. in Psychology from the International Islamic University, Islamabad. He was active in politics for three years with BSO (Azad) and for three years with BNM. He joined the BLA in 2022 as an urban warrior and moved to the mountain front in October 2023. He served on the Bolan, Kahan, and Chamalang fronts and was promoted by the organization to the position of patrol commander. He was martyred on 20 September 2026, in the Lehri area of Sibi District, Balochistan.
Haroon Rasheed Buzdar, alias Wahag Buzdar (Mubarak), was a brave, conscious, and capable commander of the Baloch Liberation Army who was deployed on patrol command duties and was a longtime Sangat of the Baloch movement. After a long political and military life and struggle, he attained the supreme rank of martyrdom on 20 September 2026 during an operation against the enemy on the Lehri-Sibi front. Haroon Rasheed Buzdar was originally from Dera Ghazi Khan, a land of Balochistan that the occupying state of Pakistan has administratively incorporated into the so-called Punjab. However, he became aware of national servitude at a young age and became politically active in the struggle for national liberation. Educated at the International Islamic University Islamabad, Haroon Baloch began his fundamental struggle for national liberation during his student days through the platform of the Baloch Students Organization Azad and remained active in student politics for three years. Later, he spent his political life on the platform of the Baloch National Movement. He played a historic role in encouraging Baloch youth in various areas of Dera Ghazi Khan and Koh-e-Suleiman to pursue national liberation and in providing them with mental and ideological training.
After a long political struggle, in 2022, he chose a military platform for Baloch national liberation and began his activities as an urban guerrilla fighter. For one year, he continued his guerrilla activities on the urban front under organizational directives, where he successfully carried out organizational programs by utilizing his experience within a short period. After spending a year on the urban front, he was sent to the Bolan front under organizational directives, where his steadfastness, perseverance, and combat abilities were fully demonstrated. He applied his political and civilian-front experience and academic insight on the war front in a command role and took part in significant operations against the enemy. Alongside his political awareness and consciousness, he also possessed innate military abilities. He served as a frontline commander in historic operations, including Operation Herof.
In light of these abilities, the organization entrusted him with patrol command responsibilities, which he carried out responsibly until his last breath. As a patrol commander on the Chamalang and Kahan fronts, he played a prominent role in expanding the organization, developing operational plans, and carrying out military and guerrilla activities against the enemy. Despite his active role on the battlefield, he continued to fulfil his responsibilities of raising awareness about the national movement through his writing. Under the pen name Wahag Buzdar, he wrote numerous articles and expressed his views on a variety of subjects. Martyr Haroon spent a long life of resistance for the great cause of freedom. In the struggle to restore the Baloch national state, he will be remembered as a great hero, a resistance fighter, and a dignified Sangat of deep insight.

On 22 July 2026, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) released the details of seven martyred members of the organization: Abdul Ghafoor, alias Chakar, son of Jan Mohammad; Imdad Baloch, alias Nodh, son of Rahmatullah; Hafiz Mumtaz Baloch, alias Zeerak, son of Sabir Ali; Hafiz Zaid Baloch, alias Sagaar, son of Mullah Khudadad; Yasir Baloch, alias Ajiz, son of Mohammad Ayub; Shahjan Baloch, alias Sawad, son of Ali Mohammad; and Ali Raza Baloch, alias Shayhaq, son of Haji Ali Ahmad. They were martyred in a drone strike by Pakistani forces on 29 January 2026 in the Pardan area of Panjgur District, Balochistan.

Shahjahan Baloch, alias Sawad, son of Ali Mohammad, was a resident of Gramkan, Panjgur District, Balochistan. He joined the BLA on 27 August 2024 and served on the Panjgur front. He was martyred on 29 January 2026 in the Pardan area of Panjgur, Balochistan.
Shahjahan Baloch, alias Sawad, inherited from his family the legacy of continuing the struggle against Pakistan, which had established its authority over the Baloch homeland through what he viewed as an unlawful international power struggle. Two of Shahjahan’s brothers, martyrs Abdi and Hasrat Jan, had already sacrificed their lives for the homeland and fulfilled what they considered their responsibility. Continuing this legacy of sacrifice and martyrdom, Shahjahan joined the organization’s camp in August 2024 after Operation Herof Phase One. After joining the camp, he began carrying out his responsibilities with dedication and hard work.
Shahjahan had understood from a young age that only an independent and sovereign state could safeguard the free life and collective interests of a nation. He believed that enslaved nations had no standing in the world and that living under the control of an unnatural and uncivilized enemy like Pakistan was equivalent to collective death. For this reason, he chose the path of national resistance against what he considered an occupation, in the interest of collective welfare, and joined the ranks of the BLA to confront the enemy. During his two-year revolutionary and Sarmachari career in the organization, he confronted the enemy with courage and commitment and took part in several attacks. Along with his companions, he carried out important operations in Panjgur and the surrounding areas.
Even after the martyrdom of his two brothers, he continued to follow the path of sacrifice and struggle for national freedom, sending a message to young people that every Baloch youth should strive for national freedom and the restoration of their state and should not hesitate to make any kind of sacrifice. By shedding his blood for the freedom of his homeland, he immortalized himself in the pages of history.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Asad Baloch, alias Sher Jan, son of Haji Sher Mohammad, was a resident of the Sorgaz area of Mastung District, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in April 2025 and served on the Kalat front. He was martyred in Noshki during Operation Herof Phase II. He was a member of the BLA’s elite unit, the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS).
Asad was among those fighters of the Baloch independence movement who carried a deep conviction and unwavering resolve for the liberation of their homeland and people. He did not merely dream of freedom from subjugation; rather, he chose the path of active resistance against the system of occupation and became part of the armed struggle in the mountains of Balochistan. The life and sacrifice of Asad became a clear example of the truth that freedom is not a gift granted by others, but a right that must be achieved through determination, sacrifice, and continuous resistance. Such individuals, through their courage and steadfastness, become enduring symbols of hope and inspiration for future generations.
Asad carried out his responsibilities on the Kalat front with dedication and commitment. Later, due to his combat skills and capabilities, he became part of the organization’s special unit, STOS. During Operation Herof Phase II, Asad fought bravely against the enemy on the Noshki front. In this historic battle, he stood firm alongside his comrades and ultimately sacrificed his life for the cause of freedom.

data.biography: Bada Bugti, son of Hear Deen Nousani Bugti, a 27-year-old labourer and resident of Pir Koh, Dera Bugti, was killed by the Pakistani Army on 16 July 2026 in the Kadkocha area of Mastung. Bada Bugti was a working man who earned his livelihood through hard labour to support his family. Like countless other Baloch civilians, he posed no threat to anyone, yet his life was taken without charge, and without any due process.

On 30 December 2023 Pakistani forces carried out a drone attack and attempted to surround a camp of BRAS in Gurandi Zeera Kaur area of Mashkay by dropping commandos through helicopters. Following professional military tactics, Baloch freedom fighters formed multiple teams to foil enemy aggression and carried several successful attacks against the advancing enemy troops. At least 7 enemy commandos were eliminated in two separate attacks, whereas, three Baloch freedom fighters, identified as Sarwar alias Duruk, Azam alias Basit and Abdul Sattar alias Maraij made ultimate sacrifices. Two freedom fighters of BRAS, Kenagi alias Muslim and Ali alias Atta, while forestalling enemy advances for hours and providing a safe route for Baloch freedom fighters, also embraced martyrdom. Both valiant fighters fought the enemy troops until their last bullets, and made the ultimate sacrifices at their own hands after running out of ammunition. The fallen comrades were affiliated with the allied organisations of BRAS. Abdul Sattar, alias Meraj, a resident of Nokjo, Mashkay was affiliated with Baloch Liberation Army since 2016. He took part in numerous operations against the occupying forces.

On 12 August 2026, several Baloch people, including women and children, were killed and several others were injured as a result of an aerial bombardment of a civilian population by the Pakistan Air Force, reportedly using American-made F-16 fighter aircraft, in the Gidar Gindan area of Surab District, Balochistan. Following the airstrike, the injured and deceased were transported by police and local residents to DHQ Hospital in Surab, where the injured received medical treatment.

The families of the deceased and local residents subsequently began a protest by placing the bodies at Surab Main Chowk on the Quetta–Karachi National Highway (N-25). As a result, traffic on the highway was disrupted, with long queues of vehicles forming on both sides. Videos and photographs of the protest subsequently circulated widely on social media under the hashtag #SurabMassacre.

Those killed in the airstrike were identified as Shabir Ahmad Sumalani, son of Khudadad Sumalani, a resident of Marap, Surab; Noor Jan Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, a resident of Gindan; Karim Dad Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, a resident of Gandan; Raj Babu, wife of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani; Safia, wife of Noor Jan Mirwani; and Jalal Mirwani, son of Noor Jan Mirwani.

Those injured were identified as Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, son of Jan Muhammad Mirwani; Abdul Karim Mirwani, son of Jan Muhammad Mirwani; Mehrullah Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani; Nadeem Mirwani, son of Abdul Salam Mirwani; Shoaib Mirwani, son of Abdul Karim Mirwani; Sarah, wife of Baseer Ahmed Mirwani; Sabira, wife of Tufail Ahmed Mirwani; Zamra, daughter of Abdul Aziz Mirwani; Hajira, wife of Abdul Fattah Mirwani; Asim, son of Baseer, aged 1; Rahabia, daughter of Abdul Karim, aged 3; Sadia, daughter of Abdul Salam, aged 5; Fatima, daughter of Abdul Karim, aged 7; Zia-ur-Rehman, son of Abdul Karim, aged 2; Amir, son of Abdul Karim, aged 1; and Hasina, daughter of Muhammad Aslam, aged 4.

Following a detailed technical and scientific analysis of remnants of rocket components recovered from debris at the site of the aerial bombardment, important evidence reportedly emerged indicating that the recovered fragments belonged to an air-launched missile fired from an F-16 fighter aircraft.

Photographs of the recovered debris and the subsequent technical analysis reportedly indicated that the fragment was part of an AIM-120 Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile (AMRAAM), an American-made air-to-air missile.

Key technical evidence and serial numbers

According to the information and serial numbers reportedly engraved on the surface of the debris, the following details were recorded:

Assembly Number: ASSY 872128-1

Serial Number: 09-987138

Date of Manufacture: 09/09 (September 2009)

According to open-source intelligence (OSINT) records, the part number “872128-1” reportedly corresponds to the control section and rocket motor assembly of an AMRAAM missile manufactured by the American defense company Raytheon. Based on this evidence and the reported matching serial numbers, it is claimed that the debris was not part of an aircraft’s internal structure but instead consisted of remnants from an operational missile fired from an F-16 aircraft.
