data.biography:
Naeem Baloch was born on May 8, 1992, in Tootak and completed his matriculation in his hometown in 2008. He was pursuing his FSc at Degree College Khuzdar when he was killed by the Pakistan Army on February 18, 2011.
He also had a passion for playing cricket, but due to his political activities, he did not have much time to devote to sports. He had a strong interest in resolving the issues of the masses.
He joined BSO Azad in 2006 and was actively involved in all the activities of the organization. He was threatened by Pakistani secret agencies and a local death squad leader to stop speaking out against the alleged crimes of the Pakistan Army, but he did not abandon his peaceful and legitimate political activism despite these threats to his life.
Due to his commitment and political dedication, he was elected Deputy Organizer of the Khuzdar Zone. As an active member of the organization, he devoted all his time to its activities.
Before he was killed, he was arrested twice by security forces to intimidate him for his political activism: first in 2009, when he was returning from Naal after a successful BSO Azad gathering, and again in 2010 along with six of his friends. On both occasions, he was subjected to severe torture, but such acts did not deter him from continuing his political struggle for the national cause of the Baloch people.
His commitment to the organization greatly strengthened its agenda, and he did his utmost to protect both organizational and national interests. For this cause, he laid down his life. His arrests and the severe torture he endured only strengthened his resolve to work harder for the bright future of the nation.

Martyr Shoaib Baloch, alias Imran Baloch , Son of Miyyadad resident of Kolwa, area of Kech, Balochistan. He affiliated with a pro-independence organization Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) since 2021. He embraced martyrdom along with eight comrades, Jalil Sher Baloch, Samad Baloch, Dad Shah, Kambar Baloch, Javid Baloch, Rahmdil, Haris Baloch and Nawaz Baloch  in a drone attack of Pakistan Army  on Nov 29, 2022 in Jath, Kolwa area of Kech, Balochistan.

On 22 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch stated that BLF fighters had formally launched Operation Almas with a large-scale, coordinated attack on the main camp of the Pakistani army’s Frontier Works Organization (FWO) at Gwadar Zero Point. Fighters from the BLF’s special Saddo Operational Battalion, alongside members of other units, are participating in this major military engagement. The battle continued into the following day, 23 October 2026, with loud explosions and intense gunfire heard from the location. On 23 October 2026, a statement issued by the BLF spokesperson announced the completion of Operation Almas. The statement claimed that dozens of military and intelligence personnel had been killed, the hub of colonial projects had been destroyed, and army and Frontier Corps posts had been wiped out. It declared that the historic Operation Almas had concluded after achieving all its intended objectives. Operation Almas was carried out in Gwadar and the surrounding areas. It has formally concluded after reportedly achieving all its planned strategic, military, and economic objectives following prolonged and intense clashes. During this wide-ranging operation, the occupying Pakistani army and intelligence network suffered what the statement described as irreparable human and material losses. The BLF’s self-sacrificing fighters targeted the Frontier Works Organization’s (FWO) main camp, destroying a key centre for the implementation of colonial projects, particularly in Gwadar and across Makuran. This, the statement asserted, demonstrated to the world that, without the will and consent of the Baloch nation, colonial projects in Balochistan would never be safe. The offices and camps of Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) and Military Intelligence (MI) inside the FWO’s main camp were also targeted by the organisation’s fighters. Several soldiers, including senior officers, were reportedly killed in the attacks. Throughout Operation Almas, the Jind-Nadr Sarmachars not only thwarted every counterattack by the occupying army, every attempt by armoured vehicles to advance, and every reinforcement convoy, but also forced them to retreat, maintaining control of the camp for twenty hours. As a result of the actions of the Saddo Operational Battalion’s fighters during Operation Almas, Military Intelligence (MI) officers, Special Services Group (SSG) personnel, and dozens of regular army personnel were reportedly killed. In addition, the enemy’s main camp, posts, internal barracks, and administrative offices were reportedly destroyed in explosions and attacks. A number of the occupying army’s armoured vehicles, along with surveillance drones and quadcopters, were also reportedly destroyed during the operation. After repeatedly inflicting defeats on the occupying enemy during Operation Almas, the Jind-Nadr Sarmachars of the Saddo Operational Battalion, adhering to the philosophy of the last bullet, sacrificed their lives in the struggle for freedom, adding a new chapter of bravery to Baloch national history. The following Jind-Nadr Sarmachars played key roles in the operation: Khalid, alias Zamur; Bilqees Didag, alias Almas; Hamidullah, alias Badil; Shakeel, alias Sohrab; Majeed Zaib, alias Aftab; Nasir Ali, alias Nodan; Mujahid Mehr, alias Sagar Zamurani; and Barat, alias Safar Jan. All eight were reported to have embraced martyrdom during this historic operation. On 27 October 2026, the spokesperson issued another detailed statement, announcing that BLF special units had carried out a comprehensive, coordinated, organized, and effective attack on the centres of the occupying Pakistani army, the colonial intelligence network, and exploitative institutions in Gwadar. The statement claimed that more than 80 military and intelligence personnel had been killed; several armoured vehicles, the main army barracks, and intelligence offices had been destroyed; four quadcopters and two surveillance drones had been shot down; and a police station had been seized. It also reported that operations had been conducted at Gabd and Rimdan 250. Following these deadly blows to the state's exploitative structures, Operation Almas was declared successfully concluded. The spokesperson stated that the BLF was formally presenting to the nation, subjugated peoples, and the international community a comprehensive account of the far-reaching military and political achievements of Operation Almas. The historic, organized, effective, coordinated, and comprehensive operation was launched at 4:00 p.m. on 22 October 2026 against the occupying Pakistani state apparatus in Gwadar and the adjoining coastal region. The operation was described as the most organized, coordinated, and far-reaching attack to date against the occupying Pakistani state, its usurping army, intelligence network, exploitative economic institutions, and local puppet administration. It was presented as an expression of the organization's resolve and capabilities. The revolutionary participation of fearless Baloch women, standing shoulder to shoulder with men in the struggle for Baloch national freedom, national survival, and the defence of the coast and its resources, was portrayed as heralding the end of the usurping colonizer. This historic operation was named after the BLF's fearless and courageous guerrilla commander, Almas Baloch. For the past eight years, Commander Almas had been actively involved in the armed national struggle under the BLF banner, driven by her ideological convictions. Bilqees Didag, alias Almas, daughter of Allah Bakhsh Didag, resident of Dasht Kumbel, is a shining chapter of courage, steadfastness and revolutionary sacrifice. She spent her early life in ordinary circumstances and received regular education up to the eighth grade. She was married and has a beloved daughter, but rising above herself and her family circle, she made the cause of the motherland's freedom her whole life. In 2018 she formally joined the armed struggle for national freedom through BLF's revolutionary platform. After joining the organization, she served for four years as a volunteer in the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB), rendering highly valuable and arduous service. For the past eight years Shaheed Almas had been fully active and ideologically committed in the armed defense struggle through the BLF platform. During her organizational life she served as a very active and fearless member of the intelligence wing in sensitive and difficult areas such as Dasht, Turbat and Gwadar. She kept herself in motion day and night to deliver vital intelligence about the enemy to the organization in time. During military fronts and operations, she always carried out, with courage and steadfastness, the very difficult and dangerous responsibility of delivering supplies, weapons and logistics to the sarmachars across Dasht's harsh and rugged mountain ranges. On the path of her revolutionary struggle, the occupying Pakistani army and operatives of the state's death squads made every effort to obstruct her. The occupying army repeatedly attempted to abduct her, hold her in illegal detention and break her mentally and physically, and on one occasion state personnel subjected her to severe torture that left her badly injured. But this tactic of state oppression, taunting and torture could not shake her steadfastness. She faced every hardship with a smile and always stood firm like a rock on the armed front, keeping the flag of freedom high. Even in these grave conditions under state oppression, the wise and courageous way she carried out organizational responsibilities while hiding in various areas is eloquent proof of her high military insight and ideological maturity. Shaheed Bilqees Didag alias Almas put into practice the idea that on the difficult path of national freedom, all hardships, troubles and sacrifices are acceptable, but national slavery and state domination are not acceptable under any circumstances. To realize this idea, she made the final decision to sacrifice herself for the motherland. Shaheed Almas carried out her duties with great devotion in various military detachments and units of the BLF, and from the time the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB) was founded she was its active founder and core member.

On December 14, 2024 three brave BLA fighters were martyred in SabzKoh, Panjgur, while valiantly resisting a Pakistani military offensive. That morning, Pakistani forces launched a large-scale air and ground operation, deploying hundreds of troops, SSG commandos, gunship helicopters, and drones. At SabzKoh, BLA fighters engaged in an intense battle from 10 AM to 3 PM. Commander Majeed Baloch, Commander Diljan Baloch, and fighter Zakir Jan fought courageously before embracing martyrdom.
Diljan Baloch, alias Javed Baloch, hailed from Gramkan, Panjgur. He began his armed struggle in 2012 under BLA’s banner. After receiving training in Bolan in 2012, he served as an urban guerilla for a significant period. Before his martyrdom, he was serving as the second-in-command alongside Shaheed Majeed Baloch at the Panjgur camp. He played a crucial role in organizing the movement in Panjgur, Washuk, and other parts of Makuran. His sincerity, competence, and dedication were beyond question, and among fellow fighters, he is always remembered as a kind and compassionate comrade. Shaheed Diljan was a highly educated and politically conscious revolutionary whose name will forever be remembered.

On 11 August 2025, the umbrella alliance of Baloch armed organizations in Balochistan, Baloch Raji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS), launched coordinated operations during which several government installations were destroyed and dozens of Pakistani military personnel were killed. A large quantity of military equipment was also reportedly seized. Images showing the bodies of the deceased Pakistani soldiers, destroyed vehicles, and military uniforms hanging at various locations subsequently went viral on social media.
Even after the coordinated attacks had ended, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), a member of the BRAS alliance, maintained control of the Zehri area and successfully repelled multiple attempts by Pakistani forces to advance into the region.
After holding control of the area for several days, the BLA eventually withdrew. Following its withdrawal, the Pakistani military entered Zehri with gunship helicopters, battle tanks, and a large contingent of troops. According to reports, the forces spread fear and panic through looting and other actions in the area. Since then, Zehri and its surrounding regions have remained under military operations and repression.
Following their defeat at the hands of the armed groups, Pakistani forces allegedly targeted civilians in retaliation. As a result of this repression, 11 Baloch individuals were reportedly killed.
On 16 April 2026, several people from Zehri and its surrounding areas - including Wadera Mohammad Dayaan, Imam Bakhsh, Manzoor Ahmad Miraji, Munir Hayat Dayaan, Izzatullah Pandrani, Habibullah, Mohammad Sharif, Mohammad Ramzan, and three unidentified individuals - were reportedly extrajudicially executed by Pakistani forces while traveling along roads in the Sohinda area. One individual, Abdul Salam, survived with serious injuries.
During the ongoing military operation in the area, these individuals were allegedly detained by Pakistani forces from various locations and transferred to the Sohinda Rest House, approximately five kilometres from Noorgama. There, their hands and feet were allegedly bound, they were blindfolded, and they were subsequently shot dead.
The incident occurred one day after the BLA claimed that two of its fighters had been killed during clashes in the Sohinda area.
In its statement, the BLA said that, on 15 April 2026, its fighters targeted advancing Pakistani military units with a remote-controlled explosive device. Following the explosion, they allegedly carried out an ambush on a military convoy moving toward the area.
The organization claimed that ten Pakistani military personnel were killed in the two attacks, while two of its own fighters, Tanveer Mengal and Saadullah, were also killed.

On 4 March 2026, a statement issued by the spokesperson of the Balochistan Liberation Front, Major Gwahram Baloch, stated that on 3 February 2026, fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front launched a coordinated operation at four different locations in Hoshap against Pakistani forces. In this organized operation, various BLF units simultaneously targeted the enemy army at four different locations in Hoshap.
In the initial phase of the operation, one unit of fighters surrounded the police station located in Hoshap Bazaar and took control of the station, holding the personnel hostage. While this unit was seizing government weapons, ammunition, and other equipment, an enemy military convoy consisting of four vehicles approached the area, resulting in an intense face-to-face clash between BLF fighters and enemy forces. During the clash, the fighters targeted and destroyed two enemy vehicles, killing several Pakistani military personnel on board.
Meanwhile, a second unit of fighters positioned at another location attacked two armored enemy vehicles with heavy weapons. Several military personnel were killed or wounded in the clash. Witnessing the defeat and retreat of their ground forces, the enemy resorted to gunship helicopters and advanced drone technology to halt the BLF fighters’ advance.
In this prolonged clash, seven BLF fighters - Shaneed Baloch (alias Shohaz Baloch), Zabad Baloch (alias Deedag), Atta Baloch (alias Obaid), Ghaffar Baloch (alias Noroz), Abdul Samad Baloch (alias Muheem Jan), Zaheer Baloch (alias Istaal), and Nadeem (alias Sahil) - fought valiantly until their last bullet and last breath and embraced martyrdom while courageously defending their motherland.
Nadeem, alias Sahil Son of Ameer Bakhsh, resident of Balour Kolwah, formally joined the armed struggle against the occupying forces under the Balochistan Liberation Front platform in March 2025. In a short period, he earned a distinguished position among his friends and within the organizational ranks due to his unparalleled dedication, steadfastness, and perseverance. In the clash against the enemy forces at Hoshap, he fought valiantly and set a supreme example of bravery before embracing martyrdom. The great sacrifice of Shaheed Nadeem Baloch will always be remembered as a shining chapter in the history of the Baloch national struggle.

In continuation of the Fidayee (self-sacrificing) operation carried out on 8 July 2026 in Khuzdar city, Balochistan, against the compound of state asset and national traitor Shafiq Mengal, alias Shafiq Laghor (the coward) which resulted in the deaths of 34 members of Shafiq's death squad and the martyrdom of five members of the BLA. According to the organization, this operation, marking the commencement of the first phase of 'Operation Marg-e-Ghadaran' manifests the BLA's growing operational and intelligence capabilities against the colonial system and the criminal networks nurtured under it.

The five Fidayeen involved in this complex battle successfully breached the enemy's siege and retreated safely, while five other freedom fighters sacrificed their lives during various stages of this organized action to complete this crucial operation.
The operation commenced with the breaching of the outer security perimeter of Shafiq Laghor’s house, a responsibility undertaken by a talented Fidayee of the Majeed Brigade, Beebarg alias Pulliya Osama. The 22 year old Fidayee Beebarg hailed from the Tindilan area of Mastung and belonged to the Bangulzai tribe of the Baloch, formally joining the BLA and the Majeed Brigade in 2025. Following his enlistment into the organization's ranks, he remained active on the challenging military fronts of Khuzdar and Dasht, Quetta. Prior to this operation, he had demonstrated outstanding performance during 'Operation Herof 2' in the attack on the Frontier Corps central camp established at the Agriculture Office in Quetta. During the Khuzdar operation, he commanded the explosive laden vehicle, skillfully ramming it into the main gate of Shafiq Laghor's compound. Consequently, the outer defensive lines and checkpoints were reduced to rubble within seconds, instantly killing a large number of the enemy's armed guards stationed there and thereby clearing the path for the inner advance.
Immediately after the severe chaos caused by the explosion at the main gate, the next operational objective was to breach the security network of the compound's inner building, a task completed with utmost dedication and bravery by another valiant Fidayee of the Majeed Brigade, Zia Ur Rahman alias Imran. Hailing from Khadkocha, the 19-year-old Fidayee Zia Ur Rahman belonged to the Shahwani tribe and became a part of the BLA and the Majeed Brigade in 2025. Due to his exceptional combat skills, he quickly rose to the forefront of organizational activities on rigorous fronts such as Khuzdar and Koh-e-Maran. He had also been part of the frontline against the enemy on the Hazarganji front during 'Operation Herof 2.' In this battle of Khuzdar, right after Beebarg’s Fidayee strike, he courageously braved enemy fire to gain entry into the inner building of the compound and detonated the Fidayee jacket strapped to his body. As a result, the inner defensive line was completely destroyed, and the enemy's internal command-and-control system was paralyzed, providing the remaining Fidayeen with the opportunity to secure internal positions.
As soon as the inner security line collapsed, the remaining Fidayeen entered the compound and assumed various positions, where Fidayee Mohammad Ramzan Zehri, alias Shaban, took a stand at the main gate and its surrounding vital sectors to confront the enemy on the frontline. The 25-year-old Fidayee Mohammad Ramzan hailed from the Yakboozi area of Zehri, was the son of Chakar Khan, and belonged to the Zehri tribe. He joined the BLA in 2020 and became part of the Majeed Brigade in 2025 after extensive operational service. He was part of the guerrilla war for a long time across vast and highly sensitive fronts such as Bolan, Harboi, Nagaho, Zehri and Khuzdar and played a key role in the sensitive attack on the Quetta Red Zone during 'Operation Herof 2.' During the Khuzdar operation, he stood firm against the enemy's private death squad and uniformed collaborators at the central gate, fighting a close quarter battle and embracing martyrdom on the frontline while inflicting heavy casualties on the enemy.
The phase of maintaining resistance inside this enemy stronghold until the final moments and penetrating Shafiq Laghor’s residential block to clear all sides was carried out by two Fidayeen comrades of the Majeed Brigade, Shahzaib Baloch alias Sagaar and Shahzain Baloch alias Chedag. A resident of Manguchar, the son of Khalil Ahmed and belonging to the Nichari tribe of the Baloch, Fidayee Shahzaib Baloch began his journey in the organization as an urban guerrilla in December 2024, after which he transitioned to the regular mountain front in March 2025 and became part of the Majeed Brigade in June 2025. He was active on the Nagaho and Shoor fronts and had put up prolonged resistance against the enemy's heavy military strength under the direct command of the martyred Comrade Sameer during the battle at the Noshki main camp in 'Operation Herof 2.' Alongside him was Fidayee Shahzain Baloch alia

On 12 August 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahran Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of nine fighters of the organization: 1. Zubair Baloch, alias Shahvez; 2. Shahnawaz Baloch, alias Rahchar; 3. Rahim Baloch, alias Ajiz Baloch; 4. Musharaf Baloch, alias Basham; 5. Munir Baloch, alias Khalid Baloch; 6. Mohammad Zaman, alias Yahya; 7. Jasim Baloch, alias Babar; 8. Gaji Khan Baloch, alias Aftab; and 9. Abdullah Baloch, alias Usman, and paid tribute to all the martyred comrades who sacrificed their lives for the freedom of the motherland, Balochistan.

On 29 July 2026, occupying Pakistani forces launched a large-scale military operation in the mountainous areas of Mand. During the operation, the forces used quadcopters to fire mortar shells, severely wounding Jasim Baloch, alias Babar, son of Hafeez, a resident of Suro, Mand. Despite sustaining severe wounds and deep injuries, he continued fighting the enemy until his final breath and embraced martyrdom, setting a profound example of refusing to bow before the occupier.
Jasim Baloch, alias Babar Baloch, had joined the BLF one year before his martyrdom. After successfully carrying out operations on the urban front and providing intelligence services against the enemy, he was transferred to the mountainous warfare front in June 2026 under an organizational decision, where he took a leading role in several important battles within a short period.

Shah Mohammad Bugti was born in November 1958 in Sui, Dera Bugti, Balochistan. He was a senior activist of the Baloch Republican Party (BRP) and was martyred by Pakistani forces.
He was the brother of Sher Mohammad Bugti, the central spokesperson of the BRP. He was known for his honesty, bravery, and cheerful personality. He always brought joy to those around him, which earned him the affectionate nickname “Washudi” from his friends and party members.
Shah Mohammad Bugti was also a revolutionary poet. His poetry focused on freedom, resistance, and revolution, and he often urged the youth to embrace the revolutionary struggle.
On 5 December 2010, he was abducted by Pakistani forces in the Jatero Rakho area near the Punjab border. Two days later, on 7 December 2010, his bullet-riddled body was found in the same area.
He was a fearless and charismatic figure — the heart and soul of every gathering. This shining light of the Baloch resistance was cruelly taken from us by the brutal Pakistani army.

Faheem Baloch, son of Qasim Baloch, a part-time labourer in a shop and a resident of Chidagi, Awaran, was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani military forces from Awaran’s Main Bazaar on September 11, 2025.

After nine days of enforced disappearance, his mutilated body, bearing clear signs of torture and severe abuse, was discovered on September 20 in the Majid Pir area of Jahoo, Awaran.

Faheem was also a relative of Bakar Baloch, who was subjected to the same fate at the hands of Pakistani military forces.
Irfan Baloch, alias Imdad Jan, was a resident of the Koshqalat, Tump area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 28 September 2020 in Balochistan.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Inayat, also known as Tokali, son of Imam Deen Sarmastani, was a resident of the Samwani area of Zehri, Khuzdar district, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in January 2024 and moved to the mountain front in January 2025. In February 2025, he joined the Majeed Brigade and served on the Nagaho front.
After joining the BLA, Fidayee Inayat served on the urban front for one year. He carried out his urban responsibilities with bravery and maturity. Later, following an organizational decision, he was transferred to the mountainous front in Nagaho at the beginning of 2025. Tokali, who hailed from the land of Zehri in Khuzdar, carried within him a quiet yet iron determination. After joining the mountain front, he further strengthened his role amid rugged terrain and constant dangers. Upon joining the Majeed Brigade, he embodied the philosophy of sacrifice and resistance in his actions. On the Nagaho front, he emerged as a Sarmachar who remained ready for struggle at every moment, one whose steps never retreated and who believed that the destination of freedom could only be achieved through sacrifice and steadfastness. Tokali’s resolve became a symbol of the truth that when a Sarmachar values the freedom of his homeland more than his own life, he becomes a living symbol of resistance in history.
Inayat Tokali was present on the Noshki front during Operation Herof Phase II, where he set an example of bravery, courage, and combat capability by delivering decisive blows to the enemy—blows whose echoes will continue to resonate until the freedom of Balochistan is achieved. On the Noshki front, Fidayee Inayat sacrificed his life for the great cause of freedom.

On 2 June 2026, in the Zehri area of Khuzdar district, Balochistan, Pakistani forces shot and killed Khalil ur Rehman Musiyani, son of Sardar Naseer Musiyani, and Umair Sumalani, son of Haji Naseer Ahmed Samalani, in two separate incidents.

The Zehri area of Khuzdar district, Balochistan, which had been under a Pakistani military siege and curfew for the previous nine months, was raided by Pakistani forces with armored vehicles, military helicopters in the air, and a large contingent of personnel. They attacked the home of 73 year old Sardar Naseer Ahmad Musiyani in the Balbal Zehri area and assaulted him in front of his son, Khalil ur Rehman Musiyani. In reaction, his son, Khalil ur Rehman Musiyani, grabbed a Pakistani Army major by the collar, upon which the Pakistani Army opened fire.

Sardar Naseer Ahmed Musiyani, his injured son Khalil ur Rehman Musiyani, another of his son, and several of his relatives were taken into custody and forcibly disappeared. According to later reports, they were taken to a school at Balbal Zehri Cross, which had been converted into a detention camp. They were released several hours later that night, and the following morning they were summoned and asked to sign a written confession in order to receive the body of Khalil Ur Rahman. The written statement stated that their son, Khalil ur Rehman Musiyani, was a terrorist.
Sardar Naseer Ahmed Musiyani was a white-bearded and respected political and tribal figure, an elected member of the Union Council, and a member of the Balochistan National Party (Mengal). He was beaten during his arrest, and his son, Khalil ur Rehman Musiyani, was shot and injured in front of him. Later, he succumbed to his injuries due to the lack of proper medical facilities. His body was then withheld from the family for several hours before being handed over.
The killing of Khalil ur Rehman Musiyani by Pakistani forces was condemned by political parties and other organizations across Balochistan, and shutdown strikes were also observed in Quetta and other areas of Balochistan.

On 21 December 2010, journalist, human rights defender, and member of the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) Siddique Eido, along with Yousuf Nazar, a member of the Baloch Student Organisation (Azad) (BSO-Azad), went to the District and Sessions Court of Gwadar, a port city in Balochistan. They were returning home to the sub-district of Pasni under the security of five policemen, including one Assistant Sub-Inspector (ASI) and four police constables.
As they reached the Frontier Corps (FC) check post in the Karwat area on the coastal highway, they were stopped by the officials of the Pakistani Frontier Corps. Siddique Eido and Yousuf Nazar were dragged into a van. The accompanying policemen tried to protect them but were severely beaten by the Frontier Corps and held in custody for several hours. Meanwhile, Siddique Eido and Yousuf Nazar were forcibly disappeared.
On 28 April 2011, the bodies of Siddique Eido and Yousuf Nazar were found in Ormara, Balochistan. Both showed visible signs of torture, and both men had been shot in the head. Their families have continued to receive threats not to pursue the cases.
After Naeem Sabir, who was killed on 1 March 2011, Siddique Eido became the second member of the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP) to be killed in 2011.

On 17 November 2024, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Army spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 25 February 2024, three members of the BLA - Mohammad Deen alias Chakar Bolani, Shoaib Shahwani alias Riaz Baloch, and Asim Kurd alias Nazir Baloch - were killed in an attack by death squads in Kahan, district Kohlu, Balochistan.
The three comrades were returning to their frontlines after completing a special organizational mission in Kahan when operatives of a death squad, lying in ambush, opened fire on them. As a result, all three members of the organization were killed.
Commander Mohammad Deen alias Chakar Bolani, son of Faiz Mohammad, hailed from Chamalang. For the past ten years, he had been serving on the Bolan front under the platform of the BLA. He carried out his duties with dedication, courage, and integrity as a commander on critical fronts such as Bolan, Kohlu, and Kahan. During the Kahan mission, Shoaib Shahwani and Asim Kurd were under his command. He was the brother of the BLA’s first Fidayee (self-sacrificing) member, Darvesh Baloch, and senior member Gul Hamd Marri. He was also a cousin of Mohammad Gul alias Waheed Baloch, who was killed earlier this year in an airstrike on a BLA camp. Due to the oppression of the occupying state, his family has been forced to live in exile for nearly two decades. Despite this, they have not hesitated to make generational sacrifices for national freedom.

On 19 November 2025 in the Mand Gawak area of Turbat district, Balochistan, Pakistani forces opened indiscriminate fire on people who were on a picnic, killing Ismail Baloch, son of Jalal Khan, on the spot and injuring his friend Nouman Baloch, son of Haider. Nouman Baloch was later taken into custody despite being injured and was forcibly disappeared.

After being held in illegal detention for more than two months, on 21 January 2026, the mutilated and bullet-riddled body of Nouman Baloch, son of Haider, was recovered from the Rodbun area of Turbat district, Balochistan. The body bore clear signs of torture.

Zeeshan, a 21 year old student and resident of Khudabadan, Panjgur, was forcibly disappeared by a state backed death squad on the night of 29 June 2025 at approximately 8:00 PM from Football Chowk, Panjgur. Zeeshan was the son of Zaheer Ahmed, who himself has been forcibly disappeared since 13 April 2015 and remains missing to this day.

In the hours following Zeeshan’s abduction, his family staged a sit-in protest on the CPEC Road in Panjgur, demanding his immediate release and raising urgent alarm over his safety.

On the morning of 30th June 2025 at around 9:00 AM, the family received devastating news: Zeeshan’s bullet-riddled body was discovered near Surdu Ghareeb Nawaz Hotel. His body bore multiple gunshot wounds.

The targeted killing of Zeeshan, who had already endured the trauma of growing up without his father due to an enforced disappearance illustrates the multigenerational cycle of violence and repression inflicted on Baloch families by Pakistani authorities.

Farooq Naeem, son of Naeem Baloch and a resident of Khairabad, a small town in District Kech, Balochistan, was detained by Pakistan’s law enforcement agencies and paramilitary forces at the Talar checkpoint, located between Kech and Gwadar, on April 24, 2025. He had been travelling to Karachi to obtain a medical certificate required for his visa to Qatar.

After seven months of enforced disappearance, his bullet-riddled body was discovered on 17 November 2025 in Banok-e-Chadai, an area of Kech. According to eyewitnesses, Farooq’s body bore clear signs of severe torture, including cigarette burns, electric shocks, and multiple other injuries.

Shaheed Sher Mohd Baloch was born in 1971 in Mand, Turbat, Balochistan. He studied at Mand High School & began his political work through the BSO, serving as General Secretary & President of the Mand Zone in 1986–87. In the late 1980s, he moved to Karachi, continued his studies at National College, and remained active in BSO as Karachi Zone President, CC member & BSO Sindh General Secretary.

In 2005, he returned to politics & joined the Jamhoori Watan Party under Shaheed Akbar Bugti. Bugti praised his joining as a sign of renewed party strength. As conditions worsened in Dera Bugti, Sher Mohd led protests in Karachi against military operations. After Bugti’s martyrdom, he became one of the most active political workers.

On 3 December 2006, while preparing for a public meeting in Lyari with Shaheed Ghulam Moh Baloch, he was abducted along with him when Pakistani forces surrounded Haidari Football Club. After 10 months of protests & hunger strikes, both were produced in Sibbi on 20 September 2007, showing signs of severe torture.

After Bugti’s martyrdom, Brahumdagh Bugti renamed the party as the Baloch Republican Party (BRP). Sher Mohd became a CC member & was elected Central Deputy Secretary General on 10 October 2008 in BRP’s first council session in Quetta. He played an important role in strengthening BRP work in Karachi & Makuran.

On 3 April 2009, Sher Mohd, Ghulam Mohd, and Lala Munir were abducted from Advocate Kachkol Ali’s chamber in Turbat. A week later, on 9 April, their bodies were found in the Murgaap mountains near Turbat. The incident marked the intensification of the (pick, kill & dump) policy, through which thousands of Baloch political workers & civilians were killed & their mutilated bodies dumped.

On 13 March 2026, a statement issued by the Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson, Azad Baloch, paid rich tribute to the courage and bravery of the valiant BLA fighter Ghulam Hussain Baloch, alias Nasir, who hailed from Johan.
Ghulam Hussain Baloch, alias Nasir, joined the BLA in 2020 and began fulfilling his national duties. He was a hardworking, sincere, fearless, and devoted Baloch freedom fighter committed to serving the Baloch motherland.
Through the platform of the BLA, he carried out fierce attacks against the occupying Pakistani army, their bases, and their infrastructure in Nagaho, Ge Shishak, Harboi, Koh Maran, Kadh Kocha, Dilband, and adjoining areas. At this stage of his life, he made a firm decision to make the mountains his base and became a supporting arm of the Baloch fighters.
On 4 December 2024, he was arrested by the Pakistani enemy while carrying out an organizational special mission of the BLA. For nearly two years, he endured inhumane torture in the torture cells of the occupying forces, yet the enemy could neither buy his thoughts and ideology nor force him to bow.
On 24 January 2026, he fulfilled his duty to the Baloch homeland with his precious blood, nourishing the land of the homeland and sacrificing his life for the cause.

On November 12, 2024, in the Balgatar area, during an organizational mission, the comrades of the organization were martyred while bravely fighting the enemy. The martyrs include Second Lieutenant Azum, alias Qasim, son of Muhammad Rahim, a resident of Teertej Awaran; Second Lieutenant Anwar, alias Sana, son of Hussain, a resident of Red Tok Balgatar; Arab Nawaz, alias Jahanzaib, a resident of Gresha; and Zaheer, alias Azad, son of Fazal, a resident of Biront Keelkor. They all sacrificed their lives in defense of their motherland.

On 3 February 2024, the Pakistani Army’s Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) issued a statement declaring that 24 terrorists had been neutralized in a military operation conducted in the Mach area of Bolan. The operation was launched in response to Operation Darra-e-Bolan, an operation launched by the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), a Baloch pro-independence militant group, in the Mach area of Bolan district. The group reportedly maintained control of the area for three days.

However, subsequent investigations revealed that four of the deceased individuals had previously been reported as victims of enforced disappearances, and some of their cases had been registered with Baloch human rights organizations.

The identities of the deceased individuals were confirmed as follows:

- Bashir Ahmed, son of Haji Khan Marri, a resident of Mashriqi Bypass, Quetta, who was forcibly disappeared on 2 July 2023.

- Arman Marri, son of Nihal Khan Marri, a resident of Mashriqi Bypass, Quetta, who was forcibly disappeared on 2 July 2023.

- Sobadar, son of Gulzar Khan Tengani, a resident of the Main Kor area of Harnai district, who was forcibly disappeared on 9 September 2023.

- Shakil, son of Ramzan, a resident of the Mishk area of Zehri, Khuzdar district.

The family members of Bashir and Arman were also actively participating in a sit-in protest in Islamabad. Organized by the Baloch Yakjehti Committee (BYC), the sit-in was held outside the National Press Club to protest enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings.

The families tirelessly appealed to the government to secure the return of their forcibly disappeared loved ones, but all their pleas fell on deaf ears. Ultimately, they were devastated to receive the mutilated bodies of their young relatives, whom they believed had been victims of a staged encounter.

On 5 February 2024, when the family members went to Civil Hospital Quetta to receive the bodies, they were reportedly coerced into signing an unlawful form falsely stating that the deceased had links to militant groups and labeling them as terrorists. The family members refused to comply. Following a large demonstration, the bodies were eventually handed over to them.

Sameer Baloch, son of Abdul Khaliq and a resident of Balicha, Tump, worked along the border routes that sustain families across this region. These routes exist only because the Pakistani state has offered nothing else, and this sole means of livelihood is also under their control.
On 25 September 2026, he joined a picnic in the Lutham area of Balicha, Tump district, with his friends. They informed the Pakistani army about their picnic at the mentioned location, and they were met with a rocket fired by a drone operated by Pakistani forces, which ended his life along with those of his three other friends: Yasir, son of Mohammad Karim; Zubair Nawab, son of Nawab; and Didag Baloch, son of Mohammad Omar. Two other people were also injured in the incident.

Balakh Sher, son of Siddique, was a 28 year old driver from the Loti area of Dera Bugti District, Balochistan.
On 11 October 2026, personnel of the Pakistan Coast Guards opened fire on him in Winder and killed him extrajudicially.

Ayaz Baloch, son of Akbar, was abducted on 12 November 2025 from the main bazaar of Buleda Menaz in Turbat, Balochistan, by Pakistani forces and their allied death squad. On 19 November 2025, his tortured and mutilated body was found in the Reko Dem area of Buleda.

When the Prime Minister of Pakistan, Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto, feared that the first elected government of Balochistan was educating the Baloch masses about their rights and how they had been deliberately kept backward by Pakistani imperialists, the so-called first democratically elected Prime Minister of Pakistan illegally dismissed the Balochistan government on 13 February 1973. The anger of the Baloch nation erupted into an armed revolt for the independence of Balochistan. Gunship helicopters provided by the Iranian regime, along with the full might of the Pakistan Air Force, were used to carry out indiscriminate aerial bombardment on the unarmed civilian population in an attempt to force the Baloch rebels to surrender. As a result, thousands of Baloch perished. Under these circumstances, a young man from Mastung, Abdul Majeed Langove, took it upon himself to avenge the massacre of his people at the hands of the ruthless Prime Minister of Pakistan, Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto. On 2 August 1974, armed with a hand grenade, he attempted to attack the Prime Minister during a public meeting in Quetta. Although Shaheed Abdul Majeed Langove did not succeed in his mission, he sacrificed his life in the attempt and sent a powerful message: the occupying forces of our motherland and their leaders should know that the brave sons of the Baloch nation are willing to sacrifice everything for the freedom of their homeland and its people.

On 31 May 2021, Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) fighters attacked the Pakistani military’s “Awais” camp (Ghazaband Scouts’ 129 Wing) in Marwaar, Bolan. The three-hour assault completely destroyed the camp. BLA fighters killed 24 Pakistani soldiers on the spot and captured Lance Naik Bilal from Dera Ismail Khan. He was later tried by a Baloch national court and executed.
Following a coordinated plan, the fighters surrounded the camp, cut through barbed wire, and stormed inside. After intense fighting lasting over three hours, they overran the base, killed 24 enemy personnel, seized a large quantity of arms and ammunition, and took one prisoner. As usual, the Pakistani military downplayed its losses.
Three BLA fighters embraced martyrdom in the operation: Hangal Marri (alias Laila), Aftab Jattak (alias Washain), and Shahwez Zehri (alias Saraang). They were buried in Bolan with full military honours.
The three belonged to the elite Fateh Squad, formed in 2018 and named after Martyr Fateh Qambrani (alias Chairman), who single-handedly enabled the capture of an enemy camp in Meshdari, Shahrag, the same year. Fateh Squad members are selected for exceptional bravery and close-combat skills.
In the Marwaar attack, these three charged the enemy lines, breached the perimeter, and created openings that allowed the BLA to capture the camp entirely.
Hangal Marri (alias Laila) joined the BLA in 2006 and served with distinction on the Kahan and Bolan fronts for 15 years.
Aftab Yousuf Jattak (alias Washain), a highly educated economics graduate from Zehri, joined in 2019 and quickly earned a place in the Fateh Squad due to his skill and courage.
Shahwez Zehri (alias Saraang) joined in 2017, served in urban units, then volunteered for the Bolan front and the Fateh Squad, where he fought bravely until his martyrdom.

Rahmat Baloch, son of Abdul Karim and a resident of Gajjar Mashkai, began his education in Jeebri and later continued it in Nukjo. He started his career as a JVT teacher in Awaran. After several years, he was transferred to Koh-e-Aspeet, Mashkai.
After 2000, when the Baloch liberation movement was gaining momentum across Balochistan, Rahmat played a vital role in organizing and ensuring the success of rallies and mass gatherings of the BSO. When a crackdown against political activists intensified throughout Balochistan, Rahmat decided to join the armed struggle under the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in 2009.
Due to his dedication, hard work, and capabilities, he soon rose to the position of commander within his organization. He was martyred in a clash with the Pakistan Army on 21 January 2015 in Mashkai.

During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Hamid Bugti, alias Ghani, son of Qasum Bugti, was a resident of the Mach area of District Bolan, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in January 2024 and later joined the Majeed Brigade in June 2024.
Hamid Bugti belonged to the historic resistance front of Bolan, a region where, in every era, the Baloch people have waged a struggle against occupying forces and inscribed a legacy of resistance. Since the beginning of the Pakistani occupation, Bolan has been regarded as a significant symbol of resistance. Shaheed Fidayee Hamid Bugti carried forward this tradition of resistance by actively participating in the Baloch national liberation struggle.
Fidayee Hamid Bugti was a highly trained sarmachar (freedom fighter), proficient in military strategy, combat skills, and guerrilla warfare techniques. He possessed in-depth knowledge of the battlefield’s geography and climatic conditions. On the Bolan front, he played an effective role in various engagements against the occupying forces. He was also ideologically and intellectually conscious. Shortly after joining the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), he decided to become part of the Majeed Brigade, reflecting his serious commitment and determination.
During Operation Dara-e-Bolan II, he was in the front ranks during the hijacking of the Jaffar Express. Throughout the operation, he remained on the frontline for several days, delivering decisive blows to the enemy and inflicting heavy losses.
In Operation Herof II, he was part of the Dalbandin front. There, fighting on the frontline with strategic acumen and bravery, he compelled the occupying forces to retreat within their own headquarters. Shaheed Fidayee Hamid Bugti embraced martyrdom while fighting on the Dalbandin front.

On December 9, 2025, enemy army personnel were eliminated and several others were injured during a clash with the occupying Pakistani army in the Sunni area of Kachi. Baloch Liberation Army freedom fighter Ismail Jattoi was martyred in this two hour long clash.
Ismail Jattoi, alias Sufi, son of Din Muhammad Jattoi, belonged to the Sunni area of Kachi. He had been associated with the Baloch Liberation Army for the past two years and served on the Mastung and Kachi fronts. He was a symbol of discipline and steadfastness and a source of encouragement to his comrades in difficult situations. One of his brothers, Farooq Jattoi, was martyred in 2016, which stands as a shining example of the continuous sacrifices of this family.

An armed encounter took place between the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) freedom fighters and the enemy forces at Jantro on Saturday, October 23, 2021 in Bolan and Harnai mountainous area. Several occupying Pakistani army personnel were killed and wounded in the battle. While valiantly defending the motherland, four BLA members also made the ultimate sacrifice. The combat with the Pakistani occupying forces began when a a patrolling party of BLA came face to face with the advancing enemy forces. BLA fighters charged at the enemy and a battle ensued that lasted for more than three hours. The BLA Sarmachars set high examples of bravery by eliminating and injuring several enemy troops and completely halting their advance. During the battle, four brave comrades, Tariq Marri alias Nasir, Mohammed Hussain Marri alias Jabal, Bakhtiar Sumalani alias Yusuf and Saifullah Zehri alias Sohrab embraced martyrdom. Deprived of moral values, the enemy army also killed two unarmed Baloch farmers named Juma Khan son of Ali Murad and Mahmood son of Shahu from nearby areas, and threw their dead bodies in the said area to portray them as BLA fighters. 
Among the BLA’s fallen soldiers, Tariq Marri alias Nasir, a resident of Kahan, was the commander of BLA’s Special Tactical Operational Squad( STOS) of Bolan Region. Tariq Marri had been associated with BLA since 2017. His personality was rich in leadership skills. Over the past four years, he played a key role in the organization's significant achievements, taking part in many important battles against the enemy. As the STOS Commander, he led the organization's various risky and important missions and achieved many significant victories for the nation and the organization.
