data.biography:
Dr. Khalid Baloch was born in 1967 in the house of Haji Aali Baloch in Kuwait. When the occupying forces returned with a new agenda to annihilate the Baloch nation through settlement, the motherland called upon its brave sons to defend it. He was among the first to take up arms and join the ranks of the Balochistan Liberation Front to defend the nation and the motherland.
He and his companion Dilwash Baloch took upon themselves the pain of their motherland and, with their lives, lit the path of freedom for their nation. They shed their blood in affirmation of their noble cause.
On 8th August 2007, the Pakistan Army received a tip-off from some Baloch traitors that Dr. Khalid and Dilwash were in Sorap, Mand. The Pakistani army cordoned off the area and demanded that Dr. Khalid and Dilwash surrender. But both Baloch freedom fighters fought back; they preferred death over surrender to the occupying enemy. In the intense battle that followed, both Baloch freedom fighters laid down their lives and embraced martyrdom, becoming immortal heroes for the Baloch nation.
The mother of Shaheed Dr. Khalid Baloch said: “He was not only my son but a brave son of Balochistan. He sacrificed his life for his motherland and fulfilled his duty toward me. Khalid and Dilwash were honest, fearless, and brave sons of the Baloch motherland. They have not only etched their names in history but also brought pride to their mothers and their motherland. I am proud to be the mother of such sons.

On 24th August 2011 Pakistani forces raided the hotel of Mulla Haneef & Asghar in Gayab Mand, District Turbat, Balochistan. 19 people were taken into custody & forcibly disappeared, including Gwahram Khalid & Khayham Mohammad Umer, the forces removed the abductees’ shirts, blindfolded them & claimed they belonged to the Baloch Musallah Difa Tanzeem, a notorious death squad.

The abductees were taken to the Mand military camp & forced to chant pro-Pakistan slogans, the next morning, they were shifted to Turbat military camp, lined up & ordered to introduce themselves, when Khayam spoke, a soldier kicked him from behind, knocking him unconscious, an elderly man who protested was also beaten.

The abductees were divided into groups of five & kept in small rooms, it was Ramzan & most were fasting, yet they were given only one glass of water for the entire day.

All abductees were released within a week except Gwahram Khalid & Khayam Mohammad Umer.

On 3rd November 2011, their bodies were found stuffed in flour sacks in Turbat. Khayam showed signs of severe torture; his hand, three fingers & backbone were broken.

On 2 June 2026, in the Zehri area of Khuzdar district, Balochistan, Pakistani forces allegedly opened fire in two separate incidents, killing Khalil Rehman Musiani, son of Sardar Naseer Musiani, and Umair Samalani, son of Haji Naseer Ahmed Samalani.

On 2 June 2026, in the Khuzdar area of Balochistan, Pakistani forces allegedly fired indiscriminately at a vehicle while it was travelling, killing Umair Samalani, son of Haji Naseer Ahmed Samalani, in front of his brother and sister.

Tariq Hamza, son of Haji Hamza, a resident of Dasht Sholeeg, district Gwadar, was enforcedly disappeared by Pakistani forces on November 12, 2024.

Following his disappearance, his family repeatedly sought information about his whereabouts, but no response was provided. On September 19, 2025, Tariq Hamza was killed in a fake encounter alongside three other previously enforcedly disappeared individuals, including Abdul Sattar in Dasht, Kech. His body bore clear signs of severe physical torture followed by bullet wounds. His remains, along with three other Baloch victims, were transferred to Civil Hospital Turbat by FC personnel.

On 22 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch stated that BLF fighters had formally launched Operation Almas with a large-scale, coordinated attack on the main camp of the Pakistani army’s Frontier Works Organization (FWO) at Gwadar Zero Point. Fighters from the BLF’s special Saddo Operational Battalion, alongside members of other units, are participating in this major military engagement. The battle continued into the following day, 23 October 2026, with loud explosions and intense gunfire heard from the location. On 23 October 2026, a statement issued by the BLF spokesperson announced the completion of Operation Almas. The statement claimed that dozens of military and intelligence personnel had been killed, the hub of colonial projects had been destroyed, and army and Frontier Corps posts had been wiped out. It declared that the historic Operation Almas had concluded after achieving all its intended objectives. Operation Almas was carried out in Gwadar and the surrounding areas. It has formally concluded after reportedly achieving all its planned strategic, military, and economic objectives following prolonged and intense clashes. During this wide-ranging operation, the occupying Pakistani army and intelligence network suffered what the statement described as irreparable human and material losses. The BLF’s self-sacrificing fighters targeted the Frontier Works Organization’s (FWO) main camp, destroying a key centre for the implementation of colonial projects, particularly in Gwadar and across Makuran. This, the statement asserted, demonstrated to the world that, without the will and consent of the Baloch nation, colonial projects in Balochistan would never be safe. The offices and camps of Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) and Military Intelligence (MI) inside the FWO’s main camp were also targeted by the organisation’s fighters. Several soldiers, including senior officers, were reportedly killed in the attacks. Throughout Operation Almas, the Jind-Nadr Sarmachars not only thwarted every counterattack by the occupying army, every attempt by armoured vehicles to advance, and every reinforcement convoy, but also forced them to retreat, maintaining control of the camp for twenty hours. As a result of the actions of the Saddo Operational Battalion’s fighters during Operation Almas, Military Intelligence (MI) officers, Special Services Group (SSG) personnel, and dozens of regular army personnel were reportedly killed. In addition, the enemy’s main camp, posts, internal barracks, and administrative offices were reportedly destroyed in explosions and attacks. A number of the occupying army’s armoured vehicles, along with surveillance drones and quadcopters, were also reportedly destroyed during the operation. After repeatedly inflicting defeats on the occupying enemy during Operation Almas, the Jind-Nadr Sarmachars of the Saddo Operational Battalion, adhering to the philosophy of the last bullet, sacrificed their lives in the struggle for freedom, adding a new chapter of bravery to Baloch national history. The following Jind-Nadr Sarmachars played key roles in the operation: Khalid, alias Zamur; Bilqees Didag, alias Almas; Hamidullah, alias Badil; Shakeel, alias Sohrab; Majeed Zaib, alias Aftab; Nasir Ali, alias Nodan; Mujahid Mehr, alias Sagar Zamurani; and Barat, alias Safar Jan. All eight were reported to have embraced martyrdom during this historic operation. On 27 October 2026, the spokesperson issued another detailed statement, announcing that BLF special units had carried out a comprehensive, coordinated, organized, and effective attack on the centres of the occupying Pakistani army, the colonial intelligence network, and exploitative institutions in Gwadar. The statement claimed that more than 80 military and intelligence personnel had been killed; several armoured vehicles, the main army barracks, and intelligence offices had been destroyed; four quadcopters and two surveillance drones had been shot down; and a police station had been seized. It also reported that operations had been conducted at Gabd and Rimdan 250. Following these deadly blows to the state's exploitative structures, Operation Almas was declared successfully concluded. The spokesperson stated that the BLF was formally presenting to the nation, subjugated peoples, and the international community a comprehensive account of the far-reaching military and political achievements of Operation Almas. The historic, organized, effective, coordinated, and comprehensive operation was launched at 4:00 p.m. on 22 October 2026 against the occupying Pakistani state apparatus in Gwadar and the adjoining coastal region. The operation was described as the most organized, coordinated, and far-reaching attack to date against the occupying Pakistani state, its usurping army, intelligence network, exploitative economic institutions, and local puppet administration. It was presented as an expression of the organization's resolve and capabilities. The revolutionary participation of fearless Baloch women, standing shoulder to shoulder with men in the struggle for Baloch national freedom, national survival, and the defence of the coast and its resources, was portrayed as heralding the end of the usurping colonizer. This historic operation was named after the BLF's fearless and courageous guerrilla commander, Almas Baloch. For the past eight years, Commander Almas had been actively involved in the armed national struggle under the BLF banner, driven by her ideological convictions. Bilqees Didag, alias Almas, daughter of Allah Bakhsh Didag, resident of Dasht Kumbel, is a shining chapter of courage, steadfastness and revolutionary sacrifice. She spent her early life in ordinary circumstances and received regular education up to the eighth grade. She was married and has a beloved daughter, but rising above herself and her family circle, she made the cause of the motherland's freedom her whole life. In 2018 she formally joined the armed struggle for national freedom through BLF's revolutionary platform. After joining the organization, she served for four years as a volunteer in the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB), rendering highly valuable and arduous service. For the past eight years Shaheed Almas had been fully active and ideologically committed in the armed defense struggle through the BLF platform. During her organizational life she served as a very active and fearless member of the intelligence wing in sensitive and difficult areas such as Dasht, Turbat and Gwadar. She kept herself in motion day and night to deliver vital intelligence about the enemy to the organization in time. During military fronts and operations, she always carried out, with courage and steadfastness, the very difficult and dangerous responsibility of delivering supplies, weapons and logistics to the sarmachars across Dasht's harsh and rugged mountain ranges. On the path of her revolutionary struggle, the occupying Pakistani army and operatives of the state's death squads made every effort to obstruct her. The occupying army repeatedly attempted to abduct her, hold her in illegal detention and break her mentally and physically, and on one occasion state personnel subjected her to severe torture that left her badly injured. But this tactic of state oppression, taunting and torture could not shake her steadfastness. She faced every hardship with a smile and always stood firm like a rock on the armed front, keeping the flag of freedom high. Even in these grave conditions under state oppression, the wise and courageous way she carried out organizational responsibilities while hiding in various areas is eloquent proof of her high military insight and ideological maturity. Shaheed Bilqees Didag alias Almas put into practice the idea that on the difficult path of national freedom, all hardships, troubles and sacrifices are acceptable, but national slavery and state domination are not acceptable under any circumstances. To realize this idea, she made the final decision to sacrifice herself for the motherland. Shaheed Almas carried out her duties with great devotion in various military detachments and units of the BLF, and from the time the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB) was founded she was its active founder and core member.

Saleh Baloch, son of Hamza Baloch, was a resident of Kohad, Tehsil Tump, District Kech. He was a student of High School Nizarabad and a zonal member of BSO Azad, Tump Zone. He joined BSO Azad to play his role in the national cause of his homeland. He had a keen interest in politics since childhood. That is why, at an early age, he joined BSO Azad to work for his nation and people.
He was a peaceful political activist and worked to spread awareness regarding his nation and education. He was among hundreds of BSO activists who were killed by the Pakistani army for expressing their political views. He also actively participated in social activities in his hometown. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising peaceful political expression.
He was abducted on 1st September 2011 from the Kulbar area of Kech by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agencies. He was killed because of his association with the mother organization of the Baloch homeland. His dumped body was found on 7th September 2011 in the Kulbar area of Kech district, Balochistan. His body bore extreme signs of torture.
He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a very young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Abdul Salam Kurd, alias Nasrullah, son of Huzoor Bakhsh Kurd, was 21 years old and a resident of Maro, Spilenji area of Mastung district, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2025 and later became part of the Majeed Brigade in the same year. He served on the Nagaho front and was martyred in Mastung.
After joining the BLA, Abdul Salam was transferred to the Nagaho front by the organization. On the Nagaho front, Nasrullah carried out his role with revolutionary conviction and remained steadfast in the struggle against the enemy. He dedicated his life to the national struggle and soon joined the Majeed Brigade, reflecting his belief that the cause of freedom was more important than his personal life. This determination made him a strong figure within the ranks of the resistance despite his young age. Abdul Salam was the cousin of Majeed Baloch, who carried out a fidayee attack in the Red Zone on the Quetta front during Operation Herof Phase II.
Abdul Salam embraced martyrdom while fighting on the Mastung front during Operation Herof Phase II, adding another bright chapter to the history of resistance. Nasrullah’s martyrdom became a testament to the fact that the struggle for freedom lives on through the determination and sacrifices of young hearts, and such figures remain forever alive in the collective memory of their nation.

On 8 August 2016, terrorists attacked the Government Hospital in Quetta, Balochistan, in a suicide bombing and shooting. More than 70 people were killed, mainly lawyers, and more than 130 others were injured.
The majority of those killed were lawyers who had gathered at the hospital after the body of Advocate Bilal Anwar Kasi, president of the Balochistan Bar Association, was brought there. Kasi had been shot dead by a gunman near Mengal Chowk on Manno Jan Road in Quetta while he was leaving his home for his office.
Responsibility for the attack was claimed by various Islamist groups, including Jamaat-ul-Ahrar and the Islamic State Khorasan Province. However, nationalist groups have alleged that these extremist organisations are backed by the Pakistani state and its military to counter the nationalist movement in the region and exploit its natural resources.
Estimates of the death toll ranged between 70 people, while more than 120 were injured. Of those killed, 54 were lawyers. Among them, 15 were Baloch by ethnicity, while the majority were Pashtuns by ethnicity.

The Baloch advocates or lawyers who were killed are identified as follows:

01 Ghulam Farooq Badini, son of Haji Abdul Ghani.
02 Bashir Ahmed Qazi, son of Qazi Ahmed Jan.
03 Bashir Ahmad Zehri, son Haji Mir Ahmed Zehri.
04 Naseer Ahmed Langove, son Abdul Rahim.
05 Chakar Khan Rind, son of Mehmood.
06 Abdul Rashid, son of Abdul Latif.
07 Nooruddin Rakshani, son Haji Naseeruddin.
08 Muhammad Imran, son Ghulam Farooq.
09 Muneer Ahmed Mengal, son Ghulam Murtaza.
10 Sangat Jehan Jamaldini, son of Dr. Jahanzaib.
11 Mohammad Ali Satakzai, son of Taj Mohammad Khan.
12 Mehmood Ahmed Lehri, son Haji Abdul Hameed.
13 Jamil Ur Rehman, son of Qazi Abdul Hameed.
14 Amanullah Langove, son of Haji Dad Karim.
15 Sabir Ali, son of Abdul Rasheed.

Nooruddin Rakhshani was an active member of the lawyers’ movement and an advocate for rule of law.
He was 45 years old.
Wife of Dosta Mahmood Baloch, and mother to his children. She was martyred alongside her family in the missile strike in Sistan and Balochistan.

Mumtaz Baloch, son of Bohair Baloch and a resident of Bahoot-Chat, Dasht, was a brave and honest freedom fighter of the BLF. He was a highly skilled comrade who, in a very short time, developed great expertise in guerrilla warfare. He fought bravely against the enemy in various areas of Balochistan. He embraced martyrdom in a battle against Pakistani forces in Kaheer Kor, Dasht, on 25 January 2022.

On June 6, 2025 at around 7 AM, a large contingent of operatives from the puppet militia (Bugti Peace Force) operating under the patronage of the occupying Pakistani army and intelligence agencies, and led by the puppet Chief Minister of Balochistan, Sarfraz Bugti, launched an attack on a patrol team’s camp of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in the mountainous region of Koh Jandar, Rakhni, Barkhan.
The Sarmachars (freedom fighters) immediately adopted a defensive strategy and, after an intense battle lasting approximately three hours, successfully thwarted the enemy’s advance and encirclement attempts, managing to withdraw safely. During this clash, two members of the death squad were killed.
However, the battle did not end with this initial phase. The enemy pursued the Sarmachars and implemented a strategy to block their escape routes. A few kilometres from the site of the initial clash, the Sarmachars encountered fresh reinforcements of the occupying Pakistani army, leading to another intense confrontation. This fierce battle continued for seven hours. In this prolonged combat, four fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front embraced martyrdom and etched their names in the pages of history, while two soldiers of the occupying Pakistani army were killed and several others were severely injured.
Among the martyrs who laid down their lives in the clash with the occupying forces at Koh Jandar, Rakhni, were Rasaan Qadir (alias Rehan), Mustafa Noor (alias Diljan), Samiullah (alias Meeran), and Shahzaib (alias Shahshan).
Sarmachar Samiullah alias Meeran, son of Noor Muhammad, was from Malai Bazaar, Turbat. He joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in March 2024. Initially, he was attached to the organization’s secret urban network in Turbat, where he provided several crucial pieces of intelligence that foiled many of the enemy’s plots. Later, he was stationed at the mountainous camp in Barkhan, where his courage and bravery on the military front set shining examples for future generations of freedom fighters.

data.martyrdomPlace: Noshki and Kharan mountainous area, Balochistan
data.biography:
In a face to face battle with the Pakistani military and its agents in the mountainous regions of Noshki and Kharan on 24 September 2021, more than a dozen enemy personnel were killed, whereas six freedom fighters, including five members of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), also embraced martyrdom.
The battle commenced early Friday morning in Siyah Lop, near Baddo Dor, when enemy forces attempted to encircle a patrolling party of Baloch freedom fighters. In the face-to-face battle that lasted for more than four hours, scores of enemy personnel were killed and injured. Five freedom fighters of the BLA and one freedom fighter of the United Baloch Army (UBA), while evacuating their comrades from the battle zone, embraced martyrdom.
The fallen comrades include Commander Ganjal alias Comrade Mazar, Nazeer alias Sangar, Faisal alias Yasir, Kaleem alias Bolani, and Rehan alias Mehrwaan, all members of the Baloch Liberation Army. A member of the United Baloch Army, Nodaan alias Hammal, bravely fought alongside BLA comrades and embraced martyrdom.
Nazeer alias Sangar, son of Mohammad Qasim Meerwani Baloch; Faisal Rodeni alias Yasir; and Kaleem alias Bolani, son of Maqbool Ahmed Reki, all of whom belonged to Soorab town, had joined the BLA three years ago. After serving for several years in the urban units of the BLA, they were deployed to the mountainous battlefronts following an organisational decision.

On 21 February 1987, in the coastal town of Jiwani, Balochistan, Pakistani forces opened indiscriminate fire on a peaceful protest rally organized by local Baloch residents over water shortages and the demand for clean drinking water. A two year old girl, Yasmeen Baloch, along with Azgul Baloch and Ghulam Nabi Baloch, were killed, and several other demonstrators were injured.

On 29 November 2025 in the Garhook Hoshab area of Turbat district, Balochistan, four children were seriously injured after being struck by mortar shells fired by Pakistani forces at the civilian population. The injured were: Durdang D/O Khalid, aged 11; Tahira D/O Khalid, aged 12; Asiya D/O Shambay, aged 18 and Yasmeen D/O Nasir, aged 13.

Yasmeen D/O Nasir, who was in critical condition, was transferred from Turbat Teaching Hospital to Karachi, where she succumbed to her injuries and passed away.

Fateh Baloch, son of Shahdad, a driver from the Mewar area of Mashkai district in Balochistan, was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani genocidal forces on January 13, 2026. He was taken near the Main Army Camp in Mashkai while carrying passengers in his vehicle. Pakistani Army soldiers stopped his vehicle in front of the main camp and took Fateh Baloch inside. According to his family, the army admitted to taking him into their custody. His father was told by the army that his son would be killed. After one and a half months of disappearance, on March 4, 2026, his bullet riddled body was found in the Mashkai River. Fateh Baloch was a civilian driver, earning his livelihood to support his family.

On 16 July 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that the BLA eliminated more than forty personnel of the Pakistani Army and injured several others in forty-eight operations across Balochistan during the previous fifteen days. As part of the economic blockade, vehicles violating the blockade on major highways were targeted and destroyed. Furthermore, four key bridges were destroyed using planted explosive devices. During various clashes with the occupying forces, five BLA fighters - Rahimullah Mohammad Hassni, alias Zafar, son of Lumma Raaj Bibi; Khair Mohammad Khairo, alias Hammal, son of Shahbaz; Kaka Baloch, alias Kaka Rasheed, son of Shahbaz; Masood Baloch, alias Sami, son of Ghulam Jan; and Shah Nazar Baloch, alias Badal, son of Khuda Nazar - embraced martyrdom.

Masood Baloch, alias Sami, son of Ghulam Jan, was a resident of the Washbod area of Panjgur. He joined the BLA in 2020, served on the Mountain Front from 2023, and was martyred on 13 July 2026 in the Chedagi area of Panjgur.
Masood Baloch, alias Sami, had been a member of the BLA for the past six years. During this period, he remained active on the urban front for four years and on the mountain front for two years, fighting against the enemy. While carrying out his responsibilities on the urban front, he repeatedly provided fellow fighters with important intelligence on the enemy, contributing to the success of several significant armed operations. During his time on the urban front, he and his fellow fighters dealt severe blows to the enemy on numerous occasions.
In accordance with the organization's directives, he later left the urban front and took up his position on the mountain battlefield, where he inflicted heavy losses on the enemy through his steadfastness and courageous conduct. He was a cadre who kept himself abreast of modern methods of armed warfare and its evolving requirements.
For Masood, the armed struggle against the occupying force was not merely a matter of war; rather, he regarded it as an important stage in the formation of a national state. He chose the path of the Baloch armed struggle within the framework of an ideological and intellectual vision and remained sincerely committed to it until the end. Under the recent military strategy aimed at disrupting the enemy's economic activities on the battlefield, he repeatedly targeted interests associated with the occupying force on the Panjgur front. In the region, he also remained at the forefront of significant military operations against the death squad and the enemy's personnel.
He was regarded as one of the organization's brave and dedicated fighters, possessing the ability to confront and defeat the occupying force's personnel on every battlefield and every front. On several occasions, he engaged the enemy in direct face-to-face combat. Among his Sangat, he was known as a courageous fighter.
Masood Baloch remained steadfast in his commitment to the ideology and vision of national liberation, upholding that vision until the very end. He embraced martyrdom in direct combat while thwarting the enemy's advance on a highway under the organization's control. He remained faithful until his last breath to the oath he had taken upon joining the organization - to defend his homeland until his final breath. His sacrifices will be remembered in the history of Baloch national liberation in golden words.

In 1838, the British sent a force led by Alexander Burnes to reinstate Shah Shuja Durrani as the king of Afghanistan by deposing Amir Dost Mohammad Khan. To reach Afghanistan, they needed passage through Balochistan, particularly the Bolan Pass. However, Khan Mehrab Khan refused to allow the British to use his land to attack a neighboring country. The British sent Lieutenant Leach to negotiate with the Baloch government, but the Khan stood firm. When British forces reached Shaal via Bolan, some patriotic Baloch, without the Khan’s knowledge, attacked British troops out of nationalist sentiment and a desire to protect their homeland.
After toppling Amir Dost Mohammad Khan, the British Governor General of India, Lord Auckland, ordered an attack on Balochistan. In 1839, around 7,000 British troops marched from Shaal to attack the Baloch Meeri (capital). Anticipating an invasion, Khan Mehrab Khan declared war and sent messages to tribal leaders, but many saw the British as allies rather than invaders and chose to collaborate with them rather than defend their land. When Khan Mehrab Khan gathered his resistance fighters, the number of loyal warriors had dwindled to only 700 due to the short sightedness of many tribal chiefs. Nevertheless, Mehrab Khan was determined to fight. At his court, a respected figure, Akhund Muhammad Siddiq, advised him that he was not in a position to wage war at that time. He suggested that the Khan should leave Kalat with his companions, regroup and strengthen his forces, and then launch an attack against the British when the time was right, on 13 November 1839, the British forces launched an attack on Kalat, and a fierce battle ensued. During the fighting, Khan Mehrab Khan Baloch was martyred by a British bullet.

Among those martyred alongside him were:

Diwan Bacha Mal, Minister of Finance

Diwan Khem Chand

Diwan Asardas Mukhi, from the Hindu Panchayat of Kalat

Abdul Karim Raisani, brother of Sardar Asad Khan Raisani

On 6 November 2026, the Baloch Liberation Army's media channel, Hakkal, published the biographies and details of six martyrs associated with the organization.

Among them, three fighters - Muneer Ahmad Jattak, alias Noora, son of Habib Khan Jattak; Shahzaib Bangulzai, alias Ehsan, son of Samiullah Bangulzai; and Fareed Langove, son of Ghulam Nabi Langove - were martyred on 20 October 2026 in the Rodinjo area of Kalat District.

Two other fighters, Parvez Ahmad Mohammad Hassni, alias Qadir, son of Shekari Mohammad Khan Mohammad Hassni, and Noman Jamaldini, alias Comrade Sameer, son of Agha Mohammad Jamaldini, were martyred on 24 October 2026 in the Gidar area of Surab.

The sixth fighter, Aurangzaib Langove, alias Asif, son of Hameedullah Langove, was martyred on 24 October 2026 in the Manguchar area of Kalat District.

Fareed Langove, alias Abiyan, son of Ghulam Nabi Langove, was a resident of the Bosa Mandi area of Quetta. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Kalat front. He was martyred on 20 October 2026 in Rodinjo, Kalat.

Fareed Langove joined the ranks of the Baloch Liberation Army this year, seeking to restore national independence and the sovereign status of the Baloch state. This brave son of Quetta firmly believed that, without the freedom of their homeland, the Baloch nation had no other path forward. This conviction led him towards the practical and ideological objectives of armed resistance, represented by the operational platform of the Baloch Liberation Army. Following organizational instructions, he was transferred to the Quetta front, where he completed his basic military training courses.

After completing his training, he was transferred to the Kalat front, where he operated on the front lines. He demonstrated revolutionary zeal, great courage, and enthusiasm in confronting the enemy. He actively participated in forward-advance operations and, alongside his comrades, carried out organizational assignments. On 20 October, he was killed while fighting against the enemy. He will be remembered by history as a courageous figure.

On the morning of January 8, 2026, at around 10 AM in the Zamuran area of Buleda, the Pakistani military carried out a drone attack on the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) camp, resulting in the martyrdom of four BLF fighters. The martyrs include Hussain, alias Kamal Baloch; Akbar, alias Tahir Baloch; Waseem, alias Mero Baloch; and Huzaifa, alias Nodan Baloch.
Waseem, alias Mero Baloch, son of Rasool Bakhsh and resident of Dasht, joined the BLF on September 10, 2025. Before moving to the camp, he had been in contact with the organization and was involved in logistics and resource management. Waseem, alias Mero, became a guiding light for every sarmachar due to his courage, diligence, and sincerity. His determination and eagerness to take on new responsibilities distinguished him on every front. He fulfilled his duties wholeheartedly, demonstrating discipline and perseverance in every task. His sacrifice and dedication will always be remembered.

Mehboob Baloch, son of Amanullah, from the Gowargu area of Panjgur district in Balochistan, was abducted and forcibly disappeared by the Frontier Corps of the Pakistani forces. After eight months, he was extrajudicially killed, and his body was dumped in the Shapatan area of Panjgur district on 8 March 2026.

In 1838, the British sent a force led by Alexander Burnes to reinstate Shah Shuja Durrani as the king of Afghanistan by deposing Amir Dost Mohammad Khan. To reach Afghanistan, they needed passage through Balochistan, particularly the Bolan Pass. However, Khan Mehrab Khan refused to allow the British to use his land to attack a neighboring country. The British sent Lieutenant Leach to negotiate with the Baloch government, but the Khan stood firm. When British forces reached Shaal via Bolan, some patriotic Baloch, without the Khan’s knowledge, attacked British troops out of nationalist sentiment and a desire to protect their homeland.
After toppling Amir Dost Mohammad Khan, the British Governor General of India, Lord Auckland, ordered an attack on Balochistan. In 1839, around 7,000 British troops marched from Shaal to attack the Baloch Meeri (capital). Anticipating an invasion, Khan Mehrab Khan declared war and sent messages to tribal leaders, but many saw the British as allies rather than invaders and chose to collaborate with them rather than defend their land. When Khan Mehrab Khan gathered his resistance fighters, the number of loyal warriors had dwindled to only 700 due to the short sightedness of many tribal chiefs. Nevertheless, Mehrab Khan was determined to fight. At his court, a respected figure, Akhund Muhammad Siddiq, advised him that he was not in a position to wage war at that time. He suggested that the Khan should leave Kalat with his companions, regroup and strengthen his forces, and then launch an attack against the British when the time was right, on 13 November 1839, the British forces launched an attack on Kalat, and a fierce battle ensued. During the fighting, Khan Mehrab Khan Baloch was martyred by a British bullet.

Among those martyred alongside him were:

Diwan Bacha Mal, Minister of Finance

Diwan Khem Chand

Diwan Asardas Mukhi, from the Hindu Panchayat of Kalat

Abdul Karim Raisani, brother of Sardar Asad Khan Raisani
