Kohdil Bugti, a 26 year old son of Ali Baksh Bugti and a resident of Sui, Dera Bugti, was a member of the Baloch Republican Students Organization (BRSO). On 20 February 2011, he was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. A month later, on 26 March 2011, his body was dumped in the Pat Mundrani area of Dera Bugti, Balochistan.

On 31 October 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Front issued a statement claiming that 28 personnel of the occupying army had been killed and several others wounded in 13 operations. The statement further claimed that weapons had been seized from the police, drone surveillance cameras and vehicles belonging to the occupying army had been destroyed, and the organization's fighter, Hashum, alias Noor Baloch, had been martyred.

On 28 October 2026, fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front's KAAD and Qurban units carried out an operation in Mainaz, Buleida. They set up an effective blockade on two sides of Mainaz Bazaar and conducted snap checks of vehicles. Simultaneously they attacked the occupying army's camp in Alandoor with heavy and automatic weapons, with multiple rocket and grenade-launcher rounds hitting their intended targets, resulting in heavy human and material losses to the occupying army inside the camp. During the operation, a surveillance camera installed at the camp and a quadcopter were also destroyed by shooting, while a sniper tactical team remained in a protective position. A four-vehicle convoy sent as reinforcements was ambushed at Bit, killing 4 personnel and wounding several, and two of the enemy's vehicles were completely destroyed. Another army detachment tried to advance from the city's rear route, but KAAD and Qurban unit's fighters immediately counterattacked and halted its advance. In this clash another 3 enemy personnel were killed and several wounded.

In this battle, the brave Qurban unit fighter Shaheed Hashum alias Noor Baloch, son of Muhammad Umar, resident of Absar Bund Bazaar, Turbat, fought in the front ranks and successfully held back the occupying army's advance. As a result of his unparallel courage and resistance the enemy was forced to retreat, while the army's destroyed vehicles and bodies lay at the site of the attack for a long time.

Martyr Hashum joined the BLF in 2023. For more than a year he served as an urban guerrilla in a sensitive city like Turbat, inflicting human and material losses on the enemy. He played a very active role in the organization's intelligence unit, and on the basis of the information he provided the organization carried out several important missions. In 2024, by organizational decision, he moved to the mountain front. The occupying state subjected his family to collective punishment to force him to abandon the struggle. The Pakistani army attacked his house twice with grenades, his elder brother was forcibly disappeared, and his parents were forced to hold a press conference. Despite all these tactics, the state could not make him step back an inch from the national struggle, he was a firm fighter in thought and deed and kept the banner of freedom high until his last breath. His struggle and steadfastness will be a guiding light for his fellow sarmachars.

He was a very sincere and committed fighter who performed his national duty in various parts of Balochistan, including Turbat, Zamuran, Balgatar, Panjgur, Parom and Hoshab. He took part as a front-line fighter in several important military engagements of the BLF and BRAS. He played a key role in the success of the capture of an army camp at Goran, Panjgur, under BRAS, as a front-line fighter, and of the camp at Balgatar, as an LMG master. During the joint mission of KAAD, the Qurban unit and the Sniper Tactical Team in Mainaz, Buleida, on 28 October, Shaheed Hashum alias Noor Baloch stayed on the front line and fought the occupying army from a close range. After bringing all his fellow sangats safely out of the enemy's encirclement, he attained the high rank of martyrdom. The BLF offers red salutes, with reverence and respect, to Shaheed Hashim alias Noor Baloch's ultimate sacrifice and vows to carry his mission to its destination.

Ghulam Jan, son of Beijar Baloch, a resident of the mountainous Pahu area and currently living in Karkian Khad, Tehsil Kolwah, Awaran district, was extrajudicially killed on July 13, 2025. He was enforcedly disappeared in broad daylight by state-backed death squads operating under the command and protection of Pakistani armed forces.
According to local sources, Ghulam Jan had been previously subjected to persistent harassment and threats. His family was forcibly displaced from their native village, Pahu, due to repeated military intimidation.
On the evening of July 13, Ghulam Jan was forcibly disappeared by state-backed death squads. Just hours later, his bullet-riddled body bearing visible signs of torture was discovered dumped in the Kuli area of Kolwah.

data.martyrdomPlace: Sorap Dam, Buleda, Turbat district, Balochistan
data.biography: Neik Saal, son of Dilwash and a resident of the Gardank area in Buleda Tehsil, district Kech, was forcibly disappeared from the village of Minaz in Buleda by Pakistani forces and state-backed death squads, along with Nizar Arz Muhammad and Quddous Baloch. On October 1, 2025, all three were tragically killed, and their bullet-riddled bodies were discovered in the Sorap Dam area of Buleda Tehsil. Neik Saal was a driver and, like many other traders in oil packs, was engaged in cross-border trade.
Noor Khan, alias Bramsh Baloch, was a resident of the Khairabad, Kech area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 28 September 2020 in Balochistan.
Abdul Hameed, alias Shahzaib, was a resident of the Greshag, Khuzdar area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 5 July 2020 in Balochistan.

On 2 August 2024, Pakistani forces indiscriminately opened fire on a rally in Nushki that was protesting against the Baloch genocide and the crackdown on the historic Baloch National Gathering in Gwadar. As a result, many people were injured, and Hamdan Baloch, the son of Abdullah Badini, was martyred.

Malik Mohammad Hashim Shahwani, alias Salahuddin, son of Malik Abdul Kareem Shahwani, was a resident of Kili Barozai, Qambrani, Quetta. He joined the BLA in 2025 and served on the Urban Front. In January 2026, he moved to the Mountain Front in Mastung and was killed on 1 June 2026 in Kirdagap, Mastung, Balochistan.
Hailing from the Qambrani area of Quetta, Sangat Malik Mohammad, alias Salahuddin, joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2025 and, in accordance with organizational directives, began participating in urban operations. He carried out his responsibilities with honesty and dedication, provided important intelligence, and took part in other activities. Subsequently, in January 2026, he commenced his service on the mountain front.
After gaining an understanding of the political objectives and philosophy behind the Baloch armed struggle, he came to the conclusion that armed resistance was the most effective means of ending what he viewed as Pakistani violence and occupation. He believed that this philosophy would enable the Baloch people to establish an independent, sovereign, and dignified state. After completing his basic military training, he served as a frontline fighter against enemy advances and, by remaining in his position until his final days, demonstrated his commitment to defending his homeland.
Malik Mohammad was killed while fighting on the Kirdagap front. According to supporters of the Baloch national movement, his death conveyed the message that Baloch youth are no longer intimidated by the state's power and are prepared to defend what they regard as their homeland and national rights. They believe that his sacrifices will be remembered in the history of the Baloch national liberation struggle.
data.fullName: Malik Mohammad Hashim Shahwani, alias Salahuddin

data.biography:
Rasool Jan Baloch, son of Dil Murad Baloch, was born on July 22, 1993, in Kolwah, District Awaran. He was a B.A. student at Atta Shad Degree College, Turbat, Kech, and served as the General Secretary of BSO Azad, Turbat Zone.
He joined BSO Azad in 2008 when he was a student at Geshkor High School. He also worked as a teacher at the Dynamic English Language Teaching Academy (DELTA).
He was among the influential figures in student politics and played an important role in organizing the activities of the organization during very difficult times. He was passionate about reading literature and helped bring hundreds of students from his hometown to Kech for education.
He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising his right to peaceful political expression. He was an intellectual and educated individual who spread awareness about the national struggle and scientific education, for which he was reportedly ordered to be abducted by security agencies.
On January 6, 2014, he was abducted by Pakistan’s secret agencies from Turbat along with several other students. On April 13, 2015, he was killed in a reported fake encounter by the Pakistan Army in Gebun, Turbat, along with five other detained Baloch prisoners.
Rasool Jan was a strong figure in the national movement’s organizational platform. His body bore severe signs of torture. He remained a committed member of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times.
He inspired many young people to join the movement of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

On 10 July 2021, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 25 June 2021, operatives of Pakistani intelligence agencies opened fire and martyred Ayub Baloch, alias Nako Sharif, a key member of the organization, in the Pishin area of western Occupied Balochistan.

Ayub Baloch, alias Nako Sharif had been associated with the Baloch National Liberation Movement for the past 13 years. He began his armed struggle in 2008. Later, in 2018, he joined the Baloch Liberation Army. From that day until the last moment of his life, he remained sincere and honest in his commitment to the organization's manifesto, ideology, and principles.

Over a period of thirteen years, Pakistan's intelligence agencies not only offered concessions to humiliate Ayub Baloch but also raided his home several times and tortured his family to force him to surrender. However, Nako Sharif was a man of strong nerves who remained committed to the national cause with enthusiasm and courage until the end.

Even before joining the BLA, Nako Sharif naturally possessed expertise in handling freedom fighters and maintaining organizational stability within the national movement and armed struggle. Due to his previous role, experience, and qualifications, he was included among the BLA's responsible colleagues from the very beginning.

Shaheed Nako Sharif belonged to the Malant area of Kech District in Occupied Balochistan.

He rendered unforgettable services to the cause of national liberation in various parts of Occupied Balochistan, including Kech. For a long time, he played an important role in western Occupied Balochistan in accordance with an organizational decision.

On 28 June 2026, the spokesperson for the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) issued a statement announcing that five fighters of the organisation - Shoaib Zehri, alias Farooq; Zakariya Zehri, alias Ustad Zoreen Baloch; Kifayatullah Badini, alias Badil Baloch; Captain Hashum Baloch, alias Kambar; and Abdul Rahim, alias Ustad Imran - had embraced martyrdom. The statement said that the blood of the martyrs guarantees Baloch national survival and sovereignty.

Hashum Baloch, alias Kambar, son of Nasir and a resident of Minaz, Buleda, was martyred on June 21, 2026, on Garuk Road between Buleda and Turbat. He was targeted in a drone strike carried out by the occupying army.
Martyr Captain Hashum began his struggle in 2022 under the banner of the Balochistan Liberation Front. Before formally joining the mountain front, he played a key role for one year within the urban and regional networks, monitoring enemy movements and supplying rations and military equipment. After this clandestine organizational work, he transferred to the mountain front in April 2023.
Due to his exceptional military and organizational capabilities, he was promoted to the rank of Captain by the organization. He rendered valuable combat and organizational services on difficult fronts, including Buleda, Paroom, Zamuran, Dasht, Kulbar, and Seyaji. He was an extremely hardworking, resilient, kind, and fearless fighter who, through his technical and military expertise, personally developed several important defensive and military resources for the camp and the organization.
On June 21, 2026, Martyr Captain Hashum set out from camp with his unit on an organizational patrol. At 1:00 PM that day, Pakistani occupying forces launched a drone strike on them on Garuk Road between Buleda and Turbat, resulting in Captain Hashum's martyrdom.

Ikram Baloch, son of Murad Hasil, born on 1 July 1992, was a resident of Pedraak, Kech District. He was a poet and a student of Computer Science at the University of Balochistan. He served as the Information Secretary of BSO Azad, Shaal Zone. He had a keen interest in computer studies and possessed strong computer skills.
He was not allowed by the security forces to continue his education, as he was considered a threat because of his education and skills. He played an important role in organizing the organizational activities in the capital city of Balochistan, Quetta.
His family had been under surveillance by the Pakistani army and its backed death squads in Pedraak. More than six members of his family have been killed by security forces and local militias to suppress the national struggle in the area.
He was a polite political activist and a keen observer of politics. He participated in every activity of the organization to pursue the greater cause of the oppressed Baloch nation. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for his peaceful political expression.
He was a victim of extrajudicial killing along with his father and brother on 22 March 2014 at his home during a military operation conducted by the Pakistan Army in Pedraak, Kech District, Balochistan. His body showed severe signs of torture.
He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a very young age will be remembered in the golden chapters of Baloch history.

On March 8, 2023, Pakistani drones fired three missiles at a Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) guerrilla camp in the mountain range between Hoshap and Pasni. Following the strike, Pakistani forces began landing commandos around the camp from helicopters. In the missile attack, the camp commander, Hasil Baloch, along with four other fighters, was martyred. The remaining Sarmachars fought bravely in close combat, killing several commandos of the occupying forces before they themselves were martyred in the great cause of freedom for their homeland.
The Sarmachars who were martyred are:
Hasil (alias Doda), Wasdil (alias Jami), Nizam (alias Noshad), Waqas (alias Miras), Khalid (alias Kiyya), Shah Fahad (alias Aslam), and Ilyas Baloch (alias Rahmdil).
Martyr Khalid (alias Kiyya), son of Hasil and resident of Jaki Gowarkop, was a member of Lashkar-e-Balochistan. He had been associated with the organization for a year. He was a brave and true son of the homeland.

Inayat Ullah Jatak, son of Allah Dina Jatak, a 70-year-old retired government teacher and father of Asma Jatak, was killed on 4 August 2026 in Shehzad City, Khuzdar.
His daughter, Asma Jatak, had faced threats and harassment in connection with the incident and her public appeals to the authorities for protection.
Inayat Ullah Jatak was reportedly targeted and killed by Pakistani state-backed private armed groups operating in the area, locally referred to as 'death squads.' Prior to the killing, Asma Jatak released a video message stating that she was facing threats and harassment from these groups. She publicly appealed to the government and relevant authorities for protection and stated that she would hold the state responsible should any harm come to her.
Following these public appeals and warnings, her father was killed.
The killing must also be considered in the context of Asma Jatak’s enforced disappearance in February 2025. On 6 February 2025, her family and local residents blocked a highway and held a protest demanding her immediate recovery and release. She was subsequently released. Asma Jatak has stated that she was subjected to severe physical and psychological torture while in detention.
The killing of Inayat Ullah, when considered alongside the threats directed at his daughter, her previous enforced disappearance, and her public appeals for protection, raises serious concerns about the safety of Asma Jatak and her family.

Shukrullah Baloch, son of Abdul Nabi, was 28 years old and a resident of Kappar, Washuk, Balochistan. He was forcibly disappeared by the Pakistani army on 7 September 2026 from the China-Pakistan Economic Corridor (CPEC) road in Paatk, Washuk. After ten days of detention in a torture centre, he was extrajudicially killed on 17 September 2026. His tortured body was found by the roadside of the CPEC road in the Paatk area of Washuk, Balochistan.
Shukrullah was a young, talented, and ordinary individual who worked to earn a sufficient income and meet his family's daily expenses. Despite being a nonviolent individual, he was forcibly disappeared without any justification by personnel of the Pakistani army, apparently belonging to the Frontier Corps (FC). He was illegally detained and subsequently killed. His lifeless body was found by the roadside of the CPEC road in Paatk, bearing visible signs of torture.

On 2 June 2025 in the Mach area of Bolan, Pakistani forces and fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) came face to face when the fighters were travelling for organizational activities. At a location called Goni Para, clashes broke out between the BLA fighters and the Pakistani forces. During the confrontation, the forces deployed commandos using helicopters. In the clashes that continued for several hours, at least eight personnel of the opposing forces were killed, while five BLA fighters - Washdal, alias Mashmar; Samiullah, alias Sameer; Shehryar Shahwani, alias Chairman; Sajawal, alias Cheeda; and Nadir, alias Chiragh - achieved martyrdom.
Washdil, alias Mashmar, son of Lal Khan Sumalani, belonged to Sanjawal in the Bolan region. 22 old Washdal joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2024 and at a young age, took up arms with the resolve to fulfill what he saw as his national responsibility. He played an important role on many occasions on the Bolan front and ultimately embraced martyrdom after inflicting significant losses on the enemy.
Samiullah, alias Sameer, son of Muhammad Akram; the Shehryar, alias Chairman, son of Mehrab Khan Shahwani; and the Sajawal, alias Cheeda, son of Bawal Khan Shahwani - all belonged to Parangabad in Mastung. These three companions joined the BLA a year ago and as urban guerrillas, participated in several successful operations. Always active in striking the enemy and fulfilling organizational duties, they were present on every front. Their lives, devoted to the cause of national freedom, have become a guiding light for Baloch youth.
Nadir, alias Chiragh, son of Mazar Khan Lehri, was originally from Narmuk in the Kalat region but was residing in Quetta. In his guerrilla role, he was highly organized, vigilant, and steadfast, confronting the enemy with courage. Constantly engaged in organizational work, he remained firm in his responsibilities until his final breath.

In a statement issued on 26 June 2025 by Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson of the Baloch Liberation Army, it was said that three BLA fighters were martyred in clashes with the occupying Pakistani forces on the fronts of Quetta, Kalat, and Seyahji. The martyred comrades include Jamshed,  Nowroz and Munawar Baig.
On 22 June 2025 in the Daghari area of Quetta, a BLA patrol team encountered the occupying Pakistani forces as they attempted to advance in the area. A face to face battle broke out between the occupying forces and the fighters, which continued for a long time. Several personnel of the occupying army were killed and injured in the clashes, while BLA fighter Jamshed, also known as Rizwan, attained martyrdom.
In the evening, two units of BLA fighters surrounded the occupying army’s infantry in a ravine and attacked them from two sides. As a result, six soldiers of the occupying forces were killed on the spot and several others were injured. During the hour-long clash, BLA fighter Nowroz, alias King Najeeb, was martyred.
On 20 June 2025 in the Langasi area of Dasht, BLA fighters encountered the occupying Pakistani forces while travelling for organizational work. In the face to face battle that ensued, the occupying forces suffered losses. Meanwhile, in an already injured state, Sangat Munawar Baig was martyred during the clash with the occupying forces.
Jamshed, alias Rizwan, son of Noor Khan Satakzai, belonged to the Daghari area of Quetta. 29 year old Jamshed joined the BLA in 2019 and while serving as an urban guerrilla, dealt significant blows to the occupying forces on many occasions. Later, in 2024, he moved to the mountain front, where he served on the Bolan and Quetta fronts. He was a symbol of discipline, silence and agility. His presence among comrades was considered a source of confidence. In every mission, he outwitted the occupying forces with courage and intelligence.
Aman Jan, was a resident of the Jamak area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 22 December 2015 in Balochistan.

On January 12, 2026, BLF sarmachar Baddal, also known as Dildar, son of Khudabaksh and resident of Duraski, Awaran, was on leave visiting his family in the Tirteej, Ahori area of Awaran when he was martyred in a clash with the occupying Pakistani army and death squads.
Martyr Baddal, alias Dildar, joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in 2013 and served the organization for thirteen years as a loyal, steadfast, and hardworking sarmachar. As a brave and experienced sarmachar, he admirably fulfilled the responsibilities assigned to him in numerous battles. In recognition of his military capabilities and commitment, the BLF had promoted him to the rank of Second Lieutenant.
The BLF pays tribute to martyr Baddal, alias Dildar, and his sacrifice will be remembered as a distinguished chapter in the national struggle.
The martyr's relatives have not lost courage despite the oppression and tyranny of occupying Pakistan, forced displacement, and other atrocities, and have remained steadfastly connected to the Baloch national liberation movement.

Yarwar Baloch, son of Habib Baloch, from Humari Kahn, Shapuk, Balochistan, was an 18 year old tailor by profession, earning a simple living.
On June 16, 2025, he stood with his father outside the High Court after their hearing had ended. As they stepped out of the court gate, he was forcibly disappeared by state agencies - snatched from his father’s hands in broad daylight.
On June 17, 2025, his family protested and blocked the CPEC road, demanding his return. Within two days, the state offered promises - false assurances that he would be released within seven days. Trusting those words, the family stepped back.
A week later, the family approached DC Basheer, who repeated the same empty hope: “He will be released soon but after nine months and ten days, on March 26, 2026, Yarwar Baloch was found dead - shot in the head, his body thrown on Pasni Road, Banuk Chadai.

Mullah Bahram, son of Abdul Ghafoor and a resident of Koh Dagar, sub-tehsil Mand, district Kech, was shot dead by state-backed death squads on the afternoon of September 6, 2025.

This incident occurred just hours after the killing of Izhar, another young resident of Mand. According to eyewitnesses, the perpetrators were members of state-backed death squads operating under the command of Pakistani forces and law enforcement agencies.

On 2 February 2022, sixteen members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayeen unit, the Majeed Brigade, carried out simultaneous attacks, nine in Noshki and seven on the Frontier Corps headquarters in Panjgur. The organization named this action "Operation Ganjal". 90 Pakistani security personnel were killed in Noshki and 105 in Panjgur.
On 2 February 2022 at 8:00 PM Fidayee Jamal Baloch alias Chacha, son of Rehmatullah, a resident of Turbat, rammed an VBEID into the main gate of the FC camp in Panjgur. As a result, the front portion of the camp was destroyed, and all soldiers deployed for security at the spot were killed instantly. After this, under the leadership of Unit Commander Hamid Raheem alias Zubair, son of Raheem Bakhsh, a resident of Chitkan, Panjgur, the fidayee fighters Sami Sameer alias Shoaib, son of Ustad Ilahi Bakhsh, resident of Gramkan, Panjgur; Ilyas Baloch alias Qadir, son of Aslam, resident of Gramkan, Panjgur; Asad Wahag alias Sabzo, son of Sadiq, resident of Kilkor; Nasir Imam alias Hamal, son of Imam, resident of Parom; and Zameer Baloch alias Faraz, son of Mohammad Hassan, resident of Dandar, Hoshab, entered the camp. They killed the majority of the soldiers present in the camp, while the remaining enemy personnel, instead of confronting the fighters, abandoned the camp and fled. The objective of the Panjgur unit was to seize control of the camp and hold it for as long as possible. After the enemy fled, the fighters took full control of the entire camp. Subsequently, to recapture the camp from the fighters, the enemy called in SSG commandos, the army, and combat helicopters. During this time, with the support of combat helicopters and armored vehicles, the SSG commandos launched five major assaults on the Baloch fighters. In every attack, the fighters inflicted heavy casualties on the enemy and forced them to retreat. The fighters continued to hold control of the camp while fighting the enemy’s elite military units for 72 hours. After failing in ground assaults, on 5 February 2022 in the afternoon, heavy shelling was carried out against the fighters using combat helicopters. As a result, after prolonged resistance, the fighters were martyred.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Imam Akhlaq Bizenjo, alias Honak Baloch, son of Mohammad Ibrahim Bizenjo, was a resident of Gili, Jaho, in Awaran District, Balochistan. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in March 2024 and later joined the Majeed Brigade on 4 September 2024.
Imam Akhlaq Bizenjo, alias Honak Baloch, was among those young individuals who, recognizing the gravity of the circumstances, chose a responsible and conscious path. His association with the Baloch Liberation Army in March 2024, followed by his joining the Majeed Brigade, reflected his resolve not to remain a silent observer in matters concerning his people. His journey was shaped not by momentary emotion but by sustained observation, a sense of responsibility, and ideological commitment. During Operation Herof, near the Red Zone in Quetta at the railway station area, he was martyred after hours-long clashes with occupying forces while defending his motherland.

On July 18, 2025, Baloch Republican Army (BRA) spokesman Sarbaz Baloch issued a statement to the media saying that a clash occurred in the afternoon between Pakistani forces and the group’s Sarmachars (fighters) in the Gupt area of Sui Tehsil, Dera Bugti District, Balochistan. The fighting broke out when military personnel had set up a blockade on the route used by the Sarmachars.
The exchange of fire lasted for two hours, during which three Pakistani military personnel were killed on the spot.
Subsequently, Sarmachars ambushed a Frontier Corps (FC) convoy heading from Sui Cantonment toward Gupt, attacking it with rockets and heavy weapons. As a result, three more personnel were killed and over ten others wounded.
According to spokesman Sarbaz Baloch, Sangat Barkat, alias Gul Bugti, son of Hewat Bugti, was martyred in these clashes. Martyr Gul Bugti had been affiliated with the organization for the past eight years. He belonged to the Hotkani subclan of the Bugti tribe. He was an exceptionally brave and capable young man whose family has made immense sacrifices for the Baloch homeland.

On 12 August 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahran Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of nine fighters of the organization: 1. Zubair Baloch, alias Shahvez; 2. Shahnawaz Baloch, alias Rahchar; 3. Rahim Baloch, alias Ajiz Baloch; 4. Musharaf Baloch, alias Basham; 5. Munir Baloch, alias Khalid Baloch; 6. Mohammad Zaman, alias Yahya; 7. Jasim Baloch, alias Babar; 8. Gaji Khan Baloch, alias Aftab; and 9. Abdullah Baloch, alias Usman, and paid tribute to all the martyred comrades who sacrificed their lives for the freedom of the motherland, Balochistan.

Zubair Baloch, alias Shavez, son of Shikari Mohammad Bakhsh and a resident of Marmasi, Mashkai, began serving the national movement in 2024 as an urban guerrilla and supporter. Later, in 2025, he was transferred to the mountainous warfare front in accordance with an organizational decision, where he took responsibility for military affairs and carried out his duties with great courage and dedication. During a patrol in the mountainous region, he became involved in a sudden and intense clash with the occupying forces. While attempting to break through the enemy’s encirclement, he fought bravely and was martyred.

Sakim Baloch, alias Meeran Baloch, son of Noor Bakhsh, was a resident of the Pulki area of Gichk. He joined the BLA in August 2025 and served on the Ornach, Kilkoor, Gwargo, and Gichk fronts. He was promoted to the rank of Patrol Commander and was killed on 17 September 2026 in the Gwargo area of Panjgur, Balochistan.
Sakim Baloch was described as a person with wisdom, patience, and experience in guerrilla warfare. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army last year and subsequently underwent military training before taking part in operations on various fronts.
Although young, Sakim Baloch was described as capable, talented, and disciplined in his actions and conduct. He participated in combat operations during Operation Harof in Ornach, where, according to the account, enemy personnel were taken prisoner.
He was also described as having combat experience in areas ranging from Kilkoor to Ornach and later, following organizational orders, from Ornach to Gichk and Gwargo. According to the account, he was dedicated to his assigned responsibilities and participated in military operations in various locations.
He was killed alongside two other members of his group during an engagement with opposing forces in Gwargo.

Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS) carried out a coordinated attack on the main camp of the occupying Pakistani army in the Matin Goran area of Panjgur, capturing a significant part of the camp and inflicting heavy casualties. Twenty-two Pakistani soldiers were killed and more than fourteen, including Captain Usama, were injured. BRAS fighters also seized enemy weapons, ammunition, and equipment. In this operation, Comrade Sangat Ameer, known as Baba, embraced martyrdom.

The attack began around 6 p.m. on August 1, when BRAS struck the main camp of the 91st Wing and nearby outposts from three sides. In two hours of fighting, the fighters took control of major sections of the camp, including two key posts. The attack badly damaged the enemy’s command and communication structure.

BRAS seized modern weapons such as Kalashnikovs, G3 rifles, machine guns, night-vision devices, and thermal scanners. Additional BRAS squads blocked the CPEC route at two points to stop reinforcements, but the enemy forces failed to reach their trapped personnel. Freedom fighters also destroyed surveillance cameras, further weakening enemy intelligence.

During the operation, when a post was captured, three enemy soldiers were surrounded. Fighter Ameer (Baba) urged them to surrender peacefully, but he was struck by enemy fire from behind. Seriously wounded, he moved a short distance but, due to heavy bleeding, avoided capture by following the philosophy of the last bullet in line with his ideological commitment.

Martyr Ameer (Baba), son of Aasmi from Urz Muhammad Bazar in Hoshab, joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2014. He served two years as an urban guerrilla before joining the mountain front in 2016. Known for discipline and courage, he later served as a camp commander on the Kolwah front.

Ameer (Baba) was not only a committed fighter but also an ideological and insightful comrade whose dedication and loyalty made him exemplary.

Habib Faqeer, son of fisherman Faqeer, was born in Ward No. 6, Pasni, in 1987. He worked at a fish shop and later worked as a labourer for Mumtaz Transport. He was abducted during a military raid in Pasni, Pakistan, on April 30, 2014. His mutilated dead body was found in the Kulanch area on April 30, 2017.
His close relative Haneef was killed in 2011, and his two nephews, Abid Sawli in 2013 and Akil Azab in 2021, were also killed by Pakistani forces.

Mohammad Khalid, son of Ameer Mohammad, an 18 year old labourer and resident of Noshki, was killed in an inhumane manner. Khalid travelled to Quetta with two friends to sell their motorbike and purchase furniture. During their visit, they donated blood at a hospital to help save a woman's life, an act of humanity. However, later that evening near Sariab Road, they were followed by Eagle Squad personnel who, without any warning, opened fire. His two friends were thrown off the motorcycle, while Khalid was isolated, beaten, and shot at close range.
Instead of receiving medical assistance, Khalid was taken to an unknown location, where further violence was inflicted upon him. Later that night, he was brought to Civil Hospital Quetta in critical condition, yet even there he was physically abused and tortured. On 10 April 2026, he succumbed to his injuries. His family was not informed until the following day and, due to the lockdown in Noshki, could only reach Quetta the day after. His family was harassed and initially denied the body, which was only handed over after continuous struggle.

Salahuddin Shahwani, son of Gull Muhammad, belonged to Killi Shadi Khan in the Padang Abad area of Mastung. Since 2018, he had been associated with the Baloch Liberation Army and was actively serving the cause of achieving Baloch national freedom.
The 29 year old Salahuddin Shahwani inflicted decisive blows on the enemy in several engagements. He remained steadfast in his commitment to the cause of freedom until his final breath. In the Mastung region of Balochistan, during an hours long armed clash with the enemy, he embraced martyrdom alongside his brother, Martyr Salman Shahwani.

Zameer Dagarzai, son of Nasir Dagarzai, was abducted by Pakistani forces and Pakistan-backed death squads on 3 March 2026 from the Chitkaan Taar office in Panjgur district, Balochistan. On 11 March 2026, his tortured body was found under the Washaap Bridge in the Panjgur district of Balochistan.
Zameer’s father, Nasir Dagarzai, was a small restaurant owner. He was also abducted by Pakistani intelligence agencies and the Frontier Corps from a house in Panjgur along with three of his friends in January 2011. All of them were forcibly disappeared and later taken in front of a firing squad, where they were shot and dumped, Nasir miraculously survived.
On 25 May 2011, while he was travelling to Karachi for medical treatment, he was abducted again and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. On 16 July 2011, his tortured body was found in Quetta city, Balochistan.
The short film “The Line of Freedom,” written and directed by the British director David Whitney and produced by Nooruddin Mengal, Mir Bhawal Mengal, and David Whitney, was released in 2013 and was inspired by the life of Zameer’s father, Nasir Dagarzai.

Jahan Zaib Baloch, son of Meeran Baksh Baloch, was a resident of Mastung. He received his early education in his hometown and was a student of Lasbela University of Agriculture, Water and Marine Sciences, Lasbela, as well as a senior member of BSO Azad, Uthal Zone. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising peaceful political expression. He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he remained with the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom.
He had a keen interest in reading revolutionary literature about oppressed nations. He mobilized hundreds of youths to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of the Baloch homeland, due to which many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by security forces. He was killed by a Pakistani-backed death squad during his cousin’s marriage ceremony in Mastung on May 10, 2014. His body showed extreme signs of torture.
He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a very young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

Shahjan Langove, son of Abdul Baqi Langove, a 30 year old political worker and resident of Killi Ismail, Hudda, Quetta, was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 11 June 2010. His body was later found in Quetta on 13 August 2010.

On 2 February 2022, sixteen members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayeen unit, the Majeed Brigade, carried out simultaneous attacks, nine in Noshki and seven on the Frontier Corps headquarters in Panjgur. The organization named this action "Operation Ganjal". 90 Pakistani security personnel were killed in Noshki and 105 in Panjgur.
In the BLA’s operation on the Noshki FC headquarters, 9 fidayeen participated. On 2 February 2022, Meerain Jamaldini (alias Zagrain) drove an VBEID into the camp’s main gate. Following this, Badil Baloch (alias Riyasat), Murad Aajo (alias Baba), Aneel Baloch (alias Balach), Yasir Noor (alias Saif), Aziz Zehri (alias Barag), Ibraheem Baloch (alias Kabeer), Deedag Bahar (alias Rauf) and Bilal Baloch (alias Wahid) entered the camp. As a result, 90 military personnel, including one officer, were killed, and a portion of the camp was destroyed.
The operation continued throughout the night. In the early morning of 3 February 2022, after their ammunition was exhausted, the remaining eight fidayeen took their own lives by firing their weapons.
The son of Dosta Mahmood Baloch and Shazia Baloch. He was identified as an infant (reportedly 3 months old) who was martyred during the missile attack in Sistan and Balochistan.

Ghulam Farooq Mengal, son of Ghulam Rasool, a 32 year old political worker and resident of Jail Road, Hudda, Quetta, was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces on 10 May 2010. After two months, on 26 July 2010, his body was found on Qambarani Road, Quetta.
Hanif Baloch was a political activist. He was abducted and extrajudicially killed by Pakistani forces, and his body was dumped on 6 July 2011 in Pasni, Balochistan.

On March 5, 2026, Niaz Baloch, the 24-year-old son of Haji Allah Bakhsh, a driver and resident of Sabzal Bazar in Paroom, a tehsil of Panjgur District, was directly targeted and killed by a state-backed local death squad in the Kaleri area of Paroom.
Niaz Baloch worked as a driver near the border area to financially support his family.
Following the incident, his body was reportedly taken to the Paroom military camp. Authorities later contacted the family and asked them to come and receive his body. When the family arrived at the camp, they were pressured by security personnel to sign a document stating that Niaz Baloch had been involved in anti-state activities and labelling him a terrorist.
The family reportedly refused to sign the document, rejecting the allegations against him. After their refusal, the body of Niaz Baloch was handed over to his family on March 6, 2026.

On January 12, 2026 Pakistani army carried out a drone attack on a temporary patrol camp of Baloch Liberation Army in the Shurparood area of Kalat, in which four veteran freedom fighters of BLA - Sangat Zohair alias Haq Nawaz, Sangat Manzoor Kurd alias Bakhtiar Cheeta, Sangat Samiullah alias Javed Phalia and Sangat Naseer Ahmed alias Meerak - attained martyrdom.
Samiullah alias Javed Phalia, son of Dinar Khan Kiazai, belonged to Mach area of Bolan. He joined Baloch Liberation Army in 2023 and served on Bolan and Kalat fronts. In a short period of time, he proved to be an asset to the organization and earned a prominent position among fellow fighters due to his all-round character.

On May 17, 2025, during an urban mission, senior members of the organization - Amjid Basham alias Shams Sahir and Sabrullah Baloch alias Wahag Jan, launched an attack on the Pakistani army headquarters "Asghar Gate" in the central city of Turbat, Kech, at 7:00 AM. They used grenade launchers, which hit the target precisely, resulting in the death of one enemy personnel and woundings to two others.
Following the operation, both comrades attempted to withdraw, but the state forces deployed surveillance drones to track them. The enemy forces blocked the escape route, which led to an armed confrontation. In a clash that lasted for about ten minutes, two enemy personnel were eliminated and one was wounded. However, Captain Amjid Basham and Lieutenant Sabrullah embraced martyrdom during the firefight.
Amjid Basham Baloch held the rank of Captain, and Martyr Sabrullah Baloch was a Lieutenant.
Martyr Sabrullah Baloch was a quiet, determined, and steadfast comrade. He joined the Baloch National Movement at a young age and formally became part of the organization in 2021. He quickly took on active roles in organizational and public networks. His capabilities, seriousness, and understanding of the organization earned him trust, and he was soon entrusted with operational and confidential responsibilities. In 2023, he came under the radar of state forces and faced serious threats. Rather than backing down or remaining silent, Sabrullah chose the path of resistance. He transitioned from public activism to armed resistance and began performing front-line combat duties. He was involved in highly secretive and complex missions, continuously evading the enemy and staying active in various areas. Sabrullah was tireless and resolute. He never sought personal fame or recognition but remained committed to the cause of freedom and the truth of the ideology. He continued his struggle with unwavering determination until his final breath.

Usman Baloch, alias Talaar, son of Ehsan Baloch, was a resident of Jaheen Paroom, Panjgur. He joined the BLA in 2026, served on the Panjgur front, and was martyred on 3 June 2026 in the Chedagi area of Panjgur.
Usman, known as Talaar, joined the Baloch Liberation Army earlier this year. Acting on the directives of the organization, he assumed his responsibilities on the Panjgur front. He was known as a brave and determined Sarmachar who was always ready to undertake difficult and demanding tasks in pursuit of military objectives. After completing his basic military training, he actively participated in operations related to the economic blockade against the enemy and carried out his assigned responsibilities with professional discipline.
In a remarkably short period, he embraced the organization’s revolutionary ideology and military discipline and began carrying out his responsibilities with distinction. He had a thorough understanding of the culture, traditions, and principles considered essential for becoming a strong and effective fighting force. By adhering to these principles, he proved himself to be an active, steadfast, and responsible Sarmachar throughout the course of the national struggle. Alongside his fellow comrades, he took part in various engagements against the enemy and played an important individual role in thwarting the enemy’s attempts to advance.
During the recent policy of economic blockade, he was assigned responsibilities in Chedagi. It was there, while fighting against the enemy during battle, that he embraced martyrdom.
His steadfastness against the occupying enemy until his last breath and his unwavering commitment to the objective of expelling it from Balochistan through military struggle reflected his profound national consciousness and resolute dedication. He has now joined the ranks of those courageous fighters in Baloch national history who sacrificed their personal lives and all worldly comforts for the cause of national freedom and the restoration of a national state. His sacrifices will remain preserved forever in the pages of Baloch history.

On 8 August 2016, terrorists attacked the Government Hospital in Quetta, Balochistan, in a suicide bombing and shooting. More than 70 people were killed, mainly lawyers, and more than 130 others were injured.
The majority of those killed were lawyers who had gathered at the hospital after the body of Advocate Bilal Anwar Kasi, president of the Balochistan Bar Association, was brought there. Kasi had been shot dead by a gunman near Mengal Chowk on Manno Jan Road in Quetta while he was leaving his home for his office.
Responsibility for the attack was claimed by various Islamist groups, including Jamaat-ul-Ahrar and the Islamic State Khorasan Province. However, nationalist groups have alleged that these extremist organisations are backed by the Pakistani state and its military to counter the nationalist movement in the region and exploit its natural resources.
Estimates of the death toll ranged between 70 people, while more than 120 were injured. Of those killed, 54 were lawyers. Among them, 15 were Baloch by ethnicity, while the majority were Pashtuns by ethnicity.

The Baloch advocates or lawyers who were killed are identified as follows:

01 Ghulam Farooq Badini, son of Haji Abdul Ghani.
02 Bashir Ahmed Qazi, son of Qazi Ahmed Jan.
03 Bashir Ahmad Zehri, son Haji Mir Ahmed Zehri.
04 Naseer Ahmed Langove, son Abdul Rahim.
05 Chakar Khan Rind, son of Mehmood.
06 Abdul Rashid, son of Abdul Latif.
07 Nooruddin Rakshani, son Haji Naseeruddin.
08 Muhammad Imran, son Ghulam Farooq.
09 Muneer Ahmed Mengal, son Ghulam Murtaza.
10 Sangat Jehan Jamaldini, son of Dr. Jahanzaib.
11 Mohammad Ali Satakzai, son of Taj Mohammad Khan.
12 Mehmood Ahmed Lehri, son Haji Abdul Hameed.
13 Jamil Ur Rehman, son of Qazi Abdul Hameed.
14 Amanullah Langove, son of Haji Dad Karim.
15 Sabir Ali, son of Abdul Rasheed.

Sangat Jehan Jamaldini was a candidate for Finance Secretary in the upcoming elections of the Balochistan High Court Bar Association. He aspired to become a session judge and dispense justice without discrimination.

Martyr Ustad Mukhtar Baloch Alias Ustad Noor Baloch was born in house of Noor Hussain and Taj Bibi in Malikabad area of Tump, Balochistan. He affiliated with Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in 2005. The time of his martyrdom, he was camp commander and held rank of Major. He embraced martyrdom along with his two comrades Sajid Baloch Alias Asumi Baloch and Aziz Baloch alias Chakar Baloch on Dec 7, 2020 in area of Dashtuk, Zumran area of Kech, Balochistan.
