data.biography:
On 13 October 2026, Pakistani genocidal forces killed six Baloch men who had previously been subjected to enforced disappearance and dumped their bodies in the Sui area of Dera Bugti district, Balochistan.
The incident was also confirmed by Sher Mohammad Bugti, the Central Spokesperson of the Baloch Republican Party.

The victims have been identified as follows:
- Mohammad Khan Bugti, son of Yar Mohammad Bugti
- Lalu Bugti, son of Taj Mohammad Bugti
- Shahmeer Bugti, son of Shahal Bugi
- Waheed Bugti, son of Habib Bugti
- Ghulam Din Bugti, son of Kurri Bugti
- Akram Khan, son of Wadera Mazar Khan Bugti

Hameed Baloch, son of Eid Mohammad, born in 1993 and a resident of District Mastung, Balochistan, was a student of PEF University Peshawar and a member of BSO Azad Peshawar Zone. He received his early education in his native area, Mastung, and later moved to Peshawar for further studies.
He played an important role in uniting Baloch youth residing in Peshawar for educational purposes. He mobilized hundreds of youths to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of the Baloch homeland. Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by the security forces.
He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he remained with the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom. He was an example of bravery and commitment. He joined the organization at an early age and stood by his national ideology until his last breath. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising peaceful political expression.
He was abducted on 11 August 2011 from District Mastung, Balochistan, by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agencies. His bullet-riddled body was found dumped on 18 August 2011 in Dasht, District Mastung, Balochistan. His body bore severe signs of torture.
He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a very young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.
Afzal, alias Gorgaij, was a resident of the Kalar, Awaran area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 8 January 2020 in Balochistan.
Abdul Haq Mengal, was a resident of the Khuzdar area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 19 February 2013 in Balochistan.

On 21 May 2025 fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) began patrolling the Gardank area of Buleda after receiving reports of suspicious movement by the security forces and a so called local death squad. In the evening, at a place known as “Balo Koi Gaz” the fighters encountered enemy agents, which led to an intense armed clash.
The clash lasted for nearly an hour, during which the security forces and their local collaborators suffered casualties. In the same encounter, two Baloch Liberation Army fighters, Jabir Naseer and Faqeer Jan, were killed.
Jabir Naseer, alias Sameer, son of Naseer, belonged to the Zirdan area of Buleda. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2020 and initially served as an urban guerrilla. In 2021, he moved to the mountainous front, where he played a significant role in various regions.
He was serving as part of the organization’s patrol command. He participated in multiple operations on key fronts including Zamuran, Dasht, Sahiji and Turbat and played an important role in several actions carried out against opposing forces. He was a full time and committed fighter, dedicating his life to planning and executing operations.

Asmatullah Sarparah, son of Ibrahim Khan Sarparah, was born in 1988 in Kardigap, Mastung, Balochistan. He was an M.A. student at the University of Balochistan and a member of BSO Azad Shaal Zone. He received his early education in his hometown, Mastung.
He believed in political struggle and was targeted for his peaceful political expression. He mobilized many young people to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of their homeland. Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by security forces.
He was threatened by Pakistani agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he stood by the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom. He was an example of bravery and commitment. He joined the organization at an early age and remained steadfast in his national ideology until the end.
He was abducted by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agencies on October 2, 2010, and his bullet-riddled body was found dumped in Mastung, Balochistan, on November 17, 2010. His body bore severe signs of torture.
He was among the most committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many young people to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

On 25 August 2024 Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch announced the launch of a "Fidayeen Operation" named "Herof" across Balochistan. As part of this operation, fidayeen from the BLA's elite unit, Majeed Brigade, have attacked the main camp of the Pakistani forces in Bela and have successfully infiltrated it. Meanwhile, other BLA fighters have taken full control of all major highways across Balochistan, blocking them completely.
During Operation “Herof,” 44 attacks were carried out simultaneously at 40 locations across 13 districts of Balochistan. As a result, 130 Pakistani army personnel were killed and 55 were injured. In addition, gas pipelines were destroyed at 2 locations, railway tracks at 7 locations, and 2 bridges were blown up.
During the operation, 13 vehicles transporting minerals were set on fire. Blockades were also established at 14 locations across Balochistan, and 3 members of a “death squad” were killed.
As part of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayee (suicide) operation “Herof,” the BLA’s Majeed Brigade carried out an attack on the Pakistani army’s Bela camp. The Majeed Brigade maintained control of the camp for twenty hours, during which 68 enemy personnel were killed.
Nine fidayeen (self-sacrificing fighters) of the Majeed Brigade at Bela camp - Ghaus Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Talib), Mahal Baloch (alias Zilan Kurd), Rizwan Baloch (alias Hammal), Mohammad Baloch (alias Meerak), Fazal Gul Zehri (alias Shawaiz), Tayyab Baloch (alias Lala), Junaid Zehri (alias Kami), Mohammad Asif Nechari (alias Naveed), and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Khalid) - along with Shafqat (alias Dayar) of the Fateh Squad in Mastung, were martyred in the operation.
Ghaus Baksh Sumalani, alias Talib, and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani, alias Khalid, were brothers. They took part in the same operation and were martyred while defending their motherland.

On March 21, 2026, on the night of Eid ul-Fitr, Pakistani Frontier Corps forces raided Mastung, Balochistan. During the raid, Mohammad Amir, son of Dil Murad and a young resident of Killi Kariz Sur, Mastung, was forcibly taken from his home and shot dead by FC personnel. He was killed within five minutes of the raid, without any warrant or explanation.
Following the killing, FC personnel withheld his body for approximately 12 hours before returning it to the family. Upon its return, the family was forced to sign an unlawful document on stamp paper without being allowed to read its contents. Several illiterate community elders were also made to sign the same document without being given the time to have it read to them.

Operation Dara-e-Bolan, which began on 29 January 2024 continued for two days until 31 January 2024 and was successfully concluded after achieving its intended objectives. A total of 385 Sarmachars from four different units of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) participated in Operation Dara-e-Bolan. Among them were 12 Fidayeen from the BLA’s Majeed Brigade. The other participating units included the Fateh Squad, the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS) and the Intelligence Wing.
Operation Dara-e-Bolan commenced on the evening of 29 January 2024 at 9:00 pm local time and continued for two days. After achieving the desired results, the BLA’s Senior Command Council announced the conclusion of Operation Dara-e-Bolan on 31 January 2024 at 7:00 pm and issued instructions to all units to vacate their positions and report back to their base camps.
During the operation, BLA Sarmachars took complete control of an area within a 70 kilometre radius, including Mach city and the strategically important National Highway N-65. Over the course of Operation Dara-e-Bolan, a total of 78 enemy personnel were killed. These included 45 Frontier Corps (FC) personnel who were killed within the first three hours of the operation in Mach city; 10 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on an army camp at the Pir Ghaib Bolan location; 4 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on a military convoy at the Gokurt Mach location; 12 regular army personnel who were killed on 30 January when Majeed Brigade Fidayeen eliminated them and entered the FC headquarters; and at least 5 SSG commandos who were targeted and killed by the Fidayeen on 31 January 2024. In addition, two police personnel were also killed, including one Station House Officer (SHO).
A large number of Levies and police personnel were captured by the BLA during the operation; however, as they were Baloch, they were released. During Operation Dara-e-Bolan, 13 brave fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army attained martyrdom. Of these, 12 martyred Sarmachars belonged to the Majeed Brigade Fidayeen, while one martyred Sarmachar was from the BLA’s Fateh Squad.
The martyred Sarmachars were: Qasim Baloch, Saddam Hussain, Salal Baloch, Farooq Baloch, Atta Baloch, Hammal Momin, Zeeshan Zehri, Nadir Bangulzai, Nizam Baloch, Zeeshan Baloch, Jamal Baloch, Wadood Satakzai, and Kashif Shahwani.
Atta Baloch, alias Sheikh Gazak, son of Mohammad Baloch, belonged to the Heronk area of Turbat. He joined the armed struggle for Baloch national liberation in 2016 and, for eight years, fulfilled his national duties with courage, bravery, and complete sincerity. Before joining the armed struggle, he was active against national subjugation through the platform of the BSO. In 2019, Atta Baloch voluntarily offered his services to the BLA - Majeed Brigade. He was a highly trained soldier of the national liberation movement. Owing to his military skills, he was also entrusted with the responsibilities of a trainer at a BLA camp, duties which he carried out efficiently for a long period. During Operation Dara-e-Bolan, he served as the operational commander of the Majeed Brigade. He was also a talented poet in the Balochi language. Two of Atta Baloch's brothers-in-law had previously been killed by the occupying Pakistani army, while his father and uncle have been forcibly disappeared by the enemy forces for many years.

On August 19, 2024, Nasrullah, also known as Ustad Chakar Baloch, was martyred in a clash with enemy forces in the Ab-e-Gul area of Sarawan, Mastung. Displaying exceptional bravery and courage, he ensured that all his comrades safely escaped the enemy's encirclement. He fought valiantly against the enemy until his last breath and the last bullet.
Martyr Major Engineer Nasrullah, alias Ustad Chakar, was born in 2001 in the home of Waja Murad, a resident of Gujjar, Mashkay. Major Nasrullah was a highly skilled civil engineer and a courageous, knowledgeable, and dedicated son of Balochistan. He joined the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in December 2017 to contribute to the freedom struggle. Due to his abilities and leadership qualities, the BLF entrusted Major Chakar Baloch with leadership responsibilities in Sarawan and promoted him to the rank of Major. He efficiently fulfilled his duties, organizing the Balochistan Liberation Front in areas such as Mach, Bolan, Jhalawan, Mastung, Kalat, Kachhi, and Sivi, alongside his ideological comrades. Major Nasrullah Baloch played a key role in the military operations of Baloch Raji Ajohi Sangar (BRAS) in these regions. Due to his steadfastness, bravery, and foresight, he was given the responsibilities of camp commander, a position he held until his martyrdom.

On 3rd April 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that fighters of the BLA launched a series of coordinated attacks against the occupying Pakistani army across occupied Balochistan on 29th March 2026, which continued until 1st April 2026. The fighters carried out 65 operations in Panjgur, Shapuk, Basima, Sibi, Mastung, Quetta, Noshki, Zamuran, Dasht, Surab, Jhal Magsi, Dalbandin, Kharan, Washuk, and Kalat. In these actions, more than 86 personnel of the Pakistani army, death squads, and intelligence agencies were killed, and dozens were injured. These attacks targeted occupying army camps, an airbase, radar systems, communication towers, railway tracks, bridges, and gas pipelines, while major highways were brought under control for several hours.
During clashes with Pakistani forces, five BLA fighters in Panjgur - Zahid alias Nawaz, Saeedullah alias Meraj, Jahanzeb alias Qambar, Aamir alias Khalid, and Saddam alias Shahwaiz - along with Abdust (Abdul Rehman) alias Alman in Zamuran, attained martyrdom.
Saeedullah, alias Meraj (son of Adil Jan): Originally from Raghay, Washuk, he joined in April 2025 and proved his bravery as a frontline soldier in Guwargo and Panjgur.

A press statement issued by the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) on 16 October 2024 stated that on Friday, 11 October 2024, two of the organization’s fighters were travelling to Pirandar Sorak Kor in Awaran for organizational work when they were ambushed by agents of a death squad formed by the Pakistani state. As soon as the agents spotted the comrades, they opened indiscriminate fire and attempted to surround them. Both Captain Talib Baloch and Adil Baloch embraced martyrdom as a result of the gunfire.
Captain Talib Baloch, known as Modi, son of Mir Muhammad and a resident of Draski, Awaran, had been associated with the Balochistan Liberation Front since 2012 and had dedicated his life to the cause of Balochistan’s national freedom. He participated in numerous significant battles, inflicting heavy losses on the enemy in terms of both lives and resources. His important role was evident in successful operations across various regions, including Basima, Rakhshan, Balgatar, Washuk, Mashkay, Awaran, Kech, Ormara, Gichk, and Panjgur.
Martyr Talib Baloch was compassionate and kind to his comrades and remained steadfast, committed, and active with unwavering determination.
In an attempt to weaken their resolve and force them to abandon the national struggle, state forces subjected his family to collective punishment: family members were forcibly disappeared, their property was set on fire, and they were forced to flee their homes. Yet, despite all these atrocities, the martyr’s determination remained unshaken. Even under severe hardship and oppression by state forces, Martyr Talib Baloch never wavered from his commitment to national freedom. His courage and sacrifice are proof that no obstacle in the path of the struggle could defeat him. His twelve-year struggle stands as a living testament to the philosophy of sacrifice, and in the end, he joined the caravan of martyrs.
Martyr comrade Adil, known as Nasir, son of Nawab and a resident of Ziarat Dan, had been associated with the Balochistan Liberation Front for the past year and was part of the organization’s urban network. He was a determined, educated, and courageous comrade who sacrificed his life for the freedom of his homeland. The enemy’s intelligence agencies forcibly disappeared him twice, but despite all the difficulties, they failed to break his resolve.
data.martyrdomPlace: Pirandar Sorak Kor, Awaran District, Balochistan

data.biography: On 14 March 2011, Agha Mahmood Khan Ahmadzai was shot dead in Kalat, Balochistan, by Pakistani agents. Motorcyclists opened indiscriminate fire on him when he was heading towards Kalat Market. As a result, he died on the spot, while two passersby also sustained serious injuries after being hit by his car, as he lost control of the vehicle after receiving multiple bullet wounds.

Yahya Baloch, son of Fazal Karim, a 17 year old student and resident of Khudabadan Kohe Metag, was forcibly disappeared on March 3, 2026. He was taken from his home by a death squad along with Frontier Corps (FC) personnel. No warrant was presented, no charges were filed, and he was not produced before any court of law.
A day later, on March 4, 2026, his body was discovered near the Frontier Corps camp of Pakistani genocidal forces in Panjgur district, Balochistan.

data.martyrdomPlace: Madag Kaur, Kolwah, Kech district, Balochistan
data.biography: Pervez Mehr Alias Malok Baloch son of Nuguman and Haneefa Baloch, was a resident of Howr, Kolwa area of Awaran, Balochistan. According to organizational statement; He was become part of the Baloch liberation movement in the platform Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in 2014. He embraced martyrdom along with other his comrades Asad Baloch, alias Basit Baloch; Akil Azab, alias Riaz Baloch and Saki Baksh, alias Mureed Baloch during a clash with Pakistan’s Army in Madag Kaur, area of Kolwa, Kech, Balochistan on Oct 9, 2021.

data.fullName: Jan Mohammad Marri, alias Barin Baloch
Mohammed Sharif Notwani, alias Shay Mureed
data.biography:
Mohammad Sharif Notwani, alias Shay Mureed, son of Muhammad Amin Notwani, was a resident of Mula, Khuzdar. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Kalat and Surab fronts. He was martyred in the Hajikeh area of Surab on 18 August 2026.
Martyr Muhammad Sharif Notwani joined the ranks of the Baloch Liberation Army on the Surab front this year. Through his actions, character, and hard work, he quickly established himself among his comrades as a dynamic fighter. On the Surab front, he took part in devastating attacks against the enemy in a short period of time, proved his abilities, and struck terror into the enemy’s ranks. He not only embraced the organisation’s policies of advancing and establishing territorial dominance but also made them a part of his practical life, becoming a scourge to the enemy.
Martyr Sharif did not regard war as an emotional act; rather, he made its profound purpose a part of his life and sacrificed himself for that cause. He was an exceptionally brave fighter on the ground who understood the realities of the battlefield and was capable of thwarting the enemy’s policies and strategies at any time. Among his other qualities was a fierce spirit and methodology for waging war against the enemy, which made him unique. These combat skills were amply demonstrated through fierce assaults, including tightening the noose around the enemy on the Surab front. He was a guerrilla fighter who displayed great presence of mind and creative ability during wartime—qualities that are extremely important on the battlefield.
Sharif proved himself by participating in the actual theatre of war and remained wholeheartedly committed to his cause until his last breath. He sacrificed his personal life in the struggle for national liberation and the restoration of the state. He attained martyrdom while fighting the enemy on the Surab front, shedding his blood to fulfil his duty in the struggle for national freedom. His sacrifices will forever be remembered in the pages of history as those of a great freedom fighter.

On June 27, 2025, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) issued a statement saying that on June 22, 2025, its fighters were on an organizational patrol in the Gresha area when they encountered operatives of a state-sponsored death squad near the Badrang region. A fierce clash ensued, during which three BLF fighters embraced martyrdom, while one enemy operative was killed and several others were wounded.
The martyrs of this encounter were Second Lieutenant Maqbool Baloch (alias Qandeel Baloch), Siraj Baloch (alias Zubair Baloch) and Khalid Baloch (alias Safar Baloch).
Shaheed Second Lieutenant Maqbool Baloch (alias Qandeel) son of Nosherwan, hailed from the Jawarji area of Gresha. He was a well-educated young man who had studied at the National University of Modern Languages (NUML) in Islamabad. In 2021, he was forcibly disappeared by state agencies and endured seven months of severe torture in secret detention centers before being released.
After his release, he joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in 2022 to fight for the freedom of Balochistan. In a short span of time, through his intellectual clarity, organizational commitment, and military capabilities, he emerged as an active, talented, and frontline guerrilla fighter.
He took part in operations across several key areas, including Kalatkor, Gichk, Mashkay, Jhao, Wadh, Ornach, Naal, and Gresha. In recognition of his intelligence and spirit of sacrifice, the organization inducted him into the “Qurban Unit” - a highly trusted and significant wing of the movement.

On 13 October 2026, Pakistani genocidal forces killed six Baloch men who had previously been subjected to enforced disappearance and dumped their bodies in the Sui area of Dera Bugti district, Balochistan.
The incident was also confirmed by Sher Mohammad Bugti, the Central Spokesperson of the Baloch Republican Party.

The victims have been identified as follows:
- Mohammad Khan Bugti, son of Yar Mohammad Bugti
- Lalu Bugti, son of Taj Mohammad Bugti
- Shahmeer Bugti, son of Shahal Bugi
- Waheed Bugti, son of Habib Bugti
- Ghulam Din Bugti, son of Kurri Bugti
- Akram Khan, son of Wadera Mazar Khan Bugti

Basheer Ahmed Baloch was a resident of District Mastung. He received his primary education in his native area. He was a student and a member of BSO Azad. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for his peaceful political expression. He mobilized many young people to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of the Baloch homeland. Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by the security forces.
He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he remained with the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom. He was an example of bravery and commitment. He joined the organization at an early age and stood by his national ideology until the end.
He was abducted from his home in Mastung by Pakistan’s secret agencies on August 30, 2010. His bullet-riddled body was found in Gunja Dori, Mastung, on November 18, 2010. His body showed extreme signs of torture. He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times.
He inspired many young people to join the ranks of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a young age will be remembered in the golden words of Baloch history.

Elahi Baksh, son of Rasool Baksh, was a 60 year old shopkeeper from Naal, Balochistan. On 30 October 2026, at approximately 4:00 PM, personnel of the Frontier Corps (FC), Pakistani forces, forcibly disappeared him from his home. Three days later, on 2 November 2026, his dead body was found dumped in Laghorzard, Naal, Balochistan.

Mehraj Ahmad, son of Sher Mohammad and a resident of Gilli, Tehsil Buleda, district Kech, was forcibly disappeared by Frontier Constabulary (FC) forces on September 5, 2025, while traveling from Buleda to Turbat.

Eyewitnesses reported that he was brutally tortured before being enforcedly disappeared by the Pakistani forces. His whereabouts remained unknown for 18 days until his mutilated and decomposed body was recovered from Alandoor, Buleda, on September 23, 2025.

Mehraj body was identified only through his national identity card, which had been placed beside his body. His condition showed clear signs of prolonged torture and that he had been killed days before his body was dumped.

On June 27, 2025, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) issued a statement saying that on June 22, 2025, its fighters were on an organizational patrol in the Gresha area when they encountered operatives of a state-sponsored death squad near the Badrang region. A fierce clash ensued, during which three BLF fighters embraced martyrdom, while one enemy operative was killed and several others were wounded.
The martyrs of this encounter were Second Lieutenant Maqbool Baloch (alias Qandeel Baloch), Siraj Baloch (alias Zubair Baloch) and Khalid Baloch (alias Safar Baloch).
Shaheed Khalid Baloch (alias Safar), son of Muhammad Bakhsh, was from Gishtari, Gresha. He was also forcibly disappeared for a few months in 2020. Upon his release, he resolved to play an active role in the national liberation struggle and joined the Balochistan Liberation Front a year ago.

On 07 February 2026, a press statement issued by the Balochistan Liberation Front stated that three of its fighters - Captain Farooq Baloch alias Sohrab, Adeel Baloch alias Hameed Baloch, and Ahmad Baloch alias Deedar - were martyred in the Tasp area of District Panjgur, Balochistan. A fourth fighter, Hafiz Abdul Wahab Badini, was martyred in Kalat District, Balochistan.
Fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front went to the Tasp area of Panjgur on January 25, 2026, to carry out a covert organizational mission. There, FC personnel attempted to surround them, resulting in an intense face to face clash between the fighters and state forces. During the clash, the BLF fighters demonstrated extraordinary courage, bravery, and steadfastness, and did not retreat even under the most difficult circumstances.
In the clash, several FC personnel were killed or wounded, while three BLF fighters embraced martyrdom while fighting valiantly. The martyred fighters continued to perform their duties until their last breath and set a practical example of determination, discipline, and commitment in the national struggle.
Captain Farooq Baloch alias Sohrab, son of Mohammad Anwar, resident of Paroom Panjgur, who was martyred in the Tasp clash, participated in the struggle in 2012 by joining BRA. Later, in 2015, he decided to continue the struggle through the platform of Balochistan Liberation Front. He fulfilled responsibilities on various fronts and demonstrated his combat skills, organizational discipline, and military capability in every field. Considering his leadership abilities, military capabilities, and wisdom, BLF appointed him to the rank of Captain, which he maintained until his martyrdom. His sacrifice, discipline, and extraordinary courage are a beacon for his friends. Captain Farooq Baloch's journey is a monument of steadfastness, determination, and selfless commitment to the cause, whose light will continue to guide fighters in the organizational mission for a long time.

On 11 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch announced the martyrdom of 14 fighters of the organization who attained martyrdom in confrontations with the Pakistani army and in airstrikes while defending their homeland, Balochistan, and fighting for national liberation and the right to self-determination.

On 13 August 2026, Pakistani Air Force fighter jets bombarded the Pandran area of Kalat District in Balochistan, resulting in the martyrdom of four members of the organization: Waseem Baloch, alias Farhan; Obaidullah Baloch, alias Shaheen; Nawaz Ali Baloch, alias Dilshad; and Mohammad Hassan, alias Ahmad.

On 25 August 2026, during an organizational mission in the Kech area of Balochistan, Sher Jan, alias Jamal, was shot from behind by a traitor, resulting in his martyrdom.

On 3 September 2026, while patrolling in the Mastung area of Balochistan, the organization’s brave fighters, Mohammad Younis, alias Salal; Sameer Ahmad, alias Zemal; Aziz Ahmad, alias Janan; and Sikandar Baloch, confronted Pakistani forces, targeted several enemy personnel, and embraced martyrdom.

On 14 September 2026, while engaging Pakistani forces and defending his fellow fighters in the Machani Kor Paroom area of Panjgur District, Babar Baloch, alias Kambar, embraced martyrdom.

On 18 September 2026, during a confrontation with Pakistani forces in the Chagi area of Balochistan, fighters of the organization, Riaz Baloch, alias Sabir; Taimoor Shah, alias Shaheen; Zia Ul Haq, alias Ziaullah; and Jumma Baloch, alias Commando, embraced martyrdom.

Sameer Ahmad, alias Zemal, son of Abdul Qadir, resident of KhadKocha, Mastung district, began his struggle through the BLF platform on 17 June 2025. For three years he served in various ranks of the Frontier Corps, while working for BLF intelligence and passing the enemy's information to the organization. After coming to the enemy's attention, he was moved to the mountain front on the organization's instructions. He was entrusted as patrol commander on the Shor Parod front and then on the KhadKocha, Mastung front. On 3 September 2026, during a patrol in Mastung city, after three of his fellow fighters were martyred in a clash with the enemy, he continued attacking the enemy despite being severely wounded. When his bullets ran out, he followed the last bullet philosophy and attained martyrdom.

Nisar Ahmad Mohammad Hassni, alias Salal, son of Ghaus Bakhsh Mohammad Hassni, was a resident of Zangi Nawad, Noshki. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Chagi front. He was martyred on 31 August 2026 in the Nokcha area of Chagi District, Balochistan.
Nisar began his struggle on 2026 in the Shor front for Baloch national liberation, the restoration of the state, and national identity and survival, joining the Baloch Liberation Army fighters who, in a short time, established himself as a revolutionary and dynamic cadre. He took part in the organization’s rigorous military training with great dedication, and after completing his training, he joined the patrols, where he played a key role both in the ongoing economic blockade against the enemy and in inflicting heavy blows on the army. He played a key role, together with other comrades, in restricting the enemy’s movement in the area and in building organizational strength.
Nisar bravely faced the harsh conditions of war and embraced every hardship with revolutionary thought and spirit. He was one of those revolutionary comrades who was always ready to go to any extreme for the sake of his homeland and national freedom. He took an active part in the organizational activities in the region and remained true to his ideals and objectives until the end. He was martyred for his country after a prolonged clash with the enemy. His sacrifice will be remembered in history as that of a great revolutionary fighter who, rather than prioritizing personal life, valued the freedom of his homeland and state above all else, freedoms that guarantee our collective survival.
data.fullName: Nisar Ahmad Mohammad Hassni, alias Salal

data.biography:
Ali Sher Kurd was born on 13 January 1976 in Mach, Balochistan. He practiced as lawyer of Balochistan
High Court after completing his studies. He was also a regular columnist in Daily Tawar and other news
papers, Ali Sher Kurd was politically conscious and ideologically committed to Baloch nationalism.
He saw the prosperity of his nation in the independence of Balochistan and armed struggle as the
means to achieve it.
He joincd the Baloch armed resistance movement for freedom of Balochistan in 1998 and remaincd
active and devoted to it, until he was enforced disappeared by the Pakistan army on 21September
2010, in front of many witnesses from a relative's house in Quetta. His tortured body with a bullet
wound on his forehead was found from Ibrabim Road of Khuzdar on 24 September
2010, just three days after his abduction,
In the presence of thousands of activist, Shaheed Advocate Ali Sher Kurd, was bestowed with the
title "Martyr of Freedom" and laid to rest with full national honor in his home town Mach. On the
martyrdom of her son, his mother said am proud ofmy son because he vindicated his mother and
motherland. He disownod the luxurious life and preferred the difficult but righteous pah. His
sacrifice has become guiding beacon for al of us towards the great cause of freedom.
Today he sleeps prestigiously in the bosom of his motherland, with the dream of freedom in his
closed eyes, but his commitment and sacrifice has awakened many hearts to follow his path of
struggle till victory.

Hassan Rafiq, son of Rafiq Baloch, was a 26-year-old resident of Singani Sar, Turbat, and worked at Star Plus Market in Turbat. In September 2025, Frontier Corps, military personnel, and CTD personnel forcibly disappeared Hassan from Star Plus Market. He was taken into custody, transferred to Turbat Central Jail, and later moved to Gadani Jail.
His family sought justice through the courts and paid five lakh rupees for his bail. Hassan was finally granted bail and released on August 14, 2026. After his release, Military Intelligence personnel stopped him in front of the Hub Chowki Court and again forcibly disappeared him in front of his family, before their very eyes. Thirty-four days later, on September 17, 2026, Hassan’s body, alongside the bodies of Ehsan Baloch and Nadil Baloch, was found dumped in Kuldan, Dannuk, Gwadar, Balochistan.
Hassan was taken alive. His family fought for him through the courts. A court granted him bail. He was returned to his family and then forcibly taken away again. He did not return home alive. He returned as a dead body.
Hassan’s body bore signs of severe violence and gunshot injuries.

On 2 February 2022, sixteen members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayeen unit, the Majeed Brigade, carried out simultaneous attacks, nine in Noshki and seven on the Frontier Corps headquarters in Panjgur. The organization named this action "Operation Ganjal". 90 Pakistani security personnel were killed in Noshki and 105 in Panjgur.
In the BLA’s operation on the Noshki FC headquarters, 9 fidayeen participated. On 2 February 2022, Meerain Jamaldini (alias Zagrain) drove an VBEID into the camp’s main gate. Following this, Badil Baloch (alias Riyasat), Murad Aajo (alias Baba), Aneel Baloch (alias Balach), Yasir Noor (alias Saif), Aziz Zehri (alias Barag), Ibraheem Baloch (alias Kabeer), Deedag Bahar (alias Rauf) and Bilal Baloch (alias Wahid) entered the camp. As a result, 90 military personnel, including one officer, were killed, and a portion of the camp was destroyed.
The operation continued throughout the night. In the early morning of 3 February 2022, after their ammunition was exhausted, the remaining eight fidayeen took their own lives by firing their weapons.

On 16 July 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that the BLA eliminated more than forty personnel of the Pakistani Army and injured several others in forty-eight operations across Balochistan during the previous fifteen days. As part of the economic blockade, vehicles violating the blockade on major highways were targeted and destroyed. Furthermore, four key bridges were destroyed using planted explosive devices. During various clashes with the occupying forces, five BLA fighters - Rahimullah Mohammad Hassni, alias Zafar, son of Lumma Raaj Bibi; Khair Mohammad Khairo, alias Hammal, son of Shahbaz; Kaka Baloch, alias Kaka Rasheed, son of Shahbaz; Masood Baloch, alias Sami, son of Ghulam Jan; and Shah Nazar Baloch, alias Badal, son of Khuda Nazar - embraced martyrdom.

Rahim Ullah Mohammad Hassni, alias Zafar, son of Lumma Raaj Bibi, was a resident of Zek, Basima. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) on 18 August 2024, served on the Bolan Front, and was martyred on 7 July 2026 in the Harnai area of Balochistan.
He joined the BLA after making the final decision to defend his nation and took up a position on the Bolan Front against the enemy. In a very short period, he proved his abilities and came to be regarded as one of the organization's capable fighting comrades. On the Bolan Front, at different times, while challenging the occupation of Balochistan by the occupying and unnatural enemy, he advanced like a flame of fire and reduced the enemy's arrogance to dust.
Rahimullah was originally from Basima. However, when he realized the reality of slavery, he did not allow it to remain merely a realization. Instead, he decided to take an active role in the ongoing struggle. By joining the ranks of the Baloch Liberation Army, he became part of a caravan of brave, professional, and nationally conscious young men who have significantly limited the enemy's presence in Balochistan and, through their struggle and sacrifices, have made the enemy's defeat an unmistakable reality.
During the past two years on the war front, he was counted among the comrades who remained active, constantly on the move, and always ready to inflict heavy blows on the enemy. Martyr Rahim fought the enemy with bravery and strategy until his last breath, consistently maintaining the organization's strength and superiority over the enemy.

On 30 December 2023 Pakistani forces carried out a drone attack and attempted to surround a camp of BRAS in Gurandi Zeera Kaur area of Mashkay by dropping commandos through helicopters. Following professional military tactics, Baloch freedom fighters formed multiple teams to foil enemy aggression and carried several successful attacks against the advancing enemy troops. At least 7 enemy commandos were eliminated in two separate attacks, whereas, three Baloch freedom fighters, identified as Sarwar alias Duruk, Azam alias Basit and Abdul Sattar alias Maraij made ultimate sacrifices. Two freedom fighters of BRAS, Kenagi alias Muslim and Ali alias Atta, while forestalling enemy advances for hours and providing a safe route for Baloch freedom fighters, also embraced martyrdom. Both valiant fighters fought the enemy troops until their last bullets, and made the ultimate sacrifices at their own hands after running out of ammunition. The fallen comrades were affiliated with the allied organisations of BRAS. Azam alias Basit, a resident of Achren, Mashkay, joined BLF in 2013. He had valiantly took part in several successful operations against the enemy forces.

On 07 February 2026, a press statement issued by the Balochistan Liberation Front stated that three of its fighters - Captain Farooq Baloch alias Sohrab, Adeel Baloch alias Hameed Baloch, and Ahmad Baloch alias Deedar - were martyred in the Tasp area of District Panjgur, Balochistan. A fourth fighter, Hafiz Abdul Wahab Badini, was martyred in Kalat District, Balochistan.
Captain Hafiz Abdul Wahab, alias Babar, son of Haji Abdul Mannan Badini, resident of Hazar Ganji, Quetta. He joined the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front for the Baloch national liberation movement in 2019. Initially, he served as an urban guerrilla in Quetta. Later, he moved to the mountain front in 2024, where he served in the areas of Bolan, Nagaho, and Harboi. Recognizing his leadership capabilities, military competence, and strategic thinking, the organization promoted him to the rank of Captain, a position he held until his martyrdom. He continued to perform his responsibilities with consistency, discipline, and in accordance with organizational principles.
On December 6, 2025, Captain Hafiz Abdul Wahab, alias Babar, was travelling for organizational duties when a clash occured on the way, with the army. In the clash, Captain Babar bravely confronted the enemy and kept them from advancing so that his other companions could withdraw safely.
Captain Babar remained in charge of the Harboi area of Kalat until his martyrdom and actively performed his duties with full commitment.
data.fullName: Hafiz Abdul Wahab Badini, alias Babar

data.biography:
On 29 March 2026, a statement issued by the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson, Jeeyand Baloch, stated that between 19 March and 28 March, the Sarmachars of the Baloch Liberation Army carried out 14 separate operations in Washuk, Kharan, Kalat, Mastung, Surab, Khuzdar, Quetta, Turbat, and Barkhan. These actions resulted in the deaths of 18 personnel of the occupying army and left several others injured. The Sarmachars successfully took control of various check posts, detained personnel, and confiscated weapons and military equipment. During these operations, two BLA Sarmachars - Abdullah Rodeni, alias Sarban (19 March 2026), and Yaqoob Baloch, alias Durra (21 March 2026) - attained martyrdom during direct clashes with the occupying forces.
Abdullah Rodeni Baloch, alias Sarban, son of Nazir Ali Rodeni and a resident of Khudabadan, Panjgur, was a graduate with a BS in English Literature from the University of Balochistan. He joined as an urban guerrilla on 21 May 2023 and moved to the mountain front in July 2025. He attained martyrdom on 19 March 2026 while fighting the enemy in the Lijje area of Kharan.

On 21 October 2025, a statement was released by Spokesman Baloch Khan of Baloch Raaji Ajoi Sangar (BRAS), an umbrella alliance of Baloch armed organizations. The statement said that in defence of the Baloch population in Zehri, BRAS forces eliminated dozens of enemy personnel, while six freedom fighters embraced martyrdom. Among them was Martyr Umer alias Janan.

The statement added that the occupying Pakistani army attempted to advance for aggressive purposes in the Zehri area of Khuzdar, which is under the control of Baloch Raaji Ajoi Sangar, resulting in fierce clashes. Dozens of occupying Pakistani army personnel were eliminated in these clashes, while six freedom fighters of Baloch Raaji Ajoi Sangar were martyred in the defence of the motherland.

Among the fallen were Martyr Hafiz Muhammad Umar Baloch and Sangat Abdul Aziz Baloch, who were martyred on 26 September, while Sangat Sanaullah Baloch, Sangat Abdul Aziz Baloch, Sangat Rashid Ahmed Baloch, and Sangat Fayyaz Baloch were martyred on 30 September.

The statement further said that Martyr Hafiz Muhammad Umar Baloch, alias Janan, son of Noorullah, belonged to Quetta. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army two years ago. Hafiz Umar Baloch gained political awareness during his studies and chose the path of resistance against state atrocities. After joining the Baloch Liberation Army, he received military training and played a key role in several operations. He held a unique position among his comrades due to his ideological maturity, organizational discipline, and fearless nature. The core of his beliefs was the establishment of a free, independent, and dignified Balochistan, for which he sacrificed his life.

Martyr Rahmdil Baloch, alias Wahid Baloch, was born in the house of Wahab Baloch in the Hoshab area of Kech, Balochistan. He was affiliated with the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) since 2021. He embraced martyrdom along with eight comrades - Jalil Sher Baloch, Samad Baloch, Dad Shah, Shoaib Baloch, Haris Baloch, Nawaz Baloch, and Kambar Baloch - in a drone attack carried out by the Pakistan Army on November 29, 2022, in the Jath, Kolwa area of Kech, Balochistan.

Mohammad Omar, son of Mohammad Ilyas, a 20-year-old laborer and resident of Shaban Bazaar, Mand, Kech, was taken into custody along with his brother, Imam Baloch, by the Frontier Corps on 10 July 2026 near Balicha Keras while they were returning home. They were neither produced before a court of law nor afforded any legal process. Instead, both were allegedly extrajudicially killed on the same day. Their bodies, bearing signs of severe torture and multiple bullet wounds, were later handed over to their family.

Zaheer Ahmad Mengal, alias Zakir, son of Mohammad Yahya Mengal, was a resident of the Ghareeb Abad area of Noshki, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Noshki and Chagi fronts. He was martyred on 31 August 2026 in the Nokcha area of Chagi District, Balochistan.
Zaheer Ahmad Mengal decided to join the Baloch Liberation Army in the struggle for national liberation and the protection and preservation of national identity, and he moved to the Shor front. After successfully completing the basic training courses, he joined the organizational patrols and, in a short time, proved himself to be an effective fighter. He faced the harsh and difficult conditions of war with a strong revolutionary mindset and spirit, remained steadfast in every combat situation, stayed true to his ideas and principles, and continued to take part in economic blockade operations against the enemy.
Zaheer Ahmad Mengal was a proponent of the ideological and intellectual belief that the enemy must be confronted with the utmost strength, and that a merciless and powerful war is necessary against those who seek to eradicate our identity, survival, and national security from the very foundation. Under this ideology, he proved it on the battlefield in a short time through his actions and remained committed to this principle until the end. The sacrifices of Martyr Zaheer Mengal will remain a golden chapter in Baloch national history, which will lead to the formation of a Baloch national state, and his sacrifices will be remembered in history as those of a great freedom fighter.

Kareem Baloch, known to his comrades by the alias Raheem Baloch, was born and raised in Kohlu, Balochistan, a region that would define his life's commitment. His political awakening and subsequent dedication to the Baloch liberation cause led him to join the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in 2003. From that point forward, his life became inextricably linked with the struggle for Baloch self determination.

In 2012, Kareem Baloch faced a critical moment of peril when he was abducted by Pakistani forces. Despite facing intense interrogation and pressure, his defining characteristic a fierce commitment to secrecy and integrity held fast. He successfully concealed his affiliation with the BLA, a testament to his discipline, which ultimately secured his release.

Undeterred by the severe trauma of his detention, Kareem Baloch immediately returned to his revolutionary duties. He became a pivotal figure in the post-2012 BLA, dedicating himself to the crucial work of organizing and revitalizing the movement in the rugged and strategically vital area of Koh-e-Suleman. His ability to structure operations and motivate personnel in this complex environment demonstrated his profound capacity for leadership and organization.

It was this combination of unflinching honesty, organizational prowess, and battlefield bravery that led the BLA leadership to bestow upon him the supreme honorific title of "Sagaar" .

Shaheed Kareem Baloch embraced martyrdom on December 25, 2018. He fell in a coordinated strike alongside several key figures of the movement, including General Aslam Baloch, Babar Majeed, Taj Muhammad Baloch, Aman Ullah Baloch, and Akhtar Baloch. His sacrifice remains a powerful symbol of courage and resilience in the ongoing Baloch struggle.

On 31 December 2025, a statement released by the spokesperson of the Balochistan Liberation Front, Major Gwahram Baloch, stated that five of its fighters embraced martyrdom and sacrificed their lives for the homeland in an enemy drone strike in Kalat on 25 December 2025.
The martyrs include Abdul Ahad Dehwar alias Gazzain, son of Hamayun Dehwar, resident of Keli Kahriz Mastung; Israr Ahmad alias Ibrar, son of Hussain, resident of Gargina Mastung; Shoaib Ahmad alias Subedar, son of Muhammad Ali, resident of Jiwa Khuzdar; Obaidullah Siyahpad alias Sabzu, son of Peerjan, resident of Kharan; and Faisal Badini alias Qazi, son of Muhammad Ibrahim, resident of Kharan.
Abdul Ahad joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in 2023 and served his organizational and national duties as an urban fighter in different areas. Following an organizational decision, he moved to Shor Parodh Camp in 2025. In view of the martyr’s capabilities and hard work, he was assigned important responsibilities as training commander at the camp. He served with exceptional dedication as training commander until his martyrdom. Shaheed Abdul Ahad was a hardworking and capable fighter, equipped with political consciousness. Abdul Ahad Jan was seriously wounded in the drone strike. Fellow sarmachars transferred him to a safe location for medical aid, but due to critical injuries, he embraced martyrdom on 27 December 2025 and joined the immortals of Baloch national history.

On February 23, 2022 the occupying forces of Pakistan struck the Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) guerrilla camp in the Satak Kor mountain range of Hoshab, district Kech, and fired three chemical-laden missiles that wreaked havoc over a large area, destroying palm groves and other vegetation at the site. Following the drone missile attacks, the infantry team of the occupying forces surrounded the area and, with the support of more than eight state helicopters, entered the camp. Five Sarmachaars, including two commanders of the organization, Master Asif Baloch and Siraj Baloch, were martyred in this attack. Meanwhile, five other Sarmachaars - Shoaib, Munir, Arif Jan, Diljan, Kamal, Kamash Malang, Jangi Khan, and Daolat - were martyred defending their homeland, fighting the enemy for over an hour and killing several commandos of the occupying forces.
Kamal Jan, alias Gulab, son of Muhammad Saeed, resident of Dandal Shapak, had been associated with the armed resistance since 2019. He was a true son of the homeland and a courageous Sarmachaar.
data.martyrdomPlace: Satak Kor, Hoshap, Turbat district, Balochistan

data.biography:
Muslim Baloch, son of Master Imam Deen Baloch, was born in 1997 and was a resident of Gramkan, district Panjgur, Balochistan. He was a student and a member of BSO Azad. He received his primary education in his hometown, Panjgur.
Muslim was a very honest member of the organization. During his activism, he mobilized many youths to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of the Baloch homeland. Like many other comrades and brave members of the organization, he was also martyred by the security forces.
He was threatened by Pakistani agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he remained committed to the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom. He was an example of bravery and commitment. He joined the organization at an early age and remained committed to his national ideology until the end. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for his peaceful political expression.
He was abducted from district Khuzdar, Balochistan, in April 2013, and his bullet-riddled body was found dumped on 25 November 2013 in Washuk, Balochistan. His body showed severe signs of torture. He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad.
His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a very young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

On 23 January 2011, at approximately 4:15 pm, in the Chitkan area of Panjgur district in Balochistan, Pakistani intelligence agencies, the Frontier Corps, and other genocidal forces raided the house of Nasir Dagarzai. During the raid, they abducted Nasir Dagarzai, Abid Saleem, Mehrab Omar, and Abid Rasool Bakhsh while they were sitting in the guest room (Betak) drinking tea.
Before taking him away, Pakistani forces also shot Nasir Dagarzai three times, leaving him wounded at the scene. The forces then took Nasir to a hospital, after which he was transferred to detention and torture cells, where he was subjected to severe torture. His hands were ground with a grinder and his body was burned with fire.
Approximately five days later, on 27 January 2011, Pakistani forces again shot Nasir Dagarzai and Abid Rasool Bakhsh. At around 1:00 am, they took them to the forests of Gowargo in the Panjgur area and dumped them there. Abid Rasool Bakhsh succumbed to his wounds and died there. However, by chance, Nasir Dagarzai, although badly injured, was found by a person who informed the Levies. He was then transferred to Quetta for medical treatment. After receiving treatment, he was brought back to Panjgur, and due to the gunshot wounds, doctors inserted a rod in his leg.
On 11 March 2011, Nasir Dagarzai gave an interview to Samandar Askani on Radio Gwank in which he described the details of these events.
Later, on 23 May 2011, when Nasir was traveling with his brother Mohammad Gull Dagarzai to Quetta for medical treatment, Pakistani forces abducted him again at the Lak Pass area near Quetta and forcibly disappeared him. On 16 July 2011, he was killed and his mutilated body was dumped. The body was recovered from Lak Pass near Quetta on 17 July 2011.
Similarly, in the same incident, the mutilated bodies of Abid Saleem, son of Mohammad Saleem Baloch, and Mehrab Baloch, son of Haji Mohammad Umar, who had also been abducted and forcibly disappeared, were later recovered on 24 May 2011 from the Margap area of Turbat district in Balochistan.
The short film “The Line of Freedom,” written and directed by the British director David Whitney and produced by Nooruddin Mengal, Mir Bhawal Mengal, and David Whitney, was released in 2013 and was inspired by Nasir Dagarzai.
Nasir Dagarzai’s son, Zameer Dagarzai, was abducted by Pakistani forces and Pakistan-backed death squads on 3 March 2026 from the Chitkan Taar office in Panjgur district, Balochistan. On 11 March 2026, his tortured body was found under the Washaap Bridge in the Panjgur district of Balochistan.

On September 24, 2025, Pakistani genocidal forces conducted a raid on a residential house in the Dalbandin area of Chagi District, Balochistan. During the operation, former chairman of the Baloch Students Organization (Pajjar), a political activist and Advocate, Zubair Baloch, and his companion, Nisar Jan Baloch, were killed.
The incident has sparked widespread condemnation from political parties, student groups, human rights organizations, and legal bodies across Balochistan.
The Baloch Students Organization (Pajjar) described Zubair Baloch as a principled leader committed to a “peaceful struggle, education, justice, and human rights.” The group said his stance and dedication to public service had made him widely respected across the region.

On March 8, 2023, Pakistani drones fired three missiles at a Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) guerrilla camp in the mountain range between Hoshap and Pasni. Following the strike, Pakistani forces began landing commandos around the camp from helicopters. In the missile attack, the camp commander, Hasil Baloch, along with four other fighters, was martyred. The remaining Sarmachars fought bravely in close combat, killing several commandos of the occupying forces before they themselves were martyred in the great cause of freedom for their homeland.
The Sarmachars who were martyred are:
Hasil (alias Doda), Wasdil (alias Jami), Nizam (alias Noshad), Waqas (alias Miras), Khalid (alias Kiyya), Shah Fahad (alias Aslam), and Ilyas Baloch (alias Rahmdil).
Martyr Shah Fahad Kodahi (alias Aslam), son of comrade Naeem Kodahi and resident of Pidarak, joined the Baloch armed struggle in 2019. Shaheed Shah Fahad was a brave and courageous Sarmachar. Like all martyrs, he was a true lover of his homeland. He participated in several battles against the enemy in the areas of Kech and Pasni.
Shaheed Hasan Jan Gichki was killed in custody by Pakistani forces on January 29, 2006.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, the BLA’s Majeed Brigade Fidayeen targeted the main camp and the Coast Guard camp of the Pakistan Navy in the coastal city of Pasni, Balochistan. The operation was initiated by Fazal, alias Miraan, who rammed a vehicle loaded with explosives into the main entrance gate of the Navy camp. The explosion instantly killed at least seven personnel stationed at the gate.
Immediately after this initial attack, six Fidayeen - Yasma Baloch, alias Zareena; Waseem Baloch, alias Zirbaar; Zaid Zamurani, alias Abram; Sabzal Baloch, alias Kohsar; Diljan Baloch, alias Ameer Ajoo; and Operation Commander Shabeer Baloch, alias Kiya - entered the camp and took up positions. Fierce clashes with the occupying Navy and Navy special units inside the camp continued for more than five hours, during which at least 33 Pakistani personnel were killed. This operation not only inflicted significant casualties on the enemy but also dealt a severe blow to the defense structure of the Navy camp.
Sabzal Baloch joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2022 and became part of the Majeed Brigade in 2023. On 31 January 2026, he carried out a fidayee attack in Pasni.
Over a limited span of years, his path reflected sustained intent rather than momentary impulse. Each decision was taken with awareness of consequence and responsibility, shaped by lived experience rather than circumstance. What he ultimately gave was not a single act, but his entire life to a cause he consciously chose and consistently upheld.

On 11 August 2025, the umbrella alliance of Baloch armed organizations in Balochistan, Baloch Raji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS), launched coordinated operations during which several government installations were destroyed and dozens of Pakistani military personnel were killed. A large quantity of military equipment was also reportedly seized. Images showing the bodies of the deceased Pakistani soldiers, destroyed vehicles, and military uniforms hanging at various locations subsequently went viral on social media.
Even after the coordinated attacks had ended, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), a member of the BRAS alliance, maintained control of the Zehri area and successfully repelled multiple attempts by Pakistani forces to advance into the region.
After holding control of the area for several days, the BLA eventually withdrew. Following its withdrawal, the Pakistani military entered Zehri with gunship helicopters, battle tanks, and a large contingent of troops. According to reports, the forces spread fear and panic through looting and other actions in the area. Since then, Zehri and its surrounding regions have remained under military operations and repression.
Following their defeat at the hands of the armed groups, Pakistani forces allegedly targeted civilians in retaliation. As a result of this repression, 11 Baloch individuals were reportedly killed.
On 16 April 2026, several people from Zehri and its surrounding areas - including Wadera Mohammad Dayaan, Imam Bakhsh, Manzoor Ahmad Miraji, Munir Hayat Dayaan, Izzatullah Pandrani, Habibullah, Mohammad Sharif, Mohammad Ramzan, and three unidentified individuals - were reportedly extrajudicially executed by Pakistani forces while traveling along roads in the Sohinda area. One individual, Abdul Salam, survived with serious injuries.
During the ongoing military operation in the area, these individuals were allegedly detained by Pakistani forces from various locations and transferred to the Sohinda Rest House, approximately five kilometres from Noorgama. There, their hands and feet were allegedly bound, they were blindfolded, and they were subsequently shot dead.
The incident occurred one day after the BLA claimed that two of its fighters had been killed during clashes in the Sohinda area.
In its statement, the BLA said that, on 15 April 2026, its fighters targeted advancing Pakistani military units with a remote-controlled explosive device. Following the explosion, they allegedly carried out an ambush on a military convoy moving toward the area.
The organization claimed that ten Pakistani military personnel were killed in the two attacks, while two of its own fighters, Tanveer Mengal and Saadullah, were also killed.

On February 14, 2026, in the Tump area of Turbat District, Balochistan, a 17 year old student, Muhnas Baloch, son of Master Zafar, was reportedly killed in a targeted attack by a state backed death squad.

Nazam-ul-deen Marri, son of Kaher Khan Marri, a 26 year old social worker and resident of Windar, Lasbela, was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 13 September 2010 by Pakistani forces. On 4 November 2010, his body was dumped on the Makuran Coastal Highway in the Uthal area.
The daughter of Dosta Mahmood Baloch and Shazia Baloch. She was identified as a young child (reportedly 7 years old) who was martyred during the missile attack in Sistan and Balochistan.

On April 15, 2025, a statement issued by Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS) claimed that BRAS freedom fighters killed 22 personnel of the occupying Pakistani Army in attacks in Noshki and Barkhan (Chamalang). During these operations, the freedom fighters captured the main camp of the occupying army. In the ensuing clashes, the enemy forces were forced to retreat, and five BRAS freedom fighters were martyred while fighting the Pakistani Army.
On April 9, 2025, the occupying Pakistani Army attempted to advance on a side camp of Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS) freedom fighters after conducting a drone attack at Dadar in the Chamalang area of Barkhan.
Among the comrades martyred in Chamalang was Aaqil Hashmi, alias Chirag, also known as Professor, son of Hashim, from the Shahrak area of Kech. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in 2020 and fought against national oppression. Earlier, he had been a member of the Baloch Students Organization, where he educated and equipped Baloch youth with ideas of national liberation.
Sangat Aaqil, alias Chirag, who served on the fronts of Bolan, Barkhan, Chamalang, and Koh-e-Sulaiman, had completed his M.Phil in Political Science from the International Islamic University (IIUI), Islamabad.
Martyr Sangat Aaqil, alias Professor Chirag, was serving as the unit commander of the Fatah Squad, a special unit of the BLA. He was not only an outstanding guerrilla fighter but also a source of guidance, from whose intelligence and experience other fighters greatly benefited.
Another comrade martyred in Chamalang was Ghulam Raza, alias Kabeer, son of Ali Gul, from Holangi Tank in the Raskoh area of Kharan. Having grown up in the foothills of Raskoh, Ghulam Raza joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in 2022 and fought against national oppression as an urban guerrilla. A year later, he moved to the Barkhan front.
Armed with the consciousness of national liberation, Martyr Sangat Raza was a hardworking and kind-hearted comrade. He inflicted heavy blows on the enemy in numerous battles on the Barkhan front.
The third comrade martyred in Chamalang was Mohsin, alias Durra, son of Mayar, from the Gulshanabad area of Turbat. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2023 and initially served as an urban guerrilla. After striking the enemy army in Turbat city and its surrounding areas for a year, he moved to the mountain front in 2024.
Sangat Mohsin served against national oppression on the Barkhan front. He had the ability to make critical decisions in extremely difficult situations — a quality he demonstrated by shooting himself with the “last bullet” in the throat rather than being captured alive by the enemy.

Muslim, son of Akhtar and a resident of Koadsik in Khuzdar district, Balochistan, was shot and killed by members of a state-backed death squad, operating with the support of Pakistani security forces.
According to local sources, operatives led by Samad Broth called Muslim out of his home late at night and opened fire, killing him on the spot.
Muslim had previously been forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces on October 10, 2024, and was released on December 3, 2024, following nearly two months in incommunicado detention. On June 3, 2025—six months after his release—he was targeted and killed.

On 21 August 2026, Pakistani forces conducted an aerial drone strike on a garden located in the Gaith area of Khadkucha, Mastung District, Balochistan. The strike resulted in the martyrdom of four orchard workers - Gul Khan Mughairi, Imran Baloch, Obaidullah Baloch and Jahanzaib Abdo - and left three others - Ali Raza Mengal, Naseebullah Abdo and Khalid Hussein - badly injured.
Rescue personnel transferred the dead and injured to Shaheed Nawab Ghaus Bakhsh Raisani Memorial Hospital in Mastung, where the wounded received treatment.
All the victims were reportedly associated with Haji Shahr in Kachhi District. Rescue sources said all of the casualties were working as labourers in the orchard at the time of the incident.
The reported strike also follows other incidents in which civilians were reportedly killed during Pakistani military operations or aerial attacks in Balochistan.
On 12 August 2026, reports emerged from Sorab’s Goandhan area alleging that an aerial bombardment had killed innocent civilians, including women and children.
The Mastung incident also comes weeks after reports from Khuzdar District alleging that four civilians were killed in a reported drone strike on a house in the Moola Manjalo area.
Aurangzeb Baloch, was a resident of the Sistagaan, Jahoo area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 7 September 2018 in Balochistan.

In Gwadar, nine Fidayeen of the BLA Majeed Brigade were divided into two units and took part in the operation. The first unit, which included Fidayeen Hawa Baloch (alias Droshum), Yahya Lal (alias Lashari), Adnan Arman (alias Changaiz), and Yousif Baloch (alias Yagi), attacked the compound of the occupying Pakistani intelligence agencies, resulting in the elimination of 12 personnel. Women and children in residential quarters near the compound were provided safe passage; however, the occupying army later martyred these same civilians by opening fire.
About forty minutes later, occupying forces advanced toward the compound, leading to clashes that continued until the evening. In these clashes, more than 24 personnel were eliminated, and three military vehicles, including an armored vehicle, were destroyed.
The second squad, which included Fidayeen Kambar Ismail (alias Sarbaz), Khurshid KB (alias Arman), Waseem Baloch (alias Kareem), Shoaib Baloch (alias Shehzad), and Yasir, took up strong positions in Port Bazaar near Gwadar Port. After announcements were made in mosques, freedom fighters went to the bazaar, met the public, and held political discussions. After repelling the advance of occupying forces in the city, the freedom fighters later advanced toward the port and fired several rockets that hit their targets. Clashes continued until the next day, eliminating more than 19 personnel.
Kambar Ismail, alias Sarbaz, son of Mohammad Ismail, was born in 2003 and is a resident of Sorap, Panjgur district of Balochistan. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in July 2022 and assumed fidayee responsibilities in August 2022. His decision reflected a serious and well-considered choice, marked by discipline, patience, and a strong sense of responsibility. During Operation Herof, he carried out unit command duties on the Gwadar front. In frontline conditions, his presence symbolized organizational coordination and ground-level connectivity, reminding us that leadership is sometimes recognized not through loud assertions, but through quiet resilience and timely responsibility.

Shayhaq Rahim, son of Rahim Bakhsh, was an 18 year old student from Minaz Buleda who belonged to a poor family.
On March 31, 2026, he was forcibly disappeared from Main Bazar Turbat at 4:00 PM by death squads operating under the command and control of the Pakistani state and its forces.
After six days, on April 5, 2026, his dead body was dumped at Banuk-e-Chadai, Pasni Road, in Turbat district.

Junaid Ahmed, son of Ali Ahmed, a 22 year old student and resident of Surab, was forcibly disappeared on January 23, 2026. He was abducted from the Children’s Hospital in Quetta, Balochistan, by personnel of the Eagle Force and the Counter Terrorism Department. On February 14, 2026, his body was recovered from the Eastern Bypass area of Quetta. His hands and feet were bound, and his body bore multiple gunshot wounds and signs of severe torture, indicating a custodial killing following his enforced disappearance.

On 2 February 2022, sixteen members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayeen unit, the Majeed Brigade, carried out simultaneous attacks, nine in Noshki and seven on the Frontier Corps headquarters in Panjgur. The organization named this action "Operation Ganjal". 90 Pakistani security personnel were killed in Noshki and 105 in Panjgur.
On 2 February 2022 at 8:00 PM Fidayee Jamal Baloch alias Chacha, son of Rehmatullah, a resident of Turbat, rammed an VBEID into the main gate of the FC camp in Panjgur. As a result, the front portion of the camp was destroyed, and all soldiers deployed for security at the spot were killed instantly. After this, under the leadership of Unit Commander Hamid Raheem alias Zubair, son of Raheem Bakhsh, a resident of Chitkan, Panjgur, the fidayee fighters Sami Sameer alias Shoaib, son of Ustad Ilahi Bakhsh, resident of Gramkan, Panjgur; Ilyas Baloch alias Qadir, son of Aslam, resident of Gramkan, Panjgur; Asad Wahag alias Sabzo, son of Sadiq, resident of Kilkor; Nasir Imam alias Hamal, son of Imam, resident of Parom; and Zameer Baloch alias Faraz, son of Mohammad Hassan, resident of Dandar, Hoshab, entered the camp. They killed the majority of the soldiers present in the camp, while the remaining enemy personnel, instead of confronting the fighters, abandoned the camp and fled. The objective of the Panjgur unit was to seize control of the camp and hold it for as long as possible. After the enemy fled, the fighters took full control of the entire camp. Subsequently, to recapture the camp from the fighters, the enemy called in SSG commandos, the army, and combat helicopters. During this time, with the support of combat helicopters and armored vehicles, the SSG commandos launched five major assaults on the Baloch fighters. In every attack, the fighters inflicted heavy casualties on the enemy and forced them to retreat. The fighters continued to hold control of the camp while fighting the enemy’s elite military units for 72 hours. After failing in ground assaults, on 5 February 2022 in the afternoon, heavy shelling was carried out against the fighters using combat helicopters. As a result, after prolonged resistance, the fighters were martyred.
