Following their defeat at the hands of the armed groups, Pakistani forces allegedly targeted civilians in retaliation. As a result of this repression, 11 Baloch individuals were reportedly killed.
On 16 April 2026, several people from Zehri and its surrounding areas - including Wadera Mohammad Dayaan, Imam Bakhsh, Manzoor Ahmad Miraji, Munir Hayat Dayaan, Izzatullah Pandrani, Habibullah, Mohammad Sharif, Mohammad Ramzan, and three unidentified individuals - were reportedly extrajudicially executed by Pakistani forces while traveling along roads in the Sohinda area. One individual, Abdul Salam, survived with serious injuries.
During the ongoing military operation in the area, these individuals were allegedly detained by Pakistani forces from various locations and transferred to the Sohinda Rest House, approximately five kilometres from Noorgama. There, their hands and feet were allegedly bound, they were blindfolded, and they were subsequently shot dead.
The incident occurred one day after the BLA claimed that two of its fighters had been killed during clashes in the Sohinda area.
In its statement, the BLA said that, on 15 April 2026, its fighters targeted advancing Pakistani military units with a remote-controlled explosive device. Following the explosion, they allegedly carried out an ambush on a military convoy moving toward the area.
The organization claimed that ten Pakistani military personnel were killed in the two attacks, while two of its own fighters, Tanveer Mengal and Saadullah, were also killed.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Hamid Baloch, alias Wahid, son of Fakhar Baloch, was a resident of the Hoshap area of Turbat district in Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2020 and later joined the Majeed Brigade in 2022. He was part of Operation Herof Phase 2 and served on the Noshki front.
Hamid Baloch was one of those individuals whose appearance gave little indication of the magnitude of the choices he had made. He became part of the BLA in 2020, and two years later, when he joined the ranks of the Majeed Brigade, his conduct remained free of display, marked only by simplicity and resolve.
Hamid Baloch’s personality resembled his hometown, Hoshap - quiet, yet silently alert, with a hidden rhythm of inner discipline and resistance behind an outward calm. His martyrdom affirms a life of struggle founded on order, dignity, and unwavering responsibility.

Shahram, son of Bahran, a 38 year old shepherd and resident of Gishtagan, was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces on 21 February 2026 from Nehing Zamuran. For weeks, his family remained in anguish and was unaware of his whereabouts. After nearly two months, on 16 April 2026, he was killed, and his death was presented as an encounter in the Parom area of Panjgur district, Balochistan.

On June 6, 2025 at around 7 AM, a large contingent of operatives from the puppet militia (Bugti Peace Force) operating under the patronage of the occupying Pakistani army and intelligence agencies, and led by the puppet Chief Minister of Balochistan, Sarfraz Bugti, launched an attack on a patrol team’s camp of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in the mountainous region of Koh Jandar, Rakhni, Barkhan.
The Sarmachars (freedom fighters) immediately adopted a defensive strategy and, after an intense battle lasting approximately three hours, successfully thwarted the enemy’s advance and encirclement attempts, managing to withdraw safely. During this clash, two members of the death squad were killed.
However, the battle did not end with this initial phase. The enemy pursued the Sarmachars and implemented a strategy to block their escape routes. A few kilometres from the site of the initial clash, the Sarmachars encountered fresh reinforcements of the occupying Pakistani army, leading to another intense confrontation. This fierce battle continued for seven hours. In this prolonged combat, four fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front embraced martyrdom and etched their names in the pages of history, while two soldiers of the occupying Pakistani army were killed and several others were severely injured.
Among the martyrs who laid down their lives in the clash with the occupying forces at Koh Jandar, Rakhni, were Rasaan Qadir (alias Rehan), Mustafa Noor (alias Diljan), Samiullah (alias Meeran), and Shahzaib (alias Shahshan).
Sarmachar Shahzaib alias Shashan, son of Amir Bakhsh, was from Goni, Greshag. An educated comrade, he studied Zoology at Islamia University Bahawalpur. He joined the BLF in August 2023. Due to his academic, research, and intellectual abilities, the organization initially placed him in the media wing. However, in November 2024, he was transferred to the Barkhan camp, where he achieved the great rank of martyrdom in the Koh Jandar battle.

Zubair Sarparah, son of Ghulam Rabbani Sarparah, was born in 1987 and was a resident of Kardigap, Mastung, Balochistan. He was a student of Psychology at the University of Balochistan and a member of BSO Azad Shaal Zone. He received his primary education in his hometown, Mastung.
He believed in peaceful political struggle and was targeted for his political expression. He mobilized many young people to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of their homeland. Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by security forces. He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he remained committed to the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom.
He was an example of bravery and commitment. He joined the organization at an early age and remained devoted to his national ideology until the end.
He was abducted by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agencies on 2nd October 2010 from Mian Gundi, Quetta, Balochistan. His bullet-riddled body was found dumped on 2nd December 2010 in Qilli Qambarani Shaal, Balochistan. His body bore severe signs of torture.
He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

Martyr Nawaz Baloch, alias Fazal Baloch, son Sabzal Baloch was a resident of Gardank, Buleda area of Kech, Balochistan. He affiliated with Baloch Liberation Army, BLA since 2019. He embraced martyrdom along with eight comrades, Jalil Sher Baloch, Samad Baloch, Dad Shah, Samad Baloch, Shoaib Baloch, Rahmdil Baloch, Haris Baloch and Kambar Baloch  in a drone attack of Pakistan Army  on Nov 29, 2022 in Jath, Kolwa area of Kech, Balochistan.

Wadood Baloch was a resident of Chitkan, Panjgur. He was abducted by Pakistani forces on April 27, 2023, in the Turbat area of Kech. After eight months, on November 22, 2023, he was killed by the CTD in a fake encounter, along with three others - Balach Baloch, Shakoor Baloch, and Saif Baloch - in Banuk-e-Chadai, Turbat, Kech, Balochistan.

Martyr Comrade Maqsood Baloch, alias Comrade Mehrwan Baloch, son of Ahmed and was a resident of Herronk, area of Kech Balochistan. He started his students politics in platform of BSO Azad and he was known as a dedicated and active comrade. After years in 2012, he joined the Baloch armed struggle in the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF). Later in 2015, he joined Baloch Liberation Army (BLA). 
According organizational statement; Comrade Maqsood was a valiant and hardworking member of BLA. His commitment to the cause and strong adherence to the philosophy of sacrifice secured him prominent reputation in the organization. He suffered from illnesses during this period but never let this become a hurdle in accomplishment of his national responsibilities. He took part in several successful operations against the enemy forces.
Pakistani military targeted a temporary camp of BLA in a drone attack in Samaan e Kaor area of Turbat, Kech. This was followed by enemy forces being deployed in the area through helicopters. The enemy forces tried to surround the BLA fighters, however, this attempt was foiled with professional tactical measures. The enemy forces were engaged at different places for several places. At least five enemy personnel were killed and seven were injured in these battles.
While breaking the enemy siege and securing a safe passage for their comrades, two fighters of BLA made the ultimate sacrifice. These fallen freedom fighters were Comrade Maqsood alias Comrade Mehrwaan and Muslim Raza alias Guru Jabbar.

data.fullName: Asmat Ullah Mohammad Hassni, alias Mullah Chakar
data.biography:
Asmat Ullah Mohammad Hassni, alias Mullah Chakar, son of Nematullah Mohammad Hassni, was a Hafiz of the Quran and a resident of the Zorabad area of Noshki. He joined the armed struggle for the Baloch national liberation movement in June 2025 and later joined the BLA in April 2026, where he served on the Noshki front. On 13 September 2026, he was martyred in the Sultan Shar area of Qila Abdullah.
Asmatullah Muhammad Hassani, known as Mulla Chakar, belonged to Zorabad, Noshki. He was a Hafiz of the Quran, and his religious education was a prominent aspect of his personality. In June 2025, he joined the armed movement. In April 2026, he became part of the Baloch Liberation Army and was later associated with the Noshki front. According to his comrades, he was a serious and quiet young man who gave importance to his responsibilities.
His association with the Noshki front connected the final months of his life with an environment where everyday life was not easy. During this brief period, he lived among his comrades, experienced different circumstances alongside them, and gradually developed his own identity within that environment. His religious background as a Hafiz of the Quran was a distinct aspect of his personality in the eyes of his comrades, while he was known among his circle by the name Mulla Chakar.
September 13, 2026, proved to be the final day of his physical life. Asmatullah Muhammad Hassani, known as Mulla Chakar, was martyred during a clash in Sultan Shar, Qila Abdullah.

Maqsood Baloch, alias Beebagr, son of Abdul Hameed, was a resident of Tump, Talokan. He joined the BLA in 2023 and served on the Kulbar front with the rank of Patrol Commander. He was killed on 28 July 2026 in Turbat, Balochistan.
Martyr Maqsood Baloch, alias Beebagr, closely examined the occupation and colonial policies of the enemy, understood its colonial conduct, and, having become conscious of a life of national subjugation, humiliation, and degradation, took practical part in the Baloch Liberation Army’s political and armed resistance program for national freedom and the restoration of the Baloch state in 2023. Following an organizational decision, he joined the camp at Kalbar. His decision was rooted in a historical reality that forms part of Baloch civilization, culture, and tradition: the decision to resist bondage.
Martyr Maqsood was well acquainted with the Baloch traditions that the Baloch people have upheld for centuries, traditions grounded in resistance against foreign occupiers and in the restoration of their freedom and sovereignty. After completing his training, Beebagr became active in the war zones and took full part in important and difficult military operations against the enemy. In his assigned region, he also continued to raise awareness among the people and youth about the organization’s structure, the discipline of the BLA, and its program based on revolutionary conduct. Among the organization’s ongoing programs of advancement, he was regarded as one of the comrades who remained highly active and constantly engaged. Owing to the courage he displayed on the battlefield, his alertness and presence of mind, and his unwavering adherence to revolutionary principles, he was entrusted with the responsibilities of Patrol Commander in the relevant area, duties that he carried out with diligence and dedication.
Until his final moments, Martyr Maqsood was known for his sincere commitment to his responsibilities and his ability to carry out organizational activities with discipline. His combat skills continued to be employed against the enemy until the end. He was killed while fighting in Turbat after dismantling an important enemy espionage network and launching an attack against the enemy. His sacrifices will be remembered by generations to come.

On 16 July 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that the BLA eliminated more than forty personnel of the Pakistani Army and injured several others in forty-eight operations across Balochistan during the previous fifteen days. As part of the economic blockade, vehicles violating the blockade on major highways were targeted and destroyed. Furthermore, four key bridges were destroyed using planted explosive devices. During various clashes with the occupying forces, five BLA fighters - Rahimullah Mohammad Hassni, alias Zafar, son of Lumma Raaj Bibi; Khair Mohammad Khairo, alias Hammal, son of Shahbaz; Kaka Baloch, alias Kaka Rasheed, son of Shahbaz; Masood Baloch, alias Sami, son of Ghulam Jan; and Shah Nazar Baloch, alias Badal, son of Khuda Nazar - embraced martyrdom.

Kaka Baloch, alias Kaka Rasheed, son of Shahbaz, was a resident of the Sangan area of Bolan. He joined the BLA in 2014 and served on the Bolan and Mastung fronts. He was martyred on 7 July 2026 in the Harnai area of Balochistan.
Kaka Baloch and Khair Mohammad Khairo were brothers. They joined the BLA on intellectual and conscious grounds, continuing their family's tradition of sacrifices for national liberation. Kaka Baloch became part of the armed struggle in 2014 and was deployed to the Bolan front. Throughout this period, he remained among those fighters on the front who were determined, brave, and inflicted heavy losses on the enemy. He left a lasting impact on the battlefield and earned recognition as an experienced and exemplary Sarmachar, serving as an inspiration to newer cadres.
He did not join the BLA merely because of his family's sacrifices; rather, he regarded it as a national duty and became part of the armed struggle on intellectual and conscious grounds. Through his actions and character, he demonstrated the role of a true Sarmachar on the battlefield. During the historic Battle of Dara-e-Bolan, he fulfilled his responsibilities as a front-line fighter and fought the enemy with exceptional courage. In addition, he served as a front-line Sarmachar in the battles of Mashdari and Loni, where he continued to inflict heavy losses on the enemy. Whether during the organization's two-day control of Mach city or the historic rail hijacking operation, in which the enemy was fiercely attacked, he consistently proved himself to be a courageous and steadfast fighter. Through his dedication and commitment, he remained a practical example for his fellow fighters.
Throughout this long period, he did not show a single sign of exhaustion or weakness. Instead, his unwavering determination, constant presence on the front line, and resolute confrontation with the enemy remained an example for his fellow fighters. He fought with bravery until his last breath and, as always, kept the ideals and flag of national liberation held high until the final moments of his life. Fighting courageously, he embraced martyrdom on 7 July 2026 in the Harnai area of Balochistan.

On 15 May 2026, a press statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that the Sarmachars (freedom fighters) of the Baloch Liberation Army carried out eighteen successful operations against the enemy across Balochistan between 4 May 2026 and 14 May 2026, resulting in the deaths of 31 personnel of the occupying Pakistani army, including a Major-rank officer, while several others were seriously injured. These attacks included seven powerful IED strikes. Additionally, the Sarmachars seized control of main highways for hours at various locations, targeting vehicles belonging to exploitative companies and occupying forces, and detaining individuals associated with these companies. In these coordinated operations, seven personnel and operatives of the state-backed “Death Squads” and Military Intelligence (MI) were also killed.
During intense clashes with the occupying forces at various locations, five BLA fighters - Ali Jan Siahpad alias Sudais, Ahsanullah alias Master Maran, Nasrullah alias Mama Zagreen, Tanveer Mengal alias Murad Khan, and Saadullah Baloch alias Wajid - embraced martyrdom while fighting valiantly against the enemy.

Saadullah Baloch, alias Wajid, and Tanveer Mengal, alias Murad Khan, were martyred on 15 April 2026 while fighting bravely against the occupying Pakistani forces during an intense clash in the Sohinda area of Zehri.
Saadullah Baloch, alias Wajid, son of Amanullah, was a resident of the Gulkand area of Mastung. He joined the BLA in June 2025 and served on the Kalat and Zehri fronts before being martyred on 15 April 2026 in Sohinda, Zehri.
Saadullah Baloch, alias Wajid, was from Mastung, where he received his basic ideological upbringing and, upon recognizing the reality of national subjugation, decided to resist it. He chose the BLA’s military doctrine in pursuit of the great objective of national liberation, which today has become a symbol of the end of the enemy’s occupation of Balochistan. With this conscious commitment, he took part in the struggle with the resolve that he would continue the fight for the restoration of an independent Baloch state until his last breath and would end the presence of the enemy on Baloch land.
This awareness and sense of national liberation freed him from fear and hesitation, placing him among the ranks of the national resistance, where he played a role that will be remembered in the history of the war of independence as a symbol of courage, sincerity, and dedication to his land and nation.
He confronted the enemy in Kalat and Zehri with steadfastness and bravery and sacrificed his life for freedom. He remained committed until his last breath to the pledge he had made upon joining the organization. By attaining martyrdom in this struggle for Baloch national survival, he inscribed his name in the pages of history and became an example for others that the freedom of the homeland demands great sacrifice from us.

On 21 August 2026, Pakistani forces conducted an aerial drone strike on a garden located in the Gaith area of Khadkucha, Mastung District, Balochistan. The strike resulted in the martyrdom of four orchard workers - Gul Khan Mughairi, Imran Baloch, Obaidullah Baloch and Jahanzaib Abdo - and left three others - Ali Raza Mengal, Naseebullah Abdo and Khalid Hussein - badly injured.
Rescue personnel transferred the dead and injured to Shaheed Nawab Ghaus Bakhsh Raisani Memorial Hospital in Mastung, where the wounded received treatment.
All the victims were reportedly associated with Haji Shahr in Kachhi District. Rescue sources said all of the casualties were working as labourers in the orchard at the time of the incident.
The reported strike also follows other incidents in which civilians were reportedly killed during Pakistani military operations or aerial attacks in Balochistan.
On 12 August 2026, reports emerged from Sorab’s Goandhan area alleging that an aerial bombardment had killed innocent civilians, including women and children.
The Mastung incident also comes weeks after reports from Khuzdar District alleging that four civilians were killed in a reported drone strike on a house in the Moola Manjalo area.

Martyr Hazza Baloch Alias Meeral Baloch, son of Mohammad Saleh Baloch and was a resident Mand area of  Kech, Balochistan. He became part of Baloch liberation movement in platform the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in 2017. He strived against of occupation and  on Aug 8, 2022, joined military camp of BLF. 
He embraced martyrdom in a drone attack of Pakistan’s military along with his seven comrades, Kareem Baloch, Mullah Bakhsh, Manzoor Baloch,  Asif Baloch, Shezad Baloch, Jalal Baloch, and Talab Baloch on Feb 23, 2023 in Mazanband area of Kech, Balochistan.

Uzair Ahmad Mandai, alias Tanveer, son of Abdul Shakoor, was a resident of the Zangi Nawad area of Noshki, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Chagai Front. He was martyred on 31 August 2026 in the Nokcha area of Chagi District, Balochistan.
Uzair Ahmad Mandai, having recognized national slavery, humiliation, looting, and ongoing torture and violence, and grasped the importance of national freedom and statehood, decided this year to join the great revolutionary cause and program of the Baloch Liberation Army, enlisted in the organization, and became active on the Shor front. After completing the organization’s rigorous combat training, he became active on organizational patrols and took full part in military operations against the enemy. Alongside establishing the organization’s strength and dominance in the region, he played an outstanding individual role in economic and military measures against the enemy.
Uzair was well aware of the fact that if the enemy was not stopped here, and if a practical and powerful war was not launched against them, they would abolish Balochistan’s historical independent status and impose the worst form of Punjabi imperialism, which could, in every respect, lead to our permanent destruction. He put this realization into practice; from the BLA front, he worked to thwart the enemy’s policies and fought to the end for Balochistan’s freedom, fulfilling his individual responsibilities. Uzair Mandai will be counted among the great freedom fighters in Balochistan’s history who dedicated their blood and lives to the freedom of future generations.

Noor Ahmad Sumalani, alias Notak, son of Noor Khan Sumalani, was a resident of Pira Ismail, Narowari. He joined the BLA in 2018 and served on the Bolan and Quetta fronts. He was martyred on 30 July 2026 in Wali Tangi, Quetta, Balochistan.
Noor Ahmad Sumalani, alias Notak, remained actively engaged on the war fronts against the enemy for the eight years of his association with the Baloch Liberation Army. Because of his ideological commitment and dedication to the movement, he faced extremely adverse circumstances with bravery, courage, and determination. He remained a Sarmachar on the war front, distinguished by his steadfastness, constant activity, and active participation in the battlefield. He was always on the front line, taking part in heavy attacks against the enemy during his service on the Bolan front. He also demonstrated the ability to adapt to changing wartime circumstances and turn them to his advantage.
In addition, Martyr Notak's brother, Martyr Mohammad Jan, alias Lila, had also remained in the ranks of the BLA and sacrificed his life in the line of duty for the cause of national freedom. Following his brother's martyrdom, Notak decided to join the battlefield and, on the organization's directive, established the Bolan front as the center of his military activities.
During the following eight years, he gained an advantage over the enemy on the Bolan front and in surrounding areas. He contributed to advancing the front lines, increasing manpower and military capabilities, planning large-scale military operations, and carrying out assigned responsibilities. He proved himself to be a Sarmachar who remained committed to the organization's directives. His consistency on the war front was one of the foremost qualities that distinguished him.
Martyr Notak remained committed to the organization's policies and discipline until the very end and used his capabilities and individual strength against the enemy in an organized manner. By capturing enemy checkpoints on the Bolan front and inflicting heavy losses on the enemy on the front line, he sacrificed his life for national freedom, the sovereignty of the motherland, and the restoration of Balochistan as an independent state. He thus became part of the legacy of Baloch martyrs forever.

Yahya Baloch, son of Noor Muhammad, was a 17 year old driver from Paroom, Panjgur. He belonged to a poor family and took on responsibilities at a very young age.
On October 1, 2025, at around 7:30 PM, he was forcibly disappeared from Airport Road, Chitkan, Panjgur, by a local death squad operating under the command of the occupying Pakistani genocidal forces. For six months, his family waited in pain and uncertainty. On March 3, 2026, his dead body was dumped in the Washbood area of Panjgur.

Jalil Baloch, son of Munir Ahmed, was critically injured during a patrol when a landmine planted by Pakistani forces exploded. He later succumbed to his injuries, embracing martyrdom.
Jalil Baloch, alias Jorak, son of Munir Ahmed, was a resident of Dizder Dasht. He joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in August 2023 and became part of the urban network. He also served in the organization’s intelligence wing. On 3 October 2024, he was transferred to the camp, where he carried out his duties with utmost dedication, commitment, and enthusiasm.
On 23 January 2026, Jalil Ahmed was on patrol with other fighters in the mountainous area of Mand while carrying out an organizational task, when he was critically injured by a landmine explosion planted by enemy forces along the route. He was being transferred to a safe location for medical treatment; however, he succumbed to his injuries on the way and attained martyrdom.

Following the deadly SVBEID bombing at a Pakistani Coast Guard camp in Jiwani, Balochistan, on 3 July 2026, carried out by Attaullah Baloch, alias Ajmal, of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) Majeed Brigade Fidayee Unit, which took the lives of more than 30 Pakistani security personnel, Pakistani forces, in reaction, extrajudicially killed four Baloch on the very next day, 4 July 2026 - Mohammad Abdul Haq, son of Mohammad Murad; Chakar, son of Hassa Baksh; Peeri Assa and Shah Baksh Omar, son of Omar - in a staged encounter and claimed that they had been killed in the Jiwani attack. Later, all four were identified as previously forcibly disappeared persons.

Chakar, the son of Hassa Bakhsh, was a 25-year-old shopkeeper and resident of Baloch Ward, Gwadar. He was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces during an early morning raid on 12 May 2025. From that day onward, his whereabouts remained unknown, while his family waited for his safe return.
After more than fourteen months of enforced disappearance, Chakar was extrajudicially killed. His body was later recovered bearing severe signs of torture and inhumane treatment. The visible injuries on his body, including extensive facial trauma, showed the brutal violence inflicted upon him during his prolonged detention. Instead of returning him alive to his family, Pakistani forces returned him as another tortured body.

Hatim Baloch, son of Haji Muhammad and a resident of Shapatan, Panjgur, was a seventeen-year-old student who was forcibly disappeared by FC personnel from Legork, Paroom, Panjgur, on April 5, 2026. His bullet-riddled body was later dumped.
After several days of enforced disappearance, during which he was subjected to physical and psychological torture in a detention cell, his mutilated body was found on April 16, 2026, in Panjgur, Balochistan.

data.fullName: Martyr Fedayi Ayoob Alias Doda Baloch

data.biography: Shoaib Hameed Baloch was a resident of the Mand area of Kech, Balochistan. He was a driver by profession. He was killed by FC personnel of the Pakistani forces in the Abdoi border area of Kech, Balochistan, on November 27, 2023.

On January 21, 2026, in the Washbud area of Panjgur district, Balochistan, armed groups working under Pakistani forces, locally known as death squads, abducted Jasim Jan, son of Mohammad Adam, and forcibly disappeared him. A few days later, on February 3, 2026, his tortured body was recovered from Washbud.

On June 6, 2025 at around 7 AM, a large contingent of operatives from the puppet militia (Bugti Peace Force) operating under the patronage of the occupying Pakistani army and intelligence agencies, and led by the puppet Chief Minister of Balochistan, Sarfraz Bugti, launched an attack on a patrol team’s camp of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in the mountainous region of Koh Jandar, Rakhni, Barkhan.
The Sarmachars (freedom fighters) immediately adopted a defensive strategy and, after an intense battle lasting approximately three hours, successfully thwarted the enemy’s advance and encirclement attempts, managing to withdraw safely. During this clash, two members of the death squad were killed.
However, the battle did not end with this initial phase. The enemy pursued the Sarmachars and implemented a strategy to block their escape routes. A few kilometres from the site of the initial clash, the Sarmachars encountered fresh reinforcements of the occupying Pakistani army, leading to another intense confrontation. This fierce battle continued for seven hours. In this prolonged combat, four fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front embraced martyrdom and etched their names in the pages of history, while two soldiers of the occupying Pakistani army were killed and several others were severely injured.
Among the martyrs who laid down their lives in the clash with the occupying forces at Koh Jandar, Rakhni, were Rasaan Qadir (alias Rehan), Mustafa Noor (alias Diljan), Samiullah (alias Meeran), and Shahzaib (alias Shahshan).
Sarmachar Mustafa Noor alias Zubair Jan, son of Noor Jan, was from Tasp, Panjgur. He had been associated with the BLF for the past two and a half years in the national liberation struggle. He was actively involved in the urban guerrilla cells of Quetta and Panjgur and played a prominent role in intellectual gatherings and revolutionary public awareness programs. Recognizing his intellectual training and practical capabilities, the organization assigned him to the sensitive mission in Barkhan, where he attained martyrdom in the Koh Jandar battle.

Tariq Baloch, son of Allah Dad, was a 40-year-old police constable and a resident of Malant, Tump, Kech. On 12 September 2026, death squads opened fire and deliberately targeted his son, Tahir Baloch, killing him. Tariq was also critically injured in the same attack.
Tariq fought for his life in hospital for five days. On 17 September 2026, he succumbed to his injuries and died. Within a matter of days, a family lost both a son and a father - two lives taken through targeted violence, leaving their loved ones to bear the unbearable consequences.

Salman Bangulzai, son of Abdul Nabi Bangulzai, was a 33-year-old shopkeeper and resident of Khudabadan, Panjgur. He was forcibly disappeared by a Pakistani state-backed death squad shortly after Eid in 2026. He remained in torture cells until 31 July 2026, when his body was recovered from the Newan Kour (Newan River) area of Panjgur district, Balochistan.

On 3 May 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said that between 25 April 2026 and 3 May 2026, BLA fighters carried out eleven operations, resulting in the deaths of eleven personnel from Pakistani forces. These attacks targeted the Pakistani army, vehicles transporting minerals, and local collaborators.
In four IED attacks, the army suffered significant personnel and financial losses, while three Military Intelligence (MI) personnel were taken into custody.
On 24 April 2026, during clashes with Pakistani forces at Taadez in Nushki, three BLA fighters - Asad Jamaldini (alias Baba Darwesh), Shakeel-ur-Rehman Bangulzai (alias Sheikh Atta), and Shehak Mengal (alias Siddiq) - were killed.
Shayhaq Mengal, alias Siddiq, son of Bohair Khan, was a resident of Dalbandin. He joined the BLA on 12 January 2025 and served in Shor Parood, Kalat, and Noshki. He was martyred on 24 April 2026 in Tadeez, Noshki.
Shayhaq was young in age, but in terms of intellectual maturity, knowledge, and awareness, he had reached a firm conclusion: that armed resistance against the occupying force was the ultimate means of defending his homeland, safeguarding national freedom, and restoring independence. This realization led him to the center of Baloch national resistance, the BLA, where he remained committed to the organization’s intellectual, ideological, military, and professional discipline until his last breath.
In a very short period, he established himself within the organization as a capable, trustworthy, confident, brave, and determined Sarmachar. He accepted every kind of military and political responsibility assigned to him and carried them out effectively in the field. In recent times, he played an active combat role alongside his fellow Sarmachar in key operations and advances in the areas of Shor Parood and Noshki, fulfilling his individual responsibilities in implementing the organization’s policies.
By dedicating his services to the homeland, Shayhaq left a clear message for Baloch youth: they must fully recognize their national responsibilities today and play their part in the restoration of a Baloch state, as the bright future of any nation cannot be complete without a state.

Hatum Baloch, son of Khuda Bakhsh, a 26 year old shopkeeper from Shapuk, was brutally targeted by state backed death squads on March 4, 2026.
He was lured out of his shop by men in a white-colored car. When he tried to escape, the attackers opened fire, fatally wounding him. Hatum came from a poor Baloch family and worked tirelessly in his shop to support his loved ones. Even during the holy month of Ramzan, the state showed no mercy, attacking innocent Baloch families and trying to break their spirit.

Sherbaz Bangulzai, alias Gazzain, son of Haji Imam Bakhsh Bangulzai, was a resident of Killi Qambrani, Quetta. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Mastung and Dasht fronts. He was martyred on 14 July 2026 in Dasht, Mastung.
Martyr Sherbaz was a brave fighter, full of national pain and feeling. He had fully realized that armed resistance against the occupation of Balochistan was the only solution through which the Baloch could live a free and sovereign life and achieve state sovereignty. To put this goal into practice, he chose the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army and joined the organization this year. He moved to the revolutionary front in Mastung, where he completed the basic physical training courses provided by the organization with hard work, dedication, and national zeal.
Martyr Sherbaz was also forcibly disappeared by the enemy in August of last year, where he was subjected to severe physical and mental torture. Yet more important to him than the enemy’s inhuman torture was the fact that the Baloch, as a collective, were forced to live a life of slavery on their own land, and that Balochistan was occupied by an unnatural state with no identity or recognition of its own—one that survives on our plunder. That is why, in the face of his national purpose and ideology, the enemy’s torture held no sway, and this year he embraced the goal of national liberation. He remained active on the Mastung front and took full part in the ongoing attacks against the enemy, while assisting his comrades in maintaining organizational superiority and strength in the region and playing his individual role.
Martyr Sherbaz had assumed a position as a dynamic and operationally active fighter in his area and, in a short time, earned a unique standing among his comrades, which reflected his national, conscious, and revolutionary thinking. He was in Mastung Dasht for operational purposes when he was martyred in a drone attack by the enemy. He made his mark in Baloch history alongside those great fighters who chose their homeland and sacrificed their lives.

Mushtaq Mengal, alias: Kohyar, son of Abdul Sattar Mengal was resident of Basima, his Education qualification was F.Sc, he joined the BLA as Urban Guerrilla in 2021 and moved in mountain Front on 10 February 2022 and served in Bolan, Nushki, Basima fronts and promoted Patrol Command rank by organizations and martyred on 16 August 2026 in Zik area of Basima, Balochistan.
Martyr Mushtaq Mengal, one of the resilient, decisive fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army, decided to join the national liberation movement on the platform of the BLA in 2021 and assumed responsibilities on the urban front. For almost one year, he served on the urban front with exceptional courage and remarkable performance, providing much-needed  operational information, collecting data, and providing essential support for the urban operations of the organization. After one year of service on the urban front, he moved to the Bolan front on the direction of the organization’s command. He proved to be a great warrior and an excellent fighter at the beginning of the guerrilla combat operations.
After joining the mountain front with excellent experience in urban warfare, Kohyar established himself as a warrior who had a deep understanding of warfare, its tactics, and its requirements, and who followed the revolutionary approach of the organization. He had a sensitive approach to understanding the challenges of war and to addressing matters concerning the movement and the organization. His ability to maintain good relations with the public and people, even in uncertain situations, set him apart from many others. He was a qualified and educated youth who did not join the war merely to fight, but to establish a strong and capable force that could defeat the enemy on its own terms. He was a remarkable fighter when he joined frontline combat, while as an educated youth, he also worked to raise awareness among the people when he was among the public. Based on those capabilities, the organization entrusted him with patrol command responsibilities.
After serving on the Bolan front with great and extraordinary performance, he was later deployed in Nushki, where he was known to every Sangat for his bravery and warfare skills. Later, he moved to Basima to establish the organization’s dominance in the region and was involved in multiple key military operations against the enemy, making great contributions to expanding the organization’s operational capabilities in the region. Martyr Mushtaq’s sacrifices will remain an enduring part of Baloch history. His commitment, courage, and contributions will continue to be remembered by his fellow Sangat and by those who carry forward his legacy in the struggle for the independence of the Baloch homeland.

On the night of May 23, 2025, Haneef Aziz Baloch, a resident of the Toboo Kad area in Jahoo, Awaran District, was forcibly abducted from his home by Pakistani law enforcement agencies (LEAs), including paramilitary forces. Without presenting any legal warrant or justification, armed personnel stormed his house and took him into custody in front of his family, an act that has become tragically commonplace across Balochistan.
Less than 24 hours later, on the morning of May 24, Haneef’s body was found dumped. It bore clear signs of brutal torture and multiple bullet wounds, undeniable evidence of extrajudicial execution.

Arz Mohammed Pirkani, son of Abdulla, was a resident of Smangali Road, Shaal. He was a student and a member of BSO Azad, Shaal Zone. He received his primary education from his native area. He mobilized many youths to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of the Baloch homeland. Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by security forces. He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he remained with the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom. He was an example of bravery and commitment. He joined the organization at an early age and stood by his national ideology until the end. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for his peaceful political expression.
He was abducted from Quetta on August 8, 2010. His bullet-riddled body was found in Quetta in August 2010. His body bore extreme signs of torture. He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a very young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

data.martyrdomPlace: Satak Kor, Hoshap, Turbat district, Balochistan
data.biography:
On February 23, 2022 the occupying forces of Pakistan struck the Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) guerrilla camp in the Satak Kor mountain range of Hoshab, district Kech, and fired three chemical-laden missiles that wreaked havoc over a large area, destroying palm groves and other vegetation at the site. Following the drone missile attacks, the infantry team of the occupying forces surrounded the area and, with the support of more than eight state helicopters, entered the camp. Five Sarmachaars, including two commanders of the organization, Master Asif Baloch and Siraj Baloch, were martyred in this attack. Meanwhile, five other Sarmachaars - Shoaib, Munir, Arif Jan, Diljan, Kamal, Kamash Malang, Jangi Khan, and Daolat - were martyred defending their homeland, fighting the enemy for over an hour and killing several commandos of the occupying forces.
Shoaib, alias Siraj, son of Eid Muhammad, resident of Hoshab Damb, had been associated with the organization since a year before his martyrdom. He was a patriotic and courageous Sarmachar.

Mohammad Shafi Baloch, son of Haji Jangi Khan Mengal, from Kalat, Balochistan, was abducted by Pakistani secret agencies on 27 July 2011. His dead body was found on 10 October 2011 in Bagbana, Khuzdar, Balochistan.
He was a student and an active member of BSO Azad. Mohammad Shafi Baloch was a resident of Anjira, Tehsil Surab, District Kalat, Balochistan. He received his early education at Government School Anjeera and also obtained Islamic education at Tablighi College, Hub. He completed his F.Sc at Government Degree College Khuzdar. Due to financial difficulties, he could not continue his formal education and later completed a private BA.
He began his political career with BSO Pajjar during his matriculation but later joined BSO Azad. After joining BSO Azad, he was threatened multiple times by security officials to withdraw from political activities. However, he did not stop and continued advocating for the freedom of Balochistan.
He was one of the dedicated members of the organization and actively participated in its activities. He regularly took part in BSO Azad activism. Exercising his political rights, he distributed pamphlets, books, and other materials to raise awareness among the Baloch nation about the oppression they faced at the hands of Pakistani forces.
He had a passion for cricket and played at the district level in his area. He consistently opposed the tribal system in the region. Because of this, he was beaten and imprisoned several times on the orders of a local Sardar. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising his right to peaceful political expression.
He was abducted on 7 August 2011 from Aga Khan Hospital, Karachi. His bullet-riddled body was later found dumped on 10 October 2011 in Bhagbana, District Khuzdar, Balochistan.

On 12 August 2026, several Baloch people, including women and children, were killed and several others were injured as a result of an aerial bombardment of a civilian population by the Pakistan Air Force, reportedly using American-made F-16 fighter aircraft, in the Gidar Gindan area of Surab District, Balochistan. Following the airstrike, the injured and deceased were transported by police and local residents to DHQ Hospital in Surab, where the injured received medical treatment.

The families of the deceased and local residents subsequently began a protest by placing the bodies at Surab Main Chowk on the Quetta–Karachi National Highway (N-25). As a result, traffic on the highway was disrupted, with long queues of vehicles forming on both sides. Videos and photographs of the protest subsequently circulated widely on social media under the hashtag #SurabMassacre.

Those killed in the airstrike were identified as Shabir Ahmad Sumalani, son of Khudadad Sumalani, a resident of Marap, Surab; Noor Jan Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, a resident of Gindan; Karim Dad Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, a resident of Gandan; Raj Babu, wife of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani; Safia, wife of Noor Jan Mirwani; and Jalal Mirwani, son of Noor Jan Mirwani.

Those injured were identified as Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, son of Jan Muhammad Mirwani; Abdul Karim Mirwani, son of Jan Muhammad Mirwani; Mehrullah Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani; Nadeem Mirwani, son of Abdul Salam Mirwani; Shoaib Mirwani, son of Abdul Karim Mirwani; Sarah, wife of Baseer Ahmed Mirwani; Sabira, wife of Tufail Ahmed Mirwani; Zamra, daughter of Abdul Aziz Mirwani; Hajira, wife of Abdul Fattah Mirwani; Asim, son of Baseer, aged 1; Rahabia, daughter of Abdul Karim, aged 3; Sadia, daughter of Abdul Salam, aged 5; Fatima, daughter of Abdul Karim, aged 7; Zia-ur-Rehman, son of Abdul Karim, aged 2; Amir, son of Abdul Karim, aged 1; and Hasina, daughter of Muhammad Aslam, aged 4.

Following a detailed technical and scientific analysis of remnants of rocket components recovered from debris at the site of the aerial bombardment, important evidence reportedly emerged indicating that the recovered fragments belonged to an air-launched missile fired from an F-16 fighter aircraft.

Photographs of the recovered debris and the subsequent technical analysis reportedly indicated that the fragment was part of an AIM-120 Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile (AMRAAM), an American-made air-to-air missile.

Key technical evidence and serial numbers

According to the information and serial numbers reportedly engraved on the surface of the debris, the following details were recorded:

Assembly Number: ASSY 872128-1

Serial Number: 09-987138

Date of Manufacture: 09/09 (September 2009)

According to open-source intelligence (OSINT) records, the part number “872128-1” reportedly corresponds to the control section and rocket motor assembly of an AMRAAM missile manufactured by the American defense company Raytheon. Based on this evidence and the reported matching serial numbers, it is claimed that the debris was not part of an aircraft’s internal structure but instead consisted of remnants from an operational missile fired from an F-16 aircraft.

On February 12, 2026, the 25 year old, Kamal Dad,  son of Haji Dad Mohammad and a driver by profession from Sholeeg Dasht, was targeted and killed by a Pakistani state backed death squad in Kontani, Gwadar District, Balochistan. He was attacked while returning to Gwadar from Kontani and later succumbed to his injuries.
Kamal Dad had previously been forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces in 2025 and was released after one month of illegal detention. Following his release, he survived an assassination attempt in Faqeer Colony, where he sustained injuries.

Following the deadly SVBEID bombing at a Pakistani Coast Guard camp in Jiwani, Balochistan, on 3 July 2026, carried out by Attaullah Baloch, alias Ajmal, of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) Majeed Brigade Fidayee Unit, which took the lives of more than 30 Pakistani security personnel, Pakistani forces, in reaction, extrajudicially killed four Baloch on the very next day, 4 July 2026 - Mohammad Abdul Haq, son of Mohammad Murad; Chakar, son of Hassa Baksh; Peeri Assa and Shah Baksh Omar, son of Omar - in a staged encounter and claimed that they had been killed in the Jiwani attack. Later, all four were identified as previously forcibly disappeared persons.

Peeri Assa, a 28-year-old fisherman from Rober, Jiwani, Gwadar, was forcibly taken from his home during a late-night raid on 6 January 2026. From that day onward, his whereabouts remained unknown.
For nearly six months, he remained a victim of enforced disappearance. After months in torture cells, Peeri Assa was brutally tortured and killed. His body bore visible injuries, showing signs of severe physical violence.
His case, along with those of many others who have been inhumanely killed, reflects the "kill and dump" policy, in which individuals are forcibly taken, held in detention cells, subjected to physical and psychological torture by Pakistani security and intelligence agencies, and later killed in staged encounters before their bodies are dumped like trash.

On 3 May 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said that between 25 April 2026 and 3 May 2026, BLA fighters carried out eleven operations, resulting in the deaths of eleven personnel from Pakistani forces. These attacks targeted the Pakistani army, vehicles transporting minerals, and local collaborators.
In four IED attacks, the army suffered significant personnel and financial losses, while three Military Intelligence (MI) personnel were taken into custody.
On 24 April 2026, during clashes with Pakistani forces at Taadez in Nushki, three BLA fighters - Asad Jamaldini (alias Baba Darwesh), Shakil-ur-Rehman Bangulzai (alias Sheikh Atta), and Shehak Mengal (alias Siddiq) - were killed.
Shakil ur Rahman Bangulzai, alias Sheikh Atta, son of Abdul Kareem Bangulzai, was a resident of Saryab, Quetta, Balochistan. His educational qualification was Intermediate. He joined the BLA in June 2025 and served on the Shor Parood, Kalat, and Noshki fronts. He was martyred on 24 April 2026 in Tadeez, Noshki.
On the Noshki front, while bravely confronting the enemy alongside his fellow Sarmachars, Shakil ur Rahman Bangulzai attained the esteemed status of martyrdom. He rendered his finest military services to the organization on the fronts of Shor Parood, Kalat, and Noshki. In the defense of national freedom, the strengthening of defensive positions, and the repelling of enemy advances, he is remembered among his comrades as a brave and fearless Sarmachar.
He was quiet by nature, yet physically and mentally a very strong Sarmachar. He was an active fighter who helped implement the organization’s military discipline, professional standards, and forward strategy. He adhered strictly to the command structure and followed orders faithfully. Like his fellow comrades, he played a very important role in firmly maintaining the organization’s regional positions.
He upheld all organizational principles and the oath of combat in his practical life principles he had accepted with full conviction when he chose to join the battlefield. He remained steadfast to these ideals until his last breath and set an example for his fellow comrades.
data.fullName: Shakil Ur Rahman, alias Sheikh Atta

data.biography: Alam Khan, son of Dad Bakhsh, was a 47-year-old farmer from Sohrdap, Gresha, Khuzdar. On 17 September 2026, Alam Khan was targeted and killed. He and his friends were returning home after attending a wedding when members of a death squad opened fire on them. Alam Khan was killed, while his friend, Barkat Azeem, sustained injuries.

Naseem Baloch, a 15-year-old boy and son of Qadir Baksh, was forcibly disappeared from his home on 7 November 2025 by a state-backed death squad in Hoshap, district Kech. The following morning, his bullet-riddled body was found dumped in a remote area of Hoshap.

According to local sources, Naseem had previously been subjected to repeated harassment and had been summoned multiple times to the Hoshap military cantonment. Before his abduction and subsequent killing, he worked as a laborer in Kuntani, struggling to earn a livelihood to support his family.

Asif Nadeem, son of Lal Baksh and a resident of Gwarjak, Mashkai, was a poet of the Balochi language. He joined the Baloch liberation struggle during a critical period when the prominent Baloch leader Akbar Khan Bugti was assassinated along with his colleagues in 2006, and a massive military crackdown was launched against freedom-seeking people in Balochistan. Asif played a vital role in promoting the Baloch liberation movement, and during his activism, he was martyred on May 30, 2010, in Gajjari, Mashkai.

On 13 October 2026, Pakistani genocidal forces killed six Baloch men who had previously been subjected to enforced disappearance and dumped their bodies in the Sui area of Dera Bugti district, Balochistan.
The incident was also confirmed by Sher Mohammad Bugti, the Central Spokesperson of the Baloch Republican Party.

The victims have been identified as follows:
- Mohammad Khan Bugti, son of Yar Mohammad Bugti
- Lalu Bugti, son of Taj Mohammad Bugti
- Shahmeer Bugti, son of Shahal Bugi
- Waheed Bugti, son of Habib Bugti
- Ghulam Din Bugti, son of Kurri Bugti
- Akram Khan, son of Wadera Mazar Khan Bugti

On 26 September 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch stated that fighters from the Karima Armed Assault Division (KAAD), the newly formed female unit of the Balochistan Liberation Front, had carried out two major operations: one on the CPEC highway in the Jusak area of Turbat and the other on the Quetta - Karachi highway in Manguchar, Kalat. According to the statement, six personnel of the Pakistani army were killed and several others were wounded in the Jusak operation.

On 22 September 2026, KAAD fighters, acting on an intelligence report, ambushed a 3-vehicle Quick Response Force (QRF) convoy of the occupying Pakistani army on the CPEC highway in Jusak, Turbat district. This was KAAD's first military operation. As the QRF convoy reached the target point, the fighters advanced onto the road, surrounded the convoy and opened fire from the front. The LMG gunner mounted on the first armored vehicle was directly targeted and killed on the spot, attack on the second vehicle killed one more soldier, and both vehicles fled the target area. Meanwhile the fighters heavily attacked the arriving third vehicle from multiple directions with automatic weapons, killing all 4 soldiers onboard. In total, 6 occupying army personnel were killed and several more wounded, while severely damaging the enemy's vehicles. KAAD received strong reinforcement from BLF's Qurban unit in carrying out this operation.
After the attack, when the occupying army attempted a counter encirclement, KAAD and Qurban unit fighters repelled it, providing cover for the fellow fighters and ensuring the safe withdrawal of all units. In this engagement, Qurban unit's fearless and brave fighter Captain Chakar Murad, alias Dileep Ameer, son of Murad, resident of Balochi Bazaar, Apsar, Turbat, was martyred fighting courageously.

Captain Chakar Murad formally joined the armed struggle under the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front in February 2021, though from his early youth he held a deep emotional and ideological attachment to the national freedom cause and the organization. Before formally joining BLF, despite his youth, he remained exceptionally active in guiding sarmachars, providing intelligence information, and in other organizational matters. Because of the affiliation with the movement, the occupying enemy arrested him in his youth and held him in their dark, dreadful prisons for six months. In the enemy torture chambers, martyr Captain Chakar endured suffering, brutal torture and horrific pain, while the enemy also made every possible attempt to entice him but this fighter of iron resolve neither broke under torture, nor fell silent, nor could temptation or fear pull him away from the national struggle.
After his release, formally joining the BLF, he received deep political and ideological training within the organization's ranks, through which he transformed his feelings into elevated revolutionary consciousness, accurately assessed the exploitative policies of the oppressor state, and stood firm before the enemy like a fearless, solid rock. At a young age he achieved complete mastery of guerrilla warfare strategy and came to be counted among the organization's senior, long-standing members, where no one could sense that his age or length of membership was less than theirs.
Owing to Captain Chakar Murad's unmatched diligence, unwavering sincerity and superior leadership abilities, the organization promoted him to the responsible rank of Captain and appointed him second-in-command of the camp. He was a front-line, hardworking member of the Qurban unit, which is BLF's special vanguard unit that engages the enemy on the front line without regard for its own life in every major and minor battle. Martyr Captain Chakar bravely fulfilled all his combat duties as a fearless fighter of the Qurban unit on the difficult and hard fronts of Turbat, Kilkour, Balgatar, Panjgur, Shapuk, Paroom, Zamuran and Buleida.
Particularly in Turbat city, which the enemy considered a secure zone due to its army, ISI, MI, headquarters, hundreds of checkpoints and paid informants, Captain Chakar Murad made the occupiers lose sleep day and night. He intensified and played a key role in organizing urban guerrilla warfare in Turbat city at a time when military operations on the urban front were considered almost nonexistent and extremely difficult. He paved the way for the urban front and continuously assisted BLF's allied organizations by providing them with logistics, intelligence and tactical support.
Captain Chakar Murad, under daring strategy, carried out attacks by penetrating into the enemy's stronghold and confined the occupying army and intelligence agencies' network to their camps. Captain Chakar Murad and his comrades repeatedly dealt the occupying army defeats in the heart of Turbat city, and the enemy suffered irreparable losses in successive attacks.
Captain Chakar Murad played a key and historic role

Mehraj Rehmat, son of Rehmat Baloch, was a resident of Gajjar Mashkai, District Awaran, Balochistan. He received his early education in his hometown, Gajjar Mashkai, and was a student of class 9 at Government High School Gajjar. He was also a member of BSO Azad, Mashkai Zone. He belonged to a revolutionary family. His father and a brother were also killed by the Pakistan Army due to their affiliation with the Baloch liberation movement.
He joined BSO Azad at an early age and took part in every activity of the organization in his region. He served in different unit positions before being elected as a zonal member of the organization in Mashkai Zone. He was targeted under the state policy of “kill and dump” against Baloch political activists. He was also targeted for his peaceful political activism.
He was abducted on 19 May 2015 by Pakistan’s army from Zong, Mashkai. His bullet-riddled body was found on the same day in Gajjar Mashkai, District Awaran, Balochistan. His body showed extreme signs of torture.
He was among the most committed sangats (comrades) of the organization and continued his struggle during its most difficult times. Because of his commitment, many youths were inspired to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a very young age will be remembered in the golden words of Baloch history.

Swearing upon the Qur’an as a solemn guarantee, the state of Pakistan sent a jirga to negotiate with Nawab Noroz Khan. Trusting the sanctity of the Qur’an as a binding assurance, Nawab Noroz Khan descended from the mountains along with his son, Battay Khan, and his companions. However, rather than engaging in meaningful negotiations or addressing their legitimate demands, the state - consistent with its pattern of duplicity - arrested them.
Nawab Noroz Khan was sentenced to life imprisonment, while his son and several of his companions were condemned to death and executed in the prisons of Sukkur and Hyderabad in Sindh.
When the armed fighters came down from the mountains, they kissed the Qur’an and declared, 'We offer ourselves in its name, but we will not surrender our weapons.' The official delegation repeatedly invoked the Qur’an to reassure them that the government would honor its commitments, insisting that no greater guarantee could exist than the Holy Book itself. Yet once they had descended, those promises were broken, and they were taken into custody. They were confined in harsh prison cells dating back to the British colonial period.
Four companions of Nawab Noroz Khan - Bhawal Khan, Masti Khan, Jamal Khan, and Wali Mohammad - were hanged in Hyderabad Jail, Sindh on 15 July 1960. Their bodies were received by Mir Rasool Bakhsh, the paternal uncle of Mir Mohammad Ali Talpur. After the funeral rites were performed, the martyrs were transported to their ancestral homeland for burial.
Nawab Noroz Khan’s son, Mir Battay Khan, along with Sabzal Khan and Ghulam Rasool, was executed in Sukkur Jail, Sindh on 15 July 1960.
Nawab Nauroz Khan himself passed away on 25 December 1965 at Civil Hospital Hyderabad, Sindh, while in custody. His body was received by Mir Rafique Ahmed. Following the funeral rites, Mir Rasool Bakhsh arranged for his body to be transported to his ancestral place.
His youngest son, Jalal Khan, remained imprisoned until 1970. He was spared execution because he was a minor at the time of his arrest.
Nawab Noroz Khan and the seven martyrs were laid to rest in the Chashma area of Kalat District, a few kilometres from Kalat Bazaar in Balochistan.
Wali Mohammad was born in 1925 in the Gazan Zehri area of Khuzdar district. He was an ordinary farmer who made a living from a modest income. At the time of his execution, he was 35 years old.

Shaheed Noor Zaman alias Raees Baloch, son of Qadir Bakhsh, was a resident of Hoshab Perkotag. He joined the BLF platform to pursue national independence in November 2020. He was martyred on May 1, 2024 in Gichk Kahan. Noor Zaman began his primary education at Government High School Hoshab in 2010 but was unable to continue his education after completing the ninth grade in 2020. Shaheed Noor Zaman Baloch was a sincere, hard-working, and fighting fellow, dedicated to the freedom struggle.

On January 15, 2026, during close-quarters combat in the Battle of Kharan, four fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front - Mubeen, alias Mulla Rahmin; Abdul Raziq Baloch, alias Barag Jan; Hafeez Baloch, alias Yasir; and Mohsin Baloch, alias Mureed - laid down their lives for the homeland. 
Mohsin Baloch, alias Mureed, son of Mohammad Noor, from Khaleed, Mashkay, recently joined the Balochistan Liberation Front and opted for deployment on the mountain front. He participated in the Battle of Kharan. Martyr Mohsin's family has made extraordinary sacrifices for the Baloch national liberation movement. Two of his brothers, Abdul Latif and Nasrullah, had previously been martyred at the hands of enemy forces. Despite these profound hardships, their unwavering commitment to the movement reflects the family's deep patriotism and dedication to the nation. Martyr Mohsin was killed in an enemy drone strike in the mountain ranges following the successful completion of the Kharan operation.

On 29 November 2022, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 26 November 2022, at 6:00 am, the Pakistani army fired hundreds of missiles from Iranian kamikaze drones in and around the Siakoh area of Kahan, Kohlu district of Balochistan. Out of these, two missiles fell within the premises of a BLA camp located in Siakoh. As a result, eight freedom fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army embraced martyrdom.
Afterward, the enemy launched a large scale ground and air operation in Kahan and adjoining areas. The spokesperson stated that for a long time Pakistan and Iran have maintained joint military cooperation against the Baloch national cause, including intelligence coordination. They also exchange advanced and lethal weapons.
In the first phase of the operation, following the drone attacks, several special forces commandos were dropped from around a dozen Pakistan Army combat helicopters, and shelling began from the air. Subsequently, military troops from Kohlu, Dera Bugti, and nearby areas - consisting of more than 400 personnel - participated in the operation using several armored and other military vehicles.
As soon as the Pakistani army initiated the operation, nearby BLA camps in the area began countering the enemy’s advance from different fronts by adopting a joint defense strategy.
The combat between the enemy forces and the freedom fighters continued intermittently until the evening. As a result, the freedom fighters inflicted heavy casualties on the Pakistani forces from all sides. Breaking the army’s land and air siege through skilled combat tactics, they carried their injured comrades, along with weapons and other sensitive equipment, to safe locations.
During the conflict, after several hours of fierce resistance by the fighters, the army turned its guns toward the local population in Nissau, Siakoh, Drehis, Parhki, Jantali, and adjoining areas. The enemy set fire to many houses and severely tortured residents. Meanwhile, troops stopped two innocent Baloch pedestrians and killed them.
The organization’s fighters who embraced martyrdom were - Gahmar Khan alias Garra, Thal Khan alias Thallu, Hameed Baloch alias Sado
Shadi Khan alias Kooda, Abu Bakr Baloch alias Rehan, Jameel alias Naadi
Kareem Khan alias Jamal, Muhammad Nusrat alias Asif - The organization also rejected reports claiming that BLA fighters had been arrested during the operation. Through the media, it challenged ISPR to substantiate its narrative with concrete evidence.

On 9 September 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of ten fighters belonging to the organization. He paid tribute to the Sarmachars who were martyred while defending national liberation and their homeland, Balochistan.
- The statement identified the following fighters:
1-  Akhtar Dawood, alias Ali Sher, son of Asad Sajidi.
2- Khalil Ahmad, alias Ustad Awais, son of Sher Ahmad.
3-  Imran, alias Aajo, son of Saifullah.
4-  Hasil, alias Munir Ahmad, son of Sher Mohammad.
5- Inayatullah, alias Sher Zaman, son of Manzoor Ahmad.
6- Asad Rahim, son of Rahim Baksh.
7- Mujeeb Ur Rehman, alias Shay Mureed, son of Saeed Ahmad.

Mohammad Younis, alias Talib, son of Muhammad Umar, was a resident of Kelli Choto, Mastung. As an urban guerrilla, he carried out national duties under the command of martyred Major Chakar. He was a very brave, hardworking, and devoted fighter. Under urban guerrilla strategy, he kept close watch on enemy movement and military activity and took part very cautiously in actions against the enemy army. However, in keeping with the principles of urban guerrilla strategy, he never revealed his identity. He remained active alongside Martyr Shay Mureed on various fronts and took part in important military actions against the enemy army and its collaborator, the local death squad. He attained the exalted rank of martyrdom in August 2025 in a direct clash with the enemy in the Choto area of Mastung. This clash took place during an attack on an SHO, in which the SHO and four of his personnel were killed. The clash continued after military reinforcements arrived at the scene, in which several more army personnel were killed.

As the organization has not specified his date of martyrdom, the Baluch Martyrs Memorial uses the date of the organization’s statement as his date of martyrdom.

Zahoor Baloch, a 20-year-old labourer, the son of Arz Muhammad and a resident of Jaeen, Paroom, was forcibly abducted by a state-backed death squad in the early hours of October 20, 2025. Witnesses reported that the abductors arrived in a Surf vehicle and took Zahoor from his residence. The next morning, his mutilated body was found.
Abdul Quddous Baloch was killed by Pakistani forces in Bolan, Balochistan on 3 March 2009.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Shoaib, alias Shahzad, son of Malik Naz, was a resident of New Town, Gwadar District, Balochistan. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2024, beginning his role as an urban guerrilla. In 2025, he joined the Majeed Brigade and served on the Saheji, Mazanband, and Kulbar fronts. His last operation was Operation Herof 2, during which he was martyred in Gwadar.
Shoaib, alias Shahzad, was known for his unwavering commitment to his cause and his courage. A resident of New Town, Gwadar, he joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2024 and initially operated as an urban guerrilla against the enemy. While serving on the urban front, he demonstrated discipline, secrecy, and the ability to maintain composure under high-risk conditions—qualities essential for any urban guerrilla operative.
Following his activities on the urban front, he voluntarily offered his services to the Majeed Brigade in 2025 as part of an organizational decision. This step reflected his determination, ideological maturity, and willingness to make the ultimate sacrifice for national liberation. On the fronts of Saheji, Mazanband, and Kalbar, he gained operational experience and participated in various engagements against enemy forces, proving himself not merely as a participant but as a disciplined and responsible fighter.
During Operation Herof in Gwadar, he took part in a fidayee attack and played a decisive role against the enemy. His participation demonstrated that he was not only committed to resistance but also prepared for its highest level of sacrifice. Through his actions, Fidayee Shoaib, alias Shahzad, made it clear that Baloch youth neither bow under pressure nor retreat in fear, but remain steadfast in their commitment to the pursuit of national liberation.
His life and sacrifice have become part of the broader narrative of the Baloch national struggle, and his name now stands among those who strengthened the movement through their blood.

On 1 July 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said that BLA freedom fighters had carried out 23 successful operations in different areas of occupied Balochistan over the previous ten days. These attacks targeted the occupying forces and exploitative companies, while operations were also conducted against vehicles belonging to exploitative entities as part of the economic blockade on major highways. In these attacks, 16 personnel of the occupying army were killed and several others were injured. Meanwhile, four valiant BLA sarmachars - Raziq Baloch, alias Jahanzaib; Israr Baloch, alias Kohzad; Haji Khalil Shahwani, alias Mama Marjan; and Anwar Bilsum, alias Dr Aziz - were martyred while defending the motherland during intense clashes at various locations.

Anwar Bilsum, alias Dr. Aziz, son of Habibullah Zehri, was a resident of Baghbana, Zehri, Balochistan. He joined and served in the Urban Front from 2016 and moved to the Mountain Front in 2022. He served on the Kalat and Khuzdar fronts and was promoted to the rank of Patrol Commander. He was martyred on 26 June 2026 in Bulbul, Zehri, Balochistan.
Known among his fellow Sarmachars by the revolutionary name Dr. Aziz, Anwar Bilsum was originally from Baghbana, Zehri, Khuzdar. He was among the battle-tested BLA fighters who endured every hardship and challenge throughout his ten-year association with the organization. Owing to his ideological beliefs, he continuously adapted himself to the organization's evolving culture and changing circumstances over time. He remained steadfast in this revolutionary ideology until his final days and, with each passing day, developed into an even stronger and more committed revolutionary cadre. Among his fellow Sarmachars in the Kalat and Zehri regions, he is remembered as a kind, courageous, brave, and hardworking Sarmachar.
More than a decade ago, he began his struggle for the restoration of the independent and sovereign status of the Baloch state through the platform of the BLA. Acting on the directives of the organization's command, he served as an urban guerrilla for six years, actively participating in mine-laying operations and ambushes against the enemy in urban areas. As a Patrol Commander on the Kalat and Zehri fronts, he successfully led military operations with disciplined planning and well-organized strategy. Under his command and through his strategic leadership, the enemy suffered heavy losses on numerous occasions. Alongside his fellow Sarmachars, he also played a significant role in strengthening and expanding the organization and its capabilities in the region. He played a prominent role in several important and historic battles against the enemy.
Anwar Bilsum was not only active on the battlefield but was also known among his fellow Sarmachars as a resistance poet. Through his resistance poetry, he distinguished himself on the literary front as well. A firm believer in the philosophy of freedom or martyrdom, Anwar Bilsum stood like an iron wall against the enemy's advance in Bulbul, Zehri, on 26 June 2026. After several hours of intense fighting, he was martyred while engaging the enemy face to face. Until his final moments, he upheld the organization's position in the region as a brave fighter and Patrol Commander, thwarting the enemy's advances.
