Imtiaz Baloch, alias Haji Taukal, son of Jangiyaan Baloch, was a resident of Balicha Talukan. He became affiliated with the armed movement in 2017 and moved to the mountain fronts in 2018. He joined the BLA in 2020 and served on the Zamuran, Kulbar, Dasht, and Turbat fronts. He was also appointed as the in-charge of the urban network in the Nasirabad and Mirabad areas. Additionally, he was a member of the camp’s advisory committee and served as the commander during Operation Herof Phase II on the Rodbun front.
Imtiaz Baloch, alias Haji Taukal, was among the experienced sarmachars who remained actively involved in the armed struggle for national liberation for many years. After becoming associated with the armed movement in 2017, he soon gained recognition among his fellow sarmachars as a reliable figure because of his seriousness, organizational acumen, and combat skills. In 2018, he moved to the mountainous front, where he took part in various engagements across the regions of Zamuran, Kulbar, Dasht, and Turbat, further sharpening his abilities in the field.
Haji Taukal not only played an active role on the mountainous fronts but also carried significant responsibility in organizing urban networks. As the in-charge of the urban networks in the areas of Nasirabad and Mirabad, he carried out his duties with strict secrecy, discipline, and caution. His experience on both urban and mountain fronts made him a versatile sarmachar capable of operating effectively under different conditions.
Because of his combat capabilities and organizational insight, Haji Taukal was inducted into the organization’s frontline unit, the Fateh Squad, and was also appointed a member of the camp’s advisory committee. These responsibilities reflected that he was not only an effective fighter but also capable of contributing to planning and strategic decision-making.

Jan Mohammad, son of Qadir Baloch, was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces and their backed death squads from Jusak, Turbat, on 24 January 2026. For more than three months, his family waited in fear and pain, hoping for his safe return. Instead, on 13 May 2026, his tortured body was dumped in the Banuk-e-Chadai area of Kech. His body bore bullet wounds and clear signs of brutal torture. His grieving family identified him through his student ID card.
Jan Muhammad was a young 8th-grade student who loved books and had dreams, but they were taken away before he could even complete his education.

On a stormy night, 7 October 1992, a child was born in Gomazi, a small, remote village in Kech district, Balochistan. The proud father, Dost Mohammed, named his son Sikandar. The child grew up in the household of a social and political activist in Tump tehsil. His father was popularly known as Chairman Dost Mohammed because he had once been elected Chairman of Union Council Gomazi. He was affiliated with the Pakistan National Party (PNP) and was a close confidant of Mir Ghaus Bakhsh Bizenjo.
At a young age, Sikandar Baloch joined the Baloch Student Organization Azad (BSO-A). He was a student at Government Boys High School, Gomazi. His commitment and bold stance made him popular among students. In 2008, at the age of 16, he was elected Secretary General of BSO-A Gomazi.
As the Baloch freedom struggle gained momentum, the Pakistani state’s repression against Baloch activists intensified, and the “kill and dump” policy reached pandemic proportions. It became increasingly difficult to work openly as a political activist in the villages and cities of Balochistan. In 2013, Sikandar decided it was time to take up arms against Pakistani state subjugation. He went to the mountains and joined the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF). His energetic attitude, political awareness, commitment, and fearless actions quickly helped him rise through the ranks of the BLF to the position of Captain.
In early 2017, the Frontier Corps (FC) summoned Chairman Dost Mohammed to its camp in Tump, where he met Colonel Chandio and Major Haider Ali. They told him that although his political and social activities were within the legal framework of Pakistan, they had information suggesting he was affiliated with Sarmachars (freedom fighters) and that his son Sikandar was a member of the BLF. They demanded that he ensure his son surrendered to Pakistan. Dost Mohammed replied that his son was an adult, did not live with him, and was beyond his influence. Despite this, state authorities continued to harass the family to force Sikandar to surrender. An Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) colonel also summoned Chairman Dost Mohammed to the Turbat FC camp and later visited his home, threatening him with severe consequences if Sikandar did not surrender.
On 15 February 2017, in broad daylight, a local death squad operating under the patronage of the Pakistani state killed Sikandar’s elder brother, Tahir Baloch, in cold blood inside the Gomazi Health Center, where he worked as a male nurse. This made it clear to Chairman Dost Mohammed and his family that the state was pursuing collective punishment, targeting the entire family due to Sikandar’s resistance activities.
On 21 May 2017, the bus in which Chairman Dost Mohammed was traveling from Turbat to Karachi was stopped by Pakistani security agencies at a place called Talar. He was forcibly removed from the vehicle, and this was the last time he was seen alive. It is believed that he was handed over to Military Intelligence (MI), where he was tortured to death in custody. His mutilated body was found on 25 May 2017 in Kunchiti, Balochistan.
The suffering of this Baloch family did not end in 2017. As Balochistan continued to bleed, their struggle went on. On 1 April 2022, the family was informed that their son, Sikandar Baloch, had been martyred while fighting the Pakistani army in the mountains of Mand.
On that fateful day, Sikandar Baloch, also known as Shay Mureed, was serving as a camp commander. He and a comrade were on a routine patrol in the mountains of Mand, near Talidar, when they encountered the Pakistan army. The army was supported by the Air Force and was quickly reinforced by commandos from the Special Service Group (SSG). The two Baloch Sarmachars fought bravely, killing and injuring three SSG commandos. During the skirmish, Sikandar was severely wounded. Although they managed to break the enemy’s encirclement, he could not walk far enough to reach safety. Sikandar Baloch breathed his last in the mountains of his beloved motherland. The Pakistan army handed over his body to his family after three days. He was laid to rest as a hero beside his martyred father and brother in the family graveyard in Gomazi.

Liaquat Zahri, also known as Waseem Baloch, son of Abdul Rahman Zehri, was a resident of the Kand Kashmi area of Zehri, Khuzdar district, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in June 2024 and the Majeed Brigade in September 2024, serving on the Nagaho Front in the rank of Patrol Commander.
Liaquat Zehri was a committed soldier in the war of freedom who had made the hardships of the battlefield part of his training. For him, the struggle was an organized, continuous process carried out with complete seriousness. In his combat approach, patience, observation, and striking at the right moment were more important than haste. He was skilled in long ambushes, silent movement, and advancing through difficult terrain. His steadfastness and discipline not only kept him strong but also raised the morale of those fighting alongside him. He remained firm until the end, believing that steadfastness is the true strength on the path of freedom, and with this conviction, he carried his struggle to its conclusion.
Liaquat Zehri was forcibly disappeared on June 9, 2021, from Khuzdar along with the young Brahui-language poet Tabish Waseem. Two years later, he was released from the enemy’s torture cells and, instead of silently succumbing to the hands of the enemy, chose the path of armed resistance and joined the BLA. It is noteworthy that Liaquat’s cousin, Tabish Waseem, was killed on October 17, 2022, in Kharan in a fake encounter by Pakistan’s so-called Counter Terrorism Department (CTD), and his body was dumped.
Liaquat Zehri served as Patrol Commander on the Nagaho Front. During Operation Herof II, he was active on the Noshki Front. Fighting on the front line, he made the ground difficult for the enemy and played an important role in the success of Operation Herof Phase II. By sacrificing his life on the Noshki Front, martyr Liaquat Zehri upheld the great tradition of sacrificing one’s life for the homeland.

On 15 May 2026, a press statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that the Sarmachars (freedom fighters) of the Baloch Liberation Army carried out eighteen successful operations against the enemy across Balochistan between 4 May 2026 and 14 May 2026, resulting in the deaths of 31 personnel of the occupying Pakistani army, including a Major-rank officer, while several others were seriously injured. These attacks included seven powerful IED strikes. Additionally, the Sarmachars seized control of main highways for hours at various locations, targeting vehicles belonging to exploitative companies and occupying forces, and detaining individuals associated with these companies. In these coordinated operations, seven personnel and operatives of the state-backed “Death Squads” and Military Intelligence (MI) were also killed.
During intense clashes with the occupying forces at various locations, five BLA fighters - Ali Jan Siahpad alias Sudais, Ahsanullah alias Master Maran, Nasrullah alias Mama Zagreen, Tanveer Mengal alias Murad Khan, and Saadullah Baloch alias Wajid - embraced martyrdom while fighting valiantly against the enemy.

Tanveer Mengal, alias Murad Khan, and Saadullah Baloch, alias Wajid, were martyred on 15 April 2026 while bravely fighting against the occupying Pakistani forces during an intense clash in the Sohinda area of Zehri.
Tanveer Mengal, alias Murad Khan, son of Abdullah Mohammadzai Mengal, was a resident of the Mamatawa area of Kalat District, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2025, served on the Kalat and Zehri fronts, and was martyred on 15 April 2026 in Sohinda, Zehri.
Tanveer Mengal, alias Murad Khan, made a conscious decision last year to join the armed front through the platform of the BLA and serve the cause of national liberation, initiating a struggle against slavery. He completed his training within a short period and took part in active military operations and activities, working alongside other Sarmachars to strengthen the organization’s defensive positions in the Kalat region.
He was a Sarmachar aligned with the demands of modern warfare and carried out his duties in accordance with the organization’s policies while taking into account the requirements of war. He was an exemplary Sangat who fulfilled the responsibilities assigned by the organizational command in the best possible manner. During his deployment in Kalat and Zehri, he performed notable military duties and left a lasting practical impact.
He remained committed until the end to the philosophy and awareness under which he had joined the armed resistance. Prioritizing the defense of the homeland and freedom, he stood against the enemy until his last breath in their protection and pursuit of independence. He demonstrated that Sangats who make a conscious national and revolutionary decision remain part of the struggle until their final moments.

Zahid Askani was a prominent Baloch educator and social reformer who pioneered modern English-medium education in Gwadar, Balochistan. He is remembered for his dedication to promoting co-education, quality schooling, and awareness of the English language in a region where such opportunities were scarce.
Zahid Askani was born on January 2, 1979, in the village of Paroom, Panjgur District, Balochistan, Pakistan. He completed his early education, including graduation, in his hometown and later earned a Master’s degree in English from the University of Balochistan in Quetta.
Driven by a passion to serve his community, Askani moved to Gwadar in the late 1990s. He initially taught English at the Aga Khan School for about a year. In an era when English language proficiency was rare in Gwadar, he founded the American English Language Centre (later renamed The Oasis English Language Centre) in May 1999.
Despite significant challenges and opposition, he established The Oasis School on January 10, 2002 – the first English-medium co-educational institution in Gwadar. The school introduced innovative teaching methods, activity-based learning, talent shows, and encouraged girls’ participation in education and opportunities. Over time, The Oasis School expanded to four campuses (established in 2002, 2007, 2008, and 2013), significantly transforming access to quality education in the region.
Askani also served as Vice President and later General Secretary of the Private Schools Association in Gwadar. For over 16 years, he worked tirelessly as a teacher, administrator, and advocate for education. He was known for his punctuality, sincerity, motivational approach with students, and friendly demeanor. He often inspired others with quotes emphasizing change, optimism, and finding opportunities in challenges.
On December 4, 2014, Zahid Askani was assassinated by unknown gunmen near his school in Gwadar. He was shot multiple times and died on the spot. Although a group claimed responsibility, many sources attribute the killing to targeted attacks on Baloch intellectuals promoting progressive education, particularly co-education and women’s empowerment.
Askani was buried in his hometown of Paroom. His death was widely mourned as a profound loss to the Baloch nation. Despite his physical absence, his vision for an educated and enlightened society endures through The Oasis School system, which continues to benefit thousands.

On 6 August, 2025 the freedom fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front attacked the operatives of the death squad in Tump. In this attack, one death squad operative was injured, while in the same battle, our fearless, loyal, and brave comrade, Second Lieutenant Jabbar alias Asad, laid down his life for the motherland and attained the great rank of martyrdom.
Jabbar Baloch joined the Baloch national independence movement in 2020 and began his struggle from the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front. Initially, he was engaged in organizational activities on the urban front, and due to his intelligence, insight, and organizational understanding, he quickly emerged as an important and active comrade. In 2022, as per organizational decisions, he was transferred to a camp in the Sarawan region, where he diligently and sincerely fulfilled his responsibilities on the front lines. Later, due to further organizational needs, the martyr was transferred to the Makran region.
The martyr actively participated in several major BLF battles in Bolan, Mastung, Tump, Turbat, Mand, Kulbar, Siahji, Mazan Band, and other areas. He played a practical role in notable operations such as the capture of the Mand Matsing military post and Operation BAAM, inflicting heavy losses on the enemy.
Jabbar alias Asad Baloch, son of Deen Muhammad, belonged to the Tump area of Kech. He was an intelligent, hardworking, talented, and conscientious young man. The martyr received his early education in his native town of Tump, later moving to Quetta for further studies. He was an important and trusted technical freedom fighter of the organization, who fulfilled key responsibilities on various fronts with great technical skill. Due to his leadership qualities, intellectual maturity, and technical expertise, he quickly earned a prominent position within the organization. The martyr carried out his duties with utmost loyalty, truthfulness, and steadfastness, remaining true to his oath until his final moment.

Raza Jahangeer was born on December 1, 1987, at Tertej Awaran in the house of (martyred) Bakthiyar Baloch. Bakthiyar Baloch, Father of Raza Jahangir, was killed by Pakistani security forces backed death squad for belonging to a political family. Raza acquired his primary and secondary education in Tertej Awaran. During school life, he started writing poetry and short stories in the Balochi language. After that, Raza became a Balochi poet and writer. As in touch with literature, he staged his second name as "Jahangeer."
Further, to continue his higher studies, Raza went to Shaal {Quetta} and sought admission to Government Poly Technique College Quetta. He did a Bachelor of Arts (BA) and studied in International Relations (IR) Master Program at the University of Balochistan (UOB).
Well, it was the time when BSO strived to come out of parliamentary politics and started campaigning for the freedom of Balochistan. Raza Jahangeer, a forever devotee of his motherland, soon joined BSO. As the president of BSO Awaran Zone, he organized BSO in Awaran. Many youths inspired by him joined the national struggle on the platform of BSO Azad. Thus, very soon, he was recognized as a brilliant figure in the organization. In the same way, due to his commitment and intelligence, Raza was elected as a central committee member of BSO Azad in the 18th Central Council Session of the organization.
In 2009 the Pakistan Army and its secret agencies started the "Kill and Dump" policy against Baloch political workers. At this time, Pakistani security forces had begun a brutal crackdown on the members of BSO Azad. Hundreds of members were forcefully disappeared and then extra-judicially killed by the Pakistani security forces. Nevertheless, Raza continued his political activities when his organizational colleagues suffered regularly. However, Raza remained unbowed, and as a revolutionary, he tried very hard to fulfill his national responsibility. His hard work and commitment made him the organization's secretary general in the 19th Central Council Session.
He was arrested twice by Pakistani security forces. Many illegal First Information Reports (FIRs) were filed against him due to his political struggle. Pakistani security forces targeted and harassed his family when he did not stop his political activities. His family faced physical and economic losses and continues to suffer, even today.
Raza Jahangeer was martyred along with Imdad Bojer, a regional leader of the Baloch National Movement (BNM) in Apsar Turbat, on August 14, 2013, during a military raid by the Pakistani forces on the house of Imdad Bojer. His commitment and devotion to the Baloch cause were always remarkable, and his struggle shall continue until the freedom of Balochistan.

Salman Zehri, alias Farzind, son of Muneer Ahmad Zehri, was a resident of Norgama, Zehri, Khuzdar. He joined the BLA on 15 March 2025 and served on the Kalat front. He was martyred on 18 May 2026 in Sorab, Balochistan.
Salman Zehri, alias Farzind, regarded the defense of his homeland, its dignity, and its freedom as an inseparable part of his identity, and considered the protection of his nation a sacred national duty. Through his actions and character on the armed front, he consistently demonstrated these beliefs and remained committed to them until his final days.
Joining the struggle for the freedom of his homeland and the restoration of the Baloch national state last year, Farzind chose Nagawo as his battlefield. There, he took part in numerous significant engagements and military operations, inflicting defeats on the enemy and proving that, as long as the sons of this homeland remain alive, no occupier can breathe in peace on Baloch soil.
During the past year, he played an active role in offensive military operations against the enemy on the battlefield. Through his courage and dedication, he contributed significantly to forcing the enemy to abandon its positions and adopt a defensive posture on his respective front. He was a man of principle who not only embraced military discipline and professional standards but also embodied them in his daily life. Remaining steadfast in these ideals and upholding the same philosophy through his actions, he embraced martyrdom in Surab while delivering a heavy blow to the enemy.
He will forever remain in the memories of his comrades and in the hearts of the Baloch people for his steadfastness, perseverance, and unwavering commitment to the struggle. In the pages of history, he will be remembered as a Sarmchar who laid down his life in defense of his homeland.

Zakria Zaheer, an employee of the Balochistan Levies Force who had previously been a victim of enforced disappearance by Pakistani forces, was abducted on September 27, 2024, and later released. He was killed on January 11, 2025, near The Oasis School in Gwadar, Balochistan.

Illahi Baksh Baloch, son of Raheem Jan and a resident of Bedri Keelkor, was born in 2002 in his native area of Bedri Keelkor. He joined the Baloch liberation struggle in August 2022 through the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front. He embraced martyrdom due to a critical illness in the mountains of Balochistan, in the Keelkor area, on July 3, 2023.

Baloch Republican Army spokesperson Sarbaz Baloch, speaking via satellite from an unknown location, told the media that senior commander of the Baloch Republican Army (BRA), Haq Nawaz Bugti, son of Sher Mohammad Bugti, was martyred in a clash with Pakistani forces in the Noshki area of Balochistan on Tuesday, 13 November 2012. The Pakistani forces reportedly suffered heavy casualties and damage.
The spokesperson further said that Shaheed Haq Nawaz Bugti was a senior commander who had been affiliated with the Baloch Republican Army for many years and had led many successful missions in the past, during which he inflicted heavy losses on the occupying forces. He was the son of Baloch Republican Party central spokesperson Sher Mohammad Bugti. The Baloch Republican Army pays rich tribute to the struggle and ultimate sacrifice of Shaheed Haq Nawaz Bugti.
In a separate statement, Sher Mohammad Bugti said, “I have no sorrow over the martyrdom of my son. My son chose the path of the martyrs; he fought to defend his motherland, sacrificed his life doing so, and became a martyr. My only grief is that his martyrdom came too early; he could have made the enemies of Baloch suffer more and seen his dream of a Balochistan free from occupiers fulfilled.
If, by giving us the dead bodies of our loved ones, the enemies of the Baloch - the Pakistani occupying forces - think they can stop our path to freedom, then it is wishful thinking. We shall never withdraw from this struggle until our last drop of blood, for which our martyrs have sacrificed their lives.”

On 8 August 2016, terrorists attacked the Government Hospital in Quetta, Balochistan, in a suicide bombing and shooting. More than 70 people were killed, mainly lawyers, and more than 130 others were injured.
The majority of those killed were lawyers who had gathered at the hospital after the body of Advocate Bilal Anwar Kasi, president of the Balochistan Bar Association, was brought there. Kasi had been shot dead by a gunman near Mengal Chowk on Manno Jan Road in Quetta while he was leaving his home for his office.
Responsibility for the attack was claimed by various Islamist groups, including Jamaat-ul-Ahrar and the Islamic State Khorasan Province. However, nationalist groups have alleged that these extremist organisations are backed by the Pakistani state and its military to counter the nationalist movement in the region and exploit its natural resources.
Estimates of the death toll ranged between 70 people, while more than 120 were injured. Of those killed, 54 were lawyers. Among them, 15 were Baloch by ethnicity, while the majority were Pashtuns by ethnicity.

The Baloch advocates or lawyers who were killed are identified as follows:

01 Ghulam Farooq Badini, son of Haji Abdul Ghani.
02 Bashir Ahmed Qazi, son of Qazi Ahmed Jan.
03 Bashir Ahmad Zehri, son Haji Mir Ahmed Zehri.
04 Naseer Ahmed Langove, son Abdul Rahim.
05 Chakar Khan Rind, son of Mehmood.
06 Abdul Rashid, son of Abdul Latif.
07 Nooruddin Rakshani, son Haji Naseeruddin.
08 Muhammad Imran, son Ghulam Farooq.
09 Muneer Ahmed Mengal, son Ghulam Murtaza.
10 Sangat Jehan Jamaldini, son of Dr. Jahanzaib.
11 Mohammad Ali Satakzai, son of Taj Mohammad Khan.
12 Mehmood Ahmed Lehri, son Haji Abdul Hameed.
13 Jamil Ur Rehman, son of Qazi Abdul Hameed.
14 Amanullah Langove, son of Haji Dad Karim.
15 Sabir Ali, son of Abdul Rasheed.

Bashir Ahmed Zehri earned his LLB from Law College, Quetta. He was a philanthropist who fought cases for voiceless clients without charging any fees. He was 50 years old.

Swearing upon the Qur’an as a solemn guarantee, the state of Pakistan sent a jirga to negotiate with Nawab Noroz Khan. Trusting the sanctity of the Qur’an as a binding assurance, Nawab Noroz Khan descended from the mountains along with his son, Battay Khan, and his companions. However, rather than engaging in meaningful negotiations or addressing their legitimate demands, the state - consistent with its pattern of duplicity - arrested them.
Nawab Noroz Khan was sentenced to life imprisonment, while his son and several of his companions were condemned to death and executed in the prisons of Sukkur and Hyderabad in Sindh.
When the armed fighters came down from the mountains, they kissed the Qur’an and declared, 'We offer ourselves in its name, but we will not surrender our weapons.' The official delegation repeatedly invoked the Qur’an to reassure them that the government would honor its commitments, insisting that no greater guarantee could exist than the Holy Book itself. Yet once they had descended, those promises were broken, and they were taken into custody. They were confined in harsh prison cells dating back to the British colonial period.
Four companions of Nawab Noroz Khan - Bhawal Khan, Masti Khan, Jamal Khan, and Wali Mohammad - were hanged in Hyderabad Jail, Sindh on 15 July 1960. Their bodies were received by Mir Rasool Bakhsh, the paternal uncle of Mir Mohammad Ali Talpur. After the funeral rites were performed, the martyrs were transported to their ancestral homeland for burial.
Nawab Noroz Khan’s son, Mir Battay Khan, along with Sabzal Khan and Ghulam Rasool, was executed in Sukkur Jail, Sindh on 15 July 1960.
Nawab Nauroz Khan himself passed away on 25 December 1965 at Civil Hospital Hyderabad, Sindh, while in custody. His body was received by Mir Rafique Ahmed. Following the funeral rites, Mir Rasool Bakhsh arranged for his body to be transported to his ancestral place.
His youngest son, Jalal Khan, remained imprisoned until 1970. He was spared execution because he was a minor at the time of his arrest.
Nawab Noroz Khan and the seven martyrs were laid to rest in the Chashma area of Kalat District, a few kilometres from Kalat Bazaar in Balochistan.
Sabzal Khan Zehri was born in 1928 in the Zehri area of Khuzdar. He was a landlord by profession. At the age of 32, before his execution, he spent 14 months in solitary confinement at Kuli Camp and Sukkur Jail.
According to the book, “Sabzal was not afraid of his death because he believed that a person may die, but their memories endure in the world forever.”

Majeed Langove (Sani – The Second), son of Mohammad Khan Langove, and brother of Majeed Langove (Awal – The First) and Ameer Baksh Langove, was one of the prominent and pioneering urban guerrilla commanders of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).
He embraced martyrdom in a face-to-face battle on March 17, 2010, after an hours-long battle.
In his honor, the Baloch Liberation Army named its elite, self-sacrificing unit the Majeed Brigade after him.

Following the deadly SVBEID bombing at a Pakistani Coast Guard camp in Jiwani, Balochistan, on 3 July 2026, carried out by Attaullah Baloch, alias Ajmal, of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) Majeed Brigade Fidayee Unit, which took the lives of more than 30 Pakistani security personnel, Pakistani forces, in reaction, extrajudicially killed four Baloch on the very next day, 4 July 2026 - Mohammad Abdul Haq, son of Mohammad Murad; Chakar, son of Hassa Baksh; Peeri Assa and Shah Baksh Omar, son of Omar - in a staged encounter and claimed that they had been killed in the Jiwani attack. Later, all four were identified as previously forcibly disappeared persons.

Shah Bakhsh Omar, son of Omar, a 33-year-old fisherman and resident of Rober Jiwani, Gwadar, was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces during a late-night raid on his home on 7 January 2026. From that day onward, his whereabouts remained unknown, leaving his family in deep distress.
After nearly six months of enforced disappearance, Shah Bakhsh Omar was subjected to brutal torture. His body was later recovered, bearing extensive signs of abuse. His facial structure had been severely damaged, with multiple broken facial bones and injuries indicating extreme physical violence.

On 2 February 2022, sixteen members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayeen unit, the Majeed Brigade, carried out simultaneous attacks, nine in Noshki and seven on the Frontier Corps headquarters in Panjgur. The organization named this action "Operation Ganjal". 90 Pakistani security personnel were killed in Noshki and 105 in Panjgur.
In the BLA’s operation on the Noshki FC headquarters, 9 fidayeen participated. On 2 February 2022, Meerain Jamaldini (alias Zagrain) drove an VBEID into the camp’s main gate. Following this, Badil Baloch (alias Riyasat), Murad Aajo (alias Baba), Aneel Baloch (alias Balach), Yasir Noor (alias Saif), Aziz Zehri (alias Barag), Ibraheem Baloch (alias Kabeer), Deedag Bahar (alias Rauf) and Bilal Baloch (alias Wahid) entered the camp. As a result, 90 military personnel, including one officer, were killed, and a portion of the camp was destroyed.
The operation continued throughout the night. In the early morning of 3 February 2022, after their ammunition was exhausted, the remaining eight fidayeen took their own lives by firing their weapons.

The fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front’s special unit, the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB), attacked the Brigade Headquarters in the Nokundi area of Chagai, Balochistan, at around 8:19 PM on the night of November 30, 2025. SOB fighters successfully entered the offices and residential compound of foreign employees of the Saindak and Reko Diq projects, located in the centre of the camp, and managed to take several foreigners present in the compound hostage. The Pakistani army deployed its air force, SSG commandos, and modern heavy weapons against the fighters, but the brave Sarmachars of SOB repelled every attempt and forced them to retreat. During the operation, the Balochistan Liberation Front offered the Pakistani side an opportunity to negotiate on its demands; however, 18 hours after the offer, the Pakistani army chose to use force and began directly targeting the compound with artillery and aerial attacks. This resulted in intense clashes between the occupying forces and the fighters, which continued until the martyrdom of the SOB fighters.
In this special operation by the Saddo Operational Battalion, 76 military personnel, including foreign hostages, were killed, and 6 SOB fighters embraced martyrdom. The Nokundi operation by SOB was a continuation of the BLF’s long-standing armed resistance strategy for the independence of Balochistan and the protection of its natural wealth.
Among the martyrs were:
1 Asif alias Khalid Baloch, son of Mulla Ghulam Jan.
2 Inayat Sahil alias Gwahram Baloch, son of Ishaq Baloch.
3 Zareena Rafiq alias Tranag Maho, daughter of Master Rafiq Ahmed.
4 Nabeel Ahmed alias Ustad Adil Baloch, son of Haji Muhammad Ishaq.
5 Meer Jan Meeral alias Janan Baloch, son of Muhammad Raheem Baloch.
6 Ghulam Jan alias Istaal Baloch, son of Faiz Muhammad.
Ghulam Jan alias istaal Baloch, son of Faiz Muhammad, resident of Mehnaz Buleida, joined the BLF in February 2024 and offer his services to Saddo Operational Battalion in 2025 for a prosperous national future. He participated in SOB's first successful mission in Nokundi alongside his fellow fighters, demonstrating excellent military expertise against the enemy and embraced martyrdom while fighting courageously.

data.biography: Ahmad Khan Marri was a tribal elder. He was abducted on 30 April 2011 and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. On 2 June 2011, he was extra-judicially killed, and his body was dumped in Lasbela District of Balochistan.

On 8 August 2016, terrorists attacked the Government Hospital in Quetta, Balochistan, in a suicide bombing and shooting. More than 70 people were killed, mainly lawyers, and more than 130 others were injured.
The majority of those killed were lawyers who had gathered at the hospital after the body of Advocate Bilal Anwar Kasi, president of the Balochistan Bar Association, was brought there. Kasi had been shot dead by a gunman near Mengal Chowk on Manno Jan Road in Quetta while he was leaving his home for his office.
Responsibility for the attack was claimed by various Islamist groups, including Jamaat-ul-Ahrar and the Islamic State Khorasan Province. However, nationalist groups have alleged that these extremist organisations are backed by the Pakistani state and its military to counter the nationalist movement in the region and exploit its natural resources.
Estimates of the death toll ranged between 70 people, while more than 120 were injured. Of those killed, 54 were lawyers. Among them, 15 were Baloch by ethnicity, while the majority were Pashtuns by ethnicity.

The Baloch advocates or lawyers who were killed are identified as follows:

01 Ghulam Farooq Badini, son of Haji Abdul Ghani.

14 Amanullah Langove, son of Haji Dad Karim.
15 Sabir Ali, son of Abdul Rasheed.

Bashir completed his LLB from Law College, Quetta. He was also an active political worker and secretary at the lawyers’ wing of the National Party.
Advocate Bashir’s wife was an assistant professor at a girls’ college in Quetta. The couple strongly believed in providing the best available education for their children.
He was 46 years old.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Sarawan Raisani, alias Sarang, son of Abdul Nabi Raisani, was a resident of Hudda, Quetta. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in August 2025 and became part of the Majeed Brigade the same month. He was active on the Nagaho front and was martyred during the Dalbandin camp clash as part of Operation Herof 2.
Raised in the Hudda area of Quetta, Sarang was one of those young men who do not stand out in a crowd, yet prove themselves when the moment demands it. There was a seriousness in his nature that seemed beyond his years. When he chose to join the organization, he did not treat it as a gradual journey; instead, he placed himself directly in its most demanding test. His immediate inclusion in the Majeed Brigade reflected the intensity of his decision and the clarity of his resolve.
From the streets of Hudda, Quetta, to the front lines of Nagaho, this young man quickly assumed active operational responsibilities. During the clash at the Dalbandin camp, as the situation grew increasingly complex, Sarang chose not to remain in a zone of relative safety. He moved to the front line and continued fighting until he embraced martyrdom.
His death was not part of a dramatic tale, but a decisive moment in action. He fell while fighting, without hesitation, struck in the chest by bullets. Some lives are not long, yet they carry within them a complete and unwavering decision. Sarang’s life was such a decision.

On September 13, 2025, clashes broke out between Baloch Raaji Ajoi Sangar (BRAS) freedom fighters and the Pakistani army in the Kotan area of Zamuran while the freedom fighters were on patrol. In these clashes, four enemy army personnel were killed and several others were injured, while two freedom fighters, Sudeer alias Bramsh and Islam alias Sagaar, were martyred.

Martyr Islam alias Sagaar, son of Atta Muhammad, belonged to the Tanak area of Maskay. Islam alias Sagaar, who studied at LUAWMS University Uthal, joined the Baloch Liberation Army earlier this year and was active on the Panjgur front.

Martyr Sudeer Baloch alias Barmash, son of Pir Jan, was a resident of the Sri Kahan area of Tump, though he originally belonged to Zamuran. He joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in November last year and served on the Zamuran, Mand, and Tump fronts.

Waseem, alias Abrar, son of Faiz Mohammad Badini, was a sarmachar commander of the Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA). He was a resident of Khelan, Kharan, and was known for his dedication, resilience, and commitment to the Baloch national cause.
Although he did not receive a high level of formal education, Wasim Baloch possessed a deep understanding of the suffering and helplessness of his people. Motivated by this awareness, he abandoned the comforts of ordinary life and, in 2014, chose the path of underground armed struggle. He joined the Baloch Republican Army (BRA), later known as the Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) and formally began his resistance alongside other sarmachars. He remained active on the Rakhshan and Makuran fronts, where he played a significant role in confronting enemy forces.
For nearly a decade, Wasim served as a commander in the Rakhshan region under the BNA platform, carrying out what he regarded as national duties. During this period, multiple FIRs were registered against him by the state. His involvement in the armed struggle came at a heavy personal cost. Three of his brothers - Jafar Badini, Yousaf Badini and Parvez Badini - were forcibly disappeared by the Pakistani military. Although Jafar and Yousaf were later released, Parvez Badini remains missing.
His family was also subjected to persistent harassment by security forces and local death squads. Their home was raided on numerous occasions, and members of his family, particularly women, were subjected to physical abuse and intimidation. These actions were intended to pressure Wasim into surrendering and abandoning his struggle. He, however, remained steadfast and repeatedly stated that he would not retreat from his objective under any circumstances and would continue to fight for the freedom of his homeland until his last breath.
Wasim was martyred on 18 February 2024 during an armed clash in the Khudaan area of Mashkel while he was on an important and confidential mission. Through his life and actions, he demonstrated unwavering commitment to his cause, ultimately accepting death in the same manner as many of his fellow sarmachar comrades before him.

Cries from the killing fields of Balochistan narrate tales of human endurance - of people who faced the barbarism of occupation forces and left their mark on the hearts and minds of humanity.
One such soft-spoken and humble person was Malik Noor Ahmed Qambrani of Killi Qambrani, Sariab, Quetta. He did not receive much formal schooling but was self-taught. He became involved in politics in the late 1950s or early 1960s and soon emerged as a staunch supporter of Nawab Khair Bakhsh Marri, joining the National Awami Party (NAP).
Living a simple life and commuting through Quetta on his bicycle, he never believed that parliamentary politics under Pakistan’s corrupt system could ever provide or guarantee the rights of the Baloch nation.
When NAP was banned on February 10, 1975, by Pakistan’s Prime Minister, Zulfikar Ali Bhutto, and later when Baba Marri went into exile in Afghanistan, Mr. Qambrani did not accompany him. Instead, he stayed behind and kept the politics of resistance to Pakistani occupation alive. When Baba Marri returned from exile to Balochistan in 1992 and established the study circle “Haq Tawar,” he became an active member.
In January 2000, following the killing of Justice Muhammad Nawaz Marri, Nawab Marri was arrested along with 160 Marri tribesmen and his close confidants, including Mr. Qambrani. He was later released, but state harassment never ceased.
Mr. Qambrani was instrumental in spreading Baba Marri’s philosophy of resistance and in educating the cadre that helped revive the Baloch armed resistance movement.
On June 30, 2012, ISI operatives stabbed Malik Noor Ahmed Qambrani with a knife at his shop in the Satellite Town area of Quetta. He was rushed to the hospital, where he succumbed to his injuries. This was not an isolated incident: on June 19, 2012, the same operatives killed Master Nazir Ahmed Marri, and on February 14, 2012, the mutilated body of Haji Jan Mohammad Marri was dumped in the Windar area of Balochistan. All three were close confidants of Baba Marri and activists of Haq Tawar, which was engaged in politically educating the Baloch masses.
Political education is the death of slavery. The mission of Shaheed Malik Noor Ahmed Qambrani and his comrades - to politically educate the Baloch masses - will continue until the Pakistani occupation forces are defeated and forced out of Balochistan.

Sohbat Khan Marri, a political activist, was abducted on 28 September 2010 and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. He was later extrajudicially killed in custody on 26 September 2010, and his body was dumped in the Hub area of Balochistan.

On 22 July 2026, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) released the details of seven martyred members of the organization: Abdul Ghafoor, alias Chakar, son of Jan Mohammad; Imdad Baloch, alias Nodh, son of Rahmatullah; Hafiz Mumtaz Baloch, alias Zeerak, son of Sabir Ali; Hafiz Zaid Baloch, alias Sagaar, son of Mullah Khudadad; Yasir Baloch, alias Ajiz, son of Mohammad Ayub; Shahjan Baloch, alias Sawad, son of Ali Mohammad; and Ali Raza Baloch, alias Shayhaq, son of Haji Ali Ahmad. They were martyred in a drone strike by Pakistani forces on 29 January 2026 in the Pardan area of Panjgur District, Balochistan.

Abdul Ghafoor, alias Chakar, son of Jan Mohammad, was a resident of Kashani Bazaar, Gwargo, in the Panjgur district. By profession, he was a school teacher. He joined the BLA on 20 November 2025 and was martyred on 29 January 2026 in the Pardan area of Panjgur district, Balochistan.
Abdul Ghafoor, alias Chakar, who was a school teacher by profession, joined the Baloch Liberation Army camp in November 2025 and became part of the great caravan of freedom. In accordance with the organization’s directives, he was transferred to the Panjgur front, where he received his basic military training and later became part of the organization’s patrol unit. Although his period of service was brief, his commitment to the organization and his sincere fulfillment of every responsibility entrusted to him became a source of encouragement and morale for all his fellow fighters.
As a teacher, Chakar was aware that Balochistan was under the occupation of an unnatural state, a scourge upon humanity, which was incapable of understanding the language of knowledge and reason, nor was it familiar with the fundamental democratic principles that constitute the very foundation of any state. Therefore, Chakar decided to take part in resistance against the occupying force and joined the armed struggle. Even during this short period, he laid the foundation of the thought and courage that demand an organized and unwavering struggle against the enemy. He remained active against the enemy until his final moments, continuing his activities to the very end.
Chakar was martyred alongside his fellow Sarmachars in an enemy drone strike while on the frontline in Panjgur. He gave precedence to collective life and the cause of freedom over his personal life and embraced martyrdom while remaining steadfast in this philosophy. His martyrdom is a message to all educated teachers that we must embrace the true spirit of knowledge and, instead of serving within the administrative structure of the occupying force, work for the restoration of the Baloch state, which is the demand of our collective life.
Shaheed Saleem Afshani is among the victims of the Pakistani state’s kill and dump policy.

On 4 March 2026, a statement issued by the spokesperson of the Balochistan Liberation Front, Major Gwahram Baloch, stated that on 3 February 2026, fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front launched a coordinated operation at four different locations in Hoshap against Pakistani forces. In this organized operation, various BLF units simultaneously targeted the enemy army at four different locations in Hoshap.
In the initial phase of the operation, one unit of fighters surrounded the police station located in Hoshap Bazaar and took control of the station, holding the personnel hostage. While this unit was seizing government weapons, ammunition, and other equipment, an enemy military convoy consisting of four vehicles approached the area, resulting in an intense face-to-face clash between BLF fighters and enemy forces. During the clash, the fighters targeted and destroyed two enemy vehicles, killing several Pakistani military personnel on board.
Meanwhile, a second unit of fighters positioned at another location attacked two armored enemy vehicles with heavy weapons. Several military personnel were killed or wounded in the clash. Witnessing the defeat and retreat of their ground forces, the enemy resorted to gunship helicopters and advanced drone technology to halt the BLF fighters’ advance.
In this prolonged clash, seven BLF fighters - Shaneed Baloch (alias Shohaz Baloch), Zabad Baloch (alias Deedag), Atta Baloch (alias Obaid), Ghaffar Baloch (alias Noroz), Abdul Samad Baloch (alias Muheem Jan), Zaheer Baloch (alias Istaal), and Nadeem (alias Sahil) - fought valiantly until their last bullet and last breath and embraced martyrdom while courageously defending their motherland.
Abdul Samad Baloch, alias Muheem Jan Son of Sardu, resident of Gandhchai, affiliated with the armed struggle under the Balochistan Liberation Front platform in January 2023 and emerged as a hardworking fighter. Including his final battle against the enemy, he fulfilled his responsibilities on various fronts with great bravery and dedication.

data.biography:
On 2 June 2025 in the Mach area of Bolan, Pakistani forces and fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) came face to face when the fighters were travelling for organizational activities. At a location called Goni Para, clashes broke out between the BLA fighters and the Pakistani forces. During the confrontation, the forces deployed commandos using helicopters. In the clashes that continued for several hours, at least eight personnel of the opposing forces were killed, while five BLA fighters - Washdal, alias Mashmar; Samiullah, alias Sameer; Shehryar Shahwani, alias Chairman; Sajawal, alias Cheeda; and Nadir, alias Chiragh - achieved martyrdom.
Washdil, alias Mashmar, son of Lal Khan Sumalani, belonged to Sanjawal in the Bolan region. 22 old Washdal joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2024 and at a young age, took up arms with the resolve to fulfill what he saw as his national responsibility. He played an important role on many occasions on the Bolan front and ultimately embraced martyrdom after inflicting significant losses on the enemy.
Samiullah, alias Sameer, son of Muhammad Akram; the Shehryar, alias Chairman, son of Mehrab Khan Shahwani; and the Sajawal, alias Cheeda, son of Bawal Khan Shahwani - all belonged to Parangabad in Mastung. These three companions joined the BLA a year ago and as urban guerrillas, participated in several successful operations. Always active in striking the enemy and fulfilling organizational duties, they were present on every front. Their lives, devoted to the cause of national freedom, have become a guiding light for Baloch youth.
Nadir, alias Chiragh, son of Mazar Khan Lehri, was originally from Narmuk in the Kalat region but was residing in Quetta. In his guerrilla role, he was highly organized, vigilant, and steadfast, confronting the enemy with courage. Constantly engaged in organizational work, he remained firm in his responsibilities until his final breath.

On September 24, 2025, Pakistani genocidal forces conducted a raid on a residential house in the Dalbandin area of Chagi District, Balochistan. During the operation, former chairman of the Baloch Students Organization (Pajjar), a political activist and Advocate, Zubair Baloch, and his companion, Nisar Jan Baloch, were killed.
The incident has sparked widespread condemnation from political parties, student groups, human rights organizations, and legal bodies across Balochistan.

On June 3, 2025, 17-year-old Ehsan Syed, son of Syed Manzoor Shah and a resident of Mastung, was fatally shot by personnel of the Frontier Corps (FC) near the Lak Pass Tunnel checkpoint. Ehsan had travelled to Quetta for Eid-ul-Azha shopping and was returning home when FC troops reportedly opened fire without warning or provocation.
Initially, the local administration informed the family that Ehsan had been injured in a road accident. However, upon reaching the site, his father discovered that his son had died as a result of direct gunfire from security forces.
In a press conference held at Sarawan Press Club in Mastung, Ehsan’s father publicly refuted the official narrative and demanded accountability. He stated that the authorities deliberately misled the family and attempted to cover up the incident by mischaracterizing it as a traffic accident.

data.martyrdomPlace: Noshki and Kharan mountainous area, Balochistan
data.biography:
In a face to face battle with the Pakistani military and its agents in the mountainous regions of Noshki and Kharan on 24 September 2021, more than a dozen enemy personnel were killed, whereas six freedom fighters, including five members of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), also embraced martyrdom.
The battle commenced early Friday morning in Siyah Lop, near Baddo Dor, when enemy forces attempted to encircle a patrolling party of Baloch freedom fighters. In the face-to-face battle that lasted for more than four hours, scores of enemy personnel were killed and injured. Five freedom fighters of the BLA and one freedom fighter of the United Baloch Army (UBA), while evacuating their comrades from the battle zone, embraced martyrdom.
The fallen comrades include Commander Ganjal alias Comrade Mazar, Nazeer alias Sangar, Faisal alias Yasir, Kaleem alias Bolani, and Rehan alias Mehrwaan, all members of the Baloch Liberation Army. A member of the United Baloch Army, Nodaan alias Hammal, bravely fought alongside BLA comrades and embraced martyrdom.
Nazeer alias Sangar, son of Mohammad Qasim Meerwani Baloch; Faisal Rodeni alias Yasir; and Kaleem alias Bolani, son of Maqbool Ahmed Reki, all of whom belonged to Soorab town, had joined the BLA three years ago. After serving for several years in the urban units of the BLA, they were deployed to the mountainous battlefronts following an organisational decision.

Janzaib Baloch, son of Ali and a 20 year old resident of Soorag Niyam Patak Essai in Panjgur district, Balochistan, was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 13 October 2024 by state backed death squads operating under the direct command of Pakistani forces. His mutilated body was recovered in Panjgur on 20 February 2025. According to reports, it bore clear signs of severe torture, indicating that he had been brutally abused before his killing.

On 31 December 2025, a statement released by the spokesperson of the Balochistan Liberation Front, Major Gwahram Baloch, stated that five of its fighters embraced martyrdom and sacrificed their lives for the homeland in an enemy drone strike in Kalat on 25 December 2025.
The martyrs include Abdul Ahad Dehwar alias Gazzain, son of Hamayun Dehwar, resident of Keli Kahriz Mastung; Israr Ahmad alias Ibrar, son of Hussain, resident of Gargina Mastung; Shoaib Ahmad alias Subedar, son of Muhammad Ali, resident of Jiwa Khuzdar; Obaidullah Siyahpad alias Sabzu, son of Peerjan, resident of Kharan; and Faisal Badini alias Qazi, son of Muhammad Ibrahim, resident of Kharan.
Obaidullah Siyahpad alias Sabzu, son of Peerjan and resident of Kharan, officially joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in November 2025. Prior to this, as a sympathizer of the BLF, he assisted fighters in organizational activities in Kharan city. Although he joined the training camp for a short period, during this brief time he proved to be a brave, hardworking, and disciplined fighter. He was martyred in the Kalat drone strike on 25 December 2025.

On 11 May 2011 on the bank of the Rakhshan River at Damb, Panjgur, some labourers spotted a body in a shallow ditch. When residents of the area conducted a search, they found two more mutilated bodies. They were later identified by their relatives as Agha Abid Shah, Master Abdul Sattar Baloch, and Safeer Baloch.
Agha Abid Shah was born on 1 October 1980 to Dr. Syed Ali, also known as Gul Agha, in Ghareeb Abad, Chitkan, Panjgur. He completed his master’s degree in Sociology from the University of Balochistan. During his student life, he was elected Vice-Chairman of BSO (Azad). After completing his studies, he joined the World Health Organization (WHO) as Deputy Coordinator for Panjgur district.
Agha Abid Shah, Master Abdul Sattar Baloch, and Safeer Baloch were abducted by state agencies on 15 August 2010 from the vicinity of the District Headquarter Hospital, Panjgur. Panjgur erupted in agitation, and for a week the entire district remained shut down. Both male and female protesters in Panjgur besieged the office of the Deputy Commissioner against this travesty of justice and the enforced disappearance of the three Baloch political workers.
The Frontier Corps (FC) used excessive force to suppress the protest, and on 17 August 2010 opened fire on the protesters, killing one protester, Hussain Baloch.

data.biography:
Operation Dara-e-Bolan, which began on 29 January 2024 continued for two days until 31 January 2024 and was successfully concluded after achieving its intended objectives. A total of 385 Sarmachars from four different units of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) participated in Operation Dara-e-Bolan. Among them were 12 Fidayeen from the BLA’s Majeed Brigade. The other participating units included the Fateh Squad, the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS) and the Intelligence Wing.
Operation Dara-e-Bolan commenced on the evening of 29 January 2024 at 9:00 pm local time and continued for two days. After achieving the desired results, the BLA’s Senior Command Council announced the conclusion of Operation Dara-e-Bolan on 31 January 2024 at 7:00 pm and issued instructions to all units to vacate their positions and report back to their base camps.
During the operation, BLA Sarmachars took complete control of an area within a 70 kilometre radius, including Mach city and the strategically important National Highway N-65. Over the course of Operation Dara-e-Bolan, a total of 78 enemy personnel were killed. These included 45 Frontier Corps (FC) personnel who were killed within the first three hours of the operation in Mach city; 10 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on an army camp at the Pir Ghaib Bolan location; 4 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on a military convoy at the Gokurt Mach location; 12 regular army personnel who were killed on 30 January when Majeed Brigade Fidayeen eliminated them and entered the FC headquarters; and at least 5 SSG commandos who were targeted and killed by the Fidayeen on 31 January 2024. In addition, two police personnel were also killed, including one Station House Officer (SHO).
A large number of Levies and police personnel were captured by the BLA during the operation; however, as they were Baloch, they were released. During Operation Dara-e-Bolan, 13 brave fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army attained martyrdom. Of these, 12 martyred Sarmachars belonged to the Majeed Brigade Fidayeen, while one martyred Sarmachar was from the BLA’s Fateh Squad.
The martyred Sarmachars were: Qasim Baloch, Saddam Hussain, Salal Baloch, Farooq Baloch, Atta Baloch, Hammal Momin, Zeeshan Zehri, Nadir Bangulzai, Nizam Baloch, Zeeshan Baloch, Jamal Baloch, Wadood Satakzai, and Kashif Shahwani.
Zeeshan Zehri, alias Saeen Beebarg, son of Dr. Khan Mohammad Zahri, belonged to the Peer Sher Zehri area of Khuzdar. He joined the Baloch armed struggle in 2021 and offered his services to the BLA - Majeed Brigade in 2022. He was an educated political activist with strong national consciousness and an exceptionally brave national fighter. He was also a Hafiz of the Qur’an and was among those fidayeen who fought the enemy until the very end.

On 31 January 2012 in Karachi, Zamur Domki (née Bugti, aged 34) sister of Brahamdagh Bugti, sister-in-law of Mehran Baluch and granddaughter of Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti, together with her 13 year old daughter Janna Domki, were visiting the house of Zamur’s maternal uncle after attending a cousin’s wedding at the Carlton Hotel in Defence Housing Authority (DHA), Karachi. They were travelling in a black Toyota sedan (registration: ANR-353) bearing a Balochistan MPA number plate, accompanied by their driver, Barkat Baloch, and a 12-year-old daughter of the household helper.
Between 1:00 and 1:30 AM on 31 January 2012 shortly after leaving the uncle’s house, a black car intercepted their vehicle near Gizri Bridge in Clifton. A man dressed in a black shalwar kameez, believed to belong to Pakistan’s intelligence agencies (ISI and MI), jumped out and opened fire on the driver, Barkat Baloch, as the car attempted to escape. Barkat Baloch was killed instantly by multiple gunshot wounds to the head.
The assailant then opened the rear door. At that moment, two motorcycles arrived and positioned themselves on either side of the car. Zamur Bugti pleaded with the gunman to spare her daughter and offered her own life instead. Ignoring her pleas, the killer moved to the front passenger seat and fired several shots into Janna Domki’s chest and neck.
Zamur Bugti was forced to watch her daughter being murdered. She was then shot more than a dozen times in the head, face, and neck at point-blank range and left dying in a pool of blood. Throughout the attack, police personnel reportedly watched from a distance without intervening.
Zamur Bugti was the daughter of the late Rehan Bugti, the elder sister of Baloch Republican Party leader Brahamdagh Bugti, and the wife of Bakhtiar Domki, a former Member of the Provincial Assembly (MPA) of Balochistan who was then part of the opposition in the provincial assembly. Bakhtiar Domki is also a maternal grandson of Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti.
Bakhtiar Domki has directly accused state intelligence agencies of carrying out the targeted killings.
Zamur Bugti had received death threats prior to the incident. Several other Baloch women related to prominent Baloch nationalist leaders have also received similar threats in the past.

Hamid Baloch, son of Ismail Baloch, was from Turbat, district Kech, Balochistan. He was a mechanic by profession. He was abducted on 16 September 2010 and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. On 18 November 2010, his mutilated body, along with the body of Lala Hameed, who had been disappeared a few months earlier, was found in Hironk, a village 55 kilometers from Turbat. The bodies of both young activists were discovered with a note attached that read: “Eid gift for the Baloch nation.”

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Abdul Waheed Qalandarani, alias Dostain, was a resident of Shahdadkot, Sindh. He joined the BLA in 2023 and remained active on the Bolan and Kalat fronts. He was martyred on the Noshki front during Operation Herof Phase 2.
Abdul Waheed Qalandarani, known among his Sarmachar comrades as "Dostain", was a sentinel of those undying passions that remain connected to one's roots regardless of geographical boundaries. Although he was born and lived in the city of Shahdadkot, Sindh, the Baloch blood in his veins constantly echoed the call of his ancestral land. Dostain's personality reflected the truth that no matter where a Baloch may be in the world, his heart beats for the freedom of his motherland. When he chose the path of armed struggle by joining the BLA in 2023, it was a testament to his profound consciousness that his true identity and survival lay within the rugged mountains of Balochistan.
Dostain proved himself on the arduous paths of Bolan and on the freezing fronts of Kalat. He was a warrior who bid farewell to the comforts of Sindh to answer the call of his soil, embracing the difficult life of the mountains. When "Operation Herof" commenced, Dostain played a leading role on the Noshki front. During intense clashes, he embraced martyrdom while successfully halting the enemy's advance and providing defensive support to his comrades. Abdul Waheed Qalandarani's sacrifice serves as a beacon for all Baloch who, despite being away from their land, cherish the dream of its independence.

On September 16, 2025 the Balochistan Liberation Front carried out an ambush on the convoy of the occupying army near Kunchati Cross in Dasht, Kech. The military convoy consisted of several buses and three escort vehicles. As a result of the Sarmachars’ attack, a clash erupted which continued for 45 minutes, during which at least 4 enemy personnel were eliminated and three were wounded. In this clash, BLF comrades Sarmachar Atiq alias Captain Miran and Sarmachar Shehak alias Ashob fought bravely and attained martyrdom.

In 1838, the British sent a force led by Alexander Burnes to reinstate Shah Shuja Durrani as the king of Afghanistan by deposing Amir Dost Mohammad Khan. To reach Afghanistan, they needed passage through Balochistan, particularly the Bolan Pass. However, Khan Mehrab Khan refused to allow the British to use his land to attack a neighboring country. The British sent Lieutenant Leach to negotiate with the Baloch government, but the Khan stood firm. When British forces reached Shaal via Bolan, some patriotic Baloch, without the Khan’s knowledge, attacked British troops out of nationalist sentiment and a desire to protect their homeland.
After toppling Amir Dost Mohammad Khan, the British Governor General of India, Lord Auckland, ordered an attack on Balochistan. In 1839, around 7,000 British troops marched from Shaal to attack the Baloch Meeri (capital). Anticipating an invasion, Khan Mehrab Khan declared war and sent messages to tribal leaders, but many saw the British as allies rather than invaders and chose to collaborate with them rather than defend their land. When Khan Mehrab Khan gathered his resistance fighters, the number of loyal warriors had dwindled to only 700 due to the short sightedness of many tribal chiefs. Nevertheless, Mehrab Khan was determined to fight. At his court, a respected figure, Akhund Muhammad Siddiq, advised him that he was not in a position to wage war at that time. He suggested that the Khan should leave Kalat with his companions, regroup and strengthen his forces, and then launch an attack against the British when the time was right, on 13 November 1839, the British forces launched an attack on Kalat, and a fierce battle ensued. During the fighting, Khan Mehrab Khan Baloch was martyred by a British bullet.

Among those martyred alongside him were:

Diwan Bacha Mal, Minister of Finance

Diwan Khem Chand

Diwan Asardas Mukhi, from the Hindu Panchayat of Kalat

Abdul Karim Raisani, brother of Sardar Asad Khan Raisani

Sardar Wali Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (maternal uncle of Martyr Amir Mehrab Khan)

Mir Taj Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (cousin of Mehrab Khan)

Mir Muhammad Ali Shahizai Mengal

Mir Fazal Muhammad Lehri, brother of Sardar Muhammad Khan Lehri

Sardar Zaman Khan Pandrani

Mir Dad Karim Chandozai Shahwani

Mir Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Mir Badal Khan, brother of Sardar Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Khan Muhammad Dehwaar, Arbab-e-Kalat.

Mir Nabi Bakhsh Jatoi, from the Narmak region of Kalat

Mir Qaiser Khan Bizenjo

Mir Shah Dost Bizenjo

Muhammad Raza Waziri Khel

Noor Muhammad Shahizai, son of Polat Sagaar Sarmastani, in charge of the armory

Taj Muhammad Shagasi

On 8 August 2016, terrorists attacked the Government Hospital in Quetta, Balochistan, in a suicide bombing and shooting. More than 70 people were killed, mainly lawyers, and more than 130 others were injured.
The majority of those killed were lawyers who had gathered at the hospital after the body of Advocate Bilal Anwar Kasi, president of the Balochistan Bar Association, was brought there. Kasi had been shot dead by a gunman near Mengal Chowk on Manno Jan Road in Quetta while he was leaving his home for his office.
Responsibility for the attack was claimed by various Islamist groups, including Jamaat-ul-Ahrar and the Islamic State Khorasan Province. However, nationalist groups have alleged that these extremist organisations are backed by the Pakistani state and its military to counter the nationalist movement in the region and exploit its natural resources.
Estimates of the death toll ranged between 70 people, while more than 120 were injured. Of those killed, 54 were lawyers. Among them, 15 were Baloch by ethnicity, while the majority were Pashtuns by ethnicity.

The Baloch advocates or lawyers who were killed are identified as follows:

On 6 November 2026, the Baloch Liberation Army's media channel, Hakkal, published the biographies and details of six martyrs associated with the organization.

Among them, three fighters - Muneer Ahmad Jattak, alias Noora, son of Habib Khan Jattak; Shahzaib Bangulzai, alias Ehsan, son of Samiullah Bangulzai; and Fareed Langove, son of Ghulam Nabi Langove - were martyred on 20 October 2026 in the Rodinjo area of Kalat District.

Two other fighters, Parvez Ahmad Mohammad Hassni, alias Qadir, son of Shekari Mohammad Khan Mohammad Hassni, and Noman Jamaldini, alias Comrade Sameer, son of Agha Mohammad Jamaldini, were martyred on 24 October 2026 in the Gidar area of Surab.

The sixth fighter, Aurangzaib Langove, alias Asif, son of Hameedullah Langove, was martyred on 24 October 2026 in the Manguchar area of Kalat District.

Muneer Ahmad Jattak, alias Noora, son of Habib Khan Jattak, was a resident of Mashakal, Gazk, Kalat. He joined the BLA in December 2025 and served on the Kalat front. He was martyred on October 20, 2026, in the Rodinjo area of Kalat District, Balochistan.

Muneer Ahmad, a native of Kalat, was a brave comrade brimming with revolutionary thought and awareness. It was this intellectual and political awareness that led him, last year, to decide to join the armed resistance against the enemy and drive them out of Balochistan. After joining the BLA in 2025, he was transferred to a training camp, where he completed his basic training courses. Upon completing his training, he became actively engaged on the Kalat front.

On the Kalat front, Comrade Muneer Ahmad displayed extraordinary bravery and courage, carrying out every assigned task with the utmost valour and dedication. From actively participating in organizational activities to taking part in deadly strikes against the enemy, he inflicted severe losses on the enemy at every turn. He remained committed to the very purpose for which he had joined the struggle until the final days of his life.

On 20 October 2026, while confronting the enemy with the utmost bravery and courage, he was martyred. The sacrifices of Martyr Muneer Ahmad for the cause of national liberation will forever be remembered in the pages of history.

It all started with a cell phone video. Stormed by comments from angry Baloch Facebook and Twitter users, the video went viral within hours of its upload. It featured the testimony of a sexual assault victim, Shakila Basharat, pleading for justice.
Shakila, a housewife and a mother, recounts the horrific attack carried out by a powerful local figure, Noor Ahmed.
“He broke into our house late at night and started beating me. I cried, but he was drunk and didn’t listen,” Shakila says.
Pampered by his elder brother, Zahoor Buledi, a former minister of Balochistan, Noor Ahmed is also known to run a local death squad in Buleda under the patronage of the powerful Pakistan Army.
“He hit me on the head with the butt of a gun. When I regained consciousness a few moments later, he was touching me everywhere. He even forced me to drink alcohol. I kept resisting. Then he poured alcohol over my clothes,” Shakila recalls.
The low-quality video of Shakila’s testimony continued to circulate on various social networking sites for days. It sparked heated debates across Baloch circles, leaving many outraged. Nothing like this had happened before, where technology was used so effectively to highlight the plight of a helpless woman—a sexual assault victim—in a society where women are regarded with the highest respect.
As the shameful act drew widespread condemnation, the video caused great unease and anxiety for Noor Ahmed.
Frustrated, Noor Ahmed tasked his men with finding the person responsible for recording Shakila’s testimony. After days of interrogating various sources, they identified Gulzar.
Gulzar Ryaz, 35, a talented poet with a well-regarded social reputation, became Noor Ahmed’s target as he sought revenge.
A fun-loving, caring, and open-hearted man, Gulzar was also known for his affection for animals, often seen caring for dogs in his neighborhood. He lived a simple and honest life.
After learning about Shakila’s ordeal, Gulzar chose not to remain silent but to speak out for justice. He knew Noor Ahmed was powerful and that his actions could cost him his life. Nevertheless, he actively campaigned to raise awareness about Shakila’s case across different platforms. Gulzar could not stand by and watch a helpless woman suffer in silence. He publicly named and shamed Noor Ahmed as a sex offender.
Finally, on the evening of June 18, Noor Ahmed received information that Gulzar was present at a local tea house in the Koh-e-Pusht area of Buleda’s main town. Noor decided to act personally.
At around 4 p.m. local time, Noor and his men arrived at the scene. He dragged Gulzar out of the tea house in front of dozens of eyewitnesses. Noor Ahmed was heard swearing at him, repeating: “The time has come to pay the price for being so courageous.”
In a brutal act, Noor fired multiple rounds from his AK-47 at Gulzar, killing him on the spot.
Gulzar’s murder left the local community in deep shock. However, there was little anyone could do; Noor Ahmed’s death squad is an open secret.
Gulzar gave his life fighting against injustice for a helpless woman who still awaits justice. Noor Ahmed continues to roam free.

Dilwash Baloch, alias Diljaan, son of Mulla Rahmatullah, was born on 13 February 1978 in Dalsar, Mand tehsil, Turbat district, Balochistan. He completed his education up to matriculation. Even as a student, he was a highly talented painter.
Martyr Diljaan Baloch fought alongside Dr Khalid Baloch in numerous battles during the Baloch freedom struggle. He was an exceptionally skilled marksman and brought the enemy to its knees hundreds of times.
In the early 2000s, during the initial years of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF), when state forces launched brutal military operations in Siyahji and Talaar, Baloch resistance fighters found themselves surrounded by the enemy. It was in this critical moment that Martyr Diljaan Baloch, along with his comrades, employed such daring and ingenious guerrilla tactics that no parallel can be found in the entire history of the struggle.
On 8 August 2007, around noon, in the jungles of Souraap in the Mand area, Pakistani forces completely surrounded their position and demanded their surrender. Refusing to surrender, Diljaan and his comrade Dr Khalid Baloch put up brave and fearless resistance. The intense fighting continued until 4 p.m. In the end, both Dilwash and his comrade Dr Khalid Baloch embraced martyrdom.
The next morning, their bodies were brought to Tump police station.
At 9 a.m., the bodies were handed over to the family. Dr Khalid Baloch was buried in the Tump graveyard, while the mortal remains of Martyr Dilwash Baloch were taken to his ancestral graveyard in Mand-Sooro and laid to rest beside his father.

Abdul Wadood Satakzai, alias Shehak, belonged to the city of Mach. In 2021, he was forcibly disappeared by the occupying forces and after months of torture in detention cells, was released.
