data.biography:
Shehak Shah, alias Nako Talang, had been engaged in the armed struggle for freedom under the banner of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) since 2013. He was extremely brave and also an aware, revolutionary young poet. He served on the fronts of Tump, Dasht, Balgatar, Buleda, and Zamuran. Through his ability, sincerity, and tireless dedication, he had attained the rank of Second Lieutenant.
On 5 October 2021 at around 2 PM, he and one of his comrades were on a routine patrol in the mountainous area of Nag in Anjeer Kan Kulbar when members of a state sponsored death squad, who had already laid an ambush, opened fire on them. This led to a long and bloody confrontation. In this clash, Second Lieutenant Shehak Shah, alias Nako Talang, son of Diljan, resident of Tump Sarenkahn fought with exceptional courage. He managed to pull his comrades out of the enemy’s encirclement and he himself was martyred while defending the Baloch homeland. During the battle, the Pakistani Army also arrived to support the death squad.

On 9 September 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of ten fighters belonging to the organization. He paid tribute to the Sarmachars who were martyred while defending national liberation and their homeland, Balochistan.
- The statement identified the following fighters:
1-  Akhtar Dawood, alias Ali Sher, son of Asad Sajidi.
2- Khalil Ahmad, alias Ustad Awais, son of Sher Ahmad.
3-  Imran, alias Aajo, son of Saifullah.
4-  Hasil, alias Munir Ahmad, son of Sher Mohammad.
5- Inayatullah, alias Sher Zaman, son of Manzoor Ahmad.
6- Asad Rahim, son of Rahim Baksh.
7- Mujeeb Ur Rehman, alias Shay Mureed, son of Saeed Ahmad.
8- Sahil, alias Arman, son of Peeral.
9- Javed, alias Murshid.
10- Mohammad Younis, alias Taleb, son of Mohammad Omar.

Sahil, alias Arman, son of Peeral, resident of Kaisak, formally joined the Baloch national liberation struggle through the BLF platform on 29 November 2025. During military training he gained organizational discipline, ideological maturity, and a basic grounding in the principles of warfare, after which he moved to the regular front with firm resolve. He was a sincere, hardworking, fearless, and diligent fighter. In this brief period, he carried out various military and national duties during guerrilla warfare on Balochistan’s difficult fronts, fulfilling every organizational duty faithfully. He remained constantly engaged in the performance of national duties and devoted every moment of his life to the nation. He held to these national principles until his martyrdom.

As the organization has not specified his date of martyrdom, the Baluch Martyrs Memorial uses the date of the organization’s statement as his date of martyrdom.

On 21 August 2026, Pakistani forces conducted an aerial drone strike on a garden located in the Gaith area of Khadkucha, Mastung District, Balochistan. The strike resulted in the martyrdom of four orchard workers - Gul Khan Mughairi, Imran Baloch, Obaidullah Baloch and Jahanzaib Abdo - and left three others - Ali Raza Mengal, Naseebullah Abdo and Khalid Hussein - badly injured.
Rescue personnel transferred the dead and injured to Shaheed Nawab Ghaus Bakhsh Raisani Memorial Hospital in Mastung, where the wounded received treatment.
All the victims were reportedly associated with Haji Shahr in Kachhi District. Rescue sources said all of the casualties were working as labourers in the orchard at the time of the incident.
The reported strike also follows other incidents in which civilians were reportedly killed during Pakistani military operations or aerial attacks in Balochistan.
On 12 August 2026, reports emerged from Sorab’s Goandhan area alleging that an aerial bombardment had killed innocent civilians, including women and children.
The Mastung incident also comes weeks after reports from Khuzdar District alleging that four civilians were killed in a reported drone strike on a house in the Moola Manjalo area.

Ameer Abbas Kurd, alias Sajid, son of Bahar Kurd, was a resident of the Marao area of Mastung. He joined the BLA as an urban guerrilla in June 2024 and moved to the mountain front in October 2025. He served on the Mastung and Kalat fronts and was martyred on 19 September 2026 in the Shirnaap area of Mastung, Balochistan.
After enduring the worst torture and torment and feeling enslaved in the enemy’s torture chambers for four months, Ameer Abbas Kurd of Maro, Mastung, regarded national liberation as the ultimate goal of Baloch collective life and, upon his release in 2024, made the historic decision to join the Baloch Liberation Army. After joining the organization, he took on his first responsibilities on the urban front, where, carrying out organizational orders, he performed important and impactful work as an urban guerrilla. During his time on the urban front, he provided the organization with essential and important information on multiple occasions, which proved highly useful in its operational activities.
He served on the urban front for two years with the utmost integrity and then, by the organization’s decision, joined the war front this year. After completing his training, he was deployed to the battle lines. He had been carrying out his duties on the front lines for the past few months as an outstanding and highly capable fighter. He first fulfilled his combat duties in Quetta and later in Mastung, taking part in inflicting several significant blows on the enemy in the field. On September 19, 2026, he was martyred while carrying out his combat duties and joined the ranks of the great fighters who will be remembered as heroes in the nation’s history.

On March 8, 2023, Pakistani drones fired three missiles at a Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) guerrilla camp in the mountain range between Hoshap and Pasni. Following the strike, Pakistani forces began landing commandos around the camp from helicopters. In the missile attack, the camp commander, Hasil Baloch, along with four other fighters, was martyred. The remaining Sarmachars fought bravely in close combat, killing several commandos of the occupying forces before they themselves were martyred in the great cause of freedom for their homeland.
The Sarmachars who were martyred are:
Hasil (alias Doda), Wasdil (alias Jami), Nizam (alias Noshad), Waqas (alias Miras), Khalid (alias Kiyya), Shah Fahad (alias Aslam), and Ilyas Baloch (alias Rahmdil).
Martyr Mohammad Ilyas (alias Rahmdil), son of Zabad and resident of Talsar, Hoshap, began his political struggle for Baloch national liberation in 2014. In 2018, he joined the armed resistance. He was an educated young man with strong combat skills. One of his brothers, Shaheed Mohammad Jan, was martyred in 2017 during a clash with the enemy at Shadi Kaur. Another brother, Shaheed Amir Bakhsh, was martyred in 2021 by death squad operatives after being abducted from a local vehicle in Heronk.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
In Gwadar, nine Fidayeen of the BLA Majeed Brigade were divided into two units and took part in the operation. The first unit, which included Fidayeen Hawa Baloch (alias Droshum), Yahya Lal (alias Lashari), Adnan Arman (alias Changaiz), and Yousif Baloch (alias Yagi), attacked the compound of the occupying Pakistani intelligence agencies, resulting in the elimination of 12 personnel. Women and children in residential quarters near the compound were provided safe passage; however, the occupying army later martyred these same civilians by opening fire.
About forty minutes later, occupying forces advanced toward the compound, leading to clashes that continued until the evening. In these clashes, more than 24 personnel were eliminated, and three military vehicles, including an armored vehicle, were destroyed.
The second squad, which included Fidayeen Kambar Ismail (alias Sarbaz), Khurshid KB (alias Arman), Waseem Baloch (alias Kareem), Shoaib Baloch (alias Shehzad), and Yasir, took up strong positions in Port Bazaar near Gwadar Port. After announcements were made in mosques, freedom fighters went to the bazaar, met the public, and held political discussions. After repelling the advance of occupying forces in the city, the freedom fighters later advanced toward the port and fired several rockets that hit their targets. Clashes continued until the next day, eliminating more than 19 personnel.
Yahya Lal, known as Lashari, a 23-year-old resident of Kalleri in Panjgur district, joined the BLA in March 2023 and the Majeed Brigade in April 2023. He was among those young men who carried both a pen and a decision in their hands. Hailing from Parom Kalleri in Panjgur, the twenty-three-year-old was not merely a fighter but a thinking individual. He wrote and he fought. Poetry and writing were his means of expression, yet when he joined the BLA in March 2023, he chose to translate thought into action.
Serving initially as an urban guerrilla, he undertook early responsibilities with discipline and focus, and within a short period his seriousness and organizational understanding led to his induction into the Majeed Brigade.
During the Gwadar operation in Operation Herof, he served as the Second Operation Commander. He was involved in planning while also standing alongside his fellow Sarmachars on the ground.

During Operation Herof Phase 2, the BLA’s Majeed Brigade Fidayeen targeted the main camp and the Coast Guard camp of the Pakistan Navy in the coastal city of Pasni, Balochistan. The operation was initiated by Fazal, alias Miraan, who rammed a vehicle loaded with explosives into the main entrance gate of the Navy camp. The explosion instantly killed at least seven personnel stationed at the gate.
Immediately after this initial attack, six Fidayeen - Yasma Baloch, alias Zareena; Waseem Baloch, alias Zirbaar; Zaid Zamurani, alias Abram; Sabzal Baloch, alias Kohsar; Diljan Baloch, alias Ameer Ajoo; and Operation Commander Shabeer Baloch, alias Kiya - entered the camp and took up positions. Fierce clashes with the occupying Navy and Navy special units inside the camp continued for more than five hours, during which at least 33 Pakistani personnel were killed. This operation not only inflicted significant casualties on the enemy but also dealt a severe blow to the defense structure of the Navy camp.
Before becoming part of the movement, Shaheed Fidayee Shabeer Baloch was a fisherman by livelihood, closely connected to the sea and the coastal life of Pasni. He joined the Movement in 2019 and later became part of the Majeed Brigade in July 2024. Known as a capable and disciplined fighter, he rose through the ranks not by position but through natural ability, field experience, and personal resolve.

During Operation Herof, Shabeer Baloch served as the operational commander on the Pasni front. His leadership was shaped by courage, clarity, and an instinctive understanding of the battlefield. From a fisherman to a frontline commander, his journey reflected a transformation driven by commitment, skill, and an unwavering sense of responsibility.

On 22 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch stated that BLF fighters had formally launched Operation Almas with a large-scale, coordinated attack on the main camp of the Pakistani army’s Frontier Works Organization (FWO) at Gwadar Zero Point. Fighters from the BLF’s special Saddo Operational Battalion, alongside members of other units, are participating in this major military engagement. The battle continued into the following day, 23 October 2026, with loud explosions and intense gunfire heard from the location. On 23 October 2026, a statement issued by the BLF spokesperson announced the completion of Operation Almas. The statement claimed that dozens of military and intelligence personnel had been killed, the hub of colonial projects had been destroyed, and army and Frontier Corps posts had been wiped out. It declared that the historic Operation Almas had concluded after achieving all its intended objectives. Operation Almas was carried out in Gwadar and the surrounding areas. It has formally concluded after reportedly achieving all its planned strategic, military, and economic objectives following prolonged and intense clashes. During this wide-ranging operation, the occupying Pakistani army and intelligence network suffered what the statement described as irreparable human and material losses. The BLF’s self-sacrificing fighters targeted the Frontier Works Organization’s (FWO) main camp, destroying a key centre for the implementation of colonial projects, particularly in Gwadar and across Makuran. This, the statement asserted, demonstrated to the world that, without the will and consent of the Baloch nation, colonial projects in Balochistan would never be safe. The offices and camps of Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) and Military Intelligence (MI) inside the FWO’s main camp were also targeted by the organisation’s fighters. Several soldiers, including senior officers, were reportedly killed in the attacks. Throughout Operation Almas, the Jind-Nadr Sarmachars not only thwarted every counterattack by the occupying army, every attempt by armoured vehicles to advance, and every reinforcement convoy, but also forced them to retreat, maintaining control of the camp for twenty hours. As a result of the actions of the Saddo Operational Battalion’s fighters during Operation Almas, Military Intelligence (MI) officers, Special Services Group (SSG) personnel, and dozens of regular army personnel were reportedly killed. In addition, the enemy’s main camp, posts, internal barracks, and administrative offices were reportedly destroyed in explosions and attacks. A number of the occupying army’s armoured vehicles, along with surveillance drones and quadcopters, were also reportedly destroyed during the operation. After repeatedly inflicting defeats on the occupying enemy during Operation Almas, the Jind-Nadr Sarmachars of the Saddo Operational Battalion, adhering to the philosophy of the last bullet, sacrificed their lives in the struggle for freedom, adding a new chapter of bravery to Baloch national history. The following Jind-Nadr Sarmachars played key roles in the operation: Khalid, alias Zamur; Bilqees Didag, alias Almas; Hamidullah, alias Badil; Shakeel, alias Sohrab; Majeed Zaib, alias Aftab; Nasir Ali, alias Nodan; Mujahid Mehr, alias Sagar Zamurani; and Barat, alias Safar Jan. All eight were reported to have embraced martyrdom during this historic operation. On 27 October 2026, the spokesperson issued another detailed statement, announcing that BLF special units had carried out a comprehensive, coordinated, organized, and effective attack on the centres of the occupying Pakistani army, the colonial intelligence network, and exploitative institutions in Gwadar. The statement claimed that more than 80 military and intelligence personnel had been killed; several armoured vehicles, the main army barracks, and intelligence offices had been destroyed; four quadcopters and two surveillance drones had been shot down; and a police station had been seized. It also reported that operations had been conducted at Gabd and Rimdan 250. Following these deadly blows to the state's exploitative structures, Operation Almas was declared successfully concluded. The spokesperson stated that the BLF was formally presenting to the nation, subjugated peoples, and the international community a comprehensive account of the far-reaching military and political achievements of Operation Almas. The historic, organized, effective, coordinated, and comprehensive operation was launched at 4:00 p.m. on 22 October 2026 against the occupying Pakistani state apparatus in Gwadar and the adjoining coastal region. The operation was described as the most organized, coordinated, and far-reaching attack to date against the occupying Pakistani state, its usurping army, intelligence network, exploitative economic institutions, and local puppet administration. It was presented as an expression of the organization's resolve and capabilities. The revolutionary participation of fearless Baloch women, standing shoulder to shoulder with men in the struggle for Baloch national freedom, national survival, and the defence of the coast and its resources, was portrayed as heralding the end of the usurping colonizer. This historic operation was named after the BLF's fearless and courageous guerrilla commander, Almas Baloch. For the past eight years, Commander Almas had been actively involved in the armed national struggle under the BLF banner, driven by her ideological convictions. Bilqees Didag, alias Almas, daughter of Allah Bakhsh Didag, resident of Dasht Kumbel, is a shining chapter of courage, steadfastness and revolutionary sacrifice. She spent her early life in ordinary circumstances and received regular education up to the eighth grade. She was married and has a beloved daughter, but rising above herself and her family circle, she made the cause of the motherland's freedom her whole life. In 2018 she formally joined the armed struggle for national freedom through BLF's revolutionary platform. After joining the organization, she served for four years as a volunteer in the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB), rendering highly valuable and arduous service. For the past eight years Shaheed Almas had been fully active and ideologically committed in the armed defense struggle through the BLF platform. During her organizational life she served as a very active and fearless member of the intelligence wing in sensitive and difficult areas such as Dasht, Turbat and Gwadar. She kept herself in motion day and night to deliver vital intelligence about the enemy to the organization in time. During military fronts and operations, she always carried out, with courage and steadfastness, the very difficult and dangerous responsibility of delivering supplies, weapons and logistics to the sarmachars across Dasht's harsh and rugged mountain ranges. On the path of her revolutionary struggle, the occupying Pakistani army and operatives of the state's death squads made every effort to obstruct her. The occupying army repeatedly attempted to abduct her, hold her in illegal detention and break her mentally and physically, and on one occasion state personnel subjected her to severe torture that left her badly injured. But this tactic of state oppression, taunting and torture could not shake her steadfastness. She faced every hardship with a smile and always stood firm like a rock on the armed front, keeping the flag of freedom high. Even in these grave conditions under state oppression, the wise and courageous way she carried out organizational responsibilities while hiding in various areas is eloquent proof of her high military insight and ideological maturity. Shaheed Bilqees Didag alias Almas put into practice the idea that on the difficult path of national freedom, all hardships, troubles and sacrifices are acceptable, but national slavery and state domination are not acceptable under any circumstances. To realize this idea, she made the final decision to sacrifice herself for the motherland. Shaheed Almas carried out her duties with great devotion in various military detachments and units of the BLF, and from the time the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB) was founded she was its active founder and core member.

On January 15, 2026, during close-quarters combat in the Battle of Kharan, four fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front - Mubeen, alias Mulla Rahmin; Abdul Raziq Baloch, alias Barag Jan; Hafeez Baloch, alias Yasir; and Mohsin Baloch, alias Mureed - laid down their lives for the homeland. 
Captain Mubeen, alias Molla Rahmin, son of Mohammad Yaqoob, from Mastung Karez Noth, was an exceptionally devoted and educated young Baloch. He joined the BLF as an urban guerrilla in 2020. A highly skilled fighter proficient in urban guerrilla warfare, he formally transferred to the mountain front in 2022 under organizational directives. He served as a frontline fighter and played an important role in numerous critical operations against enemy forces in Kalat, Mastung, Kharan, Noshki, and Quetta. In these regions, Martyr Captain Mubeen Baloch played a pivotal leadership role in establishing BLF operations. After successfully executing the Kharan operation and withdrawing into the mountain ranges, Captain Mubeen, alias Mulla Rahmin, was martyred in an enemy drone strike.

Nizar Ahmed, son of Jan Muhammad and a resident of Mazarabad, Mashkai, was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani security forces on 23 December 2024. His whereabouts remained unknown for nearly six months.
On 11 June 2025, his body was recovered in Mashkai, bearing multiple signs of torture and bullet wounds, raising serious concerns of extrajudicial execution following prolonged incommunicado detention.
Prior to his disappearance, Nizar Ahmed was reportedly summoned to a local military cantonment. His brother, Guldad, also remains missing to date.

Majid Baloch, son of Mohammad Umar, born in 1994, was a resident of Mashkai, District Awaran. He received his early education in his hometown and was a student of F.A. at Inter College Mashkai. He joined the Baloch Students Organization at a very early age. He served as the Unit Secretary of Inter College Mashkai in the BSO Azad Mashkai Zone.
He was abducted on 27 February 2016 by the Pakistan Army from Awaran Bazaar. After two months, his bullet-riddled body was found dumped on 19 April 2016 in District Awaran, Balochistan. His body bore severe signs of torture during his custody.
He engaged himself in the political activities of the organization at a very young age and played a crucial role in his hometown in raising national consciousness among Baloch students. He was killed for exercising his basic political rights and participating in the lawful struggle of the Baloch national movement. His body showed extreme signs of torture. He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many young people to join the caravan of BSO Azad.
His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a very young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

On 17 May 2019, a statement issued by the spokesperson of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) said that two BLA fighters and one fighter of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) were killed in combat with the Pakistan Army and its affiliated death squad, which operates under the supervision of Qambar Khan, in the Kalat area of Balochistan on Thursday, 16 May 2019.
Qambar Khan is a local tribal chief in the Parod area of Kalat and the son of a well-known Baloch freedom fighter, the late Lawang Khan, who was killed by the Pakistani Army during the insurgency in Balochistan in the 1970s.
According to locals and pro-freedom organizations, Qambar Khan is now working with the Pakistan Army and has formed a death squad in the area to fight against Baloch freedom fighters. Several skirmishes between BLA fighters and Qambar Khan’s death squad have also been reported in the past.
The BLA spokesperson said, “Several Pakistani forces personnel and affiliates of Qambar Khan were killed in the combat, during which two BLA fighters, Mama Shams Pirkani Baloch and Doctor Shoaib Baloch alias Gazain, along with a Balochistan Liberation Front fighter, Zafar Mohammed Hasni alias Khuddal, embraced martyrdom.”

Rehan Baloch, son of Ulfath, was a 17 year old student and resident of Ward No. 6 in the Pasni area of Balochistan. On 14 October 2026, he was abducted from his home and forcibly disappeared by death squads backed by the Pakistani state and military.

After eight days of enforced disappearance, on 22 October 2026, his lifeless body was found dumped in the Kulanch area of Pasni.

Liaquat Baloch, alias Nodh, son of Mola Bakhsh, was a resident of Kohad, Tump. He joined the BLA in 2019 and served on the Zamuran and Kulbar fronts as a Patrol Commander and Side Camp Commander in Zamuran. He was skilled as an Improvised Explosive Device (IED) specialist and was a member of the Fateh Squad. During Operation Herof Phase II, he was commanding on the Pul Abad front.
Liaquat Baloch, alias Nodh, belonged to the Kohad area of Tump. After joining the BLA in 2019, he remained continuously active on the Zamuran and Kulbar fronts and soon established himself as a capable fighter. Despite the difficult mountainous terrain and constant enemy surveillance, Nodh consistently remained on the offensive. His battlefield approach was shaped by practical experience and a clear understanding of guerrilla warfare.
Because of his competence and strong sense of responsibility, Nodh was assigned the role of Patrol Commander. In this position, he led his units across mountainous routes and difficult passages, delivering effective blows to the enemy and playing an important role in restricting enemy movement. Later, he was appointed as the Side Camp Commander in Zamuran, where he effectively managed the camp’s discipline, defense, and training operations.
He was regarded as a specialist in Improvised Explosive Device (IED) warfare and used explosive tactics with great skill, enabling him to halt enemy advances and weaken their military capability. He also participated in numerous battles under the alliance of pro-independence organizations, BRAS, demonstrating steadfastness and strong battlefield discipline in every engagement.
Due to these abilities and his extensive combat experience, Nodh was inducted into the organization’s frontline unit, the Fateh Squad. Being part of the Fateh Squad signified that he was not only a capable fighter but also trusted with highly sensitive and decisive operations. During Operation Herof Phase II, he led his unit on the Pul Abad front in an intense confrontation with the enemy and ultimately sacrificed his life, becoming immortal in the history of the war of freedom.

On the night between Saturday and Sunday, at 3:00 AM on April 25, 2020, Pakistani forces, along with local death squads, surrounded Baloch fighters (Sarmachaars) in Yar Mohammad Bazaar, located in the Parom Kallag Kor area of Panjgur district. A clash broke out between the forces and the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) fighters, which continued for twelve hours.
The fighting lasted until 2:30 PM on April 26, 2020. After the Pakistani ground forces retreated, military helicopters shelled the fighters, resulting in the killing of four Sarmachaars - Major Noora, son of Sher Dil, alias Peerak; Lieutenant Nawaz, son of Haji Ghulam Hussain; Abdul Malik, son of Haji Ghulam Hussain; Momin, son of Mohammad Azeem - During this prolonged twelve hour clash, several soldiers of the Pakistani army and associated death squads were killed and injured.

Major Noora, alias Peerak, son of Sher Dil, was born in 1992 in Parom, Panjgur, Balochistan. He had been associated with the Baloch national liberation movement and armed struggle for over a decade. He was a highly intelligent and capable fighter. He not only served in various roles across different regions of Balochistan, providing significant military contributions, but also played an important role in organizing the Balochistan Liberation Front through his abilities.

Lieutenant Nawaz, alias Gulab, son of Ghulam Hussain, was born in Parom. He had been associated with the BLF and the armed struggle for ten years and, due to his dedication and capabilities, attained the rank of Lieutenant.

Abdul Malik, son of Ghulam Hussain, was also born in Parom and had been associated with the armed organization BLF for two years.

Momin Baloch, son of Mohammad Azeem, was born in Buleda Salo and had been actively engaged in the armed struggle for two years.

data.biography:
On December 14, 2025, prolonged clashes broke out between the occupying Pakistani army and Baloch Liberation Army freedom fighters in the Daghari area of Quetta when the fighters were traveling for organizational work. The occupying army attempted to surround the freedom fighters using civilian vehicles, to which the freedom fighters immediately retaliated. In this clash, seven occupying army personnel were eliminated and several others were wounded, while two Baloch Liberation Army freedom fighters, Asmatullah Satakzai alias Siraj and Sajjad Zehri alias Sarang, attained martyrdom.
Asmatullah Satakzai alias Siraj, son of Takri Eywaz, belonged to the Daghari area of Quetta. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2024 and served on the Bolan, Quetta, and Mastung fronts for the achievement of national liberation. Sangat Asmat led a simple life, was a shepherd by profession, and was known among his comrades for his quiet courage and unwavering determination.

On 2 February 2022, sixteen members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayeen unit, the Majeed Brigade, carried out simultaneous attacks, nine in Noshki and seven on the Frontier Corps headquarters in Panjgur. The organization named this action "Operation Ganjal". 90 Pakistani security personnel were killed in Noshki and 105 in Panjgur.
On 2 February 2022 at 8:00 PM Fidayee Jamal Baloch alias Chacha, son of Rehmatullah, a resident of Turbat, rammed an VBEID into the main gate of the FC camp in Panjgur. As a result, the front portion of the camp was destroyed, and all soldiers deployed for security at the spot were killed instantly. After this, under the leadership of Unit Commander Hamid Raheem alias Zubair, son of Raheem Bakhsh, a resident of Chitkan, Panjgur, the fidayee fighters Sami Sameer alias Shoaib, son of Ustad Ilahi Bakhsh, resident of Gramkan, Panjgur; Ilyas Baloch alias Qadir, son of Aslam, resident of Gramkan, Panjgur; Asad Wahag alias Sabzo, son of Sadiq, resident of Kilkor; Nasir Imam alias Hamal, son of Imam, resident of Parom; and Zameer Baloch alias Faraz, son of Mohammad Hassan, resident of Dandar, Hoshab, entered the camp. They killed the majority of the soldiers present in the camp, while the remaining enemy personnel, instead of confronting the fighters, abandoned the camp and fled. The objective of the Panjgur unit was to seize control of the camp and hold it for as long as possible. After the enemy fled, the fighters took full control of the entire camp. Subsequently, to recapture the camp from the fighters, the enemy called in SSG commandos, the army, and combat helicopters. During this time, with the support of combat helicopters and armored vehicles, the SSG commandos launched five major assaults on the Baloch fighters. In every attack, the fighters inflicted heavy casualties on the enemy and forced them to retreat. The fighters continued to hold control of the camp while fighting the enemy’s elite military units for 72 hours. After failing in ground assaults, on 5 February 2022 in the afternoon, heavy shelling was carried out against the fighters using combat helicopters. As a result, after prolonged resistance, the fighters were martyred.

On 8 August 2016, terrorists attacked the Government Hospital in Quetta, Balochistan, in a suicide bombing and shooting. More than 70 people were killed, mainly lawyers, and more than 130 others were injured.
The majority of those killed were lawyers who had gathered at the hospital after the body of Advocate Bilal Anwar Kasi, president of the Balochistan Bar Association, was brought there. Kasi had been shot dead by a gunman near Mengal Chowk on Manno Jan Road in Quetta while he was leaving his home for his office.
Responsibility for the attack was claimed by various Islamist groups, including Jamaat-ul-Ahrar and the Islamic State Khorasan Province. However, nationalist groups have alleged that these extremist organisations are backed by the Pakistani state and its military to counter the nationalist movement in the region and exploit its natural resources.
Estimates of the death toll ranged between 70 people, while more than 120 were injured. Of those killed, 54 were lawyers. Among them, 15 were Baloch by ethnicity, while the majority were Pashtuns by ethnicity.

The Baloch advocates or lawyers who were killed are identified as follows:

01 Ghulam Farooq Badini, son of Haji Abdul Ghani.
02 Bashir Ahmed Qazi, son of Qazi Ahmed Jan.
03 Bashir Ahmad Zehri, son Haji Mir Ahmed Zehri.
04 Naseer Ahmed Langove, son Abdul Rahim.
05 Chakar Khan Rind, son of Mehmood.
06 Abdul Rashid, son of Abdul Latif.
07 Nooruddin Rakshani, son Haji Naseeruddin.
08 Muhammad Imran, son Ghulam Farooq.
09 Muneer Ahmed Mengal, son Ghulam Murtaza.
10 Sangat Jehan Jamaldini, son of Dr. Jahanzaib.
11 Mohammad Ali Satakzai, son of Taj Mohammad Khan.
12 Mehmood Ahmed Lehri, son Haji Abdul Hameed.
13 Jamil Ur Rehman, son of Qazi Abdul Hameed.
14 Amanullah Langove, son of Haji Dad Karim.
15 Sabir Ali, son of Abdul Rasheed.

Jamil ur Rehman Qazi moved recently to Quetta in search for a safer base for his family, after he was seriously injured in Khuzdar in 2013 when gunmen opened fire on him, hitting three bullets in his leg.
"Can you imagine our misfortune? We migrated from Khuzdar for protection but we lost our beloved son here in Quetta," says his father Qazi Abdul Hameed.
Advocate Qazi was 40 years old.

Imran Ali, a Baloch student, was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani CTD and intelligence agencies from his apartment at Arif Plaza, A-one city, Quetta on 27 August 2025. For nearly a year, his family was left searching for him while the Pakistani state denied holding him.
On 6 August 2026, police finally disclosed that Imran had been killed on 23 May 2026. His family was never informed. His body was buried without their knowledge, and they were denied the basic right to know where their son was laid to rest.
Imran was in the custody of Pakistan’s intelligence agencies for months. Three individuals who were later released confirmed seeing him in custody.

On 16 October 2026, a statement issued by the Baloch Republican Guards (BRG) stated that, on the night of 30 September 2026, occupying Pakistani forces arrived in the Sunni area of Kachhi district, Balochistan, to conduct an operation. A sudden confrontation took place between the occupying forces and the freedom fighters, who launched a deadly attack against the enemy. As a result, the occupying army suffered significant casualties and material losses.

During the clashes, five devoted BRG freedom fighters - Bafa Jan Jatoi, son of Lal Jan Jatoi, a resident of Sunni, Kachhi; Fareed Jan Jatoi, alias Zahri, son of Ghulam Jan, a resident of Sunni, Kachhi; Obaidullah Jan Jatoi, son of Sajjar Khan, a resident of Sunni, Kachhi; Imam Din Jatoi, alias Mumtaz, son of Nihal Khan, a resident of Sunni, Kachhi; and Ayaz Jan Ghola, alias Alim, son of Abdul Sattar, belonging to the Ghola Baloch tribe and a resident of Sunni, Kachhi - embraced martyrdom while defending their homeland and fighting for national independence.

All these freedom fighters were highly dedicated, brave, hardworking, and disciplined comrades. They inflicted various forms of losses on the occupying enemy in several areas of Balochistan, including Kachhi, Dhadar, Sunni, Bolan, and Sibi.

On 12 October 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that Baloch Liberation Army fighters had carried out 16 organised and intense attacks against the occupying Pakistani military in various regions of Balochistan over the previous six days, inflicting severe personnel and material losses on the enemy. The fighters successfully maintained complete control over major highways while targeting enemy convoys, supply lines, and operatives. During this period, dedicated BLA Sarmachar Nawaz Hoth, alias Ustad Gajiyan, embraced martyrdom in clashes.
On 11 October 2026, the maritime unit of the BLA, the Hammal Maritime Defence Force (HMDF), simultaneously targeted two Rigid Hull Inflatable Boats of the occupying Pakistani military's coast guards in an organized and intense attack in Jiwani, Gwadar, resulting in 13 personnel of the occupying forces being killed on the spot.
During this battle, intense clashes also continued with a nearby post of the occupying forces, during which Hammal Maritime Defence Force unit commander Nawaz Baloch alias Ustad Gajiyan was wounded and subsequently embraced martyrdom. Martyred Commander Nawaz Baloch alias Ustad Gajiyan, son of Rasool Bakhsh Hoth, hailed from the Gokdan area of Turbat. He became part of the Baloch Liberation movement in 2010 and officially affiliated with the BLA in 2020. Nawaz Hoth rendered invaluable services for Baloch national freedom in Tump, Mand, Dasht, Turbat, Prom, Panjgur, and the coastal belt, and was commanding the naval unit of the Hammal Maritime Defence Force at the time.
It is also noteworthy that this family has rendered immortal sacrifices for national freedom.
His brother Mubashir Hoth, alias Shah Dost embraced martyrdom at the Kulbar front in October 2020, and another brother Nabeel Ahmad, alias Ali embraced martyrdom in direct combat against the enemy at the Turbat front on 29 April 2025. His entire family has maintained steadfastness despite state repression, torture, and enforced disappearances.

Qasum Arman Baloch, alias Almas, son of Master Sudir, was a resident of the Absar area of Turbat, with his primary affiliation from Shapuk. He was an intelligent, educated and exceptionally talented young man — a BS student of literature. He was always active in the creation of revolutionary literature, ideological discourse, and the promotion of resistance consciousness. During his studies, he was active in the Baloch Students Organization and later joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2023, where he served on both urban and mountainous fronts. At the time of his martyrdom, Almas Baloch was associated with the Intelligence Wing ZIRAB of the BLA, where he demonstrated great responsibility, deep thinking, and technical expertise in a short period. He was martyred on December 2, 2025, due to a sudden accident.

Sherdil, son of Qadir Bakhsh, was an elderly farmer from Drachko Dasht, Turbat. On 21 May 2026, while working on his farmland, Pakistani Frontier Corps (FC) personnel opened fire near his land. Local people stated that Sherdil was struck by the gunfire and lost his life on his own farm.

Hilal Sayad, son of Sayad, was a 28-year-old worker and resident of Malikabad, Tump. On 5 July 2026, he was allegedly unlawfully arrested from his home in Hub Chowki, Balochistan. On 19 September 2026, he was allegedly extrajudicially killed in a fake encounter by the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) in Karachi.
For more than three months, the whereabouts of Hilal Sayad remained unknown to his family members. This unlawful act of enforced disappearance further compounded the situation when he was allegedly killed in a fake encounter by the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD).

Maqsood Qalandarani, son of Sher Mohammad Qalandarani, was born in 1986 in Tootak, District Khuzdar. He received his early education in his native town, Tootak. He was a very quiet person by nature. Due to financial issues, he also started working to continue his education and support his family. He was fond of football and chess, and in his free time, he played chess.
Maqsood commenced his political career on the platform of BSO Azad in 2006. His family discouraged him from engaging in nationalist politics through the Baloch Students Organization, as the organization’s members were continuously targeted by security agencies for their strong role in raising awareness among the Baloch nation about the perceived Pakistani colonization of Baloch land. He always loved reading books and newspapers to enhance his political awareness. He was a very brave and well-loved person within his circle. He valued the Baloch cause above his own life, due to which he continued to perform his national duties on the platform of the Baloch Students Organization Azad.
He was among the closest friends of Ameer-ul-Mulk. He was always proud of his organizational friends and had a strong belief in comradeship in the national struggle.
He was abducted on 8th February 2011 from Tootak, District Khuzdar, Balochistan. His bullet-riddled body was found dumped on 16th July 2011 in Jabal-e-Noor, Quetta, Balochistan.
He showed strong bravery even in the torture cell; when some of the detainees returned home, they narrated stories of his courage in state torture cells. He was as strong as a revolutionary can be in the struggle for independence.

On 20 October 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 25 September 2026, the occupying Pakistani army launched a military operation, during which BLA fighters thwarted the assault and eliminated approximately fourteen enemy soldiers. Engaging the enemy with great valour, BLA fighters repelled the assault in a clash that began at 6:00 AM.

During the battle, three brave sons of Baloch soil - Hameedullah Baloch, alias Bilali Baloch; Abdul Hameed, alias Bilali Baloch, a resident of Noshki; and Naseeb Baloch, alias Asad, a resident of Manguchar - were martyred, making the ultimate sacrifice in defence of the Baloch motherland.

A large number of enemy forces participated in the engagement, supported by drones. BLA fighters demonstrated exceptional courage and bravery, engaging the occupying army in direct combat from 6:00 AM until 4:00 PM.

All three brave fighters had joined the BLA in 2023. They participated in several significant battles against the occupying enemy on various fronts, delivering a jaw-dropping response to the enemy.

Akil Azab, alias Riaz Baloch, son of Sawali and Rasheeda Baloch, was a resident of Pasni Gwadar, Balochistan. He was a revolutionary poet in the Balochi Language. According to organizational statement; He was become part of Baloch liberation movement in the platform Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in 2012 and he was on the rank of lieutenant.

His family members were  made victim of collective punishment, several family member abducted and tortured for years. His brother Abid Sawali was abducted and killed in  2013, His uncle, Habib Faqeer was abducted in 2013 and after four years in 2017 was killed and also, his a close relative Haneef was killed on 2011. 

Akil Azab embraced martyrdom along with other his three comrades Asad Baloch, alias Basit Baloch; Pervez Mehr, alias Malok Baloch and Saki Baksh, alias Mureed Baloch during a clash with Pakistan’s Army in Madag Kaur,  area of Kolwa, Kech, Balochistan on Oct 9, 2021.
data.martyrdomPlace: Madag Kaur, Kolwah, Kech district, Balochistan

data.biography:
Kabeer Baloch, alias Waheed, son of Mohammad Ayub Sumalani and a resident of Zard, Ghulam Jan, Mangochar, Kalat, joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Mastung front. He was martyred on 1 June 2026 in Kardigap, Mastung.
Kabeer Baloch, alias Waheed, joined the BLA earlier this year after coming to view the organization's military doctrine as the ultimate path to ending Pakistani occupation. Upon completing his basic military training, he swiftly moved to the operational front and took up defensive positions against enemy forces in the Mastung region. Over the past six months, he carried out his military responsibilities as a hardworking, conscientious, and committed fighter, demonstrating dedication and resolve in the execution of his duties.
Within a short period of time, he established himself as a capable fighter and a hardworking Sarmachar within the organization. In accordance with the organization's policy of firmly holding its defensive fronts, he, alongside his fellow Sarmachars, thwarted enemy advances on numerous occasions in Mastung and Kirdagap, forcing enemy forces to retreat. In multiple clashes with the enemy, he confronted enemy forces with courage, steadfastness, and commitment, displaying remarkable determination on the battlefield.
For the cause of national freedom, he endured all the hardships and difficulties of war and remained firmly committed, with sincerity and steadfastness, to the decision he had made before joining the organization. Until his martyrdom, he remained devoted to his beliefs and to the ideology of freedom that guided his struggle.

In 1838, the British sent a force led by Alexander Burnes to reinstate Shah Shuja Durrani as the king of Afghanistan by deposing Amir Dost Mohammad Khan. To reach Afghanistan, they needed passage through Balochistan, particularly the Bolan Pass. However, Khan Mehrab Khan refused to allow the British to use his land to attack a neighboring country. The British sent Lieutenant Leach to negotiate with the Baloch government, but the Khan stood firm. When British forces reached Shaal via Bolan, some patriotic Baloch, without the Khan’s knowledge, attacked British troops out of nationalist sentiment and a desire to protect their homeland.
After toppling Amir Dost Mohammad Khan, the British Governor General of India, Lord Auckland, ordered an attack on Balochistan. In 1839, around 7,000 British troops marched from Shaal to attack the Baloch Meeri (capital). Anticipating an invasion, Khan Mehrab Khan declared war and sent messages to tribal leaders, but many saw the British as allies rather than invaders and chose to collaborate with them rather than defend their land. When Khan Mehrab Khan gathered his resistance fighters, the number of loyal warriors had dwindled to only 700 due to the short sightedness of many tribal chiefs. Nevertheless, Mehrab Khan was determined to fight. At his court, a respected figure, Akhund Muhammad Siddiq, advised him that he was not in a position to wage war at that time. He suggested that the Khan should leave Kalat with his companions, regroup and strengthen his forces, and then launch an attack against the British when the time was right, on 13 November 1839, the British forces launched an attack on Kalat, and a fierce battle ensued. During the fighting, Khan Mehrab Khan Baloch was martyred by a British bullet.

Among those martyred alongside him were:

Diwan Bacha Mal, Minister of Finance

Diwan Khem Chand

Diwan Asardas Mukhi, from the Hindu Panchayat of Kalat

Abdul Karim Raisani, brother of Sardar Asad Khan Raisani

Sardar Wali Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (maternal uncle of Martyr Amir Mehrab Khan)

Mir Taj Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (cousin of Mehrab Khan)

Mir Muhammad Ali Shahizai Mengal

Mir Fazal Muhammad Lehri, brother of Sardar Muhammad Khan Lehri

Sardar Zaman Khan Pandrani

Mir Dad Karim Chandozai Shahwani

Mir Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Mir Badal Khan, brother of Sardar Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Khan Muhammad Dehwaar, Arbab-e-Kalat.

Mir Nabi Bakhsh Jatoi, from the Narmak region of Kalat

Mir Qaiser Khan Bizenjo

Mir Shah Dost Bizenjo

Muhammad Raza Waziri Khel

Noor Muhammad Shahizai, son of Polat Sagaar Sarmastani, in charge of the armory

Taj Muhammad Shagasi

On 1 July 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said that BLA freedom fighters had carried out 23 successful operations in different areas of occupied Balochistan over the previous ten days. These attacks targeted the occupying forces and exploitative companies, while operations were also conducted against vehicles belonging to exploitative entities as part of the economic blockade on major highways. In these attacks, 16 personnel of the occupying army were killed and several others were injured. Meanwhile, four valiant BLA sarmachars - Raziq Baloch, alias Jahanzaib; Israr Baloch, alias Kohzad; Haji Khalil Shahwani, alias Mama Marjan; and Anwar Bilsum, alias Dr Aziz - were martyred while defending the motherland during intense clashes at various locations.

Raziq Baloch, alias Jahanzaib, son of Ghulam Mohiudden Kurd, was a resident of Bahram Shahi, Mastung. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in June 2025 and served on the Nagaho and Mastung fronts. He was martyred on 28 June 2026 in Kambela, Mastung.
Raziq, alias Jahanzaib, joined the Baloch Liberation Army after witnessing national subjugation and the inhumane treatment of his people at the hands of the occupying forces. Recognizing the need for a Baloch state as the fundamental basis of collective life, he chose to begin armed resistance against the enemy. In a very short period, he fully embraced the organization's discipline and chain of command and played a significant individual role in maintaining its strength and influence in the region. He was known as a sensible, serious, and hardworking Sarmachar who diligently fulfilled every responsibility assigned to him by the organization.
After joining the organization, he was deployed to the Mastung front on the directives of the command, where he carried out his duties with professionalism and dedication. Due to his skills and bravery, he became a frontline fighter. Whenever the enemy attempted to advance into areas under the organization's control, he, along with his fellow Sarmachars, played a key role in firmly defending the front lines. Through his abilities, he demonstrated that Baloch youth are fully capable of effectively defending their homeland.
He was not only involved in securing defensive positions but also played a significant individual role in offensive military operations such as Herof. Remaining committed to his motherland until his final day and accepting the ultimate sacrifice reflects a clear reality: that Baloch youth are willing to make every sacrifice for the restoration and defense of the Baloch state. His sacrifices will always remain inscribed in the pages of history.

Arif Noor Baloch was an employee of the Gwadar Development Authority. He was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces in Karachi on 31 October 2010. Months later, he was extrajudicially killed; his body was found on 23 March 2011 near the town of Hub in Balochistan.

On 2 February 2022, sixteen members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayeen unit, the Majeed Brigade, carried out simultaneous attacks, nine in Noshki and seven on the Frontier Corps headquarters in Panjgur. The organization named this action "Operation Ganjal". 90 Pakistani security personnel were killed in Noshki and 105 in Panjgur.
In the BLA’s operation on the Noshki FC headquarters, 9 fidayeen participated. On 2 February 2022, Meerain Jamaldini (alias Zagrain) drove an VBEID into the camp’s main gate. Following this, Badil Baloch (alias Riyasat), Murad Aajo (alias Baba), Aneel Baloch (alias Balach), Yasir Noor (alias Saif), Aziz Zehri (alias Barag), Ibraheem Baloch (alias Kabeer), Deedag Bahar (alias Rauf) and Bilal Baloch (alias Wahid) entered the camp. As a result, 90 military personnel, including one officer, were killed, and a portion of the camp was destroyed.
The operation continued throughout the night. In the early morning of 3 February 2022, after their ammunition was exhausted, the remaining eight fidayeen took their own lives by firing their weapons.

Yasir Mengal, alias Shah Yar, son of Noor Mohammad Mengal, was a resident of the Ahmadwal area of Noshki. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Noshki front. On 13 September 2026, he was in the Sultan Shar area of Qila Abdullah.
Yasir Mengal, known as Shah Yar, belonged to Ahmadwal area of Noshki. Professionally, he was a driver and remained connected with travel and roads in his everyday life. In 2026, he joined the armed movement and later became associated with the Noshki front. According to his close comrades, he was simple in nature and had a sociable personality. His profession as a driver gave him the opportunity to interact with different people and travel through different areas, due to which he was well acquainted with journeys and routes. Even after joining the front, the same simplicity and practical nature remained evident in his personality.
His association with the Noshki front proved to be the important stage of his life. The brief period he spent with his comrades was completely different from his ordinary life. On September 13, 2026, Yasir Mengal, alias Shah Yar, was martyred in a clash in the Sultan Shar area of Qila Abdullah.

Martyr Gulab Baloch, alias Mullah Noor, was born to Shokat Baloch and Fatima Baloch in the Swali Dan Shapuk area of Kech, Balochistan. He had been affiliated with the pro-independence organization Baloch Republican Army (BRA) since 2014. He embraced martyrdom during a clash with the Pakistan Army in the Parom area of Panjgur on October 17, 2021. His organization titled him “Kohsar-e-Watan.”

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, the BLA’s Majeed Brigade Fidayeen targeted the main camp and the Coast Guard camp of the Pakistan Navy in the coastal city of Pasni, Balochistan. The operation was initiated by Fazal, alias Miraan, who rammed a vehicle loaded with explosives into the main entrance gate of the Navy camp. The explosion instantly killed at least seven personnel stationed at the gate.
Immediately after this initial attack, six Fidayeen - Yasma Baloch, alias Zareena; Waseem Baloch, alias Zirbaar; Zaid Zamurani, alias Abram; Sabzal Baloch, alias Kohsar; Diljan Baloch, alias Ameer Ajoo; and Operation Commander Shabeer Baloch, alias Kiya - entered the camp and took up positions. Fierce clashes with the occupying Navy and Navy special units inside the camp continued for more than five hours, during which at least 33 Pakistani personnel were killed. This operation not only inflicted significant casualties on the enemy but also dealt a severe blow to the defense structure of the Navy camp.

Nazar Jan Mohammadshai was born on 27 April 1948 in Killi Mohammadshai, Mastung. Influenced by the political atmosphere at home, he joined the Baloch Students Organization (BSO) at an early age and remained an active member until his graduation in Quetta.
In the early 1970s, he took up teaching. However, when Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto dissolved Balochistan’s National Awami Party (NAP) government in February 1973, he, along with a small group of close confidants, joined the Baloch armed resistance against the Pakistani army’s operations. Later, he merged his group with Agha Salman Jan’s resistance group, the son of Prince Agha Kareem.
Agha Salman surrendered when the Khan of Kalat, Mir Ahmed Yar Khan, his uncle, was made the governor of Balochistan. They were kept in the governor’s house for interrogation. As soon as Nazar Jan was released, he contacted the resistance leadership, as he and his friends never accepted the surrender. Pakistani agencies, suspicious of him, re-arrested and tortured him in Quetta Kuli Camp. However, he was later released on the intervention of Nawab Abdul Qadir Shahwani and the Khan of Kalat. He kept a low profile but remained in contact with Baloch resistance leaders Safar Khan Zahri, Abdul Nabi Bangulzai, and Khair Jan Bizenjo.
He bid farewell to his family on 27 April 1977 with the intention of joining the resistance in the mountains. However, he was abducted by Pakistani intelligence agencies, and till today his fate remains unknown to his family and friends.
His father met General Zia-ul-Haq through the reference of Prince Agha Mohyuddin and asked for his help in locating his son. After a conversation with someone on the phone, Zia told him, “Your son is alive, but you should forget him; he has now become a loyal supporter of the state.” Upon further insistence, Zia advised him to contact the Kalat army camp. There, he was shown another person and realized the reality. Upon returning, he told his family, “Be proud, my son has sacrificed his life for the freedom of his motherland and has glorified mine, yours, and the name of the Baloch nation.”

Altaf Atta son of Muhammad Atta, a resident of Nizarabad tehsil Tump, district Kech, was extrajudicially killed by state-backed death squads at inside his residence late night of Thursday on September 11th, 2025. 

Around 3:am, State-backed death Squads has entered the house of Muhammad Atta and directly opened fire, in result his son Altaf succumbed his injuries before being hospitalised.

Salman Baloch and Abdul Waheed Baloch were friends who longed for a Balochistan free from occupation and tyranny. Both were students at Degree College Khuzdar. Salman Baloch was the son of Sher Mohammad Baloch, while Abdul Waheed was the son of Ghaus Baksh Mohammad Shahi, a veteran of the 1970s uprising against the Bhutto regime, from the town of Kathan.
Abdul Waheed was no stranger to the brutality of the occupying forces. His father suffered a severe head injury from a gunshot wound in the 1970s, and his brother, Abdul Kabeer, was abducted on March 27, 2009.
The two youths were specifically targeted and shot dead on February 29, 2012, in Khuzdar by local death squad leader Shafiq Mengal, who led Tehreek Nifaz-e-Amn, an organization allied with the Pakistani state and its forces.
Abdul Waheed once famously declared, “Death is unavoidable; if we overcome the fear of it, then nobody in this world can keep our motherland enslaved."

Mehmood Baloch, son of Abdul Qadir, was born in 1992. He was a resident of District Mastung, Balochistan. Mehmood Baloch was an MBBS student at Khyber Medical College, Peshawar, and a member of BSO Azad, Peshawar Zone. He received his early education in his native area of Mastung.
He played an important role in mobilizing and uniting Baloch youth residing in Peshawar for educational purposes. He mobilized hundreds of youths to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of the Baloch homeland. Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by security forces.
He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he remained committed to the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom. He was an example of bravery and commitment. He joined the organization at an early age and remained steadfast in his national ideology until the end. He had a keen interest in reading revolutionary literature about oppressed nations. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising peaceful political expression.
He was abducted on 8th August 2011 from Shaal, Balochistan, by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agencies. His bullet-riddled body was found dumped on 18th August 2011 in Ganjadori, District Mastung, Balochistan. His body showed clear signs of extreme torture.
He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a very young age will be remembered in the golden pages of Baloch history.

On 9 October 2025, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) released a statement announcing that on 7 October 2025, Qurban Unit member Abdullah Maiyar, known as Saugat, attained martyrdom while fighting bravely.
The BLF spokesperson stated that Abdullah Maiyar had joined the organization a year earlier and, due to his hard work, dedication, and combat skills, had been selected for the front-line Qurban Unit.
Abdullah Maiyar participated in several important operations across Turbat, Paroom, Kolwah, Gorkop, Jhao, Shapuk, and Balgatar. He was martyred during a major battle in Balgatar.

Sageer Ahmed, son of Basheer Ahmed and a resident of Gwrjak, Mashkai, in Awaran district, was shot and killed by members of a state-backed death squad in Shareeki, Mashkai, Awaran. Sageer was employed by the Police department at the time of his killing.

General Ustad Aslam Baloch (1975 – 25 December 2018) was a founding pillar of the modern Baloch liberation movement and Commander in Chief of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) from 2017 until his martyrdom.
Born in 1975 on Haji Ghaibi Road, Quetta, in the home of Raheem Dad Dehwar, Aslam Baloch received his early education at Special High School Quetta. At the age of nineteen, inspired by Nawab Khair Bakhsh Marri’s return from exile, he joined the Baloch national resistance.
By 1995 he had become a central figure in the establishment and expansion of the Baloch Liberation Army. His exceptional leadership, political maturity, and organisational discipline rapidly earned him widespread respect. In 2017 he was appointed Commander in Chief of the BLA, a position that reflected the complete trust of the movement.
One of the earliest members of the organisation, Aslam Baloch built and strengthened its network across Balochistan. Under his command, the Bolan region became an impregnable stronghold of resistance. He played a decisive role in shaping the BLA’s organisational vision and combat structure while serving simultaneously as a profound political thinker, strategist, and teacher whose writings and speeches guided an entire generation of Baloch youth.
In 2010, following the martyrdom of Majeed Langav II, he founded the Majeed Brigade, the BLA’s elite unit for self-sacrificial operations. He personally trained, organised, and led the Brigade in some of its most significant actions. In recognition of his lifelong service, the BLA posthumously conferred upon him its highest title, “General.”
Despite severe heart disease and a bypass surgery in 2010, Aslam Baloch refused medical advice to leave the battlefield. Rejecting comfort and family pleas for rest, he returned to the mountains of Bolan, declaring that only there would he regain strength.
General Aslam Baloch stood as an uncompromising barrier against Pakistan and China’s exploitation of Balochistan’s resources, repeatedly warning occupying forces and foreign investors against plundering the land. He also achieved historic unity among different fronts of the Baloch resistance, navigating internal challenges and political conspiracies with extraordinary wisdom and always placing national interest above all else.
On 25 December 2018, General Ustad Aslam Baloch was martyred in an operation in Kandahar, Afghanistan. His ideas, strategies, and indomitable spirit continue to guide the Baloch liberation movement, and his legacy remains etched in every mountain and trench of the resistance.
