data.biography:
On 3 May 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said that between 25 April 2026 and 3 May 2026, BLA fighters carried out eleven operations, resulting in the deaths of eleven personnel from Pakistani forces. These attacks targeted the Pakistani army, vehicles transporting minerals, and local collaborators.
In four IED attacks, the army suffered significant personnel and financial losses, while three Military Intelligence (MI) personnel were taken into custody.
On 24 April 2026, during clashes with Pakistani forces at Taadez in Nushki, three BLA fighters - Asad Jamaldini (alias Baba Darwesh), Shakeel-ur-Rehman Bangulzai (alias Sheikh Atta), and Shehak Mengal (alias Siddiq) - were killed.
Asad Jamaldini, alias Baba Darwesh, son of Mohammad Younus, was a resident of Saryab Road in Quetta, Balochistan. His educational qualification was Intermediate. He joined the BLA in 2025 and served on the Shor Parood, Kalat, and Nushki fronts. His rank was Patrol Commander, and he was martyred on 24 April 2026 in Tadeez, Nushki.
Asad Jamaldini, who was known among his companions by the name “Darwesh,” was not just a darwesh in name; in his character and practical life, he was also a selfless and devoted Sarmachar. He was a figure of affection and respect among his fellow Sarmachars, and in his practical life, he maintained simplicity. Although he possessed derwesh like qualities among his ideological companions, whenever he faced the enemy or carried out combat operations, he became a brave, courageous, fearless, and bold fighter who confronted the enemy decisively.
With strong ideological and intellectual awareness, he lived his practical life under strict military discipline. Alongside maintaining the organization’s firm hold in urban areas, he played an important role in organizing and strengthening the group’s presence with his fellow fighters. After rendering his military services in Operation Herof Phase Two, he established himself as a frontline Sarmachar, working to consolidate the organization’s position in areas under its influence.
Observing his practical life, mindset, courage, and bravery, the organization entrusted him with patrol command responsibilities within a short period. He fulfilled these duties wholeheartedly until his last breath. In direct combat with enemy forces and their collaborators, he sacrificed his life for the defense of the homeland and the restoration of a Baloch state, thereby immortalizing himself in Baloch national history.

On 15 March 2025, in the Naal area of Khuzdar district in Balochistan, armed groups of the State of Pakistan and Pakistani forces - locally referred to as “death squads” - opened fire and killed Shahjan Kurd.
Shahjan Kurd was the brother of Zahid Kurd, the former chairman of the Baloch Students Organization (Azad). Zahid Kurd was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces on 18 March 2014 from the city of Quetta in Balochistan, along with BSO Junior Joint Secretary Asad Baloch. The abduction was witnessed by Karima Baloch.

Early Life and Political Beginnings

Lala Muneer Baloch was born around 1959 in Balochistan. He emerged as a committed political figure during the heightened era of Baloch nationalist mobilization. His political journey was deeply intertwined with the ideology of the Baloch National Movement (BNM), where he served as a central leader alongside Chairman Ghulam Muhammad.

Leadership and Roles

Lala Muneer was a key strategist and organizational leader, eventually serving as the General Secretary of the Baloch National Front (BNF) an alliance of various Baloch nationalist groups. He also held the position of Vice Chairman of the BNM during critical periods of the movement.

His leadership was characterized by:

Political Resistance: Standing alongside Chairman Ghulam Muhammad in the 2002 and 2004 cycles, he was instrumental in the BNM’s decision to disengage from parliamentary politics in favor of a struggle for national liberation.

National Unity: He worked to foster ideological cohesion between different student and political wings, often mediating during internal party conflicts to maintain a unified front against state oppression.

Advocacy for the Disappeared: He was a vocal advocate against the illegal abduction of Baloch workers, a cause that eventually led to his own repeated detentions.

Abduction and Martyrdom

Lala Muneer’s life was marked by extreme personal hardship due to his political beliefs. Like his comrades, he faced state-sponsored threats and was illegally abducted on December 3, 2006, before being released in late 2007.

On April 3, 2009, Lala Muneer was abducted for the final time. The incident took place at the chamber of Advocate Kachkol Ali in Turbat, shortly after a court had acquitted him and his colleagues Chairman Ghulam Muhammad and Sher Muhammad Baloch of various charges.

Six days later, on April 9, 2009, his bullet-riddled body was discovered in the Murgaap area. This event, now known as the "Murgaap Incident," is regarded by the BNM as a defining moment in the Baloch struggle, sparking widespread protests across the region and internationalizing the issue of "kill and dump" policies in Balochistan.

Mir Balach Khan Marri, the son of the revered pro independence leader Nawab Khair Bakhsh Marri, was a towering figure in the Baloch national movement. Born on January 17, 1966, in Kahan, Balochistan, he dedicated his life to the struggle for the national independence of the Baloch people.

Education and Early Activism

Balach Khan Marri's early life was marked by self-exile. Alongside his father and thousands of Marri tribesmen, he migrated to Afghanistan to escape the oppressive political climate. He later moved to Russia, where he pursued and completed his higher education. During this period, he rendered crucial services as a representative of the Baloch nation in both Afghanistan and Russia, working to raise awareness for the national cause on international platforms.

In 1993, Balach Khan Marri returned to Balochistan, ending his self-exile to actively engage in the national struggle on the ground. He further extended his efforts internationally, traveling to the United Kingdom in 1999 to establish contacts with representatives of other oppressed nations and highlight the Baloch national question on various international forums.

The Path of Resistance

Balach Khan Marri held a deep skepticism regarding the Pakistani parliamentary system. Although he symbolically participated in the 2002 elections, his actions and words clearly defined his resistance to the system. During his oath-taking ceremony, he publicly pledged allegiance to Balochistan rather than the state.

In his inaugural speech, he powerfully articulated his rejection of the parliament, stating that assemblies "predominantly controlled by Punjab" could not address the wounds of oppressed nations, and that relying on such a "puppet assembly" was a "false belief" and a betrayal of the nation. He recognized the futility of symbolic representation and consequently attended only two sessions before dedicating his time entirely to organizing the national struggle for freedom.

Man of Action

A man of action rather than mere rhetoric, Balach Khan Marri was well-educated and had meticulously studied other global resistance movements. He concluded that a militant front was inevitable to effectively resist Pakistan's state apparatus. Eschewing the political mainstream, he took the path of armed resistance, making his home in the mountains and leading the opposition against the Pakistani army for many years.

Shaheed Mir Balach Khan Marri embraced martyrdom on November 21, 2007, cementing his legacy as a distinguished Baloch guerrilla and revolutionary leader who chose the path of armed struggle for the independence of his nation.

On 20 October 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that Sarmachars (freedom fighters) of the BLA had carried out 34 high-intensity military operations over 12 days across various regions of Balochistan between 9 and 20 October 2026. In these attacks, 14 personnel of the occupying army and nine operatives of Military Intelligence and death squads were killed, while operational control and snap-checking on key highways continued successfully under the organisational policy of an “economic blockade.”

During these operations, the freedom fighters also captured a serving soldier of the Pakistani army. In face-to-face clashes with occupying forces on various fronts, six BLA fighters fought courageously and attained the highest status of martyrdom.

Amanullah Mengal, alias Meerak, who was severely injured in a quadcopter attack by the occupying army at Ziarat Cross, succumbed to his injuries and was martyred on 8 August 2026.

On 18 September 2026, intense clashes took place between the occupying Pakistani army and BLA fighters at Siah Chang in Chagai, resulting in the deaths and injuries of several occupying army personnel, while the brave BLA fighter Ishaq Shokat Baloch, alias Meeran Baloch, attained martyrdom while fighting courageously.

On 19 September 2026, a prolonged and bloody confrontation took place between the occupying Pakistani army and BLA fighters at Paroom in Panjgur. During these clashes, four personnel of the occupying army were killed, several were injured, and one military vehicle was destroyed. In this battle, four BLA fighters - Ali Baloch, alias Salman Baloch; Ikhtiyar Baloch, alias Fareed Baloch; Sanaullah Baloch, alias Shay Mureed; and Sohail Baloch, alias Haji Absar - fought heroically and attained the highest status of martyrdom.

Sohail Baloch, alias Haji Absar, son of Haji Baloch Khan, was a resident of Jaheen, Paroom, Panjgur. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in 2026 and served on the Paroom front in Panjgur. He was killed on September 19, 2026, in Paroom, Panjgur, Balochistan.

Sohail Baloch, alias Haji Absar, decided in 2026 to resist what he viewed as the enemy’s occupation, oppression, looting, enslavement, humiliation, and inhumane actions. With the aim of pursuing national liberation, defending his homeland, and restoring sovereignty, he chose to join the struggle through the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army. In accordance with the organization’s procedures, he was transferred to a training camp to complete basic training. There, he completed his courses with courage, sincerity, and honesty and participated enthusiastically in various organizational activities. Through his dedication and hard work, he soon came to be regarded within the organization as a capable and trusted comrade.

Sohail Baloch was deeply committed to the struggle for national liberation. He was able to remain composed under challenging battlefield conditions and was actively involved in confrontations with the enemy. Guided by his convictions, political awareness, and commitment to the organization, he remained active until his death. On September 19, alongside several of his comrades, he engaged in a confrontation with the enemy. According to this account, after inflicting significant losses, he lost his life while fighting for the freedom and defense of his homeland and what he believed would be a brighter future for his nation. His sacrifice is remembered by his supporters as part of the broader struggle to preserve their survival, identity, and freedom.

On 2 February 2022, sixteen members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayeen unit, the Majeed Brigade, carried out simultaneous attacks, nine in Noshki and seven on the Frontier Corps headquarters in Panjgur. The organization named this action "Operation Ganjal". 90 Pakistani security personnel were killed in Noshki and 105 in Panjgur.
In the BLA’s operation on the Noshki FC headquarters, 9 fidayeen participated. On 2 February 2022, Meerain Jamaldini (alias Zagrain) drove an VBEID into the camp’s main gate. Following this, Badil Baloch (alias Riyasat), Murad Aajo (alias Baba), Aneel Baloch (alias Balach), Yasir Noor (alias Saif), Aziz Zehri (alias Barag), Ibraheem Baloch (alias Kabeer), Deedag Bahar (alias Rauf) and Bilal Baloch (alias Wahid) entered the camp. As a result, 90 military personnel, including one officer, were killed, and a portion of the camp was destroyed.
The operation continued throughout the night. In the early morning of 3 February 2022, after their ammunition was exhausted, the remaining eight fidayeen took their own lives by firing their weapons.

On 25 August 2024 Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch announced the launch of a "Fidayeen Operation" named "Herof" across Balochistan. As part of this operation, fidayeen from the BLA's elite unit, Majeed Brigade, have attacked the main camp of the Pakistani forces in Bela and have successfully infiltrated it. Meanwhile, other BLA fighters have taken full control of all major highways across Balochistan, blocking them completely.
During Operation “Herof,” 44 attacks were carried out simultaneously at 40 locations across 13 districts of Balochistan. As a result, 130 Pakistani army personnel were killed and 55 were injured. In addition, gas pipelines were destroyed at 2 locations, railway tracks at 7 locations, and 2 bridges were blown up.
During the operation, 13 vehicles transporting minerals were set on fire. Blockades were also established at 14 locations across Balochistan, and 3 members of a “death squad” were killed.
As part of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayee (suicide) operation “Herof,” the BLA’s Majeed Brigade carried out an attack on the Pakistani army’s Bela camp. The Majeed Brigade maintained control of the camp for twenty hours, during which 68 enemy personnel were killed.
Nine fidayeen (self-sacrificing fighters) of the Majeed Brigade at Bela camp - Ghaus Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Talib), Mahal Baloch (alias Zilan Kurd), Rizwan Baloch (alias Hammal), Mohammad Baloch (alias Meerak), Fazal Gul Zehri (alias Shawaiz), Tayyab Baloch (alias Lala), Junaid Zehri (alias Kami), Mohammad Asif Nechari (alias Naveed), and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Khalid) - along with Shafqat (alias Dayar) of the Fateh Squad in Mastung, were martyred in the operation.
Ghaus Baksh Sumalani, alias Talib, and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani, alias Khalid, were brothers. They took part in the same operation and were martyred while defending their motherland.

Ashfaq Ahmad Mullazai, the 36 year old son of Khuda Baksh, a political worker and resident of Jail Road, Hudda, Quetta, was abducted on 28 May 2010 and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. His body was later dumped on Qambarani Road, Quetta, on 26 July 2010.

Riaz Baloch, the 35-year-old son of Sajin Baloch and a tractor driver from Dera Bugti, was forcibly disappeared by the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) during a raid on his home on 12 June 2026. The raid was led by CTD SHO Umar Khosa, who detained Riaz without due legal process. During his detention, he was subjected to severe torture.
According to his family, CTD officials demanded PKR 5 million in exchange for his release. After the payment was made, Riaz was released on 13 June 2026 in critical condition. Due to the severity of the torture he had endured, he was transferred to Aga Khan University Hospital in Karachi for medical treatment. He later succumbed to his injuries on 10 July 2026.

Sameer Baloch, son of Nasir Baloch, was a 17-year-old student and resident of the Goburd area of Mand. He was forcibly disappeared by the Frontier Corps (FC), part of the Pakistani security forces, from his home in Goburd, Mand, at approximately 2:00 a.m. on 24 October 2026.
After 15 days of enforced disappearance, his bullet-riddled body was recovered on 8 November 2026 near the water supply facility in the Dazin area of Tump, Balochistan.

Ehsan Baloch, son of Mohammad Hassan, was a 29-year-old resident of Kohsar Bazar, Jiwani, Gwadar. He was a graduate of the Science Department at the University of Turbat.
On 22 January 2026, at around 1:00 a.m., Ehsan was forcibly disappeared from his home by personnel from Pakistani Military Intelligence and the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD). For eight months, his family remained without answers. On 17 September 2026, his body was found dumped alongside the bodies of Hassan Rafiq and Nadil Baloch in Kuldan, Danuk, Gwadar, bearing severe signs of torture.
Ehsan was a graduate who carried a pen and dreamed of building a better life. Instead, his freedom was taken away, and he was disappeared to an unknown location. The pen in his hand was replaced by handcuffs, and after eight months, his family received his dead body.

On 28 October 2025, at approximately 6:30 PM, Burhan Uddin, son of Mohammad Naeem, was abducted and forcibly disappeared from his home in Bug Meeri by Pakistani state-backed death squads and Military Intelligence personnel. For over six months and fourteen days, his family endured unbearable uncertainty while demanding his safe recovery.
Instead of justice, his family was handed his tortured and lifeless body on 12 May 2026. His body was later found dumped in Kech Kour (Kech River), Turbat, bearing clear signs of severe torture.
He was a 19-year-old Zamyad (light truck) driver by profession. Originally from Naag Zamuran, he was residing in Bug Meeri, Turbat, where he worked hard to support his family.

data.fullName: Abdul Aziz Baloch, alias Mohammad Ibrahim
data.biography:
On 21 October 2025, a statement was issued by Baloch Khan, the spokesperson of the Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS), an umbrella alliance of Baloch armed organizations. The statement said that, in defence of the Baloch population in Zehri, Khuzdar, Balochistan, BRAS forces eliminated dozens of enemy personnel, while six freedom fighters embraced martyrdom. Among them was Abdulaziz Baloch,alias Mohammad Ibrahim

The statement added that the occupying Pakistani army attempted to advance for aggressive purposes in the Zehri area of Khuzdar, which is under the control of the Baloch Raaji Ajoi Sangar (BRAS), resulting in fierce clashes. Dozens of occupying army personnel were eliminated in these clashes, while six freedom fighters of the Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar were martyred in defence of the motherland.

Among the martyrs, Abdul Aziz Baloch and Hafiz Muhammad Umar Baloch were martyred on 26 September, while Sanaullah Baloch, Abdul Aziz Baloch, Rashid Ahmed Zehri, and Fiaz Jattak were martyred on 30 September.

Martyr Sangat Abdul Aziz Baloch alias Muhammad Ibrahim, son of Abdul Hakeem, also belonged to Kalat Khadi. He was an activist of resistance politics who did underground organizational work to create political consciousness and national awareness among the Baloch youth. Later, after joining Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), he played an active role in field operations. He was considered a figure of discipline, tolerance and ideological tenacity, who provided the intellectual basis for the struggle.

Saddam Baloch, son of Ali Nawaz, was a resident of Zehri, District Khuzdar, Balochistan. He received his early education from his hometown, Zehri, and was an FSc student at Balochistan Residential College Khuzdar and a member of BSO Azad Khuzdar Zone.
He played a key role in mobilizing Baloch youth to join the Baloch liberation struggle for the independence of their homeland. Many of his friends were abducted and later killed by security forces for practicing nationalist politics for their people. He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he stood firm with the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom.
He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising peaceful political expression. He joined BSO Azad at an early age and participated in every activity of the organization in his region.
He was a victim of target killing by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agency on 15th January 2010 during a rally of the Baloch National Front (BNF) at Degree College Khuzdar City, Balochistan. His body bore severe signs of torture. He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times.
His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a very young age will be remembered in the golden words of Baloch history.

Ali Haider Mohammad Shahi, alias Kamal, son of Shah Mohammad, was a resident of the Mian Ghundi area of Quetta. He joined the BLA in May 2025, served on the Mastung front, and was promoted to the rank of Patrol Commander. He was martyred on 22 August 2026 in Mastung, Balochistan.
Ali Haider was among the brave and courageous comrade who proved to be a scourge to the enemy on the battlefield. Through his battlefield leadership, practical life, and actions against the enemy, he demonstrated his strong individual character. Ali Haider joined the ranks of the Baloch Liberation Army in May 2025 and was transferred to the active and dynamic front in Mastung. After successfully completing the basic military courses, he was sent to the active battlefield in Mastung on the orders of the command, where, due to his individual abilities, he quickly understood the demands of the battlefield and began putting them into practice.

Martyr Ali Haider's military and administrative abilities proved highly destructive to the enemy on the active and dynamic ground in Mastung, and he took an active part in combat operations against the enemy. Recognizing these military and administrative abilities, the command assigned him patrol command responsibilities. He played an excellent role in advancing against the enemy in the area, establishing blockades on the main highways under operational-level strategic objectives, taking military measures in important military operations and public defense against the enemy, and carrying out important organizational responsibilities. His role, along with his fellow comrades, was very important in pushing the enemy back and maintaining organizational superiority in the area, and he remained committed to these responsibilities until the end.
This brave revolutionary commander from Quetta inflicted severe losses on the occupying enemy through his actions and conduct and played an important role in maintaining organizational strength, power, and territorial superiority. He continued fighting until the end while maintaining his positions against the enemy. After carrying out a devastating attack on the enemy and, together with his comrades, killing 13 enemy personnel and inflicting severe financial and human losses on them, he attained martyrdom. History will remember him as a great fighter and Sarmachar.

On 7 October 2024, a statement was issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch, stating that on 6 October 2024, the Majeed Brigade, the elite Fidayeen unit of the Baloch Liberation Army, targeted a high level convoy of Chinese engineers and investors leaving Jinnah Airport in Karachi in a Fidayeen attack. According to the statement, more than five Chinese engineers and investors were killed and more than twelve were injured. At least fifteen Pakistani military personnel assigned to protect them were also killed, with many others injured, including more than four high-ranking officers of the Pakistani army and intelligence agencies. As a result of the explosion, fifteen vehicles in the convoy were destroyed. Due to the careful tactics of the BLA, civilians were spared casualties in the blast despite the densely populated area.
This operation was carried out by Shah Fahad, alias Aftab; Saddam Baloch, alias Fareed and Sohail, alias Baba, of the BLA’s Majeed Brigade.
Sohail, alias Baba, son of Abdul Hameed, belonged to the Khudabadan area of Panjgur. A graduate, Sangat Sohail joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2017 and volunteered his services to the BLA’s Majeed Brigade in 2022. He was a versatile colleague with professional skills. During his seven-year struggle, he worked in the Urban Network, Mountain Front, Majeed Brigade, and ZIRAB, leaving a positive impression on all these units through his hard work and intelligence.

On 31 May 2025, Dilawar, alias Jasim, a member of the Baloch Liberation Army, was martyred after being injured in an armed attack by local agents of the Pakistani military. The martyred comrade Dilawar, son of Hamza Baloch, was from the Ligorak Bazaar area of Panjgur. He had been involved in the armed struggle since 2011 and spent fifteen years on the fronts of Saiji, Parom, Zamuran and Panjgur, fighting the enemy with unwavering courage. Every moment of Dilawar’s life was guided by the philosophy of national freedom or martyrdom, and he remained steadfast in his beliefs until his last breath.
Aftab Baloch, was a resident of the Mashkai area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 21 April 2015 in Balochistan.

On 13th April 2026, in the Barkhan area of Balochistan, Pakistani forces shelled and bombed civilian populations, killing twelve innocent Baloch civilians, including women and children, and seriously injuring three others.

The martyrs are:

- Ali, son of Sultan Umair, aged 40
- Babul, daughter of Gulzar, aged 30
- Mir Jan, son of Ali, aged 2
- Somri, daughter of Bhangan, aged 35
- Balach, son of Sabzo, aged 70
- Shari, aged 22
- Rehman, son of Balach, aged 18
- Naikho, daughter of Jamalan, aged 17
- Allah Bakhsh, son of Balach, aged 6
- Saddo, daughter of Balach, aged 13
- Hapo, daughter of Balach, aged 8
- Mahrang, daughter of Balach, aged 2

The injured are:

- Zarbibi, daughter of Sher, aged 55
- Hazar Khan, son of Balach, aged 9
- Israr, daughter of Balach, aged 15

This is not the first time that Pakistani forces have bombed civilians in Balochistan, targeting unarmed and innocent women and children as a form of collective punishment. Nor can this be considered “collateral damage.” Rather, the Pakistani state and its forces are deliberately targeting the Baloch people to maintain an atmosphere of fear in the region, suppress internal dissent, exploit Baloch coastal resources, and continue policies of genocide against the Baloch nation.

On 8 August 2016, terrorists attacked the Government Hospital in Quetta, Balochistan, in a suicide bombing and shooting. More than 70 people were killed, mainly lawyers, and more than 130 others were injured.
The majority of those killed were lawyers who had gathered at the hospital after the body of Advocate Bilal Anwar Kasi, president of the Balochistan Bar Association, was brought there. Kasi had been shot dead by a gunman near Mengal Chowk on Manno Jan Road in Quetta while he was leaving his home for his office.
Responsibility for the attack was claimed by various Islamist groups, including Jamaat-ul-Ahrar and the Islamic State Khorasan Province. However, nationalist groups have alleged that these extremist organisations are backed by the Pakistani state and its military to counter the nationalist movement in the region and exploit its natural resources.
Estimates of the death toll ranged between 70 people, while more than 120 were injured. Of those killed, 54 were lawyers. Among them, 15 were Baloch by ethnicity, while the majority were Pashtuns by ethnicity.

The Baloch advocates or lawyers who were killed are identified as follows:

01 Ghulam Farooq Badini, son of Haji Abdul Ghani.
02 Bashir Ahmed Qazi, son of Qazi Ahmed Jan.
03 Bashir Ahmad Zehri, son Haji Mir Ahmed Zehri.
04 Naseer Ahmed Langove, son Abdul Rahim.
05 Chakar Khan Rind, son of Mehmood.
06 Abdul Rashid, son of Abdul Latif.
07 Nooruddin Rakshani, son Haji Naseeruddin.
08 Muhammad Imran, son Ghulam Farooq.
09 Munir Ahmed Mengal, son Ghulam Murtaza.
10 Sangat Jehan Jamaldini, son of Dr. Jahanzaib.
11 Mohammad Ali Satakzai, son of Taj Mohammad Khan.
12 Mehmood Ahmed Lehri, son Haji Abdul Hameed.
13 Jamil Ur Rehman, son of Qazi Abdul Hameed.
14 Amanullah Langove, son of Haji Dad Karim.
15 Sabir Ali, son of Abdul Rasheed.

Munir Ahmed Mengal is remembered by his colleagues as a compassionate soul who worked for the marginalised.
He was 46 years old.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Sohail Ahmed, alias Sangar, son of Rasool Bakhsh Sumalani, was a resident of Killi Jamaldini, Noshki. He joined the BLA in February 2025 and joined the Majeed Brigade in May 2025.
Sohail Ahmed belonged to the resistant land of Noshki, a soil that has always produced figures of resistance, steadfastness, and sacrifice. Raised in the embrace of this land, when Sohail Ahmed joined the armed struggle for national liberation, he was no longer just an individual; rather, like his chosen name “Sangar,” he became a strong trench of resistance in the struggle. His personality reflected quiet determination, deep commitment, and selfless love for his homeland. With this ideological maturity and revolutionary conviction, he immediately joined the Majeed Brigade after becoming part of the BLA, dedicating his life to the cause of national liberation.
Sohail Ahmed, alias Sangar, was present on the Noshki front during Operation Herof Phase 2, where he fought a fierce, organized, and decisive battle against the enemy alongside the Herofi force. In this long and difficult battle, Sangar remained steadfast on the front line until the final moment. Putting the philosophy of sacrifice into practice, he offered his life and thus engraved his name forever in the history of the war of freedom. Sangar’s martyrdom became a symbol of the resolve that every step taken on the path of freedom writes a new story in the pages of history.

In 1838, the British sent a force led by Alexander Burnes to reinstate Shah Shuja Durrani as the king of Afghanistan by deposing Amir Dost Mohammad Khan. To reach Afghanistan, they needed passage through Balochistan, particularly the Bolan Pass. However, Khan Mehrab Khan refused to allow the British to use his land to attack a neighboring country. The British sent Lieutenant Leach to negotiate with the Baloch government, but the Khan stood firm. When British forces reached Shaal via Bolan, some patriotic Baloch, without the Khan’s knowledge, attacked British troops out of nationalist sentiment and a desire to protect their homeland.
After toppling Amir Dost Mohammad Khan, the British Governor General of India, Lord Auckland, ordered an attack on Balochistan. In 1839, around 7,000 British troops marched from Shaal to attack the Baloch Meeri (capital). Anticipating an invasion, Khan Mehrab Khan declared war and sent messages to tribal leaders, but many saw the British as allies rather than invaders and chose to collaborate with them rather than defend their land. When Khan Mehrab Khan gathered his resistance fighters, the number of loyal warriors had dwindled to only 700 due to the short sightedness of many tribal chiefs. Nevertheless, Mehrab Khan was determined to fight. At his court, a respected figure, Akhund Muhammad Siddiq, advised him that he was not in a position to wage war at that time. He suggested that the Khan should leave Kalat with his companions, regroup and strengthen his forces, and then launch an attack against the British when the time was right, on 13 November 1839, the British forces launched an attack on Kalat, and a fierce battle ensued. During the fighting, Khan Mehrab Khan Baloch was martyred by a British bullet.

Among those martyred alongside him were:

Diwan Bacha Mal, Minister of Finance

Diwan Khem Chand

Diwan Asardas Mukhi, from the Hindu Panchayat of Kalat

Abdul Karim Raisani, brother of Sardar Asad Khan Raisani

Sardar Wali Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (maternal uncle of Martyr Amir Mehrab Khan)

Mir Taj Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (cousin of Mehrab Khan)

Mir Muhammad Ali Shahizai Mengal

Mir Fazal Muhammad Lehri, brother of Sardar Muhammad Khan Lehri

Sardar Zaman Khan Pandrani

Mir Dad Karim Chandozai Shahwani

Mir Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Mir Badal Khan, brother of Sardar Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Khan Muhammad Dehwaar, Arbab-e-Kalat.

Mir Nabi Bakhsh Jatoi, from the Narmak region of Kalat

Mir Qaiser Khan Bizenjo

Mir Shah Dost Bizenjo

Muhammad Raza Waziri Khel

Noor Muhammad Shahizai, son of Polat Sagaar Sarmastani, in charge of the armory

Taj Muhammad Shagasi

On 26 November 2025, Mohammad Allam, son of Mulla Bakhsh, aged 26 and a resident of Grisha, Kohat, was shot dead by state-backed armed groups. He was travelling to Rowaat, a nearby village, along the Mashkai bypass road to visit his father-in-law’s family when masked gunmen opened fire directly at him, killing him on the spot.
Eyewitnesses reported that Mohammad Allam was indiscriminately targeted by Pakistani military-sponsored armed groups. He was the sole provider for his family, which included a disabled brother, an elderly father, and young children.

On 22 July 2026, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) released the details of seven martyred members of the organization: Abdul Ghafoor, alias Chakar, son of Jan Mohammad; Imdad Baloch, alias Nodh, son of Rahmatullah; Hafiz Mumtaz Baloch, alias Zeerak, son of Sabir Ali; Hafiz Zaid Baloch, alias Sagaar, son of Mullah Khudadad; Yasir Baloch, alias Ajiz, son of Mohammad Ayub; Shahjan Baloch, alias Sawad, son of Ali Mohammad; and Ali Raza Baloch, alias Shayhaq, son of Haji Ali Ahmad. They were martyred in a drone strike by Pakistani forces on 29 January 2026 in the Pardan area of Panjgur District, Balochistan.

Ali Raza Baloch, alias Shayhaq, son of Haji Ali Ahmed, was a resident of Tasp, Panjgur. He was a BS Sociology graduate from the Islamic International University Islamabad. He joined the BLA on 21 October 2024 and served on the Panjgur front. He was martyred on 29 January 2026 in the Pardan area of Panjgur.
Ali Raza Baloch, alias Shayhaq, was an educated and conscious young man who had studied at a prestigious educational institution. As he continued his intellectual journey, he decided to put his convictions into practice through the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army. Following Operation Herof I in 2024, he joined the organization’s camp, where he completed his basic military training courses as a capable cadre. He was intellectually and politically mature and was fully committed to the ideology of national liberation and the restoration of a Baloch state. This intellectual and ideological conviction led him to believe that there could be no scholarly justification for Pakistan, which he viewed as an artificial state, to occupy a civilization and culture spanning thousands of years, such as that of the Baloch people.
After completing his training courses, he began working alongside his fellow Sarmachars against the enemy in Panjgur and its surrounding areas, remaining at the forefront of several operations against them. Along with his intellectual abilities, he had considerable experience in mine warfare and took part in mine-laying operations on the battlefield on numerous occasions. He also possessed a strong desire to learn and gain experience. Whatever responsibilities were assigned to him, he learned them quickly and developed a deep understanding of them. As a result, after joining the camp, he quickly adopted modern concepts of warfare and incorporated them into his practical activities.
Instead of continuing his personal professional life and serving within the administrative structure of the state, he dedicated his abilities and efforts to the struggle for national liberation, demonstrating his belief that collective life holds true meaning and importance. The sacrifices he made for the restoration of a Baloch state will never be forgotten, and future generations will witness their impact.

On 12 August 2026, several Baloch people, including women and children, were killed and several others were injured as a result of an aerial bombardment of a civilian population by the Pakistan Air Force, reportedly using American-made F-16 fighter aircraft, in the Gidar Gindan area of Surab District, Balochistan. Following the airstrike, the injured and deceased were transported by police and local residents to DHQ Hospital in Surab, where the injured received medical treatment.

The families of the deceased and local residents subsequently began a protest by placing the bodies at Surab Main Chowk on the Quetta–Karachi National Highway (N-25). As a result, traffic on the highway was disrupted, with long queues of vehicles forming on both sides. Videos and photographs of the protest subsequently circulated widely on social media under the hashtag #SurabMassacre.

Those killed in the airstrike were identified as Shabir Ahmad Sumalani, son of Khudadad Sumalani, a resident of Marap, Surab; Noor Jan Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, a resident of Gindan; Karim Dad Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, a resident of Gandan; Raj Babu, wife of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani; Safia, wife of Noor Jan Mirwani; and Jalal Mirwani, son of Noor Jan Mirwani.

Those injured were identified as Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, son of Jan Muhammad Mirwani; Abdul Karim Mirwani, son of Jan Muhammad Mirwani; Mehrullah Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani; Nadeem Mirwani, son of Abdul Salam Mirwani; Shoaib Mirwani, son of Abdul Karim Mirwani; Sarah, wife of Baseer Ahmed Mirwani; Sabira, wife of Tufail Ahmed Mirwani; Zamra, daughter of Abdul Aziz Mirwani; Hajira, wife of Abdul Fattah Mirwani; Asim, son of Baseer, aged 1; Rahabia, daughter of Abdul Karim, aged 3; Sadia, daughter of Abdul Salam, aged 5; Fatima, daughter of Abdul Karim, aged 7; Zia-ur-Rehman, son of Abdul Karim, aged 2; Amir, son of Abdul Karim, aged 1; and Hasina, daughter of Muhammad Aslam, aged 4.

Following a detailed technical and scientific analysis of remnants of rocket components recovered from debris at the site of the aerial bombardment, important evidence reportedly emerged indicating that the recovered fragments belonged to an air-launched missile fired from an F-16 fighter aircraft.

Photographs of the recovered debris and the subsequent technical analysis reportedly indicated that the fragment was part of an AIM-120 Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile (AMRAAM), an American-made air-to-air missile.

Key technical evidence and serial numbers

According to the information and serial numbers reportedly engraved on the surface of the debris, the following details were recorded:

Assembly Number: ASSY 872128-1

Serial Number: 09-987138

Date of Manufacture: 09/09 (September 2009)

According to open-source intelligence (OSINT) records, the part number “872128-1” reportedly corresponds to the control section and rocket motor assembly of an AMRAAM missile manufactured by the American defense company Raytheon. Based on this evidence and the reported matching serial numbers, it is claimed that the debris was not part of an aircraft’s internal structure but instead consisted of remnants from an operational missile fired from an F-16 aircraft.

On 25 August 2024 Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch announced the launch of a "Fidayeen Operation" named "Herof" across Balochistan. As part of this operation, fidayeen from the BLA's elite unit, Majeed Brigade, have attacked the main camp of the Pakistani forces in Bela and have successfully infiltrated it. Meanwhile, other BLA fighters have taken full control of all major highways across Balochistan, blocking them completely.
During Operation “Herof,” 44 attacks were carried out simultaneously at 40 locations across 13 districts of Balochistan. As a result, 130 Pakistani army personnel were killed and 55 were injured. In addition, gas pipelines were destroyed at 2 locations, railway tracks at 7 locations, and 2 bridges were blown up.
During the operation, 13 vehicles transporting minerals were set on fire. Blockades were also established at 14 locations across Balochistan, and 3 members of a “death squad” were killed.
As part of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayee (suicide) operation “Herof,” the BLA’s Majeed Brigade carried out an attack on the Pakistani army’s Bela camp. The Majeed Brigade maintained control of the camp for twenty hours, during which 68 enemy personnel were killed.
Nine fidayeen (self-sacrificing fighters) of the Majeed Brigade at Bela camp - Ghaus Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Talib), Mahal Baloch (alias Zilan Kurd), Rizwan Baloch (alias Hammal), Mohammad Baloch (alias Meerak), Fazal Gul Zehri (alias Shawaiz), Tayyab Baloch (alias Lala), Junaid Zehri (alias Kami), Mohammad Asif Nechari (alias Naveed), and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Khalid) - along with Shafqat (alias Dayar) of the Fateh Squad in Mastung, were martyred in the operation.
Ghaus Baksh Sumalani, alias Talib, and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani, alias Khalid, were brothers. They took part in the same operation and were martyred while defending their motherland.
Shahnawaz Baloch, was a resident of the Mashkai area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 21 April 2015 in Balochistan.

data.martyrdomPlace: Noshki and Kharan mountainous area, Balochistan
data.biography:
In a face to face battle with the Pakistani military and its agents in the mountainous regions of Noshki and Kharan on 24 September 2021, more than a dozen enemy personnel were killed, whereas six freedom fighters, including five members of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), also embraced martyrdom.
The battle commenced early Friday morning in Siyah Lop, near Baddo Dor, when enemy forces attempted to encircle a patrolling party of Baloch freedom fighters. In the face-to-face battle, which lasted for more than four hours, scores of enemy personnel were killed and injured. Five freedom fighters of the BLA and one freedom fighter of the United Baloch Army (UBA), while evacuating their comrades from the battle zone, embraced martyrdom.
The fallen comrades include Commander Ganjal alias Comrade Mazar, Nazeer alias Sangar, Faisal alias Yasir, Kaleem alias Bolani, and Rehan alias Mehrwaan, all members of the Baloch Liberation Army. A member of the United Baloch Army, Nodaan alias Hammal, bravely fought alongside BLA comrades and embraced martyrdom.
Faisal Rodeni, alias Yasir, belonged to Sorab town and had joined the BLA three years earlier. After fulfilling his role in the urban units of the BLA for several years, he was deployed to the mountainous battlefronts following an organisational decision.
Adil Raheem, was a resident of the Awaran area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 19 April 2016 in Balochistan.

Uzaifa Baloch, also known as Ganjal, son of Abdul Hameed, belonged to Jiwani, Kaushara. He had been a member of the Baloch Liberation Army for a year and, despite his young age, carried out his duties with extraordinary discipline and responsibility. On November 16, 2025, while on duty at the Kilkor front, he was bitten by a snake and succumbed to the poison within a few hours, despite receiving first aid. He was soft-spoken, dignified, and a quiet yet remarkable comrade. His martyrdom demonstrates that Baloch freedom fighters not only face the enemy’s bullets with determination but also dedicate their lives to the motherland, even in the face of unforeseen circumstances.

On 29 November 2022, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 26 November 2022, at 6:00 am, the Pakistani army fired hundreds of missiles from Iranian kamikaze drones in and around the Siakoh area of Kahan, Kohlu district of Balochistan. Out of these, two missiles fell within the premises of a BLA camp located in Siakoh. As a result, eight freedom fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army embraced martyrdom.
Afterward, the enemy launched a large scale ground and air operation in Kahan and adjoining areas. The spokesperson stated that for a long time Pakistan and Iran have maintained joint military cooperation against the Baloch national cause, including intelligence coordination. They also exchange advanced and lethal weapons.
In the first phase of the operation, following the drone attacks, several special forces commandos were dropped from around a dozen Pakistan Army combat helicopters, and shelling began from the air. Subsequently, military troops from Kohlu, Dera Bugti, and nearby areas - consisting of more than 400 personnel - participated in the operation using several armored and other military vehicles.
As soon as the Pakistani army initiated the operation, nearby BLA camps in the area began countering the enemy’s advance from different fronts by adopting a joint defense strategy.
The combat between the enemy forces and the freedom fighters continued intermittently until the evening. As a result, the freedom fighters inflicted heavy casualties on the Pakistani forces from all sides. Breaking the army’s land and air siege through skilled combat tactics, they carried their injured comrades, along with weapons and other sensitive equipment, to safe locations.
During the conflict, after several hours of fierce resistance by the fighters, the army turned its guns toward the local population in Nissau, Siakoh, Drehis, Parhki, Jantali, and adjoining areas. The enemy set fire to many houses and severely tortured residents. Meanwhile, troops stopped two innocent Baloch pedestrians and killed them.
The organization’s fighters who embraced martyrdom were - Gahmar Khan alias Garra, Thal Khan alias Thallu, Hameed Baloch alias Sado
Shadi Khan alias Kooda, Abu Bakr Baloch alias Rehan, Jameel alias Naadi
Kareem Khan alias Jamal, Muhammad Nusrat alias Asif - The organization also rejected reports claiming that BLA fighters had been arrested during the operation. Through the media, it challenged ISPR to substantiate its narrative with concrete evidence.

On 7 September 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 4 September 2026, as part of an operation, the BLA launched a coordinated attack on an enemy post at Garri in the Panjpai area of Balochistan. Freedom fighters of the BLA heavily targeted the enemy’s Saidal Kach post with rocket launchers and modern weapons. In the fierce battle that lasted from 2 pm to 4 pm, ten soldiers of the occupying forces were killed and several others were injured. During this battle, a brave BLA soldier, Nisar Ahmed, alias Yasir, sacrificed his life while fighting bravely for the country.
The spokesperson stated that during the attack on the Saidal Kach Frontier Corps (FC) base, the occupying enemy forces hid in their trenches. BLA commanders, under the leadership of Nisar Ahmed, delivered effective blows to the enemy as a bold and effective war strategy. Nisar Ahmed, alias Yasir, who sacrificed his life for the Baloch motherland, had joined the BLA three years before his martyrdom. In a short period of time, he played a prominent role on both the urban and mountainous fronts. He was associated with the urban network in Quetta for one year. For the past two years, he fulfilled his national responsibilities as a frontline fighter on the BLA war fronts in a dedicated and sincere manner. The young fighters were highly impressed by his war strategy and guerrilla warfare skills.

On April 16, 2026, in Panjgur, Pakistani forces reportedly killed four Baloch individuals in a staged encounter and brought their tortured bodies to Panjgur Hospital, claiming they were killed during a combat engagement. However, the victims have been identified as individuals who had previously been subjected to enforced disappearance by Pakistani military institutions. Among them was 18-year-old student Marwan, son of Hamza Baloch and a resident of Shapatan, Panjgur. He had been forcibly disappeared by FC personnel from Legork Paroom and was later killed alongside three other previously disappeared individuals in this staged encounter.

Following the deadly SVBEID bombing at a Pakistani Coast Guard camp in Jiwani, Balochistan, on 3 July 2026, carried out by Attaullah Baloch, alias Ajmal, of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) Majeed Brigade Fidayee Unit, which took the lives of more than 30 Pakistani security personnel, Pakistani forces, in reaction, extrajudicially killed four Baloch on the very next day, 4 July 2026 - Mohammad Abdul Haq, son of Mohammad Murad; Chakar, son of Hassa Baksh; Peeri Assa and Shah Baksh Omar, son of Omar - in a staged encounter and claimed that they had been killed in the Jiwani attack. Later, all four were identified as previously forcibly disappeared persons.

Mohammad Abdul Haq, son of Muhammad Murad, was a teacher, school principal, and resident of Mondi, Gwadar. He was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces during a raid on his home on 24 January 2026. From that day onward, his whereabouts remained unknown. His family spent months searching for him while government officials repeatedly assured them that he would be released, urging them not to raise the case publicly.
Following the deadly bombing in Jiwani, Pakistani forces extrajudicially killed four forcibly disappeared individuals and dumped their bodies. Mohammad Abdul Haq was among them. After months in custody, he was tortured and killed. His killing reflects a recurring pattern in Balochistan, where forcibly disappeared Baloch are later killed and portrayed as militants following major security incidents and security failures.
Mohammad Abdul Haq was more than an educator; he was the pillar of a family already devastated by enforced disappearance. He was the uncle of Ali Haider, who, as a child, walked from Karachi to Islamabad in 2013 to demand the return of his father, Mohammad Ramazan, who was forcibly disappeared on the Makran Coastal Highway in July 2010. Sixteen years later, instead of returning Mohammad Ramazan, the state took the life of the man who had assumed the responsibility of raising and supporting his brother's children.

On April 15, 2025, a statement issued by Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS) claimed that BRAS freedom fighters killed 22 personnel of the occupying Pakistani Army in attacks in Noshki and Barkhan (Chamalang). During these operations, the freedom fighters captured the main camp of the occupying army. In the ensuing clashes, the enemy forces were forced to retreat, and five BRAS freedom fighters were martyred while fighting the Pakistani Army.
On April 9, 2025, the occupying Pakistani Army attempted to advance on a side camp of Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS) freedom fighters after conducting a drone attack at Dadar in the Chamalang area of Barkhan.
Among the comrades martyred in Chamalang was Aaqil Hashmi, alias Chirag, also known as Professor, son of Hashim, from the Shahrak area of Kech. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in 2020 and fought against national oppression. Earlier, he had been a member of the Baloch Students Organization, where he educated and equipped Baloch youth with ideas of national liberation.
Sangat Aaqil, alias Chirag, who served on the fronts of Bolan, Barkhan, Chamalang, and Koh-e-Sulaiman, had completed his M.Phil in Political Science from the International Islamic University (IIUI), Islamabad.
Martyr Sangat Aaqil, alias Professor Chirag, was serving as the unit commander of the Fatah Squad, a special unit of the BLA. He was not only an outstanding guerrilla fighter but also a source of guidance, from whose intelligence and experience other fighters greatly benefited.
Another comrade martyred in Chamalang was Ghulam Raza, alias Kabeer, son of Ali Gul, from Holangi Tank in the Raskoh area of Kharan. Having grown up in the foothills of Raskoh, Ghulam Raza joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in 2022 and fought against national oppression as an urban guerrilla. A year later, he moved to the Barkhan front.
Armed with the consciousness of national liberation, Martyr Sangat Raza was a hardworking and kind-hearted comrade. He inflicted heavy blows on the enemy in numerous battles on the Barkhan front.
The third comrade martyred in Chamalang was Mohsin, alias Durra, son of Mayar, from the Gulshanabad area of Turbat. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2023 and initially served as an urban guerrilla. After striking the enemy army in Turbat city and its surrounding areas for a year, he moved to the mountain front in 2024.
Sangat Mohsin served against national oppression on the Barkhan front. He had the ability to make critical decisions in extremely difficult situations — a quality he demonstrated by shooting himself with the “last bullet” in the throat rather than being captured alive by the enemy.

On 2 February 2022, sixteen members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayeen unit, the Majeed Brigade, carried out simultaneous attacks, nine in Noshki and seven on the Frontier Corps headquarters in Panjgur. The organization named this action "Operation Ganjal". 90 Pakistani security personnel were killed in Noshki and 105 in Panjgur.
In the BLA’s operation on the Noshki FC headquarters, 9 fidayeen participated. On 2 February 2022, Meerain Jamaldini (alias Zagrain) drove an VBEID into the camp’s main gate. Following this, Badil Baloch (alias Riyasat), Murad Aajo (alias Baba), Aneel Baloch (alias Balach), Yasir Noor (alias Saif), Aziz Zehri (alias Barag), Ibraheem Baloch (alias Kabeer), Deedag Bahar (alias Rauf) and Bilal Baloch (alias Wahid) entered the camp. As a result, 90 military personnel, including one officer, were killed, and a portion of the camp was destroyed.
The operation continued throughout the night. In the early morning of 3 February 2022, after their ammunition was exhausted, the remaining eight fidayeen took their own lives by firing their weapons.

Shakoor Baloch was a resident of Pullabad, Tump, Balochistan. He was abducted by Pakistani forces on June 25, 2023, in Pullabad, Tump. After six months, on November 22, 2023, he was killed by the CTD in a fake encounter along with three others - Balach Baloch, Wadood Baloch, and Saif Baloch - in Banuk-e-Chadahi, Turbat, in the Kech district of Balochistan.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Maryam Buzdar, alias Sammi, was a resident of Allah Abad Colony, Dera Ghazi Khan. She joined the Majeed Brigade on 3rd March 2023 and was part of Operation Herof Phase Two.
Maryam Buzdar joined the Baloch Liberation Army with clear awareness, a strong sense of responsibility, and ideological commitment. Becoming part of the Majeed Brigade in 2023 marked a formal, serious, and decisive phase in her life, during which she chose the path of practical struggle.
Her husband, Rasheed Buzdar alias Meeral, was also a fidayee. Both Maryam and Rasheed had wished to carry out a fidayee mission together, but circumstances made this impossible. During an enemy offensive, Rasheed Buzdar attained martyrdom while he was preparing for his fidayee mission. After his martyrdom, the morally degraded and barbarous enemy displayed brutality by beheading him and taking his head away.
Despite Rasheed Buzdar’s martyrdom and the events that followed, Maryam Buzdar’s resolve did not weaken. She remained firm in her decision and demonstrated that resistance is not merely a reaction, but an informed, responsible, and conscious course of action.
Maryam Buzdar made the ultimate sacrifice on the third day of Operation Herof 2.0 at the Noshki front. She achieved martyrdom while taking part in close-quarters combat inside the Pakistani military’s main headquarters in Noshki on 2nd February 2026.
Musafir Baloch, son of Pir Dad and a resident of Apsar, Turbat, was shot and killed by members of a state-backed death squad. Musafir is a driver by profession.

On November 12, 2024, in the Balgatar area, during an organizational mission, the comrades of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) were martyred while bravely fighting the enemy. The martyrs include Second Lieutenant Azum, alias Qasim, son of Muhammad Rahim, a resident of Teertej Awaran; Second Lieutenant Anwar, alias Sana, son of Hussain, a resident of Red Tok Balgatar; Arab Nawaz, alias Jahanzaib, a resident of Gresha; and Zaheer, alias Azad, son of Fazal, a resident of Biront Keelkor. They all sacrificed their lives in defense of their motherland.

Suhrab Baloch was a prominent leader and former Vice Chairman of the Baloch Students Organization (BSO) Mutahida, as well as one of its founding members. He played a vital role in promoting and strengthening student politics among Baloch youth, inspiring a generation to engage in political and social activism. He was killed by Pakistani forces on 6 February 2008.

On the night of September 21, 2024, at around 9:00 PM, fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) attacked a post of the occupying Pakistani Army and a mobile phone tower in the Uchti area of Barkhan, setting the tower and its machinery on fire. Immediately after the attack, members of the death squads arrived at the scene and began firing indiscriminately. One group of armed death squad members pursued the fighters, who were already lying in wait. It is important to note that these death squads, created to assist the occupying Pakistani Army, have been patrolling the area for a long time, harassing the Baloch people and extorting money from them.
The strategy behind attacking the military post and the mobile tower was to lure the death squads, led by the state’s so-called Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti and his brother Aftab Bugti, out of their safe zone and punish them for their extortion activities. The fighters successfully executed this strategy.
After the operation, the fighters anticipated pursuit by the death squads and positioned themselves in ambush. As soon as the death squad arrived, the fighters launched a heavy attack. The skirmish continued from the night of September 21 until the following day, resulting in the deaths of 11 death squad members and injuries to several others, including Aftab Bugti, the brother of the puppet Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti.
On September 23, another clash occurred between the fighters and the death squad, in which one more death squad member was eliminated. Later in September 2024, two additional death squad members were eliminated in another skirmish.
Fighters from allied organizations, including the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) and the Baloch Republican Guard (BRG), fought alongside BLF fighters during the operation. After completing the operation, the fighters retreated to a safe location. However, on September 27, Pakistani forces and death squads attempted to encircle the fighters in the Chitri Gorchani area, leading to another skirmish in which three members of the forces and death squads were killed.
During this intense battle, BLA fighter Imran Langove, known as “Meerain Baloch,” was martyred. The organization honors him with the highest respect. Martyr Imran Langove was a brave and patriotic fighter, highly skilled in warfare. He had been associated with the BLA for the past one and a half years. With exceptional battle tactics, he courageously blocked the enemy’s advance, ensured the safe escape of his comrades, and ultimately embraced martyrdom while adhering to the philosophy of “the last bullet.”

On 14 July 2010, Habib Jalib Baloch was killed by two gunmen affiliated with Pakistani intelligence agencies outside his home in Musa Colony, Quetta, Balochistan.
He was the Secretary General of the Balochistan National Party (Mengal).

On December 14, 2024 three brave BLA fighters were martyred in SabzKoh, Panjgur, while valiantly resisting a Pakistani military offensive. That morning, Pakistani forces launched a large-scale air and ground operation, deploying hundreds of troops, SSG commandos, gunship helicopters, and drones. At SabzKoh, BLA fighters engaged in an intense battle from 10 AM to 3 PM. Commander Majeed Baloch, Commander Diljan Baloch, and fighter Zakir Jan fought courageously before embracing martyrdom.
Senior Commander Shaheed Majeed Baloch, alias Murtaza Kareem, belonged to Khudabadan, Panjgur. He joined BLA in 2012 and was among the organization’s most significant and invaluable commanders. He began his armed struggle from the Bolan front in 2012 and was later associated with the Shoor and Parod fronts in Kalat for a considerable period. Before his martyrdom, he was commanding operations in various regions of Panjgur, Washuk, and Makran. He was an exceptional commander who played a vital role in organizing BLA. His personality embodied sincerity, honesty, intelligence, perseverance, and resilience, with countless qualities hidden within him that history will always remember.

Wahid Suwali, son of Suwali, a resident of Nasirabad, Turbat, Kech, was abducted, subjected to inhumane torture, and brutally killed by the death squad with the Frontier Corps and Military Intelligence of Pakistan’s security apparatus.
Wahid Siwali, a young labourer in Dubai who had recently returned to Balochistan to visit his family, was forcibly abducted on June 2, 2025, from Civil Hospital Turbat by death squad and MI.
During his two-day captivity, Wahid was subjected to extreme and barbaric torture. His fingers and feet were amputated while he was alive, and his body bore signs of severe mutilation and abuse. After enduring unimaginable pain, he was shot dead. His mutilated body was later dumped in a deserted area near Pasni Cross.
