data.biography: Rasool Baksh Baloch was a resident of the Gebun area of Turbat, Kech. He had been affiliated for years with a pro-independence armed organization, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF). Pakistan’s military forces carried out a military operation across the entire Gebun area of Turbat, Kech, at midnight on December 5, 2012. During this operation, three people - Rasool Baksh Baloch, Mulla Baksh Baloch, and Hakeem Baloch - embraced martyrdom.

data.martyrdomPlace: Fatah Ali Bazar, Gwargo, Panjgur district, Balochistan
data.biography:
On 3 October 2026, Pakistani forces carried out an aerial bombing using a quadcopter drone targeting civilians in Fateh Ali Bazaar, Gwargo, in Panjgur district of Balochistan.

The attack resulted in the martyrdom of two children: 9 year old Arman Anwar, son of Anwar and 10 year old Amal Salim, son of Salim Jan.

Three other children were injured: 9 year old Shahid, 7 year old Zahid, son of Shahid and 12 year old Noorullah, son of Rafiq.

Noor ul Haq Baloch, son of Allah Baksh, was born in Nokjo, Mashkai, on 20th May 1983. He received his elementary education in Nokjo itself. For further studies, he moved to Khuzdar Degree College, where he completed his FSc (Higher Secondary education).
During his student life, he was an active member of the Baloch Students Organization (BSO). He was one of those people who could not remain indifferent to the suffering of his Baloch homeland. His passion and dream of a free Balochistan, and of giving the Baloch people their rightful place, motivated him to join the armed struggle, which he believed was the only way forward. Under the banner of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF), he actively opposed the enemy.
On 18th May 2005, during a mission to plant a roadside bomb near Meerani Dam in Turbat, an explosive device detonated while he was setting it up, resulting in his death.
data.martyrdomPlace: Meerani Dam, Nasirabad, Turbat district, Balochistan

data.biography:
On 3 February 2024, the Pakistani Army’s Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) issued a statement declaring that 24 terrorists had been neutralized in a military operation conducted in the Mach area of Bolan. The operation was launched in response to Operation Darra-e-Bolan, an operation launched by the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), a Baloch pro-independence militant group, in the Mach area of Bolan district. The group reportedly maintained control of the area for three days.

However, subsequent investigations revealed that four of the deceased individuals had previously been reported as victims of enforced disappearances, and some of their cases had been registered with Baloch human rights organizations.

The identities of the deceased individuals were confirmed as follows:

- Bashir Ahmed, son of Haji Khan Marri, a resident of Mashriqi Bypass, Quetta, who was forcibly disappeared on 2 July 2023.

- Arman Marri, son of Nihal Khan Marri, a resident of Mashriqi Bypass, Quetta, who was forcibly disappeared on 2 July 2023.

- Sobadar, son of Gulzar Khan Tengani, a resident of the Main Kor area of Harnai district, who was forcibly disappeared on 9 September 2023.

- Shakil, son of Ramzan, a resident of the Mishk area of Zehri, Khuzdar district.

The family members of Bashir and Arman were also actively participating in a sit-in protest in Islamabad. Organized by the Baloch Yakjehti Committee (BYC), the sit-in was held outside the National Press Club to protest enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings.

The families tirelessly appealed to the government to secure the return of their forcibly disappeared loved ones, but all their pleas fell on deaf ears. Ultimately, they were devastated to receive the mutilated bodies of their young relatives, whom they believed had been victims of a staged encounter.

On 5 February 2024, when the family members went to Civil Hospital Quetta to receive the bodies, they were reportedly coerced into signing an unlawful form falsely stating that the deceased had links to militant groups and labeling them as terrorists. The family members refused to comply. Following a large demonstration, the bodies were eventually handed over to them.

On 29 November 2022, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 26 November 2022, at 6:00 am, the Pakistani army fired hundreds of missiles from Iranian kamikaze drones in and around the Siakoh area of Kahan, Kohlu district of Balochistan. Out of these, two missiles fell within the premises of a BLA camp located in Siakoh. As a result, eight freedom fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army embraced martyrdom.
Afterward, the enemy launched a large scale ground and air operation in Kahan and adjoining areas. The spokesperson stated that for a long time Pakistan and Iran have maintained joint military cooperation against the Baloch national cause, including intelligence coordination. They also exchange advanced and lethal weapons.
In the first phase of the operation, following the drone attacks, several special forces commandos were dropped from around a dozen Pakistan Army combat helicopters, and shelling began from the air. Subsequently, military troops from Kohlu, Dera Bugti, and nearby areas - consisting of more than 400 personnel - participated in the operation using several armored and other military vehicles.
As soon as the Pakistani army initiated the operation, nearby BLA camps in the area began countering the enemy’s advance from different fronts by adopting a joint defense strategy.
The combat between the enemy forces and the freedom fighters continued intermittently until the evening. As a result, the freedom fighters inflicted heavy casualties on the Pakistani forces from all sides. Breaking the army’s land and air siege through skilled combat tactics, they carried their injured comrades, along with weapons and other sensitive equipment, to safe locations.
During the conflict, after several hours of fierce resistance by the fighters, the army turned its guns toward the local population in Nissau, Siakoh, Drehis, Parhki, Jantali, and adjoining areas. The enemy set fire to many houses and severely tortured residents. Meanwhile, troops stopped two innocent Baloch pedestrians and killed them.
The organization’s fighters who embraced martyrdom were - Gahmar Khan alias Garra, Thal Khan alias Thallu, Hameed Baloch alias Sado
Shadi Khan alias Kooda, Abu Bakr Baloch alias Rehan, Jameel alias Naadi
Kareem Khan alias Jamal, Muhammad Nusrat alias Asif - The organization also rejected reports claiming that BLA fighters had been arrested during the operation. Through the media, it challenged ISPR to substantiate its narrative with concrete evidence.
Gahmar Khan alias Garra had been rendering national service from the BLA platform for the past 15 years. Earlier, he was associated with the organization as a sympathizer and supporter for a long time, and in 2007 he formally joined the struggle through the BLA. He was a commander and one of the most senior, sincere, experienced, and hardworking members.

On August 5, 2024, enemy agents martyred freedom fighter Sabir Baloch, alias Shahmen.
Sabir Baloch son of Dad Shah, a resident of Goristani Teertej, joined the national liberation struggle through the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in 2014. During the course of his struggle, Pakistani forces inflicted collective punishment on his family. However, despite facing severe state oppression and hardships, he and his family remained steadfastly committed to the freedom movement.
In 2016, his brother, Mohammad Azeem, was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. Later, his mutilated body was found dumped in Hub.
In 2023, during a military operation in the mountainous regions of Awaran, the Pakistani army contaminated natural springs with toxic chemicals. As a result, Sabir’s father, Dad Shah - a shepherd - was martyred after drinking the poisoned water.
Despite these atrocities, the family of Sabir Baloch remains more determined than ever and unwavering in their loyalty to the Baloch national liberation movement.

Doda Baloch, alias Sarbaz, son of Ibrahim Baloch, was a resident of the Kulanchi Pada area of Gwadar. He joined the BLA in 2026, served in Seyahji, and was martyred on 1 September 2026 in the Dasht area of Kech, Balochistan.
Doda Baloch, alias Sarbaz, understood the importance of the Baloch Liberation Army’s armed resistance as the central point in 2026 and became part of the intellectual, ideological, and state-building process of Baloch national liberation, taking up active operations against the enemy on the Makuran front. He actively participated in the organization’s military training courses and always carried out his responsibilities diligently. As a new cadre, he quickly embraced the new needs and demands of war and became active on the front lines, while also serving as a promising and capable sangat during organizational patrols.
Doda Baloch was a courageous and fearless fighter who, on numerous occasions, confronted the enemy with exceptional skill and inflicted crushing defeats on them. He took an active part in organizational activities in his assigned area, made organizational discipline the centerpiece of his practical work, and proved that Baloch fighters have today become a powerful front against the enemy in every respect. His sacrifices will be recorded in the pages of history alongside those of the great fighters who placed their homeland and national freedom above their own lives and sacrificed themselves for the attainment of that goal.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Bani Sumalani, alias Banri, spouse of Martyr Dur Mohammad alias Rostu, daughter of Yar Khan Sumalani and a resident of Gharbog, Bolan, Shahrag, joined the BLA in 2014. She was inducted into the Majeed Brigade in 2022 and was martyred on 3 February 2026 on the Noshki front.
Bani Baloch’s life was not simply a tale of individual sacrifice, but rather a symbol of the organizational discipline and ideological maturity that has shaped the Baloch Liberation Army into a structured political and military institution.
Since joining the BLA in 2014, Commander Bani Baloch did not establish her identity through any single moment or dramatic act, but through a sustained commitment over years of consistent service. She was among those cadre members who contributed to the foundational organization of the movement. Despite the harsh conditions of mountain encampments, persistent threats, and deprivation, her endurance transcended personal hardship and embodied organizational resilience.
Following her induction into the Majeed Brigade in 2022, her responsibilities expanded both militarily and morally. She oversaw the training of Fidayee fighters, maintained psychological cohesion within the ranks, and ensured operational discipline under pressure. Her style of leadership was defined not by spectacle or rhetoric, but by reason, principle, and consistency.
On a personal level, Commander Bani’s struggle was shared with her comrade and spouse, Martyr Dur Muhammad alias Rostu. He was not only a devoted partner but also a frontline guerrilla fighter who commanded during the most perilous stages of the conflict. For eight years, they shared not only a life together but also the burdens of a common revolutionary cause. When Dur Muhammad was martyred in an intense battle on 31 October 2022, Bani Baloch did not falter. She transformed her personal loss into intellectual resolve and recommitted herself to the organizational mission with even greater dedication.
During Operation Herof II, Commander Bani led the attack on the ISI headquarters in Noshki. As unit commander, she remained on the frontlines for three consecutive days, organizing and guiding her Fidayee unit under relentless fire. Until the moment of her martyrdom, she led from the front. During this period, she personally engaged in close combat and eliminat

Fida Hussain Jamaldini, alias Amir, son of Mohammad Omar, was a resident of the Kadi Deedar area of Noshki District in Balochistan. He joined the BLA in December 2023 and was martyred on the Noshki front during Operation Herof Phase 2.
Emerging from the rugged plains of Noshki, Fida Hussain Jamaldini, recognized among his comrades as “Amir,” was a silent yet deeply committed activist. After joining the BLA in December 2023, he fulfilled his responsibilities within the urban network with exceptional skill and secrecy. When the call for Operation Herof was sounded, Amir dedicated all his energies to halting the enemy’s advance on the Noshki front. He demonstrated unwavering steadfastness until his last breath and embraced martyrdom.
Ayub Faqeer, alias Imran, was a resident of the Buleda area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 24 April 2014 in Balochistan.
Saatak Baloch was resident of Parood, Kalat martyred on 18 November 2017.

Murtaza Zehri, a 36 year old political worker and son of Abdul Haq, and a resident of Khuzdar, was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces on 9 September 2010. After several months, his body was found on 25 April 2011 in the Sorgaz area of Khuzdar, Balochistan.
Ali Baloch was a resident of the Nokjo, Mashkai area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 5 March 2020 in Balochistan.

On November 19, 2024, while traveling on an organizational mission in the Gishkor area of Kolwah, a group of BLF fighters was ambushed and attacked by enemy forces. As a result, two key and long-standing members of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) were martyred. Captain Niaz Qadir, known as Ustad Guman, was martyred on the spot, while Lieutenant Zarif Baloch, known as Shay Jan, was severely injured. Despite the attack, the comrades involved in the mission mounted a strong counterattack against the enemy forces and, during the fighting, successfully recovered the body of martyr Captain Niaz Qadir, their injured comrade Shay Jan, and their weapons and equipment.
Captain Niaz Qadir, son of Qadir Bakhsh and a resident of Gudop Paho, joined the freedom movement in 2013 and became an official member of the BLF in 2014. Throughout his long struggle, his entire family faced severe hardships due to collective punishment by the occupying forces. Yet he never wavered in his commitment to national freedom. His elder brother, martyred Lieutenant Sabir Baloch (alias Taheer), and his cousin, Captain Zahoor Bali, along with their comrades Second Lieutenant Sajid Sameer and Akbar Hammal, were martyred in 2022 during an aerial attack by enemy forces. His parents were repeatedly subjected to enforced disappearance by Pakistani forces and are currently living as internally displaced persons (IDPs).
Over the years, Captain Niaz Qadir played a vital role in the political, military, and intelligence sectors of the organization and succeeded in disrupting several critical enemy operations. He was a central figure in numerous battles across Balochistan, including in Awaran, Jhao, Kolwah, Ormara, Keelkor, and Balgatar, where he led deadly attacks against enemy forces.
Captain Niaz Qadir held a significant leadership position within BRAS in the Kolwah and Awaran regions. Renowned for his combat skills and mastery of modern technology, he was regarded as a mentor by his comrades. With tireless dedication and deep commitment, he trained members of the Martyrdom Unit, focusing on their military preparedness and physical fitness.

On 8 April 2025, Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) fighters were on patrol in the Kapudi area of Dukki when they came face to face with enemy forces. The clashes continued for hours. During the fighting, the BLA fighters managed to kill 9 enemy personnel and injure several others. In this battle, three BLA fighters - Abdul Wahab alias Deedag, Rahim Khan Marri alias Saarang, and Zahid Ali alias Washdil - were martyred.
Rahim Khan Marri alias Saarang, son of Rozi Khan, belonged to Yakho in the Bolan region. He had been part of the struggle since 2019. He was the elder brother of Ghani Khan Marri Baloch alias Hassan Rocky, who was martyred on the Bolan front in April 2023. Rahim served on the Bolan and Nigaho fronts as a member of the “Fateh Squad.” As a patrol commander, he guided fighters on multiple fronts. His presence strengthened any battlefield. He was always regarded as a source of courage, understanding, and military bravery. His name had become a symbol of discipline and composure in combat.

Naseer Kamalan was a senior leader of the Baloch National Movement (BNM). He was abducted at gunpoint on November 5, 2010, from a passenger van on the Makran Coastal Highway near Pasni in Gwadar District.
His body, along with the body of Baloch Republican Party (BRP) leader Ahmad Dad Baloch, was found on January 17, 2011, dumped on the Makran Coastal Highway near Pasni, Balochistan.

On 1 November 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson, Gwahram Baloch, issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of eight of the organisation’s fighters: Captain Yahya, alias Ustad Khalid Jan; Aris Baloch, alias Omar Jan; Hafeez Baloch, alias Karwan, son of Dad Mohammad; Javid Baloch, alias Gulab, son of Bori Baloch; Abdul Khaliq, alias Nothak; Sajid Baloch, alias Mehran; Hameed Baloch, alias Buzerg; and Akram Baloch, alias Gwahram.

The statement paid tribute to these brave and ideologically committed members of the organisation, who embraced martyrdom while engaging in clashes with the Pakistani army and its death squads on various fronts across Balochistan.

Martyr Javid Baloch, alias Gulab, son of Bori Baloch, resident of Gano Kulanch, Pasni, formally began the national freedom war through the BLF platform on 27 April 2025. Enduring the hardships of guerrilla warfare on long marches on foot through the mountains, he struggled in very important and strategic areas of Makuran. On the fronts of Pasni, Shadikor, Gwarkop, Kulanch and Pidrak, he carried out his military duties with great courage, steadfastness and hard work. He was a very quiet, hardworking, resolute and devoted sarmachar who stayed away from show and regarded his duties as his first obligation. He stood firm against all adverse conditions and enemy aggression, and finally, on 18 October 2026, he embraced martyrdom fighting the death squad nurtured by the occupying army in the Chakli, Kulanch clash.

Mewa Bugti, a resident of Dera Bugti, was a freedom fighter. He was popularly known as the "Ud Commander." He fought alongside Shaheed Akbar Khan Bugti in the Tratani Mountains of Kohlu. Both were martyred in an attack by the Pakistan Army in Tratani, Balochistan, on 26 August 2006.

On 11 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch announced the martyrdom of 14 fighters of the organization who attained martyrdom in confrontations with the Pakistani army and in airstrikes while defending their homeland, Balochistan, and fighting for national liberation and the right to self-determination.

On 13 August 2026, Pakistani Air Force fighter jets bombarded the Pandran area of Kalat District in Balochistan, resulting in the martyrdom of four members of the organization: Waseem Baloch, alias Farhan; Obaidullah Baloch, alias Shaheen; Nawaz Ali Baloch, alias Dilshad; and Mohammad Hassan, alias Ahmad.

On 25 August 2026, during an organizational mission in the Kech area of Balochistan, Sher Jan, alias Jamal, was shot from behind by a traitor, resulting in his martyrdom.

On 3 September 2026, while patrolling in the Mastung area of Balochistan, the organization’s brave fighters, Mohammad Younis, alias Salal; Sameer Ahmad, alias Zemal; Aziz Ahmad, alias Janan; and Sikandar Baloch, confronted Pakistani forces, targeted several enemy personnel, and embraced martyrdom.

On 14 September 2026, while engaging Pakistani forces and defending his fellow fighters in the Machani Kor Paroom area of Panjgur District, Babar Baloch, alias Kambar, embraced martyrdom.

On 18 September 2026, during a confrontation with Pakistani forces in the Chagi area of Balochistan, fighters of the organization, Riaz Baloch, alias Sabir; Taimoor Shah, alias Shaheen; Zia Ul Haq, alias Ziaullah; and Jumma Baloch, alias Commando, embraced martyrdom.

Aziz Ahmed, alias Janan, son of Mohammad Azum, resident of Quetta, joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in early 2026. After military training, he fearlessly carried out his duties on the Nagahu front. On 3 September 2026, under an organizational decision, he was on patrol on the Mastung front and was martyred while fighting the enemy army in a clash.
Dr. Ahmad Mari was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani genocidal forces from the Hyderabad area of Sindh. A few days later, on 13 November 2011, his mutilated body was dumped in Quetta.

On 25 August 2024 Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch announced the launch of a "Fidayeen Operation" named "Herof" across Balochistan. As part of this operation, fidayeen from the BLA's elite unit, Majeed Brigade, have attacked the main camp of the Pakistani forces in Bela and have successfully infiltrated it. Meanwhile, other BLA fighters have taken full control of all major highways across Balochistan, blocking them completely.
During Operation “Herof,” 44 attacks were carried out simultaneously at 40 locations across 13 districts of Balochistan. As a result, 130 Pakistani army personnel were killed and 55 were injured. In addition, gas pipelines were destroyed at 2 locations, railway tracks at 7 locations, and 2 bridges were blown up.
During the operation, 13 vehicles transporting minerals were set on fire. Blockades were also established at 14 locations across Balochistan, and 3 members of a “death squad” were killed.
As part of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayee (suicide) operation “Herof,” the BLA’s Majeed Brigade carried out an attack on the Pakistani army’s Bela camp. The Majeed Brigade maintained control of the camp for twenty hours, during which 68 enemy personnel were killed.
Nine fidayeen (self-sacrificing fighters) of the Majeed Brigade at Bela camp - Ghaus Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Talib), Mahal Baloch (alias Zilan Kurd), Rizwan Baloch (alias Hammal), Mohammad Baloch (alias Meerak), Fazal Gul Zehri (alias Shawaiz), Tayyab Baloch (alias Lala), Junaid Zehri (alias Kami), Mohammad Asif Nechari (alias Naveed), and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Khalid) - along with Shafqat (alias Dayar) of the Fateh Squad in Mastung, were martyred in the operation.
Ghaus Baksh Sumalani, alias Talib, and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani, alias Khalid, were brothers. They took part in the same operation and were martyred while defending their motherland.

Faheem Ahmad Magsi, alias Nazar Jan, son of Nisar Ahmad Magsi, was a resident of Mola, Karzana, Khuzdar, Balochistan. He had an FSc qualification. He joined the BLA on 7 July 2025 and served in Nagaho, Jal Magsi, and Kark as a patrol commander. He was martyred on 10 July 2026 in Zaidi, Khuzdar, at the age of 20.
Martyr Faheem Ahmad Magsi decided to join the Baloch Liberation Army last year after conscious and moral deliberation. He joined the organizational camp at the Nagaho front and began his national service. He soon adapted to the rapidly evolving and modern requirements of warfare and became active on the front lines with great enthusiasm. After completing basic military training, he joined the fighting on the front line. Alongside rendering his services during Operation Herof II, he participated in numerous significant and deadly ambushes. He demonstrated an outstanding ability to understand strategies and different patterns of warfare. He also possessed the ability to quickly adapt to changing circumstances and use emerging battlefield conditions to his advantage during active engagements.
He was a sensible and educated young man who did not accidentally or suddenly decide to join the national resistance against what he regarded as Punjabi occupation. Rather, his decision was the result of an understanding shaped by the historical and ground realities of Balochistan. Through critical thinking, he developed the ability to reach what he considered realistic and informed conclusions on the issues before him, and this consciousness became the guiding philosophy of his practical life. He always participated in organizational activities with deep interest and carried out every responsibility with great dedication and commitment. He remained at the forefront alongside his fellow Sarmachars, working to maintain the organization's position and push back the enemy in the respective region. Recognizing these abilities, the organization entrusted him with patrol command responsibilities, which he carried out with discipline and professionalism until the end.
Martyr Faheem Ahmad Magsi remained committed to the ideological foundations upon which he had chosen the path of resistance until the last breath of his life. By sacrificing his life for his motherland, he sought to raise the flag of his nation high. His sacrifice, in this account, will remain an unforgettable chapter in Baloch history, and the legacy of such sacrifices will be passed on to future generations in the pursuit of an independent Baloch state.

data.biography:
Zahir Baloch, alias KD, son of Nasir Baloch, was a resident of the Ligork area of Paroom, Panjgur. He joined the BLA in 2023 and moved to the mountain front in October 2025. He served in Paroom, Gwargo, Panjgur, and Zamuran, and was promoted to the rank of Second Patrolling Commander. He was martyred on 19 August 2026 in the Pullabad area of Panjgur District, Balochistan.
Zahir Baloch, a native of Panjgur, had been working with the organization on the urban and military fronts for the past three years with a strong, revolutionary, and responsible approach. During his urban duties, he provided the organization with access to important information and timely updates on major battles against the enemy. He carried out his urban guerrilla duties with exceptional cunning and, after falling under enemy surveillance, joined the front lines on organizational orders, where, for the past year, he served as a brave, devoted, and hardworking Sarmachar.
Zahir Baloch assumed organizational responsibilities in various areas of Makuran over the past year and fulfilled them with outstanding competence. He took an active part in military operations carried out in different regions from Zamuran to Panjgur. In view of these military and administrative capabilities, the organization appointed him as Second Patrolling Commander, where he carried out his duties in the best possible manner. He was a valiant and courageous fighter of the BLA and, on August 19, attained the supreme rank of martyrdom in a clash with the enemy. History will remember him as a great national fighter.

After suffering losses from the Baloch Liberation Army’s coordinated attacks under Operation Herof across the length and breadth of Balochistan, Pakistani forces on 29 August 2024 took nine forcibly disappeared individuals out of their torture centers and extrajudicially executed them. The bodies of five individuals were dumped in Khuzdar, while the bodies of four others were thrown in Hub. Among them, the identities of four bodies were confirmed as those of forcibly disappeared persons Saeed Ghulamani, Fayaz Jattak, Saeed Meeraji and Nisar Ahmad.

After Faizan Shahwani, Asifa Mengal rammed another vehicle loaded with explosives into the gate of the main camp of the occupying forces, causing severe damage to the enemy’s defenses. Asifa Mengal, the daughter of Mohammad Ismail, was from Killi Qazi Abad, Noshki. She was born on October 2, 2002. She joined the Baloch Liberation Army’s Majeed Brigade on October 2, 2023, and made her fidayee decision in January 2024. At a young age, she became part of a trajectory shaped by conviction rather than circumstance. On January 31, 2026, she carried out a VBIED operation targeting the ISI headquarters in Noshki.

Adnan Baloch, son of Haji Akram Baloch, was abducted by Pakistani security forces from the Kahnek area of Mand, Balochistan, on 30 June 2012.
On 26 January 2013, his tortured and mutilated body was found in the Malir area of Karachi.

On January 12, 2026 Pakistani army carried out a drone attack on a temporary patrol camp of Baloch Liberation Army in the Shurparood area of Kalat, in which four veteran freedom fighters of BLA - Sangat Zohair alias Haq Nawaz, Sangat Manzoor Kurd alias Bakhtiar Cheeta, Sangat Samiullah alias Javed Phalia and Sangat Naseer Ahmed alias Meerak - attained martyrdom.
Manzoor Kurd alias Bakhtiar Cheeta, son of Mohammad Rahim Kurd, belonged to Burma Hotel area of Quetta. Manzoor Kurd joined Baloch Liberation Army in 2016 and served as an urban guerrilla and in 2018 he was moved to the mountain front. He served on Bolan, Nagahau and Kalat fronts. Manzoor Kurd’s brother, Mohiuddin alias Sangat Najeeb was martyred in a clash with enemy Pakistani army commandos oduring the attack on Martyr General Aslam Baloch in Yakho area of Bolan in 2016, while several members of his family were continuously victims of forced disappearances and raids as collective punishment by the occupying army. However, Sangat Manzoor Kurd remained steadfast in his stance for liberation until his last breath.
On 16 December 2014, Ali Jajrani Bugti was killed by a state-sponsored death squad in Sindh.

On 22 July 2026, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) released the details of seven martyred members of the organization: Abdul Ghafoor, alias Chakar, son of Jan Mohammad; Imdad Baloch, alias Nodh, son of Rahmatullah; Hafiz Mumtaz Baloch, alias Zeerak, son of Sabir Ali; Hafiz Zaid Baloch, alias Sagaar, son of Mullah Khudadad; Yasir Baloch, alias Ajiz, son of Mohammad Ayub; Shahjan Baloch, alias Sawad, son of Ali Mohammad; and Ali Raza Baloch, alias Shayhaq, son of Haji Ali Ahmad. They were martyred in a drone strike by Pakistani forces on 29 January 2026 in the Pardan area of Panjgur District, Balochistan.

Hafiz Zaid Baloch, alias Sagaar, son of Mulla Khudadad, was a resident of the Tasp area of Panjgur, Balochistan. He was a Hafiz of the Quran and joined the BLA on 26 August 2025. He served on the Panjgur front and was killed on 29 January 2026 in the Pardan area of Panjgur.
Hafiz Zaid, alias Sagaar, joined the BLA camp in August last year and began his service on the path of freedom. As a Hafiz of the Quran, he believed that Pakistan’s presence in Balochistan was an unnatural act on both Islamic and scientific grounds, and that the ongoing Baloch resistance against it was a just and natural struggle. Based on this conviction, he joined the Baloch movement and became actively involved as a Sarmachar.
After joining the organizational camp, he devoted himself to training with great determination and successfully completed the organization’s rigorous physical and military training course. Afterward, he participated in military patrols. He carried out every responsibility assigned to him by the organization to the best of his ability and was known among his fellow Sangats as a hardworking and dedicated Sarmachar who remained committed to his duties.
He joined the conflict with the belief that every symbol of occupation should be removed from the Baloch homeland and that an independent Balochistan should be established, where history, culture, civilization, and humanity could be preserved. He believed that as long as the Punjabi occupation continued, the Baloch people would not be able to live a prosperous and independent life.
He continued his efforts and struggle until his final moments. Along with six other Sarmachars, he was killed in a drone strike in Pardan, Panjgur, and became a part of history. His sacrifices will continue to be remembered.

Naeem Sabir Baloch was a resident of Khuzdar and a social activist associated with the Human Rights Commission of Pakistan (HRCP). He was shot seven times and killed on 1 March 2011. Responsibility for his killing was claimed by the Baloch Musallah Difai Tanzeem, a group reportedly operating under the Pakistan Army and led by the notorious Shafiq Mengal.

Arsalan Baloch, alias Moosa, son of Munawar Khan Mandai, was a resident of Killi Ata Muhammad, Nushki. His educational qualification was in Fine Arts from the University of Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2025 and served on the Nushki and Kharan fronts, where he was martyred in Kharan.
Arsalan Baloch, alias Moosa, represented the educated Baloch class that chose to shed blood for the freedom of their soil rather than weave dreams with pens and colors. As a Fine Arts student at the University of Balochistan, Arsalan had a keen eye for aesthetics, but he realized that when a nation’s identity is at stake, the greatest masterpiece of art is rendered through sacrifice. Rising from the land of Nushki, he formally became part of the BLA in 2025.
Arsalan proved his political and military mettle on the challenging fronts of Nushki and Kharan. The sensitivity of an artist and the toughness of a soldier were uniquely combined in his personality. During the decisive battle of "Operation Herof Phase 2," Arsalan was present on the Kharan front, where he embraced martyrdom in an intense clash. His martyrdom stands as a testament to the fact that the educational institutions of Balochistan are now producing skilled individuals who know the art of adorning the features of their motherland with their own blood.

Hatim Dilpul, son of Dilpul Baloch, a 22-year-old resident of Tejaban, district Kech, was extrajudicially killed by state-backed death squads on August 15, 2025.

Hatim, a civilian who regularly traveled to the mountainous area to support his grandparents by bringing groceries and essential supplies, was shot at by armed state-sponsored death squads while carrying out this routine task.

He had previously been threatened, harassed, and intimidated by the same death squads. On Friday, his bullet-riddled body was recovered in the mountainous area of Tejaban, showing clear evidence of targeted shooting before he succumbed to his injuries.

Imran, alias Umar Farooq, son of Maulvi Mohammad Saeed, was a resident of the Zamuran area of Kech district in Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2025, served on the Washuk front, and was martyred on 7 August 2026 in the Washuk area of Balochistan.
A year before his martyrdom, Maulvi Imran made the great caravan of Balochistan’s freedom the purpose of his life and, from the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army, joined the armed resistance to restore the independent statehood of Balochistan. After successfully completing the organisation’s rigorous physical, mental, and ideological training courses, he was transferred to the Washuk front under the orders of the organisational command. On the Washuk front, he made the best use of his skills and carried out significant actions against the enemy. He not only took an active part in the organisation’s military operations in the area but also dealt a severe blow to the enemy’s advancing policies.
Maulvi Imran was a Hafiz of the Qur’an and was well aware of his national and religious duties and responsibilities. He had gained a profound understanding of the situation in Balochistan and was also aware of the occupiers’ ambitions, which aimed to destroy the Baloch national identity and existence forever. Therefore, having chosen this great path, he made the practical methods of resistance a part of his life. He was a courageous comrade on the battlefield, always at the forefront of boosting the morale of his fellow fighters and encouraging them, and he had the ability to enter any situation or harsh phase of combat. He was a top-tier fighter on the battlefield, always delivering devastating results against the enemy. These abilities consistently proved him to be a unique and purposeful fighter.
Maulvi Imran proved through his practical activities and struggle that a nation’s freedom is its fundamental human right and that achieving it is a basic step toward national prosperity, and he sacrificed his personal life for that very purpose. The Baloch nation and fellow freedom fighters will always remember Maulvi Imran as a great national hero and will bring his sacrifices to fruition through the establishment of an independent and sovereign Balochistan.

On 2 February 2022, sixteen members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayeen unit, the Majeed Brigade, carried out simultaneous attacks, nine in Noshki and seven on the Frontier Corps headquarters in Panjgur. The organization named this action "Operation Ganjal". 90 Pakistani security personnel were killed in Noshki and 105 in Panjgur.
On 2 February 2022 at 8:00 PM Fidayee Jamal Baloch alias Chacha, son of Rehmatullah, a resident of Turbat, rammed an VBEID into the main gate of the FC camp in Panjgur. As a result, the front portion of the camp was destroyed, and all soldiers deployed for security at the spot were killed instantly. After this, under the leadership of Unit Commander Hamid Raheem alias Zubair, son of Raheem Bakhsh, a resident of Chitkan, Panjgur, the fidayee fighters Sami Sameer alias Shoaib, son of Ustad Ilahi Bakhsh, resident of Gramkan, Panjgur; Ilyas Baloch alias Qadir, son of Aslam, resident of Gramkan, Panjgur; Asad Wahag alias Sabzo, son of Sadiq, resident of Kilkor; Nasir Imam alias Hamal, son of Imam, resident of Parom; and Zameer Baloch alias Faraz, son of Mohammad Hassan, resident of Dandar, Hoshab, entered the camp. They killed the majority of the soldiers present in the camp, while the remaining enemy personnel, instead of confronting the fighters, abandoned the camp and fled. The objective of the Panjgur unit was to seize control of the camp and hold it for as long as possible. After the enemy fled, the fighters took full control of the entire camp. Subsequently, to recapture the camp from the fighters, the enemy called in SSG commandos, the army, and combat helicopters. During this time, with the support of combat helicopters and armored vehicles, the SSG commandos launched five major assaults on the Baloch fighters. In every attack, the fighters inflicted heavy casualties on the enemy and forced them to retreat. The fighters continued to hold control of the camp while fighting the enemy’s elite military units for 72 hours. After failing in ground assaults, on 5 February 2022 in the afternoon, heavy shelling was carried out against the fighters using combat helicopters. As a result, after prolonged resistance, the fighters were martyred.

During this extensive military operation by the Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar, freedom fighter Martyr Jahanzeb Mengal alias Balach Jan was martyred during a fierce clash in Noshki. 
The clash took place on the night of March 27, 2025 in the Qadirabad area of Noshki, when the occupying Pakistani army raided to arrest a freedom fighter. During the fierce clash that lasted for three hours, Jahanzeb fought alone against the enemy, eliminating eight personnel of the occupying army while injuring several others and thwarting the enemy’s advance. 
During the clash, the enemy used heavy weapons, including rocket launchers but Jahanzeb resisted in a very organized, courageous and warlike manner. He remained on the front line until the last moment. Even after being seriously injured, he continued to fight and attained the high status of martyrdom.
Jahanzeb Mengal alias Balach son of Shah Khalid Mengal was a resident of the Qadirabad area of Noshki. He had been associated with the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) for the last two years. Due to his fighting skills he became a member of the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS), a special unit of the BLA. 
This unit has been formed for highly sensitive, complex and skilled operations and Martyr Balach was always at the forefront of these operations. He successfully completed several important missions in which the enemy suffered heavy casualties and property losses. 
Martyr Balach was not only a combat expert but also a resistance worker with political and national consciousness, who prioritized organizational training, discipline and national interest above any personal passion. He provided practical strength, intellectual direction and military confidence to the liberation movement during his short but fruitful resistance journey.

On 22 July 2026, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) released the details of seven martyred members of the organization: Abdul Ghafoor, alias Chakar, son of Jan Mohammad; Imdad Baloch, alias Nodh, son of Rahmatullah; Hafiz Mumtaz Baloch, alias Zeerak, son of Sabir Ali; Hafiz Zaid Baloch, alias Sagaar, son of Mullah Khudadad; Yasir Baloch, alias Ajiz, son of Mohammad Ayub; Shahjan Baloch, alias Sawad, son of Ali Mohammad; and Ali Raza Baloch, alias Shayhaq, son of Haji Ali Ahmad. They were martyred in a drone strike by Pakistani forces on 29 January 2026 in the Pardan area of Panjgur District, Balochistan.

Imdad Baloch, alias Nodh, son of Rahmatullah, was a resident of the Gramkan area of Panjgur District, Balochistan. He joined the BLA on 17 September 2025 and served on the Panjgur front. He was killed in January 2026 in the Pardan area of Panjgur District, Balochistan.
Imdad Baloch, alias Nodh, served as a capable and courageous member of the Baloch Liberation Army in Panjgur and its surrounding areas. Despite being a new cadre, he was someone upon whom the leadership could rely during even the most difficult and demanding military operations. Having joined the ranks of the Baloch Liberation Army only the previous year, he remained active and committed in his role. After completing his basic military training courses, he assumed an active role and participated in activities carried out in Panjgur and its surrounding areas.
His bravery, courage, and combat skills were considered valuable by his fellow members in the region. During his training, he received instruction in the use of the LMG, and in many operations, he served as an LMG gunner. He remained actively engaged in combat situations and was capable of handling the LMG effectively. During the previous year, he participated in the organization’s road blockades and other operations across the region. He remained active until his final moments and was killed alongside his fellow members in a drone strike.
The fighting skills and dedication of Nodh will remain a part of the memories of his fellow members. The sacrifices attributed to him will become part of the organization’s history, and his supporters believe such sacrifices contribute to their stated goal of a free Balochistan.

He joined the BLA as an urban guerrilla in 2023. In September 2024, he moved to the mountain fronts and joined the Majeed Brigade in November 2024. He served on the Nagaaho front and was martyred during Operation Herof Phase 2 on the Kharan front.
Hafeez Baloch, alias Ahsan, was among those fighters who embraced resistance as a serious and organized responsibility. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2023 as an urban guerrilla and became part of a quiet, coordinated, and long-term struggle. His role on the urban front was grounded in organizational continuity, intelligence accuracy, and strict discipline. He belonged to a generation that understood that warfare is not merely about pulling a trigger, but also about endurance, composure, and the disciplined use of time.
His transfer to the mountain front in September 2024 marked the next stage of his ideological and operational journey. On the Nagaaho front, he not only assumed military responsibilities but also demonstrated practical resilience under harsh conditions. His decision to join the Majeed Brigade in November 2024 reflected his readiness to carry the Baloch national liberation movement to its ultimate limits.
During Operation Herof II, he engaged in prolonged clashes at the main gate of the Kharan central military camp alongside his fellow fighters, successfully breaking through the enemy’s fortified defensive perimeter. The confrontation was not merely a military engagement but also a symbolic message that Baloch fighters now possess the capability to reach the core centers of the enemy. It was on this front that he embraced martyrdom. His sacrifice marks the decisive culmination of a young fighter who adopted resistance not as a temporary reaction, but as a national duty.

Zareef Faraz Baloch, son of Balach Baloch, was a Balochi singer and a resident of Kalatuk. He was abducted on 21 April 2011 by Pakistani forces from Zero Point, Gwadar, and was forcibly disappeared. On 25 April 2011, his body was found in Murgaap, Turbat District, Balochistan.

On May 16, 2025, Sarmachar Zahid Sumalani Baloch, a dedicated member of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF), was on an important mission as part of the organization's program in the Jorkeen area of Kharan. During the journey, he encountered members of a state-backed armed death squad. A fierce and prolonged clash ensued between the fighters and the enemy’s death squad operatives.
In this intense battle, Zahid Sumalani Baloch, son of Haji Ghulam Nabi Sumalani, resident of Nal, Kodask, fought with exceptional bravery. Despite being injured during the exchange of fire, he continued to resist the enemy with unwavering courage, holding them off for several hours. His actions ensured the safe withdrawal of his comrades. Embracing the philosophy of "the last bullet," he ultimately attained martyrdom on the battlefield.
Martyr Zahid Sumalani Baloch joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in March 2022 to contribute to the struggle for Balochistan’s freedom. In a short span of time, he actively participated in numerous operations against the enemy in areas such as Mashkay, Jhao, Awaran, Gichk, and Kharan.

A 22 year old Baloch youth, Mudassir Sumalani, was killed after customs personnel allegedly threw a nail chain on his vehicle, causing it to overturn on the Noshki National Highway (RCD). The incident also left another passenger critically injured. Mudassir was the only brother of six sisters and the sole breadwinner of his family, succumbed to his injuries on the spot.
Eyewitnesses claim that customs officials fled the scene immediately after the crash, leaving the victims behind without medical assistance. No justification has been provided by the authorities. After the incident protesters blocked the national highway, carried Sumalani’s body in protested and Two customs vehicles were torched as demonstrators chanted slogans against the authorities.

On 30 December 2023 Pakistani forces carried out a drone attack and attempted to surround a camp of BRAS in Gurandi Zeera Kaur area of Mashkay by dropping commandos through helicopters. Following professional military tactics, Baloch freedom fighters formed multiple teams to foil enemy aggression and carried several successful attacks against the advancing enemy troops. At least 7 enemy commandos were eliminated in two separate attacks, whereas, three Baloch freedom fighters, identified as Sarwar alias Duruk, Azam alias Basit and Abdul Sattar alias Maraij made ultimate sacrifices. Two freedom fighters of BRAS, Kenagi alias Muslim and Ali alias Atta, while forestalling enemy advances for hours and providing a safe route for Baloch freedom fighters, also embraced martyrdom. Both valiant fighters fought the enemy troops until their last bullets, and made the ultimate sacrifices at their own hands after running out of ammunition. The fallen comrades were affiliated with the allied organisations of BRAS. Sarwar alias Durak, a resident of Mashkay Gajjar, joined Balochistan liberation Front (BLF) in 2012. Due to his continuous hardwork and military skills, he had achieved the rank of a captain in BLF.

Asmatullah, also known as Salal, son of Hafiz Abdul Sattar Mengal, was a resident of the Qadir Abad area in Noshki District, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in April 2024 and moved to the mountainous front in April 2025, where he served in the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS).
Asmatullah was a revolutionary soldier in the war of freedom, who transformed his very being into a dynamic force shaped by the consciousness of the freedom movement. For him, resistance was not a temporary reaction but a continuous commitment, advanced through awareness, discipline, and practical action. He believed that only those nations that embrace sacrifice as their creed and steadfastness as their tradition could achieve freedom. With this conviction, he remained firm on every front, disregarding pressure, fatigue, and danger. His struggle testified that a revolutionary fighter draws strength not merely from weapons but from unwavering resolve and a living consciousness.
After joining the BLA in 2024, Asmatullah remained active on the urban front for one year. In 2025, following an organizational decision, he was transferred to the mountainous front. Based on his combat capabilities, he was inducted into the organization’s Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS).
Asmatullah was present on the Noshki front during Operation Herof II, where he held key positions alongside his STOS team. He embraced martyrdom while fighting on this front.

data.biography: Dad Jan Baloch, was a resident of the Dramkol, Pidrak area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 22 December 2015 in Balochistan.

Mir Hammal Khan Pirukani devoted 33 years of his life as a freedom fighter, struggling to liberate Balochistan and, in the end, sacrificed his precious life for the freedom of his nation. We know very little about this brave Baloch warrior. As a young man, he used to accompany his father, Mir Abdul Karim Pirukani, to the camps of freedom fighters under the command of the legendary commander Safer Khan Zehri. Mir Hammal Pirukani was a keen listener and a quick learner. It was a time of great upheaval in Baloch politics, when Prime Minister Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto had dismissed the democratically elected National Awami Party (NAP) government in Balochistan. The Baloch nation was outraged and took up arms to resist the Pakistani state and its military, which had been sent in to quell the uprising.
On one such visit to the camps of freedom fighters with his father and brother in the mountains of Sarlat, Shaheed Safar Khan Zehri asked his father to let one of his sons join the liberation movement. As both brothers were eager to join the fight, his father tossed a coin, and Hammal Khan won. He went on to become a revolutionary freedom fighter, and the year was 1975.
Shaheed Mir Hammal Khan Pirukani’s name surfaced only after the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) issued a statement in May 2008, stating that one of its commanders and a veteran fighter of more than 30 years had been martyred in a battle with the Pakistani army. Neither the name nor the place of the battle was mentioned in the statement. Two years later, in an article, Sikander Pirukani revealed his name, and only then did the nation come to know about the martyrdom of Mir Hammal Pirukani.
On May 20, 2008, Mir Hammal Khan Pirukani, a hero of the Baloch nation, called Ustad (teacher) by his comrades, departed, leaving behind a treasure trove of knowledge on Baloch history, culture, language, nationalism, and guerrilla warfare, now passed on to the new generation, which will guide the Baloch liberation movement to victory.

Juniad Baloch, son of Ramzan Mengal, was born on 7 January 1991. He was a resident of Khuzdar District, Balochistan. He received his early education in his native area, Khuzdar, and was a BS Honors (Civil Engineering) student at Balochistan University of Engineering and Technology, Khuzdar, at the time of his martyrdom.
He joined BSO Azad at a very young age and was a senior member of the BSO Azad Khuzdar Zone. He was a political activist affiliated with the Baloch Students Organization Azad. He had a keen interest in reading newspapers and revolutionary literature.
He was the victim of a target killing carried out by Pakistan’s intelligence agency on 2 March 2010 during a Cultural Day event at Balochistan University of Engineering and Technology, Khuzdar. Along with Sikander, he was martyred by a Pakistani army-backed death squad in Khuzdar during an event organized by the Baloch Students Organization Azad on the occasion of Baloch Culture Day.
His sacrifices for the national cause and in defense of Baloch culture will always be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

Kamal Baloch, son of Bakhtiyar Baloch, was born in 1992 in Gresha, District Khuzdar. He was an intermediate student at Inter College Naal and served as the president of BSO Azad, Naal Zone. He held various positions within the organization and was elected president of the Naal Zone at a time when organizational activities were banned throughout Balochistan, and members were facing a crackdown by the Pakistani army for being activists of BSO Azad and advocating for the people of Baloch homeland.
He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising his right to peaceful political expression. He was killed at his home in Gresha on September 18, 2015, by the Pakistani army. Like other cadres, he also played an important role in expanding the organization’s activities in his region.

Kamran Baloch, son of Lal Baksh, was a 20 year old FSc student from the Moola area of Khuzdar, Balochistan.
On 8 July 2026, Kamran Baloch was targeted and killed by a death squad in Khuzdar.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, the BLA’s Majeed Brigade Fidayeen targeted the main camp and the Coast Guard camp of the Pakistan Navy in the coastal city of Pasni, Balochistan. The operation was initiated by Fazal, alias Miraan, who rammed a vehicle loaded with explosives into the main entrance gate of the Navy camp. The explosion instantly killed at least seven personnel stationed at the gate.
Immediately after this initial attack, six Fidayeen - Yasma Baloch, alias Zareena; Waseem Baloch, alias Zirbaar; Zaid Zamurani, alias Abram; Sabzal Baloch, alias Kohsar; Diljan Baloch, alias Ameer Ajoo; and Operation Commander Shabeer Baloch, alias Kiya - entered the camp and took up positions. Fierce clashes with the occupying Navy and Navy special units inside the camp continued for more than five hours, during which at least 33 Pakistani personnel were killed. This operation not only inflicted significant casualties on the enemy but also dealt a severe blow to the defense structure of the Navy camp.
Zaid Yaseen Zamurani completed his intermediate education (FA) and grew up in a large family, being the second eldest among his brothers. He became connected with the organizational network in 2018, a phase that shaped his political awareness and sense of responsibility. In September 2024, he formally joined the Baloch Liberation Army and became part of the Majeed Brigade.
He fought with commitment and quiet determination and was bravely martyred on the Pasni front. His journey reflected a conscious choice, carried with dignity, resolve, and unwavering belief in the path he had chosen. Those who knew him recall his calm presence, disciplined mind, and willingness to shoulder responsibility without seeking recognition.

In a statement issued on 26 June 2025 by Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson of the Baloch Liberation Army, it was said that three BLA fighters were martyred in clashes with the occupying Pakistani forces on the fronts of Quetta, Kalat, and Seyahji. The martyred comrades include Jamshed,  Nowroz and Munawar Baig.
On 22 June 2025 in the Daghari area of Quetta, a BLA patrol team encountered the occupying Pakistani forces as they attempted to advance in the area. A face to face battle broke out between the occupying forces and the fighters, which continued for a long time. Several personnel of the occupying army were killed and injured in the clashes, while BLA fighter Jamshed, also known as Rizwan, attained martyrdom.
In the evening, two units of BLA fighters surrounded the occupying army’s infantry in a ravine and attacked them from two sides. As a result, six soldiers of the occupying forces were killed on the spot and several others were injured. During the hour-long clash, BLA fighter Nowroz, alias King Najeeb, was martyred.
On 20 June 2025 in the Langasi area of Dasht, BLA fighters encountered the occupying Pakistani forces while travelling for organizational work. In the face to face battle that ensued, the occupying forces suffered losses. Meanwhile, in an already injured state, Sangat Munawar Baig was martyred during the clash with the occupying forces.
Munawar Baig, alias Meerk, son of Baig, belonged to the Balnigwar Bazaar, Kalero area of Dasht in Kech. He joined the BLA a year ago and served on the Seyahji and Dasht fronts. In a very short time, he proved that sacrifice is not dependent on age. Munawar Baig was not merely a fighter, but a living symbol of awareness.
Rahmdil Baloch was a resident of the Sami, Kech area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 4 March 2020 in Balochistan.
Omar Amin Baloch was a resident of the Kahan-e-Pusht, Turbat area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 4 December 2012 in Balochistan.

Ibadullah Zehri, alias Saqib, son of Fazalullah Zehri, was a resident of the Zard area of Washuk, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served in Washuk and Basima. He was killed on 7 September 2026 in the Basima area of Surab, Balochistan.
Ibadullah Zehri, in the same year, expressing his alignment with the goals and program of Baloch national liberation, chose the true path of armed Baloch resistance and joined the Baloch Liberation Army. Ibad Ullah Zehri, a native of Washuk, had fully understood the importance of the national and collective objectives of the Baloch war. Therefore, he chose this great path against the enemy and became active on the Shor front. After completing the basic training courses, he joined armed patrols and, in a short period, proved himself to be a brave and capable fighter. His inherent abilities soon began to prove useful on the ground in pursuit of national objectives.
Saqib was a mature and capable fighter in terms of thought and action and was fully aware of the hardships and realities of war. This awareness brought him to the point where he sacrificed his personal life in the cause of national liberation. He served on the battlefield for a short period, but throughout that time, he remained a steadfast and active fighter, carrying out every responsibility and activity assigned by the organization with great sincerity and honesty. He attained martyrdom while confronting the enemy and remained committed until the end to the ideological truth he had embraced before joining the war. His sacrifices will remain etched in history as those of a brave fighter who offered his life for the freedom of his homeland.

On 11 May 2011, on the bank of the Rakhshan River at Damb, Panjgur, some labourers spotted a body in a shallow ditch. When the residents of the area searched, they found two more mutilated bodies. They were later identified by their relatives as Agha Abid Shah, Abdul Sattar Baloch, and Safeer Baloch.
Safeer Baloch was born on 16 July 1975 to Haneef Baloch at Sari Kouran, Panjgur. He completed his master’s from Balochistan University and, after finishing his education, became a teacher.
Agha Abid Shah, Abdul Sattar Baloch, and Safeer Baloch were abducted by state agencies on 15 August 2010 from the vicinity of the District Headquarters Hospital, Panjgur. Panjgur erupted in protest; for a week, the entire district was shut down, and both male and female protesters besieged the office of the Deputy Commissioner to oppose this travesty of justice and the enforced disappearance of these three Baloch political workers. The Frontier Corps (FC) used excessive force to crush the protest and, on 17 August 2010, fired upon the protesters, killing one protester, Hussain Baloch.

Younis Zehri, alias Sarang, son of Abdul Qayyum Zehri and a resident of Kahan in the Zehri area of Khuzdar district, Balochistan, joined the BLA on June 30, 2025. He served on the Zehri and Kalat fronts and was martyred on the Noshki front during Operation Herof Phase 2.
Younis Zehri, known in revolutionary circles as “Sarang,” was a custodian of the ancient hills of Zehri, where the roots of resistance are deeply embedded in the soil. When he formally joined the BLA on June 30, 2025, he carried not only a gun but also a firm political and ideological consciousness, forged by witnessing the injustices inflicted upon his land. Through his military prowess and discipline, he established his identity as a fearless soldier on the arduous fronts of Zehri and Kalat in a very short period.
Sarang was among those youths who believed in fulfilling their national duties with silent resolve. When the clarion call of “Operation Herof” was sounded, Younas Zehri chose to stand firm against the enemy on the Noshki front. In the intense clashes on the scorching lands of Noshki, he fought until his last bullet and last breath, without regard for the enemy’s numerical superiority, and embraced martyrdom.

Zulfiqar Baloch, son of Musafer Baloch, a 47-year-old shepherd from Gishtagan, was taken on February 21, 2026, from Nehing Zamuran. He earned his livelihood through livestock.
He was taken without any legal warrant or explanation. After his disappearance, his family continued searching for him and repeatedly attempted to obtain information about his whereabouts, but no details were provided.
On April 16, 2026, his body was found in the Parom area of Panjgur district, Balochistan, in an incident described as an encounter. His death came after nearly two months of complete uncertainty for his family.

Altaf Hussain Baloch was born on January 25, 1975, to Khuda Baksh Baloch in Buleda, Kech. During his student years, he became affiliated with the Baloch Students Organization (BSO). He was shot and killed by Pakistani forces on August 25, 2008, during a public gathering of the Baloch National Front (BNF) held in memory of Akbar Khan Bugti in Turbat, Kech.

On March 8, 2023, Pakistani drones fired three missiles at a Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) guerrilla camp in the mountain range between Hoshap and Pasni. Following the strike, Pakistani forces began landing commandos around the camp from helicopters. In the missile attack, the camp commander, Hasil Baloch, along with four other fighters, was martyred. The remaining Sarmachars fought bravely in close combat, killing several commandos of the occupying forces before they themselves were martyred in the great cause of freedom for their homeland.
The Sarmachars who were martyred are:
Hasil (alias Doda), Wasdil (alias Jami), Nizam (alias Noshad), Waqas (alias Miras), Khalid (alias Kiyya), Shah Fahad (alias Aslam), and Ilyas Baloch (alias Rahmdil).
Martyr Waqas (alias Miras), son of Nazir and resident of Tijaban, joined the Baloch armed struggle in 2019. He was a deeply sincere and hardworking comrade. Shaheed Waqas faithfully carried out his national duties in Kech, Pasni, and other areas of Makran.

On 29 November 2022, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 26 November 2022, at 6:00 am, the Pakistani army fired hundreds of missiles from Iranian kamikaze drones in and around the Siakoh area of Kahan, Kohlu district of Balochistan. Out of these, two missiles fell within the premises of a BLA camp located in Siakoh. As a result, eight freedom fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army embraced martyrdom.
Afterward, the enemy launched a large scale ground and air operation in Kahan and adjoining areas. The spokesperson stated that for a long time Pakistan and Iran have maintained joint military cooperation against the Baloch national cause, including intelligence coordination. They also exchange advanced and lethal weapons.
In the first phase of the operation, following the drone attacks, several special forces commandos were dropped from around a dozen Pakistan Army combat helicopters, and shelling began from the air. Subsequently, military troops from Kohlu, Dera Bugti, and nearby areas - consisting of more than 400 personnel - participated in the operation using several armored and other military vehicles.
As soon as the Pakistani army initiated the operation, nearby BLA camps in the area began countering the enemy’s advance from different fronts by adopting a joint defense strategy.
The combat between the enemy forces and the freedom fighters continued intermittently until the evening. As a result, the freedom fighters inflicted heavy casualties on the Pakistani forces from all sides. Breaking the army’s land and air siege through skilled combat tactics, they carried their injured comrades, along with weapons and other sensitive equipment, to safe locations.
During the conflict, after several hours of fierce resistance by the fighters, the army turned its guns toward the local population in Nissau, Siakoh, Drehis, Parhki, Jantali, and adjoining areas. The enemy set fire to many houses and severely tortured residents. Meanwhile, troops stopped two innocent Baloch pedestrians and killed them.
The organization’s fighters who embraced martyrdom were - Gahmar Khan alias Garra, Thal Khan alias Thallu, Hameed Baloch alias Sado
Shadi Khan alias Kooda, Abu Bakr Baloch alias Rehan, Jameel alias Naadi
Kareem Khan alias Jamal, Muhammad Nusrat alias Asif - The organization also rejected reports claiming that BLA fighters had been arrested during the operation. Through the media, it challenged ISPR to substantiate its narrative with concrete evidence.
Thal Khan alias Thallu had been fighting as a senior comrade with the Baloch Liberation Army since 2009. He also rendered national service in Bolan and Bambur. He belonged to a brave Baloch family that sacrificed for national freedom generation after generation. Before him, his two brothers, Shaheed Bahlil and Shaheed Sher Ali, were also martyred while fighting under the BLA organization.
