Saad Mengal, alias Shehak, son of Ghaus Bakhsh Mengal, was a resident of the Giddar area of Soorab. He joined the BLA in November 2023 and joined the Majeed Brigade in January 2025. He had been active on the Bolan Front.
Saad Mengal served as the operations commander at the Adda Camp headquarters in Noshki during Operation Herof Phase II. As both an operations commander and a fidayee sarmachar, he delivered decisive blows to the enemy through organized strategy, iron discipline, and quiet yet effective advances, forcing the enemy to face a severe defeat during the six-day battle of Operation Herof. Fidayee Saad Baloch also participated in Operation Dara-e-Bolan Phase II, where he played a decisive role in the battle through his exceptional combat capabilities.
After joining the BLA, Saad Mengal rendered services on the Bolan Front. There, he also served as a training instructor. Before every operation, he carefully assessed ground realities, maintained coordinated logistics and communications, and delivered decisive strikes at the right moment. Working effectively with limited resources, sustaining prolonged trench positions, and maintaining discipline under pressure were among his defining qualities.
He was a determined and conscious soldier of the war of freedom who made the struggle not merely a duty but the central purpose of his life. With this conviction and resolve, he sacrificed his life on the Noshki Front.

On 26 November 2025, in the Gomazi Tump tehsil of Kech district, Balochistan, 26 year old Imran Baloch, son of Nadil Hayat and a resident of Gomazi, was forcibly disappeared by operatives of a state-backed death squad. The abduction took place at his home around 2 AM on Wednesday, 26 November 2025, while his wedding celebrations were underway. Armed personnel stormed the house and took him into custody.
According to Imran’s family, the operatives acting in coordination with law enforcement agencies contacted them shortly after detaining him. Within a day of the enforced disappearance, they demanded a ransom of up to 20 million rupees for his release, threatening that failure to pay would result in the family receiving Imran’s tortured body. Although the family, unable to meet the full demand, managed to collect 7 million rupees, the armed group nevertheless dumped Imran’s mutilated body in the Gomazi area of Tump on the 28 November 2025.

On 2 June 2025 in the Mach area of Bolan, Pakistani forces and fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) came face to face when the fighters were travelling for organizational activities. At a location called Goni Para, clashes broke out between the BLA fighters and the Pakistani forces. During the confrontation, the forces deployed commandos using helicopters. In the clashes that continued for several hours, at least eight personnel of the opposing forces were killed, while five BLA fighters - Washdal, alias Mashmar; Samiullah, alias Sameer; Shehryar Shahwani, alias Chairman; Sajawal, alias Cheeda; and Nadir, alias Chiragh - achieved martyrdom.
Washdil, alias Mashmar, son of Lal Khan Sumalani, belonged to Sanjawal in the Bolan region. 22 old Washdal joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2024 and at a young age, took up arms with the resolve to fulfill what he saw as his national responsibility. He played an important role on many occasions on the Bolan front and ultimately embraced martyrdom after inflicting significant losses on the enemy.
Samiullah, alias Sameer, son of Muhammad Akram; the Shehryar, alias Chairman, son of Mehrab Khan Shahwani; and the Sajawal, alias Cheeda, son of Bawal Khan Shahwani - all belonged to Parangabad in Mastung. These three companions joined the BLA a year ago and as urban guerrillas, participated in several successful operations. Always active in striking the enemy and fulfilling organizational duties, they were present on every front. Their lives, devoted to the cause of national freedom, have become a guiding light for Baloch youth.
Nadir, alias Chiragh, son of Mazar Khan Lehri, was originally from Narmuk in the Kalat region but was residing in Quetta. In his guerrilla role, he was highly organized, vigilant, and steadfast, confronting the enemy with courage. Constantly engaged in organizational work, he remained firm in his responsibilities until his final breath.

Swearing upon the Qur’an as a solemn guarantee, the state of Pakistan sent a jirga to negotiate with Nawab Noroz Khan. Trusting the sanctity of the Qur’an as a binding assurance, Nawab Noroz Khan descended from the mountains along with his son, Battay Khan, and his companions. However, rather than engaging in meaningful negotiations or addressing their legitimate demands, the state - consistent with its pattern of duplicity - arrested them.
Nawab Noroz Khan was sentenced to life imprisonment, while his son and several of his companions were condemned to death and executed in the prisons of Sukkur and Hyderabad in Sindh.
When the armed fighters came down from the mountains, they kissed the Qur’an and declared, 'We offer ourselves in its name, but we will not surrender our weapons.' The official delegation repeatedly invoked the Qur’an to reassure them that the government would honor its commitments, insisting that no greater guarantee could exist than the Holy Book itself. Yet once they had descended, those promises were broken, and they were taken into custody. They were confined in harsh prison cells dating back to the British colonial period.
Four companions of Nawab Noroz Khan - Bhawal Khan, Masti Khan, Jamal Khan, and Wali Mohammad - were hanged in Hyderabad Jail, Sindh on 15 July 1960. Their bodies were received by Mir Rasool Bakhsh, the paternal uncle of Mir Mohammad Ali Talpur. After the funeral rites were performed, the martyrs were transported to their ancestral homeland for burial.
Nawab Noroz Khan’s son, Mir Battay Khan, along with Sabzal Khan and Ghulam Rasool, was executed in Sukkur Jail, Sindh on 15 July 1960.
Nawab Nauroz Khan himself passed away on 25 December 1965 at Civil Hospital Hyderabad, Sindh, while in custody. His body was received by Mir Rafique Ahmed. Following the funeral rites, Mir Rasool Bakhsh arranged for his body to be transported to his ancestral place.
His youngest son, Jalal Khan, remained imprisoned until 1970. He was spared execution because he was a minor at the time of his arrest.
Nawab Noroz Khan and the seven martyrs were laid to rest in the Chashma area of Kalat District, a few kilometres from Kalat Bazaar in Balochistan.
Battay Khan Zarakzai was born in 1935 in the Zehri area of Khuzdar District to Nawab Noroz Khan. He was educated up to the sixth grade. He was married and had one son.
As he grew older, Battay Khan would sit beside his father and attend the tribal court (kacheri) sessions with him.
While he was in jail, some visitors from Sindh told him, “We are saddened that you will be hanged in two days.” Battay Khan replied, “We are not afraid of danger or death. We know how to struggle and how to make sacrifices for a higher cause. Our history bears witness to this.

Saeed Ahmad Mengal, son of Noor Ahmad Mengal, was a 34 year old political worker of the Balochistan National Party - Mengal and a resident of Leezo, Khuzdar. On 6 February 2011, he was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. After months under the state’s “kill and dump” policy, his body was found at Nazar Nadi, Khuzdar, on 14 February 2011.

On 25 August 2024 Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch announced the launch of a "Fidayeen Operation" named "Herof" across Balochistan. As part of this operation, fidayeen from the BLA's elite unit, Majeed Brigade, have attacked the main camp of the Pakistani forces in Bela and have successfully infiltrated it. Meanwhile, other BLA fighters have taken full control of all major highways across Balochistan, blocking them completely.
During Operation “Herof,” 44 attacks were carried out simultaneously at 40 locations across 13 districts of Balochistan. As a result, 130 Pakistani army personnel were killed and 55 were injured. In addition, gas pipelines were destroyed at 2 locations, railway tracks at 7 locations, and 2 bridges were blown up.
During the operation, 13 vehicles transporting minerals were set on fire. Blockades were also established at 14 locations across Balochistan, and 3 members of a “death squad” were killed.
As part of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayee (suicide) operation “Herof,” the BLA’s Majeed Brigade carried out an attack on the Pakistani army’s Bela camp. The Majeed Brigade maintained control of the camp for twenty hours, during which 68 enemy personnel were killed.
Nine fidayeen (self-sacrificing fighters) of the Majeed Brigade at Bela camp - Ghaus Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Talib), Mahal Baloch (alias Zilan Kurd), Rizwan Baloch (alias Hammal), Mohammad Baloch (alias Meerak), Fazal Gul Zehri (alias Shawaiz), Tayyab Baloch (alias Lala), Junaid Zehri (alias Kami), Mohammad Asif Nechari (alias Naveed), and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Khalid) - along with Shafqat (alias Dayar) of the Fateh Squad in Mastung, were martyred in the operation.
Ghaus Baksh Sumalani, alias Talib, and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani, alias Khalid, were brothers. They took part in the same operation and were martyred while defending their motherland.

Zareef Baloch S/O Lal Bakhsh & a resident of the Balor Kulowa area in Kech, was forcibly disappeared on 31/3/2025 in Ormara by Pakistani forces, he was subjected to enforced disappearance along with his relative, Rahm Dil S/O Haider.

Rahm Dil was released the following day, while Zareef remained disappeared. Both men worked as laborers in a local general store 17/11/2025 Zareef Baloch’s tortured & bullet riddled body was recovered from the Banoke Chadai area of Kech.

Tariq Kareem, son of Mohammad Kareem, was born on 3 March 1988 and was a resident of Basima, in the Washuk district of Balochistan. He received his early education in his native town. For further education, he moved to Quetta. Tariq Kareem was an M.A. English student at the University of Balochistan. He was the former president of BSO Azad Basima Zone.
Tariq Kareem was whisked away by Pakistani intelligence agencies from Al-Rauf Royal City, Block 19, Flat No. C-614, Gulistan-e-Johar, Karachi, on 21 October, along with two of his friends. His bullet-riddled body was found dumped on 11 May 2011 at Eastern Bypass, Quetta, Balochistan.
Two of his brothers, Saqib Kareem and Asim Kareem, were also killed by Pakistani security forces on different occasions.
Tariq Kareem played a key role in expanding the Baloch liberation movement. He mobilized hundreds of Baloch youth to join the movement and was among the first in his region to raise awareness about it. Due to his tireless efforts, hundreds of young people from his region joined the Baloch liberation movement.

On 15 May 2026, a press statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that the Sarmachars (freedom fighters) of the Baloch Liberation Army carried out eighteen successful operations against the enemy across Balochistan between 4 May 2026 and 14 May 2026, resulting in the deaths of 31 personnel of the occupying Pakistani army, including a Major-rank officer, while several others were seriously injured. These attacks included seven powerful IED strikes. Additionally, the Sarmachars seized control of main highways for hours at various locations, targeting vehicles belonging to exploitative companies and occupying forces, and detaining individuals associated with these companies. In these coordinated operations, seven personnel and operatives of the state-backed “Death Squads” and Military Intelligence (MI) were also killed.
During intense clashes with the occupying forces at various locations, five BLA fighters - Ali Jan Siahpad alias Sudais, Ehsanullah alias Master Maran, Nasrullah alias Mama Zagreen, Tanveer Mengal alias Murad Khan, and Saadullah Baloch alias Wajid - embraced martyrdom while fighting valiantly against the enemy.
Nasrullah Pirkani, alias Mama Zagrain, son of Nazar Mohammad and a resident of Quetta, Balochistan, joined the BLA in November 2025. He served on the Shoorparood and Kalat fronts and was martyred on 10 May 2026 in the Chapar area of Kalat.
Nasrullah Pirkani chose to join the movement’s armed front under the platform of the BLA with a conscious and revolutionary belief that he would not accept the presence of any occupying force on the land of Balochistan under any circumstances. From an informed perspective, he understood that armed resistance and strong military power were the only means of ensuring collective survival and prosperity against an adversary believed to rely on looting and occupation.
Mama Zagrain originally belonged to Quetta, and when he decided to join the armed struggle, he was sent to the Shoorparood and Kalat fronts, where he carried out his national, revolutionary, and organizational responsibilities with sincerity and professionalism. He was not only active in practice, but through his behavior and comradeship as well, he fully embodied the qualities of a true Sarmachar.
He also upheld revolutionary principles on the battlefield with great honesty and remained committed until his last breath to the pledge he had made upon joining the organization. He stayed loyal to the homeland and to the organization’s principles and program until his final moments, rendering valuable services to the national liberation movement.

On 6 February 1976 in Karachi, Asad Mengal, son of former Chief Minister of Balochistan Atta Ullah Mengal, and his friend Ahmed Kurd were sitting at the home of Baloch politician Balakh Sher Mazari. They were discussing politics over tea. As they stepped out to leave, shots and sirens suddenly filled the air. The pair were shot and whisked away by Pakistani state forces.
On 5 July 1977, Army Chief Zia-ul-Haq declared martial law and imprisoned Prime Minister Zulfikar Ali Bhutto. Bhutto wrote several books from jail. His last book, titled “Ufwah aur Haqeeqat” (Rumour and Reality), reveals shocking insights in Chapter Three about Asad Mengal’s disappearance. According to the book, Bhutto received a call from Ghulam Mustafa Jatoi, the Chief Minister of Sindh, who informed him about the abduction of Asad Mengal and Ahmed Kurd. After several days of unsuccessful searches for the two men, Bhutto spoke to General Tikka Khan about them. In a sad tone, Tikka Khan informed Prime Minister Bhutto that they had been killed during detention and that their bodies were buried somewhere along the route to Quetta. Nobody ever found them or their bodies.
Asad Mengal and Ahmed Kurd were the first missing persons in Balochistan under Pakistani occupation, and their case was the first high-profile case of its kind. The practice of enforced disappearances began in 1973 when Bhutto dissolved the provincial assembly of Balochistan, which was headed by Chief Minister Ataullah Mengal. Bhutto initiated a military operation, and as a result, thousands of Baloch went into exile, including Marri chieftain Khair Baksh Marri, a powerful and popular Baloch nationalist politician. This led to a militant movement against Bhutto’s regime.
Mir Mohammad Ali Talpur was one of the comrades of Khair Baksh Marri and remembers the beginning of the resistance movement and what led up to it. “Enforced disappearances began during the 1973–77 insurgency. Apart from Asad Mengal and Ahmed Kurd, Shafi Mohammad Marri, Bahar Khan Marri, Ali Dost Marri, and Allah Bakhsh Marri were picked up and never heard from again,” Mir Mohammad Ali Talpur told Lok Sujag about the early days. “There must have been other Marris and Mengals too. These people were picked up on suspicion and were likely tortured to death during interrogation.”
Baloch people from diverse religious and class backgrounds participated in the mid-1970s insurgency. For example, Duleep Dass (Dali), a Christian Marxist from Karachi, was part of Khair Bux Marri’s militant movement. He was picked up in the summer of 1976 along with his friend Sher Ali Marri from Belpat, Balochistan, and was never heard from again.
In a telephonic interview with a Pakistani media channel, conducted in the presence of Akhtar Mengal, former ISI chief General (retd.) Hamid Gul admitted that Asad Mengal and Ahmed Kurd were captured injured but alive during clashes. He stated that they were later tortured and extrajudicially killed, and that their bodies were buried near Thatta in Sindh.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Naimatullah Gurgunari, alias Javed, son of Meer Ahmed Gurgunari, was a resident of Killi Pedda, Mastung. He joined the BLA in 2025, and in the same year, he became part of the BLA’s Majeed Brigade.
Naimatullah was a symbol of unparalleled courage and steadfast resolve on the battlefield. In uncertain and high-pressure circumstances, he stood firm, guided by unwavering determination and a strong sense of responsibility. His presence on the front lines inspired and encouraged his fellow Sarmachar, as he led not merely with words but through decisive action, sound judgment, and strategic wisdom, effectively managing the battlefield. In addition to his courage, he possessed exceptional combat skills.
During Operation Herof Phase II, Fidayee Naimatullah was stationed on the Mastung front, where he made the enemy vulnerable even within its own stronghold, successfully carrying out the true objectives of the operation. Pressing the enemy on all sides, he advanced into what they had considered their secure headquarters and fought bravely for several hours. On that very front, he sacrificed his life, giving concrete expression to the profound philosophy of sacrifice through his ultimate devotion.

Khuda Peer Mohammad, son of Haji Abdullah Rasheed, was a 55-year-old farmer and respected elder from Dambani Syahgesi, Zamuran, Kech. He was forcibly disappeared on 2 May 2026 at around 4:30 a.m. when FC personnel raided his home, assaulted his family, and took him and his son, Abdullah, into custody.
Khuda Peer Muhammad had spoken out against the destruction and burning of Baloch civilians’ homes and warned the FC against carrying out such actions in his area. For speaking out against oppression, he and his son, Abdullah, were forcibly disappeared.
Five hours later, the bodies of Khuda Peer Muhammad and his son were reportedly dumped near the FC camp.
data.martyrdomPlace: Dambani Syahgesi, Zamuran, Turbat district, Balochistan

data.biography: Victim of enforced disappearances

The spokesman of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), Azad Baloch, said in a statement to the media that one of its most senior commanders was shot and killed in the Bambore area of Kahan in the Kohistan Marri region on 12 April 2021.
The BLA honoured Commander Balla Marri, alias Jalal, with the title of ‘Sagaar-e-Baloch (the Sword of Baloch)’.
‘It is the highest military title of honour,
Balla Marri was one of the few fighters in the current Baloch liberation struggle who had also taken part in the Baloch freedom struggle in 1973 to resist the Pakistani military’s barbarism.
He remained steadfast and committed to the freedom movement from the age of 16 until his martyrdom at the age of 66.
Spokesman said that over the last 50 years, Balla made selfless sacrifices for the Baloch independence movement and served the struggle with utmost sincerity, honesty, and courage.
After the military attacks of the 1970s and Pakistani state terrorism in Balochistan, Balla Marri was among thousands of Marri Baloch migrants who fled Balochistan for Afghanistan, where he lived in Lashkar Gah, Helmand.
He provided invaluable services in reorganising the Baloch liberation struggle and played a vital role in the formation of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in the 1990s. Upon his return to Balochistan, he continued the freedom struggle until his martyrdom.
He bravely fought against the enemy on various fronts in Kohistan Marri and Bolan. ‘The role of Shaheed Balla Marri in organising the movement will always be remembered.’
In several military operations, especially in 2016 and 2017, when the enemy army conducted airstrikes on BLA camps, Shaheed Balla Marri was wounded on several occasions while defending the organisation’s camps and his comrades.
However, he preferred to continue fighting on the battlefield with perseverance rather than succumb to physical hardships. His commitment to the struggle for freedom was such that, in the last fifteen years—from 2006 until his martyrdom—he had not seen his family.
‘He continued to fulfil his national responsibility on the battlefield without any break. The role of Shaheed Balla Marri in the Baloch freedom struggle is a beacon for the Baloch nation.

data.martyrdomPlace: Bolan and Harnai Mountainous area, Balochistan
data.biography:
An armed encounter took place between the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) freedom fighters and the enemy forces at Jantro on Saturday, October 23, 2021 in Bolan and Harnai mountainous area. Several occupying Pakistani army personnel were killed and wounded in the battle. While valiantly defending the motherland, four BLA members also made the ultimate sacrifice. The combat with the Pakistani occupying forces began when a a patrolling party of BLA came face to face with the advancing enemy forces. BLA fighters charged at the enemy and a battle ensued that lasted for more than three hours. The BLA Sarmachars set high examples of bravery by eliminating and injuring several enemy troops and completely halting their advance. During the battle, four brave comrades, Tariq Marri alias Nasir, Mohammed Hussain Marri alias Jabal, Bakhtiar Sumalani alias Yusuf and Saifullah Zehri alias Sohrab embraced martyrdom. Deprived of moral values, the enemy army also killed two unarmed Baloch farmers named Juma Khan son of Ali Murad and Mahmood son of Shahu from nearby areas, and threw their dead bodies in the said area to portray them as BLA fighters. 
Mohammad Hussain Marri alias Jabal son of Qaim Khan resident of Lakhi Bolan had also been performing national services for the last four years by joining BLA. Equipped with national consciousness, Sangat Muhammad Hussain was a very brave and sociable companion.

On 16 February 2022, the ground forces of the Pakistani state, accompanied by air support, attacked a camp of the Baloch Nationalist Army in the early hours of the morning in the mountainous area of Kulbar, Tump. A prolonged skirmish ensued, beginning at 6:00 AM and continuing until 5:00 PM, during which the Baloch Sarmachars killed several enemy commandos and partially damaged two enemy helicopters.
In this clash, Noor Salam Noor alias Istaal, son of Bahar Baloch and a resident of Dashtuk Zamuran; Zubair Akram alias Asadjan, son of Akram Baloch and a resident of Hotabad Zamuran Bazaar; Kambar Baloch alias Mehrwan, son of Tariq and a resident of Kolaho; Sageer Baloch alias Tariq, son of Noorbakhsh and a resident of Basima; Rasool Jan alias Chirag, son of Ali Jan and a resident of Sarankan; and Hafiz Faraz alias Mullah Darwish, son of Abdul Ghani and a resident of Sarankan, were martyred.

On February 21, 2025, organizational comrades and freedom fighters Sakhi Bakhsh alias Qandeel and Balach alias Aslam were martyred in a clash with Pakistani forces and their militia (Death Squad) in the Teertej area of Awaran during an organizational mission.
Martyr Sakhi Bakhsh alias Qandeel Baloch, son of Ali Bakhsh Baloch, a resident of Teertej, Awaran, joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in 2023 and played a significant role in various battles across Balochistan.
Sakhi Baloch was also a young Balochi poet and essayist who beautifully depicted the bravery of martyrs and the natural beauty of his homeland in his poetry and writings.

On 9 September 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of ten fighters belonging to the organization. He paid tribute to the Sarmachars who were martyred while defending national liberation and their homeland, Balochistan.
The statement identified the following fighters:
1-  Akhtar Dawood, alias Ali Sher, son of Asad Sajidi.
2- Khalil Ahmad, alias Ustad Awais, son of Sher Ahmad.
3-  Imran, alias Aajo, son of Saifullah.
4-  Hasil, alias Munir Ahmad, son of Sher Mohammad.
5- Inayatullah, alias Sher Zaman, son of Manzoor Ahmad.
6- Asad Rahim, son of Rahim Baksh.
7- Mujeeb Ur Rehman, alias Shay Mureed, son of Saeed Ahmad.
8- Sahil, alias Arman, son of Peeral.
9- Javed, alias Murshid.
10- Mohammad Younis, alias Taleb, son of Mohammad Omar.

Khalil Ahmad, alias Ustad Awais, son of Sher Ahmed, resident of Dasht, Pangwa, joined the Balochistan Liberation Front a year ago and became part of the armed struggle. Martyr Khalil Ahmed possessed natural talents, and the organization entrusted him with the responsibility of training master. In this role he carried out the military training of fighters at camp as needed, which is why he was known as “Ustad”. To further mobilize and energize the Baloch national struggle and the organization, he rendered national service on various fronts including Naghau and continued to inflict defeats on the enemy in important operations. On 14 August 2026, while he and Martyr Imran, alias Aajo, were on an organizational patrol with other fighters, they encountered the occupying Pakistani army in the Daghari area of Quetta, who were dressed in plain clothes and traveling in civil vehicles. When the enemy forces attempted to encircle the fighters, the fighters counterattacked. In a clash lasting about an hour, Martyr Khalil Ahmed and Martyr Imran Aajo held the enemy back, giving their fellow fighters a chance to withdraw safely, and embraced martyrdom while fighting bravely and valiantly. More than five enemy personnel were killed and several others wounded in this clash.

Shaheed Abdul Rehman Arif Baloch was a teacher by profession and a senior member of pro independence political party, Baloch Republican Party (BRP),was abducted by the Pakistani military intelligence agencies and martyred in military custody after several months of abduction.

Ali Mohammad, son of Hakeem Baloch and a resident of Mashkai Khandri, was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani security forces on February 1, 2025. After more than four months of incommunicado detention, he was extrajudicially executed. On June 11, 2025, his body—bearing visible signs of custodial torture—was found dumped at a local hospital in Mashkai.

Mohiuddin Kurd, alias Najeeb Baloch, was born in the Sariab area of Quetta city in Balochistan. He had been associated with the freedom movement through the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army for three years prior to his martyrdom. He took part in organizational activities in Quetta and its surrounding areas. Due to his bravery and sharp intellect, he earned a distinct and respected position among his fellow comrades in a very short period of time.
On 6 March 2016, during an operation in the Yakho area of Bolan, he was martyred along with four other brave comrades,  Lal Khan Marri, aliaa Chacha; Imtiaz Zehri, alias Sangat Dilwash Baloch and Dad Ali Marri, also known as Mister. In this bloody operation, General Aslam Baloch was also injured.
Saadullah Baloch was a resident of the Mehi, Mashkai area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 18 September 2020 in Balochistan.

On March 8, 2023, Pakistani drones fired three missiles at a Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) guerrilla camp in the mountain range between Hoshap and Pasni. Following the strike, Pakistani forces began landing commandos around the camp from helicopters. In the missile attack, the camp commander, Hasil Baloch, along with four other fighters, was martyred. The remaining Sarmachars fought bravely in close combat, killing several commandos of the occupying forces before they themselves were martyred in the great cause of freedom for their homeland.
The Sarmachars who were martyred are:
Hasil (alias Doda), Wasdil (alias Jami), Nizam (alias Noshad), Waqas (alias Miras), Khalid (alias Kiyya), Shah Fahad (alias Aslam), and Ilyas Baloch (alias Rahmdil).
Martyr Commander Hasil (alias Doda), son of Shahdad and resident of Heronk, joined the Baloch armed struggle in 2014. He possessed exceptional abilities and fought many successful battles against the enemy in various parts of Makran, including Kalat and the Bolan area of Balochistan. In recognition of his dedication and skills, the organization appointed him camp commander of Kech Hoshap in 2017. He discharged his duties with distinction until his final moment. He was a brave and highly capable fighting commander.

Nazeer Ahmad Bangulzai, son of Abdul Waheed Bangulzai, a 37 year old resident of Mastung and a tailor by profession, was abducted on 29 June 2010 by Pakistani forces. On 9 August 2010, his body was found in the Pash Karam area of Mastung.

Waheed Ishaq Musiyani, alias Bahot, son of Mohammad Ishaq Musiyani, was a resident of the Chashma area of Zehri, Khuzdar. He joined the BLA in 2024, moved to the mountain front in July 2025, and served on the Kalat front. He was martyred on 15 July 2026 in Nighar, Surab, Balochistan.
Martyr Waheed, alias Bahot, conscious of his collective and national responsibilities, joined the Baloch Liberation Army two years ago and became active on the Kalat front with the aim of confronting enemy troops and their presence. After completing his basic training and familiarizing himself with important military strategies, he took part in significant military operations and engagements against the enemy. He was among those guerrilla sarmachars who did not allow the enemy time or opportunity to make war plans, but instead possessed the ability to strike them and inflict losses before they could execute any plan or movement.
Martyr Waheed, alias Ishaq, took a full part in all of the organization’s active operations on the Kalat front and was counted among those comrades at the forefront of efforts aimed at establishing important blockades against the enemy and gaining control of highways. He was a comrade who possessed both dynamism and the capacity for swift decision-making in the field. He took an active interest in, and worked diligently to complete, every responsibility assigned to him by the organization. Achieving results with limited resources; preparing thoroughly, both militarily and mentally, for any battle or military operation; taking a full part in the cleaning and maintenance of weapons and in planning; and consistently adhering to military discipline were among his notable qualities. These military and revolutionary attributes remained with him until the end.
He remained committed to military discipline and revolutionary conduct until the very end and continued to confront the enemy. During an attempt by the enemy to advance and commit aggression against the local population in the Nighar area of Surab, he, together with other comrades, confronted the enemy and forced it to retreat. After driving it back, he attained martyrdom alongside two other comrades while defending the people and the homeland. His sacrifices will be remembered with pride by generations to come.
Irfan Sarwar Baloch, a political activist, was abducted on 5 November 2010 by Pakistani forces and forcibly disappeared. On 31 December 2010, his body was found near Quetta.

Ahmed Ali Baloch, son of Ali Khan Bugti, was an 18 year old resident of the Yaro Pat area of Sui, Dera Bugti District, Balochistan. He lost his life in a landmine explosion on the morning of 19 July 2026. The landmine was allegedly planted by state-operated death squads.

On 9 November 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Republican Guards spokesperson Dostain Baloch announced the martyrdom of five members of the organisation and paid red salutes to them.

The spokesperson said: “We pay heartfelt tribute and offer red salutes to the sincere, brave, and ideologically committed fighters of the Baloch Republican Guards: Commander Habibullah Jan Jatoi, alias Laghari; Sharif Jatoi, alias Commando; Saeed Jan Jatoi, alias Nana; Hazrat Jatoi, alias Bolani; and Umeed Ali Jatoi, alias Nadir. They embraced martyrdom while bravely fighting against the occupying Pakistani army in the Sanni area of Kachhi for the freedom and right to self-determination of Balochistan."

On 1 November 2026, in the Sanni area of Kachhi, Commander Habibullah Jan and his revolutionary comrades launched an ambush against a convoy of the occupying Pakistani army.
Commander Habibullah Jan and his brave fighters fiercely engaged the enemy on the front lines, inflicting significant human and material losses on the occupying forces.
During the clash, an enemy drone suddenly launched an attack, seriously injuring Commander Habibullah Jan, Saeed, Hazrat, and Umeed. Despite their injuries, they continued to face the consequences of the attack. However, unable to survive their severe injuries, Habibullah Jan and his comrades later embraced martyrdom. All five members were residents of the Sanni area of Kachhi.

Martyr Commander Habibullah Jan Jatoi, alias Laghari Jan, son of Anwar Jatoi, resident of Sanni, Kachhi, joined the urban unit of the Baloch Republican Guards, Parvez Urban Warriors, in 2023. During the initial years, he remained associated with the urban unit and performed organizational duties with extreme secrecy, courage, and skill. He also took command of clandestine organizational activities in cities. Habibullah Jan was a fighter who strictly adhered to organizational discipline, was deeply committed to ideological thinking, possessed immense patience, and was hardworking. He was an expert instructor in explosives, mining, and heavy weapons. He always introduced new military techniques to bring Baloch guerrilla warfare in line with the requirements of the modern era and made extensive use of them in operations. Whenever and wherever the organization needed him, he always participated practically in organizational activities while remaining on the front lines.

Martyr Commander Habibullah Jan Jatoi participated in battles against the enemy on difficult and challenging fronts throughout Balochistan, including Kachhi, Sanni, Bolan, Dhadar, Sibi, and Quetta. After successfully completing his responsibilities on the urban front, he formally moved to the mountainous front in 2026. Martyr Habibullah Jan Jatoi also played an extremely key and courageous role in BRG's historic Bhagh City Operation. Among his friends, he was always cheerful, affectionate, and kind.

On 22 September 2026, a statement released by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 13 September 2026, two brave and conscientious fighters of the organization were martyred in a drone strike carried out by the Pakistani army in the Baloch homeland. The BLA paid tribute to its fallen fighters, Hidayatullah, alias Naqeeb, and Muhaibullah, alias Waheed.
‎Muhaibullah, alias Waheed made a conscious and far-sighted decision in 2023 to join the BLA, taking up the cause of defending Balochistan and the Baloch nation as a national duty. He wreaked havoc on the enemy while defending the Baloch homeland in the mountains of Mach, Rubdar, Geshk, Shorparod, Chagai, and Bolan. He challenged the enemy's occupation and stood firm like a rock against the occupier.

On 8 April 2025, Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) fighters were on patrol in the Kapudi area of Dukki when they came face to face with enemy forces. The clashes continued for hours. During the fighting, the BLA fighters managed to kill 9 enemy personnel and injure several others. In this battle, three BLA fighters - Abdul Wahab alias Deedag, Rahim Khan Marri alias Sarang, and Zahid Ali alias Washdil - were martyred.
Zahid Ali alias Washdil, son of Hazar Hamad, belonged to Jhaldi, Bolan. He joined the BLA in 2018 and remained active on the Makuran, Bolan, and Kahan fronts. He was the cousin of the martyred Nasir Marri. Comrade Washdil had dedicated his entire life to the struggle for freedom. His quiet dedication and courageous actions made him deeply respected among his comrades.

Tariq Baloch, son of Mohammad Ashraf, was born on September 12, 1993, in the district of Mastung. He was a resident of Mastung. He was an MBBS student at Khyber Medical College, Peshawar, and served as the president of BSO Azad, Peshawar Zone.
He played a key role in mobilizing Baloch students and uniting them on a single platform in areas such as Peshawar. He was abducted because of his political beliefs and his efforts to mobilize Baloch youth regarding their basic rights, education, and freedom. Like other activists of BSO Azad, he was abducted and severely tortured by the security agencies of the Pakistani state.
He had a strong passion for education. Because of this dedication, he was able to gain admission to the MBBS program at Khyber Medical College. However, the state did not allow him to complete his studies. While pursuing his medical degree, he also fulfilled his national responsibilities by actively participating in political activities under the banner of the Baloch Students Organization Azad. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising his right to peaceful political expression.
On August 18, 2011, he was abducted by Pakistan’s secret agencies in Quetta. His bullet-riddled body was found in Ganjadori, Mastung, on the same day.

Zafar Sumalani was a student at the University of Balochistan and a member of BSO Azad. He believed in peaceful political struggle and was targeted for his political expression. He mobilized many young people to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of their homeland. Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by security forces.
He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he stood firmly with the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom. He was an example of bravery and commitment. He joined the organization at an early age and remained devoted to his national ideology until the end.
He was abducted by the Frontier Corps, a paramilitary force, on 3 August 2013 from Shaal, Balochistan. His bullet-riddled body was found on 5 September 2013 in Dera Allah Yar, District Jaffarabad, Balochistan. His body bore severe signs of torture.
He was among the most committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.
data.martyrdomPlace: Dera Allah Yar, Jaffarabad district, Balochistan

data.biography: Hameed Mulla Anwar, was a resident of the Balgatar area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 5 September 2020 in Balochistan.

On 20 October 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that Sarmachars (freedom fighters) of the BLA had carried out 34 high-intensity military operations over 12 days across various regions of Balochistan between 9 and 20 October 2026. In these attacks, 14 personnel of the occupying army and nine operatives of Military Intelligence and death squads were killed, while operational control and snap-checking on key highways continued successfully under the organisational policy of an “economic blockade.”

During these operations, the freedom fighters also captured a serving soldier of the Pakistani army. In face-to-face clashes with occupying forces on various fronts, six BLA fighters fought courageously and attained the highest status of martyrdom.

Amanullah Mengal, alias Meerak, who was severely injured in a quadcopter attack by the occupying army at Ziarat Cross, succumbed to his injuries and was martyred on 8 August 2026.

On 18 September 2026, intense clashes took place between the occupying Pakistani army and BLA fighters at Siah Chang in Chagai, resulting in the deaths and injuries of several occupying army personnel, while the brave BLA fighter Ishaq Shokat Baloch, alias Meeran Baloch, attained martyrdom while fighting courageously.

On 19 September 2026, a prolonged and bloody confrontation took place between the occupying Pakistani army and BLA fighters at Paroom in Panjgur. During these clashes, four personnel of the occupying army were killed, several were injured, and one military vehicle was destroyed. In this battle, four BLA fighters - Ali Baloch, alias Salman Baloch; Ikhtiyar Baloch, alias Fareed Baloch; Sanaullah Baloch, alias Shay Mureed; and Sohail Baloch, alias Haji Absar - fought heroically and attained the highest status of martyrdom.

Amanullah Mengal, alias Meerak Baloch, son of Abdul Kabeer Mengal, was a resident of Ahmed Wall, Noshki, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Bolan and Ziarat fronts. He was martyred on 8 August 2026 in Ziarat, Balochistan.


Amanullah Mengal, a native of Noshki, joined the Baloch Liberation Army this year in support of national freedom, state sovereignty, and the public interest and was deployed to the Bolan front. He was among the Sarmachar who excelled in the BLA’s physical and mental training. After completing the training, he was sent to the front lines, where he carried out his duties as a national fighter with great bravery and courage. He was counted among those comrades who adhered to and upheld the organization’s discipline.

Amanullah Mengal, imbued with the spirit and awareness of national liberation, was among those who displayed extraordinary bravery on the battlefield. In addition to Bolan, he also carried out his duties in Ziarat in defense of the homeland and its liberation. His hard work, boundless love for his country, and devotion to his national duty were always his hallmarks. On August 8, following a confrontation with the enemy, he offered his life in defense of his country, remaining true to his promise and commitment and giving practical expression to the conviction that had led him, through ideological awakening, to choose the path of national liberation.

Operation Dara-e-Bolan, which began on 29 January 2024 continued for two days until 31 January 2024 and was successfully concluded after achieving its intended objectives. A total of 385 Sarmachars from four different units of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) participated in Operation Dara-e-Bolan. Among them were 12 Fidayeen from the BLA’s Majeed Brigade. The other participating units included the Fateh Squad, the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS) and the Intelligence Wing.
Operation Dara-e-Bolan commenced on the evening of 29 January 2024 at 9:00 pm local time and continued for two days. After achieving the desired results, the BLA’s Senior Command Council announced the conclusion of Operation Dara-e-Bolan on 31 January 2024 at 7:00 pm and issued instructions to all units to vacate their positions and report back to their base camps.
During the operation, BLA Sarmachars took complete control of an area within a 70 kilometre radius, including Mach city and the strategically important National Highway N-65. Over the course of Operation Dara-e-Bolan, a total of 78 enemy personnel were killed. These included 45 Frontier Corps (FC) personnel who were killed within the first three hours of the operation in Mach city; 10 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on an army camp at the Pir Ghaib Bolan location; 4 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on a military convoy at the Gokurt Mach location; 12 regular army personnel who were killed on 30 January when Majeed Brigade Fidayeen eliminated them and entered the FC headquarters; and at least 5 SSG commandos who were targeted and killed by the Fidayeen on 31 January 2024. In addition, two police personnel were also killed, including one Station House Officer (SHO).
A large number of Levies and police personnel were captured by the BLA during the operation; however, as they were Baloch, they were released. During Operation Dara-e-Bolan, 13 brave fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army attained martyrdom. Of these, 12 martyred Sarmachars belonged to the Majeed Brigade Fidayeen, while one martyred Sarmachar was from the BLA’s Fateh Squad.
The martyred Sarmachars were: Qasim Baloch, Saddam Hussain, Salal Baloch, Farooq Baloch, Atta Baloch, Hammal Momin, Zeeshan Zehri, Nadir Bangulzai, Nizam Baloch, Zeeshan Baloch, Jamal Baloch, Wadood Satakzai, and Kashif Shahwani.
Jamal Baloch, alias Qambar Mehrwan, son of Abdul Majeed, belonged to the Jhao Kodo area of Awaran. He was a highly educated young man who had completed his university graduation. Jamal Baloch had been an active BSO worker since 2009 during his student years. In 2015, he joined the armed front of the Baloch national liberation struggle. He was an exceptionally capable guerrilla fighter as well as an ideologically committed political activist. Two years prior, he offered his services to the BLA - Majeed Brigade and completed his fidayeen training with dedication. During Operation Dara-e-Bolan, he held a difficult front and, until his last bullet and final breath, did not allow his position to fall into enemy hands.

data.martyrdomPlace: Baddo Naddi, Zardain Koti, Kharan, Balochistan
data.biography:
Salahuddin Baloch, son of Mohammad Ali and a resident of Kulan, Kharan, was forcibly disappeared by security forces along with his brother, Azar, on 7 August 2026 at approximately 2:00 PM from their home.

Salahuddin worked as a vegetable vendor at Chief Chowk, Kharan. A few days after their enforced disappearance, his brother, Azar, was released, while Salahuddin remained in the custody of the security forces. After two months of enforced disappearance, Salahuddin was killed in a staged encounter on 31 October 2026. His body was found near Baddo Naddi, Zardain Koti, Kharan.

The massacre of Baloch by the Muttahida Qaumi Movement (MQM) in Karachi on January 7, 2010, sparked a series of protests all over Balochistan. Baloch people marched in support of their brothers in Karachi in every major city and town. The Baloch Student Organization (BSO-Azaad) called for a peaceful demonstration in Khuzdar to express their anger against Pakistan’s planned genocide of Baloch living in Karachi. On January 15, 2010, students gathered at Degree College Khuzdar. Activists of the Baloch National Front (BNF) also came and joined them to show their solidarity. As the protest rally departed from the college, within a few minutes it came under fire from all sides. The Pakistani army’s assault on the unprovoked peaceful rally was so brutal and severe that it left many dead and injured.
Baloch activists rushed their fallen comrades to the hospital. Two Baloch youths, Ali Dost Baloch, who worked in the municipal office, and Saddam Hussain Baloch, a member of BSO-Azaad and a student of Residential College Khuzdar, succumbed to their injuries and joined the martyrs of the Baloch heroic struggle for the liberation of their motherland. Liaqat Ali Baloch, Zafar Baloch, Inayat Baloch, Ghulam Fareed Baloch, and Nazeer Baloch were severely injured. The wounded were later shifted to Karachi due to the lack of medical facilities in Balochistan. Doctors in Karachi amputated Liaqat Ali Baloch’s leg from the knee to save his life.

Life and Occupation

Jameel Yaqoob was a resident of the Turbat district in Balochistan. He was known as a dedicated grassroots worker who balanced his political commitments with his responsibilities as a laborer. His life represented the involvement of the common working class in the Baloch national movement, and he was respected for his humility and persistence in advocating for provincial autonomy and rights.

Political Affiliation

He was an active member of the Balochistan National Party (BNP-Mengal). Within the party, he was recognized as a committed activist who worked to mobilize the local population in Kech. Unlike high-profile leaders, Jameel focused on the day to day struggles of the people, connecting the broader political goals of the BNP Mengal to the socio economic realities of Baloch laborers.

Abduction and Martyrdom

Jameel Yaqoob’s life was cut short during a period of intense political unrest in Balochistan:

The Abduction: On August 28, 2010, at approximately 4:00 AM, Jameel was abducted from a motor service station in Turbat. According to reports from the Asian Human Rights Commission (AHRC), he was taken by individuals in both uniform and plain clothes. His family later alleged that they recognized one of the men as being associated with a state intelligence agency.

The "Kill and Dump": After being missing for nearly six months, his bullet-riddled body was discovered on February 10, 2011, in the Herronk area of the Kech district. His body reportedly bore marks of extreme physical torture.

The Herronk Incident

Jameel Yaqoob was martyred alongside Comrade Qayyum Baloch, a student activist from Gwadar. Their discovery in Herronk sparked significant protests in Turbat and across the Kech region, as they became symbols of the "kill and dump" policy targeting Baloch political workers during that era.

Habeeb Ul Rehman Baloch, son of Noor Mohammad Bangulzai, was born in 1987. He was a resident of District Mastung. Habeeb Ul Rehman was a matric-level student and a member of BSO Azad. He received his early education in his hometown, Mastung.
He mobilized many young people to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of their homeland. Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by security forces. He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he stood firmly with the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom.
He was an example of bravery and commitment. He joined the organization at an early age and remained dedicated to his national ideology until the end. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for his peaceful political expression.
He was abducted from Quetta on November 19, 2010. His bullet-riddled body was found in Mastung on December 12, 2010. His body bore severe signs of torture.
He was among the most committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many young people to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

Martyr Haris Baloch, alias Sawad Baloch, was born in the house of Ghulam Ali in Gaddagi, Balgtar area of Panjgur, Balochistan. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in 2019. He embraced martyrdom along with eight comrades - Jalil Sher Baloch, Samad Baloch, Dad Shah, Shoaib Baloch, Rahmdil Baloch, Nawaz Baloch, and Kambar Baloch - in a Pakistan Army drone attack on November 29, 2022, in the Jath, Kolwa area of Kech, Balochistan.

Tariq Tahir Baloch, a poet and social activist, was abducted on 13 November 2010 by Pakistani forces and forcibly disappeared. He was extrajudicially killed in custody, and on 2 June 2011, his body was dumped in the Uthal area of Balochistan.
Mohammad Yaqoob Baloch, was a resident of the Anjira, Khuzdar area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 14 April 2014 in Balochistan.
Younis Tokali Baloch was a resident of Zamuran, martyred on 16 November 2017.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
In Gwadar, nine Fidayeen of the BLA Majeed Brigade were divided into two units and took part in the operation. The first unit, which included Fidayeen Hawa Baloch (alias Droshum), Yahya Lal (alias Lashari), Adnan Arman (alias Changaiz), and Yousif Baloch (alias Yagi), attacked the compound of the occupying Pakistani intelligence agencies, resulting in the elimination of 12 personnel. Women and children in residential quarters near the compound were provided safe passage; however, the occupying army later martyred these same civilians by opening fire.
About forty minutes later, occupying forces advanced toward the compound, leading to clashes that continued until the evening. In these clashes, more than 24 personnel were eliminated, and three military vehicles, including an armored vehicle, were destroyed.
The second squad, which included Fidayeen Kambar Ismail (alias Sarbaz), Khurshid KB (alias Arman), Waseem Baloch (alias Kareem), Shoaib Baloch (alias Shehzad), and Yasir, took up strong positions in Port Bazaar near Gwadar Port. After announcements were made in mosques, freedom fighters went to the bazaar, met the public, and held political discussions. After repelling the advance of occupying forces in the city, the freedom fighters later advanced toward the port and fired several rockets that hit their targets. Clashes continued until the next day, eliminating more than 19 personnel.
Khurshid KB, alias Arman, son of Khuda Baksh and a resident of Kallag Sorani, Turbat District, was born in 1999 and joined the Baloch Liberation Army on 1 June 2022. After joining the organization, he gradually assumed responsibilities and reached the stage of making a fidayee decision in January 2023. This decision was not the result of haste or a momentary impulse, but emerged from a sustained process of reflection and ground-level experience.
During his deployment on the Gwadar front, his responsibilities were not limited to frontline presence alone. They also included coordination, maintaining discipline, and meeting operational requirements according to circumstances. His role reflects the reality that, at times, significance in a struggle is recognized not through noise or display, but through continuity, responsibility, and quiet action.

On 20 October 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that Sarmachars (freedom fighters) of the BLA had carried out 34 high-intensity military operations over 12 days across various regions of Balochistan between 9 and 20 October 2026. In these attacks, 14 personnel of the occupying army and nine operatives of Military Intelligence and death squads were killed, while operational control and snap-checking on key highways continued successfully under the organisational policy of an “economic blockade.”

During these operations, the freedom fighters also captured a serving soldier of the Pakistani army. In face-to-face clashes with occupying forces on various fronts, six BLA fighters fought courageously and attained the highest status of martyrdom.

Amanullah Mengal, alias Meerak, who was severely injured in a quadcopter attack by the occupying army at Ziarat Cross, succumbed to his injuries and was martyred on 8 August 2026.

On 18 September 2026, intense clashes took place between the occupying Pakistani army and BLA fighters at Siah Chang in Chagai, resulting in the deaths and injuries of several occupying army personnel, while the brave BLA fighter Ishaq Shokat Baloch, alias Meeran Baloch, attained martyrdom while fighting courageously.

On 19 September 2026, a prolonged and bloody confrontation took place between the occupying Pakistani army and BLA fighters at Paroom in Panjgur. During these clashes, four personnel of the occupying army were killed, several were injured, and one military vehicle was destroyed. In this battle, four BLA fighters - Ali Baloch, alias Salman Baloch; Ikhtiyar Baloch, alias Fareed Baloch; Sanaullah Baloch, alias Shay Mureed; and Sohail Baloch, alias Haji Absar - fought heroically and attained the highest status of martyrdom.

Ikhtayar Baloch, alias Fareed Baloch, son of Ghulam Nabi, was a resident of Sindh. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served in Paroom, Panjgur, Balochistan. He was martyred on 19 September 2026 in the Paroom area of Panjgur District, Balochistan.

Recognizing the significance of Baloch national dignity and honor and the great caravan of national liberation, Sangat Ikhtayar, who hailed from Sindh, made the decision without fear or hesitation to resist the Pakistani occupying force through the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army in the struggle for national freedom. He began his journey toward freedom from the Panjgur front this year. As per the usual organizational process, he underwent various stages of training and prepared himself physically and mentally for the field with great fighting spirit and enthusiasm. Afterwards, he took an active part in military actions against the enemy on the battlefront and inflicted losses on them.

Through his active participation on the battlefield and his steadfastness until his martyrdom, Sangat Ikhtayar Baloch demonstrated bravery, courage, and patriotism, conveying a clear message to millions of other young people rather than leaving them in uncertainty. Sangat Ikhtayar Baloch participated in various military engagements against the enemy and inflicted losses on them. On September 19, during ongoing actions against the enemy, he attained the supreme rank of martyrdom alongside some other comrades in an enemy attack, bringing honor to his name in the history of national liberation.

Deen Mohammad Marri, son of Sher Mohammad, was a 55 year old tribal elder and a resident of Hub, Lasbela. On 28 February 2011, he was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. A few days later, on 8 March 2011, his body was dumped at Uthal Zero Point in Lasbela.

Haneef Baloch, son of Shambay Baloch, was born in 1989 in Pasni, District Gwadar. He was an intermediate student at an inter college in Pasni and served as the president of BSO Azad Pasni Zone. From an early age, he became involved in the struggle for Baloch national liberation under the umbrella of the Baloch Students Organization Azad.
He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising his right to peaceful political expression. On July 4, 2011, he was abducted from Hub Chowki by Pakistan’s secret agencies.
Haneef played an important role in mobilizing the youth of Pasni, encouraging them to join the organization. He actively participated in its activities, including wall-chalking, distributing pamphlets, books, and other literature.
After two days of extreme torture, his bullet-riddled body was found dumped in Chakoli, Pasni, located on the Coastal Highway, on July 6, 2011. He had been shot in the head and chest, and his body bore deep marks of torture during custody.
He was killed under the Pakistani state’s “kill and dump” policy. His sacrifice for the greater cause of the Baloch nation will be remembered for generations.

On November 10, 2024 (Sunday) at 5:00 PM, fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) surrounded a Pakistani Army camp in the Dasht Kuddan area of District Kech from two sides and launched a fierce attack using modern and heavy weapons. During the assault, 16 Pakistani military personnel, including one officer, were killed on the spot, while several others were injured. The enemy also suffered significant material losses.
Prior to the attack, the Sarmachars (BLF fighters) sealed off all access and escape routes in the area before striking the enemy camp. The assault was so intense that the defeated occupying forces had no opportunity to regroup or recover.
The Sarmachars also targeted enemy reinforcements rushing to the camp, inflicting further casualties and material damage.
The operation involved fighters from the BLF’s intelligence wing as well as the elite Qurban Unit. Using advanced and heavy weaponry, the Sarmachars subjected the camp to intense fire. Upon reaching close proximity, they destroyed the camp’s protective walls and bunkers with rocket-propelled grenades. The fighters were on the verge of entering the camp to seize weapons when Captain Jamal Baloch of the Qurban Unit was martyred. As a result, the Sarmachars retrieved the body of their fallen comrade and safely withdrew from the area.
In this operation, BLF fighter Captain Jamal Baloch, alias Nako Brahim, son of Mola Bakhsh, resident of Sari Bazaar, Tump (Gomazi), attained martyrdom while bravely fighting the enemy.
Martyr Captain Jamal Baloch was a politically conscious, highly skilled, and battle-tested fighter. He joined the Baloch liberation movement with the BLF in 2010. After serving in the urban network for two years, he came under enemy surveillance and, in 2012, moved to the mountains to formally join the armed wing.
Captain Jamal Baloch (Nako Brahim) participated in successful operations against occupying forces in areas including Siyahji, Mazanband, Kulbar, Zamuran, Buleda and Balgatar, inflicting heavy human and material losses on the enemy. He was widely respected among his comrades for his self-sacrifice, combat proficiency, courage and composure. Thanks to his strong political awareness, he also played a vital role in strengthening the organization’s institutions and camps.
During the Dasht Kuddan attack, Martyr Jamal Baloch was commanding the frontline “Qurban Unit.” With the support of his comrades, he successfully reached the camp’s perimeter and caused panic and disarray in the enemy ranks.
Captain Jamal Baloch had joined the Qurban Unit one year before his martyrdom and carried out his duties with distinction. While leading his unit in this operation, he embraced the highest honor of martyrdom and etched his name forever in the annals of Baloch history.

Ilyas Nizar was born on 12 July 1984, in the home of Nizar Mohammad Baloch in Shahrak, Kikken, Makuran, District Kech. He completed his early schooling in his native village and graduated from Government Degree College Turbat in 2017. He then moved to Quetta for higher education, where he gained admission to a Master’s program (MCS) at the University of Balochistan.
Understanding the forced deprivation of Baloch society by the Pakistani state made him a sensitive teacher, dedicated to a cause to which he remained committed throughout his life. He taught in various institutions in Turbat and later in Quetta until his final year. He remained committed to the BSO Azad’s junior teaching policy, under which he taught junior fellow students at the university.
The first Balochi-language children’s monthly magazine, “Darwant”, which remained in circulation for two years until his involuntary disappearance by the Pakistani state, was the vision and effort of this young Baloch journalist.
A mystic soul with a secular mind, he visited churches, temples, and mosques and practiced meditation late at night in search of his Creator. In Quetta, as a BSO Azad activist, he frequently visited the Voice for Baloch Missing Persons (VBMP) camp at Quetta Press Club.
On 21 December 2010, while en route to Turbat from Quetta, he was forced to disembark from a bus at the Badok checkpoint on the Coastal Highway by Pakistani state intelligence agencies and became one among thousands of Baloch activists who have been forcibly disappeared by Pakistan.
After two weeks, on 5 January 2011, Ilyas Nizar Baloch’s tortured body, bearing four bullet wounds, was found alongside another BSO Azad activist, Qambar Chakar, in Murghap area of Pedrak. His body showed severe signs of torture. He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad.
His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

Hatim Baloch, son of Ahmed, was a 29-year-old government teacher and resident of the Washbod area of Panjgur. He was forcibly disappeared from Washbod Main Bazaar before Eid. He was allegedly taken by state-backed death squads, and his whereabouts remained unknown for weeks.
Hatim was a teacher whose life was dedicated to educating others. Instead of being protected as a civilian and educator, he became another victim of the violence inflicted upon the Baloch people. On 8 August 2026, his body was found dumped near Jaffar Scheme on the Main CPEC Road, bringing a devastating end to the period of uncertainty endured by his family.

On 11 August 2025, the umbrella alliance of Baloch armed organizations in Balochistan, Baloch Raji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS), launched coordinated operations during which several government installations were destroyed and dozens of Pakistani military personnel were killed. A large quantity of military equipment was also reportedly seized. Images showing the bodies of the deceased Pakistani soldiers, destroyed vehicles, and military uniforms hanging at various locations subsequently went viral on social media.
Even after the coordinated attacks had ended, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), a member of the BRAS alliance, maintained control of the Zehri area and successfully repelled multiple attempts by Pakistani forces to advance into the region.
After holding control of the area for several days, the BLA eventually withdrew. Following its withdrawal, the Pakistani military entered Zehri with gunship helicopters, battle tanks, and a large contingent of troops. According to reports, the forces spread fear and panic through looting and other actions in the area. Since then, Zehri and its surrounding regions have remained under military operations and repression.
Following their defeat at the hands of the armed groups, Pakistani forces allegedly targeted civilians in retaliation. As a result of this repression, 11 Baloch individuals were reportedly killed.
On 16 April 2026, several people from Zehri and its surrounding areas - including Wadera Mohammad Dayaan, Imam Bakhsh, Manzoor Ahmad Miraji, Munir Hayat Dayaan, Izzatullah Pandrani, Habibullah, Mohammad Sharif, Mohammad Ramzan, and three unidentified individuals - were reportedly extrajudicially executed by Pakistani forces while traveling along roads in the Sohinda area. One individual, Abdul Salam, survived with serious injuries.
During the ongoing military operation in the area, these individuals were allegedly detained by Pakistani forces from various locations and transferred to the Sohinda Rest House, approximately five kilometres from Noorgama. There, their hands and feet were allegedly bound, they were blindfolded, and they were subsequently shot dead.
The incident occurred one day after the BLA claimed that two of its fighters had been killed during clashes in the Sohinda area.
In its statement, the BLA said that, on 15 April 2026, its fighters targeted advancing Pakistani military units with a remote-controlled explosive device. Following the explosion, they allegedly carried out an ambush on a military convoy moving toward the area.
The organization claimed that ten Pakistani military personnel were killed in the two attacks, while two of its own fighters, Tanveer Mengal and Saadullah, were also killed.

Zahoor Ahmad Bangulzai, son of Haider Bangulzai, a 33 year old resident of Mastung, was a member of the Baloch Students Organization – Azad (BSO-Azad). He was abducted on 23 September 2010 by Pakistani forces, and a month later, on 22 October 2010, his body was found in Ghanja Dori, Mastung.

Hikmatullah Lehri, alias Fahad, son of Abdul Baqi Lehri, was a resident of the Killi Barezei area of Quetta, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Mastung fronts. He was martyred on September 19, 2026, in the Shirnaap area of Mastung, Balochistan.
After developing a sense of hatred for the enemy’s forcible occupation and enslavement of Pakistan and an appreciation for the greatness of freedom and self-determination, Hikmat Ullah Lehri, a native of Quetta, made the historic decision this year to join the Baloch Liberation Army. After joining, in accordance with organizational procedures, he was sent to a training camp for physical, mental, moral, and revolutionary training. There, after completing basic courses in combat, discipline, a sense of responsibility, and physical training, he was deployed to the front lines. On the active and mobile front lines against the enemy, Martyr Hikmat Ullah Lehri proved himself to be an exceptionally brave and capable fighter, inflicting severe losses on the enemy.
Hikmatullah Lehri, as a dynamic fighter on the front lines, firmly demonstrated his combat skills and took part in several deadly attacks against the enemy occupying the homeland. Targeting enemy movements on the Mastung front and coordinating attacks on their convoys, he also took part in disrupting the enemy’s supply chain. He stood alongside his fellow fighters in activities aimed at expanding organizational strength and influence in the region and broadening operational activities, playing a responsible combat role. He remained active on the BLA platform with these same revolutionary and combat commitments until the end. He sacrificed his life for his homeland on September 19 at Shirnaap, giving his life for national liberation. History will always remember him.

Imtiaz Baloch, alias Azal, son of Sabir Ahmad, was a resident of Maripur, Karachi. He joined the BLA in June 2022 and went to the mountainous front in 2023, joining the Majeed Brigade in February 2024. He served on the Bolan, Kahan, Nagaho, Duki, and ShorParood fronts and was martyred in Noshki. After joining the BLA, Imtiaz Baloch remained active on the urban front. A year later, under an organizational decision, he was transferred to the mountainous front in Bolan. In addition to Bolan, he also served on the fronts of Kahan, Nagaho, Duki, and ShorParood. Fidayee Imtiaz Baloch also participated in Operation Dara-e-Bolan Phase I and Operation Herof Phase I.
Imtiaz Baloch was a devoted fighter in the war of freedom, whose mind, steps, and weapon were all focused on a single objective. He viewed the battlefield not merely as a confrontation but as a decisive struggle, where every move was calculated and every moment demanded vigilance. Breaking the enemy’s formations, restricting its movements, and securing his own positions were among his key combat strengths. Therefore, before every engagement, he thoroughly surveyed the area, maintained strong communications, and advanced each phase of the operation in an organized manner.
Imtiaz Baloch belonged to the Maripur area of Karachi. He began his journey in the national freedom movement through revolutionary political activism. Absorbing revolutionary thought, he started his path from Maripur and later moved to the Bolan front. Rather than seeking comfort and luxury in a city like Karachi, martyr Imtiaz chose the hard path of resistance against national subjugation. On this basis, he joined the BLA and played his role in the war of national liberation, becoming immortal in history. In an attempt to distance him from the freedom movement, his two brothers were subjected to enforced disappearance, one of whom remains missing to this day. Yet his resolve never wavered, as he was intellectually strong and highly conscious, remaining steadfast in his cause until his last breath.
