During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Sakim Baloch, alias Hakim, son of Shameem Ahmed, was born in 2004 and was a resident of the Apsar area of Turbat district in Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2023 and later became part of the BLA wing, Majeed Brigade, in 2025.
Sakim belonged to a family that had already made profound sacrifices over the years. Two members of his family, Shaheed Fidayee Kareem and Shaheed Muslim Guro, had previously embraced martyrdom. Against this backdrop, Sakim Baloch’s path was not the result of a sudden decision, but the outcome of a sustained intellectual and emotional journey.
Before joining the organization, he led an ordinary life and worked as a driver. Alongside this, he was also a poet, expressing his emotions, observations, and inner conflicts through words. His poetry reflected both the harshness of life and the persistence of hope and questioning.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, his life came to an end on the Turbat front. His martyrdom left behind the memory of a young man shaped by his circumstances, family history, and personal sensitivity. Sakim Baloch’s identity is not confined to a name or a single moment; he will be remembered as someone who carried both words and decisions, feelings and a deep sense of responsibility.

On 4th January 2025 Majeed Brigade, the elite Fidayee unit of the Baloch Liberation Army, attacked an occupying Pakistani army convoy at Behman, eight kilometers from Turbat city, yesterday at 5:45 pm, causing heavy casualties to the enemy. The Pakistani army convoy, which included five buses and seven military vehicles, was heading from Karachi to the FC Headquarters in Turbat. The Majeed Brigade’s Fidayee unit detonated a VBIED into the convoy, eliminating 47 army personnel and wounding more than 30. One bus was completely destroyed, others were partially disabled and a military vehicle was completely destroyed in the attack.
The convoy, consisting of 13 vehicles, included personnel from the occupying army’s MI 309, FC SIU, FC 117 Wing, FC 326 Wing and FC 81 Wing. The convoy also included the vehicle of SSP Police retired army Captain Zohaib Mohsin, who was on vacation.
This operation was carried out based on information provided by the organization’s intelligence wing, “ZIRAB.” ZIRAB had provided authentic information that an enemy convoy was leaving Karachi for Turbat and included important troops of the occupying army. The success of this mission reflects the excellent performance of our intelligence and the unparalleled sacrifice of the Fidayee Sangat. This attack is a clear message that the land of Balochistan will never be safe for the occupying state.
The Fidayee attack was carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army’s Bahar Ali, alias Karwan. Sangat Bahar Ali belonged to Qohda Murad Muhammad Bazar in the Dasht Hochat area of ​​Turbat. He joined the Baloch National Movement in 2017 and fought vigorously against the enemy on both urban and mountain fronts through his exceptional services. In 2022, he willingly offered himself for the Fidayee mission and became part of the Majeed Brigade, where he made his final sacrifice and became immortal in the history of the Baloch national struggle.

On May 20, 2025, Yasir, son of Nasram Baloch and a resident of Geshkur, Tehsil Buleda in the Kech district of Balochistan, was extrajudicially shot and killed by operatives of a death squad acting under the aegis of Pakistani forces. Yasir, a daily-wage labourer working in an orchard, was deliberately targeted. He was the sole breadwinner for his family, and his death has left them devastated.

The resistance and courage shown by the martyrs of Mehi, Mashkay against the aggression of the occupying Pakistani army on June 30, 2015, will be remembered in golden words in the pages of history. Thanks to the sacrifices of these martyrs, awareness of the struggle against Pakistani occupation is spreading to every corner of Balochistan. History honors those who stand up for the defense of their nation and homeland at decisive moments.
The Baloch national freedom movement is ongoing and strong thanks to the sacrifices of these martyrs. These great sacrifices of the martyrs have fostered the consciousness within the Baloch nation that the enemy occupying Balochistan should not be allowed to breathe in peace until they suffocate and run away. It should be remembered that the occupier has always treated the enslaved people with the same inhumane treatment that the state of Pakistan is doing with the Baloch in occupied Balochistan, including killings, enforced disappearances and dumping of mutilated bodies and other atrocities included.
The Martyrs of Mehi area of Mashkay Shaheed Major Sulaiman alias Shehak Jan, Zakir Jan, and Safar Khan Baloch are the great sons of the nation. Those who bravely and courageously adopted the path of resistance against the Pakistani occupation and colonial policy and laid down their lives fighting for the freedom of the country. These great sacrifices of martyrs are encouraging us to leave tribalism, territorialism and become a part of this national struggle as Baloch and strengthen it. Martyrs of Balochistan sacrificed their precious lives so that the Baloch nation could live with freedom and dignity. The national movement needs to be further strengthened and organized while carrying forward this great ideology of martyrs and the spirit of sacrifice.
Rahmat Jamal, alias Faris, was a resident of the Kapkapar, Dasht area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 12 August 2020 in Balochistan.

On 11 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch announced the martyrdom of 14 fighters of the organization who attained martyrdom in confrontations with the Pakistani army and in airstrikes while defending their homeland, Balochistan, and fighting for national liberation and the right to self-determination.

On 13 August 2026, Pakistani Air Force fighter jets bombarded the Pandran area of Kalat District in Balochistan, resulting in the martyrdom of four members of the organization: Waseem Baloch, alias Farhan; Obaidullah Baloch, alias Shaheen; Nawaz Ali Baloch, alias Dilshad; and Mohammad Hassan, alias Ahmad.

On 25 August 2026, during an organizational mission in the Kech area of Balochistan, Sher Jan, alias Jamal, was shot from behind by a traitor, resulting in his martyrdom.

On 3 September 2026, while patrolling in the Mastung area of Balochistan, the organization’s brave fighters, Mohammad Younis, alias Salal; Sameer Ahmad, alias Zemal; Aziz Ahmad, alias Janan; and Sikandar Baloch, confronted Pakistani forces, targeted several enemy personnel, and embraced martyrdom.

On 14 September 2026, while engaging Pakistani forces and defending his fellow fighters in the Machani Kor Paroom area of Panjgur District, Babar Baloch, alias Kambar, embraced martyrdom.

On 18 September 2026, during a confrontation with Pakistani forces in the Chagi area of Balochistan, fighters of the organization, Riaz Baloch, alias Sabir; Taimoor Shah, alias Shaheen; Zia Ul Haq, alias Ziaullah; and Jumma Baloch, alias Commando, embraced martyrdom.

Mohammad Younis, alias Salal, son of Haji Abdul Qadir, resident of Keli Shahnawaz, Quetta, joined the BLF in 2026. After inflicting human and material losses on the enemy in numerous engagements on the Nagahu front, he became part of a patrol team on the Mastung front. On 3 September 2026, during a patrol in Mastung, he confronted an attack by the occupying enemy, targeted several enemy personnel, and attained martyrdom.

Yasin Baloch, son of Muhammad Ghaus, was a 28 year old farmer and resident of Zahoor Colony, Dalbandin. He was killed by the Pakistani army on 5 October 2024, near Kor Nali Patek, Dalbandin, after being shot while passing through a checkpoint.
Yasin was his parents’ only son. Both of his parents had already passed away, and he was the sole breadwinner of the family. He was responsible for supporting his sisters when army personnel opened fire on him as he passed through a checkpoint. His colleague, Sami, was also injured in the firing. Yasin was his sisters’ only hope and the person they depended on for survival. His killing left his two sisters without the brother who had shouldered the responsibility of supporting their household.

On the night of June 27, 2025, the bullet-riddled body of Qaim Hayat, son of Mahmed Hayat, a 22-year-old resident of Asiabad, Tump, was recovered near Zubaida Jalal Road in the Meerabad area of Tump. According to Levies officials, Qaim was brutally shot multiple times and left dead by the roadside.
Qaim Hayat was a driver and lived a simple life. His killing was carried out by members of a state-backed death squad operating in the region, part of the broader network supported by Pakistani forces.

In the early hours of 27th May 2025, the Pakistani military once again demonstrated its unrelenting brutality through a heinous and unlawful operation in the Malaar Machhi area of Awaran, Balochistan. The attack resulted in the extrajudicial execution of two Baloch individuals and the critical wounding of a third, an elderly woman, all belonging to a single Baloch family that has already endured years of state persecution.
Naeem Baloch, son of Sanjar Baloch, and his aunt Hoori, daughter of Qasim, were shot dead by Pakistani forces after security personnel stormed their home around 1 AM and opened indiscriminate fire. Naeem’s mother, Dadi Baloch, was critically injured and left without medical assistance until the following morning, her condition deteriorating due to state-imposed neglect. This massacre marks the fourth such incident in Awaran within a single week, part of an intensifying campaign of systematic violence.
This was not the first time this family had suffered at the hands of the state. In 2015, seven of their relatives, including another aunt, Gohar, were killed in an aerial bombardment. In 2023, Naeem himself was forcibly disappeared. His mother, now critically injured, had previously been detained in 2015.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Aqib Bangulzai, alias Lala Tayyab, son of Ali Sher Bangulzai, was a resident of Smalabad, Quetta. He was 24 years old. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2025 and later joined the Majeed Brigade in 2025. He was appointed as the Second Operational Commander in the Mastung Camp Attack.
Aqib Bangulzai, alias Lala Tayyab, was one of those young men who stayed away from spectacle and remained close to action. He belonged to that quiet kind of soldier, speaking rarely, but when he did, it was with conviction, and when he fought, it was with full focus, never looking back.
After joining the Majeed Brigade, he quickly became one of those individuals trusted in the field. During the Mastung camp operation, as the Second Operational Commander, Lala Tayyab not only provided tactical leadership but also became a source of morale and confidence for those around him.
Muslim Baloch was a resident of the Mehi, Mashkai area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 18 September 2020 in Balochistan.

Nadil Baloch, the son of Muhammad Naseem and a resident of Pawan, Gwadar, was a 20-year-old student. On 19 April 2026, at around 1:30 a.m., personnel from the Frontier Corps and Military Intelligence forcibly disappeared him from his home.
For five months, his family waited for his return, living with fear and uncertainty. On 17 September 2026, following his extrajudicial killing, Nadil’s body was found dumped alongside the bodies of Ehsan Baloch and Hassan Rafiq in Kuldan, Dannuk, Gwadar.
Amjid Baloch, was a resident of the Kolwah area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 16 October 2015 in Balochistan.

On 22 September 2026, a statement released by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 13 September 2026, two brave and conscientious fighters of the organization were martyred in a drone strike carried out by the Pakistani army in the Baloch homeland. The BLA paid tribute to its fallen fighters, Hidayatullah, alias Naqeeb, and Muhaibullah, alias Waheed.
‎Hidayatullah, alias Naqeeb joined the BLA in 2025, deciding to play an active role in the Baloch national liberation movement. He hailed from the Gazg area of ​​Manguchar, Sarlat, Balochistan. Operating from the BLA platform, he participated in numerous operations against the enemy across various fronts, including Sanni Shoran, Teepal, Dhadar, Nagahau, Gazg, Kalat, Surab, and Noshki. In a short span of time, he played a pivotal role in thwarting the enemy's nefarious designs through his experience and combat skills.

Asmatullah Kubdani, alias Kandeel, son of Haji Abdullah Kubdani, was a resident of Sheikh Zayed Hospital in Kharan District of Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2025 and served on the Noshki and Kharan fronts under the BLA’s Special Tactical Operations Squad. He was martyred on the Noshki front during Operation Herof 2.
Asmatullah Kubdani, who belonged to the intellectually aware and conscious environment of Kharan and was known as “Kandeel” (The Lamp) among guerrilla circles, was a son of the soil who chose to become a beacon against darkness. After joining the movement in 2025, Asmatullah secured his place in the BLA’s special unit, STOS, due to his extraordinary intelligence and technical skills. His selection was proof that he was not merely an emotional youth but a warrior of deep consciousness, capable of striking the enemy through modern warfare tactics.
Kandeel’s struggle served as a bridge between the fronts of Kharan and Noshki. He was among the few soldiers who remained at the forefront of the most challenging missions. During Operation Herof, when the battlefield of Noshki turned into a nightmare for the enemy, Asmatullah broke through the enemy’s siege by fully utilizing his technical and military prowess. He sacrificed his life for the greater cause of his land’s freedom, proving that when one “Kandeel” (The Lamp) is extinguished, it ignites thousands of new lights.

data.biography:
Ibrahim Baloch was a resident of Anjeera, Surab. He was a student and a member of BSO Azad, Surab Zone. He received his primary education in his hometown. He joined the Baloch Students Organization at a very early age and remained with the organization until his martyrdom.
He served the national cause by giving his full potential to the national struggle. He participated in every activity of the organization. He inspired many youths from his area to join the Baloch liberation movement.
He believed in political struggle and was targeted for his peaceful political expression. He was killed by Pakistan-backed religious extremists from Anjeera, Surab, on February 9, 2011. He was killed because of his national consciousness and love for his people. His body showed severe signs of torture.
He was among the committed members of the organization who continued their struggle during the very difficult times the organization was facing. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad.
His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a very young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.
On 2 February 2026, Pakistani forces killed Yasir Lehri, son of Mohammad Hanif Lehri, in broad daylight in the Mastung area of Balochistan.
A Resident of mand Bollow, was abducted in 2013 by Pakistani Army. Though Later Released He suffered Mental instability Until His death

Usman Maqbool, son of Maqbool Baloch and a resident of Pidarak, district Kech, was forcibly disappeared from his home in Pidarak on 24 August 2025 by Pakistani forces.

Just two days later, on 26 August, his mutilated body was recovered in the remote area of Banuk-e-Chadai, Turbat, Kech. The corpse bore clear signs of extreme torture and multiple gunshot wounds, underscoring the brutality of his killing.

This was not the first time Usman was targeted. In 2019, he was previously disappeared by Pakistani forces, kept incommunicado for two years, and subjected to severe torture. He was released in 2021 only after relentless protests and demands by his family.

Hafiz Hameed Baloch, alias Doda, son of Yaseen and a resident of Gramkan, Panjgur, was affiliated with the Baloch Liberation Army for one and a half years prior to his martyrdom on 31 May 2021. During this period, he served the independence movement with dedication and bravery and participated in several important battles against the enemy. His services and name will forever be remembered in history.
Even after his martyrdom, the enemy army, through its mercenary death squads, attempted to attack those attending Martyr Hameed’s funeral, an act that demonstrated the occupier’s defeat and desperation.

The Baloch Liberation Army’s Majeed Brigade attacked a large Pakistani army convoy at Kunchiti Cross in Dasht, Kech, on 18 September 2025. The convoy included six buses carrying army personnel and an escort squad. It had arrived in Gwadar from Karachi a day earlier and was travelling toward Turbat when the attack occurred around 1 p.m.

The operation began when Altaf alias Chakar drove a VBIED into the main bus, destroying it. After the explosion, Gwahram alias Zagrain and Khalil alias Kulmeer targeted the remaining buses and the security squad. The clash continued for over thirty minutes. According to BLA’s sources, at least 32 army personnel were killed, several wounded, and multiple buses destroyed. Reinforcements and drones arrived later, but rescue operations were delayed.

Altaf (from Alandur Buleda), Gwahram (from Paroom, Panjgur), and Khalil (from Saami, Turbat) had all joined the BLA in 2023. Each had served as an urban guerrilla before moving to the mountains and becoming part of the Majeed Brigade, where they underwent training and took on various responsibilities.

Sajid Baloch, alias Asumi Baloch, son of Chakar Baloch and Hatoon Bibi Baloch, was a resident of Sari Gaddagi in the Keelkaor area of Panjgur, Balochistan. He affiliated with the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in 2013, and at the time of his martyrdom, he was serving as a network commander and held the rank of Lieutenant. He embraced martyrdom along with his two comrades, Ustad Mukhtar Baloch (alias Ustad Noor) and Aziz Baloch (alias Chakar Baloch), on December 7, 2020, in the Dashtuk area of Zamuran, Kech, Balochistan.

Adham Baloch, son of Shah Murad and a resident of Mand, was a brilliant football player and an active member of civil society, sports, and other social activities. He worked tirelessly to engage the youth in productive and healthy activities instead of allowing them to become involved in harmful activities. He was assassinated by a Pakistani military-backed death squad at the football ground in Bullow, Mand, on 27 January 2022.

Sabzal Baloch, son of Badal, from the Khairabad area of Turbat district in Balochistan, belonged to a poor family. On 25 July 2025, he was abducted and forcibly disappeared from the Talar Check Post between Gwadar and Turbat by Pakistani Frontier Corps soldiers. After eight months and seven days, on 1 April 2026, his dead body was dumped in the Pelleri area of Gwadar.

On 3rd April 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that fighters of the BLA launched a series of coordinated attacks against the occupying Pakistani army across occupied Balochistan on 29th March 2026, which continued until 1st April 2026. The fighters carried out 65 operations in Panjgur, Shapuk, Basima, Sibi, Mastung, Quetta, Noshki, Zamuran, Dasht, Surab, Jhal Magsi, Dalbandin, Kharan, Washuk, and Kalat. In these actions, more than 86 personnel of the Pakistani army, death squads, and intelligence agencies were killed, and dozens were injured. These attacks targeted occupying army camps, an airbase, radar systems, communication towers, railway tracks, bridges, and gas pipelines, while major highways were brought under control for several hours.
During clashes with Pakistani forces, five BLA fighters in Panjgur - Zahid alias Nawaz, Saeedullah alias Meraj, Jahanzeb alias Qambar, Aamir alias Khalid, and Saddam alias Shahwaiz - along with Abdust (Abdul Rehman) alias Alman in Zamuran, attained martyrdom.
Jahanzeb, alias Qambar (son of Bahram): A resident of Nokabad, Tasp, he joined in January 2025. His ideological commitment and military dedication dealt severe blows to the enemy in Nagahu and Panjgur.

On 15 April 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said that between April 3 and April 14, 2026, fighters of the BLA killed 29 personnel of the occupying Pakistani army and injured several others in fourteen different operations across various areas of Balochistan, including Surab, Kharan, Washuk, Mastung, Uthal, Jhal Magsi, and Panjgur. During these operations, full control was established over various highways and checkposts of the occupying forces, where blockades were set up, and 13 Levies and police personnel were taken into custody. In these attacks, the occupying army’s supply lines were also targeted and destroyed at two locations. In intense clashes in the Surab area of Balochistan with the occupying army, three BLA fighters - Saleem Jattak, alias Qazi Naveed; Ali Dost, alias Mulla Zakir; and Samiullah Shahwani, alias Hakkal - attained martyrdom while fighting gallantly.
Samiullah Shahwani, alias Hakkal, son of Hameedullah Shahwani, was a resident of the Shekhri area of Kalat District in Balochistan. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in 2025 and served in Kalat and Surab. He was martyred on April 6, 2026, in Surab.
Samiullah Shahwani, known as Hakkal, embodied in action the strength reflected in his name. He was characterized by an intense fighting spirit and a bold, uncompromising approach on the battlefield. Against the enemy, he demonstrated relentless determination, remaining steadfast in every encounter and responding with full force.
He remained consistently active across all fronts of resistance, and in every confrontation, he displayed exceptional bravery, never allowing fear to take hold even for a moment. Through both his conduct and character, he fulfilled the essential qualities expected of a Sarmachar (freedom fighter).
Like his fellow Sarmachars, he embraced martyrdom on the Surab front while defending his homeland, falling in direct combat with the enemy. Until his final breath, he remained loyal to his national and ideological convictions.
Hakkal’s sacrifice stands as a powerful testament to the principle that a revolutionary must remain committed to the struggle and its ideals until the very end. He understood that the collective life of a nation often demands profound sacrifices from individuals. With this awareness, he gave his life for the freedom of his people. His legacy will endure, inscribed with honor in the pages of history.

Majid Baloch, alias Commando Badil, son of Amjad Baloch, was a resident of Sind Bazar, Hoshab District of Balochistan. He became affiliated with the BLA in December 2023, joined the Majeed Brigade in 2024, and was martyred on January 29, 2026, in Turbat District of Balochistan.
Majid Baloch was a product of that Baloch national consciousness which evolved in resistance to decades of oppression, national subjugation, and the Baloch genocide. This young man from Sind Bazar was not a representative of temporary provocation; rather, he was the voice of a generation that views the questions of national identity and national liberation as the fundamental questions of life.
Majid grew up in an environment where the national question was a part of daily existence. For him, freedom was not just a slogan but a historical necessity. He was a close relative of Commander Fidayi Badal (aka Riyasat), who was martyred in Operation Ganjal. On January 29, while en route to participate in Operation Herof in Turbat, he encountered the army and was martyred after fighting to his last bullet. The martyrdom of Fidayee Majid Baloch is not merely the sacrifice of an individual but a symbol of an era in which Baloch youth have decided to shatter the wall of silence.

Majid Hameed, son of Abdul Hameed, was a resident of Basima. He was an active member of BSO Azad Basima Zone. He believed in a peaceful political struggle and was targeted for his political expression. He mobilized many young people to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of their homeland. Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by security forces.
He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he remained committed to the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom. He was an example of bravery and commitment. He joined the organization at an early age and stood by his national ideology until the end.
Although he believed in peaceful political struggle, on 10 February 2015, Pakistani forces raided his house and killed him. He remained a dedicated member of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in golden words in the history of Balochistan.

On 28 June 2026, the spokesperson for the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) issued a statement announcing that five fighters of the organisation - Shoaib Zehri, alias Farooq; Zakariya Zehri, alias Ustad Zoreen Baloch; Kifayatullah Badini, alias Badil Baloch; Captain Hashum Baloch, alias Kambar; and Abdul Rahim, alias Ustad Imran - had embraced martyrdom. The statement said that the blood of the martyrs guarantees Baloch national survival and sovereignty.

Zakria Zehri, alias Ustad Zoreen Baloch, son of Muheem Khan and a resident of Zehri Bulbul, was martyred on April 14, 2026, while fighting valiantly in a clash with the occupying army in the Nagao area of Kalat.
Martyr Zakria Zehri began his struggle in 2025 under the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front. Before formally transferring to the military front, he received basic organizational and ideological training.
After attaining ideological maturity, he formally transferred to the Kalat front for military service.
Through his military and organizational capabilities, he fulfilled several important organizational responsibilities within a very short period. He always remained at the forefront of guerrilla warfare on various fronts in Kalat and Nagao and kept patrol units active. He was an extremely hardworking, loyal, sincere, and fearless fighter who, after joining the organizational ranks, strove to accomplish every military objective and earned a distinguished position among his comrades through his resilience and dedication.
On April 14, the fighters' unit was on patrol as part of an organizational duty when the occupying army had established a checkpoint along their route. Upon seeing the fighters, the occupying army immediately opened fire, whereupon the fighters quickly took up positions and launched a counterattack. During this clash, Sangat Zakria Zehri was martyred while courageously confronting the enemy.
data.fullName: Zakria Zehri, alias Ustad Zoreen Baloch

data.biography:
On 1 November 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson, Gwahram Baloch, issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of eight of the organisation’s fighters: Captain Yahya, alias Ustad Khalid Jan; Aris Baloch, alias Omar Jan; Hafeez Baloch, alias Karwan, son of Dad Mohammad; Javid Baloch, alias Gulab, son of Bori Baloch; Abdul Khaliq, alias Nothak; Sajid Baloch, alias Mehran; Hameed Baloch, alias Buzerg; and Akram Baloch, alias Gwahram.

The statement paid tribute to these brave and ideologically committed members of the organisation, who embraced martyrdom while engaging in clashes with the Pakistani army and its death squads on various fronts across Balochistan.

Martyr Hameed Baloch, alias Buzerg, son of Haji Hussain, resident of Jan Muhammad Bazaar, Dasht, formally joined the national war through the BLF platform in 2012. After joining the organization, for the first year he performed valuable duties on the urban front with great secrecy, courage and skill, and played a vanguard role in several armed operations against the enemy inside Gwadar city.

After the martyrdom of his younger brother, Shaheed Ghani alias Qasum, in the Balgatar battle on 23 December 2013, his secrets were exposed to the enemy, making it impossible for him to remain active on the urban front. In view of circumstances, he formally headed for the mountain front and kept fighting continuously in the difficult terrain of Dhadamb, Siyaji and Dasht. In 2017, as a result of the occupying state's brutal measures of forced eviction and burning of homes in the area, his family was forced to migrate and endured the hardship of exile, but his resolve and morale did not diminish in the least. Shaheed Hameed's whole family has a bright history of sacrifice for the freedom movement. Besides his brother, many other close relatives of his honorable family have offered their blood on this path of freedom. Shaheed Hameed alias Buzerg traveled a very long military and ideological journey from 2012 to 2025, and on 21 October 2025 he embraced martyrdom in a clash with the occupying army in the Kech area, becoming immortal in national history.

On 12 August 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahran Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of nine fighters of the organization: 1. Zubair Baloch, alias Shahvez; 2. Shahnawaz Baloch, alias Rahchar; 3. Rahim Baloch, alias Ajiz Baloch; 4. Musharaf Baloch, alias Basham; 5. Munir Baloch, alias Khalid Baloch; 6. Mohammad Zaman, alias Yahya; 7. Jasim Baloch, alias Babar; 8. Gaji Khan Baloch, alias Aftab; and 9. Abdullah Baloch, alias Usman, and paid tribute to all the martyred comrades who sacrificed their lives for the freedom of the motherland, Balochistan.

Shah Nawaz, alias Rahchar, son of Essa, a resident of Jhao Lanjar, began his struggle through the platform of the BLF in 2025. During his initial year, he served the national movement as an urban guerrilla. During this period, he played an important role in supporting the organization and handling security-related responsibilities in the city. Later, in February 2026, he was transferred to the mountainous warfare front in accordance with an organizational decision, where he became actively involved in the armed struggle. While carrying out organizational responsibilities in the mountains, he was involved in a clash that followed a blockade and encirclement by the occupying forces. He inflicted heavy losses on the enemy forces and fought bravely until his last bullet, ultimately attaining martyrdom.

Rahim Bakhsh Baloch was an ordinary businessman, born and raised in Paroom, Panjgur. He was targeted and killed on 21 June 2015 when he was leaving the mosque after the Ramadan evening (Taraweeh) prayers by a notorious death squad led by Maqbool Shambayzai under the patronage of the Pakistani state.
Being a member of BNP-Mengal, Rahim Bakhsh was a politically conscious person but was never affiliated with any Baloch armed resistance group. He happened to be the father-in-law of Gulzar Baloch, who is the Makuran regional commander of the Baloch Republican Army. He was under threat from different quarters to stay away from Gulzar’s house and family, to which he bravely responded as a father and a Baloch that he would never abandon his daughter and her family. Therefore, the Pakistani state ordered its proxy death squad to kill Rahim Bakhsh, and Gulzar’s family has suffered the consequences of this brutal political murder.

Nisar Ahmed Mengal, son of Ameer Baksh, aged 36, was a leader of the Baloch Watan Movement (BWM) and a resident of Salehabad, Khuzdar. He was the brother of the martyred Joint Secretary of the Baloch National Movement, Mir Rasool Baksh Mengal, whose assassination was carried out with extreme brutality and barbarity by Pakistani forces. Nisar’s assassination was no different.
On 15 October 2010, Nisar Ahmed Mengal was abducted near Do Talwar Chowk in Lasbela, on the night between 6 and 7 November 2010. He was on his way when masked men, believed to be from Pakistani intelligence agencies, suddenly attacked him, forced him into their vehicle at gunpoint, and drove him to an undisclosed location, as reported by multiple eyewitnesses.
His body was recovered on Majid Road in the Khuzdar area after two months of disappearance, on 17 January 2011.

On the night of April 29, 2025 in the Dannuk area of Turbat, the Pakistani occupying forces attempted to surround members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s urban guerrilla network. In response, the fighters launched a strong counter-attack. The clashes, which began at 3:30 AM, continued until sunrise. The fighters held their positions for three hours and continued to inflict heavy blows on the enemy. During this time, they also targeted a convoy of the occupying forces, causing significant casualties. Thirteen enemy personnel were killed and several others were injured during the clashes.
Three Baloch Liberation Army fighters were killed in the fighting: Nabeel, alias Ali; Feroz Sarban, alias Nodbandag and Mohammad Umar Zaka, alias Guru.
Feroz Sarban, alias Nodbandag, son of Master Allah Bakhsh, belonged to Aapsar Daki Bazaar in Turbat. He was also the brother-in-law of Martyr Ilyas Nazar. He joined the armed struggle in 2022 and remained active as an urban guerrilla for more than a year, moving to the mountains in 2023. A lover of singing and poetry, Feroz studied in Lahore and was a BS Political Science student at the University of Turbat.
Feroz Nodbandag transformed his political awareness into combat skill. He was fearless not only on the battlefield but also a symbol of intellectual resistance. His presence brought energy to both the urban and mountainous fronts of the struggle.

Martyr Mir Abdul Nabi Badozai Bangulzai played a steadfast and courageous role on the front of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in the Baloch national liberation struggle for two decades. He joined the organization in 2002 and remained firmly committed to the movement and the organization with unwavering resolve, courage, and bravery until the day of his martyrdom on 27 May 2021.
He was a very close associate of Martyr General Aslam Baloch, Martyr Agha Mahmood Khan, Martyr Mir Abdul Ghaffar Langove and the renowned martyr Ameer Bakhsh Lango.
In 2012, in recognition of his bravery, intelligence, and steadfast character, the Baloch Liberation Army entrusted Martyr Mir Abdul Nabi Badozai Bangulzai with the responsibilities of an organizational commander. As a commander, he not only led his fellow Sarmachars with exceptional valor in significant battles against the enemy, inflicting decisive defeats upon them, but also played an important role in strengthening and expanding the BLA due to his wise understanding of organizational and tribal affairs.
Martyr Mir Abdul Nabi Badozai Bangulzai was not merely an asset to the Baloch Liberation Army; he was always prepared to support all Baloch pro-freedom organizations. His bravery, hospitality, and generosity were unparalleled.
The lifelong struggle of an elder and seasoned comrade like Mir Abdul Nabi Bangulzai, who stood shoulder to shoulder with Baloch youth and his martyrdom prove that in the Baloch national liberation movement, elders and youth participate as equals. In the ongoing movement, alongside the passion and enthusiasm of the youth, the wisdom and perseverance of elders like Martyr Mir Bangulzai continued to guide and shape this spirit.
data.fullName: Mir Abdul Nabi Badozai Bangulzai, alias Chunka Mir

data.biography: Nabi Dad, son of Lewari Baloch, was a resident of Balgatar, Kech. He was abducted along with seven of his close relatives from different areas on August 22, 2023. After four months, on November 20, 2023, he was killed, along with two relatives, Adil and Shah Jan, sons of Assa Baloch, by a Pakistan military-backed death squad in Balgatar, Kech.

On 15 October 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Republican Guards (BRG) spokesperson Dostain Baloch stated On 15 october 2026, from 5:00 AM to 7:00 AM, the freedom fighters of the Baloch Republican Guards established Roadblockde on the main highway in the Mithri area of Balochistan’s Sibi district and thoroughly searched vehicles. During this time, the occupying Pakistani forces attempted to advance. The freedom fighters responded promptly by attacking the forces. During an intense clash that continued for a considerable period, six personnel of the occupying enemy forces were killed on the spot, while several others were wounded. Meanwhile, the freedom fighters attacked a police post located in the area. The police personnel, overcome by fear, fled the scene. The fighters took control of the post, seized all equipment and motorcycles, and set the post on fire.

While carrying out this determined mission, one of the organization’s brave freedom fighter, Asghar Ali Jatoi, son of Abdul Hameed, a resident of Kachhi, embraced martyrdom while confronting the enemy. His great devotion and everlasting sacrifice will be written in golden letters in the history of Balochistan’s struggle for independence. Asghar Jan Jatoi joined the BRG in 2025. He was an exceptionally brave fighter who played his role effectively in the Baloch national liberation struggle, confronting the occupying enemy in various areas of Balochistan, including Kachhi, Dhadar, Sunni, Bolan, and Sibi, and inflicting defeats on the enemy.

Faraz Baloch was a resident of Gareeb Shah, Lyari, Karachi. He was an F.Sc. student at Degree College Lyari and a member of BSO Azad Karachi Zone. He received his early education in Lyari. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising his right to peaceful political expression. He became a victim of target killing by Pakistan’s intelligence agencies.
He stood firmly with the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom. He was an example of bravery and commitment. He had a keen interest in reading revolutionary literature about oppressed nations. He joined the organization at an early age and remained committed to his national ideology until the end.
He was targeted on 3rd January 2011 in Gulshan-e-Iqbal, Karachi. His body bore severe signs of torture. He was among the most dedicated members of the organization and continued his struggle even during difficult times. He inspired many young people to join the caravan of BSO Azad.
His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

On 12 August 2026, several Baloch people, including women and children, were killed and several others were injured as a result of an aerial bombardment of a civilian population by the Pakistan Air Force, reportedly using American-made F-16 fighter aircraft, in the Gidar Gindan area of Surab District, Balochistan. Following the airstrike, the injured and deceased were transported by police and local residents to DHQ Hospital in Surab, where the injured received medical treatment.

The families of the deceased and local residents subsequently began a protest by placing the bodies at Surab Main Chowk on the Quetta–Karachi National Highway (N-25). As a result, traffic on the highway was disrupted, with long queues of vehicles forming on both sides. Videos and photographs of the protest subsequently circulated widely on social media under the hashtag #SurabMassacre.

Those killed in the airstrike were identified as Shabir Ahmad Sumalani, son of Khudadad Sumalani, a resident of Marap, Surab; Noor Jan Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, a resident of Gindan; Karim Dad Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, a resident of Gandan; Raj Babu, wife of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani; Safia, wife of Noor Jan Mirwani; and Jalal Mirwani, son of Noor Jan Mirwani.

Those injured were identified as Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, son of Jan Muhammad Mirwani; Abdul Karim Mirwani, son of Jan Muhammad Mirwani; Mehrullah Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani; Nadeem Mirwani, son of Abdul Salam Mirwani; Shoaib Mirwani, son of Abdul Karim Mirwani; Sarah, wife of Baseer Ahmed Mirwani; Sabira, wife of Tufail Ahmed Mirwani; Zamra, daughter of Abdul Aziz Mirwani; Hajira, wife of Abdul Fattah Mirwani; Asim, son of Baseer, aged 1; Rahabia, daughter of Abdul Karim, aged 3; Sadia, daughter of Abdul Salam, aged 5; Fatima, daughter of Abdul Karim, aged 7; Zia-ur-Rehman, son of Abdul Karim, aged 2; Amir, son of Abdul Karim, aged 1; and Hasina, daughter of Muhammad Aslam, aged 4.

Following a detailed technical and scientific analysis of remnants of rocket components recovered from debris at the site of the aerial bombardment, important evidence reportedly emerged indicating that the recovered fragments belonged to an air-launched missile fired from an F-16 fighter aircraft.

Photographs of the recovered debris and the subsequent technical analysis reportedly indicated that the fragment was part of an AIM-120 Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile (AMRAAM), an American-made air-to-air missile.

Key technical evidence and serial numbers

According to the information and serial numbers reportedly engraved on the surface of the debris, the following details were recorded:

Assembly Number: ASSY 872128-1

Serial Number: 09-987138

Date of Manufacture: 09/09 (September 2009)

According to open-source intelligence (OSINT) records, the part number “872128-1” reportedly corresponds to the control section and rocket motor assembly of an AMRAAM missile manufactured by the American defense company Raytheon. Based on this evidence and the reported matching serial numbers, it is claimed that the debris was not part of an aircraft’s internal structure but instead consisted of remnants from an operational missile fired from an F-16 aircraft.

Yousuf Bugti, son of Shah Nawaz Bugti and a resident of Siah Aaf, Dera Bugti, was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani security forces on October 18, 2024, from Dera Bugti city. After nearly eight months of detention, he was extrajudicially killed in custody. On June 12, 2025, his mutilated body bearing visible signs of severe torture was found in Piara Colony, Sui, District Dera Bugti.
data.martyrdomPlace: Piara Colony, Sui, Dera Bugti, Balochistan

data.biography: Omar Jan Baloch, was a resident of the Tump, Kech area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 24 May 2013 in Balochistan.

Allah Dad Baloch, alias Sawad, son of Allah Bakhsh Baloch, was a resident of Paroom, Dazz, Panjgur. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Paroom front. He was martyred on 19 August 2026 in Pullabad, Paroom, Panjgur, Balochistan.
Allah Dad Baloch, alias Sawad, decided to join the great collective cause of national liberation this year, enlisted in the ranks of the Baloch Liberation Army, and was deployed to the Paroom front. After completing basic organizational courses, he began participating in combat operations and soon proved himself to be a capable and courageous fighter. Recognizing his abilities and professional military interest, he was sent on patrol, where he faithfully carried out his organizational duties until the end and worked to establish organizational dominance in the areas.
As a guerrilla in the practical struggle for national liberation and state formation, he joined his comrades on numerous occasions in deadly attacks against the occupying enemy and made it clear that no place or position would remain safe for the enemy in Balochistan. Under policies to maintain organizational strength and control over trade routes, he took full part in operations in his respective areas and, together with his comrades, continuously disrupted the enemy’s trade. His sacrifices for the great cause of national liberation will be inscribed in the pages of history in the finest words, and the Baloch nation will always remember him as a son of freedom.

On 30 September 2024, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that they pay tribute to their six comrades - Shafo Sumalani alias Tadain, Samad Khan Chalgari Marri alias Dostain, Mohammad Gul Marri alias Waheed Baloch, Ghulam Qadir Marri alias Anjeer Baloch, Obaid Baloch alias Fida, and Taj Mohammad Chalgari Marri alias Babul - who were martyred in a bombing by jet fighters of the Pakistani Air Force in Harnai, Balochistan. On 12 September, at 4 AM, jet fighters of the Pakistani Air Force dropped several heavy and deadly bombs on BLA fighters, with the support of drone surveillance, in the Ali Khan Thal area of Harnai, Balochistan. As a result of the bombing, six fighters were martyred. After the attack, the morally bankrupt enemy desecrated the bodies of the martyred fighters and took their body parts using gunship helicopters.

Mohammad Gul Marri alias Waheed Baloch hailed from Chamalang Berg and was a cousin of Shaheed Fidayi Baaz Khan Marri, alias Darwesh, Shaheed Chakar Bolani, and Shaheed Gul Hamd Marri. His family has been in exile for the past twenty years due to the tyranny of the enemy state. He had been serving on the front lines for the last three years and was a fearless and brave fighter with a deep sense of national pride.
data.fullName: Mohammad Gul Marri, alias Waheed Baloch

data.biography:
Sudais Baloch, son of Mohammad Ashraf, was a 20 year old student and resident of Madrisa Road, Langove Mohalla, Killi Ismail, Quetta. He was forcibly disappeared from his home at 2:00 AM on 20 May 2026.

His case was submitted to the Missing Persons Committee, which operates under the supervision of the Home Department. At the committee’s first hearing, held at the DG office on 16 October 2026, his family was given no information about his whereabouts. Then, at the second hearing on 21 October 2026, the Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) informed the committee that Sudais had been killed in an encounter in Aghbarg, Qilla Abdullah, on 20 August 2026 and labelled him a terrorist.

Sudais Baloch was killed exactly three months after he was taken from his home, and his family was kept in the dark for another two months while his case remained before a government committee.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Jafar Mengal, alias Comrade Sameer, son of Mohammad Bakhsh Mengal, was a resident of Sariab, Quetta. He held an MA in Political Science. He joined the BLA in March 2022 and became part of the Majeed Brigade in March 2024, where he was promoted to the rank of Regional Commander. He served in the Sarawan and Rakhshan regions, as well as on the Noshki, Shoor Parod, and Kharan fronts. He was martyred on 5 February 2026 during Operation Heirof Phase 2 on the Noshki front.
Jafar Mengal belonged to Sariab, a suburban area of Quetta - a place sustained not only by the prayers of mothers but also by the questions of its youth. Commander Jafar was among those young men who did not question only themselves but also interrogated politics, society, and history. He did not confine himself to seeking answers in books alone but chose a practical path through which those answers could be lived and tested.
Despite attaining higher education in political science, Jafar did not pursue the career paths commonly chosen by educated middle-class youth. He came to view struggle as a political act, a moral responsibility, and an intellectual stance. Within only two years of joining the BLA, he earned command responsibilities in some of the most critical operational zones of the Majeed Brigade. Among his comrades, his leadership was recognized for its trustworthiness, prudence, and unwavering discipline.
During Operation Heirof Phase 2, Jafar Mengal fought continuously for five days against some of the most sensitive targets in Noshki, including the ISI office, the FC headquarters, and the bus terminal headquarters. He not only held his own position but repeatedly moved between fronts to assist fellow fighters, strengthen their positions, and, after five days of combat and the successful completion of the operation, stayed behind to provide cover so that his comrades could withdraw safely. This conduct was not merely military judgment but a measure of moral courage, found only in those who regard struggle not as personal pride but as a collective duty.
Jafar was martyred at a moment when he had already ensured the safe withdrawal of his comrades, placing himself in the line of enemy fire so that others might be spared. His martyrdom was not only that of a commander but also of a brother, a teacher, and a quiet soldie

On 8 August 2016, terrorists attacked the Government Hospital in Quetta, Balochistan, in a suicide bombing and shooting. More than 70 people were killed, mainly lawyers, and more than 130 others were injured.
The majority of those killed were lawyers who had gathered at the hospital after the body of Advocate Bilal Anwar Kasi, president of the Balochistan Bar Association, was brought there. Kasi had been shot dead by a gunman near Mengal Chowk on Manno Jan Road in Quetta while he was leaving his home for his office.
Responsibility for the attack was claimed by various Islamist groups, including Jamaat-ul-Ahrar and the Islamic State Khorasan Province. However, nationalist groups have alleged that these extremist organisations are backed by the Pakistani state and its military to counter the nationalist movement in the region and exploit its natural resources.
Estimates of the death toll ranged between 70 people, while more than 120 were injured. Of those killed, 54 were lawyers. Among them, 15 were Baloch by ethnicity, while the majority were Pashtuns by ethnicity.

The Baloch advocates or lawyers who were killed are identified as follows:

15 Sabir Ali, son of Abdul Rasheed.

On 9 October 2025, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) received complaints from local residents in Gorki, Mangochar, in the Kalat District of Balochistan, stating that Shakir, the head of a local death squad, was collecting extortion money and taxes from vehicles in the area and harassing people without cause. Acting on these complaints, BLA fighters went to meet Shakir to discuss the matter. Upon their arrival, they detained two of Shakir’s men and asked that Shakir be called. At that point, women from Shakir’s house came out and placed the Qur’an before the fighters, pleading for the release of the detained men. The BLA members reassured them that they had come only to speak with Shakir and warn him not to trouble the local people.
When Shakir arrived, the fighters spoke with him, explaining that they had received complaints about his harassment of locals and his collection of illegal taxes from vehicles, and they urged him to stop such actions. After hearing this, Shakir claimed he would not repeat such behavior. However, as soon as the fighters departed, Shakir and his men opened fire on them.
As a result of the firing, four BLA comrades - Gul Khan alias Yaseen, Inayatullah alias Hafiz, Izzatullah alias Saeed, and Shah Murad alias Salam - were martyred. All four had joined the organization in 2023 and courageously fulfilled their national duties until the day of their martyrdom.

Zareef Baloch, son of Faqeer Baloch and a resident of Siahkal in the Malar area of Awaran District, was forcibly disappeared on September 29, 2025, when Pakistani genocidal forces reportedly raided his home and took him into custody.
After remaining missing for more than three months, his bullet-riddled body was recovered alongside the body of Ayaz Ahmad on January 6, 2026, from the Nondara area of Awaran District. The discovery of his body confirms fears that Zareef Baloch was subjected to an extrajudicial killing while in illegal detention.

On 16 October 2024, Ayaz Baloch, son of Dost Muhammad, was forcibly disappeared from his home by Pakistani security forces along with his cousin Imdad Baloch. Since their abduction, the family repeatedly sought information regarding their whereabouts, but authorities failed to provide any response.
On 6 January 2026, the bullet-riddled body of Ayaz Baloch was recovered from the Nondara area of Awaran District, confirming fears that he had been subjected to an extrajudicial killing while in custody. His cousin Imdad Baloch remains missing to date.

Sikander Baloch, son of Asif Baloch, was a resident of Khuzdar. He received his early education in his hometown, Khuzdar, and was a BS (Honors) Civil Engineering student at the Balochistan University of Engineering and Technology, Khuzdar. He was an active and senior member of the BSO Azad Khuzdar Zone. He had an interest in studying revolutionary literature from around the world. He actively participated in every activity of the organization and was involved in organizing political activities at the university.
Because of his political struggle, he was targeted by the colonizers.
He was a victim of a target killing carried out on 2nd March 2010 during a Cultural Day event at the Balochistan University of Engineering and Technology, Khuzdar. A Pakistan intelligence agency-backed armed group attacked the Cultural Day event on the university campus organized by the Baloch Students Organization Azad to celebrate National Culture Day. Following the attack, Sikander along with Junaid was martyred, while more than 24 activists of BSO Azad and students were injured.
His sacrifices for preserving Baloch culture and for the Cultural Day will always be remembered in the chapters of Baloch history, as long as Baloch culture exists in the world.

In 1838, the British sent a force led by Alexander Burnes to reinstate Shah Shuja Durrani as the king of Afghanistan by deposing Amir Dost Mohammad Khan. To reach Afghanistan, they needed passage through Balochistan, particularly the Bolan Pass. However, Khan Mehrab Khan refused to allow the British to use his land to attack a neighboring country. The British sent Lieutenant Leach to negotiate with the Baloch government, but the Khan stood firm. When British forces reached Shaal via Bolan, some patriotic Baloch, without the Khan’s knowledge, attacked British troops out of nationalist sentiment and a desire to protect their homeland.
After toppling Amir Dost Mohammad Khan, the British Governor General of India, Lord Auckland, ordered an attack on Balochistan. In 1839, around 7,000 British troops marched from Shaal to attack the Baloch Meeri (capital). Anticipating an invasion, Khan Mehrab Khan declared war and sent messages to tribal leaders, but many saw the British as allies rather than invaders and chose to collaborate with them rather than defend their land. When Khan Mehrab Khan gathered his resistance fighters, the number of loyal warriors had dwindled to only 700 due to the short sightedness of many tribal chiefs. Nevertheless, Mehrab Khan was determined to fight. At his court, a respected figure, Akhund Muhammad Siddiq, advised him that he was not in a position to wage war at that time. He suggested that the Khan should leave Kalat with his companions, regroup and strengthen his forces, and then launch an attack against the British when the time was right, on 13 November 1839, the British forces launched an attack on Kalat, and a fierce battle ensued. During the fighting, Khan Mehrab Khan Baloch was martyred by a British bullet.

Among those martyred alongside him were:

Diwan Bacha Mal, Minister of Finance

Diwan Khem Chand

Diwan Asardas Mukhi, from the Hindu Panchayat of Kalat

Abdul Karim Raisani, brother of Sardar Asad Khan Raisani

Sardar Wali Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (maternal uncle of Martyr Amir Mehrab Khan)

Martyr Asif Baloch Alias Junaid Baloch, son of Hebatan Baloch and was a resident of Darchko, Dasht area of Kech, Balochistan. He became part of Baloch liberation movement in 2014 and on Dec 1, 2022, he joined Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF).
He embraced martyrdom in a drone attack of Pakistan’s military along with his seven comrades, Kareem Baloch, Mullah Bakhsh, Hazza Baloch,  Shezad Baloch, Jalal Baloch, Talib Baloch, and Manzoor Baloch on Feb 23, 2023 in Mazanband area of Kech, Balochistan.

On 16 July 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that the BLA eliminated more than forty personnel of the Pakistani Army and injured several others in forty-eight operations across Balochistan during the previous fifteen days. As part of the economic blockade, vehicles violating the blockade on major highways were targeted and destroyed. Furthermore, four key bridges were destroyed using planted explosive devices. During various clashes with the occupying forces, five BLA fighters - Rahimullah Mohammad Hassni, alias Zafar, son of Lumma Raaj Bibi; Khair Mohammad Khairo, alias Hammal, son of Shahbaz; Kaka Baloch, alias Kaka Rasheed, son of Shahbaz; Masood Baloch, alias Sami, son of Ghulam Jan; and Shah Nazar Baloch, alias Badal, son of Khuda Nazar - embraced martyrdom.

Shah Nazar Baloch, alias Badal, son of Khuda Nazar, was a resident of the Paroom area of Panjgur. He joined the Urban Front in 2023 and later served on the Shorparod and Panjgur mountain fronts. He was martyred on 13 July 2026 in the Chedagi area of Panjgur.
Shah Nazar, alias Badal, had been a member of the BLA for the past three years. During the early days of his association with the organization, he served as an urban guerrilla and played an important role in providing the organization with access to valuable intelligence. In 2023, in accordance with the organization's directives, he moved to the mountain front, where he began fulfilling his national responsibilities on the Shorparod front. During his deployment there, he dealt devastating blows to the enemy on several important occasions and was known among his fellow fighters for his perseverance and tireless dedication. He was counted among those hardworking fighters who knew neither fatigue, physical weakness, nor negligence. It was this resilience and unwavering resolve that distinguished him from others.
Alongside his hard work and enduring spirit, he was a highly active fighter on the battlefield. During the historic Operation Dara-e-Bolan I, he took part in several important engagements against the enemy, while in Operation Herof I he also carried out his assigned responsibilities with distinction. Beyond these historic operations, he participated in numerous major and minor military operations, targeting the enemy and inflicting significant losses upon them. Following his service on the Shorparod front, he was deployed to the Panjgur front, where he played a significant role in military operations in Panjgur city and its surrounding areas. Whatever responsibilities were entrusted to him by the organization, he was counted among those fighters who possessed the ability to carry them out in the best possible manner. This revolutionary spirit remained a defining feature of his service and activities until the very end.
Shah Nazar struggled continuously for three years for the restoration of the national state and ultimately, by shedding his blood, immortalized himself in Baloch national history. By sacrificing himself for the freedom of his homeland, he conveyed a message through his sacrifice to hundreds of other young people, urging them to join this great struggle for national liberation and fulfill their national responsibilities. His sacrifices will remain an enduring part of Baloch national history.

On 30 September 2024, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that they pay tribute to their six comrades - Shafo Sumalani alias Tadain, Samad Khan Chalgari Marri alias Dostain, Mohammad Gul Marri alias Waheed Baloch, Ghulam Qadir Marri alias Anjeer Baloch, Obaid Baloch alias Fida, and Taj Mohammad Chalgari Marri alias Babul - who were martyred in a bombing by jet fighters of the Pakistani Air Force in Harnai, Balochistan. On 12 September, at 4 AM, jet fighters of the Pakistani Air Force dropped several heavy and deadly bombs on BLA fighters, with the support of drone surveillance, in the Ali Khan Thal area of Harnai, Balochistan. As a result of the bombing, six fighters were martyred. After the attack, the morally bankrupt enemy desecrated the bodies of the martyred fighters and took their body parts using gunship helicopters.

Obaid Baloch, alias Fida, son of Mohammad Ameen hailed from Gwadar Panwan and joined the Bolan front in March of this year. In a very short time, he proved himself to be an outstanding fighter through his natural talents, passion, and tireless hard work.

On February 23, 2025, in the Gulo Shamchudi area of ​​Barkhan the occupying Pakistani army advanced into the area with motorcycles, convoys of vehicles and on personnel for the purpose of aggression where the freedom fighters who had already laid ambushes, launched attacks on the occupying army from different directions. In these attacks five personnel of the occupying Pakistani army were eliminated on the spot while the enemy army retreated after suffering further casualties and property losses.  
Freedom fighters of BRAS as planned, brought one of their temporary camps into the enemy’s sight. On the second day of the aggression the occupying army was trapped and reached the said location where the fighters of BRAS launched intense attacks from two different directions. In these attacks eight more enemy personnel were eliminated and at least eight were injured. The distraught personnel of the occupying Pakistani army fled abandoning their motorcycles.  
In the combat with the occupying Pakistani army Ghulam Rasool Marri alias Munshi Eidu of Baloch Raji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS) was martyred. His mortal remains were laid to rest with full military honors by the BRAS freedom fighters.  
Ghulam Rasool alias Munshi Eidu, son of Faiz Muhammad Marri, a fighter of the Baloch Liberation Army an ally of BRAS, originally belonged to Chamalang. He was the brother of Martyr Baz Khan Marri alias Darwesh Baloch, the first Fidayee of the BLA Majeed Brigade. Martyr Ghulam Rasool Marri had been associated with the Baloch national liberation struggle for the past fifteen years. He performed his duties in Bolan, Kohlu, Kahan and other fronts.  
Ghulam Rasool Marri alias Munshi Eidu, due to his combat capabilities, fought against national slavery as a member of the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS) a special unit of the Baloch Liberation Army. He defeated the enemy in many important operations.

data.martyrdomPlace: Sorap Dam, Buleda, Turbat district, Balochistan
data.biography:
Quddous Baloch, son of Umaid Baloch and a resident of Gardank, Buleda, district Kech, was a driver involved in cross-border trade. He was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces on September 30, 2025, from Minaz, Buleda.

After one day of enforced disappearance, his bullet-riddled body was recovered from the Sorap Dam area of Buleda on October 1, 2025.

On 21 February 1987, in the coastal town of Jiwani, Balochistan, Pakistani forces opened indiscriminate fire on a peaceful protest rally organized by local Baloch residents over water shortages and the demand for clean drinking water. A two year old girl, Yasmeen Baloch, along with Azgul Baloch and Ghulam Nabi Baloch, were killed, and several other demonstrators were injured.

On 26 April 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said that fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army carried out twenty-seven operations across Balochistan between 15 April and 25 April. These operations included IED blasts, drone strikes, and ambushes targeting the Pakistani military. In these attacks, 42 personnel of the forces were killed and numerous others were injured, while one soldier was taken into custody alive. BLA fighters seized control of multiple security posts and confiscated weapons. During clashes at various locations, Sangat Shah Karam Mullazai (alias Sachan), Asim Shahwani (alias Rodain), and Gwahram Baloch (alias Qambar) embraced martyrdom.
Gwahram Baloch, alias Qambar, son of Dur Mohammad Baloch, was a resident of the Zamuran area of Turbat district, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2024 and served on the Kulbar Front with the rank of Patrol Commander. His educational qualification was a Bachelor’s degree in Economics from QAU, Islamabad. He was martyred on 26 February 2026 in Buleda, Turbat district, Balochistan.
Gwahram Baloch, alias Qambar, was a courageous fighter deeply influenced by the revolutionary thought of Shaheed Qambar Chakar. He had reached a level of political and intellectual awareness at which he understood that, under the presence of an occupying state and its control over the land, the progress and prosperity of the Baloch nation can never be achieved. He also recognized that no occupying military force relinquishes control through appeals, historical arguments, or humanitarian principles; rather, the truth of history lies in resisting the occupier and acquiring the strength to determine one's own destiny. It was this historical and intellectual understanding that led Gwahram, along with several members of his family, to sacrifice their lives in defense of their homeland.
Like many educated youths, Gwahram graduated from institutions established by the occupier, yet he chose to align his intellectual awareness and sense of national responsibility with action. After completing his academic career, instead of contributing to the structures of the occupying state, he joined the BLA in 2024 to strengthen the foundations of a national future. Until his martyrdom, he remained an active and responsible Sarmachar of the organization, committed to the cause as a revolutionary cadre.
On the military front, Gwahram, alias Qambar, was known for his bravery. He was always prepared for direct confrontation with the enemy and embraced martyrdom while fighting on the front lines against hostile forces. Owing to his abilities and competence, he was entrusted with the responsibility of patrol command within a short time. Within the organization, he was recognized as a committed and responsible fighter who fulfilled his duties with dedication. His martyrdom serves as a clear message to educated youth: to use their skills not to strengthen the structures of occupation, but to reinforce national resistance and the struggle for freedom, as Gwahram did, thereby earning an enduring place in history.

Muhammad Waqas, son of Nawab Khan, was a Levies constable, a Hafiz-ul-Quran, and a resident of Kirtha, Mach, Bolan. He was abducted and forcibly disappeared, along with his brother, Mitha Khan, by personnel of the Pakistani forces, including the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) and Frontier Corps (FC), from the Mach area of Bolan ten days before Eid-ul-Azha. His family remained without answers until his mutilated body was found on 24 August 2026.

On 26 October 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that the organization’s freedom fighters had carried out 15 organized, high-intensity operations against the occupying Pakistani army and its subordinate apparatus across various fronts in Balochistan over a seven-day period, from 20 to 26 October 2026. During these coordinated attacks, more than 27 personnel of the occupying army were reportedly killed on the spot, while numerous others were severely injured. Meanwhile, in a successful intelligence-based operation conducted by the BLA’s specialized intelligence wing, 'ZIRAB,' the vehicle of a high-ranking army officer, a lieutenant colonel, was destroyed in a remote-controlled explosion in the coastal town of Pasni. Throughout these seven days of intense operations, BLA fighter Hammal Baloch, alias Comrade Salim Baloch, fought courageously and attained the highest status of martyrdom during face-to-face clashes with the occupying forces.

On 15 October 2026, intense clashes broke out between the occupying Pakistani army and Sarmachars in Kohad, Tump, when enemy forces attempted to advance into the area. Although the enemy forces reportedly suffered heavy casualties during the clashes, BLA Sarmachar Hammal Baloch, alias Comrade Salim Baloch, fought bravely and attained the highest status of martyrdom.

Hammal Baloch, alias Comrade Salim Baloch, son of Naik Bakht, was resident of Kisar, Dannuk area of Turbat, his Education qualification was LLB (8th Semester), he joined the BLA on 2023  and served in Tump, Kulbar, Turbat City, Coastal Areas fronts, and promoted to Camp Command rank, Kulbar, martyrdom on 15 Oct 2026 in Kohad area of Tump, Balochistan.

Hammal Baloch, alias Comrade Salim, was among the educated, conscious, and politically mature sangat of the Baloch Liberation Army who had been associated with the struggle for Baloch national liberation since his student days. He believed in the philosophy of violence and force as a means of achieving national liberation and ending the enemy’s occupation. During his student years, he was associated with the politics of the Baloch Students Organization Azad (BSO-Azad) and was active in encouraging young people to join the struggle for national liberation and in fostering national awareness among them. Later, after his involvement in student politics, he joined the Baloch Liberation Army and also participated in urban guerrilla operations. He was active as a guerrilla fighter in carrying out operations against the enemy in the city of Turbat. He held a firm ideological, political, intellectual, and knowledge-based position against the enemy’s occupation and chose armed struggle as a result of his awareness of the same intellectual and historical realities.

On the instructions of the organizational command, Martyr Hammal Baloch ended his urban activities in 2023 and became actively involved on the front lines. Martyr Hammal was an active fighter and was counted among the comrades who remained active on the battlefield. He demonstrated his combat abilities through his extensive participation in military operations across various fronts in Makuran, Coastal Areas, Turbat city, Hoshab, and Kulbar. In 2025, he also sustained serious injuries in an accident, and one of his hands remained severely injured for a considerable period. However, physical difficulties never became an obstacle in the face of Hammal Baloch’s high morale, and these qualities set him apart. In recognition of his combat abilities, political maturity, and administrative skills, he was appointed camp commander on the Kulbar front, a role he continued to fulfil until his final days. On October 15, Hammal Baloch demonstrated courage during an enemy attack, ensured the safety of his fellow Sangats, and attained martyrdom in a direct confrontation with the enemy. hammal Baloch will be remembered as a brave hero in Baloch national history.
