data.biography:
Swearing upon the Qur’an as a solemn guarantee, the state of Pakistan sent a jirga to negotiate with Nawab Noroz Khan. Trusting the sanctity of the Qur’an as a binding assurance, Nawab Noroz Khan descended from the mountains along with his son, Battay Khan, and his companions. However, rather than engaging in meaningful negotiations or addressing their legitimate demands, the state - consistent with its pattern of duplicity - arrested them.
Nawab Noroz Khan was sentenced to life imprisonment, while his son and several of his companions were condemned to death and executed in the prisons of Sukkur and Hyderabad in Sindh.
When the armed fighters came down from the mountains, they kissed the Qur’an and declared, 'We offer ourselves in its name, but we will not surrender our weapons.' The official delegation repeatedly invoked the Qur’an to reassure them that the government would honor its commitments, insisting that no greater guarantee could exist than the Holy Book itself. Yet once they had descended, those promises were broken, and they were taken into custody. They were confined in harsh prison cells dating back to the British colonial period.
Four companions of Nawab Noroz Khan - Bhawal Khan, Masti Khan, Jamal Khan, and Wali Mohammad - were hanged in Hyderabad Jail, Sindh on 15 July 1960. Their bodies were received by Mir Rasool Bakhsh, the paternal uncle of Mir Mohammad Ali Talpur. After the funeral rites were performed, the martyrs were transported to their ancestral homeland for burial.
Nawab Noroz Khan’s son, Mir Battay Khan, along with Sabzal Khan and Ghulam Rasool, was executed in Sukkur Jail, Sindh on 15 July 1960.
Nawab Nauroz Khan himself passed away on 25 December 1965 at Civil Hospital Hyderabad, Sindh, while in custody. His body was received by Mir Rafique Ahmed. Following the funeral rites, Mir Rasool Bakhsh arranged for his body to be transported to his ancestral place.
His youngest son, Jalal Khan, remained imprisoned until 1970. He was spared execution because he was a minor at the time of his arrest.
Nawab Noroz Khan and the seven martyrs were laid to rest in the Chashma area of Kalat District, a few kilometres from Kalat Bazaar in Balochistan.
Jamal Khan Zehri was born in the Hasui Mola area of Khuzdar District, two years before the socialist revolution. He was a landlord by profession, married, and had two sons.
He was 45 years old when he was hanged in Hyderabad Jail.

On 19 April 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson, Gwahram Baloch, announced the martyrdom of six fighters of the organization, paid tribute to them, and stated that the organization’s fighters were martyred in the national war of liberation. The martyrs include Ikram Baloch (alias Hameed), Shaibaz Shohaz (alias Kiyya), Masood Baloch (alias Bharag), Salman Waheeda (alias Chirag), Izzat Baloch (alias Jummi), and Hamza Baloch (alias Waheed).
The spokesperson further stated that the martyred fighters fulfilled their oath and national duty of defending the nation and homeland to the last drop of their blood, sacrificing their lives and achieving immortality. The martyrs proved through their great sacrifices that Baloch sarmachars do not hesitate to make any sacrifice in the defense of the nation and homeland.
Ikram Baloch alias Hameed, son of Rahim Bakhsh, a resident of Omari Kahn, Saami, Turbat district, Balochistan, joined the BLF in 2017. He rendered national services with extraordinary courage and dedication on the fronts of Shapuk, Saami, Heronk, Hoshab, Balgatar, Buleda, Paroom, and Zamuran. He was among the vanguard fighters in the two battles to capture the enemy camp at Balgatar.
He was a highly brave, hardworking, and conscientious fighter with a deep sense of responsibility, who had dedicated himself entirely to the freedom and a better future for the Baloch nation. Martyr Ikram Baloch alias Hameed was martyred on April 16, 2026, in an enemy aerial strike in the Dashtuk area of Zamuran, Turbat district, Balochistan.

Aziz Ahmad Sumalani, alias Jahanzaib, son of Shah Mohammad Sumalani, was a resident of the Qadir Abad area of Noshki. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Noshki and Basima fronts. He was martyred on 7 September 2026 in the Basima area of Surab, Balochistan.
2026 having decided to join the great cause and movement for Baloch national liberation, Martyr Aziz Ahmad Sumalani chose the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army and joined the armed resistance. After joining, he was transferred to a training camp for military training, where he completed his basic military courses with great hard work and effort. Afterwards, he began taking part in important military operations against the enemy in the field. First, he served on the Nushki front and, along with his sangats, actively participated in the ongoing economic blockade activities in the area. He also took part in patrols and public awareness activities in the area alongside his comrades.
Aziz Ahmad Sumalani carried out his responsibilities in Noshki with great sincerity and honesty, and later began fulfilling his military responsibilities in Basima. His performance in the Basima war zone was excellent, and together with his fellow fighters, he sincerely and diligently fulfilled his individual role in establishing organizational influence in the area. He was among those comrades who always remained at the forefront of movements and activities against the enemy. On September 7, in a battle with occupying enemy personnel, he attained martyrdom on the great path of national liberation and became immortal in history.

data.organization: Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) / ZIRAB / Fateh Squad
data.biography:
At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Adnan Faqeer, alias Talar, son of Faqeer Mohammad, was a resident of Alndoor, Buleda, in the Turbat district of Balochistan. He held a BS degree in English Literature and joined the BLA in August 2024. He served in the Fateh Squad and in the ZIRAB Intelligence Wing of the BLA.
Adnan Faqeer, known in the ranks of the resistance as “Talar,” was among the ideologically trained youth of the Baloch Students Organization (BSO) who gave new meaning to the relationship between the pen and the gun. A graduate in English Literature from the University of Balochistan, Adnan was not merely a student but also a sensitive poet and a conscious writer in the Balochi language. His creative sensibility compelled him to deeply feel the pain of national subjugation and to adopt the path of active resistance. Beginning his journey in student politics on the platform of the BSO in 2019, Adnan demonstrated that when consciousness transforms into action, it does not remain silent but becomes a revolutionary force.
In August 2024, he formally chose the path of armed struggle and, due to his intellectual maturity and technical competence, joined the BLA’s intelligence wing, “ZIRAB.” In 2025, he was transferred to the mountainous front, after which he was inducted into the organization’s frontline unit, the “Fateh Squad.” On the battlefield, his advance, bravery, and morale were considered unbreakable. Adnan’s political awareness, revolutionary temperament, and military discipline were regarded by his fellow Sarmachars (freedom fighters) as symbols of reliability, and he fulfilled every responsibility with professional seriousness and revolutionary resolve.
Adnan Faqeer’s role is a clear testament to the fact that the Baloch war of freedom has now taken the shape of a firm decision by educated and conscious youth who place the freedom of their homeland above every expediency. He proved that when thought connects with resistance, it gains the power to alter the course of history. Adnan’s humility and his decision to dedicate himself completely to the national liberation movement made him a shining symbol of resistance, awareness, and practical struggle for present and future generations.
Adnan Faqeer was present on the Rodbhun front during Operation Herof Phase II, where he embraced martyrdom while fighting on the fro

In continuation of the Fidayee (self-sacrificing) operation carried out on 8 July 2026 in Khuzdar city, Balochistan, against the compound of state asset and national traitor Shafiq Mengal, alias Shafiq Laghor (the coward) which resulted in the deaths of 34 members of Shafiq's death squad and the martyrdom of five members of the BLA. According to the organization, this operation, marking the commencement of the first phase of 'Operation Marg-e-Ghadaran' manifests the BLA's growing operational and intelligence capabilities against the colonial system and the criminal networks nurtured under it.

The five Fidayeen involved in this complex battle successfully breached the enemy's siege and retreated safely, while five other freedom fighters sacrificed their lives during various stages of this organized action to complete this crucial operation.
The operation commenced with the breaching of the outer security perimeter of Shafiq Laghor’s house, a responsibility undertaken by a talented Fidayee of the Majeed Brigade, Beebarg alias Pulliya Osama. The 22 year old Fidayee Beebarg hailed from the Tindilan area of Mastung and belonged to the Bangulzai tribe of the Baloch, formally joining the BLA and the Majeed Brigade in 2025. Following his enlistment into the organization's ranks, he remained active on the challenging military fronts of Khuzdar and Dasht, Quetta. Prior to this operation, he had demonstrated outstanding performance during 'Operation Herof 2' in the attack on the Frontier Corps central camp established at the Agriculture Office in Quetta. During the Khuzdar operation, he commanded the explosive laden vehicle, skillfully ramming it into the main gate of Shafiq Laghor's compound. Consequently, the outer defensive lines and checkpoints were reduced to rubble within seconds, instantly killing a large number of the enemy's armed guards stationed there and thereby clearing the path for the inner advance.
Immediately after the severe chaos caused by the explosion at the main gate, the next operational objective was to breach the security network of the compound's inner building, a task completed with utmost dedication and bravery by another valiant Fidayee of the Majeed Brigade, Zia Ur Rahman alias Imran. Hailing from Khadkocha, the 19-year-old Fidayee Zia Ur Rahman belonged to the Shahwani tribe and became a part of the BLA and the Majeed Brigade in 2025. Due to his exceptional combat skills, he quickly rose to the forefront of organizational activities on rigorous fronts such as Khuzdar and Koh-e-Maran. He had also been part of the frontline against the enemy on the Hazarganji front during 'Operation Herof 2.' In this battle of Khuzdar, right after Beebarg’s Fidayee strike, he courageously braved enemy fire to gain entry into the inner building of the compound and detonated the Fidayee jacket strapped to his body. As a result, the inner defensive line was completely destroyed, and the enemy's internal command-and-control system was paralyzed, providing the remaining Fidayeen with the opportunity to secure internal positions.
As soon as the inner security line collapsed, the remaining Fidayeen entered the compound and assumed various positions, where Fidayee Mohammad Ramzan Zehri, alias Shaban, took a stand at the main gate and its surrounding vital sectors to confront the enemy on the frontline. The 25-year-old Fidayee Mohammad Ramzan hailed from the Yakboozi area of Zehri, was the son of Chakar Khan, and belonged to the Zehri tribe. He joined the BLA in 2020 and became part of the Majeed Brigade in 2025 after extensive operational service. He was part of the guerrilla war for a long time across vast and highly sensitive fronts such as Bolan, Harboi, Nagaho, Zehri and Khuzdar and played a key role in the sensitive attack on the Quetta Red Zone during 'Operation Herof 2.' During the Khuzdar operation, he stood firm against the enemy's private death squad and uniformed collaborators at the central gate, fighting a close quarter battle and embracing martyrdom on the frontline while inflicting heavy casualties on the enemy.
The phase of maintaining resistance inside this enemy stronghold until the final moments and penetrating Shafiq Laghor’s residential block to clear all sides was carried out by two Fidayeen comrades of the Majeed Brigade, Shahzaib Baloch alias Sagaar and Shahzain Baloch alias Chedag. A resident of Manguchar, the son of Khalil Ahmed and belonging to the Nichari tribe of the Baloch, Fidayee Shahzaib Baloch began his journey in the organization as an urban guerrilla in December 2024, after which he transitioned to the regular mountain front in March 2025 and became part of the Majeed Brigade in June 2025. He was active on the Nagaho and Shoor fronts and had put up prolonged resistance against the enemy's heavy military strength under the direct command of the martyred Comrade Sameer during the battle at the Noshki main camp in 'Operation Herof 2.' Alongside him was Fidayee Shahzain Baloch alia

data.biography: On 31 January 2024 during an attack on the enemy forces at the Siyah Gazzi area of district Awaran, a tragic accident occurred in which BRAS fighter Shokat, also known as Kamash Dildar, son of Ali Murad and a resident of Kolwah Sagak, was martyred due to the accidental explosion of a rocket launcher. Shokat had been associated with the allied organization Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) since 2014. Over the course of eleven years, he served with dedication, perseverance, and sincerity in the struggle for the attainment of Baloch national freedom. Shaheed Kamash Dildar participated in BRAS operations on multiple fronts and dealt heavy blows to the enemy.

Ali, son of Niyaz Ahmed, was a 24 year old petrol pump owner from Jusak, Turbat. On 30 June 2026, at around 6:00 PM, Ali was forcibly disappeared from his petrol pump in Jusak by MI personnel and a death squad who arrived in two Surf vehicles.
On 6 July 2026, after seven days of enforced disappearance, Ali’s body was dumped near the CPEC Road in Jusak, Turbat. His body bore multiple bullet wounds and numerous visible signs of severe torture.
After seven days, Ali’s family recovered only his dead body. Before his enforced disappearance, no FIR had been registered against him, and his family was never informed of his whereabouts during his disappearance.

Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Shams ul Haq, alias Omar Jan, was the son of Murad Jan and a 26 year old resident of the Soorap area of District Panjgur, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in September 2023 and served in the Fateh Squad unit. He remained active on the Bolan, Chamalang, and Kalat fronts against the occupying genocidal forces.
Shams ul Haq, known as Omar Jan, was a 26 year old youth from the Soorap area of Panjgur who symbolized intellectual and military maturity, capable of achieving significant goals in a very short time. After becoming part of the BLA in September 2023, Shams-ul-Haq quickly secured his place in the organization’s vanguard unit, the Fateh Squad, due to his combat skills and extraordinary discipline. His brief but impactful military journey spanned the rugged valleys of Bolan, the mountains of Chamalang, and the difficult fronts of Kalat, where he proved his mettle in every encounter.
Shams ul Haq was among the selected volunteers who dealt a heavy blow to the enemy during the first phase (Phase 1) of Operation Darra-e-Bolan. He was not merely a fighter but a strategic soldier who understood the intricacies of the battlefield and the art of delivering decisive blows to the adversary. His quiet personality and dedication to the cause earned him great respect among his comrades.
At the time of his martyrdom, Shams-ul-Haq was standing firm on the Noshki front during Operation Herof Phase 2. Choosing to embrace martyrdom rather than compromise the sanctity of his motherland, he stood like an iron wall against the enemy during the clashes in Noshki.

On August 11, 2025 during an organizational mission in the Gajro Koor area of Jahoo, a fierce clash occurred between freedom fighters and so-called death squad formed by occupying army. In this engagement, Fighter Hasil Murad, alias Sarban Baloch, was martyred. At the beginning of the clash, a squad of freedom fighters was surrounded by the enemy. During this engagement, although fighter Hasil Murad was injured, he fought with exceptional courage and bravery, successfully clearing the path for his comrades to escape the enemy’s encirclement. Simultaneously, another squad of freedom fighters engaged death squad agents, providing cover with heavy fire and the injured fighter Hasil Murad was safely extracted. Unfortunately, a few hours later, fighter Hasil Murad succumbed to his injuries and was martyred. Martyr Hasil Murad, son of Murad Bakhsh and a resident of Chapbi Jahoo, joined Balochistan Liberation Front in 2014. Prior to that, he was active on the political platform and was recognized as an educated, politically aware and ideologically committed comrade. Over a struggle spanning approximately eleven to twelve years, he made significant sacrifices for Baloch national movement. Martyr Hasil Murad served as a frontline fighter in critical battles against enemy across various areas of Balochistan, including Jahoo, Gresha, Mashkay, Awaran, Ornach and Bela. In numerous operations, he displayed extraordinary courage, superior combat tactics and successfully completed every mission. Under state coercion, several relatives of martyr were subjected to enforced disappearance and his family was forcibly displaced from their native area. Martyr Hasil Murad’s father remains a victim of enforced disappearance, still held in custody of the Pakistani army. Despite these hardships, Hasil Murad remained steadfast in his commitment to an independent homeland until his last breath.

data.biography:
On 29 November 2022, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 26 November 2022, at 6:00 am, the Pakistani army fired hundreds of missiles from Iranian kamikaze drones in and around the Siakoh area of Kahan, Kohlu district of Balochistan. Out of these, two missiles fell within the premises of a BLA camp located in Siakoh. As a result, eight freedom fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army embraced martyrdom.
Afterward, the enemy launched a large scale ground and air operation in Kahan and adjoining areas. The spokesperson stated that for a long time Pakistan and Iran have maintained joint military cooperation against the Baloch national cause, including intelligence coordination. They also exchange advanced and lethal weapons.
In the first phase of the operation, following the drone attacks, several special forces commandos were dropped from around a dozen Pakistan Army combat helicopters, and shelling began from the air. Subsequently, military troops from Kohlu, Dera Bugti, and nearby areas - consisting of more than 400 personnel - participated in the operation using several armored and other military vehicles.
As soon as the Pakistani army initiated the operation, nearby BLA camps in the area began countering the enemy’s advance from different fronts by adopting a joint defense strategy.
The combat between the enemy forces and the freedom fighters continued intermittently until the evening. As a result, the freedom fighters inflicted heavy casualties on the Pakistani forces from all sides. Breaking the army’s land and air siege through skilled combat tactics, they carried their injured comrades, along with weapons and other sensitive equipment, to safe locations.
During the conflict, after several hours of fierce resistance by the fighters, the army turned its guns toward the local population in Nissau, Siakoh, Drehis, Parhki, Jantali, and adjoining areas. The enemy set fire to many houses and severely tortured residents. Meanwhile, troops stopped two innocent Baloch pedestrians and killed them.
The organization’s fighters who embraced martyrdom were - Gahmar Khan alias Garra, Thal Khan alias Thallu, Hameed Baloch alias Sado
Shadi Khan alias Kooda, Abu Bakr Baloch alias Rehan, Jameel alias Naadi
Kareem Khan alias Jamal, Muhammad Nusrat alias Asif - The organization also rejected reports claiming that BLA fighters had been arrested during the operation. Through the media, it challenged ISPR to substantiate its narrative with concrete evidence.
Shadi Khan alias Kooda began his regular armed struggle through the BLA in 2011. He was one of the senior and important members of the organization. His family had previously made sacrifices for national freedom.
Nazeer Baloch, was a resident of the Dasht, Kech area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 14 March 2017 in Balochistan.

On 1 November 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson, Gwahram Baloch, issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of eight of the organisation’s fighters: Captain Yahya, alias Ustad Khalid Jan; Aris Baloch, alias Omar Jan; Hafeez Baloch, alias Karwan, son of Dad Mohammad; Javid Baloch, alias Gulab, son of Bori Baloch; Abdul Khaliq, alias Nothak; Sajid Baloch, alias Mehran; Hameed Baloch, alias Buzerg; and Akram Baloch, alias Gwahram.

The statement paid tribute to these brave and ideologically committed members of the organisation, who embraced martyrdom while engaging in clashes with the Pakistani army and its death squads on various fronts across Balochistan.

Martyr Akram Baloch, alias Gwahram, son of Dost Mohammad, resident of Jan Muhammad Bazaar, Dasht, began his struggle through the BLF platform in 2012 and, remaining within the organization's ranks, kept the flag of the national war flying with full courage and steadfastness. From the covert and very difficult operations of the urban front to the dangerous positions of the mountain front, he inflicted human and material losses on the enemy on every front and stood firm on his ideology like a rock of steel until his last breath.

After the forced expulsion and burning of homes by the occupying army in 2017, his family too had to migrate and live as refugees in a foreign land. Despite all these hardships and family suffering, Shaheed Akram did not step back a single step from his national cause and organizational struggle.

Finally, on 5 June 2026, while carrying out movement duties he embraced martyrdom as a result of a sudden road accident. Shaheed Akram and Shaheed Hameed were very close relatives who dedicated their lives to the motherland's freedom at the call of the same soil, the same family and the same ideology.

On 16 October 2026, a statement issued by the Baloch Republican Guards (BRG) stated that, on the night of 30 September 2026, occupying Pakistani forces arrived in the Sunni area of Kachhi district, Balochistan, to conduct an operation. A sudden confrontation took place between the occupying forces and the freedom fighters, who launched a deadly attack against the enemy. As a result, the occupying army suffered significant casualties and material losses.

During the clashes, five devoted BRG freedom fighters - Bafa Jan Jatoi, son of Lal Jan Jatoi, a resident of Sunni, Kachhi; Fareed Jan Jatoi, alias Zahri, son of Ghulam Jan, a resident of Sunni, Kachhi; Obaidullah Jan Jatoi, son of Sajjar Khan, a resident of Sunni, Kachhi; Imam Din Jatoi, alias Mumtaz, son of Nihal Khan, a resident of Sunni, Kachhi; and Ayaz Jan Ghola, alias Alim, son of Abdul Sattar, belonging to the Ghola Baloch tribe and a resident of Sunni, Kachhi - embraced martyrdom while defending their homeland and fighting for national independence.

All these freedom fighters were highly dedicated, brave, hardworking, and disciplined comrades. They inflicted various forms of losses on the occupying enemy in several areas of Balochistan, including Kachhi, Dhadar, Sunni, Bolan, and Sibi.

data.biography:
Jalal, son of Haji Yar Muhammad, a local businessman and resident of Gomazi, Tump, district Kech, was shot dead by state-backed death squads on the evening of September 6, 2025.

His killing marks the third extrajudicial killing in a single day in district Kech, following the killings of Izhar and Mulla Bahram in Mand earlier that same day. Eyewitnesses and local sources confirmed that state-backed death squads, operating under the supervision of Pakistani forces, carried out the attack.

On 6 November 2026, the Baloch Liberation Army's media channel, Hakkal, published the biographies and details of six martyrs associated with the organization.

Among them, three fighters - Muneer Ahmad Jattak, alias Noora, son of Habib Khan Jattak; Shahzaib Bangulzai, alias Ehsan, son of Samiullah Bangulzai; and Fareed Langove, son of Ghulam Nabi Langove - were martyred on 20 October 2026 in the Rodinjo area of Kalat District.

Two other fighters, Parvez Ahmad Mohammad Hassni, alias Qadir, son of Shekari Mohammad Khan Mohammad Hassni, and Noman Jamaldini, alias Comrade Sameer, son of Agha Mohammad Jamaldini, were martyred on 24 October 2026 in the Gidar area of Surab.

The sixth fighter, Aurangzaib Langove, alias Asif, son of Hameedullah Langove, was martyred on 24 October 2026 in the Manguchar area of Kalat District.

Noman Jamaldini, alias Comrade Sameer, son of Agha Mohammad Jamaldini, was a resident of Killi Jamaldini, Noshki. He joined the BLA's Urban Front in 2024 and, in 2025, moved to the Mountain Front, where he served in Kalat, Nushki, and Surab. He was martyred on 24 October 2026 in Gidar, Surab.

Noman Jamaldini considered the restoration of Baloch national freedom and sovereignty, along with the establishment of an independent Baloch state, to be the only means of achieving collective prosperity. With this conviction, he decided to join the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in 2024 and play his part in the national liberation struggle. His decision to join the armed resistance was not driven by emotion; rather, it was based on his firm belief that, without national freedom and sovereignty, the Baloch people have no other collective path to survival. Under organizational guidance, he carried out urban guerrilla activities for one year.

On the urban front, he participated in various armed operations and guerrilla activities against the enemy. In 2025, following organizational directives, he moved to the mountain front. He participated in the Baloch Liberation Army's guerrilla operations and attacks on the Kalat, Surab, and Nushki fronts. He was also part of the BLA's Operation Hero II, where he fulfilled his assigned responsibilities.

From civilian life to the mountain front, he remained committed to the struggle. He sacrificed his life in the name of freedom, and history will remember him as a hero.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Hizbullah Nichari, also known as Mazar, son of Shafi Mohammad Nichari, was a resident of Manguchar, Killi Nechari.
Hizbullah Nichari earned a university degree in Accounting and Finance. He was the brother of Fidayee Asif Nichari, who was martyred during Operation Hero One. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2023 and became a member of the Fateh Squad.
During Operation Hero, Shaheed Hizbullah Nichari was martyred while fighting on the front lines at the Noshki front, demonstrating courage, discipline, and a deep sense of responsibility. He upheld the national struggle with conscious commitment and steadfast resolve, leaving behind a clear example of sacrifice on the battlefield. His life stood as a symbol of the union of knowledge, awareness, and resistance, remaining firmly rooted on the front lines until the final moment.
Belongs to BSO Azad

Mohammad Naseem Lehri, alias Girok, son of Ghulam Farooq Lehri, was a resident of Killi Farooq Abad in the Mastung area of Balochistan. His educational qualification was a B.Sc. He joined the BLA in 2026, served on the Mastung front, and was martyred on 19 September 2026 in the Shirnaap area of Mastung, Balochistan.
After understanding the historical reality of enemy occupation and the importance and status of national sovereignty, and after developing a revolutionary awareness of these realities, Muhammad Naseem Lehri decided to join the national resistance and the armed struggle for freedom. In 2026, he began providing military services through the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army. His national and military service began in Mastung, where he first received physical, moral, and revolutionary training as part of his combat education. Following an organisational decision, he was then deployed to the front lines, where he took an active part in military operations against the enemy.
As an educated youth, he fully applied his intellectual and academic abilities in the organisation’s administrative activities and remained active as a capable and promising young fighter. He always carried out all the combat and administrative responsibilities assigned by the organisation in the region on time and to the highest standard. These abilities consistently proved him to be a unique and capable fighter. Instead of prioritising his personal life, Martyr Muhammad Naseem gave precedence to national freedom and the collective cause, fighting for his country’s liberation until his last breath and attaining martyrdom. His sacrifices will be remembered in history alongside those of the great martyrs who sacrificed themselves forever for the freedom of this sacred homeland.

Nawaz Baloch son of Lal Bakhsh, a resident of Bazdad a small town in Awaran district, Balochistan. He was summoned to show his presence at main Pakistani military headquarters in Awaran on August 11, 2025. 

With Nawaz entrance, he was illegally detained by forces in the camp. After three consecutive days, his whereabouts remained unknown. Family then approached headquarter. Besides, no information about his condition delivered to the victim family. 

On August 14, 2025, his bullet-riddled body was found in a distant area of Rekan, Awaran. And the body, bearing the apparently the signs of extreme physical torture, subjection and ill-treatment before his death. 

Pakistan forces issued a threatening statement to his family that his lifeless body should be buried with no further delay.
Sarfraz Baloch, was a resident of the Anjira, Khuzdar area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 30 September 2013 in Balochistan.

On 3 November 2024, Pakistan's Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) extrajudicially killed three Baloch - Mohammad Nawaz Buzdar, Ghulam Buzdar, and Jaffar Marri - in a staged encounter in the Rarasham area of Musakhel District. All three had previously been abducted and forcibly disappeared by the so called Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) of the Pakistani genocidal forces from Rarasham.

Mohammad Nawaz Buzdar, a resident of Rarasham Barg Posht, was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 10 September 2024, from Rarasham, Musakhel District.

Ghulam Buzdar, a resident of Rarasham, was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 21 September 2024, from Rarasham, Musakhel District.

Jaffar Marri was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 2 October 2024, from Rarasham, Musakhel District.

data.biography:
On 2 June 2025 in the Mach area of Bolan, Pakistani forces and fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) came face to face when the fighters were travelling for organizational activities. At a location called Goni Para, clashes broke out between the BLA fighters and the Pakistani forces. During the confrontation, the forces deployed commandos using helicopters. In the clashes that continued for several hours, at least eight personnel of the opposing forces were killed, while five BLA fighters - Washdal, alias Mashmar; Samiullah, alias Sameer; Shehryar Shahwani, alias Chairman; Sajawal, alias Cheeda; and Nadir, alias Chiragh - achieved martyrdom.
Washdil, alias Mashmar, son of Lal Khan Sumalani, belonged to Sanjawal in the Bolan region. 22 old Washdal joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2024 and at a young age, took up arms with the resolve to fulfill what he saw as his national responsibility. He played an important role on many occasions on the Bolan front and ultimately embraced martyrdom after inflicting significant losses on the enemy.
Samiullah, alias Sameer, son of Muhammad Akram; the Shehryar, alias Chairman, son of Mehrab Khan Shahwani; and the Sajawal, alias Cheeda, son of Bawal Khan Shahwani - all belonged to Parangabad in Mastung. These three companions joined the BLA a year ago and as urban guerrillas, participated in several successful operations. Always active in striking the enemy and fulfilling organizational duties, they were present on every front. Their lives, devoted to the cause of national freedom, have become a guiding light for Baloch youth.
Nadir, alias Chiragh, son of Mazar Khan Lehri, was originally from Narmuk in the Kalat region but was residing in Quetta. In his guerrilla role, he was highly organized, vigilant, and steadfast, confronting the enemy with courage. Constantly engaged in organizational work, he remained firm in his responsibilities until his final breath.

On 7 October 2024, a statement was issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch, stating that on 6 October 2024, the Majeed Brigade, the elite Fidayeen unit of the Baloch Liberation Army, targeted a high level convoy of Chinese engineers and investors leaving Jinnah Airport in Karachi in a Fidayeen attack. According to the statement, more than five Chinese engineers and investors were killed and more than twelve were injured. At least fifteen Pakistani military personnel assigned to protect them were also killed, with many others injured, including more than four high-ranking officers of the Pakistani army and intelligence agencies. As a result of the explosion, fifteen vehicles in the convoy were destroyed. Due to the careful tactics of the BLA, civilians were spared casualties in the blast despite the densely populated area.
This operation was carried out by Shah Fahad, alias Aftab; Saddam Baloch, alias Fareed and Sohail, alias Baba, of the BLA’s Majeed Brigade.
Shah Fahad Badini, alias Aftab, son of Mir Fazal Khan Badini, belonged to the Kili Badini area of Nushki. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2019. Sangat Shah Fahad, alias Aftab, who possessed strong qualities of sincerity and perseverance, always performed his duties diligently. Twenty-eight-year-old Shah Fahad Badini was a brilliant student who completed his BBA degree at Lasbela University.

Asfand Qambarani, alias Rokyn, son of Munawar Ali and resident of Quetta, joined the BLA in November 2024 and served on the Kalat front as Patrol Commander in the Fateh Squad unit.
Asfand Qambarani hailed from Quetta. Shortly after joining the BLA, he was entrusted with the responsibility of Patrol Commander on the Kalat front due to his exceptional military capabilities. He was also inducted into the organization’s frontline unit, the Fateh Squad. Asfand maintained unwavering resolve even amidst rugged mountains, prolonged sieges, and the constant threat of gunfire. He endured fatigue, limited supplies, and relentless pressure, never abandoning his position until the very end. His advance was quiet yet decisive, and his steadfastness served as an example for his fellow Sarmachars. He demonstrated that in the war of liberation, superiority belongs to those who wield patience as a weapon, discipline as a shield, and resolve as their true strength.
On 6 December 2025, while Shaheed Asfand was on a mission preparing for Operation Heroof 2.0, he engaged the enemy in the mountains of Kalat. He stood firm on the front line alongside his Fateh Squad team, where his bravery, dynamic combat strategy, and discipline forced the enemy to retreat. By sacrificing his life, Shaheed Asfand became immortal in the history of the war for freedom.

Bebagr Baloch, son of Ghulam Mustafa, born in 1994, was a resident of District Khuzdar. He was an engineering student at the Balochistan University of Engineering and Technology, Khuzdar. He received his early education in his hometown, Khuzdar.
Bebarg Baloch was a member of BSO Azad, Khuzdar Zone. He mobilized hundreds of youth to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of their homeland. Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by security forces. He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he remained committed to the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom.
He was an example of bravery and commitment. He joined the organization at an early age and remained devoted to his national ideology until the end. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising his peaceful political expression.
He was a victim of targeted killing by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agencies on 11 June 2010 in District Khuzdar, Balochistan. He was among the most committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad.
His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

data.biography:
On February 23, 2022 the occupying forces of Pakistan struck the Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) guerrilla camp in the Satak Kor mountain range of Hoshab, district Kech, and fired three chemical-laden missiles that wreaked havoc over a large area, destroying palm groves and other vegetation at the site. Following the drone missile attacks, the infantry team of the occupying forces surrounded the area and, with the support of more than eight state helicopters, entered the camp. Five Sarmachaars, including two commanders of the organization, Master Asif Baloch and Siraj Baloch, were martyred in this attack. Meanwhile, five other Sarmachaars - Shoaib, Munir, Arif Jan, Diljan, Kamal, Kamash Malang, Jangi Khan, and Daolat - were martyred defending their homeland, fighting the enemy for over an hour and killing several commandos of the occupying forces.
Dolat, alias Chiragh, son of Yousuf, resident of Hoshab Damb, had been associated with the organization since a year before his martyrdom. He was a patriotic and courageous Sarmachar.

Mehran Baloch, the 27 year old son of Mohammad Sharif, was a young shopkeeper from a poor Baloch family. On 21 May 2026, while leaving for his shop in Sorap Bazar, Buleda, Kech District, Balochistan, he was shot dead in broad daylight by armed men. His killing added another grieving family to the long list of Baloch families mourning the loss of their loved ones across Balochistan.

data.biography:
A freedom fighter of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), Tabish Inayat, alias Rehan, embraced martyrdom in a battle with occupying forces on 29 July 2021. Tabish, a member of the BLA’s Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS), was on an important organisational mission when he encountered enemy forces near Easai, Panjgur. After a fierce battle in which Tabish inflicted heavy losses on the enemy, the brave BLA fighter chose to use his last bullet to end his own life rather than surrender to the occupying forces.
Tabish Inayat, alias Rehan, a resident of Khudabadan in Panjgur, was a highly skilled fighter who had earned his place in STOS due to his bravery, intelligence, and combat expertise. He played a key role in several battles against the enemy in Panjgur, Gichk, and Keelkor.
True to the noble tradition of the “last bullet,” Tabish Inayat protected organisational secrets by taking his own life.

data.biography:
In 1838, the British sent a force led by Alexander Burnes to reinstate Shah Shuja Durrani as the king of Afghanistan by deposing Amir Dost Mohammad Khan. To reach Afghanistan, they needed passage through Balochistan, particularly the Bolan Pass. However, Khan Mehrab Khan refused to allow the British to use his land to attack a neighboring country. The British sent Lieutenant Leach to negotiate with the Baloch government, but the Khan stood firm. When British forces reached Shaal via Bolan, some patriotic Baloch, without the Khan’s knowledge, attacked British troops out of nationalist sentiment and a desire to protect their homeland.
After toppling Amir Dost Mohammad Khan, the British Governor General of India, Lord Auckland, ordered an attack on Balochistan. In 1839, around 7,000 British troops marched from Shaal to attack the Baloch Meeri (capital). Anticipating an invasion, Khan Mehrab Khan declared war and sent messages to tribal leaders, but many saw the British as allies rather than invaders and chose to collaborate with them rather than defend their land. When Khan Mehrab Khan gathered his resistance fighters, the number of loyal warriors had dwindled to only 700 due to the short sightedness of many tribal chiefs. Nevertheless, Mehrab Khan was determined to fight. At his court, a respected figure, Akhund Muhammad Siddiq, advised him that he was not in a position to wage war at that time. He suggested that the Khan should leave Kalat with his companions, regroup and strengthen his forces, and then launch an attack against the British when the time was right, on 13 November 1839, the British forces launched an attack on Kalat, and a fierce battle ensued. During the fighting, Khan Mehrab Khan Baloch was martyred by a British bullet.

Among those martyred alongside him were:

Diwan Bacha Mal, Minister of Finance
