On 3rd April 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that fighters of the BLA launched a series of coordinated attacks against the occupying Pakistani army across occupied Balochistan on 29th March 2026, which continued until 1st April 2026. The fighters carried out 65 operations in Panjgur, Shapuk, Basima, Sibi, Mastung, Quetta, Noshki, Zamuran, Dasht, Surab, Jhal Magsi, Dalbandin, Kharan, Washuk, and Kalat. In these actions, more than 86 personnel of the Pakistani army, death squads, and intelligence agencies were killed, and dozens were injured. These attacks targeted occupying army camps, an airbase, radar systems, communication towers, railway tracks, bridges, and gas pipelines, while major highways were brought under control for several hours.
During clashes with Pakistani forces, five BLA fighters in Panjgur - Zahid alias Nawaz, Saeedullah alias Meraj, Jahanzeb alias Qambar, Aamir alias Khalid, and Saddam alias Shahwaiz - along with Abdust (Abdul Rehman) alias Alman in Zamuran, attained martyrdom.
Abdust Aziz (Abdul Rehman), alias Alman (son of Mulla Asghar): From Kochaad, Tump, he joined the struggle in 2018 and the BLA in 2019. As a member of the elite 'Fateh Squad' his combat skills were exemplary.
Abdust was a living example of continuous struggle. Despite the occupying forces martyring his uncle, Musadiq, and subjecting his family to collective punishment, he never wavered. He was raised by his mother, Bibi Umaira, a woman of revolutionary thought who not only nurtured his ideological growth but also always stood as a supporter and helper of the Baloch resistance.

On 28 June 2026, the spokesperson for the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) issued a statement announcing that five fighters of the organisation - Shoaib Zehri, alias Farooq; Zakariya Zehri, alias Ustad Zoreen Baloch; Kifayatullah Badini, alias Badil Baloch; Captain Hashum Baloch, alias Kambar; and Abdul Rahim, alias Ustad Imran - had embraced martyrdom. The statement said that the blood of the martyrs guarantees Baloch national survival and sovereignty.

Shoaib Zehri, alias Farooq, was martyred on May 17, 2026, in Khuzdar while fighting valiantly during an operation against the enemy.
Shoaib Zehri began his struggle in 2024 under the banner of the Balochistan Liberation Front. Before formally transferring to the military front, he diligently carried out ideological and political responsibilities within the organizational ranks and, in a short period, developed a strong understanding of the demands of the military environment. After completing the necessary organizational work, he formally transferred to the front.
Through his military capabilities, he fulfilled several important national responsibilities within a very short period. He participated in guerrilla operations on the difficult fronts of Khuzdar and Zehri and played an important role in organizing the network. He was an extremely sincere, resilient, loyal, and fearless fighter who served with utmost dedication, strictly adhered to organizational discipline, and consistently played a leading role during military campaigns against the enemy.
On May 17, during an operation in the Lakhoriyan area of Khuzdar, the fighters surrounded police personnel and ordered them to surrender. Instead of surrendering, the police opened fire. The fighters then took positions and launched a counter-operation. During this exchange of fire, Shoaib Zehri was martyred while fighting valiantly.

On 9 November 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Republican Guards spokesperson Dostain Baloch announced the martyrdom of five members of the organisation and paid red salutes to them.

The spokesperson said: “We pay heartfelt tribute and offer red salutes to the sincere, brave, and ideologically committed fighters of the Baloch Republican Guards: Commander Habibullah Jan Jatoi, alias Laghari; Sharif Jatoi, alias Commando; Saeed Jan Jatoi, alias Nana; Hazrat Jatoi, alias Bolani; and Umeed Ali Jatoi, alias Nadir. They embraced martyrdom while bravely fighting against the occupying Pakistani army in the Sanni area of Kachhi for the freedom and right to self-determination of Balochistan."

On 1 November 2026, in the Sanni area of Kachhi, Commander Habibullah Jan and his revolutionary comrades launched an ambush against a convoy of the occupying Pakistani army.
Commander Habibullah Jan and his brave fighters fiercely engaged the enemy on the front lines, inflicting significant human and material losses on the occupying forces.
During the clash, an enemy drone suddenly launched an attack, seriously injuring Commander Habibullah Jan, Saeed, Hazrat, and Umeed. Despite their injuries, they continued to face the consequences of the attack. However, unable to survive their severe injuries, Habibullah Jan and his comrades later embraced martyrdom. All five members were residents of the Sanni area of Kachhi.
Mohammad Siddique Sasoli was a resident of the Dosay, Noshki area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 18 August 2017 in Balochistan.

Faiz Mohammad Marri, son of Jalal Marri, was a 36 year old political worker and a resident of the New Kahan area of Quetta. On 6 November 2010, he was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. Months later, on 2 March 2011, his body was found in Dasht, Mastung.

In a statement issued on 26 June 2025 by Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson of the Baloch Liberation Army, it was said that three BLA fighters were martyred in clashes with the occupying Pakistani forces on the fronts of Quetta, Kalat and Seyahji. The martyred comrades include Jamshed,  Noroz and Munawar Baig.
On 22 June 2025 in the Daghari area of Quetta, a BLA patrol team encountered the occupying Pakistani forces as they attempted to advance in the area. A face to face battle broke out between the occupying forces and the fighters, which continued for a long time. Several personnel of the occupying army were killed and injured in the clashes, while BLA fighter Jamshed, also known as Rizwan, attained martyrdom.
In the evening, two units of BLA fighters surrounded the occupying army’s infantry in a ravine and attacked them from two sides. As a result, six soldiers of the occupying forces were killed on the spot and several others were injured. During the hour-long clash, BLA fighter Noroz, alias King Najeeb, was martyred.
On 20 June 2025 in the Langasi area of Dasht, BLA fighters encountered the occupying Pakistani forces while travelling for organizational work. In the face to face battle that ensued, the occupying forces suffered losses. Meanwhile, in an already injured state, Sangat Munawar Baig was martyred during the clash with the occupying forces.
Noroz, alias King Najeeb, son of Mir Muhammad Shahwani, belonged to the Sunger area of Mastung. He joined the BLA in 2023 and served on the fronts of Mastung, Nagaho and Kalat. His personality was marked by extraordinary perseverance and ideological commitment. He always led the resistance from the front. Through his organizational work, he proved that the youth are the true asset of the national struggle.

The Baloch Liberation Army’s Majeed Brigade attacked a large Pakistani army convoy at Kunchiti Cross in Dasht, Kech, on 18 September 2025. The convoy included six buses carrying army personnel and an escort squad. It had arrived in Gwadar from Karachi a day earlier and was travelling toward Turbat when the attack occurred around 1 p.m.

The operation began when Altaf alias Chakar drove a VBIED into the main bus, destroying it. After the explosion, Gwahram alias Zagrain and Khalil alias Kulmeer targeted the remaining buses and the security squad. The clash continued for over thirty minutes. According to BLA’s sources, at least 32 army personnel were killed, several wounded, and multiple buses destroyed. Reinforcements and drones arrived later, but rescue operations were delayed.

Altaf (from Alandur Buleda), Gwahram (from Paroom, Panjgur), and Khalil (from Saami, Turbat) had all joined the BLA in 2023. Each had served as an urban guerrilla before moving to the mountains and becoming part of the Majeed Brigade, where they underwent training and took on various responsibilities.

On 12 July 2024, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 28 December 2018, BLA member Aurangzeb, alias Mazar Baloch, was deceived and martyred after being subjected to inhumane torture by Pakistan Army–backed death squads in Koshk Buleda, in the Sorapi Dap area of Kech.
Aurangzeb, alias Mazar Baloch, son of Gulab, belonged to Koshk Buleda. He joined the organization in 2016 and continued to perform his duties with sincerity and honesty until his martyrdom.

On 19 October 2006, Pakistani occupying forces surrounded Mir Baz Khan Marri Baloch’s house near Kohlu and launched an operation. The attack resulted in the death of Baz Khan Marri Baloch and six other family members—including his wife, mother, and two children—while three other women were seriously injured in this brutal assault.

Abdul Hameed, son of Maula Bakhsh, was 31 years old and a resident of Kohdask, Khuzdar. He was forcibly disappeared on April 22, 2026, by the Pakistani forces, particularly the Frontier Corps (FC), from Basima, Washuk. After five months of unconstitutional detention, he was extrajudicially killed on September 17, 2026, and his mutilated body was found at Maskay Cross.
Abdul Hameed was a farmer who served his family through agriculture, cultivating vegetables and fruits on his irrigated land. In order to earn a sufficient income from his farmland, he fulfilled his responsibilities toward his family, like many Baloch people. Despite this, the Pakistani military, particularly the Frontier Corps (FC), allegedly subjected him to enforced disappearance, torture, and extrajudicial killing. His lifeless body was found by the roadside at Maskay Cross after he had allegedly been tortured.
After five months of detention, Abdul Hameed’s family was finally freed from the mental suffering and psychological distress caused by not knowing his whereabouts. While his family members had been awaiting his safe and peaceful return, the Pakistani authorities instead handed them his lifeless body.
Abdul Hameed was a hardworking farmer who was always concerned with improving his agricultural land and earning a sufficient income for the betterment of his family. Yet, the Pakistani state treated him as a threat.

Fidayee Sangat Mehzam alias Meerak who targeted an enemy military convoy in Noshki with a VBIED attack. This brave son, from the Jainh Paroom area of Panjgur joined BLA in 2021 and quickly became a member of the Majeed Brigade due to his bravery and dedication. He eliminated over 90 enemy personnel and wounded dozens by targeting a convoy of eight buses proving the Baloch resistance can strike anywhere. He was the brother of Martyr Fidayee Shehzad alias Cobra, who was part of the Fidayee attack on the Karachi Stock Exchange in June 2020.

Irshad Alam, the 18-year-old son of Alam Khan, was a young businessman from Badrang, Gresha Naal.
On April 30, 2026, he was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces, becoming a victim of enforced disappearance and joining the long list of Baloch individuals whose families continue to search for truth and justice. After weeks of anguish and uncertainty, the family's worst fears were realized on June 8, 2026, when his lifeless body was found in Basima, Washuk, Balochistan.

data.martyrdomPlace: Miskeen River, Buleda, Turbat district, Balochistan
data.biography:
Nasram Baloch, son of Peer Baksh, from Mohdabad Mehnaz, Buleda, belonged to a poor family and was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 12 October 2023. For nine months, his family lived in anguish and uncertainty. From 2 June to 6 June 2024, they held a sit-in protest in front of the Deputy Commissioner’s Office in Turbat, organized rallies, and staged peaceful demonstrations, demanding his safe release.
He was finally released on 13 June 2024, but his health had severely deteriorated. During his detention, he suffered torture and inhumane treatment, which left him with hepatitis and lasting physical harm.
Only a few months later, on 8 August 2024, he was again forcibly disappeared from his home in Buleda Bit. Armed men stormed the house, tortured his mother and sister, and took Nasram away.
On 26 February 2026, his tortured and lifeless body was found dumped in the Miskeen River in the Buleda area of Turbat, Balochistan, bearing clear signs of severe abuse.

Salam Haider, a young resident of Ghatti Dhoor, Gwadar, originally from Kumbail Dasht in Kech District, was tortured to death in illegal custody after being forcibly disappeared by Pakistani military forces.
On the night of 12 June 2025, around 11:00 PM, Pakistani forces raided Salam’s home and enforcedly disappeared him. He was subjected to severe physical torture during detention. On 15 June 2025, his lifeless and mutilated body was returned to his family.
Eyewitnesses reported that during the raid, security personnel looted valuables including mobile phones, cash, and gold jewelry. Following Salam’s custodial killing by Pakistani forces, his family faced further violence and coercion. Pakistani forces ordered the family to bury his body without religious or cultural rites. When Salam’s sister resisted, she was brutally assaulted by security personnel, sustaining injuries that required hospitalization. His mother and sister were denied the chance to even view his body one last time.

In a statement issued by Jeeyand Baloch, the spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), it was said that on Friday night, June 6, 2025, the occupying Pakistani forces advanced in the Splinji, Maru and Phull areas of Mastung. As a result, clashes broke out between the Baloch Liberation Army fighters and the occupying forces. The clashes continued until morning, during which at least seven enemy personnel were killed and several others injured, while two of our fighters, Zafran alias Khalil and Sana alias Angle, were martyred.
Zafran alias Khalil, son of Ismail SUmalani, belonged to Pir Ismail Marwar in the Bolan region. He had been part of the national liberation struggle since 2014 and, as a member of the Baloch Liberation Army, remained active on the frontlines against the enemy. On the Negaho front, he took part in numerous battles, defeated the enemy, and ultimately embraced martyrdom there as a commander. Martyr Zafran was a symbol of unwavering struggle, perseverance, revolutionary discipline and sincerity. For eleven years, in all seasons and all circumstances, he stood against the enemy and rendered unforgettable services.
Sana alias Angle, son of Inayatullah Satakzai, belonged to the Phull Maru area of Splinji. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army one year ago and, in a short time, proved through his dedication, revolutionary discipline, and spirit that courage and sacrifice are not dependent on age. He fulfilled his responsibilities on the Nagaho front with commitment and attained the honored status of martyrdom.

Dr. Lal Khan, alias Durak, son of Nawaz Ali, was a resident of the Parom area of Panjgur and an MBBS student at Bolan Medical College, Quetta. He joined the BLA in 2024 and moved to the mountain front in 2025. He served on the Shor, Parod, Nushki, and Washuk fronts and was promoted to the rank of Patrol Commander. He was martyred on August 30, 2026, in the Washuk area of Balochistan.
Dr. Lal Khan was an educated, conscious, capable, hardworking, and serious young fighter of the BLA who had an academic approach to life. He made a conscious and revolutionary decision to devote his knowledge to action, his personal life to a collective purpose, and his individual aspirations to the national interest. In doing so, he became an example of how, when nations face conditions of war, educated and conscious individuals may choose a collective purpose as the philosophy of their lives rather than remaining silent or prioritizing an individual life. He devoted himself to that collective purpose. This historical, academic, and intellectual approach convinced him to choose the armed resistance of the BLA and shaped him as a revolutionary comrade in history.
Dr. Lal Khan was not only a capable and talented person academically; when he chose the armed front in practical life, he made the administrative, revolutionary, and moral responsibilities of war the purpose of his life. He made adherence to organizational discipline, the establishment of organizational strength in different areas, and the development of various military skills and abilities part of his practical life. On the Shor front, he demonstrated his revolutionary and administrative abilities within a short period. During the historic Operation Herof II, he continued fighting the enemy for six days on the Nushki front. Afterward, in accordance with organizational policy, he was transferred to the Washuk front to establish organizational strength and superiority. During the following year, he not only forced the enemy to take defensive positions on the battlefield but also expanded the organization’s administrative, operational, and territorial reach through his leadership abilities.
From being a talented student pursuing medical education to becoming a capable military and administrative commander on the battlefield, he was a committed fighter on every front of his life. Dr. Lal Khan maintained this standard until his martyrdom, adhering to the principles he had made the foundation of his life. He left a message for talented young people that, at this critical point in history, they should choose the path of national purpose, freedom, and sovereignty rather than an individual life, which, according to this account, represents a guarantee of a better future.
In Baloch history, Dr. Lal Khan will be remembered as a continuing chapter.

Abdul Majeed Zehri, a 13-year-old boy from Khuzdar and an 8th-grade student, dreamed of becoming a football player. He had no desire to join counter-insurgency groups or death squads; his only ambition was to become an athlete in a free nation. To pursue this dream, he became an activist with the Baloch Student Organization (Azad). In the eyes of Pakistan, his dream was a crime. On 18 October 2010, the Pakistani army abducted him near Fapoor Chowk in Khuzdar. After torturing the Baloch child to death, the cowardly Pakistani soldiers dumped his mutilated body on the Rabka Khuzdari road in Khuzdar on 24 October 2010.
data.martyrdomPlace: Rabka Khuzdari Road, Khuzdar district, Balochistan

data.biography:
Dr. Qambar Mubarak Qazi was born into the family of prominent Baloch poet Mubarak Qazi in Pasni, Gwadar, on 14 January 1984. He received his early education and completed his matriculation in his hometown of Pasni. After completing his matriculation, he moved to Turbat for further studies. He enrolled at the historic Atta Shad Degree College, Kech, for his intermediate education. He inherited a poetic and literary legacy and became active in literary work and political activism.
It was the first decade of the 21st century, and Baloch student politics was at its peak. Therefore, he started participating in student political circles and became increasingly involved in political activities. He formally began his student political career in 2004 on the platform of the Baloch Students Organisation Azad. He was active in the region and became one of the most committed members of the organisation, organising and educating students in his circle. He established a connection between literary work and political struggle.
After completing his intermediate education, he went to Quetta for further studies. There, he chose the medical profession and passed the medical entrance examination. He gained admission to Bolan Medical College and became an MBBS student. As a medical student, he did not just study medicine; he also began studying literature, politics, philosophy, history, and Balochi literature. Soon, he became one of the most influential and respected political and literary figures in Baloch political circles.
As he had the legacy of poetry, literature, and politics in his veins, the BSO helped him become a more mature and well-educated political cadre. He started writing poetry and highlighting the oppression of the Baloch nation through his writings. He had a collection of poetry that was published after his martyrdom. Although he studied medicine professionally, he diagnosed the disease of colonialism and began fighting against it through various means.
He did not end his political career with student politics. Rather, after completing his graduation, he joined another platform of the Baloch liberation movement and began contributing to the struggle practically. He was well known for his broader approach towards the Baloch liberation movement and played an active and influential role in it.
However, the life of a revolutionary worker is never certain; one may embrace martyrdom at any time. The same occurred with Qambar Mubarak. He embraced martyrdom on 31 August 2014 in Gwarkop, Kech District, Balochistan.

Mannan Baloch, alias Saqi, had been associated with the Baloch freedom struggle through the Baloch Liberation Front (BLF) since 2014.
On 18 August 2017, when the Pakistani army launched an assault on the civilian population in the Duseh area of Nushki using eight helicopters, Shaheed Saqi took up his sniper rifle to protect the civilians and confronted the enemy face to face. After killing several enemy personnel, he himself was martyred and thus became immortal in the history of Balochistan. The defeated enemy, demoralized by the deaths of several of its hired collaborators, displayed its customary brutality by taking the martyr’s body with them instead of handing it over to his family.

Irshad Baloch, son of Mohammad Younis, was a 17-year-old FSc student from Lasi Goth, Malir, Karachi. On 29 August 2026, Irshad Baloch was forcibly disappeared from his home by the police and intelligence agencies.
On 30 August 2026, just one day after his enforced disappearance, his family received his dead body at Jinnah Hospital in Karachi. They were informed that Irshad had died from an electric shock.

On 1 July 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said that BLA freedom fighters had carried out 23 successful operations in different areas of occupied Balochistan over the previous ten days. These attacks targeted the occupying forces and exploitative companies, while operations were also conducted against vehicles belonging to exploitative entities as part of the economic blockade on major highways. In these attacks, 16 personnel of the occupying army were killed and several others were injured. Meanwhile, four valiant BLA sarmachars - Raziq Baloch, alias Jahanzaib; Israr Baloch, alias Kohzad; Haji Khalil Shahwani, alias Mama Marjan; and Anwar Bilsum, alias Dr Aziz - were martyred while defending the motherland during intense clashes at various locations.

Israr Baloch, alias Kohzad, son of Haji Amanullah Essazai, was a resident of Zek, Bisama. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in 2024 and served on the Bolan and Quetta fronts. He was martyred on 28 June 2026 in Kambela Dasht.
Driven by a commitment to defend his homeland, Sangat Israr Baloch joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2024. Along with his ideological and political commitment, he was known in the field as a brave, fearless, and effective Sarmachar. He was among those fellow Sarmachars who were always in pursuit of the occupying forces. During his two years of national service, he carried out his responsibilities in accordance with the directives of the organization's command, demonstrating bravery, courage, and unwavering determination throughout.
Before serving on the Quetta and Dasht fronts, he remained active on the Bolan front for a considerable period, where he took part in several major and deadly attacks against the enemy. Later, acting on the directives of the organization, he joined his fellow Sarmachars in carrying out important military operations against the enemy in the Quetta and Dasht regions. Together, they disrupted the army's supply routes and repelled its advances in the region. He fulfilled his professional and revolutionary responsibilities until his final days and, alongside his fellow Sarmachars, turned the areas surrounding Quetta into no-go zones for the enemy.
In his final battle, he inflicted heavy casualties on the enemy and was martyred during the fighting. The sacrifices made by Martyr Israr for the collective cause will forever remain a part of the pages of Baloch history and will stand as an example for future generations of how bravely and courageously the Baloch people fought against the enemy.

On 20 October 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that Sarmachars (freedom fighters) of the BLA had carried out 34 high-intensity military operations over 12 days across various regions of Balochistan between 9 and 20 October 2026. In these attacks, 14 personnel of the occupying army and nine operatives of Military Intelligence and death squads were killed, while operational control and snap-checking on key highways continued successfully under the organisational policy of an “economic blockade.”

During these operations, the freedom fighters also captured a serving soldier of the Pakistani army. In face-to-face clashes with occupying forces on various fronts, six BLA fighters fought courageously and attained the highest status of martyrdom.

Amanullah Mengal, alias Meerak, who was severely injured in a quadcopter attack by the occupying army at Ziarat Cross, succumbed to his injuries and was martyred on 8 August 2026.

On 18 September 2026, intense clashes took place between the occupying Pakistani army and BLA fighters at Siah Chang in Chagai, resulting in the deaths and injuries of several occupying army personnel, while the brave BLA fighter Ishaq Shokat Baloch, alias Meeran Baloch, attained martyrdom while fighting courageously.

On 19 September 2026, a prolonged and bloody confrontation took place between the occupying Pakistani army and BLA fighters at Paroom in Panjgur. During these clashes, four personnel of the occupying army were killed, several were injured, and one military vehicle was destroyed. In this battle, four BLA fighters - Ali Baloch, alias Salman Baloch; Ikhtiyar Baloch, alias Fareed Baloch; Sanaullah Baloch, alias Shay Mureed; and Sohail Baloch, alias Haji Absar - fought heroically and attained the highest status of martyrdom.

Sanaullah Baloch, alias Shay Mureed, son of Hair Mohammad, was a resident of the Gomazi area of Panjgur. He joined the BLA on 25 October 2025 and served on the Paroom, Panjgur, and Mashkeel fronts. He was promoted to Patrol Commander and was martyred on 19 September 2026 in the Paroom area of Balochistan.

Sanaullah Baloch, who was deployed on the war front in Paroom, joined the Baloch Liberation Army last October. He decided to join the organization with the intention of playing his part in the struggle to end the occupation imposed by force on Baloch land and homeland. Guided by this conviction, he carried out his duties in the war zone in the cause of national liberation. After completing basic training courses, he took part in operations against the enemy on various fronts. He carried out various activities in Panjgur and Mashkel, and later in Paroom, in accordance with the organizational command’s directives.

Sanaullah was among those who demonstrated bravery and valor on the battlefield and confronted the enemy. He took part in various economic and strategic blockades against the enemy and in numerous operations that restricted the enemy’s movement. In recognition of his discipline and combat skills in carrying out his duties, he was entrusted with patrol command responsibilities in the Paroom region, which he fulfilled with dedication until his final moments. On September 19, 2026, he lost his life on the battlefield in the cause of national freedom and the defense of his homeland, immortalizing his name in the annals of national liberation.

Shaheed Sameer Barkat Baloch was from Dasht Balnigor, Jatani Bazar, District Kech. Shaheed Sameer, along with his wife Hani Gul, was visiting their relatives in Sistan, Balochistan. On August 8, 2023, a group of militant men broke into their house and kidnapped both the husband and wife. After ten days of abduction, on August 19, 2023, the tortured and mutilated bodies of both were found on the roadside in villages between Sarawan and Khash in Gusht, Sistan, Balochistan. They were martyred in a very painful manner.

On 21 January 2026 in the Tump Koshkalat area of Turbat district Balochistan, armed groups backed by Pakistani forces locally known as death squad opened fire and killed a 21 year old, Tahir Baloch, son of Mulla Nisar.

On April 15, 2025, a statement issued by Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS) claimed that BRAS freedom fighters killed 22 personnel of the occupying Pakistani Army in attacks in Noshki and Barkhan (Chamalang). During these operations, the freedom fighters captured the main camp of the occupying army. In the ensuing clashes, the enemy forces were forced to retreat, and five BRAS freedom fighters were martyred while fighting the Pakistani Army.
On April 9, 2025, the occupying Pakistani Army attempted to advance on a side camp of Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS) freedom fighters after conducting a drone attack at Dadar in the Chamalang area of Barkhan.
Among the comrades martyred in Chamalang was Aaqil Hashmi, alias Chirag, also known as Professor, son of Hashim, from the Shahrak area of Kech. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in 2020 and fought against national oppression. Earlier, he had been a member of the Baloch Students Organization, where he educated and equipped Baloch youth with ideas of national liberation.
Sangat Aaqil, alias Chirag, who served on the fronts of Bolan, Barkhan, Chamalang, and Koh-e-Sulaiman, had completed his M.Phil in Political Science from the International Islamic University (IIUI), Islamabad.
Martyr Sangat Aaqil, alias Professor Chirag, was serving as the unit commander of the Fatah Squad, a special unit of the BLA. He was not only an outstanding guerrilla fighter but also a source of guidance, from whose intelligence and experience other fighters greatly benefited.
Another comrade martyred in Chamalang was Ghulam Raza, alias Kabeer, son of Ali Gul, from Holangi Tank in the Raskoh area of Kharan. Having grown up in the foothills of Raskoh, Ghulam Raza joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in 2022 and fought against national oppression as an urban guerrilla. A year later, he moved to the Barkhan front.
Armed with the consciousness of national liberation, Martyr Sangat Raza was a hardworking and kind-hearted comrade. He inflicted heavy blows on the enemy in numerous battles on the Barkhan front.
The third comrade martyred in Chamalang was Mohsin, alias Durra, son of Mayar, from the Gulshanabad area of Turbat. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2023 and initially served as an urban guerrilla. After striking the enemy army in Turbat city and its surrounding areas for a year, he moved to the mountain front in 2024.
Sangat Mohsin served against national oppression on the Barkhan front. He had the ability to make critical decisions in extremely difficult situations — a quality he demonstrated by shooting himself with the “last bullet” in the throat rather than being captured alive by the enemy.

In 1838, the British sent a force led by Alexander Burnes to reinstate Shah Shuja Durrani as the king of Afghanistan by deposing Amir Dost Mohammad Khan. To reach Afghanistan, they needed passage through Balochistan, particularly the Bolan Pass. However, Khan Mehrab Khan refused to allow the British to use his land to attack a neighboring country. The British sent Lieutenant Leach to negotiate with the Baloch government, but the Khan stood firm. When British forces reached Shaal via Bolan, some patriotic Baloch, without the Khan’s knowledge, attacked British troops out of nationalist sentiment and a desire to protect their homeland.
After toppling Amir Dost Mohammad Khan, the British Governor General of India, Lord Auckland, ordered an attack on Balochistan. In 1839, around 7,000 British troops marched from Shaal to attack the Baloch Meeri (capital). Anticipating an invasion, Khan Mehrab Khan declared war and sent messages to tribal leaders, but many saw the British as allies rather than invaders and chose to collaborate with them rather than defend their land. When Khan Mehrab Khan gathered his resistance fighters, the number of loyal warriors had dwindled to only 700 due to the short sightedness of many tribal chiefs. Nevertheless, Mehrab Khan was determined to fight. At his court, a respected figure, Akhund Muhammad Siddiq, advised him that he was not in a position to wage war at that time. He suggested that the Khan should leave Kalat with his companions, regroup and strengthen his forces, and then launch an attack against the British when the time was right, on 13 November 1839, the British forces launched an attack on Kalat, and a fierce battle ensued. During the fighting, Khan Mehrab Khan Baloch was martyred by a British bullet.

Among those martyred alongside him were:

Diwan Bacha Mal, Minister of Finance

Diwan Khem Chand

Diwan Asardas Mukhi, from the Hindu Panchayat of Kalat

Abdul Karim Raisani, brother of Sardar Asad Khan Raisani

Sardar Wali Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (maternal uncle of Martyr Amir Mehrab Khan)

Mir Taj Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (cousin of Mehrab Khan)

Mir Muhammad Ali Shahizai Mengal

Mir Fazal Muhammad Lehri, brother of Sardar Muhammad Khan Lehri

Sardar Zaman Khan Pandrani

Mir Dad Karim Chandozai Shahwani

Mir Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Mir Badal Khan, brother of Sardar Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Khan Muhammad Dehwaar, Arbab-e-Kalat.

Mir Nabi Bakhsh Jatoi, from the Narmak region of Kalat

Mir Qaiser Khan Bizenjo

Mir Shah Dost Bizenjo

Muhammad Raza Waziri Khel

Noor Muhammad Shahizai, son of Polat Sagaar Sarmastani, in charge of the armory

Taj Muhammad Shagasi
Noor Ahmad Baloch is a victim of the Pakistani state’s kill-and-dump policy.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). Zafar Nichari alias Muslim, son of Ali Nawaz was resident of Gazg, Kalat, he joined the BLA on April 14, 2025 and Martyred during Operation Herof Phase 2, in Noshki Front.
Zafar Nichari, known by the code name Muslim, hailed from the resilient land of Gazg in Kalat. He was among those valiant sarmachars who refused to accept national subjugation as destiny, choosing instead the path of armed resistance. Since joining the organization on April 14, 2025, Zafar demonstrated through his character and actions that when a conscious individual embraces the liberation of his nation as his life's purpose, no fear of death can falter his steps. His unwavering commitment and organizational discipline quickly established him as a dedicated soldier of the movement.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, as coordinated strikes were launched against the occupying forces across the motherland, Zafar Nichari stood at the vanguard of the Nushki front. In the intense tactical clashes at the strategic front of Nushki, he fought with exceptional courage, inflicting significant losses upon the enemy forces. Amidst this fierce battle, while maintaining steadfast resistance, he sacrificed his life for the cause of freedom. His martyrdom remains a beacon of light for the Baloch national liberation movement and an inspiration for generations to come.

Khair Baksh son of Hasil Baloch resident of Seetakan, Jhaoo . He was a political activist and he joined the Baloch National Movement in 2008. He played a great role to mobilize the public about Baloch liberation movement. Last time, Nako was serving as regional leader and president of the BNM Awaran region. He was abducted by Pakistani forces on 27th October 2011 from Bela area of Lasbela and his bulleted dead body was dumped on 27th November 2011 in same area.

Allah Noor Jamaldini, alias Rokein, and his brother Asif Jamaldini, alias Zubair, sons of Peer Bakhsh Jamaldini, were residents of the Qazi Abad area of Noshki. They joined the Baloch liberation movement in March 2023 and October 2024. They became part of the BLA Frontline in July 2024 and 2025, subsequently joining the Majeed Brigade in August 2024 and the Fateh Squad. Both brothers were martyred in Operation Herof on the Noshki Front.
The rugged valleys and scorching deserts of Balochistan are not merely witnesses to deprivation; they are cradles of resistant thought, where the dream of liberation is nurtured across generations. The life story of these two brothers from Qazi Abad, Noshki - Allah Noor and Asif Jamaldini - is not just a tale of familial sacrifice. It represents the pinnacle of a political and philosophical revolution that has permeated the very soul of modern Baloch youth.
Allah Noor Jamaldini, known in the resistance ranks as "Rokein," possessed intellectual and political foresight far removed from superficial emotionalism. He formally joined the Baloch national movement in March 2023. When he took to the mountain front in July 2024, it was the practical manifestation of a thinker on the battlefield. Allah Noor understood that in the struggle for national survival, the fear of death is dwarfed by the reality of a life in bondage. Driven by this conviction, he joined the Majeed Brigade in August 2024.

On 8 August 2016, terrorists attacked the Government Hospital in Quetta, Balochistan, in a suicide bombing and shooting. More than 70 people were killed, mainly lawyers, and more than 130 others were injured.
The majority of those killed were lawyers who had gathered at the hospital after the body of Advocate Bilal Anwar Kasi, president of the Balochistan Bar Association, was brought there. Kasi had been shot dead by a gunman near Mengal Chowk on Manno Jan Road in Quetta while he was leaving his home for his office.
Responsibility for the attack was claimed by various Islamist groups, including Jamaat-ul-Ahrar and the Islamic State Khorasan Province. However, nationalist groups have alleged that these extremist organisations are backed by the Pakistani state and its military to counter the nationalist movement in the region and exploit its natural resources.
Estimates of the death toll ranged between 70 people, while more than 120 were injured. Of those killed, 54 were lawyers. Among them, 15 were Baloch by ethnicity, while the majority were Pashtuns by ethnicity.

The Baloch advocates or lawyers who were killed are identified as follows:

01 Ghulam Farooq Badini, son of Haji Abdul Ghani.
02 Bashir Ahmed Qazi, son of Qazi Ahmed Jan.
03 Bashir Ahmad Zehri, son Haji Mir Ahmed Zehri.
04 Naseer Ahmed Langove, son Abdul Rahim.
05 Chakar Khan Rind, son of Mehmood.
06 Abdul Rashid, son of Abdul Latif.
07 Nooruddin Rakshani, son Haji Naseeruddin.
08 Muhammad Imran, son Ghulam Farooq.
09 Munir Ahmed Mengal, son Ghulam Murtaza.
10 Sangat Jehan Jamaldini, son of Dr. Jahanzaib.
11 Mohammad Ali Satakzai, son of Taj Mohammad Khan.
12 Mehmood Ahmed Lehri, son Haji Abdul Hameed.
13 Jamil Ur Rehman, son of Qazi Abdul Hameed.
14 Amanullah Langove, son of Haji Dad Karim.
15 Sabir Ali, son of Abdul Rasheed.

Mohammad Ali Satakzai, 45, was a session judge in Quetta.

The fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front’s special unit, the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB), attacked the Brigade Headquarters in the Nokundi area of Chagai, Balochistan, at around 8:19 PM on the night of November 30, 2025. SOB fighters successfully entered the offices and residential compound of foreign employees of the Saindak and Reko Diq projects, located in the centre of the camp, and managed to take several foreigners present in the compound hostage. The Pakistani army deployed its air force, SSG commandos, and modern heavy weapons against the fighters, but the brave Sarmachars of SOB repelled every attempt and forced them to retreat. During the operation, the Balochistan Liberation Front offered the Pakistani side an opportunity to negotiate on its demands; however, 18 hours after the offer, the Pakistani army chose to use force and began directly targeting the compound with artillery and aerial attacks. This resulted in intense clashes between the occupying forces and the fighters, which continued until the martyrdom of the SOB fighters.
In this special operation by the Saddo Operational Battalion, 76 military personnel, including foreign hostages, were killed, and 6 SOB fighters embraced martyrdom. The Nokundi operation by SOB was a continuation of the BLF’s long-standing armed resistance strategy for the independence of Balochistan and the protection of its natural wealth.
Among the martyrs were:
1 Asif alias Khalid Baloch, son of Mulla Ghulam Jan.
2 Inayat Sahil alias Gwahram Baloch, son of Ishaq Baloch.
3 Zareena Rafiq alias Tranag Maho, daughter of Master Rafiq Ahmed.
4 Nabeel Ahmed alias Ustad Adil Baloch, son of Haji Muhammad Ishaq.
5 Meer Jan Meeral alias Janan Baloch, son of Muhammad Raheem Baloch.
6 Ghulam Jan alias Istaal Baloch, son of Faiz Muhammad.
Nabeel Ahmed alias Ustad Adil Baloch, son of Haji Muhammad Ishaq, resident of Sand-a-Sar Essai, Panjgur, joined the Baloch National struggle in 2020 and gave his services for Saddo Operational Battalion in 2024 . Nabeel Ahmed alias Ustad Adil demonstrated his bravery and exceptional military skills in the Battle of Nokundi and was martyred on December 2 while inflicting severe blows to enemy forces.

data.biography:
On 1 September 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that, during intense fighting with the occupying forces at Dasht Goran in Chaghi, twenty personnel, including a captain, were killed and several others were wounded. Two BLA fighters were also killed while fighting for their homeland.
He stated that on 31 August 2026, the BLA began a blockade and conducted snap-checking at Nadirabad in Dasht Goran, Chagi, at around 6:00 p.m. During this, a convoy consisting of eight vehicles belonging to Pakistan's forces arrived at the location. They were also assisted by elements of the area's death squads.
Under a wartime strategy, BLA fighters took up positions and launched intense attacks against the enemy. The fighters continued to attack the Pakistani forces. During the fighting, four enemy vehicles came within their encirclement, causing severe damage, and all personnel aboard them were killed. The use of rockets and other modern weapons left the enemy with no opportunity to escape. BLA fighters targeted one of the enemy vehicles with a rocket and completely destroyed it, resulting in further casualties.
The vehicle was later lifted and taken away by a crane. Despite being greater in number, the enemy was unable to withstand the BLA fighters. This effective counter-operation by the BLA delivered a major response to the Pakistani forces. Among the twenty personnel of the occupying Pakistani Army killed in the attack was Captain Ubaid (147/LC, formerly 69/PR, 60/W). It has remained the practice of the Pakistani Army to conceal the actual number of its killed and wounded soldiers and officers. In this battle as well, it concealed the number of its killed and wounded personnel, as well as its logistical losses.
In this battle at Dasht Goran, Chagi, two BLA fighters, Nasir, alias Baba, and Bashir Ahmad, alias Shaukat, sacrificed their lives for Balochistan and made history through their courage and bravery. Despite being surrounded by the enemy, they demonstrated exceptional military skill, strategy, and bravery, inflicting heavy losses on hundreds of personnel of the occupying forces. The battle continued intermittently from 6:30 p.m. until 4:00 a.m., during which the enemy suffered what was described as a historic defeat. The enemy remained engaged until late at night in removing its destroyed vehicles and wounded personnel from the area. Local residents witnessed dozens of ambulances removing the bodies of the dead from the site. During the battle, the occupying Pakistani forces also had the assistance of drones.
Nasir Baloch, alias Baba, belonged to Dasht Goran, Chagi, in the Manguchar area of Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2014. He was an extremely brave and hardworking fighter who possessed exceptional battlefield skills. During his twelve-year struggle, he played a key role in several important and decisive battles in the areas of Shor Parod, Nagaho, Chaghai, and Dalbandin. His name will always be written in golden words for his actions against the enemy.
Bashir Ahmad, alias Shaukat, belonged to Gazg in Kalat District. He began his national responsibilities through the BLA platform in 2015. He also struck heavy blows against the enemy in areas of Balochistan, including Narmak, Nagaho, Chaghai, Saroon, and Shor Parod, among others, and remained a frontline participant in Baloch fighters' operations. His bravery, strategy, and unparalleled spirit of sacrifice for the homeland serve as a guiding light for Baloch youth.

According to a statement issued on 27 January 2026 by Mureed Baloch, spokesperson of the Baloch Nationalist Army, fighters of the Baloch Nationalist Army were traveling on 24 January 2026 in connection with organizational duties in the Hothabad area of Kech district. At around 3:00 PM, at a location known as Rodaan Kour in Hothabad, they encountered operatives of a death squad formed by the Pakistani army. The death squad operatives had already been covertly positioned along the fighters’ route.
A clash ensued between the fighters and the death squad operatives. Following an organized guerrilla strategy, the fighters promptly took defensive positions. They not only protected themselves from major losses caused by the enemy’s attack but also inflicted damage on the enemy in a counteroffensive.
During the clash, the Deputy Camp Commander of the Baloch Nationalist Army, Sajjad Baloch, alias Mureed Jan, played a crucial role in safely evacuating his fellow fighters and continued fighting until his last breath, ultimately attaining martyrdom.
Sajad Baloch, alias Mureed Jan, son of Nabi Bakhsh, was a resident of the Talokan area of Tump, Zamuran Bazaar. He joined the Baloch Nationalist Army on 25 June 2024.
Previously, he had also been forcibly disappeared by the Pakistani army, during which he endured severe and inhumane torture in the enemy’s torture cells.

Abdul Rehman Baloch, alias Khalil, son of Raheem Jan and a resident of Tasp, Panjgur District, Balochistan, joined the BLA in January 2026 and served on the Panjgur front. He was martyred on 3 June 2026 in the Chedagi area of Panjgur District, Balochistan.
Abdul Rehman, alias Khalil Jan, joined the BLA earlier this year and, in accordance with organizational directives, assumed his responsibilities on the Panjgur front. He was ideologically committed and carried out his military duties with seriousness, sincerity, and dedication. The core qualities of a conscious and steadfast Sarmachar were an integral part of his character. During his six months of service in the field, he fulfilled his responsibilities with comradeship, devotion, and integrity, earning recognition among his fellow Sarmachars as a steadfast and reliable companion.
Fully aware of the artificial strength of the occupying force, Khalil Baloch participated in numerous engagements on the armed front and inflicted significant losses on the enemy. He upheld the evolving culture of resistance shaped by the sacrifices of Baloch martyrs, striving to embody the principles they established. This sense of commitment and ideological conviction kept him steadfast on the front lines until his final moments. Despite facing numerous challenges and harsh conditions on the battlefield, his morale and courage remained as high and resolute as the mountains of Sayaji. He embraced martyrdom while fighting the enemy and, until his last breath, remained a firm barrier to enemy advances.
His bravery, courage, and capability, together with his determination to confront the enemy, have secured his place among the martyrs of the Baloch homeland. He will be remembered in history as a brave Sarmachar and a guardian of national defense.

On 21 May 2025 fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) began patrolling the Gardank area of Buleda after receiving reports of suspicious movement by the security forces and a so called local death squad. In the evening, at a place known as “Balo Koi Gaz” the fighters encountered enemy agents, which led to an intense armed clash.
The clash lasted for nearly an hour, during which the security forces and their local collaborators suffered casualties. In the same encounter, two Baloch Liberation Army fighters, Jabir Naseer and Faqeer Jan, were killed.
Jabir Naseer, alias Sameer, son of Naseer, belonged to the Zirdan area of Buleda. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2020 and initially served as an urban guerrilla. In 2021, he moved to the mountainous front, where he played a significant role in various regions.
Faqeer Jan, alias Mir Jan, son of Ghulam Rasool, belonged to the Gerdank area of Buleda. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2022 and quickly emerged as an effective member of the organization due to his maturity, sincerity and dedication. He served on the fronts of Turbat, Buledah, Zamuran, Herronk, and Sami. Faqeer Jan was known as a principled, steadfast and ideologically motivated young man.
Shaheed Javed Akhtar Baloch was shot and killed by Pakistani forces during a protest on 4 September 2006.

On 3 October 2026, Pakistani forces carried out an aerial bombing using a quadcopter drone targeting civilians in Fateh Ali Bazaar, Gwargo, in Panjgur district of Balochistan.

The attack resulted in the martyrdom of two children: 9 year old Arman Anwar, son of Anwar and 10 year old Amal Salim, son of Salim Jan.

Three other children were injured: 9 year old Shahid, 7 year old Zahid, son of Shahid and 12 year old Noorullah, son of Rafiq.
data.martyrdomPlace: Fatah Ali Bazar, Gwargo, Panjgur district, Balochistan

data.biography: Ali Jan Kurd, son of Bijjar Khan, a 36 year old resident of Mach, Bolan, was a leader of the Baloch Students Organization - Azad (BSO-Azad). He was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 12 November 2010 by Pakistani forces. After months of enforced disappearance, his body was dumped on 22 January 2011 on Qambrani Road, Quetta.

On 19 April 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson, Gwahram Baloch, announced the martyrdom of six fighters of the organization, paid tribute to them, and stated that the organization’s fighters were martyred in the national war of liberation. The martyrs include Ikram Baloch (alias Hameed), Shaibaz Shohaz (alias Kiyya), Masood Baloch (alias Bharag), Salman Waheeda (alias Chirag), Izzat Baloch (alias Jummi), and Hamza Baloch (alias Waheed).
The spokesperson further stated that the martyred fighters fulfilled their oath and national duty of defending the nation and homeland to the last drop of their blood, sacrificing their lives and achieving immortality. The martyrs proved through their great sacrifices that Baloch sarmachars do not hesitate to make any sacrifice in the defense of the nation and homeland.
Shaibaz Shohaz, alias Kiyya, son of Abdul Majeed, was a resident of Gharib Abad and originally hailed from Gar, Panjgur. He joined the BLF in 2020 and embarked on his national struggle. For the first three years, he served as an urban guerrilla responsible for managing the urban network.
Living among the enemy for three years, he inflicted heavy blows on the enemy with exceptional guerrilla skills. In 2023, he transferred to the mountain front, where he was entrusted with both combat and administrative responsibilities. As a camp commander, he carried out his duties with courage, resilience, and dedication until his martyrdom.
He was not only a skilled guerrilla commander but also a poet of the Balochi language. Shaibaz was martyred on April 15, 2026, at the hands of an enemy agent in a cowardly and treacherous plot by the occupying forces.

On May 29, 2025, Abdul Aziz, son of Noor Muhammad and a resident of Gushang in Awaran district, was summoned by Frontier Corps (FC) personnel to report to the Malar Army Camp. While travelling to the camp, he was intercepted and shot dead by members of a state-backed death squad in the Cheel area.
In Awaran, several similar cases have been reported in which Baloch civilians summoned to military camps are later found dead. In other instances, state-backed death squads target these individuals en route or after their release, further entrenching a climate of fear and impunity across the region.
