During Operation Herof Phase 2, the BLA’s Majeed Brigade Fidayeen targeted the main camp and the Coast Guard camp of the Pakistan Navy in the coastal city of Pasni, Balochistan. The operation was initiated by Fazal, alias Miraan, who rammed a vehicle loaded with explosives into the main entrance gate of the Navy camp. The explosion instantly killed at least seven personnel stationed at the gate.
Immediately after this initial attack, six Fidayeen - Yasma Baloch, alias Zareena; Waseem Baloch, alias Zirbaar; Zaid Zamurani, alias Abram; Sabzal Baloch, alias Kohsar; Diljan Baloch, alias Ameer Ajoo; and Operation Commander Shabeer Baloch, alias Kiya - entered the camp and took up positions. Fierce clashes with the occupying Navy and Navy special units inside the camp continued for more than five hours, during which at least 33 Pakistani personnel were killed. This operation not only inflicted significant casualties on the enemy but also dealt a severe blow to the defense structure of the Navy camp.
Yasma Baloch aka Zareena, and Waseem Baloch aka Zirbar, were husband and wife from Alandoor, Buleda, and Kallahdar, Zamuran.
Yasma Baloch, born on 14 February 1997 in Alandoor, Buleda, joined the Baloch Liberation Army’s Majeed Brigade in 2022.
Waseem Baloch, born on 27 April 1992 in Kallahdar, Zamuran, became active in the movement in 2014 and joined the Majeed Brigade in 2022.
They shared a marriage before they shared a final stand. Yasma Baloch and Waseem Baloch, husband and wife, sacrificed their lives together while attacking the occupying forces' camp in Pasni. Their story is not only about death, but about how private life and national duty fully converged, turning a partnership into a symbol of shared commitment and resistance. Two individuals bound by partnership and a shared decision to give everything for what they believed the freedom of their motherland demanded.

On 28 June 2026, the spokesperson for the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) issued a statement announcing that five fighters of the organisation - Shoaib Zehri, alias Farooq; Zakariya Zehri, alias Ustad Zoreen Baloch; Kifayatullah Badini, alias Badil Baloch; Captain Hashum Baloch, alias Kambar; and Abdul Rahim, alias Ustad Imran - had embraced martyrdom. The statement said that the blood of the martyrs guarantees Baloch national survival and sovereignty.

Abdul Rahim, also known as Ustad Imran, son of Mohammad Umar and a resident of Minaz, Buleda, was martyred on June 21, 2026, in an occupying army drone strike on Garuk Road between Buleda and Turbat, alongside his commander, Captain Hashum.
Abdul Rahim began his struggle in September 2024 under the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front. Before formally joining the mountain front, he served in the urban and regional network for six months, where he played a key role in ideological and political activities. After fulfilling his organizational responsibilities, he formally transferred to the mountain front.
He held a distinguished position within the organization because of his exceptional ideological and military capabilities. He had extensive experience in guerrilla warfare on difficult fronts such as Buleida, Zamuran, Paroom, and Balgatar, and he always remained active in the field.

On January 15, 2026, during close-quarters combat in the Battle of Kharan, four fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front - Mubeen, alias Mulla Rahmin; Abdul Raziq Baloch, alias Barag Jan; Hafeez Baloch, alias Yasir; and Mohsin Baloch, alias Mureed - laid down their lives for the homeland. 
Hafeez Baloch, alias Yasir, son of Kaka Pir Jan, from Haroni, Mashkay, joined the Balochistan Liberation Front one year ago in the struggle for Balochistan's independence. His family has been deeply committed to the national liberation movement and has endured severe persecution at the hands of the occupying state apparatus over the past decade, including forced displacement. Rather than abandoning the cause of national independence, they have remained steadfastly aligned with the BLF, with renewed strength and organization. Martyr Yasir Jan played a significant combat role in the Battle of Kharan, volunteering for the Qurban Unit to defend his comrades and ensure the operation's success. He remained on the front lines throughout and was martyred by enemy fire while seizing enemy weapons during close combat with occupying forces in Kharan Kalan.

On 1 November 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson, Gwahram Baloch, issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of eight of the organisation’s fighters: Captain Yahya, alias Ustad Khalid Jan; Aris Baloch, alias Omar Jan; Hafeez Baloch, alias Karwan, son of Dad Mohammad; Javid Baloch, alias Gulab, son of Bori Baloch; Abdul Khaliq, alias Nothak; Sajid Baloch, alias Mehran; Hameed Baloch, alias Buzerg; and Akram Baloch, alias Gwahram.

The statement paid tribute to these brave and ideologically committed members of the organisation, who embraced martyrdom while engaging in clashes with the Pakistani army and its death squads on various fronts across Balochistan.

Martyr Abdul Khaliq, alias Nothak began the armed struggle for Baloch national freedom through the BLF platform in 2023. Before enduring the hardships of the mountain front, he spent a year within the urban network performing very important organizational and national duties with great secrecy, iron resolve and excellent professional skill. His understanding of the demands of urban guerrilla warfare was eloquently demonstrated by the organizational network he established within the reach of the enemy's informers and intelligence apparatus, providing compelling evidence of his intellectual maturity and strategic insight.

After successfully carrying out his valuable urban front service, when he moved to the mountain front, the difficult, rugged and strategic fronts of Parom, Zamuran, Balgatar, Buleda, Panjgur and Mashkel bore witness to his courage. Members join the BLF's vanguard Qurban unit by their own will and spirit of bravery, and Shaheed Abdul Khaliq too became part of this front-rank unit and wrote guerrilla war history. He faced the enemy on the front line in every battle. His military life is a story of hard work, dedication, night watches, patrols, perseverance and ambushes against the enemy, which serves as a practical lesson for young sarmachars. He gave up his personal desires, dreams, rest and comfort and devoted himself entirely to the BLF, its revolutionary organizational goals and the freedom of the oppressed Baloch nation.

He belonged to a fearless, proud family of everlasting sacrifice, which has lit every lamp of its house for the motherland's freedom. Several other members of his family have written history by offering their blood on the path of the freedom movement. His own brother, Shaheed Nasir Sanjar alias Ramin, followed the same sacred path and has already been sacrificed for the motherland. Shaheed Abdul Khaliq made this great family legacy even brighter, writing it in the ink of his own blood. His attitude toward friends and sangats was always gentle, courteous and encouraging. He shared in the joys and sorrows of every sarmachar and stood shoulder to shoulder with them on the battlefield like a shield. When the battle against the enemy heated up on the strategic Mashkel front, this fearless sarmachar of the Qurban unit fought the enemy hard on the front line, set an everlasting example of resolve and steadfastness, embraced martyrdom and became immortal in history.

On 31 December 2025, a statement released by the spokesperson of the Balochistan Liberation Front, Major Gwahram Baloch, stated that five of its fighters embraced martyrdom and sacrificed their lives for the homeland in an enemy drone strike in Kalat on 25 December 2025.
The martyrs include Abdul Ahad Dehwar alias Gazzain, son of Hamayun Dehwar, resident of Keli Kahriz Mastung; Israr Ahmad alias Ibrar, son of Hussain, resident of Gargina Mastung; Shoaib Ahmad alias Subedar, son of Muhammad Ali, resident of Jiwa Khuzdar; Obaidullah Siyahpad alias Sabzu, son of Peerjan, resident of Kharan; and Faisal Badini alias Qazi, son of Muhammad Ibrahim, resident of Kharan.
Faisal Badini alias Qazi, son of Mohammad Ibrahim and resident of Kharan, joined the Balochistan Liberation Front two years ago for national sovereignty. Initially, he remained associated with the organization’s intelligence wing. Due to his activities, he came under the surveillance of the occupying enemy’s intelligence agencies, as a result of which the organization shifted him to the camp. During this short period, he remained active in organizational activities and was martyred in the drone strike on 25 December 2025.

On March 2, 2025 Mahikan Baloch of the Majeed Brigade carried out an attack on the convoy of the FC Wing Commander in Kalat. In this attack, the Wing Commander including several personnel were killed. Mahikan Baloch belonged to Gwadar city of Balochistan. She voluntarily joined the Majeed Brigade four years ago. She was a freedom fighter of exceptional mental strength. Over these four years, the organization not only gave her complete freedom to reconsider her decision but also subjected her to special tests from time to time to determine whether her decision was driven by emotion or consciousness. As time passed, responsibles of Majeed Brigade came to know that her decisions was firm from the very begining. Mahikan Baloch was an educated freedom fighter with a deep command over Baloch history and literature. Her passion and love for the Baloch nation, language, and land cannot be expressed in words.

On 9 October 2025, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) received complaints from local residents in Gorki, Mangochar, in the Kalat District of Balochistan, stating that Shakir, the head of a local death squad, was collecting extortion money and taxes from vehicles in the area and harassing people without cause. Acting on these complaints, BLA fighters went to meet Shakir to discuss the matter. Upon their arrival, they detained two of Shakir’s men and asked that Shakir be called. At that point, women from Shakir’s house came out and placed the Qur’an before the fighters, pleading for the release of the detained men. The BLA members reassured them that they had come only to speak with Shakir and warn him not to trouble the local people.
When Shakir arrived, the fighters spoke with him, explaining that they had received complaints about his harassment of locals and his collection of illegal taxes from vehicles, and they urged him to stop such actions. After hearing this, Shakir claimed he would not repeat such behavior. However, as soon as the fighters departed, Shakir and his men opened fire on them.
As a result of the firing, four BLA comrades - Gul Khan alias Yaseen, Inayatullah alias Hafiz, Izzatullah alias Saeed, and Shah Murad alias Salam - were martyred. All four had joined the organization in 2023 and courageously fulfilled their national duties until the day of their martyrdom.

On 13th April 2026, in the Barkhan area of Balochistan, Pakistani forces shelled and bombed civilian populations, killing twelve innocent Baloch civilians, including women and children, and seriously injuring three others.

The martyrs are:

- Ali, son of Sultan Umair, aged 40
- Babul, daughter of Gulzar, aged 30
- Mir Jan, son of Ali, aged 2
- Somri, daughter of Bhangan, aged 35
- Balach, son of Sabzo, aged 70
- Shari, aged 22
- Rehman, son of Balach, aged 18
- Naikho, daughter of Jamalan, aged 17
- Allah Bakhsh, son of Balach, aged 6
- Saddo, daughter of Balach, aged 13
- Hapo, daughter of Balach, aged 8
- Mahrang, daughter of Balach, aged 2

The injured are:

- Zarbibi, daughter of Sher, aged 55
- Hazar Khan, son of Balach, aged 9
- Israr, daughter of Balach, aged 15

This is not the first time that Pakistani forces have bombed civilians in Balochistan, targeting unarmed and innocent women and children as a form of collective punishment. Nor can this be considered “collateral damage.” Rather, the Pakistani state and its forces are deliberately targeting the Baloch people to maintain an atmosphere of fear in the region, suppress internal dissent, exploit Baloch coastal resources, and continue policies of genocide against the Baloch nation.

Abdul Wahab, son of Abdul Hakeem and a resident of Paroom, Panjgur district of Balochistan, was forcibly disappeared by state-backed death squads in November 2025 and subsequently extrajudicially killed. Wahab, aged 33, came from a poor family and worked as a driver to support his household. After a full month of enforced disappearance, his bullet-riddled body was discovered on 4 December 2025 in the Pull Abad area of Panjgur.

Asim Baloch, son of Faqeer Muhammad and a resident of Nizarabad, Turbat District, was abducted on February 2, 2013, by Pakistani intelligence agencies from Tump. After months of enforced disappearance, his bullet-riddled body was recovered on May 26, 2013, inside the Nizarabad water supply compound.

On 11 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch announced the martyrdom of 14 fighters of the organization who attained martyrdom in confrontations with the Pakistani army and in airstrikes while defending their homeland, Balochistan, and fighting for national liberation and the right to self-determination.

On 13 August 2026, Pakistani Air Force fighter jets bombarded the Pandran area of Kalat District in Balochistan, resulting in the martyrdom of four members of the organization: Waseem Baloch, alias Farhan; Obaidullah Baloch, alias Shaheen; Nawaz Ali Baloch, alias Dilshad; and Mohammad Hassan, alias Ahmad.

On 25 August 2026, during an organizational mission in the Kech area of Balochistan, Sher Jan, alias Jamal, was shot from behind by a traitor, resulting in his martyrdom.

On 3 September 2026, while patrolling in the Mastung area of Balochistan, the organization’s brave fighters, Mohammad Younis, alias Salal; Sameer Ahmad, alias Zemal; Aziz Ahmad, alias Janan; and Sikandar Baloch, confronted Pakistani forces, targeted several enemy personnel, and embraced martyrdom.

On 14 September 2026, while engaging Pakistani forces and defending his fellow fighters in the Machani Kor Paroom area of Panjgur District, Babar Baloch, alias Kambar, embraced martyrdom.

On 18 September 2026, during a confrontation with Pakistani forces in the Chagi area of Balochistan, fighters of the organization, Riaz Baloch, alias Sabir; Taimoor Shah, alias Shaheen; Zia Ul Haq, alias Ziaullah; and Jumma Baloch, alias Commando, embraced martyrdom.

Jumma Baloch, alias Commando, son of Syed, resident of Chagi, joined the BLF in 2026. Performing his duties on the mountain front with exceptional resolve, in the 18 September 2026 battle he stayed in the front ranks, launched a fierce counterattack on the enemy, and was martyred showing great courage.

On 6 November 2026, the Baloch Liberation Army's media channel, Hakkal, published the biographies and details of six martyrs associated with the organization.

Among them, three fighters - Muneer Ahmad Jattak, alias Noora, son of Habib Khan Jattak; Shahzaib Bangulzai, alias Ehsan, son of Samiullah Bangulzai; and Fareed Langove, son of Ghulam Nabi Langove - were martyred on 20 October 2026 in the Rodinjo area of Kalat District.

Two other fighters, Parvez Ahmad Mohammad Hassni, alias Qadir, son of Shekari Mohammad Khan Mohammad Hassni, and Noman Jamaldini, alias Comrade Sameer, son of Agha Mohammad Jamaldini, were martyred on 24 October 2026 in the Gidar area of Surab.

The sixth fighter, Aurangzaib Langove, alias Asif, son of Hameedullah Langove, was martyred on 24 October 2026 in the Manguchar area of Kalat District.

Aurangzaib Langove, alias Asif, son of Hameedullah Langove, was a resident of Killi Rang Abad in the Manguchar area of Kalat. He joined the BLA's Urban Front in 2025, served on the Kalat front, and was martyred on 24 October 2026 in the Manguchar area of Kalat.

Aurangzaib Langove, viewing national freedom as the fundamental principle underlying Baloch national values and prosperity, began his struggle last year under the banner of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA). Following the organization's directives, he began participating in activities on the urban front and took part in urban guerrilla operations. Alongside his comrades, he participated in combat operations aimed at maintaining psychological pressure on the enemy. He carried out the BLA's urban guerrilla strategy with determination.

Martyr Aurangzaib chose armed resistance as a means of pursuing national liberation, guided by the philosophy that enemy personnel in Balochistan should be targeted in such a way that they would have no opportunity to remain in or escape the region. Through his guerrilla warfare tactics, he sought to achieve similar objectives and psychological effects. He also participated in armed activities on the Kalat front, playing his individual role in the struggle for his country's freedom. On 24 October 2026, he was martyred during clashes in the Manguchar area of Kalat, thereby securing his place in the pages of history.

Martyr Jalal Baloch alias Bramsh Baloch, son of Hassan Baloch and was a resident of Talmab, Mand area of Kech, Balochistan. He became part of Baloch liberation movement in the platform of Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) on May 6, 2021.
He embraced martyrdom in a drone attack of Pakistan’s military along with his seven comrades, Kareem Baloch, Mullah Bakhsh, Hazza Baloch,  Asif Baloch, Shezad Baloch, Talib Baloch, and Manzoor Baloch on Feb 23, 2023 in Mazanband area of Kech, Balochistan.

On 9 October 2025, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) received complaints from local residents in Gorki, Mangochar, in the Kalat District of Balochistan, stating that Shakir, the head of a local death squad, was collecting extortion money and taxes from vehicles in the area and harassing people without cause. Acting on these complaints, BLA fighters went to meet Shakir to discuss the matter. Upon their arrival, they detained two of Shakir’s men and asked that Shakir be called. At that point, women from Shakir’s house came out and placed the Qur’an before the fighters, pleading for the release of the detained men. The BLA members reassured them that they had come only to speak with Shakir and warn him not to trouble the local people.
When Shakir arrived, the fighters spoke with him, explaining that they had received complaints about his harassment of locals and his collection of illegal taxes from vehicles, and they urged him to stop such actions. After hearing this, Shakir claimed he would not repeat such behavior. However, as soon as the fighters departed, Shakir and his men opened fire on them.
As a result of the firing, four BLA comrades - Gul Khan alias Yaseen, Inayatullah alias Hafiz, Izzatullah alias Saeed, and Shah Murad alias Salam - were martyred. All four had joined the organization in 2023 and courageously fulfilled their national duties until the day of their martyrdom.

Ajaz Baloch, son of Deen Mohammad and a 27 year old shopkeeper by profession, was forcibly disappeared on 16 November 2025 from Dasht Kunchati by soldiers of the Pakistani Frontier Corps (FC). He was later brought to Turbat Civil Hospital in a critically injured condition, admitted in a halfconscious state and suffering from severe wounds resulting from extreme violence and brutal treatment during custody. On 19 November 2025, Ajaz succumbed to his injuries. His body bore clear signs of intense physical torture, indicating that he had been subjected to harsh custodial violence.

Mazar Baloch, son of Jamal Khan and a resident of Gorkai in Tehsil Mashkai, district Awaran, was extrajudicially killed by state-backed death squads on July 21, 2025.
Mazar had previously been forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces in 2015. During his five years of illegal detention, he endured inhumane torture at the hands of the Pakistani forces. He was released in 2020, but like many former detainees, remained under constant surveillance and harassment.
After his release, Mazar was frequently summoned to the central cantonment in Mashkai by the Pakistani army and intelligence agencies. On July 21, 2025, he was again asked to report to the FC headquarters. Following the visit, he was abducted and later found shot dead in Khandri, Mashkai, by state-backed death squads operating under the patronage of the Pakistani forces.

On January 15, 2026, during close-quarters combat in the Battle of Kharan, four fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front - Mubeen, alias Mulla Rahmin; Abdul Raziq Baloch, alias Barag Jan; Hafeez Baloch, alias Yasir; and Mohsin Baloch, alias Mureed - laid down their lives for the homeland. 
Abdul Raziq Baloch, alias Barag Jan, son of Nabi Bakhsh, from Raskoh, Kharan, joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in 2023. He was the nephew of Martyr Meeral, alias Nisar Jan. An educated and politically conscious youth, he had graduated from Uthal University. Martyr Barag was an active member of the BLF's Qurban Unit. During the Battle of Kharan, he commanded his squad as team leader in the red zone, inflicting heavy casualties on enemy forces. He fought with extraordinary courage and skill to ensure the success of the Kharan operation, ultimately achieving martyrdom.
data.fullName: Abdul Razaq Baloch, alias Barag Jan

data.biography:
On 12 August 2026, several Baloch people, including women and children, were killed and several others were injured as a result of an aerial bombardment of a civilian population by the Pakistan Air Force, reportedly using American-made F-16 fighter aircraft, in the Gidar Gindan area of Surab District, Balochistan. Following the airstrike, the injured and deceased were transported by police and local residents to DHQ Hospital in Surab, where the injured received medical treatment.

The families of the deceased and local residents subsequently began a protest by placing the bodies at Surab Main Chowk on the Quetta–Karachi National Highway (N-25). As a result, traffic on the highway was disrupted, with long queues of vehicles forming on both sides. Videos and photographs of the protest subsequently circulated widely on social media under the hashtag #SurabMassacre.

Those killed in the airstrike were identified as Shabir Ahmad Sumalani, son of Khudadad Sumalani, a resident of Marap, Surab; Noor Jan Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, a resident of Gindan; Karim Dad Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, a resident of Gandan; Raj Babu, wife of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani; Safia, wife of Noor Jan Mirwani; and Jalal Mirwani, son of Noor Jan Mirwani.

Those injured were identified as Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, son of Jan Muhammad Mirwani; Abdul Karim Mirwani, son of Jan Muhammad Mirwani; Mehrullah Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani; Nadeem Mirwani, son of Abdul Salam Mirwani; Shoaib Mirwani, son of Abdul Karim Mirwani; Sarah, wife of Baseer Ahmed Mirwani; Sabira, wife of Tufail Ahmed Mirwani; Zamra, daughter of Abdul Aziz Mirwani; Hajira, wife of Abdul Fattah Mirwani; Asim, son of Baseer, aged 1; Rahabia, daughter of Abdul Karim, aged 3; Sadia, daughter of Abdul Salam, aged 5; Fatima, daughter of Abdul Karim, aged 7; Zia-ur-Rehman, son of Abdul Karim, aged 2; Amir, son of Abdul Karim, aged 1; and Hasina, daughter of Muhammad Aslam, aged 4.

Following a detailed technical and scientific analysis of remnants of rocket components recovered from debris at the site of the aerial bombardment, important evidence reportedly emerged indicating that the recovered fragments belonged to an air-launched missile fired from an F-16 fighter aircraft.

Photographs of the recovered debris and the subsequent technical analysis reportedly indicated that the fragment was part of an AIM-120 Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile (AMRAAM), an American-made air-to-air missile.

Key technical evidence and serial numbers

According to the information and serial numbers reportedly engraved on the surface of the debris, the following details were recorded:

Assembly Number: ASSY 872128-1

Serial Number: 09-987138

Date of Manufacture: 09/09 (September 2009)

According to open-source intelligence (OSINT) records, the part number “872128-1” reportedly corresponds to the control section and rocket motor assembly of an AMRAAM missile manufactured by the American defense company Raytheon. Based on this evidence and the reported matching serial numbers, it is claimed that the debris was not part of an aircraft’s internal structure but instead consisted of remnants from an operational missile fired from an F-16 aircraft.

On April 15, 2025, a statement issued by Baloch Raaji Ajoi Sangar (BRAS) claimed that BRAS freedom fighters killed 22 personnel of the occupying Pakistani Army in attacks in Noshki and Barkhan (Chamalang). During these operations, the freedom fighters captured the main camp of the occupying army. In the ensuing clashes, the enemy forces were forced to retreat, and five BRAS freedom fighters were martyred while fighting the Pakistani Army.
On April 14, 2025, Baloch Raaji Ajoi Sangar targeted the main camp of the occupying Pakistani Army in the Galangor area of Noshki. The fighters first eliminated enemy personnel stationed at security posts in a sniper attack before launching a full-scale assault. The operation began at 9:30 p.m. and continued until 1:00 a.m., during which the freedom fighters took control of a large part of the camp.
A total of 17 personnel of the occupying Pakistani Army were killed and several others injured in the attack, while the fighters seized weapons and ammunition belonging to the enemy forces. During the final clearance of the main camp, two BRAS freedom fighters, Sangat Nazar Jan and Sangat Rauf, were martyred in clashes with the enemy army.
Martyr Sangat Meeran, alias Nazar Jan, son of Ustad Syed, was martyred in the battle in the Galangor area of Noshki. He hailed from Dandalh Dil-e-Sir, Shapuk, and was a fifth-semester student in the Physics Department at the University of Balochistan (UoB). He was a member of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA). He joined the armed struggle against national oppression in 2022 and served as an urban guerrilla. Earlier, in 2018, he had been forcibly disappeared by the occupying Pakistani Army and endured torture in their detention centers for several days. One of his brothers, Kamal Jan, alias Gulab, had also attained martyrdom in a Pakistani Army drone strike in February 2022 while fighting for national liberation.
After being moved to the mountain front in 2022, Martyr Sangat Meeran alias Nazar Jan served on the fronts of Shoor Parod, Noshki, and Kharan. Due to his combat skills and determination, he was quickly appointed camp commander. He played a key role in successfully conducting several operations against the enemy forces.

24-year-old Tahir Baloch, son of Tariq and a resident of the Malant area of Tump, Balochistan, was killed in a targeted attack on 12 September 2026 involving firing by death squads of the Pakistani state army. His father, Tariq, was also injured in the incident.

Abubakar Nichari, alias Lali, son of Muhammad Akbar Nichari, was a resident of Killi Kamalo, Saryab Mill, Quetta. He held a BS degree in Nursing. He joined the BLA in September 2025 and served in Quetta and Zehri. He was a relative of Martyr Ibrahim Nechari and attained martyrdom on 11 August 2026 in Sohinda, Zehri.
Martyr Abubakar Nichari, alias Lali, joined the ranks of the Baloch Liberation Army in September last year and was deployed to the front lines in Kalat and Zehri. After completing basic training, he engaged the enemy on the Kalat and Zehri fronts and took part in deadly attacks against the occupying forces carried out by the Sarmachars. Through his military training and mental fortitude on the front lines, he rendered historic services that will forever remain part of the BLA’s combat history.
Martyr Abubakar Nichari demonstrated the utmost honesty, sincerity, and exemplary military professionalism during his patrols and duties. He did not regard the battlefield merely as the act of firing weapons, but understood it as a responsibility encompassing moral values, professional conduct, and disciplined ideological purpose, and he fought accordingly. His struggle embodied all the qualities of a revolutionary and national fighter. Whatever responsibilities were entrusted to him by the organizational command, he carried them out in an organized manner. He proved himself to be a steadfast and disciplined fighter on both the military and non-military fronts, and he maintained this mindset until the very end.
On the Zehri front, after hours of clashes with enemy forces, he killed several officers and, ensuring the safety of his fellow fighters, attained the great rank of martyrdom. By offering his life as a sacrifice on the path to national liberation, he has secured his place in the pages of history as a great revolutionary fighter. His sacrifices for the land of Balochistan will always be remembered.

data.biography:
At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Hatam Naz Sumalani, alias Gul Bibi, daughter of Noor Mohammad Sumalani, aged 60, hailed from Gharbok, Bolan, Balochistan.
Hatam Naz Sumalani joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2015. She was wounded during the 2016 operation against Ustad Aslam and was later abducted by Pakistani forces, remaining forcibly disappeared for four months. In January 2023, she made the decision to become a fidayee.
At an age when life is expected to slow down and retreat into safety, her path moved in the opposite direction. Her story is marked by injury, disappearance, and survival, carrying the weight of decades of loss and resistance. It reflects a resolve shaped not by momentary anger, but by years of lived experience and endurance.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, not only she but also her son, Saif Jan Sumalani, alias Ajiz, participated and were martyred on the Noshki front. Both mother and son became immortal in Baloch history.

On 7 October 2023, the so-called Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) of the Pakistani genocidal forces killed two Baloch men in staged encounters. Both victims had previously been forcibly disappeared. They were identified as Mohammad Shafi, who was abducted and forcibly disappeared from Quetta on 7 October 2023, and Yousuf Nichari, who was abducted and forcibly disappeared from Nichari Abad, Kali Badu, on 26 August 2023.

On March 8, 2023, Pakistani drones fired three missiles at a Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) guerrilla camp in the mountain range between Hoshap and Pasni. Following the strike, Pakistani forces began landing commandos around the camp from helicopters. In the missile attack, the camp commander, Hasil Baloch, along with four other fighters, was martyred. The remaining Sarmachars fought bravely in close combat, killing several commandos of the occupying forces before they themselves were martyred in the great cause of freedom for their homeland.
The Sarmachars who were martyred are:
Hasil (alias Doda), Wasdil (alias Jami), Nizam (alias Noshad), Waqas (alias Miras), Khalid (alias Kiyya), Shah Fahad (alias Aslam), and Ilyas Baloch (alias Rahmdil).
Martyr Washdil (alias Jami), son of Hashim and resident of Shapuk, joined the armed struggle in 2013. He was a kind-hearted, compassionate, and fearless comrade. Shaheed Wasdil served sincerely and honestly in various areas of Makuran until his martyrdom.

Sher Zaman Kurd, 22 years old, was a resident of Mach, District Bolan. He was an M.A. student at the University of Balochistan and the president of BSO Azad Mach Zone. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising his right to peaceful political expression. On February 16, 2011, he was abducted in Kulpur, District Mastung, by Pakistan’s secret agencies. For three weeks, he remained in the custody of state agencies, where he was subjected to extreme torture for the “crime” of being sincere to his nation and working for the rights of Baloch students.
He was an active and hardworking activist of the organization and played a key role in organizing its activities in areas such as Mach. His abduction occurred during a crackdown initiated by state agencies against the educated youth of the Baloch nation, particularly students affiliated with the Baloch Students Organization Azad. He was pursuing his degree at the University of Balochistan and had a keen interest in reading revolutionary literature.
Nearly a month after his abduction, his bullet-riddled body was found on the Eastern Bypass in Quetta on March 12, 2011. He will be remembered in golden words in the history of the Baloch nation for the remarkable struggle he made for the national liberation of Balochistan.

Swearing upon the Qur’an as a solemn guarantee, the state of Pakistan sent a jirga to negotiate with Nawab Noroz Khan. Trusting the sanctity of the Qur’an as a binding assurance, Nawab Noroz Khan descended from the mountains along with his son, Battay Khan, and his companions. However, rather than engaging in meaningful negotiations or addressing their legitimate demands, the state - consistent with its pattern of duplicity - arrested them.
Nawab Noroz Khan was sentenced to life imprisonment, while his son and several of his companions were condemned to death and executed in the prisons of Sukkur and Hyderabad in Sindh.
When the armed fighters came down from the mountains, they kissed the Qur’an and declared, 'We offer ourselves in its name, but we will not surrender our weapons.' The official delegation repeatedly invoked the Qur’an to reassure them that the government would honor its commitments, insisting that no greater guarantee could exist than the Holy Book itself. Yet once they had descended, those promises were broken, and they were taken into custody. They were confined in harsh prison cells dating back to the British colonial period.
Four companions of Nawab Noroz Khan - Bhawal Khan, Masti Khan, Jamal Khan, and Wali Mohammad - were hanged in Hyderabad Jail, Sindh on 15 July 1960. Their bodies were received by Mir Rasool Bakhsh, the paternal uncle of Mir Mohammad Ali Talpur. After the funeral rites were performed, the martyrs were transported to their ancestral homeland for burial.
Nawab Noroz Khan’s son, Mir Battay Khan, along with Sabzal Khan and Ghulam Rasool, was executed in Sukkur Jail, Sindh on 15 July 1960.
Nawab Nauroz Khan himself passed away on 25 December 1965 at Civil Hospital Hyderabad, Sindh, while in custody. His body was received by Mir Rafique Ahmed. Following the funeral rites, Mir Rasool Bakhsh arranged for his body to be transported to his ancestral place.
His youngest son, Jalal Khan, remained imprisoned until 1970. He was spared execution because he was a minor at the time of his arrest.
Nawab Noroz Khan and the seven martyrs were laid to rest in the Chashma area of Kalat District, a few kilometres from Kalat Bazaar in Balochistan.
Masti Khan Musiyani was born in 1915 in the Manaji tehsil of Khuzdar district. He was a landowner in his area, fond of hunting, and served in the Makuran National Militia.
Masti Khan was married. At the age of 45, like many others, he took to the mountains to join the armed struggle.
The book mentions an incident that occurred in Gandawa, in the Jhal Magsi region: “A few American officials, accompanied by Pakistani authorities, came to Gandawa for a survey. Masti Khan surrounded and captured them. Later, as a gesture of respect, he released them, saying that the Baloch are fighting against slavery, and this struggle will continue as long as even one Baloch remains.
Regarding his life, it is further written: When he was being taken to be weighed before execution, he laughed. When a jail official asked him the reason for his laughter, Masti Khan said, Today our bones and flesh are being weighed for the greatness of the homeland.

Comrade Qayyum was born on 3rd November 1984 in Shay Nizar Mohammad’s home in Gwadar. He studied at Jaded School in Gwadar in 1989 and continued his studies there until he passed his matriculation exam in 2002. Later, he completed his intermediate degree at Syed Hashmi Degree College in his hometown in 2004. In 2008, Qayyum Baloch completed his bachelor’s degree as a private candidate. He was a decent and industrious student and was considered a hardworking and well-read comrade of BSO Azad. He had a keen interest in political literature.
Comrade Qayyum, a sincere personality, joined BSO Azad at a very young age, like many other Baloch youths did, influenced by the organization’s program and activities. Joining BSO Azad enabled him to become a companion of senior activists, and this opportunity led to significant political activism. His mature political engagement and involvement in educational activities and discussions related to BSO were not mere pastimes but were seen as a national duty of every Baloch who wished to see the end of Pakistani subjugation. Due to his commitment and political maturity, he was elected as a member of the Central Committee of BSO Azad.
Soon after, he became one of the important figures in politics, particularly in the Kech district of Makran. He became so active that the authorities soon recognized him. He was first arrested by police personnel on 11 December 2008 for organizing a demonstration on the first martyrdom anniversary of Balach Marri. He was kept in a secret detention cell for 61 days and was threatened to abandon the struggle for the freedom of Balochistan, but he remained devoted and chose the difficult path of revolution.
Comrade Qayyum had two children, a son named Hairbyar and a daughter named Shefa. He was a great, dynamic activist and leader of BSO Azad. Seeing his unwavering commitment and enthusiasm, Pakistan allegedly attempted to silence him forever. On 11 September 2010, he was reportedly abducted by intelligence agencies from his uncle’s house in Gwadar. Two months later, on 10 February 2011, his severely mutilated body was recovered along with Jameel Yaqoob Baloch in Herronk, Kech District. Suppression, intimidation, enforced disappearances, and “kill and dump” tactics could not overcome the firm vision and wisdom of Comrade Qayyum Baloch, which continues to live in the sentiments of Baloch youth.

On 12 March 2026, a statement issued by the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson, Gwahram Baloch, stated that two fighters of the organization, Waheed Baloch (alias Waleed) and Sameer Baloch (alias Meraan), were martyred in a clash with a death squad in the Gresha area of Naal.
The spokesperson further stated that a unit of BLF fighters was on a routine patrol in the Gresha area of Naal on 13 February 2026 when, at around 2:00 PM, agents of a state-sponsored death squad, who had pre-positioned themselves in an ambush at the location of Nadgi, attacked them. The fighters immediately took up positions and counter-attacked the enemy, after which a prolonged clash began between the fighters and the operatives of the state-backed armed group.
During this clash, which lasted more than two hours, another unit of fighters struck the death squad from a different direction, causing them to become disoriented. The fighters’ timely tactical maneuver forced the enemy to retreat. The enemy was compelled to flee the scene, carrying their killed and wounded personnel.
In the initial phase of the clash, one fighter was martyred and another was critically wounded by enemy fire. Amid intense gunfire, a unit of fighters evacuated the wounded sarmachar and the body of the martyred fighter from the scene to a safe location. However, the second wounded fighter later succumbed to his injuries and attained martyrdom.

Sameer Baloch, alias Meraan
In this clash with the enemy, Sameer Baloch, son of Khaliq Dad and a resident of Badrang Gresha, was martyred. He joined the mountain guerrilla front under the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front in March 2024. He was a hardworking, sociable, and exceptionally brave fighter. Martyr Sameer Baloch held a special place among his fellows due to his character and sincerity. He served on various fronts in Awaran, Kolwah, Jhao, Soorgar, Ornach, Naal, and Gresha. The BLF pays tribute to him for this great sacrifice.

Waheed Baloch, alias Waleed
The other fighter martyred in this battle with the enemy was Waheed Baloch, son of Khaliq Dad and a resident of Goni Gresha. He joined the Balochistan Liberation Front as an urban guerrilla in 2024. After successfully carrying out missions for one year, he was transferred to the mountain front in 2025 pursuant to an organizational decision. He was an expert in geographical affairs. Despite being wounded in his final battle, his morale remained high. He continued guiding his comrades to safety from the enemy's encirclement until his last breath.

A committed political and military activist, Jahanzaib Baloch played a significant role in the organizational structure of the BNA in the Panjgur region. He was martyred in the final stages of the clash as the military deployed combat helicopters.

On 12 August 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahran Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of nine fighters of the organization: 1. Zubair Baloch, alias Shahvez; 2. Shahnawaz Baloch, alias Rahchar; 3. Rahim Baloch, alias Ajiz Baloch; 4. Musharaf Baloch, alias Basham; 5. Munir Baloch, alias Khalid Baloch; 6. Mohammad Zaman, alias Yahya; 7. Jasim Baloch, alias Babar; 8. Gaji Khan Baloch, alias Aftab; and 9. Abdullah Baloch, alias Usman, and paid tribute to all the martyred comrades who sacrificed their lives for the freedom of the motherland, Balochistan.

Gaji Khan Baloch, alias Aftab, son of Sher Mohammad and a resident of Jhao Patki, formally joined the Balochistan Liberation Front on August 27, 2025. Gaji Khan Baloch’s family had suffered atrocities at the hands of the occupying forces from the earliest days. On January 5, 2015, the Pakistani military carried out an aerial bombardment of their home in the Gazi Kor area of Jhao using gunship helicopters. As a result, his brother, Dare Khan, was martyred, while his mother and Gaji Khan himself were severely injured. Despite this personal and collective suffering, he chose the path of the freedom struggle and remained committed until his final moments. He stood his ground valiantly on the defensive front against the occupying forces and embraced martyrdom during a fierce clash while halting their recent advance, inflicting casualties and material losses on the enemy.

On 2 February 2022, sixteen members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayeen unit, the Majeed Brigade, carried out simultaneous attacks, nine in Noshki and seven on the Frontier Corps headquarters in Panjgur. The organization named this action "Operation Ganjal". 90 Pakistani security personnel were killed in Noshki and 105 in Panjgur.
On 2 February 2022 at 8:00 PM Fidayee Jamal Baloch alias Chacha, son of Rehmatullah, a resident of Turbat, rammed an VBEID into the main gate of the FC camp in Panjgur. As a result, the front portion of the camp was destroyed, and all soldiers deployed for security at the spot were killed instantly. After this, under the leadership of Unit Commander Hamid Raheem alias Zubair, son of Raheem Bakhsh, a resident of Chitkan, Panjgur, the fidayee fighters Sami Sameer alias Shoaib, son of Ustad Ilahi Bakhsh, resident of Gramkan, Panjgur; Ilyas Baloch alias Qadir, son of Aslam, resident of Gramkan, Panjgur; Asad Wahag alias Sabzo, son of Sadiq, resident of Kilkor; Nasir Imam alias Hamal, son of Imam, resident of Parom; and Zameer Baloch alias Faraz, son of Mohammad Hassan, resident of Dandar, Hoshab, entered the camp. They killed the majority of the soldiers present in the camp, while the remaining enemy personnel, instead of confronting the fighters, abandoned the camp and fled. The objective of the Panjgur unit was to seize control of the camp and hold it for as long as possible. After the enemy fled, the fighters took full control of the entire camp. Subsequently, to recapture the camp from the fighters, the enemy called in SSG commandos, the army, and combat helicopters. During this time, with the support of combat helicopters and armored vehicles, the SSG commandos launched five major assaults on the Baloch fighters. In every attack, the fighters inflicted heavy casualties on the enemy and forced them to retreat. The fighters continued to hold control of the camp while fighting the enemy’s elite military units for 72 hours. After failing in ground assaults, on 5 February 2022 in the afternoon, heavy shelling was carried out against the fighters using combat helicopters. As a result, after prolonged resistance, the fighters were martyred.

Ali Ahmad Marri, son of Pandhi Khan Marri, was a 24 year old resident of the Killi Kamalo area of Quetta, Balochistan. He was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces on 7 April 2010. Months later, on 13 September 2010, his body was found in the Kadkocha area of Mastung.

On 21 October 2025, a statement was issued by Spokesman Baloch Khan of the Baloch Raaji Ajoi Sangar (BRAS), an umbrella alliance of Baloch armed organizations. The statement said that, in defence of the Baloch population in Zehri, Khuzdar, Balochistan, BRAS forces eliminated dozens of enemy personnel, while six freedom fighters embraced martyrdom. Among them was Martyr Abdul Aziz, alias Kalim Ullah.

The statement added that the occupying Pakistani army attempted to advance for aggressive purposes in the Zehri area of Khuzdar, which is under the control of the Baloch Raaji Ajoi Sangar, resulting in fierce clashes. Dozens of occupying Pakistani army personnel were eliminated in these clashes, while six freedom fighters of the Baloch Raaji Ajoi Sangar were martyred in defence of the motherland.

Among the martyred, Abdul Aziz Baloch and Hafiz Muhammad Umar Baloch were martyred on 26 September, while Sanaullah Baloch, Abdul Aziz Baloch, Rashid Ahmed Baloch, and Fayyaz Baloch were martyred on 30 September.

Martyr Abdul Aziz Baloch, alias Kaleemullah, son of Pir Muhammad, belonged to the Kalat Khadi area. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) five months ago. Although his military journey was short, he proved through his determination and courage that the liberation struggle does not depend on age or experience. Kaleemullah was known among his comrades as a soft-spoken, moral, and determined young man, while on the battlefield he became an example of courage, discipline, and extraordinary steadfastness.

Martyr Muslim Raza Baloch, alias Guru Jabbar Baloch, son of Razahi Baloch and Fahmeeda Baloch and was a resident of Balochi bazar Absar, Turbat Kech. He became part of the Baloch liberation movement in the platform of Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in 2012 and joined in the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in 2015. He took part in various armed operations in different areas of Balochistan. 
According organizational statement; Martyr Muslim was a highly skilled guerrilla fighter, and was known for his expertise in the field. Last year, he voluntarily rendered his services for Majeed Brigade, and was waiting for his self-sacrificing mission.
Pakistani military targeted a temporary camp of BLA in a drone attack in Samaan e Kaor area of Turbat, Kech. This was followed by enemy forces being deployed in the area through helicopters. The enemy forces tried to surround the BLA fighters, however, this attempt was foiled with professional tactical measures. The enemy forces were engaged at different places for several places. At least five enemy personnel were killed and seven were injured in these battles.
While breaking the enemy siege and securing a safe passage for their comrades, two fighters of BLA made the ultimate sacrifice. These fallen freedom fighters were Comrade Maqsood alias Comrade Mehrwan and Muslim Raza alias Guru Jabbar.

On 16 February 2022, the ground forces of the Pakistani state, accompanied by air support, attacked a camp of the Baloch Nationalist Army in the early hours of the morning in the mountainous area of Kulbar, Tump. A prolonged skirmish ensued, beginning at 6:00 AM and continuing until 5:00 PM, during which the Baloch Sarmachars killed several enemy commandos and partially damaged two enemy helicopters.
In this clash, Noor Salam Noor alias Istaal, son of Bahar Baloch and a resident of Dashtuk Zamuran; Zubair Akram alias Asadjan, son of Akram Baloch and a resident of Hotabad Zamuran Bazaar; Kambar Baloch alias Mehrwan, son of Tariq and a resident of Kolaho; Sageer Baloch alias Tariq, son of Noorbakhsh and a resident of Basima; Rasool Jan alias Chirag, son of Ali Jan and a resident of Sarankan; and Hafiz Faraz alias Mullah Darwish, son of Abdul Ghani and a resident of Sarankan, were martyred.

An armed encounter took place between the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) freedom fighters and the enemy forces at Jantro on Saturday, October 23, 2021 in Bolan and Harnai mountainous area. Several occupying Pakistani army personnel were killed and wounded in the battle. While valiantly defending the motherland, four BLA members also made the ultimate sacrifice. The combat with the Pakistani occupying forces began when a a patrolling party of BLA came face to face with the advancing enemy forces. BLA fighters charged at the enemy and a battle ensued that lasted for more than three hours. The BLA Sarmachars set high examples of bravery by eliminating and injuring several enemy troops and completely halting their advance. During the battle, four brave comrades, Tariq Marri alias Nasir, Mohammed Hussain Marri alias Jabal, Bakhtiar Sumalani alias Yusuf and Saifullah Zehri alias Sohrab embraced martyrdom. Deprived of moral values, the enemy army also killed two unarmed Baloch farmers named Juma Khan son of Ali Murad and Mahmood son of Shahu from nearby areas, and threw their dead bodies in the said area to portray them as BLA fighters. 
The martyred comrades Bakhtiar Khan Sumalani alias Yusuf son of Mittha Khan of Shahrag and fellow sarmachar, Saifullah Zehri alias Sohrab son of Saleh Muhammad of Yakbozi Zehri had been defending the Baloch motherland through the ranks of Baloch Liberation Army for the last one year. Both colleagues managed to gain a prominent position in the organization in a short span of time.
data.martyrdomPlace: Bolan and Harnai Mountainous area, Balochistan

data.biography: Javed Gwahram, a resident of Mand, was abducted along with his brother by the FC from their hometown on May 16, 2020. After two days, Javed was released from a torture cell in critical condition. On May 25, he succumbed to his injuries while admitted to a hospital in Karachi.

Asif Baloch, the 18-year-old son of Nazeer and a resident of Singabad, was shot and killed by Pakistani state-backed death squads on 8 March 2026 in the Heronk area of Turbat district, Balochistan.
Asif was a civilian driver by profession who spent his days working to support his family.

Irfan Mengal, alias Khalil, son of Ramzan Mengal, was a resident of the Ghareebabad area of Noshki. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Mastung front. He was martyred on 6 September 2026 in the Kadkocha area of Mastung, Balochistan.
Irfan Mengal joined the Baloch Liberation Army earlier 2026 and began his military duties in Mastung. First, he joined the training camp for his military training, where he took part in various training courses with intense effort and hard work, and after completing them, he was included in the organizational patrol rotations. During training, he joined the young men who, with interest and hard work, fulfilled their responsibilities and prepared themselves for the field. With that same zeal and enthusiasm, he later descended upon the enemy. 
At the Khadkocha position, Irfan Mengal, together with his comrades, turned the area into a no-go zone for the enemy and took part in numerous combat operations against them, inflicting heavy losses on the enemy. Along with other brave fighters, he played an active role in the region and remained constantly on the move against the enemy. Martyr Irfan Mengal, a native of Nushki, was martyred in a one-on-one fight with the enemy at the Mastung location, sacrificing himself for his homeland and joining the pages of history among those great figures who sacrificed their individual lives for the freedom of their country.

The resistance and courage shown by the martyrs of Mehi, Mashkay against the aggression of the occupying Pakistani army on June 30, 2015, will be remembered in golden words in the pages of history. Thanks to the sacrifices of these martyrs, awareness of the struggle against Pakistani occupation is spreading to every corner of Balochistan. History honors those who stand up for the defense of their nation and homeland at decisive moments.
The Baloch national freedom movement is ongoing and strong thanks to the sacrifices of these martyrs. These great sacrifices of the martyrs have fostered the consciousness within the Baloch nation that the enemy occupying Balochistan should not be allowed to breathe in peace until they suffocate and run away. It should be remembered that the occupier has always treated the enslaved people with the same inhumane treatment that the state of Pakistan is doing with the Baloch in occupied Balochistan, including killings, enforced disappearances and dumping of mutilated bodies and other atrocities included.
The Martyrs of Mehi area of Mashkay Shaheed Major Sulaiman alias Shehak Jan, Zakir Jan, and Safar Khan Baloch are the great sons of the nation. Those who bravely and courageously adopted the path of resistance against the Pakistani occupation and colonial policy and laid down their lives fighting for the freedom of the country. These great sacrifices of martyrs are encouraging us to leave tribalism, territorialism and become a part of this national struggle as Baloch and strengthen it. Martyrs of Balochistan sacrificed their precious lives so that the Baloch nation could live with freedom and dignity. The national movement needs to be further strengthened and organized while carrying forward this great ideology of martyrs and the spirit of sacrifice.

Hameed Baloch, son of Afzal Chanal, a 15-year-old resident of Koto Jahoo in Awaran district, was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces on July 16, 2025. After a week of illegal detention, his lifeless body was returned to the family.
His body bore clear signs of brutal torture and multiple bullet wounds. It was found dumped by the roadside in a nearby village on July 21, 2025 — riddled with bullets and marked by severe physical torture.

Asad Ullah, son of Haji Abdul Khaliq, a 40-year-old resident of Diz, Paroom, Panjgur, was found extrajudicially killed after being forcibly disappeared from his home on September 9, 2025, at around 8:00 PM.

Asad was a driver by profession and was known for his humble life among the people. His enforced disappearance was carried out by state-backed death squads and law enforcement agencies, and he was later extrajudicially killed on September 12, 2025.

Waheed Baloch, son of Balach, was a resident of Khuzdar district, Balochistan. He received his early education in his hometown, Khuzdar. He was a 16-year-old student of Matric (10th class).
He joined BSO Azad at a very young age and was executed by the Pakistani army in his early life for the “crime” of being a member of BSO Azad. Several students belonging to BSO Azad from Khuzdar were targeted and killed by security forces to curb political activities in the area. However, such killings of Baloch students spread awareness of the Baloch freedom movement in every village of Balochistan. He was engaged in peaceful political struggle, because of which he was targeted.
He was abducted on 8th August 2011 from Khuzdar district by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agencies. After two months of abduction and severe torture, on 9th October 2011, the mutilated bodies of Waheed Baloch and Ghulamullah Baloch were found in Khuzdar district of Balochistan. The sacrifice of Waheed at an early age for the independence of the Baloch homeland will always be remembered in the golden chapters of Baloch history. His body bore severe signs of torture. He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle in difficult times.
Because of him, many youths were inspired to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a very young age will be remembered as long as a single Baloch remains on earth. His only dream was the independence of the Baloch homeland.

On 20 October 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 25 September 2026, the occupying Pakistani army launched a military operation, during which BLA fighters thwarted the assault and eliminated approximately fourteen enemy soldiers. Engaging the enemy with great valour, BLA fighters repelled the assault in a clash that began at 6:00 AM.

During the battle, three brave sons of Baloch soil - Hameedullah Baloch, alias Bilali Baloch; Abdul Hameed, alias Bilali Baloch, a resident of Noshki; and Naseeb Baloch, alias Asad, a resident of Manguchar - were martyred, making the ultimate sacrifice in defence of the Baloch motherland.

A large number of enemy forces participated in the engagement, supported by drones. BLA fighters demonstrated exceptional courage and bravery, engaging the occupying army in direct combat from 6:00 AM until 4:00 PM.

All three brave fighters had joined the BLA in 2023. They participated in several significant battles against the occupying enemy on various fronts, delivering a jaw-dropping response to the enemy.

On 13th April 2026, in the Barkhan area of Balochistan, Pakistani forces shelled and bombed civilian populations, killing twelve innocent Baloch civilians, including women and children, and seriously injuring three others.

The martyrs are:

- Ali, son of Sultan Umair, aged 40
- Babul, daughter of Gulzar, aged 30
- Mir Jan, son of Ali, aged 2
- Somri, daughter of Bhangan, aged 35
- Balach, son of Sabzo, aged 70
- Shari, aged 22
- Rehman, son of Balach, aged 18
- Naikho, daughter of Jamalan, aged 17
- Allah Bakhsh, son of Balach, aged 6
- Saddo, daughter of Balach, aged 13
- Hapo, daughter of Balach, aged 8
- Mahrang, daughter of Balach, aged 2

The injured are:

- Zarbibi, daughter of Sher, aged 55
- Hazar Khan, son of Balach, aged 9
- Israr, daughter of Balach, aged 15

This is not the first time that Pakistani forces have bombed civilians in Balochistan, targeting unarmed and innocent women and children as a form of collective punishment. Nor can this be considered “collateral damage.” Rather, the Pakistani state and its forces are deliberately targeting the Baloch people to maintain an atmosphere of fear in the region, suppress internal dissent, exploit Baloch coastal resources, and continue policies of genocide against the Baloch nation.

Meer Jan Meeral was born on January 18, 1975, to Nasrat Ullah Baloch and Ayesha Baloch in the Tump area of Kech. He completed his matriculation from High School Tump in 1994. He was pursuing his FA when his father passed away in 1996, and after his father’s death, he could not continue his education. He married in 1998.
He had four children: three sons, Miraj Meeral, Minhaj Meeral, and Nasrat Ullah, and one daughter, Mehlab Meeral. He was interested in Balochi literature and was a poet who penned his feelings and reflected on the condition of the society around him through his poetry.
He became part of the Baloch liberation movement under the platform of the Baloch Republican Army (BRA). He was highly committed and disciplined; even his close friends and villagers were unaware that he had joined an armed organization.
On September 3, 2009, he received information that a private vehicle had been hired by the Frontier Corps (FC) in Mand to transport ten of its soldiers in civilian clothes. Along with his comrades, he took positions by the roadside. When the vehicle came within range, they ambushed it, and several soldiers of the Pakistani occupying forces were killed on the spot. The mission was accomplished, but unfortunately their motorcycle did not start, and another Frontier Corps (FC) team arrived at the location. A clash began between the Baloch freedom fighters and the FC. The other fighters managed to escape, but Meer Jan was hit by several bullets and embraced martyrdom.
The mother of Shaheed Meer Jan Meeral told journalists, “Three days before his martyrdom, he told me that he had chosen a path and asked me to pray that he would accomplish the goal he had set for himself.” She further said, “I am proud of my son. He fulfilled his obligation toward me and his motherland.”
Nisar Ahmad Baloch, was a resident of the Anjira, Khuzdar area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 30 September 2013 in Balochistan.

On 6 May 2026, spokesperson of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF), Gwahram Baloch, issued a press statement stating that BLF fighters conducted a successful operation in Rakhni on 2 May 2026 at 2:00 PM, based on highly confidential and verified intelligence reports. The primary target of this operation was Wahid Bakhsh Masuri, described as a close associate of puppet Chief Minister Sarfraz Bugti. According to the statement, Wahid Bakhsh Masuri was allegedly involved in the martyrdom of BLF fighters Shahzeb Baloch, Rasan Qadir, Samiullah Baloch, and Mustafa Baloch. BLF fighters reportedly arrested him in a professionally executed tactical operation and immediately transferred him to a base for further interrogation.
During the initial interrogation, the arrested individual, Wahid Masuri, allegedly confessed to his actions and provided important information regarding death squad networks operating in the area under military patronage.
Following the arrest of Wahid Bakhsh Masuri, the statement claimed that the Pakistani military launched a large-scale operation on the morning of 3 May at 10:00 AM in an attempt to recover him and target the organization’s camp. According to the BLF spokesperson, the operation involved a joint assault by heavy contingents of the Frontier Corps, police, CTD, commandos, and armed groups allegedly led by death squad ringleader Aftab Masuri, described as a brother of Sarfraz Bugti. The statement further alleged that drones, mortar shells, and advanced automatic weapons were extensively used during the assault.
According to the statement, at the outset of the attack, BLF fighters launched a strong counterattack, resulting in the deaths of four key death squad operatives and injuries to several others. Among those reportedly killed was Ismat Masuri, identified as a gunman of Aftab Bugti. The clash reportedly continued for 16 consecutive hours.
The statement further claimed that throughout the engagement, which lasted until 2:00 AM, a total of nine death squad members were killed, while several Frontier Corps and police personnel were wounded.
During the battle, Captain Sangat Salal Baloch, alias Major Noora, son of Sohail Anwar and a resident of Dera Ghazi Khan, Koh-e-Sulaiman, reportedly held the defensive line and kept enemy forces engaged. Despite sustaining severe gunshot wounds, he allegedly refused to retreat and maintained his position to ensure the safe withdrawal of his fellow fighters to secure locations. According to the statement, he succeeded in holding back enemy forces until his comrades had safely withdrawn and ultimately attained martyrdom in the battle. The statement described his bravery as instrumental in enabling fellow sarmachars to break through the enemy encirclement.
Captain Sangat Salal Baloch, alias Major Noora, was described as a highly educated young man who had earned a degree in Software Engineering from BUITEMS. According to the statement, inspired by the struggle for freedom against national subjugation, he joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in 2022 and moved to the mountain front in July 2023. He was described as a fearless fighter skilled in modern combat tactics, who served on various fronts including Nagahu, Mastung, Dasht, Kachhi, Dhadar, Bolan, Kahan, Barkhan, and Rakhni. In recognition of his sincerity, courage, and combat expertise, the BLF reportedly promoted him to the rank of Captain, a position he held until his martyrdom.
Sabir Ali, alias Muheem, was a resident of the Greshag, Khuzdar area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 5 July 2020 in Balochistan.

In 1838, the British sent a force led by Alexander Burnes to reinstate Shah Shuja Durrani as the king of Afghanistan by deposing Amir Dost Mohammad Khan. To reach Afghanistan, they needed passage through Balochistan, particularly the Bolan Pass. However, Khan Mehrab Khan refused to allow the British to use his land to attack a neighboring country. The British sent Lieutenant Leach to negotiate with the Baloch government, but the Khan stood firm. When British forces reached Shaal via Bolan, some patriotic Baloch, without the Khan’s knowledge, attacked British troops out of nationalist sentiment and a desire to protect their homeland.
After toppling Amir Dost Mohammad Khan, the British Governor General of India, Lord Auckland, ordered an attack on Balochistan. In 1839, around 7,000 British troops marched from Shaal to attack the Baloch Meeri (capital). Anticipating an invasion, Khan Mehrab Khan declared war and sent messages to tribal leaders, but many saw the British as allies rather than invaders and chose to collaborate with them rather than defend their land. When Khan Mehrab Khan gathered his resistance fighters, the number of loyal warriors had dwindled to only 700 due to the short sightedness of many tribal chiefs. Nevertheless, Mehrab Khan was determined to fight. At his court, a respected figure, Akhund Muhammad Siddiq, advised him that he was not in a position to wage war at that time. He suggested that the Khan should leave Kalat with his companions, regroup and strengthen his forces, and then launch an attack against the British when the time was right, on 13 November 1839, the British forces launched an attack on Kalat, and a fierce battle ensued. During the fighting, Khan Mehrab Khan Baloch was martyred by a British bullet.

Among those martyred alongside him were:

Diwan Bacha Mal, Minister of Finance

Diwan Khem Chand

Diwan Asardas Mukhi, from the Hindu Panchayat of Kalat

Abdul Karim Raisani, brother of Sardar Asad Khan Raisani

Sardar Wali Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (maternal uncle of Martyr Amir Mehrab Khan)

Mir Taj Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (cousin of Mehrab Khan)

Mir Muhammad Ali Shahizai Mengal

Mir Fazal Muhammad Lehri, brother of Sardar Muhammad Khan Lehri

Sardar Zaman Khan Pandrani

Mir Dad Karim Chandozai Shahwani

Mir Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Mir Badal Khan, brother of Sardar Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Khan Muhammad Dehwaar, Arbab-e-Kalat.

Mir Nabi Bakhsh Jatoi, from the Narmak region of Kalat

Mir Qaiser Khan Bizenjo

Mir Shah Dost Bizenjo

Muhammad Raza Waziri Khel

Noor Muhammad Shahizai, son of Polat Sagaar Sarmastani, in charge of the armory

Taj Muhammad Shagasi

Abdul Rasheed Baloch was born in 1944 in the house of Mawlavi Abdullah Deirmani in Deirrman, Dashtyari, Western Balochistan. As a student, he joined the Baloch Student Organization (BSO) and became active in the struggle for Baloch rights.
In 1973, when he was a BA student, Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto, then President of Pakistan, dismissed the National Awami Party (NAP) government of Balochistan under pressure from the Shah of Iran. In Karachi, BSO activists, including Abdul Rasheed, started a protest campaign against Iran and Pakistan.
Pakistan's secret police began arresting students, forcing many of them to go underground. Abdul Rasheed left Pakistan and went to Baghdad, Iraq, where he was granted political asylum. In Baghdad, he joined other Baloch activists in exile and worked to build international pressure on Iran and Pakistan over human rights abuses committed against the Baloch nation.
Fearing their activities, the Iranian regime sent agents to stop them at any cost.
On 21 May 1976, he was assassinated by a SAVAK agent, Musa Khan Mubaraki, who strangled him and buried him in a secret location. His body was later discovered when Iraqi police arrested the culprits. The main perpetrator was tried in a military court, sentenced to death, and executed, while his three accomplices were imprisoned and later released after two to three years.
Shaheed Abdul Rasheed Baloch sacrificed his life for the freedom of Balochistan. We shall not let the sacrifices of our martyrs go in vain. Our struggle for a united and free Balochistan will continue until victory.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Shaheed Raziq Nichari, alias Haroon, son of Ahmad Ali Nechari, was originally from Manguchar and later migrated to reside in Quetta.
Raziq Nechari, also known as Haroon, was affiliated with the Fateh Squad of the Baloch Liberation Army. He served on the Noshki and Kharan fronts and attained martyrdom while fighting bravely on the front lines as part of the BLA’s vanguard unit. Despite continued state repression, including the enforced disappearance of one of his brothers as collective punishment, Haroon remained committed to the national struggle and set an example of steadfastness, discipline, and sacrifice on the battlefield.

On 9 November 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Republican Guards spokesperson Dostain Baloch announced the martyrdom of five members of the organisation and paid red salutes to them.

The spokesperson said: “We pay heartfelt tribute and offer red salutes to the sincere, brave, and ideologically committed fighters of the Baloch Republican Guards: Commander Habibullah Jan Jatoi, alias Laghari; Sharif Jatoi, alias Commando; Saeed Jan Jatoi, alias Nana; Hazrat Jatoi, alias Bolani; and Umeed Ali Jatoi, alias Nadir. They embraced martyrdom while bravely fighting against the occupying Pakistani army in the Sanni area of Kachhi for the freedom and right to self-determination of Balochistan."

On 1 November 2026, in the Sanni area of Kachhi, Commander Habibullah Jan and his revolutionary comrades launched an ambush against a convoy of the occupying Pakistani army.
Commander Habibullah Jan and his brave fighters fiercely engaged the enemy on the front lines, inflicting significant human and material losses on the occupying forces.
During the clash, an enemy drone suddenly launched an attack, seriously injuring Commander Habibullah Jan, Saeed, Hazrat, and Umeed. Despite their injuries, they continued to face the consequences of the attack. However, unable to survive their severe injuries, Habibullah Jan and his comrades later embraced martyrdom. All five members were residents of the Sanni area of Kachhi.
Adil Baloch, was a resident of the Panjgur area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 14 March 2014 in Balochistan.
Hasil Baloch, was a resident of the Shapuk, Kech area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 11 March 2017 in Balochistan.

On 11 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch announced the martyrdom of 14 fighters of the organization who attained martyrdom in confrontations with the Pakistani army and in airstrikes while defending their homeland, Balochistan, and fighting for national liberation and the right to self-determination.

On 13 August 2026, Pakistani Air Force fighter jets bombarded the Pandran area of Kalat District in Balochistan, resulting in the martyrdom of four members of the organization: Waseem Baloch, alias Farhan; Obaidullah Baloch, alias Shaheen; Nawaz Ali Baloch, alias Dilshad; and Mohammad Hassan, alias Ahmad.

On 25 August 2026, during an organizational mission in the Kech area of Balochistan, Sher Jan, alias Jamal, was shot from behind by a traitor, resulting in his martyrdom.

On 3 September 2026, while patrolling in the Mastung area of Balochistan, the organization’s brave fighters, Mohammad Younis, alias Salal; Sameer Ahmad, alias Zemal; Aziz Ahmad, alias Janan; and Sikandar Baloch, confronted Pakistani forces, targeted several enemy personnel, and embraced martyrdom.

On 14 September 2026, while engaging Pakistani forces and defending his fellow fighters in the Machani Kor Paroom area of Panjgur District, Babar Baloch, alias Kambar, embraced martyrdom.

On 18 September 2026, during a confrontation with Pakistani forces in the Chagi area of Balochistan, fighters of the organization, Riaz Baloch, alias Sabir; Taimoor Shah, alias Shaheen; Zia Ul Haq, alias Ziaullah; and Jumma Baloch, alias Commando, embraced martyrdom.

Waseem Baloch, alias Farhan, son of Mohammad Jan, resident of Chitkan Bazaar, Panjgur, joined the BLF on 24 June 2026. After military training, he was sent to the Kalat front under an organizational decision, where he carried out his national duties bravely. On the morning of 13 August 2026, in an attack by the occupying army's jets, he was martyred and became immortal along with his three other sangats.

Satik, alias Ala Malat, had been associated with the Baloch national struggle for freedom since 2005. From the very beginning, he remained steadfastly committed to serving the national cause. Throughout his long struggle, up to the time of his martyrdom, he never showed weakness in any regard.
On 18 November 2017, he was wounded during clashes with a Pakistani government-backed death squad in the Lajay area of Kharan district, Balochistan. Rather than allowing himself to be captured by the enemy, he chose martyrdom.

On 2 February 2022, sixteen members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayeen unit, the Majeed Brigade, carried out simultaneous attacks, nine in Noshki and seven on the Frontier Corps headquarters in Panjgur. On 2 February 2022 at 8:00 PM Fidayee Jamal Baloch alias Chacha, son of Rehmatullah, a resident of Turbat, rammed an VBEID into the main gate of the FC camp in Panjgur. As a result, the front portion of the camp was destroyed, and all soldiers deployed for security at the spot were killed instantly.
