The objective of the Panjgur unit was to seize control of the camp and hold it for as long as possible. After the enemy fled, the fighters took full control of the entire camp. Subsequently, to recapture the camp from the fighters, the enemy called in SSG commandos, the army, and combat helicopters. During this time, with the support of combat helicopters and armored vehicles, the SSG commandos launched five major assaults on the Baloch fighters. In every attack, the fighters inflicted heavy casualties on the enemy and forced them to retreat. The fighters continued to hold control of the camp while fighting the enemy’s elite military units for 72 hours. After failing in ground assaults, on 5 February 2022 in the afternoon, heavy shelling was carried out against the fighters using combat helicopters. As a result, after prolonged resistance, the fighters were martyred.

data.fullName: Samad Khan Chalgari Marri, alias Dostain Baloch
data.biography:
On 30 September 2024, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that they pay tribute to their six comrades - Shafo Sumalani alias Tadain, Samad Khan Chalgari Marri alias Dostain, Mohammad Gul Marri alias Waheed Baloch, Ghulam Qadir Marri alias Anjeer Baloch, Obaid Baloch alias Fida, and Taj Mohammad Chalgari Marri alias Babul - who were martyred in a bombing by jet fighters of the Pakistani Air Force in Harnai, Balochistan. On 12 September, at 4 AM, jet fighters of the Pakistani Air Force dropped several heavy and deadly bombs on BLA fighters, with the support of drone surveillance, in the Ali Khan Thal area of Harnai, Balochistan. As a result of the bombing, six fighters were martyred. After the attack, the morally bankrupt enemy desecrated the bodies of the martyred fighters and took their body parts using gunship helicopters.

Samad Khan Chalgari Marri, alias Dostain Baloch hailed from Bolan Gharbo and had been serving the national struggle through the platform of BLA for the past one and a half years. He will always be remembered as a sincere, hardworking, and brave fighter.

Faraz Rasheed, son of Abdul Rasheed, and a resident of Riaz Mohallah, Singani Sar, Turbat,  was forcibly disappeared from his home by the Pakistani forces in December 2024. After leaving school in the town. 

Following his enforced disappearance, the local media and Human Rights organisation has reported his case with an immediate release. In spite to uncover his whereabouts, the Pakistani forces has killed him in fake encounter with three other people in Dasht, Kech on September 20, 2025.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
In Gwadar, nine Fidayeen of the BLA Majeed Brigade were divided into two units and took part in the operation. The first unit, which included Fidayeen Hawa Baloch (alias Droshum), Yahya Lal (alias Lashari), Adnan Arman (alias Changaiz), and Yousif Baloch (alias Yagi), attacked the compound of the occupying Pakistani intelligence agencies, resulting in the elimination of 12 personnel. Women and children in residential quarters near the compound were provided safe passage; however, the occupying army later martyred these same civilians by opening fire.
About forty minutes later, occupying forces advanced toward the compound, leading to clashes that continued until the evening. In these clashes, more than 24 personnel were eliminated, and three military vehicles, including an armored vehicle, were destroyed.
The second squad, which included Fidayeen Kambar Ismail (alias Sarbaz), Khurshid KB (alias Arman), Waseem Baloch (alias Kareem), Shoaib Baloch (alias Shehzad), and Yasir, took up strong positions in Port Bazaar near Gwadar Port. After announcements were made in mosques, freedom fighters went to the bazaar, met the public, and held political discussions. After repelling the advance of occupying forces in the city, the freedom fighters later advanced toward the port and fired several rockets that hit their targets. Clashes continued until the next day, eliminating more than 19 personnel.
Adnan Arman remained associated with the Baloch armed struggle for more than a decade. He formally joined the armed resistance in 2013 and remained active on various fronts in the Makuran region. On the battlefield, he was known for his patience, endurance, strategic acumen, and bravery. Fidayee Adnan Arman was also the cousin of the Martyr Arif Noor.
Adnan Arman belonged to the coastal city of Gwadar, which is regarded as a symbol of national resistance. The Baloch coastal area has, for centuries, represented defiance, where in every era colonisers and occupying forces have faced fierce resistance from the Baloch people.
During his student years, Fidayee Adnan participated in student politics. He was a skilled poet and writer who, through his poetry and prose, expressed the significance and objectives of the Baloch struggle for liberation.
In 2024, Fidayee Adnan joined the BLA and dedicated his services to

On 31 May 2021, Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) fighters attacked the Pakistani military’s “Awais” camp (Ghazaband Scouts’ 129 Wing) in Marwaar, Bolan. The three-hour assault completely destroyed the camp. BLA fighters killed 24 Pakistani soldiers on the spot and captured Lance Naik Bilal from Dera Ismail Khan. He was later tried by a Baloch national court and executed.
Following a coordinated plan, the fighters surrounded the camp, cut through barbed wire, and stormed inside. After intense fighting lasting over three hours, they overran the base, killed 24 enemy personnel, seized a large quantity of arms and ammunition, and took one prisoner. As usual, the Pakistani military downplayed its losses.
Three BLA fighters embraced martyrdom in the operation: Hangal Marri (alias Laila), Aftab Jattak (alias Washain), and Shahwez Zehri (alias Saraang). They were buried in Bolan with full military honours.
The three belonged to the elite Fateh Squad, formed in 2018 and named after Martyr Fateh Qambrani (alias Chairman), who single-handedly enabled the capture of an enemy camp in Meshdari, Shahrag, the same year. Fateh Squad members are selected for exceptional bravery and close-combat skills.
In the Marwaar attack, these three charged the enemy lines, breached the perimeter, and created openings that allowed the BLA to capture the camp entirely.
Hangal Marri (alias Laila) joined the BLA in 2006 and served with distinction on the Kahan and Bolan fronts for 15 years.
Aftab Yousuf Jattak (alias Washain), a highly educated economics graduate from Zehri, joined in 2019 and quickly earned a place in the Fateh Squad due to his skill and courage.
Shahwez Zehri (alias Saraang) joined in 2017, served in urban units, then volunteered for the Bolan front and the Fateh Squad, where he fought bravely until his martyrdom.

On 21 October 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 18 October 2026, during prolonged clashes with Pakistani forces in Chaghi Dognan, Balochistan, 10 personnel of the occupying Pakistani army who had arrived to conduct an operation against the BLA were killed, while two BLA fighters, Javed Baloch, alias Malang, and Kamal Khan, alias Saddam, sacrificed their lives for the Baloch motherland.

According to the statement, the occupying Pakistani army attacked BLA positions at 6:00 AM on 18 October 2026. In retaliation, the BLA adopted a tactical approach and assumed defensive positions against the enemy. While defending their fellow fighters and the local Baloch population, BLA combatants launched a counter-offensive against the enemy's ground forces using both light and heavy weaponry. Despite possessing superior manpower and advanced weaponry, the enemy suffered casualties and material losses at the hands of the BLA. Following its defeat on the ground, the occupying Pakistani army requested aerial reinforcements. The forces were also supported by long-range mortar fire and artillery; however, our sarmachars stood like an impenetrable wall against the enemy. During the engagement, enemy drones also arrived in the area to target our fighters. The occupying Pakistani army further subjected the local civilian population to indiscriminate shelling.

In this battle, which lasted from 6:00 AM to 7:00 PM, two of BLA brave sarmachars were martyred. Fighting with exceptional valour, both sons of the soil defended their fellow fighters and the base until the very last drop of their blood. Among these fearless and noble sarmachars, Javed Baloch, alias Malang, was martyred after being struck by a drone.

He joined the BLA in 2025. He hailed from Dalbandin and had inflicted heavy losses on the occupying Pakistani army in several skirmishes.

Kamal Khan, alias Saddam, from Narmuk, fought valiantly alongside Javed Baloch, alias Malang, helping ensure the safety of their fellow fighters. During this prolonged battle, their ammunition ran out. Adhering to the philosophy of the “last bullet,” he chose martyrdom with pride rather than surrendering to the enemy.

Kamal Khan had been actively involved in the struggle under the banner of the BLA since 2022. He served the national cause across various regions of Balochistan, including Bolan, Nagahau, Suran, Narmuk, Mangochar, and Kalat. He was a brave and courageous sarmachar (freedom fighter) who possessed exceptional combat skills.

Gul Badeen Notezai, son of Safar Khan Notezai, a 33-year-old resident of Zahoor Colony, Dalbandin, Chaghi, was killed by the army on 17 June 2026 at approximately 6:30 PM.
He was killed on a road in Dalbandin. Following the incident, his body was taken from the scene and later transported to a hospital.

On 6 November 2026, the Baloch Liberation Army's media channel, Hakkal, published the biographies and details of six martyrs associated with the organization.

Among them, three fighters - Muneer Ahmad Jattak, alias Noora, son of Habib Khan Jattak; Shahzaib Bangulzai, alias Ehsan, son of Samiullah Bangulzai; and Fareed Langove, son of Ghulam Nabi Langove - were martyred on 20 October 2026 in the Rodinjo area of Kalat District.

Two other fighters, Parvez Ahmad Mohammad Hassni, alias Qadir, son of Shekari Mohammad Khan Mohammad Hassni, and Noman Jamaldini, alias Comrade Sameer, son of Agha Mohammad Jamaldini, were martyred on 24 October 2026 in the Gidar area of Surab.

The sixth fighter, Aurangzaib Langove, alias Asif, son of Hameedullah Langove, was martyred on 24 October 2026 in the Manguchar area of Kalat District.

Shahzaib Bangulzai, alias Ehsan, son of Samiullah Bangulzai, was a resident of the Saryab Mill area of Quetta. He joined the BLA in 2026, served on the Kalat front, and was martyred on 20 October 2026 in the Rodinjo area of Kalat.

Brave Shahzaib Baloch, a native of Quetta, began his struggle this year against the enemy under the banner of the Baloch Liberation Army, fighting for the cause of national freedom. He had come to realize that under enemy occupation, the Baloch nation would gain nothing but humiliation, destruction, and perpetual ruin. This realization drove him to armed resistance, which he regarded as the only means of driving the enemy out of Balochistan. After joining the organization, he was transferred to a training camp, where he received basic military training and strengthened himself both physically and mentally.

Upon completing his military training, he was transferred to Kalat under organizational directives, where he took part in front-line operations against the enemy and, alongside his fellow comrades, inflicted heavy losses on the enemy. He actively participated in various combat operations conducted by the organization. He was not merely a fighter familiar with warfare but was also known as a warrior with practical skills and expertise in combat. He was martyred on 20 October 2026 during an engagement with the enemy, in which he displayed immense courage and bravery. He will be remembered as a hero in Baloch national history.

data.martyrdomPlace: Omari Khan, Saami, Turbat district, Balochistan
data.biography:
On 19 April 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson, Gwahram Baloch, announced the martyrdom of six fighters of the organization, paid tribute to them, and stated that the organization’s fighters were martyred in the national war of liberation. The martyrs include Ikram Baloch (alias Hameed), Shaibaz Shohaz (alias Kiyya), Masood Baloch (alias Bharag), Salman Waheeda (alias Chirag), Izzat Baloch (alias Jummi), and Hamza Baloch (alias Waheed).
The spokesperson further stated that the martyred fighters fulfilled their oath and national duty of defending the nation and homeland to the last drop of their blood, sacrificing their lives and achieving immortality. The martyrs proved through their great sacrifices that Baloch sarmachars do not hesitate to make any sacrifice in the defense of the nation and homeland.
Masood Baloch, alias Bharag, son of Zakir, a resident of Omari Kahn, Saami, Turbat district, Balochistan, was part of the BLF's urban network for six months. His responsibilities included the surveillance of suspicious elements and sensitive locations, reporting, and providing logistical support to fighters.
He carried out all national duties assigned by the organization with great diligence, completing every task perfectly and on time. Masood was martyred on February 19, 2026, while en route to the organizational camp in Omari Kahn, in a quadcopter attack carried out by enemy forces. A fellow fighter, Martyr Ikram Baloch, alias Hameed, was also wounded in the same attack.
Dilawar Baloch, was a resident of the Koshkalat, Tump area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 4 December 2018 in Balochistan.

Qambar Chakar was born on October 7, 1987, in house of Chakar Baloch and Shahista Baloch in Alandor, Buleda area of district Kech, Balochistan. His family migrated to Shahi Tump Turbat of District Kech. After acquiring primary education in his native area Alandor, Qambar Chakar got admission at Atta Shad Degree College Turbat. For further education, he went to Shaal (Quetta) where he managed to seek admission at the prestigious Balochistan University of Information, Technology and Management Sciences (BUITMS) as a BS Economics student after passing a very competitive exam. Along with continuing his studies as a student at BUITMS, he also became active in student politics and worked hard to spread the awareness of Baloch nationalism among Baloch students. In this regard, he launched the first unit of Baloch Students Organization (AZAD) in BUITMS. Many of the students, after being inspired by Qambar Chakar, joined the journey of BSO Azad which was boarding clearly on the Independent Balochistan.
Qambar was a vocal person for the enforced disappeared persons too, as he had been mostly engaged with the foreign journalists as he was proficient in English language. Qambar was an extraordinary leader of the student organization. Whenever he got the mic, none could speak better than him on stage. When he held the pen, he wrote efficiently than anyone could ever. Further, he was a committed and courageous worker of BSO Azad. He even joined weekly study circles in injured conditions. He remained punctual in Organizational activities. In a very short period, Kambar became an exceptional leader among Baloch students due to his struggle for the students’ rights and independence. He very soon became a leading figure among Baloch youth when he campaigned for the rights of Balochistan in his institution BUITMS.
 Firstly, Qambar was whisked away by the security forces in 2009 when he had gone to the Takato Campus of the University to meet with the Vice-Chancellor on the issues of open merit admission policy. After being released, he confirmed that he had been brutally tortured during  the custody for being active for the rights of Baloch students as well as raising his voice for the Baloch Missing Persons. He was once again whisked away from his home at Shahi Tump (Turbat) along with his cousin on November 26, 2010. The bullet-riddled dead body of Qambar Chakar, along with Ilyas Nizar Baloch, was found in a desolate place near Pasni Road, Pidrak area of Kech, Balochistan on 5th of January, 2011.

On May 12, 2025, a 7-year-old girl, Rokia Baloch, was fatally shot while sleeping outside her home in Khudabadan, a town in Panjgur District, Balochistan. At approximately 3:00 a.m., personnel from Pakistan’s Frontier Corps (FC) indiscriminately opened fire in the area. A bullet struck Rokia in the abdomen while she was asleep.
Due to the intense heatwave conditions in Balochistan, it is common for residents to sleep outdoors at night. Rokia was immediately rushed to the hospital in Panjgur and later referred to the District Headquarters Hospital in Kech (Turbat). Despite her family’s efforts, she succumbed to her injuries on May 14, 2025.
The tragedy was compounded by the dire condition of the healthcare facilities. Upon admission, there was no proper oxygen supply, no emergency medicines, no functioning air conditioning, and no reliable electricity. The absence of these life-saving necessities reflects the systemic neglect and underdevelopment of public services in Balochistan, particularly in critical healthcare.

On 14 September 2026, while engaging Pakistani forces and defending his fellow fighters in the Machani Kor Paroom area of Panjgur District, Babar Baloch, alias Kambar, embraced martyrdom.

Sher Jan, alias Jamal, son of Shakoor, resident of Gomazi, began his revolutionary journey with the BLF's urban intelligence network. For two years he carried out his duties with great secrecy and skill, and in August 2025 he moved to the mountain front. He served on the harsh battle fronts of Zamuran, Buleida and Kech. On 25 August 2026, while he was on an armed mission, a former member of the organization who later turned traitor, Haji Gul, alias Haji Faraz, cowardly and treacherously shot him from behind. The organization acted immediately and took the culprit, Haji Faraz, into custody. After confessing to the crime during investigation, he killed himself out of fear of punishment.

On the night between Saturday and Sunday, at 3:00 AM on April 25, 2020, Pakistani forces, along with local death squads, surrounded Baloch fighters (Sarmachaars) in Yar Mohammad Bazaar, located in the Parom Kallag Kor area of Panjgur district. A clash broke out between the forces and the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) fighters, which continued for twelve hours.
The fighting lasted until 2:30 PM on April 26, 2020. After the Pakistani ground forces retreated, military helicopters shelled the fighters, resulting in the killing of four Sarmachaars - Major Noora, son of Sher Dil, alias Peerak; Lieutenant Nawaz, son of Haji Ghulam Hussain; Abdul Malik, son of Haji Ghulam Hussain; Momin, son of Mohammad Azeem - During this prolonged twelve hour clash, several soldiers of the Pakistani army and associated death squads were killed and injured.

Major Noora, alias Peerak, son of Sher Dil, was born in 1992 in Parom, Panjgur, Balochistan. He had been associated with the Baloch national liberation movement and armed struggle for over a decade. He was a highly intelligent and capable fighter. He not only served in various roles across different regions of Balochistan, providing significant military contributions, but also played an important role in organizing the Balochistan Liberation Front through his abilities.

Lieutenant Nawaz, alias Gulab, son of Ghulam Hussain, was born in Parom. He had been associated with the BLF and the armed struggle for ten years and, due to his dedication and capabilities, attained the rank of Lieutenant.

Abdul Malik, son of Ghulam Hussain, was also born in Parom and had been associated with the armed organization BLF for two years.

Momin Baloch, son of Muhammad Azeem, was born in Buleda Salo and had been actively engaged in the armed struggle for two years.

On 2 September 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that, on Tuesday, 1 September 2026, fighters of the BLA ambushed an FC check post in the Dhor area of Kalat, Balochistan.
Azad stated that the fighters used rocket launchers and modern weapons against personnel travelling in an enemy vehicle, killing seven Pakistani Frontier Corps personnel and injuring two others.
During the clash with Pakistani forces, a BLA fighter, Ghazi Khan, alias Shah Murad Baloch, was killed while fighting the enemy with what the statement described as utmost courage until the last drop of his blood.
He joined the BLA in 2023 and, according to the statement, carried out attacks against the enemy on multiple fronts within a short period. He participated in guerrilla raids in Nagaho, Nirmak, Johan, Mangchar, and Robdar, Balochistan.

Hairas Badini, alias Nodan, son of Comrade Hameed Baloch, was a resident of Killi Shareef Khan, Noshki.

A large quantity of military equipment was also reportedly seized. Images showing the bodies of the deceased Pakistani soldiers, destroyed vehicles, and military uniforms hanging at various locations subsequently went viral on social media.
Even after the coordinated attacks had ended, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), a member of the BRAS alliance, maintained control of the Zehri area and successfully repelled multiple attempts by Pakistani forces to advance into the region.
After holding control of the area for several days, the BLA eventually withdrew. Following its withdrawal, the Pakistani military entered Zehri with gunship helicopters, battle tanks, and a large contingent of troops. According to reports, the forces spread fear and panic through looting and other actions in the area. Since then, Zehri and its surrounding regions have remained under military operations and repression.
Following their defeat at the hands of the armed groups, Pakistani forces allegedly targeted civilians in retaliation. As a result of this repression, 11 Baloch individuals were reportedly killed.
On 16 April 2026, several people from Zehri and its surrounding areas - including Wadera Mohammad Dayaan, Imam Bakhsh, Manzoor Ahmad Miraji, Munir Hayat Dayaan, Izzatullah Pandrani, Habibullah, Mohammad Sharif, Mohammad Ramzan, and three unidentified individuals - were reportedly extrajudicially executed by Pakistani forces while traveling along roads in the Sohinda area. One individual, Abdul Salam, survived with serious injuries.
During the ongoing military operation in the area, these individuals were allegedly detained by Pakistani forces from various locations and transferred to the Sohinda Rest House, approximately five kilometres from Noorgama. There, their hands and feet were allegedly bound, they were blindfolded, and they were subsequently shot dead.
The incident occurred one day after the BLA claimed that two of its fighters had been killed during clashes in the Sohinda area.
In its statement, the BLA said that, on 15 April 2026, its fighters targeted advancing Pakistani military units with a remote-controlled explosive device. Following the explosion, they allegedly carried out an ambush on a military convoy moving toward the area.
The organization claimed that ten Pakistani military personnel were killed in the two attacks, while two of its own fighters, Tanveer Mengal and Saadullah, were also killed.

Faizullah Bangulzai, son of Arz Mohammad Bangulzai, a 28 year old social worker and resident of Kachi Baig, Sariab Road, Quetta, was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces on 2 May 2010. Two months later, on 5 July 2010, he was extrajudicially killed, and his body was dumped on Brewery Road, Quetta.

On 16 October 2026, a statement issued by the Baloch Republican Guards (BRG) stated that, on the night of 30 September 2026, occupying Pakistani forces arrived in the Sunni area of Kachhi district, Balochistan, to conduct an operation. A sudden confrontation took place between the occupying forces and the freedom fighters, who launched a deadly attack against the enemy. As a result, the occupying army suffered significant casualties and material losses.

During the clashes, five devoted BRG freedom fighters - Bafa Jan Jatoi, son of Lal Jan Jatoi, a resident of Sunni, Kachhi; Fareed Jan Jatoi, alias Zahri, son of Ghulam Jan, a resident of Sunni, Kachhi; Obaidullah Jan Jatoi, son of Sajjar Khan, a resident of Sunni, Kachhi; Imam Din Jatoi, alias Mumtaz, son of Nihal Khan, a resident of Sunni, Kachhi; and Ayaz Jan Ghola, alias Alim, son of Abdul Sattar, belonging to the Ghola Baloch tribe and a resident of Sunni, Kachhi - embraced martyrdom while defending their homeland and fighting for national independence.

All these freedom fighters were highly dedicated, brave, hardworking, and disciplined comrades. They inflicted various forms of losses on the occupying enemy in several areas of Balochistan, including Kachhi, Dhadar, Sunni, Bolan, and Sibi.

Changaiz Ibrahim, son of Mohammad Ibrahim, was a 24-year-old labourer from the Allandoor Buleda area of Turbat district, Balochistan. On 4 September 2026, at around 11:00 a.m., Frontier Corps personnel of the Pakistani forces forcibly disappeared Changaiz from his home in Apsar, Turbat, Balochistan.
After 14 days of enforced disappearance, on 17 September 2026, Frontier Corps personnel summoned Changaiz’s family to the Frontier Corps camp in Apsar, Turbat. They showed the family a photograph of Changaiz and informed them that they had killed him. The photograph showed that Changaiz had been brutally struck on the head with a heavy object. The Frontier Corps personnel had also disposed of his body.

Operation Dara-e-Bolan, which began on 29 January 2024 continued for two days until 31 January 2024 and was successfully concluded after achieving its intended objectives. A total of 385 Sarmachars from four different units of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) participated in Operation Dara-e-Bolan. Among them were 12 Fidayeen from the BLA’s Majeed Brigade. The other participating units included the Fateh Squad, the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS) and the Intelligence Wing.
Operation Dara-e-Bolan commenced on the evening of 29 January 2024 at 9:00 pm local time and continued for two days. After achieving the desired results, the BLA’s Senior Command Council announced the conclusion of Operation Dara-e-Bolan on 31 January 2024 at 7:00 pm and issued instructions to all units to vacate their positions and report back to their base camps.
During the operation, BLA Sarmachars took complete control of an area within a 70 kilometre radius, including Mach city and the strategically important National Highway N-65. Over the course of Operation Dara-e-Bolan, a total of 78 enemy personnel were killed. These included 45 Frontier Corps (FC) personnel who were killed within the first three hours of the operation in Mach city; 10 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on an army camp at the Pir Ghaib Bolan location; 4 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on a military convoy at the Gokurt Mach location; 12 regular army personnel who were killed on 30 January when Majeed Brigade Fidayeen eliminated them and entered the FC headquarters; and at least 5 SSG commandos who were targeted and killed by the Fidayeen on 31 January 2024. In addition, two police personnel were also killed, including one Station House Officer (SHO).
A large number of Levies and police personnel were captured by the BLA during the operation; however, as they were Baloch, they were released. During Operation Dara-e-Bolan, 13 brave fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army attained martyrdom. Of these, 12 martyred Sarmachars belonged to the Majeed Brigade Fidayeen, while one martyred Sarmachar was from the BLA’s Fateh Squad.
The martyred Sarmachars were: Qasim Baloch, Saddam Hussain, Salal Baloch, Farooq Baloch, Atta Baloch, Hammal Momin, Zeeshan Zehri, Nadir Bangulzai, Nizam Baloch, Zeeshan Baloch, Jamal Baloch, Wadood Satakzai, and Kashif Shahwani.
Kashif Shahwani, alias Roken, son of Haji Shah Mohammad Shahwani, belonged to Quetta. He had been part of the BLA for two years and had served in the BLA’s vanguard unit, the Fateh Squad, for the past year. As a guerrilla fighter, he possessed extensive combat skills. In recognition of his military knowledge, agility, and bravery, he was included in the Fateh Squad. During Operation Dara-e-Bolan, he fought in the front ranks and was among the first sarmachars to enter the city. Due to his bravery, the BLA was able to take control of Mach city.

data.martyrdomPlace: Madag Kaur, Kolwah, Kech district, Balochistan
data.biography: Saki Baksh, alias Mureed Baloch son of Mohammad Hussain and Mahrang, was a resident of Sehr, Kolwa area of Awaran, Balochistan. According to organizational statement; He was became part of Baloch liberation movement in the platform Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in 2013. Due to his combat skills, he was a lieutenant in the organization. He embraced martyrdom along with other his comrades Asad Baloch, alias Basit Baloch; Akil Azab, alias Riaz Baloch; and Pervez Mehr, alias Malok Baloch during a clash with Pakistan’s Army in Madag Kaur area of Kolwa, Kech, Balochistan on October 9, 2021.

Khalid Baloch, son of Doshambay, a resident of Nasirabad in Turbat district, Balochistan, was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces on 21 May 2011. Two days later, on 23 May 2011, his body was found in the Murgaap area of Turbat district.

Shaheed Sameer Barkat Baloch was from Dasht Balnigor, Jatani Bazar, District Kech. Shaheed Sameer, along with his wife Hani Gul, was visiting their relatives in Sistan, Balochistan. On August 8, 2023, a group of militant men broke into their house and kidnapped both the husband and wife. After ten days of abduction, on August 19, 2023, the tortured and mutilated bodies of both were found on the roadside in villages between Sarawan and Khash in Gusht, Sistan, Balochistan. They were martyred in a very painful manner.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Sohail Ahmad Gurgunari, alias Faisal, son of Mohammad Younas Gurgunari, was a resident of Killi Jamaldini, Noshki. He joined the BLA in 2022 and served in the Fateh Squad. He was active on the Shoor Parood Front in Noshki.
Sohail, known among his comrades as “Faisal,” was a son of the soil of Noshki, a land that has consistently given birth to new dimensions of resistance. When he chose the path of armed struggle in 2022, it was not merely an emotional impulse but a profound and conscious intellectual choice. Due to his innate combat skills and exceptional discipline, he was inducted into the BLA’s highly active and courageous elite unit, the “Fateh Squad,” where he left an indelible mark of bravery in a very short period.
Sohail Ahmad played a leading role in numerous encounters against the enemy on the difficult fronts of Shoor Parod and Noshki. His personality was a testament to unwavering resolve and ideological maturity. When “Operation Herof” was launched, Sohail demonstrated his military prowess in this decisive battle against the enemy in his home district of Noshki. During intense clashes, he embraced martyrdom while successfully halting the enemy’s advance and providing both defensive and offensive superiority to his comrades.

Muslim Dad, son of Malang Dad, aged 40, was a driver by profession from Gelli Bahot Bazar, Buleda, in Turbat district.
On September 7, 2025, he was abducted and forcibly disappeared from his home in Absar, Turbat, at 1:30 PM by Pakistani forces, including the Frontier Corps and Military Intelligence. This occurred in broad daylight, in front of his community, while silence was imposed on his family.
For 4 months and 28 days, his loved ones waited, suffered, and searched. No court, no charges, and no voice were given to him.
On April 10, 2026, his lifeless body was found dumped in the Kech River (Kech Kour) in Turbat.

Sadiq Sobeen, son of Sobeen Baloch, was a 17-year-old 9th-grade student at Government High School Sham Marah. He was a resident of Kolwa, District Awaran. Sadiq Sobeen served as the Unit Secretary of BSO Azad Kolwa Zone. He joined the organization at a very early age and remained associated with it until his martyrdom.
He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising peaceful political expression. He was killed by Pakistani paramilitary forces during a bloody operation in Kolwa, Awaran, on 29 July 2017. He was a committed member of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times.
He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history. His sacrifices will contribute to bringing freedom to the Baloch homeland.

Mukhtyar Baloch, son of Mureed Baloch, was born in 1995 in Lanjar Jhao, District Awaran, Balochistan. He was a resident of Jao, District Awaran. Mukhtyar Baloch was a 9th-grade student at High School Lanjar Jao and a member of BSO Azad Jhao Zone. He received his early education in his hometown, Jhao.
He mobilized hundreds of youth to join the Baloch struggle for the independence of their homeland. Many of his friends and organizational comrades were martyred by security forces. He was threatened by security agencies to quit politics and leave BSO Azad, but he remained committed to the organization and continued his struggle until his martyrdom.
He was an example of bravery and commitment. He joined the organization at an early age and remained steadfast in his national ideology until the end. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising his peaceful political expression.
He was a victim of a willful killing on 10 November 2015 by Pakistan’s army in Lanjar Jhao, District Awaran, Balochistan. He remained a dedicated member of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad.
His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

On 19 August 2010, Advocate Zaman Marri, son of Mehrab Khan, was abducted near his private office on Jinnah Road in Quetta, Balochistan, while he was on his way home to Killi Kamaloo. Advocate Marri, a resident of New Kahan, had been residing in Killi Kamaloo on Sariad Road.
On 6 September 2010, his tortured body was found in a jungle near Mastung and was laid to rest in the New Kahan “Martyrs of Balochistan” graveyard. Hundreds of Baloch activists from different political parties, student organizations, lawyers, and residents of New Kahan and Killi Kamaloo participated in his funeral to pay their last respects to Advocate Marri. He was buried with great respect and pride, and the flag of Balochistan was hoisted on his grave as a symbol to let the Baloch opponents know that Shaheed Zaman Marri’s sacrifices will not be in vain.

On November 19, 2024, while traveling on an organizational mission in the Gishkor area of Kolwah, the comrades were ambushed and attacked by enemy forces. As a result, two key and long-standing members of the organization were martyred.
Martyred fighter Captain Niaz Qadir, known as Ustad Guman, was killed on the spot, while Lieutenant Zarif Baloch, known as Shay Jan, was severely injured. The comrades involved in the mission mounted a strong counterattack against the enemy forces and, during the fighting, successfully carried the martyred Captain Niaz Qadir, his injured comrade Shay Jan, and their war gear to safety.
Lieutenant Zarif Baloch, alias Shay Jan, son of Hammal Baloch and a resident of Gishkor Sundom, joined the freedom struggle in 2013 and became an official member of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in 2014. Throughout his long struggle, he bravely resisted the enemy forces’ brutal oppression and violence. Despite violent state actions against his family, his resolve and commitment remained unshaken.
On November 19, 2024, during an organizational mission, he was severely injured in a skirmish with enemy forces. His comrades managed to evacuate him to a safe location, where a medical team associated with the organization worked tirelessly to save him using all available limited resources. Unfortunately, despite their efforts, he succumbed to his injuries on November 21, 2024.
Over the course of his ten-year involvement in the freedom struggle, Lieutenant Zarif Baloch played a significant role in several memorable and important military operations. He worked diligently and with great dedication in the organization’s economic sector, earning the trust of the Regional Command Council. Due to his military and political maturity, he was promoted to the rank of Lieutenant. He consistently prioritized the organization’s objectives and remained steadfast until his last breath. His leadership and unwavering dedication to the struggle for freedom will always be remembered.

Swearing upon the Qur’an as a solemn guarantee, the state of Pakistan sent a jirga to negotiate with Nawab Noroz Khan. Trusting the sanctity of the Qur’an as a binding assurance, Nawab Noroz Khan descended from the mountains along with his son, Battay Khan, and his companions. However, rather than engaging in meaningful negotiations or addressing their legitimate demands, the state - consistent with its pattern of duplicity - arrested them.
Nawab Noroz Khan was sentenced to life imprisonment, while his son and several of his companions were condemned to death and executed in the prisons of Sukkur and Hyderabad in Sindh.
When the armed fighters came down from the mountains, they kissed the Qur’an and declared, 'We offer ourselves in its name, but we will not surrender our weapons.' The official delegation repeatedly invoked the Qur’an to reassure them that the government would honor its commitments, insisting that no greater guarantee could exist than the Holy Book itself. Yet once they had descended, those promises were broken, and they were taken into custody. They were confined in harsh prison cells dating back to the British colonial period.
Four companions of Nawab Noroz Khan - Bhawal Khan, Masti Khan, Jamal Khan, and Wali Mohammad - were hanged in Hyderabad Jail, Sindh on 15 July 1960. Their bodies were received by Mir Rasool Bakhsh, the paternal uncle of Mir Mohammad Ali Talpur. After the funeral rites were performed, the martyrs were transported to their ancestral homeland for burial.
Nawab Noroz Khan’s son, Mir Battay Khan, along with Sabzal Khan and Ghulam Rasool, was executed in Sukkur Jail, Sindh on 15 July 1960.
Nawab Nauroz Khan himself passed away on 25 December 1965 at Civil Hospital Hyderabad, Sindh, while in custody. His body was received by Mir Rafique Ahmed. Following the funeral rites, Mir Rasool Bakhsh arranged for his body to be transported to his ancestral place.
His youngest son, Jalal Khan, remained imprisoned until 1970. He was spared execution because he was a minor at the time of his arrest.
Nawab Noroz Khan and the seven martyrs were laid to rest in the Chashma area of Kalat District, a few kilometres from Kalat Bazaar in Balochistan.
Ghulam Rasool Nechari was born in 1920 in the Mohammad Tawa area of District Kalat. He was a Hafiz of the Quran and worked as a farmer in the outskirts of Kalat.
According to the author of the mentioned book, after a military operation in Kalat, when the streets were in chaos, Ghulam Rasool Nechari took his old shotgun and went to the Zehri Ghat area of Khuzdar to join the armed struggle.
He was arrested on May 19, 1958, and on July 15, 1960, at the age of 40, he was executed by hanging in Central Jail Sukkur.

On January 29, 2026, in the Washbud area of Panjgur district, Balochistan, a death squad operating under Pakistani forces abducted 20 year old laborer Malang Baloch, son of Zahid Nadeem, and killed him extrajudicially.

Khan Mohammad Mengal, son of Atta Mohammad, a 26 year old member of the Balochistan National Party (BNP), was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces on 8 August 2010. A week later, on 14 August 2010 so called Pakistan Independence Day, his body was found in the Ferozabad area of Khuzdar district, Balochistan.

On 8 August 2016, terrorists attacked the Government Hospital in Quetta, Balochistan, in a suicide bombing and shooting. More than 70 people were killed, mainly lawyers, and more than 130 others were injured.
The majority of those killed were lawyers who had gathered at the hospital after the body of Advocate Bilal Anwar Kasi, president of the Balochistan Bar Association, was brought there. Kasi had been shot dead by a gunman near Mengal Chowk on Manno Jan Road in Quetta while he was leaving his home for his office.
Responsibility for the attack was claimed by various Islamist groups, including Jamaat-ul-Ahrar and the Islamic State Khorasan Province. However, nationalist groups have alleged that these extremist organisations are backed by the Pakistani state and its military to counter the nationalist movement in the region and exploit its natural resources.
Estimates of the death toll ranged between 70 people, while more than 120 were injured. Of those killed, 54 were lawyers. Among them, 15 were Baloch by ethnicity, while the majority were Pashtuns by ethnicity.

The Baloch advocates or lawyers who were killed are identified as follows:

01 Ghulam Farooq Badini, son of Haji Abdul Ghani.
02 Bashir Ahmed Qazi, son of Qazi Ahmed Jan.
03 Bashir Ahmad Zehri, son Haji Mir Ahmed Zehri.
04 Naseer Ahmed Langove, son Abdul Rahim.
05 Chakar Khan Rind, son of Mehmood.
06 Abdul Rashid, son of Abdul Latif.
07 Nooruddin Rakshani, son Haji Naseeruddin.
08 Muhammad Imran, son Ghulam Farooq.
09 Munir Ahmed Mengal, son Ghulam Murtaza.
10 Sangat Jehan Jamaldini, son of Dr. Jahanzaib.
11 Mohammad Ali Satakzai, son of Taj Mohammad Khan.
12 Mehmood Ahmed Lehri, son Haji Abdul Hameed.
13 Jamil Ur Rehman, son of Qazi Abdul Hameed.
14 Amanullah Langove, son of Haji Dad Karim.
15 Sabir Ali, son of Abdul Rasheed.

Sabir Ali was 29 years old.

Mir Mohammad Iqbal Shahwani, alias Master, son of Mir Haji Khan Mohammad Shahwani, was a resident of Killi Sardeh, Sariab, Quetta. A Hafiz and F.Sc. graduate, he joined the BLA on 11 June 2024 and served on the Quetta front as an urban guerrilla. He was martyred on 29 July 2026 in the Killi Sarden area of Quetta.
Mir Hafiz Muhammad Iqbal had been affiliated with the Baloch Liberation Army for the past three years. Active on the organisation’s important urban guerrilla front, he rendered great services. When he decided to join the organisation in 2024, he was assigned, by organisational command, to the urban front’s intense combat zone. After completing basic training and education, he carried out his duties. He remained in Quetta for three consecutive years, actively participating in major military operations against the enemy—from monitoring their movements to carrying out key military strikes—and ensuring that the Baloch civilian population would never be left at the enemy’s mercy.
For the past three years he worked with exceptional skill on the urban front in Quetta. There he provided crucial intelligence, conducted reconnaissance of enemy positions, gave tactical-level support to his comrades, and took an active part in major military operations and actions. Through his conduct and actions he became a beacon for other urban guerrilla fighters. He was a Hafiz of the Qur’an and had completed his education up to F.Sc., yet instead of building a personal career he made the historic decision to struggle for the national cause and the restoration of the independent status of the State of Balochistan. His decision was rooted in the conviction that freedom and identity are the fundamental philosophy and guiding principle of human life.
He fulfilled his national and military responsibilities to the very end. When the enemy surrounded him and tried to capture him, he chose to fight single-handedly. After fierce clashes and after running out of ammunition, he adhered to the organisation’s historic “last bullet” philosophy and chose martyrdom rather than fall into enemy hands. His sacrifices will be remembered in history as those of a great guerrilla fighter, a steadfast Sarmachar, and a national hero.

data.organization: Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) / Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB)
data.biography:
The fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front’s special unit, the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB), attacked the Brigade Headquarters in the Nokundi area of Chagai, Balochistan, at around 8:19 PM on the night of November 30, 2025. SOB fighters successfully entered the offices and residential compound of foreign employees of the Saindak and Reko Diq projects, located in the centre of the camp, and managed to take several foreigners present in the compound hostage. The Pakistani army deployed its air force, SSG commandos, and modern heavy weapons against the fighters, but the brave Sarmachars of SOB repelled every attempt and forced them to retreat. During the operation, the Balochistan Liberation Front offered the Pakistani side an opportunity to negotiate on its demands; however, 18 hours after the offer, the Pakistani army chose to use force and began directly targeting the compound with artillery and aerial attacks. This resulted in intense clashes between the occupying forces and the fighters, which continued until the martyrdom of the SOB fighters.
In this special operation by the Saddo Operational Battalion, 76 military personnel, including foreign hostages, were killed, and 6 SOB fighters embraced martyrdom. The Nokundi operation by SOB was a continuation of the BLF’s long-standing armed resistance strategy for the independence of Balochistan and the protection of its natural wealth.
Among the martyrs were:
1 Asif alias Khalid Baloch, son of Mulla Ghulam Jan.
2 Inayat Sahil alias Gwahram Baloch, son of Ishaq Baloch.
3 Zareena Rafiq alias Tranag Maho, daughter of Master Rafiq Ahmed.
4 Nabeel Ahmed alias Ustad Adil Baloch, son of Haji Muhammad Ishaq.
5 Meer Jan Meeral alias Janan Baloch, son of Muhammad Raheem Baloch.
6 Ghulam Jan alias Istaal Baloch, son of Faiz Muhammad.
Meer Jan Meeral alias Janan Baloch, son of Muhammad Raheem Baloch, resident of Hasanabad Meskani Kalat, Kharan, joined BLF in 2024 and volunteered for Saddo Operational Battalion in 2025 for the love of motherland and Baloch nation. Meer Jan Meeral played a key role in the operation and achieved the honour of martyrdom while courageously fighing enemy forces alongside his fellow fighters in the Battle of Nokundi.

Waleed Jan Pandrani, alias Chakar, son of Gul Mohammad Pandrani, was a resident of Sariab Mill Colony, Quetta, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in June 2025 and was martyred in the Noshki Operation Herof Phase 2.
Rising from the streets of Sariab, Waleed Jan Pandrani was not a traveler of conventional paths; instead, as “Chakar,” he chose a trail marked by constant trials. The comforts of the city could not chain his spirit, and in June 2025 he consciously chose the silence of the mountains as his voice. He was not just a warrior but a follower of a dream that found its realization in the plains of Noshki. During the scorching afternoons of Operation Herof, amidst the rising smoke of gunpowder, Chakar stood like an invincible rock against the enemy.
He was a member of BSO Azad.
Afzal Baloch, was a resident of the Jahoo, Awaran area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 20 November 2015 in Balochistan.

Ijaz Ahmad Mengal, alias Hayat, son of Mohammad Hayat Mengal, was a resident of the Ghareeb Abad area of Noshki District, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Noshki and Chagai fronts. He was martyred on 31 August 2026 in the Nokcha area of Chagai District, Balochistan.
Ijaz Ahmad Mengal, like other Baloch youth, feeling the oppression and humiliation of national servitude, decided this year to join the Baloch Liberation Army and was transferred to the Shor front. He did not accept the philosophy of armed resistance merely on intellectual grounds; he made it a part of his practical life and became an active, brave, and fearless fighter against the enemy. After graduating from basic military courses, he was sent on organizational patrols, where he carried out his duties with the utmost honesty and dedication.
Ijaz Ahmad Mengal took an active part in the war effort, supporting the organization’s established dominance in the region and its economic blockade policy against the enemy, and together with his comrades, he played his individual role effectively in strictly enforcing the organization’s policy. He succeeded in establishing trust and confidence among his comrades in a short period. Ijaz Ahmad Mengal remained true to the oath he took for his homeland and national freedom until his final moment and was martyred after fierce clashes during an operation against the enemy. He will be remembered in Baloch national history as a brave and fearless fighter who embraced martyrdom for his country’s freedom.

Ali Jan Saqib is remembered as a Baloch intellectual voice whose life became associated with ideas of dignity, identity, and cultural consciousness. He belonged to the region of Chagai District, an area known for its deep historical and cultural traditions. Growing up in a society shaped by tribal heritage, poetry, and oral storytelling, he developed a strong connection with Baloch culture and language.
From an early age, Saqib showed interest in poetry and expressive writing, a tradition deeply rooted in Baloch society. His words often reflected themes of honor, resilience, homeland, and the emotional bond between people and their land. Through poetry and spoken expression, he contributed to preserving cultural identity and encouraging awareness about social and historical realities.
Ali Jan Saqib’s life eventually came to be remembered through the idea of sacrifice and steadfastness. After his death, his name continued to circulate in cultural memory through poems, songs, and narratives shared across generations. His story is often invoked as an example of courage and devotion to principles, reflecting the enduring role of poetry and intellectual expression in Baloch society.
Today, Ali Jan Saqib’s legacy lives on through Balochi and Brahui cultural literature, where his name symbolizes determination, cultural pride, and the power of words to inspire communities. His life story remains part of the broader historical memory of Balochistan, where poetry, storytelling, and remembrance continue to preserve the contributions of influential figures.

On 9 September 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of ten fighters belonging to the organization. He paid tribute to the Sarmachars who were martyred while defending national liberation and their homeland, Balochistan.
- The statement identified the following fighters:
1-  Akhtar Dawood, alias Ali Sher, son of Asad Sajidi.
2- Khalil Ahmad, alias Ustad Awais, son of Sher Ahmad.
3-  Imran, alias Aajo, son of Saifullah.
4-  Hasil, alias Munir Ahmad, son of Sher Mohammad.
5- Inayatullah, alias Sher Zaman, son of Manzoor Ahmad.
6- Asad Rahim, son of Rahim Baksh.
7- Mujeeb Ur Rehman, alias Shay Mureed, son of Saeed Ahmad.
8- Sahil, alias Arman, son of Peeral.
9- Javed, alias Murshid.
10- Mohammad Younis, alias Taleb, son of Mohammad Omar.

Javed, alias Murshid, formally joined the Baloch national liberation struggle by enlisting in the BLF in 2013. After receiving military training, he carried out national duties on the fronts of Balgatar and its surrounding areas, dealing heavy blows to the occupying enemy. Martyr Javed, alias Murshid, played an important role on the front line in various engagements against the enemy army. He was an active fighter who was well acquainted with his duties and carried out his organizational affairs skillfully and promptly. He attained the great rank of martyrdom while carrying out organizational duties in Balgatar.

As the organization has not specified his date of martyrdom, the Baluch Martyrs Memorial uses the date of the organization’s statement as his date of martyrdom.

Rasheed Baloch, a resident of Washuk, was a brave freedom fighter who became part of the Baloch freedom struggle in 2012 through the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF). Rasheed Baloch was martyred along with his comrade Abdul Khaliq during a clash with Pakistani forces on 12 December 2015 in Tank-kor, Mashkai, Balochistan.

data.martyrdomPlace: Koh Sabz Palantak, Panjgur district, Balochistan
data.biography: Hammal Hassani, son of Samad Hassani and an advocate by profession, was killed by soldiers  of the Frontier Corps of the Pakistani forces on March 6, 2026, in the Koh Sabz Palantak area of Panjgur district of Balochistan.

Bahad Baloch, son of Rahim Bakhsh and a resident of Kolahoo village in Tump, Kech, Balochistan, was brutally killed by members of state-backed death squads in the Dehaat area of Kech on November 1, 2025.

Bahad, a laborer by profession, worked in the border region near the coastal city of Gwadar, in the Kuntani area. He earned his livelihood by transporting oil on motorcycles across the border to support his family. According to local sources, armed militia operatives affiliated with Pakistani military forces intercepted him, seized his motorcycle, valuables, and other belongings, and later killed him.

He was the sole breadwinner of his family, working tirelessly under harsh conditions to provide for them. After his killing, the perpetrators reportedly attempted to portray the incident as a suicide by placing a rope around his neck and leaving his lifeless body in a nearby mosque.

Baba Baloch, a 24 year old professional Zamyad driver from Naag, Panjgur, was abducted and forcibly disappeared from Kalam Chowk, Panjgur, by state-backed death squads. These death squads operate with the backing of the Pakistani army and are given free rein to harass, abduct, loot, beat, and kill people.

After 17 days, Baba Baloch was killed, and his body was dumped in Rakshan Kaur, Panjgur District, Balochistan, on 14 October 2026.

Operation Dara-e-Bolan, which began on 29 January 2024 continued for two days until 31 January 2024 and was successfully concluded after achieving its intended objectives. A total of 385 Sarmachars from four different units of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) participated in Operation Dara-e-Bolan. Among them were 12 Fidayeen from the BLA’s Majeed Brigade. The other participating units included the Fateh Squad, the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS) and the Intelligence Wing.
Operation Dara-e-Bolan commenced on the evening of 29 January 2024 at 9:00 pm local time and continued for two days. After achieving the desired results, the BLA’s Senior Command Council announced the conclusion of Operation Dara-e-Bolan on 31 January 2024 at 7:00 pm and issued instructions to all units to vacate their positions and report back to their base camps.
During the operation, BLA Sarmachars took complete control of an area within a 70 kilometre radius, including Mach city and the strategically important National Highway N-65. Over the course of Operation Dara-e-Bolan, a total of 78 enemy personnel were killed. These included 45 Frontier Corps (FC) personnel who were killed within the first three hours of the operation in Mach city; 10 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on an army camp at the Pir Ghaib Bolan location; 4 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on a military convoy at the Gokurt Mach location; 12 regular army personnel who were killed on 30 January when Majeed Brigade Fidayeen eliminated them and entered the FC headquarters; and at least 5 SSG commandos who were targeted and killed by the Fidayeen on 31 January 2024. In addition, two police personnel were also killed, including one Station House Officer (SHO).
A large number of Levies and police personnel were captured by the BLA during the operation; however, as they were Baloch, they were released. During Operation Dara-e-Bolan, 13 brave fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army attained martyrdom. Of these, 12 martyred Sarmachars belonged to the Majeed Brigade Fidayeen, while one martyred Sarmachar was from the BLA’s Fateh Squad.
The martyred Sarmachars were: Qasim Baloch, Saddam Hussain, Salal Baloch, Farooq Baloch, Atta Baloch, Hammal Momin, Zeeshan Zehri, Nadir Bangulzai, Nizam Baloch, Zeeshan Baloch, Jamal Baloch, Wadood Satakzai, and Kashif Shahwani.
Hammal Momin, alias Kulmeer, son of Mohammad Baloch, had been associated with the armed struggle for Baloch national liberation since 2020. The 23 yearold Hammal Momin belonged to the Panwan Jiwani area of Gwadar. Two years prior, he voluntarily offered his services to the BLA - Majeed Brigade. He was a conscious guerrilla fighter imbued with the spirit of sacrifice. During Operation Dara-e-Bolan, he was among those comrades who reached the very center of the enemy’s FC headquarters. For two days, he fought continuously without food, water, or sleep and ultimately laid down his life for the homeland. He was also an author and literary writer. On the very day he attained martyrdom, one of his books was published.

After suffering losses from the Baloch Liberation Army’s coordinated attacks under Operation Herof across the length and breadth of Balochistan, Pakistani forces on 29 August 2024 took nine forcibly disappeared individuals out of their torture centers and extrajudicially executed them. The bodies of five individuals were dumped in Khuzdar, while the bodies of four others were thrown in Hub. Among them, the identities of four bodies were confirmed as those of forcibly disappeared persons Saeed Ghulamani, Fayaz Jattak, Saeed Meeraji and Nisar Ahmad.

On 25 September 2026, Didag Baloch, son of Mohammad Omar, went on a picnic with his friends in the Lutham area of Balicha, Tump District. They informed the Pakistani army of their presence at the location. They were subsequently targeted by a rocket fired from a drone operated by Pakistani forces, which killed Didag Baloch and three of his friends: Yasir, son of Mohammad Karim; Zubair Nawab, son of Nawab; and Sameer Baloch, son of Abdul Khaliq. Two other people were also injured in the incident.

Amanullah Baloch (alias Sadiq Baloch; martyred 25 December 2018) was a committed fighter and intelligence operative of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA).
A resident of Khuzdar, Balochistan, Amanullah joined the Baloch liberation movement in 2012 and served in the organisation’s intelligence wing, where his dedication and skill contributed to its most sensitive operations.
On 25 December 2018, he embraced martyrdom alongside Commander-in-Chief General Aslam Baloch, Babar Majeed Baloch, Kareem Baloch, Akhtar Baloch, and Taj Muhammad Baloch in a targeted attack in Kandahar, Afghanistan.
His sacrifice remains an enduring part of the Baloch struggle for freedom.
