data.biography:
Sheran Dad Kareem was a native of Dasht, Makuran. In 1900, when Mir Mohammed Omar Noushervani rebelled against the local agents of the English invaders in Balochistan, Sheran raised his sword in support and joined the small band of freedom fighters. He played an important role in capturing and defending Nodaz Fort alongside Shaheed Mir Mohammed Ali Noushervani, the younger brother of Mir Mohammed Omar.
After a 50-day siege, and despite heavy weapons used by the English troops, the fort was recaptured on 20 December 1901. Severely wounded, Sheran was arrested along with 63 of his injured fellow countrymen. The Jirga sentenced Sheran Dad Karim to death. Mir Dur Mohammed Shahbaz Khan Noushervani of Kolwah was sentenced to 20 years of imprisonment with hard labor and a fine of Rs. 20,000, while Bahadur Khan Maddad Khan Noushervani of Hor Kolwah was sentenced to 10 years of imprisonment with hard labor and a fine of Rs. 10,000. Others received relatively lesser sentences.
After the Khan of Kalat endorsed the Jirga’s judgment, Sheran Dad Kareem was hanged in Turbat on 4 February 1902.

Hammal Baloch, son of Wahid Bakhsh and a resident of Gomazi, Tump, was extrajudicially killed on July 13, 2025, in the Jusak area of Turbat, Kech district. According to eyewitnesses, Hammal was shot dead in broad daylight by armed men affiliated with Pakistani state-backed death squads who are operating under the protection of Pakistani intelligence agencies and forces.
Farhad Baloch was identified as a young man (reportedly 17 years old) martyred  in the missile strike in Sistan and Balochistan.

Hamdan Baloch, alias Marwan, son of Nawaz Shambayzai and brother of Fidayee Marwan, alias Mehrab, was a resident of the Mehnaz area of Buleda, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Zamuran front. He was killed on 29 July 2026 in Zamuran.
From the revolutionary and active front of Zamuran, Hamdan Baloch, who joined the ranks of the Baloch Liberation Army this year, offered his services to the organization for a short period of time. During this period, however, the steadfastness, practical resistance, and ideological and intellectual commitment he demonstrated, along with his participation in various organizational training courses and the enthusiasm and passion he displayed, made his revolutionary spirit a lasting source of encouragement for his comrades. Hamdan was among those revolutionary cadres who, immediately upon joining the organization, accepted its organizational discipline, program, and revolutionary approach.
Following in the footsteps of his Fidayee brother, Martyr Marwan, alias Mehrab, he made those same revolutionary traditions a part of his practical life. In the Watak, he was always counted among those comrades who remained engaged in one activity or another and helped and supported his comrades in every task. His practical inclination to take an interest in every activity and remain active in every task made him an active Sarmachar of the Watak.
Whatever qualities and attitudes characterize a complete and successful Sarmachar, all of them were present in Shaheed Hamdan. Therefore, as a new cadre, when the enemy’s soldiers attempted to advance toward the organization’s Watak in large numbers, Hamdan, together with his fellow comrades, confronted the enemy and prevented its advance and its efforts to cause large-scale damage. Through his sacrifice, he helped thwart the enemy’s efforts and protect his fellow Sarmachar comrades.
The training of a true revolutionary comrade and struggler is based on the principle that he remains ready to sacrifice his life to protect his comrades. Martyr Hamdan, throughout his service, adhered to these revolutionary principles and remained committed to the ideology of national independence until the end, ultimately being killed during the conflict. His sacrifices will play a role in sustaining the struggle for independence, and he will always be remembered in the pages of history.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Nasir Jatak, alias Sadam, son of Naseer Jatak, was a resident of the Sarab area of Zehri District in Khuzdar, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2024 and served as an urban guerrilla. In 2025, he moved to the mountain front, where he served on the Kalat and Zehri fronts under the command of the Fateh Squad. He was martyred during Operation Herof Phase II on the Noshki front.
Nasir Jatak began his journey of armed resistance as an urban guerrilla. In this role, he carried out his responsibilities with great discretion and a strong sense of duty. The work of an urban guerrilla requires not only courage but also strict secrecy, constant hard work, and unwavering organizational discipline, and Saddam remained committed to all these principles. Despite limited resources and harsh conditions, he proved that a disciplined and hardworking Sarmachar forms the true foundation of a resistance movement.
In 2025, following an organizational decision, he was transferred to the mountainous front, where he served in the regions of Kalat and Zehri. Due to his experience as an urban guerrilla and his persistent dedication, he was inducted into the organization’s frontline unit, the Fateh Squad—an indication that he was not only a brave Sarmachar but also capable of playing a role in critical battles. During Operation Herof Phase II, he stood firm alongside his fellow Sarmachar against the enemy on the Noshki front and ultimately sacrificed his life in the course of this struggle.

Mohammad Yousif Baloch, a political activist, was abducted on 13 October 2010 and subjected to enforced disappearance. He was later extrajudicially killed while in custody, and his body was dumped on 18 December 2010.

On 7 October 2024, a statement was issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch, stating that on 6 October 2024, the Majeed Brigade, the elite Fidayeen unit of the Baloch Liberation Army, targeted a high level convoy of Chinese engineers and investors leaving Jinnah Airport in Karachi in a Fidayeen attack. According to the statement, more than five Chinese engineers and investors were killed and more than twelve were injured. At least fifteen Pakistani military personnel assigned to protect them were also killed, with many others injured, including more than four high-ranking officers of the Pakistani army and intelligence agencies. As a result of the explosion, fifteen vehicles in the convoy were destroyed. Due to the careful tactics of the BLA, civilians were spared casualties in the blast despite the densely populated area.
This operation was carried out by Shah Fahad, alias Aftab; Saddam Baloch, alias Fareed and Sohail, alias Baba, of the BLA’s Majeed Brigade.
Saddam Baloch, alias Fareed, son of Bahot, belonged to the Pasni area of Balochistan. Sangat Saddam, a Fidayeen attacker who used an explosive vest, joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2021, and a year later offered his services to the BLA’s Majeed Brigade. As a dedicated BS Criminology student, Sangat Saddam Baloch embodied the spirit of sacrifice and demonstrated notable fighting skills. He worked closely with ZIRAB for several months to complete this mission and ultimately sacrificed himself to ensure the success of the first phase of the operation.

Iqbal Hakeem, son of Hakeem Baloch, 19 years old, a resident of Tehsil Grisha in District Khuzdar, and a student of the BS Education program (Second Semester) at Karachi University, was shot dead by state-backed death squads in the small town of Grisha, Nadagi, on August 22, 2025.

Early that same morning, Iqbal, along with a relative, was killed in broad daylight by state-backed death squads in Grisha, Khuzdar.

Previously, Iqbal Hakeem had been harassed and kept under surveillance by the same death squads. He had also received death threats and, ultimately, had to leave his studies due to persistent harassment and surveillance.

Shabir Baloch, son of Abdullah Baloch and a resident of Suhrdap Gresha, was a freedom fighter for the independence of Balochistan. He joined the armed struggle and fulfilled his responsibilities with great dedication on the platform of the BLF. He was martyred in a clash with Pakistani forces and state-backed death squads in Surgar, Jhaoo, on 17 December 2021.

On 11 August 2025, the umbrella alliance of Baloch armed organizations in Balochistan, Baloch Raji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS), launched coordinated operations during which several government installations were destroyed and dozens of Pakistani military personnel were killed. A large quantity of military equipment was also reportedly seized. Images showing the bodies of the deceased Pakistani soldiers, destroyed vehicles, and military uniforms hanging at various locations subsequently went viral on social media.
Even after the coordinated attacks had ended, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), a member of the BRAS alliance, maintained control of the Zehri area and successfully repelled multiple attempts by Pakistani forces to advance into the region.
After holding control of the area for several days, the BLA eventually withdrew. Following its withdrawal, the Pakistani military entered Zehri with gunship helicopters, battle tanks, and a large contingent of troops. According to reports, the forces spread fear and panic through looting and other actions in the area. Since then, Zehri and its surrounding regions have remained under military operations and repression.
Following their defeat at the hands of the armed groups, Pakistani forces allegedly targeted civilians in retaliation. As a result of this repression, 11 Baloch individuals were reportedly killed.
On 16 April 2026, several people from Zehri and its surrounding areas - including Wadera Mohammad Dayaan, Imam Bakhsh, Manzoor Ahmad Miraji, Munir Hayat Dayaan, Izzatullah Pandrani, Habibullah, Mohammad Sharif, Mohammad Ramzan, and three unidentified individuals - were reportedly extrajudicially executed by Pakistani forces while traveling along roads in the Sohinda area. One individual, Abdul Salam, survived with serious injuries.
During the ongoing military operation in the area, these individuals were allegedly detained by Pakistani forces from various locations and transferred to the Sohinda Rest House, approximately five kilometres from Noorgama. There, their hands and feet were allegedly bound, they were blindfolded, and they were subsequently shot dead.
The incident occurred one day after the BLA claimed that two of its fighters had been killed during clashes in the Sohinda area.
In its statement, the BLA said that, on 15 April 2026, its fighters targeted advancing Pakistani military units with a remote-controlled explosive device. Following the explosion, they allegedly carried out an ambush on a military convoy moving toward the area.
The organization claimed that ten Pakistani military personnel were killed in the two attacks, while two of its own fighters, Tanveer Mengal and Saadullah, were also killed.

Shams Baloch embraced martyrdom in a battle against Pakistani forces on may 14, 2015 in Johan, Kalat.
He was serving the Baloch 
National cause on the platform of Baloch Liberation Army since 2008.
Zubair Jan Gichki was a resident of the Kech area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 1 December 2010 in Balochistan.

On 29 April 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson, Gwahram Baloch, announced the martyrdom of six fighters of the organization, paid tribute to them, and stated that the organization’s fighters were martyred in the national war of liberation. The martyrs include Ikram Baloch (alias Hameed), Shaibaz Shohaz (alias Kiyya), Masood Baloch (alias Bharag), Salman Waheeda (alias Chirag), Izzat Baloch (alias Jummi), and Hamza Baloch (alias Waheed).
The spokesperson further stated that the martyred fighters fulfilled their oath and national duty of defending the nation and homeland to the last drop of their blood, sacrificing their lives and achieving immortality. The martyrs proved through their great sacrifices that Baloch sarmachars do not hesitate to make any sacrifice in the defense of the nation and homeland.
Izzat Baloch, alias Jummi, son of Master Noor, and Hamza Baloch, alias Waheed, son of Nako Faiz, residents of Tump, Dazin, were martyred in an attack by death squad operatives on January 1, 2026.
Izzat alias Jummi chose armed struggle for the liberation of Balochistan through the platform of the BLF in 2013. For three years, he fulfilled his responsibilities on the urban front with tireless effort and selfless dedication. Later, after coming under the surveillance of enemy intelligence, the organization transferred him to a camp, where he diligently fulfilled his national responsibilities across various fronts and participated in several significant engagements against the enemy.
Izzat immortalized his name in history by performing his national and organizational duties with honesty and sincerity. In addition to Martyr Izzat, several members of his family also made sacrifices for national liberation, earning an honorable place in national history.
Hamza alias Waheed Baloch joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in 2009 for the national struggle. He carried out every responsibility entrusted to him by the organization with tireless effort and dedication. His sacrifices, along with those of his family, provided strength and stability to the movement and the organization. His sacrifices will forever remain a part of the Baloch national memory.
Izzat alias Jummi and Martyr Hamza alias Waheed participated in military operations against the enemy across several areas, including Gwadar, Dasht, Tump, Turbat, and Mand, where, together with other sarmachars, they captured numerous military camps and carried out attacks on military convoys.

Farooq Pirkani, alias Asif, son of Haji Mohammad Murad Pirkani, was a resident of the Gohar Abad area of Quetta. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Nushki front. He was martyred on 13 September 2026 in the Sultan Shar area of Qila Abdullah.
Farooq Pirkani, son of Haji Mohammad Murad Pirkani, became part of the Baloch Liberation Army’s resistance in 2026 for the freedom of his homeland. Choosing this path at a young age marked the beginning of a major change in his life. He was a quiet, serious young man who placed great importance on his responsibilities. He was later deployed to the Noshki area, where harsh weather conditions, long journeys, and continuous physical exertion tested his endurance. During this short period, while living alongside his comrades, he made discipline and mutual trust a part of his character.
On 13 September 2026, Farooq Pirkani attained martyrdom during an armed clash in the Sultan Shar area of Qila Abdullah. Despite his age, limited experience, and the short period of his life spent on this path, his comrades continued to remember him as a young man who was serious about the path he had chosen and who did not step back in difficult times. His martyrdom left a void for those close to him, while the memories associated with him remained among the people who had shared this journey with him.

Mumtaz Ahmad Kurd, son of Bijjar Khan, a 34 year old resident of Mach, Bolan, was a social worker. He was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 12 November 2010 by Pakistani forces. After months of enforced disappearance, his body was found on 19 January 2011 in Ghanja Dori, Mastung.

Two cousins, Shukrullah, son of Salam and Nadeem, son of Sharaf, both residents of the Rakshan area in Panjgur, who were allegedly forcibly disappeared, have been found - one dead and the other critically injured - in Panjgur district, Balochistan.
Both were reportedly detained by paramilitary Frontier Corps (FC) personnel at a checkpoint in the Washbud area of Panjgur district on February 3, 2025. Two days later on February 5, 2025 Shukrullah was found dead, while Nadeem was discovered in critical condition in the Soorap area of Panjgur. According to eyewitnesses, the two were thrown from a white Surf vehicle with black-tinted windows, a type of vehicle often associated with intelligence agencies. Witnesses confirmed that Shukrullah had already succumbed to his injuries at the time of discovery, with visible signs of severe torture on his body. Nadeem, barely alive, was rushed for medical treatment.
The victims’ families have allegedly been threatened and warned against sharing pictures or speaking out about the incident. They were reportedly pressured to bury the deceased quietly. Government officials have neither confirmed nor commented on the incident.

On 16 February 2022, the ground forces of the Pakistani state, accompanied by air support, attacked a camp of the Baloch Nationalist Army in the early hours of the morning in the mountainous area of Kulbar, Tump. A prolonged skirmish ensued, beginning at 6:00 AM and continuing until 5:00 PM, during which the Baloch Sarmachars killed several enemy commandos and partially damaged two enemy helicopters.
In this clash, Noor Salam Noor alias Istaal, son of Bahar Baloch and a resident of Dashtuk Zamuran; Zubair Akram alias Asadjan, son of Akram Baloch and a resident of Hotabad Zamuran Bazaar; Kambar Baloch alias Mehrwan, son of Tariq and a resident of Kolaho; Sageer Baloch alias Tariq, son of Noorbakhsh and a resident of Basima; Rasool Jan alias Chirag, son of Ali Jan and a resident of Sarankan; and Hafiz Faraz alias Mullah Darwish, son of Abdul Ghani and a resident of Sarankan, were martyred.

Hameed Shaheen Baloch, the former chairman of the Baloch Students Organization (BSO), was abducted on 20 March 2011 and forcibly disappeared. The following day, 21 March 2011, his body was found in Quetta.

On 11 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch announced the martyrdom of 14 fighters of the organization who attained martyrdom in confrontations with the Pakistani army and in airstrikes while defending their homeland, Balochistan, and fighting for national liberation and the right to self-determination.

On 13 August 2026, Pakistani Air Force fighter jets bombarded the Pandran area of Kalat District in Balochistan, resulting in the martyrdom of four members of the organization: Waseem Baloch, alias Farhan; Obaidullah Baloch, alias Shaheen; Nawaz Ali Baloch, alias Dilshad; and Mohammad Hassan, alias Ahmad.

On 25 August 2026, during an organizational mission in the Kech area of Balochistan, Sher Jan, alias Jamal, was shot from behind by a traitor, resulting in his martyrdom.

On 3 September 2026, while patrolling in the Mastung area of Balochistan, the organization’s brave fighters, Mohammad Younis, alias Salal; Sameer Ahmad, alias Zemal; Aziz Ahmad, alias Janan; and Sikandar Baloch, confronted Pakistani forces, targeted several enemy personnel, and embraced martyrdom.

On 14 September 2026, while engaging Pakistani forces and defending his fellow fighters in the Machani Kor Paroom area of Panjgur District, Babar Baloch, alias Kambar, embraced martyrdom.

On 18 September 2026, during a confrontation with Pakistani forces in the Chagi area of Balochistan, fighters of the organization, Riaz Baloch, alias Sabir; Taimoor Shah, alias Shaheen; Zia Ul Haq, alias Ziaullah; and Jumma Baloch, alias Commando, embraced martyrdom.

Nawaz Ali Baloch, alias Dilshad, son of Mohammad Akbar, resident of Pandran, Kalat, had been carrying out his national duties very effectively as an urban guerrilla through the BLF platform since 2024. After coming to the enemy's attention, he was moved to the mountain front in 2026 under an organizational decision. He was martyred on the morning of 13 August 2026 in an aerial bombardment by the enemy.

On 22 July 2026, the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) released the details of seven martyred members of the organization: Abdul Ghafoor, alias Chakar, son of Jan Mohammad; Imdad Baloch, alias Nodh, son of Rahmatullah; Hafiz Mumtaz Baloch, alias Zeerak, son of Sabir Ali; Hafiz Zaid Baloch, alias Sagaar, son of Mullah Khudadad; Yasir Baloch, alias Ajiz, son of Mohammad Ayub; Shahjan Baloch, alias Sawad, son of Ali Mohammad; and Ali Raza Baloch, alias Shayhaq, son of Haji Ali Ahmad. They were martyred in a drone strike by Pakistani forces on 29 January 2026 in the Pardan area of Panjgur District, Balochistan.

Hafiz Mumtaz, alias Zeerak, son of Sabir Ali, was a resident of Damban, Rakshan, Panjgur. He joined on 25 August 2025 and served in Panjgur before being killed on 29 January 2026 in Pardan, Panjgur.
Hafiz Mumtaz, alias Zeerak, decided to join the ranks of the Baloch Liberation Army in 2025 and joined the organization's camp in Panjgur, where he began his activities with remarkable dedication. He remained active in the camp as a skilled, hardworking, and resilient fighter. After completing basic military training courses, he quickly established himself among his Sangats as an active, agile, and sharp Sarmachar. In every activity within the camp, he was always at the forefront.
Within a very short period, he played a significant role in promoting what he considered the finest revolutionary culture and remained steadfast in following the principles in which he believed. There was no room for negligence or complacency in his conduct or character; rather, he was counted among those Sarmachars who devoted themselves tirelessly, day and night, to fulfilling their organizational responsibilities. He always possessed a strong eagerness to learn and contribute as much as possible, a quality that remained one of the defining aspects of his personality. Within a short span of time, he had already begun taking part in attacks against the enemy. While pursuing the enemy alongside his fellow Sangats from a temporary camp, he was killed in an enemy drone strike that occurred after their location was revealed through a tracking chip planted by informants.
During his brief period of service in the cause of national liberation, he laid the foundations of revolutionary principles and conduct that, according to his supporters, will continue to serve as a guiding light for his Sangats. By choosing the path of freedom over submission, the blood he shed for his homeland will, according to this account, never be in vain; rather, it will become a source of inspiration for generations to come.

On June 18, 2009, in the Sakrand area of Nawabshah district in Sindh, on the night between Thursday and Friday, Pakistani intelligence agencies carried out a heavy-weapons attack on the house of Mureed Bugti, a leader of the Baloch Republican Party (BRP) and a close associate of Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti. In this attack, Mureed Bugti and his relative Huzoor Bakhsh were killed, while Mureed Bugti’s two daughters were injured.
Mureed Bugti and his friend Huzoor Bakhsh were shot and killed by personnel of Pakistani intelligence agencies in Sakrand, in the Nawabshah district of Sindh.
After the killing of Nawab Akbar Khan Bugti, Mureed Bugti joined the Baloch Republican Party (BRP) in 2008, a new political party formed by Brahumdagh Bugti. As an active political worker and member of the BRP Central Committee, he had been working in Dera Bugti, Nasirabad, and Jaffarabad.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
In Gwadar, nine Fidayeen of the BLA Majeed Brigade were divided into two units and took part in the operation. The first unit, which included Fidayeen Hawa Baloch (alias Droshum), Yahya Lal (alias Lashari), Adnan Arman (alias Changaiz), and Yousif Baloch (alias Yagi), attacked the compound of the occupying Pakistani intelligence agencies, resulting in the elimination of 12 personnel. Women and children in residential quarters near the compound were provided safe passage; however, the occupying army later martyred these same civilians by opening fire.
About forty minutes later, occupying forces advanced toward the compound, leading to clashes that continued until the evening. In these clashes, more than 24 personnel were eliminated, and three military vehicles, including an armored vehicle, were destroyed.
The second squad, which included Fidayeen Kambar Ismail (alias Sarbaz), Khurshid KB (alias Arman), Waseem Baloch (alias Kareem), Shoaib Baloch (alias Shehzad), and Yasir, took up strong positions in Port Bazaar near Gwadar Port. After announcements were made in mosques, freedom fighters went to the bazaar, met the public, and held political discussions. After repelling the advance of occupying forces in the city, the freedom fighters later advanced toward the port and fired several rockets that hit their targets. Clashes continued until the next day, eliminating more than 19 personnel.
Waseem Baloch, also known as Kareem, son of Mohammad Hayat, was 21 years old and a resident of Nasirabad, Turbat district, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in 2024 and became part of the Majeed Brigade in April 2025. Waseem’s path was defined by clarity of purpose and steadfastness under pressure. At a young age, he carried responsibility with composure, remaining present and resolute at the Gwadar front during Operation Herof 2. His martyrdom marked a life remembered for courage rooted in conviction.

data.organization: Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) / Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS)

Lal Bakhsh, alias Drapshan, son of Rasool Bakhsh, was a resident of the Kurki area of Turbat district, Balochistan. He joined the BLA on August 10, 2025, and remained active on the Kalat Front.
Lal Bakhsh, alias Drapshan, was a bright student from the Kurki area of Turbat whose journey reflects a profound transition from academic pursuit to national resistance. Having completed his FSc, he was rigorously preparing to become a doctor. However, the wounds of his motherland redirected his path from healing individuals to serving the collective cause of his people.
Lal Bakhsh hailed from an illustrious family of martyrs whose blood has nurtured the liberation movement. He was the cousin of Martyr Shahmeer and Martyr Ameer, as well as the renowned Fidayeen: Fidayi Farooq, Fidayi Sawali, and Fidayi Bilal. Growing up in such a dedicated environment, it was impossible for him to ignore the call of his soil. On August 10, 2025, he formally chose the path of armed struggle, and due to his intellect and resolve, he was inducted into the specialized unit, STOS.
After remaining active on the Kalat front, Lal Bakhsh fought against the enemy in Noshki during “Operation Herof Phase II.” In the intense clashes of Noshki, he upheld his family’s valiant traditions, fighting with immense courage before embracing martyrdom. By sacrificing his life, he joined the ranks of his esteemed cousins. Lal Bakhsh’s sacrifice stands as a symbol of the conviction of educated Baloch youth, who prioritize national liberation above personal careers and worldly success.

Asim Karim Baloch, a 28-year-old son of Mohammad Karim and a resident of Basima, was a leader of the Baloch Students Organization – Azad (BSO-Azad). He was abducted on 30 October 2010 and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. On 1 November 2010, his body was found in Khanozai, Pashin.

Fareed Baloch, alias Babar, son of Zahid Baloch, was a resident of Jaheen, Paroom, Panjgur. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2026, served on the Panjgur front, and was martyred on 3 June 2026 in Chedagi, Panjgur, Balochistan.
Fareed was fully aware of the importance of preserving national dignity, collective survival, and the Baloch identity and homeland. He also understood that an occupying force, which has imposed itself upon us through arms and military might and seeks to perpetuate its occupation, can only be defeated through effective force and organized military strength. He did not confine this political consciousness to mere sympathy for the movement; rather, he translated it into practice by deciding to join the Baloch Liberation Army earlier this year. Acting upon the directives of the organization, he undertook his national and military responsibilities on the Panjgur front.
He belonged to a new generation of cadres who possessed a clear understanding of the pace and intensity of warfare, as well as modern military requirements and culture. He incorporated this military culture into his practical activities and, after completing his basic military training courses, joined the ranks of frontline fighters. His conduct reflected not only professional military discipline but also deep political consciousness and revolutionary commitment. He put these revolutionary principles into practice within the framework of military discipline and employed them effectively in the struggle against the enemy. On the Panjgur front, he played a significant role alongside his fellow Sarmachars in maintaining the economic blockade imposed by the Baloch Liberation Army against the occupying forces.
Guided by the conscious conviction and national commitment that had led him to join the war front, he remained steadfast in those principles until his last breath and embraced martyrdom in the course of this struggle. His sacrifices serve as a clear message to the younger generation: to understand the national, moral, and revolutionary realities of their time and to become part of this great national struggle, which is regarded as the guarantor of collective survival, freedom, and a brighter future.

data.fullName: Peer Mohammad Peerak, alias Major Noora
data.biography:
On the night between Saturday and Sunday, at 3:00 AM on April 25, 2020, Pakistani forces, along with local death squads, surrounded Baloch fighters (Sarmachaars) in Yar Mohammad Bazaar, located in the Parom Kallag Kor area of Panjgur district. A clash broke out between the forces and the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) fighters, which continued for twelve hours.
The fighting lasted until 2:30 PM on April 26, 2020. After the Pakistani ground forces retreated, military helicopters shelled the fighters, resulting in the killing of four Sarmachaars - Major Noora, son of Sher Dil, alias Peerak; Lieutenant Nawaz, son of Haji Ghulam Hussain; Abdul Malik, son of Haji Ghulam Hussain; Momin, son of Mohammad Azeem - During this prolonged twelve hour clash, several soldiers of the Pakistani army and associated death squads were killed and injured.

Major Noora, alias Peerak, son of Sher Dil, was born in 1992 in Parom, Panjgur, Balochistan. He had been associated with the Baloch national liberation movement and armed struggle for over a decade. He was a highly intelligent and capable fighter. He not only served in various roles across different regions of Balochistan, providing significant military contributions, but also played an important role in organizing the Balochistan Liberation Front through his abilities.

Lieutenant Nawaz, alias Gulab, son of Ghulam Hussain, was born in Parom. He had been associated with the BLF and the armed struggle for ten years and, due to his dedication and capabilities, attained the rank of Lieutenant.

Abdul Malik, son of Ghulam Hussain, was also born in Parom and had been associated with the armed organization BLF for two years.

Momin Baloch, son of Mohammad Azeem, was born in Buleda Salo and had been actively engaged in the armed struggle for two years.
data.martyrdomPlace: Yar Mohammad Bazar, kallag Kor, Parom, Panjgur district, Balochistan

data.biography: Abdul Khaliq, son of Yar Mohd Baloch and a resident of Kahndari, Mashkai, was a veterinary doctor by profession and started his job in 2004. He became part of the Baloch freedom struggle in 2009 through the platform of BLF. He was known for his bravery and for being a disciplined and courageous freedom fighter of Balochistan. Abdul Khaliq was martyred along with his comrade, Abdul Rasheed, in a clash with Pakistani forces on 12 December 2015 in Tank-kor, Mashkai.

On 9 September 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of ten fighters belonging to the organization. He paid tribute to the Sarmachars who were martyred while defending national liberation and their homeland, Balochistan.
- The statement identified the following fighters:
1-  Akhtar Dawood, alias Ali Sher, son of Asad Sajidi.
2- Khalil Ahmad, alias Ustad Awais, son of Sher Ahmad.
3-  Imran, alias Aajo, son of Saifullah.
4-  Hasil, alias Munir Ahmad, son of Sher Mohammad.
5- Inayatullah, alias Sher Zaman, son of Manzoor Ahmad.
6- Asad Rahim, son of Rahim Baksh.
7- Mujeeb Ur Rehman, alias Shay Mureed, son of Saeed Ahmad.
8- Sahil, alias Arman, son of Peeral.
9- Javed, alias Murshid.
10- Mohammad Younis, alias Taleb, son of Mohammad Omar.

Imran, alias Aajo, son of Saifullah, resident of Killi Shahnawaz, Sariyab, had been associated with the Balochistan Liberation Front in the Baloch national war of liberation for the past two years. He was a hafiz of the Quran and a conscientious person. Despite his young age, he was a shining example of courage and determination for all his friends. Wherever the organization needed him, he would go to carry out national duties. In this way he rendered national service on the fronts of Naghau, Maraan, Kachhi, and Quetta, and through his exemplary character carried out significant responsibilities in the national struggle for freedom. On 14 August 2026, he was on an organizational patrol with fellow fighters in the Deghari area of Quetta when Pakistani army personnel appeared in plain clothes and unmarked vehicles, sparking a clash that lasted about an hour. Imran, alias Aajo, and Khalil Ahmed, alias Ustad Awais, stood like a mountain before the enemy to help their friends withdraw safely. During the clash, Ustad Awais was martyred and Aajo was severely wounded but disregarding his wounds he continued to strike at the enemy and helped the remaining fighters get away safely. He fought on for an hour, standing firm before the enemy until his last breath. The Baloch national liberation movement is full of great examples of sacrifice and bravery, but Aajo, at such a young age, wrote a new chapter that stands as an enviable and proud example of courage for generations to come.

data.fullName: Martyr Fedayi Murad Hasil Alias Farhad Baloch

data.biography:
According to a statement issued by Gwahram Baloch, spokesman for the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) on 30 November 2025 the Pakistani military launched a combined air and ground operation against BLF fighters (Sarmachars) in the Dhadar area of Kachhi district on 28 November. The operation lasted for 24 hours.
During the operation, at around 1 AM the enemy air force fired three missiles using drones targeting the Sarmachars. However, all Sarmachars managed to escape the attack unharmed.
The next morning, at approximately 6 AM the Sarmachars engaged in direct combat with Pakistani forces, leading to intense fighting. In this clash, Qadir Ahmed, alias Diljan, son of Abdul Malik, was martyred.
The martyred fighter, Qadir Ahmed (alias Diljan), son of Abdul Malik Bangulzai, resident of Isplinji, Mastung, had joined the Balochistan Liberation Front just two months prior to his martyrdom in pursuit of Baloch national liberation. In this short time, he proved himself to be a dedicated and fearless fighter.

In a statement issued on 19 November 2025 by Mazaar Baloch, spokesperson of the Baloch United Army (UBA), it was said that on 4 November at 7:30 in the morning, the Pakistan Air Force carried out a drone strike using guided missiles in the mountain range of Koh-e-Nagai in the Kalat region. As a result, four Sarmachars were martyred, including a fighter from the brother organization, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF). The organization pays tribute to them.

The fire that broke out after the drone attack severely burned the surrounding land, while unusual marks were also found on nearby rocks and stones, indicating that the weapons used contained chemical elements. The attack not only caused serious damage to the local environment but also left deep effects on the area’s natural balance.

Those who attained martyrdom in the drone attack include Dr. Mudasir Shahwani, alias Sarbuland Baloch; Shahbaz Khan Budani Marri, alias Peer Jan; Shakir Jatoi Baloch, alias Rudin Baloch; and Haris Muhammad Shahi Baloch, alias Aftab Baloch.

Dr. Mudasir Shahwani was affiliated with the pro-independence organization Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF). He belonged to Killi Choto in Mastung. After joining the organization, he not only proved his abilities on the battlefield but also served exceptionally as a doctor by treating comrades and civilians. Our organization pays tribute to the great services, sacrifices and selfless struggle of our martyred comrade Dr. Mudasir Shahwani for humanity.

On 3 November 2024, Pakistan's Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) extrajudicially killed three Baloch - Mohammad Nawaz Buzdar, Ghulam Buzdar, and Jaffar Marri - in a staged encounter in the Rarasham area of Musakhel District. All three had previously been abducted and forcibly disappeared by the so called Counter Terrorism Department (CTD) of the Pakistani genocidal forces from Rarasham.

Mohammad Nawaz Buzdar, a resident of Rarasham Barg Posht, was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 10 September 2024, from Rarasham, Musakhel District.

Ghulam Buzdar, a resident of Rarasham, was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 21 September 2024, from Rarasham, Musakhel District.

Jaffar Marri was abducted and forcibly disappeared on 2 October 2024, from Rarasham, Musakhel District.

Martyr Akhtar Baloch, alias Rustom Baloch, was a resident of Mastung, Balochistan. He became part of the Baloch liberation movement on the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in 2003. He was an active member of the BLA. He embraced martyrdom on December 25, 2018, along with General Aslam Baloch, Babar Majeed, Kareem Baloch, Aman Ullah Baloch, and Taj Muhammad Baloch.

On 3rd April 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that fighters of the BLA launched a series of coordinated attacks against the occupying Pakistani army across occupied Balochistan on 29th March 2026, which continued until 1st April 2026. The fighters carried out 65 operations in Panjgur, Shapuk, Basima, Sibi, Mastung, Quetta, Noshki, Zamuran, Dasht, Surab, Jhal Magsi, Dalbandin, Kharan, Washuk, and Kalat. In these actions, more than 86 personnel of the Pakistani army, death squads, and intelligence agencies were killed, and dozens were injured. These attacks targeted occupying army camps, an airbase, radar systems, communication towers, railway tracks, bridges, and gas pipelines, while major highways were brought under control for several hours.
During clashes with Pakistani forces, five BLA fighters in Panjgur - Zahid alias Nawaz, Saeedullah alias Meraj, Jahanzeb alias Qambar, Aamir alias Khalid, and Saddam alias Shahwaiz - along with Abdust (Abdul Rehman) alias Alman in Zamuran, attained martyrdom.
Aamir, alias Khalid (son of Dr. Abdul Wahid): From Khudabadan, Panjgur, he served as an urban guerrilla from 2022 before moving to the mountain front in 2024. He performed valuable services in the Kilkor, Guargo, Parom, and Panjgur sectors.

Adam khan Lehri, alias Shoaib, son of Ghulam Mohammad Lehri was resident of Gazag, Gawar, Kalat, he Joined BLA on 2022 as urban Warrior and Remained in torture Cells for one Year later moved in Mountain Front after release on 2023 and Operated in Kalat front and martyred on 18 May 2026, in Sorab, Balochistan.
Adam Lehri endured some of the harshest conditions throughout his revolutionary journey, yet he never retreated from the struggle for national freedom. As a dedicated freedom fighter, he viewed every hardship as an integral part of the revolutionary struggle and used it to further strengthen and organize his resistance against the occupying enemy.
In his early years, he remained active as a guerrilla Sarmchar, where he inflicted significant blows upon the enemy on numerous occasions. He was also imprisoned in the enemy’s torture cells for a period of one year, during which he endured severe physical and psychological abuse. However, all these hardships, cruelties, and acts of repression only served to strengthen his resolve and determination.

With this firm conviction and unwavering resolve, he moved to the mountain front in 2023 under the decision of the party and made it his new battlefield. Over the past three years, he played a significant role in expanding the organization’s military units in Kalat and its surrounding areas, strengthening organizational policies, and participating in numerous important engagements against the enemy across different fronts, inflicting heavy losses upon them.

Adam Lehri’s steadfastness, his unwavering commitment to the movement until his last breath, and his ultimate sacrifice are clear reflections of his intellectual maturity and profound national conviction. The Baloch nation will remember him as a conscious, ideological, and nationally committed freedom fighter who embraced martyrdom while fulfilling his professional military responsibilities and performing his national duty in the struggle for the restoration of the State of Balochistan.

Izhar, son of Mullah Mujeeb and a resident of Lebanon sub-tehsil, Mand (district Kech), was shot dead by state-backed death squads in the Soro area of Mand on September 6, 2025.

According to reports, state-backed death squads opened fire on Izhar while he was at his shop earlier in the morning. He was rushed to the hospital after sustaining critical injuries, but succumbed due to excessive bleeding.

Local sources confirm that the perpetrators were state-backed death squads operating under the command of Pakistani forces.

On October 16, 2025, Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) freedom fighters took control of a Levies Force outpost at Mill Shahurai in Surab and seized the personnel’s weapons. The outpost had been involved in extortion, prompting the operation. Meanwhile, another squad blocked the Quetta–Karachi highway for over an hour and conducted snap checks.

During the blockade, a police vehicle arrived. The fighters asked the personnel to surrender their weapons with a guarantee of safety. All complied, but one personnel opened fire, resulting in the martyrdom of Maqbool Baloch, alias Bali, and serious injuries to Kamran Baloch, alias Sahrot, who later succumbed to his wounds on the way. The personnel who opened fire was neutralized in retaliation.

Martyr Maqbool Mohammad Hassni, alias Bali, son of Mola Bakhsh Muhammad Hassni, belonged to Ahmedwal, Noshki. Known for bravery and sincerity, he joined the BLA earlier this year and quickly earned respect due to his hard work and fighting skills. He served on the fronts of Shoor Parod, Noshki, and Kharan.

Martyr Kamran Sumalani, alias Sahrot, son of Martyr Jalaluddin, also from Ahmedwal, Noshki, joined the BLA in March this year. He served on the fronts of Shoor Parod, Noshki, and Kharan, dedicating his days and nights to the cause of national liberation until his last breath.

On August 22, 2025, Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) freedom fighters were traveling in the Tilukan area of Tump for organizational duties when a clash with the occupying army occurred. Several enemy personnel were neutralized and injured in the engagement, while fighter Zahid Saleh alias Wahid fought bravely and was martyred.

Martyr Zahid alias Captain Wahid, son of Saleh Muhammad, hailed from Nizarabad in the Tump area of Kech, Balochistan. Known among his comrades for his combat skills, Zahid joined the armed movement for the Baloch national liberation struggle in 2014.

Martyr Zahid alias Wahid joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2023 and served on the Tump, Zamuran, and Dasht fronts. He was a seasoned training partner who dedicated every moment of his life to the cause of the motherland.

On 16 May 2026 renowned Brahui language poet and academic Professor Mohammad Khan Sasoli, also known as Ghamkhwar Hayat, son of Abdul Majeed Sasoli, was killed in the Killi Mengal area of Noshki district, Balochistan, after armed men opened fire near his residence.
Sources said that the attackers were allegedly members of a state backed armed group locally referred to as a death squad.
Mohammad Khan was an assistant professor at Government Boys Degree College in Noshki district. He was known as a Brahui fiction writer, translator, poet and essayist and had authored 20 books.
He was also among the founders of Raskoh Adabi Diwan and Hotan Culture Academy, two literary and cultural institutions associated with the Brahui language and culture.
His name had also been placed on the Fourth Schedule some time ago, a list maintained under Pakistan's Anti Terrorism Act for proscribed persons, subjecting those listed to restrictions that can include frozen bank accounts, passport denial and limits on arms licences and employment clearances.
Rights groups, political parties, and literary figures described his killing as a serious loss to Brahui literature and Balochistan’s intellectual circles.

On 31 January 2025 during an attack on enemy forces at the Siyah Gazi area of Awaran, a BRAS sarmachar (fighter), Balochistan Shaukat, alias Kamash Dildar, son of Ali Murad and a resident of Kolwah Sagak, was martyred in an accident when a rocket launcher accidentally exploded.
Martyr Shaukat had been affiliated with the allied organization, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) since 2014. Over the course of eleven years, he served with perseverance and sincerity in the struggle to achieve Baloch national freedom. Martyr Kamash Dildar participated in Bras operations on multiple fronts and inflicted significant losses on the enemy.

On March 5, 2026, Omar Jan, son of Ali, a 19-year-old driver and resident of Sabzal Bazar in Paroom, Tehsil of Panjgur District, was directly targeted and killed by a state-backed local death squad in the Kaleri area of Paroom.
He worked as a driver near the Gold Smith line to financially support his family. Following the incident, his body was reportedly taken to the Paroom military camp. Authorities later contacted the family and asked them to come and receive his body. When the family arrived at the camp, they were reportedly pressured by security personnel to sign a document stating that Omar Jan had been involved in anti-state activities and labeling him a "terrorist." The family refused to sign the document, rejecting the allegations against him.
After their refusal, Omar Jan’s body was handed over to his family on March 6, 2026.
Atta Jan Baloch, was a resident of the Mashkai area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 30 June 2015 in Balochistan.

Martyr Hasil Baloch, son of Pullan Baloch and Zar Jan Baloch, was a resident of Awaran, Balochistan. He became part of the Baloch liberation movement through the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in 2014. After five years, in 2019, he affiliated with the pro-independence armed organization Baloch Republican Army (BRA). He was injured during a clash in Jhaoo, Awaran, in 2018. He was killed by a Pakistani military agent in Saravan, Sistan and Balochistan, on October 15, 2021.

On 15 February 2017, in broad daylight, a local death squad operating under the patronage of the Pakistani state killed Tahir Baloch in cold blood inside the Gomazi Health Center, where he worked as a male nurse. He was killed as part of state collective punishment, solely because his brother, Sikandar Baloch, was affiliated with the armed organization Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF).
Not only him, but his father, Chairman Dost Mohammed Baloch, was also abducted on 21 May 2017 and extrajudicially killed by Pakistani forces. On 25 May 2017, his body was dumped in Kunchiti Dasht.
On 1 April 2022, his brother Sikandar Baloch was martyred in the Mand Mountains by Pakistani forces.

Shahid Nadeem, son of Lal Baksh and a resident of Gwarjk, Mashkai, was a teacher by profession and a brave freedom fighter. He joined the BLF in 2009 and remained associated with it until his martyrdom. He was martyred in a clash with the Pakistan Army in the Seegak area of Kolwah on 1 August 2016.
His family suffered under Pakistan's policy of collective punishment. Several members of his family were affected, including his two brothers, Shaheed Asif Nadeem and Shaheed Basit Nadeem, who were also martyred.

Talib Nazeer, a Balochi-language singer and shopkeeper from the Menaz area of Buleda, Kech, was shot and killed at his home on 1 March 2026. Talib was unarmed. He was a civilian who used his voice to celebrate and preserve the Balochi language, culture, and identity. Pakistani state-backed death squads are empowered to carry out such targeted attacks.

Qambar Baloch, son of Khuda Baksh, was a 19 year old student from Sohlo, Buleda, in Turbat district, Balochistan.
On October 7, 2025, he was forcibly disappeared from his home in Sohlo, Buleda. For six months, his family waited in pain, hope, and silence.
On April 8, 2026, his lifeless body was dumped in D-Baloch, Turbat. His body bore multiple bullet wounds and clear signs of brutal torture.

On 30 September 2024, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that they pay tribute to their six comrades - Shafo Sumalani alias Tadain, Samad Khan Chalgari Marri alias Dostain, Mohammad Gul Marri alias Waheed Baloch, Ghulam Qadir Marri alias Anjeer Baloch, Obaid Baloch alias Fida, and Taj Mohammad Chalgari Marri alias Babul - who were martyred in a bombing by jet fighters of the Pakistani Air Force in Harnai, Balochistan. On 12 September, at 4 AM, jet fighters of the Pakistani Air Force dropped several heavy and deadly bombs on BLA fighters, with the support of drone surveillance, in the Ali Khan Thal area of Harnai, Balochistan. As a result of the bombing, six fighters were martyred. After the attack, the morally bankrupt enemy desecrated the bodies of the martyred fighters and took their body parts using gunship helicopters.

Shafo Sumalani alias Tadain Baloch hailed from Bolan Gharbo. He began his struggle in 2016 through the platform of BLA. Over the past eight years, he steadfastly served on various war fronts. He will always be remembered as a dedicated, hardworking, and sincere fighter.

On 29 April 2026, the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson, Gwahram Baloch, announced the martyrdom of six fighters of the organization, paid tribute to them, and stated that the organization’s fighters were martyred in the national war of liberation. The martyrs include Ikram Baloch (alias Hameed), Shaibaz Shohaz (alias Kiyya), Masood Baloch (alias Bharag), Salman Waheeda (alias Chirag), Izzat Baloch (alias Jummi), and Hamza Baloch (alias Waheed).
The spokesperson further stated that the martyred fighters fulfilled their oath and national duty of defending the nation and homeland to the last drop of their blood, sacrificing their lives and achieving immortality. The martyrs proved through their great sacrifices that Baloch sarmachars do not hesitate to make any sacrifice in the defense of the nation and homeland.
Izzat Baloch, alias Jummi, son of Master Noor, and Hamza Baloch, alias Waheed, son of Nako Faiz, residents of Tump, Dazin, were martyred in an attack by death squad operatives on January 1, 2026.
Izzat alias Jummi chose armed struggle for the liberation of Balochistan through the platform of the BLF in 2013. For three years, he fulfilled his responsibilities on the urban front with tireless effort and selfless dedication. Later, after coming under the surveillance of enemy intelligence, the organization transferred him to a camp, where he diligently fulfilled his national responsibilities across various fronts and participated in several significant engagements against the enemy.
Izzat immortalized his name in history by performing his national and organizational duties with honesty and sincerity. In addition to Martyr Izzat, several members of his family also made sacrifices for national liberation, earning an honorable place in national history.
Hamza alias Waheed Baloch joined the Balochistan Liberation Front in 2009 for the national struggle. He carried out every responsibility entrusted to him by the organization with tireless effort and dedication. His sacrifices, along with those of his family, provided strength and stability to the movement and the organization. His sacrifices will forever remain a part of the Baloch national memory.
Izzat alias Jummi and Martyr Hamza alias Waheed participated in military operations against the enemy across several areas, including Gwadar, Dasht, Tump, Turbat, and Mand, where, together with other sarmachars, they captured numerous military camps and carried out attacks on military convoys.

In 1838, the British sent a force led by Alexander Burnes to reinstate Shah Shuja Durrani as the king of Afghanistan by deposing Amir Dost Mohammad Khan. To reach Afghanistan, they needed passage through Balochistan, particularly the Bolan Pass. However, Khan Mehrab Khan refused to allow the British to use his land to attack a neighboring country. The British sent Lieutenant Leach to negotiate with the Baloch government, but the Khan stood firm. When British forces reached Shaal via Bolan, some patriotic Baloch, without the Khan’s knowledge, attacked British troops out of nationalist sentiment and a desire to protect their homeland.
After toppling Amir Dost Mohammad Khan, the British Governor General of India, Lord Auckland, ordered an attack on Balochistan. In 1839, around 7,000 British troops marched from Shaal to attack the Baloch Meeri (capital). Anticipating an invasion, Khan Mehrab Khan declared war and sent messages to tribal leaders, but many saw the British as allies rather than invaders and chose to collaborate with them rather than defend their land. When Khan Mehrab Khan gathered his resistance fighters, the number of loyal warriors had dwindled to only 700 due to the short sightedness of many tribal chiefs. Nevertheless, Mehrab Khan was determined to fight. At his court, a respected figure, Akhund Muhammad Siddiq, advised him that he was not in a position to wage war at that time. He suggested that the Khan should leave Kalat with his companions, regroup and strengthen his forces, and then launch an attack against the British when the time was right, on 13 November 1839, the British forces launched an attack on Kalat, and a fierce battle ensued. During the fighting, Khan Mehrab Khan Baloch was martyred by a British bullet.

Among those martyred alongside him were:

Diwan Bacha Mal, Minister of Finance

Diwan Khem Chand

Diwan Asardas Mukhi, from the Hindu Panchayat of Kalat

Abdul Karim Raisani, brother of Sardar Asad Khan Raisani

Sardar Wali Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (maternal uncle of Martyr Amir Mehrab Khan)

Mir Taj Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (cousin of Mehrab Khan)

Mir Muhammad Ali Shahizai Mengal

Mir Fazal Muhammad Lehri, brother of Sardar Muhammad Khan Lehri

Sardar Zaman Khan Pandrani

Mir Dad Karim Chandozai Shahwani

Mir Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Mir Badal Khan, brother of Sardar Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Khan Muhammad Dehwaar, Arbab-e-Kalat.

Mir Nabi Bakhsh Jatoi, from the Narmak region of Kalat

Mir Qaiser Khan Bizenjo

Mir Shah Dost Bizenjo

Muhammad Raza Waziri Khel

Noor Muhammad Shahizai, son of Polat Sagaar Sarmastani, in charge of the armory

Taj Muhammad Shagasi
Hayat Baloch, was a resident of the Buleda area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 9 February 2018 in Balochistan.

Bakar Baloch, son of Allah Bakhsh and a resident of Chidagi, Awaran, was summoned by Pakistani military personnel to their headquarters in Waja-e-Bhag, Jahoo tehsil, district Awaran, on September 12, 2025. He was subsequently detained and subjected to enforced disappearance.

After a week in captivity, on September 20, his body was discovered in the Majid area of Jahoo, Awaran, alongside that of a close relative.

Both bodies bore clear signs of brutal torture, underscoring the systematic practice of enforced disappearances, custodial torture, and extrajudicial executions carried out by Pakistani forces in Balochistan.

data.fullName: Ishaq Shokat Baloch, alias Meeran Baloch
data.biography:
On 20 October 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that Sarmachars (freedom fighters) of the BLA had carried out 34 high-intensity military operations over 12 days across various regions of Balochistan between 9 and 20 October 2026. In these attacks, 14 personnel of the occupying army and nine operatives of Military Intelligence and death squads were killed, while operational control and snap-checking on key highways continued successfully under the organisational policy of an “economic blockade.”

During these operations, the freedom fighters also captured a serving soldier of the Pakistani army. In face-to-face clashes with occupying forces on various fronts, six BLA fighters fought courageously and attained the highest status of martyrdom.

Amanullah Mengal, alias Meerak, who was severely injured in a quadcopter attack by the occupying army at Ziarat Cross, succumbed to his injuries and was martyred on 8 August 2026.

On 18 September 2026, intense clashes took place between the occupying Pakistani army and BLA fighters at Siah Chang in Chagai, resulting in the deaths and injuries of several occupying army personnel, while the brave BLA fighter Ishaq Shokat Baloch, alias Meeran Baloch, attained martyrdom while fighting courageously.

On 19 September 2026, a prolonged and bloody confrontation took place between the occupying Pakistani army and BLA fighters at Paroom in Panjgur. During these clashes, four personnel of the occupying army were killed, several were injured, and one military vehicle was destroyed. In this battle, four BLA fighters - Ali Baloch, alias Salman Baloch; Ikhtiyar Baloch, alias Fareed Baloch; Sanaullah Baloch, alias Shay Mureed; and Sohail Baloch, alias Haji Absar - fought heroically and attained the highest status of martyrdom.

Ishaq Shokat Baloch, alias Meeran Baloch, son of Shokat, was a resident of Lan Bazar, Hoshab, Turbat. He joined the BLA on 10 November 2022 and served on the Shor Parod, Kalat, Nushki, and Chagi fronts. He was promoted to the rank of Patrol Commander and was martyred on 18 September 2026 in the Siyah Chang area of Chagi District, Balochistan.

Ishaq Shokat Baloch, alias Meeran Baloch, was a brave, deeply patriotic, responsible, and revolutionarily conscious fighter belonging to the Shor Parod front of the Baloch Liberation Army. He had served on the armed front for the past four years in defense of the nation and remained active in the BLA’s ranks for the freedom and defense of his homeland. His zeal for hard work, honesty, selflessness, and sacrifice was always evident in the way he carried out his duties. It was these qualities and his diligence that earned him important patrol command responsibilities in the region. He remained active in his duties as a steadfast Sarmachar until his final days.

His activities included preparation for Operation Hero, launching attacks on the enemy, enforcing an economic blockade against the enemy, expanding organizational activities into new areas, recruiting new youth into the BLA’s ranks, and carrying out various organizational duties. He fulfilled his responsibilities in various areas of the Shor Parod region, including Chagi, Nushki, Kalat, and other locations, in accordance with the organizational command’s directives. On September 18, during an encounter with the enemy at Chagai, he sacrificed his life for the defense and freedom of his homeland, securing his place forever in the annals of Baloch national history.

Haji Khalil Shahwani, alias Mama Marjan, son of Haji Qadir Bakhsh Shahwani, was a resident of Kili Shahnawaz, Saryab Mill, Quetta, Balochistan. He held a Bachelor's degree (BA). He joined the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) in 2025 and served on the Kalat and Zehri fronts. He was martyred on 26 June 2026 in Bulbul, Zehri, Balochistan.

Haji Khalil Shahwani, alias Mama Marjan, was an educated and politically conscious Sarmachar of the Baloch Liberation Army. He completed his Bachelor's degree, but instead of pursuing a personal life, he chose to dedicate himself to the collective and national interests of his people. To end Pakistan's illegal occupation of Balochistan, he chose the path of armed resistance. His decision was not merely about taking up arms and fighting; rather, he was committed to the collective belief that without an independent state, the homeland, national identity, and history of his people could never be safeguarded. Guided by this ideological conviction, he viewed armed resistance as a political program and joined the BLA.
After completing his basic military training, he was assigned by the organization's command to serve on its frontline defensive positions, where he stood firm against enemy advances and inflicted defeats upon them. He remained steadfast in defending those frontlines until his final days, ultimately sacrificing his life for his homeland and attaining an enduring legacy. Through his actions, character, and unwavering resolve, he demonstrated that the Baloch armed force had grown strong enough to confront the enemy's artificial power and to carry its defensive and offensive strategies through to their logical conclusion.
Martyr Marjan remained steadfast in the conscious and ideological commitment he made when he joined the struggle and upheld it until his final breath. Through his actions, he left a message for the entire nation: that it must confront the enemy with full determination and drive it out of Balochistan. His sacrifices will forever remain a part of the history of an independent and sovereign Balochistan.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Raza Baloch, alias Mashmar, son of Shabir Ahmad Gishkori, was a resident of Sibi. He joined the BLA in 2025 and served on the Shor Parod Front under the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS) unit. He was martyred during Operation Herof Phase II on the Noshki Front.
In the war of liberation, a person’s greatest strength is their conviction and willingness to sacrifice. Mashmar became part of the armed resistance with this very belief and philosophy. He embraced this path with full ideological commitment, believing that for oppressed nations the road to freedom passes through long resistance, steadfastness, and sacrifice.
During the battle on the Noshki Front in Operation Herof Phase II, Mashmar sacrificed his life while fighting against the enemy. Yet his sacrifice did not remain merely the loss of an individual; it became part of a larger struggle to free a nation from subjugation. Such figures demonstrate that when the youth of a nation keep the dream of freedom alive, even at the cost of their lives, the course of history ultimately turns toward liberation.

data.biography: Martyr Javid Baloch, son of  Mohammad Usman Baloch and was a resident of Gaddagi, Balgatar, area of Panjgur, Balochistan. He became part of Baloch liberation movement in platform of Baloch Republican Army (BRA) in 2013. He newly joined in Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) before same days of his martyrdom. He embraced martyrdom along with eight comrades, Jalil Sher Baloch, Samad Baloch, Dad Shah, Kambar Baloch, Shoaib Baloch, Rahmdil Baloch, Haris Baloch and Nawaz Baloch  in a drone attack of Pakistan Army  on Nov 29, 2022 in Jath, Kolwa area of Kech, Balochistan.

On May 4, 2025, Ehsan Shoukat, a 25-year-old resident of Kolahoo, Tump (Kech District), was extrajudicially executed by Military Intelligence (MI) personnel. He had previously been forcibly disappeared by Pakistan’s Frontier Corps (FC) and subjected to severe torture and inhumane treatment. Although he was eventually released, he continued to live under constant threat.
Ehsan operated a small medical clinic, assisting his father, Dr. Shoukat, by distributing medicines to local patients. Despite returning to a peaceful civilian life, he was deliberately targeted and killed. This assassination is part of a disturbing and systematic pattern across Balochistan: former victims of enforced disappearance are being hunted down and eliminated.
