Qadir Kashani Baloch, alias Baloch Khan, son of Ghulam Mohammad Kashani, was a resident of the Killi Qasim area of Dalbandin in Chaghi District, Balochistan. He held an MA degree in Political Science from the University of Management and Technology, Lahore. He joined the BLA in February 2024 and remained active in Chamalang, Kahan, Duki, and Shoor Parod, and was later martyred in Kharan.
The life story of Qadir Kashani Baloch shatters the assumption that movements arise only from deprivation. Hailing from an affluent and wealthy family in Dalbandin, Qadir Kashani had access to all the luxuries that an average youth could only dream of. However, for Qadir, life was not merely about breathing; it was about fighting for his national identity and survival.
After earning a degree in Political Science from the University of Management and Technology in Lahore, Qadir Baloch connected the theories of state, power, and self-determination that he studied in books with the call of his homeland. His activism in student politics was not just a hobby but the nurturing of a political consciousness that eventually led him onto the arduous path of practical struggle in February 2024. He abandoned comfortable beds for the rocky fronts of Chamalang, Kahan, and Duki, proving that when ideology matures, the chains of wealth break on their own.
Known within the organizational ranks as Chairman Baloch Khan, Qadir Kashani demonstrated both political insight and military courage from Shoor Parod to the plains of Kharan. He was a political worker who believed that when the sanctity of the pen is taken away, the gun becomes the most credible argument. As a fearless soldier of the Fateh Squad, he played the role of the vanguard in every battle. His martyrdom is not merely the loss of an individual but a testament to the philosophy that the price of a motherland’s freedom is far greater than any worldly wealth.
Abdul Hayee Baloch was a resident of Khuzdar, martyred on 8 November 2012.

On 11 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch announced the martyrdom of 14 fighters of the organization who attained martyrdom in confrontations with the Pakistani army and in airstrikes while defending their homeland, Balochistan, and fighting for national liberation and the right to self-determination.

On 13 August 2026, Pakistani Air Force fighter jets bombarded the Pandran area of Kalat District in Balochistan, resulting in the martyrdom of four members of the organization: Waseem Baloch, alias Farhan; Obaidullah Baloch, alias Shaheen; Nawaz Ali Baloch, alias Dilshad; and Mohammad Hassan, alias Ahmad.

On 25 August 2026, during an organizational mission in the Kech area of Balochistan, Sher Jan, alias Jamal, was shot from behind by a traitor, resulting in his martyrdom.

On 3 September 2026, while patrolling in the Mastung area of Balochistan, the organization’s brave fighters, Mohammad Younis, alias Salal; Sameer Ahmad, alias Zemal; Aziz Ahmad, alias Janan; and Sikandar Baloch, confronted Pakistani forces, targeted several enemy personnel, and embraced martyrdom.

On 14 September 2026, while engaging Pakistani forces and defending his fellow fighters in the Machani Kor Paroom area of Panjgur District, Babar Baloch, alias Kambar, embraced martyrdom.

On 18 September 2026, during a confrontation with Pakistani forces in the Chagi area of Balochistan, fighters of the organization, Riaz Baloch, alias Sabir; Taimoor Shah, alias Shaheen; Zia Ul Haq, alias Ziaullah; and Jumma Baloch, alias Commando, embraced martyrdom.

Babar Baloch, alias Kambar, son of Bashir Ahmed, resident of Paroom, Panjgur, joined the BLF on 5 October 2023. Owing to his exceptional abilities, he became second-in-command of the patrol network. He served on the fronts of Paroom, Gwarkop, the Coastal Highway, Balgatar, Zamuran, Mashkel, Panjgur and Gwargo, and also played a key role in establishing the camp of the BRAS. On 14 September 2026, in an engagement with the enemy at Machani Kor in the Paroom area, Shaheed Babar fought the enemy army, defended fellow fighters, and embraced martyrdom.

On 29 May 2025, Nizar Jan, son of Abdul Ghani and a resident of Nasirabad in Kech district of Balochistan, was shot dead by two armed men affiliated with a state-backed death squad. The assailants arrived at his uncle’s hotel in the main bazaar of Nasirabad around sunset, where Nizar Jan was employed, opened fire on him at close range, and he died on the spot.

On 3 October 2026, a statement issued by the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) stated that on 1 October 2026, fighters from the Karima Armed Assault Division (KAAD) and Qurban Unit of the Balochistan Liberation Front carried out a joint attack on an important military camp of the Frontier Corps (FC) 58 Wing, located in Gorindar, in the Mashkel area of Washuk, killing 18 personnel and wounding several others. The fighters completely encircled the enemy camp from multiple directions and attacked it with rockets, grenade launchers, and other heavy automatic weapons. During the operation, some panicked soldiers abandoned their weapons and the camp and fled. The convoy sent as reinforcements for the occupying army was also targeted by the fighters' protection squads, leaving several soldiers killed and wounded, and the convoy was forced to retreat. Later, the occupying army transported the bodies of its dead personnel to Panjgur by helicopter. The occupying army is concealing the number and identities of its casualties, which testifies to the fact that it is fighting a lost war in Balochistan. In the course of completing this historic and resolute mission, two brave fighters of the organization, Sajid Baloch, alias Mehran, son of Khalid, resident of Buleda, and Abdul Khaliq, alias Nothak, son of Sanjar, resident of Paroom, were martyred while fighting the enemy.

Farhad Rahmat, son of Rahmat Baloch, was born on August 11, 1995, in Mashkai, District Awaran. Farhad Rehmat received his early education at the Higher Secondary School Mashkai Gajjar, his hometown. When he was pursuing his matriculation in the area, the earthquake in Mashkai occurred, after which the Pakistan Army entered the region and occupied all the schools and colleges. Due to this, Farhad was unable to continue his education in government schools. He also studied in two English language centers in the town.
He had a passion for going to the mountains of the area and photographing the landscapes and other natural scenery. He was also a keen cricket lover and played cricket frequently in his free time after school and other activities. He always played cricket with other children from the area.
He became a formal member of the organization in 2006 in the Mashkai Zone. He was one of the active members who participated in every activity of the organization, including pamphleteering, wall chalking, distribution of the organization’s magazines, and other activities. He served in different positions within the organization, including Unit Secretary, Deputy Unit Secretary, and Vice President of Mashkai Zone.
He had a deep love for books and always devoted his free time to reading, which increased his knowledge. He especially loved studying books on Baloch history.
On June 30, 2015, the Pakistani Army raided the village of Mashi, Mashkai, and martyred Farhad Baloch along with several other people in the village. His body was not handed over to his family by the Pakistani Army. He was a very sober person by nature, and whenever he had something on his mind, he did not hesitate to express it directly to others.

On 16 February 2022, the ground forces of the Pakistani state, accompanied by air support, attacked a camp of the Baloch Nationalist Army in the early hours of the morning in the mountainous area of Kulbar, Tump. A prolonged skirmish ensued, beginning at 6:00 AM and continuing until 5:00 PM, during which the Baloch Sarmachars killed several enemy commandos and partially damaged two enemy helicopters.
In this clash, Noor Salam Noor alias Istaal, son of Bahar Baloch and a resident of Dashtuk Zamuran; Zubair Akram alias Asadjan, son of Akram Baloch and a resident of Hotabad Zamuran Bazaar; Kambar Baloch alias Mehrwan, son of Tariq and a resident of Kolaho; Sageer Baloch alias Tariq, son of Noorbakhsh and a resident of Basima; Rasool Jan alias Chirag, son of Ali Jan and a resident of Sarankan; and Hafiz Faraz alias Mullah Darwish, son of Abdul Ghani and a resident of Sarankan, were martyred.

On January 29, 2026, a statement issued by Mureed Baloch, spokesperson for the Baask media wing of the Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA), stated that members of the organization were on an operational mission on January 27, 2026. They were temporarily stationed at a location in the Tejaban area of Kech district when, at approximately 4:00 AM, the occupying Pakistani army surrounded the fighters and launched an attack using quadcopters, firing multiple shells. Following this, an intense clash broke out between the occupying forces and the fighters. The fighters responded with an organized and forceful counterattack. The battle between the two sides continued from 4:00 AM until 6:00 AM. Demonstrating bravery and military skill, the fighters managed to break the siege imposed by the occupying Pakistani army and safely withdrew. As a result of this two-hour clash, five personnel of the occupying Pakistani army were killed, and several others were injured. While defending the Baloch homeland, a fighter of the Baloch Nationalist Army, Rahmdil Baloch, alias Doda Baloch, fought bravely until his last moments and embraced martyrdom.
Rahmdil Baloch, alias Doda Baloch, son of Phatan, was a resident of Sengabad in the Tejaban area. He joined the Baloch Nationalist Army on May 7, 2024. He was a very hardworking, resilient, and fearless fighter. In a short period, he traveled to various areas of Kech including Kolwah, Hoshab, Zamran, and Tump as part of organizational activities. On multiple fronts in these regions, he steadfastly and courageously carried out his national duties against the enemy. Even in his final moments, he remained committed to defending Baloch land and ensuring the survival of the Baloch nation. Without regard for his own life, he fought bravely against enemy forces and ultimately sacrificed his life.

Jalaluddin Baloch, 30, son of Deen Muhammad and employed as a driver, was shot dead by armed, masked men on a motorcycle. The assailants opened fire while he was cleaning a vehicle at a service station, killing him on the spot.
Residents report that Jalaluddin’s two brothers had previously been taken into custody by Pakistani forces. Diljan was released after several days, while his other brother, Kamal, remains forcibly disappeared, with no information on his fate or location.
According to local sources, the attackers were members of a state-backed death squad known for carrying out extrajudicial killings, enforced disappearances, and targeted attacks across Balochistan. These groups operate alongside Pakistani security forces, creating an atmosphere of fear and coercion designed to suppress dissent and silence Baloch civilians.
Niaz Ahmad Baloch, son of Shahnawaz,resident of Awaran, was abducted by Pakistani forces on 22 September 2010, forcibly disappeared, and the next day, on 23 September 2010, his body was dumped.

Eid Muhammad Baloch, alias Shikari, son of Muhammad Hayat Khan, who was martyred on February 28, 2025, was a freedom fighter of the BLA. Martyr Eid Muhammad Baloch was arrested and forcibly disappeared by the occupying forces from Mangocher on November 30, 2023. After two years of inhuman torture and physical incapacitation, the enemy left him half-dead in Quetta on February 8, 2025. A few days later, on February 28, 2025, he embraced martyrdom during treatment. Martyr Eid Muhammad belonged to the Narmuk area of Kalat. He started his national struggle in 2013 from the platform of the BLA. He was a brave, fearless, and talented fighter.

Ahmad Mengal, Alias Shehzad Malang, was martyred on July 26, 2025 in the Mashkil area as a result of firing by a death-squad of the occupying Iranian regime.
Martyr Ustad Ahmad was a resident of the Killi Gharibabad neighborhood of Noshki and formerly served in the (FC) of occupying Pakistan. After witnessing the oppression inflicted on the Baloch nation, he left service with the enemy in 2021. In late 2021 he joined the Baloch national movement and, with his courage and notable combat skills, led operations in Khuzdar, Noshki, Quetta, Mastung, Sarbaz, Pahrah (Iranshahr), Duzap (Zahedan), Shastun–Sarawan, and other areas of Balochistan. He commanded at the forefront of several key Baloch Nationalist Army operations and was a member of one of BNA’s “Maalik” intelligence units.
When he entered Iranian-occupied Balochistan, he visited many regions and played a key role in strengthening companion networks. He trained local commanders on how to organize an armed formation and how to build their institutions firmly and effectively.

Zakriya Zehri, son of Ali Dost Zehri, belonged to Anjeera in Khuzdar. He received his early education from his native town of Anjeera. For some time, he also studied Islamic education at the madrassa in his town. He completed his middle and matriculation education from Madrassah Taaleem-ul-Islam and Tablighi College Hub.
After completing his matriculation, he enrolled in Polytechnic College Quetta to obtain a diploma in Civil Engineering. He began his political career in 2009 from the Gul Bahar Unit of BSO Azad in Khuzdar, during a period when activism of BSO Azad was surging in the area. After moving to Shaal for his education, he became a member of the Polytechnic Unit of BSO Azad, Shaal zone.
He was on his way to Shaal for his exams when he was abducted by law enforcement agencies on 11 December 2010. His mutilated body was thrown by security agencies in Sorab on 15 January 2011. His body bore severe signs of torture.
His family was targeted by a state-backed Sardar of the area, who sought to seize their land. However, the family of the martyred Zakriya resisted the oppression of the tribal chiefs and did not allow them to occupy their land. One of his cousins, Yaseen, was also martyred by the Pakistani army for being a member of the organization.
Zakriya, apart from his passion for cricket, was also fond of hunting. He was a very committed member of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

On 1 August 2017, during an operation in the Nizarabad area of Tump in Kech District, Balochistan, the Pakistani army abducted Sattar, son of Dr. Mohammad, resident of Dasht Kuddan, a leading member of the urban network of the Baloch Liberation Front (BLF). He was blindfolded, taken some distance away, and shot dead. Prior to his martyrdom, Sattar had been carrying out urban responsibilities on the platform of the BLF for four years. He was an exceptionally fearless and capable guerrilla fighter, and during those four years he rendered exemplary services to the Baloch national liberation movement.

Meer Alam Kiyazai, alias Salman, son of Imam Baksh Kiyazai, was 27 years old and a resident of Barwary, Quetta, Balochistan. He held a BS in Economics from Islamia University Bahawalpur. He joined the BLA and served on the Urban Front in 2019. Later, in 2023, he moved to the Mountain Front, where he was promoted to the rank of Camp Commander. He was killed on 30 July 2026 in Wali Tangi, Quetta, Balochistan.
Meer Alam Kiyazai was counted among the brave, fearless, and courageous revolutionary Sarmachars of the Baloch Liberation Army who chose the battlefield based on revolutionary principles, human consciousness, and national needs, and demonstrated himself to be an undefeated Sarmachar on the battlefield. Martyr Alam did not take up arms merely as a result of circumstance or a temporary impulse to confront the enemy. Rather, after gaining extensive experience in urban warfare, completing his education, developing his technical understanding of the movement, and establishing an intellectual connection with its objectives, he shifted to the Bolan Front under the directives of the organization.
While pursuing his studies in economics, he remained deeply connected to the pain, national suffering, and collective consciousness of his people. This suffering and consciousness ultimately shaped his revolutionary path. After developing an understanding of what he regarded as the national, technical, economic, and political foundations of the armed Baloch resistance, he joined the ranks against the enemy and carried out operations that, according to this account, had a significant impact. During his three-year tenure, he demonstrated exceptional operational and administrative capabilities. From operational planning to effective administrative execution, he proved himself to be a disciplined and capable Sarmachar.
Recognizing these capabilities, the organization entrusted him with critical responsibilities as a camp commander on the operational front in Quetta. He fulfilled these responsibilities through his actions, character, and relentless dedication. He played a key role in maintaining the organization's position in the region while educating new Sarmachar recruits in organizational doctrine, strategic discipline, and revolutionary consciousness.
The sacrifices made by Martyr Salman in what he regarded as the struggle for national freedom, through the use of his educational, administrative, and combat abilities, are presented as a source of inspiration for the younger Baloch generation. He remained active against the enemy until the end and lost his life during an organizational operation involving the capture of an enemy camp. His supporters believe that his sacrifice will further strengthen their resolve, with the ultimate goal of achieving an independent state of Balochistan.

Nisar Hussain Baloch was born on August 20, 1960, to Mohammed Baloch in Old Haji Camp, Lyari, Karachi. He was brutally gunned down in broad daylight on November 7, 2009, for defending the ancestral land of the Baloch in the city of Karachi.

The Sarmachaars of the Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) were patrolling the Pasni Shadi Kaur area of Gwadar on Saturday morning when a clash erupted between them and the occupying forces and their backed death squads. During this prolonged battle, Hidayatullah Baloch fought the enemy with exceptional bravery and courage to enable his comrades to escape the enemy’s siege. In the hour-long battle, many enemy personnel were killed and wounded, and our Sarmachaars managed to break free from the enemy’s encirclement, except for Hidayat Jan, who sacrificed his life while defending the motherland. The organization pays rich tribute to him for his great sacrifice. Hidayatullah, alias Balach Jan, son of Nematullah, was a resident of Pidrak who joined the armed resistance struggle in 2014. Hidayat Jan belonged to a patriotic family. One of his elder brothers, Shujaatullah, was martyred by state forces, while another brother, Inayatullah, remains in the torture cells of the occupying forces. Three other members of his family - Kamaash Kamal, Islam Jan, and Ikram - were previously martyred by the enemy. Hidayatullah Baloch was an extremely hardworking and brave young man who played an important role against the so-called CPEC in the Pasni, Balgatar, Hoshap, and Turbat areas, inflicting heavy losses on the enemy. In recognition of his bravery, he was appointed as the second operational commander of the organization’s Hoshap Camp two years ago.

In 1838, the British sent a force led by Alexander Burnes to reinstate Shah Shuja Durrani as the king of Afghanistan by deposing Amir Dost Mohammad Khan. To reach Afghanistan, they needed passage through Balochistan, particularly the Bolan Pass. However, Khan Mehrab Khan refused to allow the British to use his land to attack a neighboring country. The British sent Lieutenant Leach to negotiate with the Baloch government, but the Khan stood firm. When British forces reached Shaal via Bolan, some patriotic Baloch, without the Khan’s knowledge, attacked British troops out of nationalist sentiment and a desire to protect their homeland.
After toppling Amir Dost Mohammad Khan, the British Governor General of India, Lord Auckland, ordered an attack on Balochistan. In 1839, around 7,000 British troops marched from Shaal to attack the Baloch Meeri (capital). Anticipating an invasion, Khan Mehrab Khan declared war and sent messages to tribal leaders, but many saw the British as allies rather than invaders and chose to collaborate with them rather than defend their land. When Khan Mehrab Khan gathered his resistance fighters, the number of loyal warriors had dwindled to only 700 due to the short sightedness of many tribal chiefs. Nevertheless, Mehrab Khan was determined to fight. At his court, a respected figure, Akhund Muhammad Siddiq, advised him that he was not in a position to wage war at that time. He suggested that the Khan should leave Kalat with his companions, regroup and strengthen his forces, and then launch an attack against the British when the time was right, on 13 November 1839, the British forces launched an attack on Kalat, and a fierce battle ensued. During the fighting, Khan Mehrab Khan Baloch was martyred by a British bullet.

Among those martyred alongside him were:

Diwan Bacha Mal, Minister of Finance

Diwan Khem Chand

Diwan Asardas Mukhi, from the Hindu Panchayat of Kalat

Abdul Karim Raisani, brother of Sardar Asad Khan Raisani

Sardar Wali Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (maternal uncle of Martyr Amir Mehrab Khan)

Mir Taj Muhammad Shahizai Mengal, (cousin of Mehrab Khan)

Mir Muhammad Ali Shahizai Mengal

Mir Fazal Muhammad Lehri, brother of Sardar Muhammad Khan Lehri

Sardar Zaman Khan Pandrani

Mir Dad Karim Chandozai Shahwani

Mir Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Mir Badal Khan, brother of Sardar Shahbaz Khan Nichari

Khan Muhammad Dehwaar, Arbab-e-Kalat.

Mir Nabi Bakhsh Jatoi, from the Narmak region of Kalat

Mir Qaiser Khan Bizenjo

Mir Shah Dost Bizenjo

Muhammad Raza Waziri Khel

Noor Muhammad Shahizai, son of Polat Sagaar Sarmastani, in charge of the armory

Taj Muhammad Shagasi

data.organization: Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) / Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS)
data.biography:
At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Salim Baloch, alias Molam, son of Abdul Sattar, was a resident of Absar, Turbat district of Balochistan. He held an MA degree in History from Punjab University. He was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces and was later released. After his release, having endured the hardships of captivity, he joined the armed movement and moved to the mountain fronts in September 2023.
Salim Baloch was not merely a guerrilla fighter; he was a representative of that educated Baloch consciousness that studied history in the halls of Punjab University and then chose to rewrite that very history with his own blood. This son of Absar, Turbat, followed the ideology that when the enemy forgets the language of reason and pushes youth into the dungeons of enforced disappearances, the silence of the mountains becomes the most effective response.
The trajectory of Salim’s life shifted when he was forcibly disappeared. The darkness of the torture cells could not intimidate him; instead, after his release, he preferred a dignified death over a cowardly life and formally moved to the mountain front in September 2023. As an active commander of the STOS Unit, he remained a symbol of fear for the enemy on urban fronts and in camps.
On January 29, while engaged in preparations for “Operation Herof,” he embraced martyrdom while fighting gallantly during a sudden clash with the occupying forces in Turbat. Salim’s sacrifice is an open declaration that the educated class of the Baloch nation has now entered the battlefield to shatter the chains of slavery.

On 07 February 2026, a press statement issued by the Balochistan Liberation Front stated that three of its fighters - Captain Farooq Baloch alias Sohrab, Adeel Baloch alias Hameed Baloch, and Ahmad Baloch alias Deedar - were martyred in the Tasp area of District Panjgur, Balochistan. A fourth fighter, Hafiz Abdul Wahab Badini, was martyred in Kalat District, Balochistan.
Fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front went to the Tasp area of Panjgur on January 25, 2026, to carry out a covert organizational mission. There, FC personnel attempted to surround them, resulting in an intense face to face clash between the fighters and state forces. During the clash, the BLF fighters demonstrated extraordinary courage, bravery, and steadfastness, and did not retreat even under the most difficult circumstances.
In the clash, several FC personnel were killed or wounded, while three BLF fighters embraced martyrdom while fighting valiantly. The martyred fighters continued to perform their duties until their last breath and set a practical example of determination, discipline, and commitment in the national struggle.
Adeel Baloch alias Hameed Baloch, son of Murad Jan, resident of Essa Panjgur, who joined the struggle as an urban guerrilla of BLF on January 4, 2023, and later moved to the mountain front. He demonstrated extraordinary courage and perseverance during his activities on various fronts. His character remained a symbol of responsibility, awareness, discipline, and steadfast decisions. Adeel Baloch's consistency is an example for his fellow fighters, and his sacrifice will have impacts on the organization's missions.

Pasand Khan Zehri, alias Khalid, son of Zaman Kahni, was a resident of Shafi Colony in the Zehri area of District Khuzdar, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in February 2025 and served on the Nagaho front.
Pasand Khan Zehri joined the BLA at the beginning of 2025 and served on the Nagaho front. On the battlefield, he viewed the struggle not merely as a phase but as a responsibility connected to the future of his nation. His quiet nature, strong determination, and deep commitment to the cause placed him among those figures who earn a meaningful place in the narrative of resistance. Pasand belonged to the historic region of Zehri in Balochistan, a land where people have always considered loyalty to their homeland a fundamental principle of life. When Pasand Khan joined the ranks of the resistance, his decision was driven by a profound sense of duty and devotion to his nation. He was among those who did not fear difficult paths but accepted them as their responsibility.
Pasand Khan was present on the Noshki front during Operation Herof Phase 2, where he was martyred after a prolonged clash with the enemy.
Tawod, alias Miras Baloch, was a resident of the Kulanch , Pasni area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 1 February 2020 in Balochistan.

Shakir Shad, son of Yar Mohammad, was a 19-year-old matric student. He was a resident of Kolwa, District Awaran. Shakir Shad served as the Zonal Information Secretary of BSO Azad Kolwa Zone. Before being elected to this position, he held various roles within the organization.
He joined the organization at a very early age and remained associated with it until his martyrdom. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for exercising his right to peaceful political expression. He was killed by Pakistani paramilitary forces during an operation in Kolwa, Awaran, on 29 July 2017.
He was a committed member of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapter of Baloch history.

Shezad Baloch Alias Chirag Baloch, son of Mullah Baksh Baloch and was a resident of Gomazi, Tump area of Kech, Balochistan. He became part of Baloch liberation movement in 2013 and on Oct 9, 2022, he joined Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF).
He embraced martyrdom in a drone attack of Pakistan’s military along with his seven comrades, Kareem Baloch, Mullah Bakhsh, Hazza Baloch,  Asif Baloch, Jalal Baloch, Talab Baloch, and Manzoor Baloch on Feb 23, 2023 in Mazanband area of Kech, Balochistan.

Zakir Mengal, alias Notak, son of Haji Khair Mohammad Mengal, was a resident of Killi Qabool, Zangi Nawar, Noshki. He joined the BLA in April 2025. He held a BS degree in Electronics Engineering from Bahria University, Islamabad. He served on the Shoor Parod and Noshki fronts and was martyred on the Kharan front during Operation Herof Phase 2.
Zakir Mengal, known in guerrilla ranks as “Notak,” was a son of the fertile soil of Noshki, where the intersection of knowledge and resistance has always existed. After obtaining a degree in Electronics Engineering from the prestigious Bahria University Islamabad, all paths to a luxurious life and a bright future were open to Zakir. However, his conscience chose resistance over compromise. When he formally joined the BLA in April 2025, he brought not only determination but also a scientific and technical mind aligned with the demands of modern warfare.
Notak was among those technical comrades of the movement who dedicated their professional expertise to national defense. Utilizing his education in electronics, he played a key role in modernizing the Baloch war of independence. He believed that the enemy’s numerical superiority could only be countered through technology and intelligence. His technical contributions on the Shoor Parod, Noshki, and Kharan fronts provided the organization with new dimensions in the military field.
He proved that when an intellectual and an engineer takes up a gun, he does not merely fire bullets; he disrupts the enemy’s entire system. Zakir Baloch offered the ultimate sacrifice for the great cause of his land’s freedom, leaving behind a message that the modern generation of the Baloch nation is writing a new history of independence through the fusion of knowledge and blood.

Hafeez Qambarani, son of Younis Qambarani, was a resident of Nimgargh, Kalat, Balochistan. He was 27 years old and a student, as well as a member of BSO Azad Kalat Zone. He received his primary education in his hometown, Kalat.
He believed in a peaceful political struggle. He was martyred by Pakistani paramilitary forces on 14 March 2015. He was a committed member of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad.

Sadam Baloch, was a resident of the Anjira, Khuzdar area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 3 February 2016 in Balochistan.

Sohail Ahmad Bugti, alias Watan Zad, son of Dada Kechi, belonged to the Rajio Bugti tribe. He was a resident of Mach, Bolan. He joined the BLA in March 2025 and became part of the Majeed Brigade in May 2025. He was martyred in Noshki during Operation Herof Phase 2.
Sohail Ahmad Bugti, alias Watan Zad, through his revolutionary character and actions, truly embodied the meaning of his name. His decision to become a fidayee symbolized the belief that at times history advances only when an individual rises above personal existence and embraces the ultimate level of sacrifice. Baloch Sarmachars carry this same conviction and determination as they sacrifice their lives to free their homeland from Punjabi occupation.
During Operation Herof Phase 2 on the Noshki front, Watan Zad gave practical expression to this philosophy of sacrifice. Standing firm against the enemy, he left behind the message that a fidayee is not merely a military role but a symbol of revolutionary thought, one that considers national freedom far more valuable than personal life.

Ustad Allah Dad, son of Dostain Baloch and a resident of Soler Ghichk, Panjgur, was enforcedly disappeared by Pakistani forces in the Naag area of Washuk on September 16, 2025.

After four days of illegal detention, his mutilated body was discovered in Panjgur on the night of September 20, 2025. The body showed clear signs of severe physical torture and inhumane treatment, indicating he was subjected to extreme punishment before being killed.

Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) freedom fighter Ghulam Jan, alias Ustad Sachan, was martyred on July 26, 2024, in Kilkor. On July 25, 2024, he had taken part in a Baloch Raji Ajoi Sangar (BRAS) operation against the so-called death squad formed by the occupying Pakistani military in the Kilkor area of Panjgur, where he was injured by gunfire.
BRAS comrades moved Ghulam Jan to a secure hideout while he was wounded, where he received medical treatment. Despite this, he could not recover from his injuries and attained martyrdom.
Ghulam Jan, alias Ustad Sachan, was the son of Mohammad and hailed from the Sedan area of Panjgur. He joined the Baloch Liberation Army in 2013 and took up arms against national subjugation. Due to his exceptional combat skills, he was soon appointed as a training commander, earning him the title “Ustad” (Teacher).
At the time of his martyrdom, Ghulam Jan was serving as the second-in-command of the Panjgur camp of the Baloch Liberation Army. He demonstrated his combat abilities across the fronts of Panjgur, Buleda, Hoshab, Kilkor, Parom, Balgatar, Washuk, Rakhshan, and Kolwah, inflicting significant losses on the enemy.
By participating in various operations of the Baloch Raji Ajoi Sangar (BRAS), he not only defeated the enemy but also played a key role in strengthening the Baloch national alliance. Martyr Ghulam Jan was laid to rest in his ancestral area with full military honors, under the shadow of the flag of a free Balochistan.

The resistance and courage shown by the martyrs of Mehi, Mashkay against the aggression of the occupying Pakistani army on June 30, 2015, will be remembered in golden words in the pages of history. Thanks to the sacrifices of these martyrs, awareness of the struggle against Pakistani occupation is spreading to every corner of Balochistan. History honors those who stand up for the defense of their nation and homeland at decisive moments.
The Baloch national freedom movement is ongoing and strong thanks to the sacrifices of these martyrs. These great sacrifices of the martyrs have fostered the consciousness within the Baloch nation that the enemy occupying Balochistan should not be allowed to breathe in peace until they suffocate and run away. It should be remembered that the occupier has always treated the enslaved people with the same inhumane treatment that the state of Pakistan is doing with the Baloch in occupied Balochistan, including killings, enforced disappearances and dumping of mutilated bodies and other atrocities included.
The Martyrs of Mehi area of Mashkay Shaheed Major Sulaiman alias Shehak Jan, Zakir Jan, and Safar Khan Baloch are the great sons of the nation. Those who bravely and courageously adopted the path of resistance against the Pakistani occupation and colonial policy and laid down their lives fighting for the freedom of the country. These great sacrifices of martyrs are encouraging us to leave tribalism, territorialism and become a part of this national struggle as Baloch and strengthen it. Martyrs of Balochistan sacrificed their precious lives so that the Baloch nation could live with freedom and dignity. The national movement needs to be further strengthened and organized while carrying forward this great ideology of martyrs and the spirit of sacrifice.

On 12 August 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahran Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of nine fighters of the organization: 1. Zubair Baloch, alias Shahvez; 2. Shahnawaz Baloch, alias Rahchar; 3. Rahim Baloch, alias Ajiz Baloch; 4. Musharaf Baloch, alias Basham; 5. Munir Baloch, alias Khalid Baloch; 6. Mohammad Zaman, alias Yahya; 7. Jasim Baloch, alias Babar; 8. Gaji Khan Baloch, alias Aftab; and 9. Abdullah Baloch, alias Usman, and paid tribute to all the martyred comrades who sacrificed their lives for the freedom of the motherland, Balochistan.

During the intense clashes with enemy forces, the BLF’s senior commander, Captain Munir Baloch, alias Khalid Baloch, son of Mohammad Ishaq and a resident of the Bencha area of Surab, was martyred while fighting valiantly on the front line in defense of his motherland.
Martyr Captain Munir Baloch began his armed struggle through the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front in 2022. During his first year, he remained highly active in the urban guerrilla network. In accordance with the organization’s policy, he was then transferred to the mountainous warfare front in August 2023. He rendered valuable services across the difficult fronts of Surab, Mastung, Kalat, Nushki, Kharan, and Chagai. In particular, he played a key role in operations in Kharan and Chagai that inflicted significant human and material losses on the enemy. He was a highly skilled RPG launcher operator and a fearless fighter.
Captain Munir Baloch’s family had been making sacrifices for the national movement since its early days. His elder brother, Martyr Israr, alias Saddam Baloch, an urban guerrilla of the BLF, was martyred in 2017 when occupying forces and their local death-squad operatives opened fire on him in Surab. This courageous family has now sacrificed another son for the cause.
Due to his exceptional skills, Captain Munir Baloch had assumed organizational and military command over the Surab region. He continued to confront the enemy on the front line until the final moments of his life.

Noshad Ahmed, son of Jameel Ahmed and a 28-year-old resident of Tasp, Panjgur, was targeted and killed by a state-backed death squad on June 1, 2026, on Chedagi Road in the Tasp area of Panjgur, Balochistan.
The incident took place between the Asr and Maghrib prayers when armed members of a death squad, traveling in a white Toyota Axio, opened fire on Noshad Ahmed. He sustained fatal gunshot wounds and was killed on the spot.
On February 3, 2026, in the Bazaar of Nushki district in Balochistan, Pakistani forces shot and killed 12 year old Shehzad Ahmed, son of Zafar Ahmed.

On 13 October 2026, Pakistani genocidal forces killed six Baloch men who had previously been subjected to enforced disappearance and dumped their bodies in the Sui area of Dera Bugti district, Balochistan.
The incident was also confirmed by Sher Mohammad Bugti, the Central Spokesperson of the Baloch Republican Party.

The victims have been identified as follows:
- Mohammad Khan Bugti, son of Yar Mohammad Bugti
- Lalu Bugti, son of Taj Mohammad Bugti
- Shahmeer Bugti, son of Shahal Bugi
- Waheed Bugti, son of Habib Bugti
- Ghulam Din Bugti, son of Kurri Bugti
- Akram Khan, son of Wadera Mazar Khan Bugti

Noor Jan Baloch, a resident of Harooni Dan, Awaran, was a laborer and belonged to a poor family. He was picked up along with his son by Pakistani forces and was released on the condition that he would bring his daughter to the military camp, as she had recently married a freedom fighter. The next day, on 20 May 2021, Noor Jan chose suicide instead of handing over his daughter to the Pakistani military.

On 5 January 2026, 14 year old student Raahi Assa was killed in the main bazaar of Hoshap, Kech. Eyewitnesses reported that armed men, affiliated with a death squad linked to Pakistani military intelligence, opened fire on the minor, killing him on the spot. The attackers fled the scene immediately after the killing.

Talal Ahmed son of Abdul Rasheed, a resident of Koshok, Tehsil Buleda of district Kech, was forcibly disappeared by Frontier Constabulary (FC) Forces on August 14, 2025, in a cricket ground. 

He was forcibly disappeared with three others from a cricket ground in Buleda. His whereabouts remained unknown for 40 days until his unrecognised and decomposed body was discovered with Mehraj Baloch from Alandoor, Buleda, on September 23, 2025.

Talal Ahmed was identified only through his national identity card, which had been placed beside his body. His condition showed clear signs of prolonged torture and that he had been killed days before his body was dumped.
Sanaullah Baloch, a Baloch nationalist, was killed on 1 October 2012 in Khuzdar, Balochistan, by a death squad operating under the command of Pakistani forces.
Hussain Baloch, was a resident of the Zamuran, Kech area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 3 July 2018 in Balochistan.

On 25 August 2024 Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch announced the launch of a "Fidayeen Operation" named "Herof" across Balochistan. As part of this operation, fidayeen from the BLA's elite unit, Majeed Brigade, have attacked the main camp of the Pakistani forces in Bela and have successfully infiltrated it. Meanwhile, other BLA fighters have taken full control of all major highways across Balochistan, blocking them completely.
During Operation “Herof,” 44 attacks were carried out simultaneously at 40 locations across 13 districts of Balochistan. As a result, 130 Pakistani army personnel were killed and 55 were injured. In addition, gas pipelines were destroyed at 2 locations, railway tracks at 7 locations, and 2 bridges were blown up.
During the operation, 13 vehicles transporting minerals were set on fire. Blockades were also established at 14 locations across Balochistan, and 3 members of a “death squad” were killed.
As part of the Baloch Liberation Army’s fidayee (suicide) operation “Herof,” the BLA’s Majeed Brigade carried out an attack on the Pakistani army’s Bela camp. The Majeed Brigade maintained control of the camp for twenty hours, during which 68 enemy personnel were killed.
Nine fidayeen (self-sacrificing fighters) of the Majeed Brigade at Bela camp - Ghaus Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Talib), Mahal Baloch (alias Zilan Kurd), Rizwan Baloch (alias Hammal), Mohammad Baloch (alias Meerak), Fazal Gul Zehri (alias Shawaiz), Tayyab Baloch (alias Lala), Junaid Zehri (alias Kami), Mohammad Asif Nechari (alias Naveed), and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani (alias Khalid) - along with Shafqat (alias Dayar) of the Fateh Squad in Mastung, were martyred in the operation.
Ghaus Baksh Sumalani, alias Talib, and Mohammad Bakhsh Sumalani, alias Khalid, were brothers. They took part in the same operation and were martyred while defending their motherland.

On 12 August 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahran Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of nine fighters of the organization: 1. Zubair Baloch, alias Shahvez; 2. Shahnawaz Baloch, alias Rahchar; 3. Rahim Baloch, alias Ajiz Baloch; 4. Musharaf Baloch, alias Basham; 5. Munir Baloch, alias Khalid Baloch; 6. Mohammad Zaman, alias Yahya; 7. Jasim Baloch, alias Babar; 8. Gaji Khan Baloch, alias Aftab; and 9. Abdullah Baloch, alias Usman, and paid tribute to all the martyred comrades who sacrificed their lives for the freedom of the motherland, Balochistan.

Mohammad Zaman, alias Yahya, son of Mahmood, a resident of Ward No. 1, Babrshor, Pasni, passed away from natural causes on 2 August 2026, following an illness. Martyr Mohammad Zaman joined the movement through the BLF platform in 2023 and served as an urban guerrilla for one year. In 2024, he was transferred to the mountains in accordance with an organizational decision, where he carried out his responsibilities with great sincerity and courage.

On 31 December 2025, a statement released by the spokesperson of the Balochistan Liberation Front, Major Gwahram Baloch, stated that five of its fighters embraced martyrdom and sacrificed their lives for the homeland in an enemy drone strike in Kalat on 25 December 2025.
The martyrs include Abdul Ahad Dehwar alias Gazzain, son of Hamayun Dehwar, resident of Keli Kahriz Mastung; Israr Ahmad alias Ibrar, son of Hussain, resident of Gargina Mastung; Shoaib Ahmad alias Subedar, son of Muhammad Ali, resident of Jiwa Khuzdar; Obaidullah Siyahpad alias Sabzu, son of Peerjan, resident of Kharan; and Faisal Badini alias Qazi, son of Muhammad Ibrahim, resident of Kharan.
Shoaib Ahmad, son of Mohammad Ali and resident of Jiwa Khuzdar, had recently joined the Balochistan Liberation Front and was present at the camp for training purposes. Shaheed Shoaib Jan was an educated, hardworking, committed, disciplined, and brave fighter. On 25 December, he was martyred along with other sarmachars in the occupying forces’ drone strike in Kalat.

Martyr Manzoor Baloch Alias Kiyya Baloch, son of Shafi Muhammad Baloch and was a resident of Baloch Abad, Mand area of Kech, Balochistan. According to organizational statement; He affiliated with Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in 2013.  He was at rank of lieutenant, for years. 
He embraced martyrdom in a drone attack of Pakistan’s military along with his seven comrades, Kareem Baloch, Mullah Bakhsh, Hazza Baloch, Asif Baloch, Shezad Baloch, Jalal Baloch, and Talab Baloch on Feb 23, 2023 in Mazanband area of Kech, Balochistan.

On 16 July 2026, at 7:00 AM, 16 year old Mujahid son of Zahid, a resident of Bal Nigwar Cross in Turbat district, Balochistan, was taken into custody by the Frontier Corps of Pakistani forces from the Dasht Bal Nigwar area. After being subjected to enforced disappearance, he was killed by Pakistani forces on 21 July 2026, in a fake encounter, and his body was dumped in the jungle Dasht.

On 31 May 2021, Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) fighters attacked the Pakistani military’s “Awais” camp (Ghazaband Scouts’ 129 Wing) in Marwaar, Bolan. The three hour assault completely destroyed the camp. BLA fighters killed 24 Pakistani soldiers on the spot and captured Lance Naik Bilal from Dera Ismail Khan. He was later tried by a Baloch national court and executed. Following a coordinated plan, the fighters surrounded the camp, cut through barbed wire, and stormed inside. After intense fighting lasting over three hours, they overran the base, killed 24 enemy personnel, seized a large quantity of arms and ammunition, and took one prisoner. As usual, the Pakistani military downplayed its losses. Three BLA fighters embraced martyrdom in the operation: Hangal Marri (alias Laila), Aftab Jattak (alias Washain), and Shahwaiz Zehri (alias Saraang). They were buried in Bolan with full military honours. The three belonged to the elite Fateh Squad, formed in 2018 and named after Martyr Fateh Qambrani (alias Chairman), who single handedly enabled the capture of an enemy camp in Meshdari, Shahrag, the same year. Fateh Squad members are selected for exceptional bravery and close combat skills. In the Marwaar attack, these three charged the enemy lines, breached the perimeter, and created openings that allowed the BLA to capture the camp entirely. Hangal Marri (alias Laila) joined the BLA in 2006 and served with distinction on the Kahan and Bolan fronts for 15 years. Aftab Yousuf Jattak (alias Washain), a highly educated economics graduate from Zehri, joined in 2019 and quickly earned a place in the Fateh Squad due to his skill and courage. Shahwaiz Zehri (alias Saraang) joined in 2017, served in urban units, then volunteered for the Bolan front and the Fateh Squad, where he fought bravely until his martyrdom.

Faraz Ulfat, son of Ulfat Naseem was a resident of Hub Chowki, District Lasbela, Balochistan. Faraz Naseem was a former member of the Central Committee of the Baloch Students Organization Azad and belonged to a political family. He was highly educated and took part in political activities at a time when the state continued the policy of killing Baloch political activists in fake encounters. He was a sincere political activist who played his role in the struggle of the Baloch national liberation movement. He believed in political struggle and was targeted for his peaceful political expression. He was abducted on 9 October 2011 by personnel of Pakistan’s intelligence agency from Hub town, Lasbela, Balochistan. After 24 days of detention and torture in a dungeon, his bullet-riddled body was found dumped on 2 November 2011 in Hub district, Lasbela, Balochistan. Extreme signs of torture and gunshot wounds were visible on the victim’s body. On 30 October, in a press conference outside Quetta Press Club, the sister of Faraz Baloch said, “The families fear that their loved ones might be killed and dumped like hundreds of other Baloch activists who have recently been tortured to death by Pakistani security forces while in their custody.” He was a victim of the Pakistan Army’s “kill and dump” policy against Baloch political activists. His body bore extreme signs of torture. He was among the committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times. He inspired many youths to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

Nazeer Ahmed, son of Bahram Baloch, and a resident of Jalai Kahni, was forcibly disappeared by state-backed death squads from his home in No-Dowani village on July 21, 2025. Within hours of his abduction, Nazeer was found extrajudicially killed in the Jhal Jahoo area.

Ali Nawaz Mengal, alias Faraz, son of Nayab Noor Mohammad Mengal, was a resident of Zarozi, Kharan. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served in Chagai District of Balochistan. He was martyred on 31 August 2026 in the Nokcha area of Chagi District, Balochistan.
Ali Nawaz Mengal, a native of Kharan, made the revolutionary decision to join the armed front of the national liberation struggle against the enemy. In 2026 he decided to join the Baloch Liberation Army and was transferred to the Shor front. He proved himself to be a capable comrade during the organization’s rigorous physical training and joined the battlefield equipped with combat skills and abilities. Along with other comrades, he played a leading individual role in enforcing the organization’s cordon-and-search policies in the region, consistently thwarting enemy advances and various tactics.
Ali Nawaz was well aware of the severe challenges facing the Baloch nation during this critical period, and he saw their lasting solution in an independent Balochistan, where the Baloch people could collectively live a free and autonomous life. Recognizing this reality, he embraced the philosophy of armed resistance against the enemy and remained committed to it until the end. Martyr Ali Nawaz proved himself to be an excellent guerrilla fighter throughout the war. His martyrdom reflects the national realization that the Baloch nation is prepared to take every extreme measure against the enemy to restore its freedom and state. In the pages of history, he will be remembered as a great freedom fighter.

On March 10, 2026, at around 5:30 PM in the Mawach Chowk area of Panjgur district, Balochistan, death squads operating under the command and control of Pakistani forces opened fire and killed 27 year old Abdullah Baloch, son of Kareem Jan. He was a resident of Mawach, Panjgur, Balochistan.

Samiullah Mengal, the 20-year-old son of Hafiz Ghulam and a resident of the Khatan area of District Khuzdar, was a member of the Baloch Students Organization (BSO-Azad). He was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces on 1 October 2010. After more than a month, on 17 November 2010, his body was dumped in the Ferozabad area of Khuzdar.

Adnan Sumalani, alias Sahroth, son of Jalaluddin Sumalani, was a resident of the Ahmadwal area of Noshki. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Noshki and Basima fronts. He was martyred on 7 September 2026 in the Basima area of Surab, Balochistan.
Adnan Sumalani chose the great path of national liberation by joining the Baloch Liberation Army. This year, he began his struggle at Shor through the platform of the BLA and, in a short period, proved himself among his comrades as a capable and courageous fighter. First, he fulfilled his responsibilities on the Nushki front and was later deployed to Basima, where he took part alongside fellow fighters in various armed operations, blockades, and activities carried out under guerrilla tactics.
Adnan was aware of Pakistan’s illegal and inhumane occupation of Balochistan and understood that if the enemy was not driven out of Balochistan sooner or later, they would further attack our survival and identity. Understanding the importance of this collective survival, he decided to join the national resistance through the platform of the Baloch Liberation Army, which he regarded as the sole means of achieving our freedom and sovereignty. He remained true to his ideas and philosophy until the end, holding his position against the enemy, and on December 7, sacrificed his life for national freedom and his cause. In the pages of Baloch national history, he will always be remembered as a great national Sarmachar.

data.martyrdomPlace: Satak Kor, Hoshap, Turbat district, Balochistan
data.biography:
On February 23, 2022 the occupying forces of Pakistan stroke the Baloch Nationalist Army (BNA) guerrilla camp in Satak Kor mountain range of Hoshab, district Kech and fired three missiles loaded with chemicals that wreaked havoc over a large area, destroying palm groves and other plants at the site. After the drone missile attacks, the infantry team of the occupying forces surrounded the area, and with the help of more than eight state helicopters entered the camp. Five Sarmachaars including two commanders of the organization Master Asif Baloch and Siraj Baloch were martyred in this attack. While the other five Sarmachaars - Shoaib, Munir, Arif Jan, Diljan, Kamal, Kamash Malang, Jangi Khan, and Daolat - were martyred in the defense of the homeland, fighting the enemy for over an hour and killing several commandos of the occupying forces.
The martyr comrade Siraj Zaheer, alias Zaheer Sahib son of Rasheed Baloch resident of Shapuk Dandal was associated with armed resistance since 2012. He had been fulfilling his responsibilities in different parts of Balochistan since 2015 and was recently appointed by the organization as the Operational Commander in Gwarkop area of Hoshap. He was a great Balochi poet and a great warrior.

On April 9, 2026, Chakar Baloch, son of Barkat and an 18 year old student, was extrajudicially killed by a state-sponsored death squad. He was targeted at his own shop in the Minaz area of Buleda, Turbat District, Balochistan, where armed men affiliated with a state-backed death squad opened fire on him, killing him on the spot. Chakar Baloch had only just begun his life and was starting to earn his livelihood. This is a tactic used by the state to silence the Baloch, spread fear, and ensure that everyone is targeted through collective punishment. This is a deliberate system imposed by the Pakistani state to create an environment where no one can breathe freely.
data.martyrdomPlace: Minaaz Bazaar, Buleda, Turbat district, Balochistan

data.biography:
On December 14, 2025, prolonged clashes broke out between the occupying Pakistani army and Baloch Liberation Army freedom fighters in the Daghari area of Quetta when the fighters were traveling for organizational work. The occupying army attempted to surround the freedom fighters using civilian vehicles, to which the freedom fighters immediately retaliated. In this clash, seven occupying army personnel were eliminated and several others were wounded, while two Baloch Liberation Army freedom fighters, Asmatullah Satakzai alias Siraj and Sajjad Zehri alias Sarang, attained martyrdom.
Sajjad Zehri alias Sarang, son of Muhammad Aslam Zehri, belonged to Khuzdar. Twenty-year-old Sangat Sajjad joined the Baloch Liberation Army a year ago and served on the Mastung, Bolan, and Quetta fronts. Despite his young age, he held a prominent position among his comrades due to his sense of responsibility, dedication to learning, and practical courage.
Diljan Baloch, was a resident of the Mashkai area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 13 May 2013 in Balochistan.

Ghulam Qadir, son of Murad Baksh and a resident of Gwadar, was an 18-year-old student.
On November 24, 2025, around 11 PM, he was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces from The Coast Hospital in Gwadar.
After 4 months and 7 days, on April 1, 2026, his body was found dumped in the Palleri area of Gwadar.
Ghulam Mohammad Bugti, a central committee member of the Baloch Republican Party (BRP), was killed by Pakistani forces on August 27, 2015.

On the night of April 29, 2025 in the Dannuk area of Turbat, the Pakistani occupying forces attempted to surround members of the Baloch Liberation Army’s urban guerrilla network. In response, the fighters launched a strong counter-attack. The clashes, which began at 3:30 AM, continued until sunrise. The fighters held their positions for three hours and continued to inflict heavy blows on the enemy. During this time, they also targeted a convoy of the occupying forces, causing significant casualties. Thirteen enemy personnel were killed and several others were injured during the clashes.
Three Baloch Liberation Army fighters were killed in the fighting: Nabeel, alias Ali; Feroz Sarban, alias Nodbandag and Mohammad Umar Zaka, alias Guru.
Mohammad Umar Zaka, alias Guru, son of Ali Mohammad, belonged to Gokdan, Turbat. He joined the BLA in 2021 and dedicated himself to the cause of national liberation. Even while serving in the state’s Levies force, he listened to his conscience and chose the path of struggle. Sangat Umar was an expert in IED wiring, and his skills repeatedly inflicted damage on the enemy. Because of his combat abilities, he was selected for the BLA’s elite unit, the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS).

Noor Mohammed Baloch was born on 12 November 1980 to Abdul Sattar in Mandil, Mashkay. In 2005, he obtained his Bachelor of Arts (B.A.) degree from Quetta, Balochistan. At the end of 2007, he joined the Baloch armed resistance movement to free the motherland.
On 16 November 2008, Noor Mohammed Baloch and his fellow fighters came face to face with the Frontier Corps (FC) commander of Khuzdar, Khalil, and his soldiers at Pariky, Mashkay. After a long and intense street gun battle, when the dust settled and the guns were silenced, six Frontier Corps (FC) personnel, including the commander, were dead. Shaheed Noor Mohammed stood his ground until his last breath and fulfilled his pledge to the motherland.

On 3rd April 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that fighters of the BLA launched a series of coordinated attacks against the occupying Pakistani army across occupied Balochistan on 29th March 2026, which continued until 1st April 2026. The fighters carried out 65 operations in Panjgur, Shapuk, Basima, Sibi, Mastung, Quetta, Noshki, Zamuran, Dasht, Surab, Jhal Magsi, Dalbandin, Kharan, Washuk, and Kalat. In these actions, more than 86 personnel of the Pakistani army, death squads, and intelligence agencies were killed, and dozens were injured. These attacks targeted occupying army camps, an airbase, radar systems, communication towers, railway tracks, bridges, and gas pipelines, while major highways were brought under control for several hours.
During clashes with Pakistani forces, five BLA fighters in Panjgur - Zahid alias Nawaz, Saeedullah alias Meraj, Jahanzeb alias Qambar, Aamir alias Khalid, and Saddam alias Shahwaiz - along with Abdust (Abdul Rehman) alias Alman in Zamuran, attained martyrdom.
Saddam, alias Shahwaiz (son of Altaf): From Kalag, Kech, he joined the BLA in 2025 and was a hardworking Sarmachar who completed several successful missions in Parom and Kilkor.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Saif Jan Sumalani, alias Ajiz, son of Baz Mohammad Sumalani, and Fidayee Hatam Naz Sumalani, also known as Gul Bibi, was a resident of Gharbok, Bolan. He joined the BLA in 2022, was active in the Fateh Squad, served in Bolan and Kalat, and was martyred in Noshki during Operation Herof Phase 2.
Saif Jan Sumalani, known to his comrades as Ajiz, belonged to a generation of young fighters raised not under the shadow of the enemy, but in the embrace of the motherland. He remained actively engaged as a committed Sarmachar of the Fateh Squad on some of the most grueling fronts, including Bolan and Kalat. During the second phase of Operation Herof, amidst intense clashes on the Noshki front, Saif Jan stood firm until his final breath, embracing martyrdom while resisting the enemy.
To understand the depth of his sacrifice, one must look beyond the battlefield. His mother, Fidayee Hatam Naz, was among the rare Baloch mothers who not only sent their sons into the struggle but also chose to become fidayees themselves. Hatam Naz joined the BLA in 2015. In 2016, she was injured during a major enemy operation and later abducted by state forces, remaining forcibly disappeared for four months. In January 2023, well into her sixties, she formally joined the Majeed Brigade as a Fidayee, embodying her lifelong resolve through action.
The history of Operation Herof gained a new chapter through the sacrifices of Saif Jan and his mother, both of whom fought on separate fronts yet gave their lives for the same dream. Saif Jan’s testimony was carried through the sound of gunfire; his mother’s through the silence of a fidayee’s resolve. One bore a rifle, the other carried explosives. And both expressed what words can never fully capture.

Sangat Sana Baloch was born in 10th October 1979 in Mastung, in the house of Haji Jan Muhammad. He completed his matriculation from Khuzdar and his bachelor’s degree from Quetta. He then enrolled in Balochistan University for his master’s degree in political science. He was politically conscious and socially very active. During his college life, he joined the Baloch Student’s Organization and worked tirelessly not only for Baloch students but for all the masses around him. His political consciousness and eloquent oratory made him an influential political leader in Baloch politics. He became the Senior Vice Chairman of BSO Azad. In June 2007, a cyclone hit the coastal belt of Balochistan. Sangat Sana, under the platform of BSO Azad, headed a mass relief operation for the Baloch people. He went door-to-door, working day and night for donations and relief goods for the needy people of the affected area. After student politics, he worked in the Baloch Republican Party (BRP) and became its central committee member. He traveled to rural and urban areas of Balochistan to advocate for the Baloch liberation movement, conducting rallies and public meetings. He did not accept the so-called demarcated boundaries of Pakistan separating Dg Khan from Balochistan. As the Senior Vice Chairman of BSO Azad, he went to DG Khan and addressed his nation, stating that the Baloch are a single nation, and no one can divide them by so-called demarcated borders. Neither Iranian nor Pakistani occupation can separate the Baloch. Every Baloch ought to participate in its independence movement. Today, addressing in Dg Khan is the success of our Liberation Movement. Pakistan could not accept such a fierce and dedicated Baloch leader, so Sana became a victim of its abduction policy. On 7 December 2009, while traveling from Mastung towards Sibi, he was abducted by Pakistan’s notorious intelligence agency, the Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI), from the Kolpure area of District Bolan. After his enforced disappearance, his family joined the struggle of thousands of other Baloch missing persons’ families for the safe recovery of their loved ones. Despite his case being internationally highlighted, his bullet-riddled body was found on 13 February 2012 in Murgaap, Turbat. His body bore multiple bullet wounds and showed signs of inhumane torture. Sangat Sana’s only crime was demanding justice for his people, and the occupying forces abducted and killed him, but they could not stop his struggle. The occupying forces may have killed him.

On 15 April 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch said that between April 3 and April 14, 2026, fighters of the BLA killed 29 personnel of the occupying Pakistani army and injured several others in fourteen different operations across various areas of Balochistan, including Surab, Kharan, Washuk, Mastung, Uthal, Jhal Magsi, and Panjgur. During these operations, full control was established over various highways and checkposts of the occupying forces, where blockades were set up, and 13 Levies and police personnel were taken into custody. In these attacks, the occupying army’s supply lines were also targeted and destroyed at two locations. In intense clashes in the Surab area of Balochistan with the occupying army, three BLA fighters - Abdul Saleem Jattak, alias Qazi Naveed; Ali Dost, alias Mulla Zakir; and Samiullah Shahwani, alias Hakkal - attained martyrdom while fighting gallantly.
Abdul Saleem Jattak, alias Qazi Naveed, son of Mohammad Hayat Jattak was resident of Mushk, Sar-Aap area of Zehri, Khuzdar district Balochistan, he joined the BLA Urban Front on January 2025 and to mountain Front on August 2025 and served in Zehri, Kalat, Surab fronts and martyred on April 6, 2026 in Surab.
Abdul Saleem Jattak, alias Qazi Naveed, was recognized as a fearless and resolute Sarmachar (Freedom Fighter) of the Baloch Liberation Army. He dedicated his life entirely to the national liberation movement, and every step he took became a model of commitment among his fellow sarmachar. In the early phase of his struggle, he resisted national subjugation as an urban guerrilla, delivering significant blows to the enemy on multiple occasions.
With a deep realization of the importance of national freedom, he came to regard resistance against oppression as the only meaningful path. This conviction led him to formally join the ranks of the BLA. Until his final moments, he remained unwavering in his ideological commitment and ultimately embraced the highest form of sacrifice.
During the battlefield on the Kalat and Surab fronts, he rendered remarkable service. Among his fellow sarmachar, he was remembered as a disciplined, well-mannered, and highly professional fighter, as well as a deeply responsible companion. His courage, endurance, and ability to withstand the hardships of war formed the essence of his revolutionary character. He will always be remembered as an exemplary figure in the struggle for Baloch national liberation. The sacrifices of Shaheed Qazi Naveed, along with others like him, continue to shape the vision of an independent Balochistan.
data.fullName: Abdul Saleem Jattak, alias Qazi Naveed

Faizan Shahwani, alias Rehan, son of Attaullah Shahwani, was a resident of the Killi Ghulam Khan area of Sariab, Quetta. He joined the BLA in 2024 and the Majeed Brigade in 2025. He was among the young men whose identities were shaped not by words but by action. Raised in the atmosphere of Sariab, he soon became part of ranks where decisions are measured not by rhetoric but by responsibility. After joining the BLA in 2024, he developed within a short period the discipline and seriousness required to stand among the ranks of the Majeed Brigade. His inclusion in January 2025 reflected that he had come forward not merely with emotion, but with preparation and clear resolve.
On the Nushki front, Operation Herof II was initiated by Sangat Faizan Shahwani, who carried out an attack using an explosives-laden vehicle targeting the office of Pakistan’s intelligence agency, the ISI. This action inflicted significant damage on a key enemy center and marked the beginning of the historic six-day battle of the Baloch liberation movement.
His sacrifice conveys a clear message: resistance is sustained not by slogans but by the continuity of action across generations. He was the cousin of martyred Fateh Squad fighter Hiras alias Nodan, and in this way two young men from the same family fulfilled their commitment within the same struggle, leaving behind a shared legacy of resolve.

Attahullah Baloch, son of Faqeer Jan Baloch, a 35-year-old resident of Kodask, Khuzdar, was forcibly disappeared on 24 March 2026 from Panjgur by personnel of the ISI, CTD, and MI. He remained in illegal detention and was subjected to torture for nearly three months, until 21 June 2026, when he was extrajudicially killed in Panjgur by the same forces that had forcibly disappeared him.

Arzi Khan Marri, son of Meero Khan Marri, was a 32 year old political worker and a resident of Winder, Lasbela. On 28 September 2010, he was abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. After months under the state's “kill and dump” policy, his body was dumped at Zero Point, Uthal, Lasbela, on 14 February 2011.

On 20 October 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Azad Baloch stated that on 25 September 2026, the occupying Pakistani army launched a military operation, during which BLA fighters thwarted the assault and eliminated approximately fourteen enemy soldiers. Engaging the enemy with great valour, BLA fighters repelled the assault in a clash that began at 6:00 AM.

During the battle, three brave sons of Baloch soil - Hameedullah Baloch, alias Bilali Baloch; Abdul Hameed, alias Bilali Baloch, a resident of Noshki; and Naseeb Baloch, alias Asad, a resident of Manguchar - were martyred, making the ultimate sacrifice in defence of the Baloch motherland.

A large number of enemy forces participated in the engagement, supported by drones. BLA fighters demonstrated exceptional courage and bravery, engaging the occupying army in direct combat from 6:00 AM until 4:00 PM.

All three brave fighters had joined the BLA in 2023. They participated in several significant battles against the occupying enemy on various fronts, delivering a jaw-dropping response to the enemy.

On 29 May 2024, in the Nushki area of Balochistan, operatives of a death squad operating under Pakistani forces killed Balach Baloch by opening indiscriminate fire. Prior to his killing, Balach had been abducted and forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces. He was also the brother of the renowned Baloch poet, Absar Baloch.

The name of martyred fidayee comrade Zafar Baloch, alias Manan, has been forever immortalized among the martyrs of Operation Darra-e-Bolan. This great sarmachar, hailing from the Maripur area of Karachi, joined the BLA in 2022 and soon became a part of the BLA’s Majeed Brigade due to his exceptional combat skills and unwavering resolve. He was among the fearless fighters who, through determination, bravery, and tactical expertise, carried out battles whose echoes reverberated deep within enemy camps. Every attack he carried out delivered a new message of destruction to the enemy, and every strategy he executed became a source of further strengthening the BLA’s power.

Liaquat Baloch, son of Saki Dad and a resident of Shapkol was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces from an auto mechanic shop where he had gone for car repair work.

Two days later, on August 11, 2025, his mutilated body was found in the Jusak area of Turbat. Liaquat had previously been forcibly disappeared by Pakistani intelligence agencies and military personnel on January 2, 2023, and was released after a month of illegal detention, during which he endured extreme torture, inhumane treatment, and severe punishment.

After persistent harassment by state-backed death squads in their native town of Kolwah, Liaquat’s family was forced to migrate to Aapsar, Turbat, in search of safety. Despite this relocation, they faced the same fate under the state’s policy of collective punishment, leaving the entire family traumatised.

On February 18, 2026 in the Tejaban area of District Kech, Balochistan, a death squad operating under the command of Pakistani forces killed Dolat Baloch, son of Badal, in a targeted attack. He was from Tejaban Singaband and belonged to a poor farming family, working on his ancestral land.
In March 2022, the Pakistani Frontier Corps raided his home. Dolat and his 12 year old brother were forcibly disappeared and held in detention. After one month, they were released, but the shadow of oppression never left him. Dolat returned to his daily life, carrying the memory of injustice.
On February 18, 2026, at around 2:00 PM, while returning home, he was shot and killed in cold blood by a motorcycle borne death squad.

On 11 July 2025 in the Killi Kamalo Saryab area of Quetta, Balochistan, plainclothes officers from Pakistani security forces, the Counter-Terrorism Department, and the ISI raided Abdulmutallab’s house, they took him away and disappeared him.
After being forcibly disappeared for several months, on 19 January 2026 in Dasht Mastung, he was killed in a fake encounter along with several other Baloch youths, the next day 20 January 2026 his body was returned to his family, showing obvious signs of torture while in custody.

On 8 August 2016, terrorists attacked the Government Hospital in Quetta, Balochistan, in a suicide bombing and shooting. More than 70 people were killed, mainly lawyers, and more than 130 others were injured.
The majority of those killed were lawyers who had gathered at the hospital after the body of Advocate Bilal Anwar Kasi, president of the Balochistan Bar Association, was brought there. Kasi had been shot dead by a gunman near Mengal Chowk on Manno Jan Road in Quetta while he was leaving his home for his office.
Responsibility for the attack was claimed by various Islamist groups, including Jamaat-ul-Ahrar and the Islamic State Khorasan Province. However, nationalist groups have alleged that these extremist organisations are backed by the Pakistani state and its military to counter the nationalist movement in the region and exploit its natural resources.
Estimates of the death toll ranged between 70 people, while more than 120 were injured. Of those killed, 54 were lawyers. Among them, 15 were Baloch by ethnicity, while the majority were Pashtuns by ethnicity.
