Najeebullah Langove, son of Abdul Waheed Langove, a 25 year old student and resident of Killi Ismail, Hudda, Quetta, was abducted on 14 May 2010 by Pakistani forces. On 23 July 2010, his body was dumped in Satellite Town, Quetta.

Ghulam Qadir Pirkani, the son of Mohammad Hashim Pirkani, was a 24-year-old student and a resident of New Kahan, Hazar Ganji, Quetta, Balochistan. He was abducted by Pakistani forces on 6 July 2010 and forcibly disappeared. A month later, on 6 August 2010, his body was found in Killi Khalli, Quetta.

Babar Yousif was a veteran of the Baloch national movement, having been active in the armed struggle since 2011. He was known for his strategic military mind and was a key figure in the BNA. During the Diz clash, he reportedly led a successful counter-siege that allowed other members of the unit to retreat safely before he was martyred.

In 1838, the British sent a force led by Alexander Burnes to reinstate Shah Shuja Durrani as the king of Afghanistan by deposing Amir Dost Mohammad Khan. To reach Afghanistan, they needed passage through Balochistan, particularly the Bolan Pass. However, Khan Mehrab Khan refused to allow the British to use his land to attack a neighboring country. The British sent Lieutenant Leach to negotiate with the Baloch government, but the Khan stood firm. When British forces reached Shaal via Bolan, some patriotic Baloch, without the Khan’s knowledge, attacked British troops out of nationalist sentiment and a desire to protect their homeland.
After toppling Amir Dost Mohammad Khan, the British Governor General of India, Lord Auckland, ordered an attack on Balochistan. In 1839, around 7,000 British troops marched from Shaal to attack the Baloch Meeri (capital). Anticipating an invasion, Khan Mehrab Khan declared war and sent messages to tribal leaders, but many saw the British as allies rather than invaders and chose to collaborate with them rather than defend their land. When Khan Mehrab Khan gathered his resistance fighters, the number of loyal warriors had dwindled to only 700 due to the short sightedness of many tribal chiefs. Nevertheless, Mehrab Khan was determined to fight. At his court, a respected figure, Akhund Muhammad Siddiq, advised him that he was not in a position to wage war at that time. He suggested that the Khan should leave Kalat with his companions, regroup and strengthen his forces, and then launch an attack against the British when the time was right, on 13 November 1839, the British forces launched an attack on Kalat, and a fierce battle ensued. During the fighting, Khan Mehrab Khan Baloch was martyred by a British bullet.
Khan Mehrab Khan replied:

I know that the British are rulers of England and India, and they have also established their authority over Kandahar. Confronting them now is difficult. But where can I go, abandoning my land? My father’s blood was shed for this soil. I do not want to tarnish my name in history by fleeing. Nor can I accept slavery. I would rather choose death over a life of servitude.

On 12 August 2026, several Baloch people, including women and children, were killed and several others were injured as a result of an aerial bombardment of a civilian population by the Pakistan Air Force, reportedly using American-made F-16 fighter aircraft, in the Gidar Gindan area of Surab District, Balochistan. Following the airstrike, the injured and deceased were transported by police and local residents to DHQ Hospital in Surab, where the injured received medical treatment.

The families of the deceased and local residents subsequently began a protest by placing the bodies at Surab Main Chowk on the Quetta–Karachi National Highway (N-25). As a result, traffic on the highway was disrupted, with long queues of vehicles forming on both sides. Videos and photographs of the protest subsequently circulated widely on social media under the hashtag #SurabMassacre.

Those killed in the airstrike were identified as Shabir Ahmad Sumalani, son of Khudadad Sumalani, a resident of Marap, Surab; Noor Jan Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, a resident of Gindan; Karim Dad Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, a resident of Gandan; Raj Babu, wife of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani; Safia, wife of Noor Jan Mirwani; and Jalal Mirwani, son of Noor Jan Mirwani.

Those injured were identified as Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani, son of Jan Muhammad Mirwani; Abdul Karim Mirwani, son of Jan Muhammad Mirwani; Mehrullah Mirwani, son of Rasool Bakhsh Mirwani; Nadeem Mirwani, son of Abdul Salam Mirwani; Shoaib Mirwani, son of Abdul Karim Mirwani; Sarah, wife of Baseer Ahmed Mirwani; Sabira, wife of Tufail Ahmed Mirwani; Zamra, daughter of Abdul Aziz Mirwani; Hajira, wife of Abdul Fattah Mirwani; Asim, son of Baseer, aged 1; Rahabia, daughter of Abdul Karim, aged 3; Sadia, daughter of Abdul Salam, aged 5; Fatima, daughter of Abdul Karim, aged 7; Zia-ur-Rehman, son of Abdul Karim, aged 2; Amir, son of Abdul Karim, aged 1; and Hasina, daughter of Muhammad Aslam, aged 4.

Following a detailed technical and scientific analysis of remnants of rocket components recovered from debris at the site of the aerial bombardment, important evidence reportedly emerged indicating that the recovered fragments belonged to an air-launched missile fired from an F-16 fighter aircraft.

Photographs of the recovered debris and the subsequent technical analysis reportedly indicated that the fragment was part of an AIM-120 Advanced Medium-Range Air-to-Air Missile (AMRAAM), an American-made air-to-air missile.

Key technical evidence and serial numbers

According to the information and serial numbers reportedly engraved on the surface of the debris, the following details were recorded:

Assembly Number: ASSY 872128-1

Serial Number: 09-987138

Date of Manufacture: 09/09 (September 2009)

According to open-source intelligence (OSINT) records, the part number “872128-1” reportedly corresponds to the control section and rocket motor assembly of an AMRAAM missile manufactured by the American defense company Raytheon. Based on this evidence and the reported matching serial numbers, it is claimed that the debris was not part of an aircraft’s internal structure but instead consisted of remnants from an operational missile fired from an F-16 aircraft.
On 13 August 2020, soldiers of the Pakistani force, the Frontier Corps, tied up Mohammad Hayat Baloch in front of his parents and killed him by shooting him with eight bullets.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Qudratullah Kurd, alias Majeed Baloch, son of Badal Khan Kurd, was a resident of Maro in the Spilingi area of Mastung district, Balochistan. He affiliated with the BLA in 2024 and joined the Majeed Brigade in 2025. He was martyred in the Red Zone of Quetta.
Qudratullah Kurd, alias Majeed Baloch, was among those young individuals whose life journey may be brief, but whose significance is profound. His struggle represents a generation that chooses the path of resistance not driven by accidental passion or temporary emotion, but through conscious awareness and firm resolve.
After affiliating with the organization, Qudratullah quickly distinguished himself through seriousness, discipline, and steadfastness, earning the trust to carry out the most demanding responsibilities. Joining the Majeed Brigade is not simply a result of military training, but a responsibility earned after passing through a mental and moral threshold—one that Qudratullah crossed with remarkable maturity.
During Operation Herof, the battle in Quetta became the final and most defining chapter of his life. Near the Red Zone, at the railway station, he fought enemy forces for several hours. Amidst an intense firefight, he was shot, but even in his wounded state, he exhibited neither urgency nor panic. He remained composed, with the kind of tranquility that only comes to those fully reconciled with their decisions.
His final moments are preserved in this video. Seated inside an explosives-laden vehicle, he bid farewell to his Sarmachar comrades with a smile. His face reflected neither fear nor uncertainty, but a deep and calm resolve. He said:
“We are together. We are together until freedom. Do not spare it (Pakistan).”
One of his fellow fighters kissed him on the forehead in farewell. With peaceful determination, he drove the vehicle toward the Red Zone, struck his target, and embraced martyrdom.
To understand Qudratullah’s character, witnessing those final moments is enough. In the field of resistance, the greatest strength is not in noise or aggression, but in that quiet certainty that renders one fearless before the end. His smile was the symbol of that conviction.

On 9 May 2026, the spokesperson for the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) Gwahram Baloch issued a statement saying that on 4 May 2026, fighters of the organization were conducting a routine patrol in Washuk when they suddenly came face to face with the occupying Pakistani army. The fighters immediately adopted effective guerrilla warfare tactics, swiftly dividing into different units and launching attacks on the enemy. As a result of this strategy, three enemy personnel were killed and several others were wounded.

During the clash, a BLF fighter was injured, yet he continued to confront the enemy with steadfastness. Two fighters, Captain Mukhtiyar Baloch, alias Peerak Baloch, and Gareeb Shah, alias Irfan Baloch, held their positions and kept enemy units engaged, blocking their advance so that their fellow fighters could safely withdraw from the area. Due to their courageous strategy, all other fighters successfully reached their safe bases. Both fighters continued fighting until their last bullet and breath, ultimately embracing martyrdom.

Captain Mukhtiyar Baloch, alias Peerak Baloch, was from the Kalar area of Mashkay. He was a highly educated and ideologically committed young fighter who began his struggle through the platform of the Balochistan Liberation Front in 2012 at a very young age. However, due to his age, he was not engaged in operational activities at that time. During that period, he continued his studies and, after earning a BS degree in Sociology from the University of Balochistan, formally joined operational activities on the mountain front in 2021. Due to his exceptional combat skills and organizational discipline, he quickly rose to the position of Camp Commander of the Rakhshan Region. He not only fought successful battles against the enemy on the fronts of Mashkay, Awaran, and Washuk, but also played a key role in the physical and ideological training of new fighters. His family has sacrificed more than a dozen lives for the national cause, a legacy that fills the Baloch nation with pride and continues to inspire fighters.

Muhsin, son of Muslim, was a 21-year-old hardworking driver from Suleman Bazar, Paroom, Panjgur. He belonged to a poor family and was the main source of hope and support for his household.
On 16 March 2026, he was forcibly disappeared from the Jeerak crossing point in Paroom, Panjgur. For 66 days, his family lived in fear and uncertainty, waiting for any news of his return. However, during Eid, on 19 May 2026, his dead body was recovered from Kallag Koor, Paroom.
Personnel of the Frontier Corps forcibly disappeared him and later killed him while he was in detention.

data.biography:
Khalil Ahmed, son of Ahmed, a serving employee of the Police Department and a resident of Panjgur, was abducted and forcibly disappeared on December 13, 2025, by Pakistani intelligence agencies and security personnel.
He was taken earlier that day from the Tasp area. Hours later, his body was recovered from the Chakul Kalag area. The body bore clear and visible marks of severe torture.

Dilawar Khan, son of Lal Bakhsh and a resident of Nodz, Turbat, was a lecturer at the University of Balochistan Sub-Campus in Kharan.
On the morning of March 4, 2026, Dilawar Khan and his colleague Bilal Ahmed, son of Ghulam Jan and a resident of Panjgur, were attacked by a state-backed death squad in front of the Sub-Campus in Kharan. As a result of the attack, Dilawar Khan was killed on the spot, while Bilal Ahmed was severely injured. He was initially shifted to Sheikh Zaid Hospital in Kharan and was later transferred to Quetta due to his critical condition.

Shah Dur Mengal, son of Aman Ullah Mengal and a resident of Nokundi, district Chaghi, Balochistan, was shot dead by direct and indiscriminate fire from personnel of the Federal Constabulary (FC) on July 18, 2025.
Shah Dur was a poor civilian, working as a driver of an oil transport pickup (Zamyad), earning a living through cross-border fuel trade from Iran to Pakistan—an essential means of survival for people in the border region. He was also the sole breadwinner of his family.
Following his killing, family members staged a protest and placed his lifeless body on the main highway in Nokundi the same evening. The demonstrators demanded accountability from the FC personnel responsible for the extrajudicial killing of Shah Dur.
As of July 19, the family and local residents continued their blockade across the Baab-e-Umar entry point, halting all traffic in and out of Nokundi. A widespread shutdown was also observed in nearby areas including Chaghi, Dalbandin, Chahtar, and Yakmach, with local markets remaining closed in solidarity.

In a face to face battle with the Pakistani military and its agents in the mountainous regions of Noshki and Kharan on 24 September 2021, more than a dozen enemy personnel were killed, whereas six freedom fighters, including five members of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), also embraced martyrdom.
The battle commenced early Friday morning in Siyah Lop, near Baddo Dor, when enemy forces attempted to encircle a patrolling party of Baloch freedom fighters. In the face-to-face battle that lasted for more than four hours, scores of enemy personnel were killed and injured. Five freedom fighters of the BLA and one freedom fighter of the United Baloch Army (UBA), while evacuating their comrades from the battle zone, embraced martyrdom.
The fallen comrades include Commander Ganjal alias Comrade Mazar, Nazeer alias Sangar, Faisal alias Yasir, Kaleem alias Bolani, and Rehan alias Mehrwaan, all members of the Baloch Liberation Army. A member of the United Baloch Army, Nodaan alias Hammal, bravely fought alongside BLA comrades and embraced martyrdom.
The brave and young freedom fighter Rehan alias Mehrwaan, son of Shaukat Badini, who belonged to Noshki town, had joined the BLA a year ago.
data.martyrdomPlace: Noshki and Kharan mountainous area, Balochistan

data.biography: Ishaq Baloch was born to Akbar Baloch and Zar Bibi Baloch in Kanadadi, in the Mashkay area of Awaran, Balochistan. He served as a member of the Levies Force. He was abducted and extrajudicially killed by Pakistani genocidal forces in the Mashkay area of Awaran District, Balochistan, on January 1, 2015.

On 6 November 2026, the Baloch Liberation Army's media channel, Hakkal, published the biographies and details of six martyrs associated with the organization.

Among them, three fighters - Muneer Ahmad Jattak, alias Noora, son of Habib Khan Jattak; Shahzaib Bangulzai, alias Ehsan, son of Samiullah Bangulzai; and Fareed Langove, son of Ghulam Nabi Langove - were martyred on 20 October 2026 in the Rodinjo area of Kalat District.

Two other fighters, Parvez Ahmad Mohammad Hassni, alias Qadir, son of Shekari Mohammad Khan Mohammad Hassni, and Noman Jamaldini, alias Comrade Sameer, son of Agha Mohammad Jamaldini, were martyred on 24 October 2026 in the Gidar area of Surab.

The sixth fighter, Aurangzaib Langove, alias Asif, son of Hameedullah Langove, was martyred on 24 October 2026 in the Manguchar area of Kalat District.

Parvez Ahmad Mohammad Hassni, alias Qadir, son of Shekari Mohammad Khan Mohammad Hassni, was a resident of Hilmarg, Kharan. He joined the BLA in 2026 and served on the Surab front. He was martyred on 24 October 2026 in the Gidar area of Surab.

Pervez Ahmad Mohammad Hassni began his journey in 2026 under the banner of the Baloch Liberation Army, with the aim of achieving Baloch national freedom and self-determination. He made this decision out of the belief that the Baloch people should no longer face humiliation at the hands of the enemy on their own land and should rise above this dark era of oppression. His decision reflected the collective consciousness and awareness of the Baloch people, who have declared war against the occupier and continue to sacrifice their lives for the freedom of their homeland. Upon joining the organisation, he was transferred to a training camp, where he received basic training.

After completing his training, he was deployed to the Surab front, where he demonstrated strong combat skills and participated in several military operations. Alongside his comrades, he fought against the enemy and remained committed to his cause. He was regarded as a Sarmachar who led from the front and remained steadfast in his convictions. He maintained the same zeal and determination until his final days.

He remained devoted to the national cause for which he had joined the organisation, upholding his beliefs and purpose until the very end. On 24 October 2026, he attained martyrdom during a one-on-one encounter with the enemy. He will always be remembered as a shining star in the history of Baloch national liberation.

On 21 October 2025, a statement was issued by Baloch Khan, the spokesperson of the Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar (BRAS), an umbrella alliance of Baloch armed organizations. The statement said that, in defence of the Baloch population in Zehri, Khuzdar, Balochistan, BRAS forces eliminated dozens of enemy personnel, while six freedom fighters embraced martyrdom. Among them was Martyr Fiaz Jattak, alias Shahwaiz.

The statement added that the occupying Pakistani army attempted to advance for aggressive purposes in the Zehri area of Khuzdar, which is under the control of the Baloch Raaji Ajoi Sangar (BRAS), resulting in fierce clashes. Dozens of occupying army personnel were eliminated in these clashes, while six freedom fighters of the Baloch Raaji Aajoi Sangar were martyred in defence of the motherland.

Among the martyrs, Abdul Aziz Baloch and Hafiz Muhammad Umar Baloch were martyred on 26 September, while Sanaullah Baloch, Abdul Aziz Baloch, Rashid Ahmed Zehri, and Fiaz Jattak were martyred on 30 September.

Martyr Fiaz Jattak, also known as Shahwaiz, son of Fazal Jattak, belonged to Zehri, Khuzdar, Balochistan. He joined the Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) in January this year. He was a man of discipline, calmness, and steadfastness, who always demonstrated responsibility and sacrifice on the front line. He believed that national liberation is not possible without sacrifice, and he proved this belief true with his blood.

Abdul Rehman, a 16-year-old student and resident of Tump, Kech, Balochistan, was brutally killed by state-backed militias, locally referred to as death squads, on November 2, 2025. The incident occurred at approximately 1:00 PM inside a shop, where he was shot dead in front of his father, Tariq Noor.

Abdul Rehman was an intermediate-level student known for his academic dedication and promising future. He had recently returned home to visit his family during the winter vacation.

On 9 September 2026, Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch issued a statement announcing the martyrdom of ten fighters belonging to the organization. He paid tribute to the Sarmachars who were martyred while defending national liberation and their homeland, Balochistan.
- The statement identified the following fighters:
1-  Akhtar Dawood, alias Ali Sher, son of Asad Sajidi.
2- Khalil Ahmad, alias Ustad Awais, son of Sher Ahmad.
3-  Imran, alias Aajo, son of Saifullah.
4-  Hasil, alias Munir Ahmad, son of Sher Mohammad.
5- Inayatullah, alias Sher Zaman, son of Manzoor Ahmad.
6- Asad Rahim, son of Rahim Baksh.
7- Mujeeb Ur Rehman, alias Shay Mureed, son of Saeed Ahmad.
8- Sahil, alias Arman, son of Peeral.
9- Javed, alias Murshid.
10- Mohammad Younis, alias Taleb, son of Mohammad Omar.

Asad Rahim, son of Rahim Bakhsh, formally joined the organization in 2017 and carried out armed actions and intelligence duties on the urban front. While employed with the occupying Pakistan Navy, he gathered important information from Siddique Air Base and passed it on to the organization. After coming to the enemy’s attention, he was moved from the urban front to the mountain front on 13 June 2026. On 15 July 2026, enemy forces besieged the fighters at Dilsar in Dasht Balnigwar. Fighting in the front line, he launched a counterattack on the enemy that weakened the siege, and while providing cover for other sarmachars to withdraw, he was martyred fighting bravely. He was a brave and knowledgeable fighter well versed in guerrilla strategy. Working in a sensitive location like Siddique Air Base, he provided the organization with extremely important information about the enemy; his decade spent working close to the enemy while serving the national war is clear proof of his guerrilla capabilities.

Ali Baloch, son of Musa and a resident of Rothbon, in Tump, district Kech, was brutally shot and killed by state-backed death squads in broad daylight on May 5, 2025. He sustained critical bullet wounds after death squads operating with the full backing of Pakistani armed forces opened direct fire on him. He succumbed to his injuries later the same day.
Local sources have confirmed that the assailants were affiliated with state-sponsored death squads that operate openly in the region under the patronage of the Pakistani Army, Federal Constabulary, and intelligence agencies.

On 14 January 2026 in Geshkor Reakchai of Awaran district, Balochistan, a criminal armed group operating under the Pakistani forces locally known as the “death squad” abducted Dr. Zareef Baloch, son of Mohammad Yaqoob, in broad daylight from his medical store at around 5 PM. Approximately two hours later, at about 7 PM his tortured body was recovered from a river.

In the early hours of May 24, 2025, at approximately 3:00 a.m., journalist Abdul Latif Baloch was brutally assassinated inside his home in Mashkay, Awaran District, Balochistan, by Pakistani state-backed death squads. He was shot dead in front of his wife and children.
Abdul Latif was far more than a journalist in a war-torn region. He was a voice for the oppressed and a courageous documenter of Baloch suffering, resistance, and resilience. In a land where speaking truth is punished with bullets, his reporting made him a target of a state that treats journalism as treason.

Abu Bakr Hasil, son of Hasil and a resident of Dasht Balnigwar Kaliro, Turbat district, who was currently living in Gwadar Baloch Ward, was forcibly disappeared by Pakistani forces on November 26, 2024. The local community reported that Abu Bakr was forcibly taken by Pakistani soldiers from Gwadar Baloch Ward. He was an ordinary Baloch man who supported his family by running a small cart on which he sold vegetables and earned a modest income. After a year of his disappearance, on November 28, 2025, his mutilated body bearing clear signs of torture and severe abuse was found in D-Baloch, an area in District Kech, early in the morning.

On 22 October 2026, a statement issued by Balochistan Liberation Front (BLF) spokesperson Gwahram Baloch stated that BLF fighters had formally launched Operation Almas with a large-scale, coordinated attack on the main camp of the Pakistani army’s Frontier Works Organization (FWO) at Gwadar Zero Point. Fighters from the BLF’s special Saddo Operational Battalion, alongside members of other units, are participating in this major military engagement. The battle continued into the following day, 23 October 2026, with loud explosions and intense gunfire heard from the location. On 23 October 2026, a statement issued by the BLF spokesperson announced the completion of Operation Almas. The statement claimed that dozens of military and intelligence personnel had been killed, the hub of colonial projects had been destroyed, and army and Frontier Corps posts had been wiped out. It declared that the historic Operation Almas had concluded after achieving all its intended objectives. Operation Almas was carried out in Gwadar and the surrounding areas. It has formally concluded after reportedly achieving all its planned strategic, military, and economic objectives following prolonged and intense clashes. During this wide-ranging operation, the occupying Pakistani army and intelligence network suffered what the statement described as irreparable human and material losses. The BLF’s self-sacrificing fighters targeted the Frontier Works Organization’s (FWO) main camp, destroying a key centre for the implementation of colonial projects, particularly in Gwadar and across Makuran. This, the statement asserted, demonstrated to the world that, without the will and consent of the Baloch nation, colonial projects in Balochistan would never be safe. The offices and camps of Inter-Services Intelligence (ISI) and Military Intelligence (MI) inside the FWO’s main camp were also targeted by the organisation’s fighters. Several soldiers, including senior officers, were reportedly killed in the attacks. Throughout Operation Almas, the Jind-Nadr Sarmachars not only thwarted every counterattack by the occupying army, every attempt by armoured vehicles to advance, and every reinforcement convoy, but also forced them to retreat, maintaining control of the camp for twenty hours. As a result of the actions of the Saddo Operational Battalion’s fighters during Operation Almas, Military Intelligence (MI) officers, Special Services Group (SSG) personnel, and dozens of regular army personnel were reportedly killed. In addition, the enemy’s main camp, posts, internal barracks, and administrative offices were reportedly destroyed in explosions and attacks. A number of the occupying army’s armoured vehicles, along with surveillance drones and quadcopters, were also reportedly destroyed during the operation. After repeatedly inflicting defeats on the occupying enemy during Operation Almas, the Jind-Nadr Sarmachars of the Saddo Operational Battalion, adhering to the philosophy of the last bullet, sacrificed their lives in the struggle for freedom, adding a new chapter of bravery to Baloch national history. The following Jind-Nadr Sarmachars played key roles in the operation: Khalid, alias Zamur; Bilqees Didag, alias Almas; Hamidullah, alias Badil; Shakeel, alias Sohrab; Majeed Zaib, alias Aftab; Nasir Ali, alias Nodan; Mujahid Mehr, alias Sagar Zamurani; and Barat, alias Safar Jan. All eight were reported to have embraced martyrdom during this historic operation. On 27 October 2026, the spokesperson issued another detailed statement, announcing that BLF special units had carried out a comprehensive, coordinated, organized, and effective attack on the centres of the occupying Pakistani army, the colonial intelligence network, and exploitative institutions in Gwadar. The statement claimed that more than 80 military and intelligence personnel had been killed; several armoured vehicles, the main army barracks, and intelligence offices had been destroyed; four quadcopters and two surveillance drones had been shot down; and a police station had been seized. It also reported that operations had been conducted at Gabd and Rimdan 250. Following these deadly blows to the state's exploitative structures, Operation Almas was declared successfully concluded. The spokesperson stated that the BLF was formally presenting to the nation, subjugated peoples, and the international community a comprehensive account of the far-reaching military and political achievements of Operation Almas. The historic, organized, effective, coordinated, and comprehensive operation was launched at 4:00 p.m. on 22 October 2026 against the occupying Pakistani state apparatus in Gwadar and the adjoining coastal region. The operation was described as the most organized, coordinated, and far-reaching attack to date against the occupying Pakistani state, its usurping army, intelligence network, exploitative economic institutions, and local puppet administration. It was presented as an expression of the organization's resolve and capabilities. The revolutionary participation of fearless Baloch women, standing shoulder to shoulder with men in the struggle for Baloch national freedom, national survival, and the defence of the coast and its resources, was portrayed as heralding the end of the usurping colonizer. This historic operation was named after the BLF's fearless and courageous guerrilla commander, Almas Baloch. For the past eight years, Commander Almas had been actively involved in the armed national struggle under the BLF banner, driven by her ideological convictions. Bilqees Didag, alias Almas, daughter of Allah Bakhsh Didag, resident of Dasht Kumbel, is a shining chapter of courage, steadfastness and revolutionary sacrifice. She spent her early life in ordinary circumstances and received regular education up to the eighth grade. She was married and has a beloved daughter, but rising above herself and her family circle, she made the cause of the motherland's freedom her whole life. In 2018 she formally joined the armed struggle for national freedom through BLF's revolutionary platform. After joining the organization, she served for four years as a volunteer in the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB), rendering highly valuable and arduous service. For the past eight years Shaheed Almas had been fully active and ideologically committed in the armed defense struggle through the BLF platform. During her organizational life she served as a very active and fearless member of the intelligence wing in sensitive and difficult areas such as Dasht, Turbat and Gwadar. She kept herself in motion day and night to deliver vital intelligence about the enemy to the organization in time. During military fronts and operations, she always carried out, with courage and steadfastness, the very difficult and dangerous responsibility of delivering supplies, weapons and logistics to the sarmachars across Dasht's harsh and rugged mountain ranges. On the path of her revolutionary struggle, the occupying Pakistani army and operatives of the state's death squads made every effort to obstruct her. The occupying army repeatedly attempted to abduct her, hold her in illegal detention and break her mentally and physically, and on one occasion state personnel subjected her to severe torture that left her badly injured. But this tactic of state oppression, taunting and torture could not shake her steadfastness. She faced every hardship with a smile and always stood firm like a rock on the armed front, keeping the flag of freedom high. Even in these grave conditions under state oppression, the wise and courageous way she carried out organizational responsibilities while hiding in various areas is eloquent proof of her high military insight and ideological maturity. Shaheed Bilqees Didag alias Almas put into practice the idea that on the difficult path of national freedom, all hardships, troubles and sacrifices are acceptable, but national slavery and state domination are not acceptable under any circumstances. To realize this idea, she made the final decision to sacrifice herself for the motherland. Shaheed Almas carried out her duties with great devotion in various military detachments and units of the BLF, and from the time the Saddo Operational Battalion (SOB) was founded she was its active founder and core member.

Abdul Razaq Baloch, son of Abdul Ghani and a resident of Marri Abad, Mach, Bolan, was forcibly disappeared on 1 January 2026 after being taken into custody at Abdul Ghaffar Qalandrani Petrol Pump in Marri Abad, Mach. His family remained unaware of his whereabouts for more than five months and received no information about his condition.
On 12 June 2026, Abdul Razaq's body was identified among those of individuals killed in an alleged staged fake encounter conducted by the CTD in Sibi.

On 27 October 2025 at around 4:30 in the evening, fighters of the United Baloch Army (UBA) set up checkpoints at the entry points of Bhag Nari town in Kachhi district. They entered the town in large numbers and carried out attacks on the police station, the NADRA office, the Levies station, the Tehsildar’s office, and the National Bank.
During the siege of the police station, the personnel present were warned based on their identification and being Baloch, but they opened fire on the fighters. In response, the fighters retaliated in self-defense, leading to intense clashes. Three personnel, including SHO Lutf Ali, were killed and three were injured. At the same time, the fighters surrounded the Levies station, released the 11 detainees present there, and seized the official weapons of the Levies personnel. The building of the station was then set on fire. The National Bank and the Tehsildar’s office were also targeted and set ablaze.
After holding control of the town for several hours and completing their objectives, the fighters were preparing to withdraw when a large contingent of the Frontier Corps arrived around the town. As a result, heavy clashes continued for about an hour between the fighters and the FC, during which three FC personnel were killed and several others injured.
During the fighting, Sahib Khan Bangulzai, also known as Shaukat, remained at the final defensive position. Without regard for his own safety, he confronted the incoming fire, allowing his companions a chance to retreat. By sacrificing his life, Sahib Khan Bangulzai enabled the others to withdraw safely, and the remaining fighters managed to escape without harm.
Sahib Khan Bangulzai, known as Shaukat, joined the United Baloch Army in 2024. Within a short period, due to his notable intelligence, strong dedication, and military skills, he gained a prominent position. As an urban guerrilla, he closely monitored enemy movements, established a strong intelligence network, and played an important role in local defense. Until his final moments, he continued to resist and ultimately lost his life, which the organization describes as martyrdom.

On 26 April 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army carried out twenty-seven operations across Balochistan between 15 April and 25 April. These operations included IED blasts, drone strikes, and ambushes targeting the Pakistani military. In these attacks, 42 personnel were killed and numerous others were injured, while one soldier was captured alive. BLA fighters seized control of multiple security posts and confiscated weapons. During clashes at various locations, Sangat Shah Karam Mullazai (alias Sachan), Asim Shahwani (alias Rodain), and Gwahram Baloch (alias Qambar) embraced martyrdom.
Shah Karam Mullazai, alias Sachan, son of Haji Amin Mullazai, was a resident of the Tasp area of Panjgur district, Balochistan. He joined the BLA in December 2023 and served on the Zamuran front with the rank of Camp Commander and Training Instructor. He held a Master’s degree in English Literature and Linguistics from QAU, Islamabad. During his student years, he was active in student politics and served as Chairman and General Secretary of the Baloch Students Organization. He was martyred on 19 April 2026 in Zamuran, Momech.
Chairman Shah Karam Mullazai, alias Sachan, was among the early ranks of the BLA’s conscious and intellectual cadre. He was a Sarmachar commander who viewed Baloch national resistance and the armed struggle not merely as military confrontation, but as a process of building a modern Baloch national state. For Shah Karam, leadership was not about display or the acquisition of power, but about a profound sense of responsibility—one in which the future of coming generations rests upon the shoulders of those who lead.
Despite receiving his education in the capital of the occupying state, he remained intellectually aligned with the conscious struggle for the freedom of Balochistan—a struggle that today stands as a guarantor of collective survival. When he transformed his political thought into action by joining the armed front, he quickly distinguished himself through his capabilities and became a training instructor, preparing young fighters for the struggle. He was known for his strong operational planning in military engagements. Later, due to his outstanding performance and the organization’s merit-based system, he was appointed as a Camp Commander, where he led significant operations.
During his three-year tenure as a Sarmachar and military cadre within the BLA, he was remembered among his fellow Sarmachars as a model for strengthening organizational activity in Makuran, adapting to the demands of modern warfare, integrating knowledge with practice and discipline, and upholding revolutionary and military principles. On the battlefield, he embodied this conscious ideology, ultimately embracing martyrdom during direct combat with enemy forces—an act reflecting historical awareness rooted in resistance against subjugation. On the Zamuran front, he was martyred in a clash with enemy forces on 19 April, leaving his mark in history as a steadfast Sarmachar against occupation.

data.biography:
On 15 May 2026, a press statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that the Sarmachars (freedom fighters) of the Baloch Liberation Army carried out eighteen successful operations against the enemy across Balochistan between 4 May 2026 and 14 May 2026, resulting in the deaths of 31 personnel of the occupying Pakistani army, including a Major-rank officer, while several others were seriously injured. These attacks included seven powerful IED strikes. Additionally, the Sarmachars seized control of main highways for hours at various locations, targeting vehicles belonging to exploitative companies and occupying forces, and detaining individuals associated with these companies. In these coordinated operations, seven personnel and operatives of the state-backed “Death Squads” and Military Intelligence (MI) were also killed.
During intense clashes with the occupying forces at various locations, five BLA fighters - Ali Jan Siahpad alias Sudais, Ahsanullah alias Master Maran, Nasrullah alias Mama Zagreen, Tanveer Mengal alias Murad Khan, and Saadullah Baloch alias Wajid - embraced martyrdom while fighting valiantly against the enemy.

On 4 May 2026, in the Eri Kalag area of Ras Koh, Kharan, local agents of the occupying Pakistani army carried out a cowardly attack, martyring BLA fighter Ali Jan Siahpad alias Sudais.
Ali Jan Siahpad alias Sudais, son of Ali Asghar and a resident of Hari Kalag, Ras Koh, Kharan, joined the BLA in 2025 and served on the Nushki and Kharan fronts. He embraced martyrdom on 4 May 2026 in the Ras Koh area of District Kharan, Balochistan.
Ali Jan Siahpad alias Sudais made a revolutionary and conscious decision to join the ranks of the BLA in 2025. During the past year, he rendered valuable military services on the frontlines. On the Nushki and Kalat fronts, he played the role of a frontline Sarmachar in strengthening the organization’s defensive positions. He was among those revolutionary Sangats who firmly believed in adhering to organizational decisions and carrying out orders without delay.
Within a short period, he understood the demands of the battlefield and proved himself to be a brave, trustworthy, and dedicated Sarmachar through his outstanding performance. He played an active role in strengthening defensive positions and participating in offensive operations. He was among those Sarmachars who believed in delivering decisive blows to the enemy and therefore always remained a fearless warrior on the frontlines.
While defending the homeland in Ras Koh, the sacrifices he made for the restoration of the national state will forever remain inscribed in the pages of history. History will remember him as a great national hero who, instead of accepting a life of slavery, chose martyrdom for the restoration of a free homeland and never accepted the enemy’s occupation.

Sixteen year old Hayat Sazbal forcibly disappeared on July 3, 2024, from a car wash in Turbat, Kech, and was later killed in a staged encounter in Panjgur on the night of February 11, 2025. After his abduction, Hayat Sabzal's family protested in front of the Deputy Commissioner's (DC) office in Turbat in July, demanding his release. The forces assured them that he would be produced before a court, but he was never brought to trial.

On 3rd April 2026, a statement issued by Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) spokesperson Jeeyand Baloch stated that fighters of the BLA launched a series of coordinated attacks against the occupying Pakistani army across occupied Balochistan on 29th March 2026, which continued until 1st April 2026. The fighters carried out 65 operations in Panjgur, Shapuk, Basima, Sibi, Mastung, Quetta, Noshki, Zamuran, Dasht, Surab, Jhal Magsi, Dalbandin, Kharan, Washuk, and Kalat. In these actions, more than 86 personnel of the Pakistani army, death squads, and intelligence agencies were killed, and dozens were injured. These attacks targeted occupying army camps, an airbase, radar systems, communication towers, railway tracks, bridges, and gas pipelines, while major highways were brought under control for several hours.
During clashes with Pakistani forces, five BLA fighters in Panjgur - Zahid alias Nawaz, Saeedullah alias Meraj, Jahanzeb alias Qambar, Aamir alias Khalid, and Saddam alias Shahwaiz - along with Abdust (Abdul Rehman) alias Alman in Zamuran, attained martyrdom.
Zahid, alias Nawaz (son of Sher Mohammad): A resident of Gichk, Panjgur, he joined the armed struggle in 2016 and became part of the BLA in 2023. He was a fearless warrior and an experienced Sarmachar who served on the fronts of Gichk, Kilkor, Ornach, Rakhshan, and Panjgur.
Hafeez Baloch alias Hamal, son of Dawood was a freedom fighter of BLA, who was martyred by the firing of a state-backed death squad in the Minaz Bazaar area of ​​Buleda on February 23, 2025.

data.biography:
On 23 January 2011, at approximately 4:15 pm, in the Chitkan area of Panjgur district in Balochistan, Pakistani intelligence agencies, the Frontier Corps, and other genocidal forces raided the house of Nasir Dagarzai. During the raid, they abducted Nasir Dagarzai, Abid Saleem, Mehrab Omar, and Abid Rasool Bakhsh while they were sitting in the guest room (Betak) drinking tea.
Before taking him away, Pakistani forces also shot Nasir Dagarzai three times, leaving him wounded at the scene. The forces then took Nasir to a hospital, after which he was transferred to detention and torture cells, where he was subjected to severe torture. His hands were ground with a grinder and his body was burned with fire.
Approximately five days later, on 27 January 2011, Pakistani forces again shot Nasir Dagarzai and Abid Rasool Bakhsh. At around 1:00 am, they took them to the forests of Gowargo in the Panjgur area and dumped them there. Abid Rasool Bakhsh succumbed to his wounds and died there. However, by chance, Nasir Dagarzai, although badly injured, was found by a person who informed the Levies. He was then transferred to Quetta for medical treatment. After receiving treatment, he was brought back to Panjgur, and due to the gunshot wounds, doctors inserted a rod in his leg.
On 11 March 2011, Nasir Dagarzai gave an interview to Samandar Askani on Radio Gwank in which he described the details of these events.
Later, on 23 May 2011, when Nasir was traveling with his brother Mohammad Gull Dagarzai to Quetta for medical treatment, Pakistani forces abducted him again at the Lak Pass area near Quetta and forcibly disappeared him. On 16 July 2011, he was killed and his mutilated body was dumped. The body was recovered from Lak Pass near Quetta on 17 July 2011.
Similarly, in the same incident, the mutilated bodies of Abid Saleem, son of Mohammad Saleem Baloch, and Mehrab Baloch, son of Haji Mohammad Umar, who had also been abducted and forcibly disappeared, were later recovered on 24 May 2011 from the Margap area of Turbat district in Balochistan.
The short film “The Line of Freedom,” written and directed by the British director David Whitney and produced by Nooruddin Mengal, Mir Bhawal Mengal, and David Whitney, was released in 2013 and was inspired by Nasir Dagarzai.
Nasir Dagarzai’s son, Zameer Dagarzai, was abducted by Pakistani forces and Pakistan-backed death squads on 3 March 2026 from the Chitkan Taar office in Panjgur district, Balochistan. On 11 March 2026, his tortured body was found under the Washaap Bridge in the Panjgur district of Balochistan.

Siraj Baloch, son of Faiz Mohammad, was born on January 15, 1998, in Awaran Bazdad. He served as the organizer of BSO Azad Awaran Zone. Siraj Baloch was a 9th-grade student at Ladh High School, Bazdad.
He held various positions within the organization and was eventually elected as the organizer of BSO Azad Awaran Zone. He remained committed to the organization until his martyrdom. He inspired many youths from the Awaran region to join the Baloch liberation movement.
He joined the organization at an early age and stayed dedicated to it throughout his life. He believed in peaceful struggle and was targeted for his peaceful political expression.
Nineteen-year-old Siraj Baloch was martyred by Pakistan paramilitary forces on May 12, 2017, in Bazdad, Awaran, Balochistan. He was among the most committed members of the organization and continued his struggle during difficult times.
He motivated many young people to join the caravan of BSO Azad. His sacrifices for the independence of the Baloch homeland at such a young age will be remembered in golden words in the chapters of Baloch history.

Operation Dara-e-Bolan, which began on 29 January 2024 continued for two days until 31 January 2024 and was successfully concluded after achieving its intended objectives. A total of 385 Sarmachars from four different units of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) participated in Operation Dara-e-Bolan. Among them were 12 Fidayeen from the BLA’s Majeed Brigade. The other participating units included the Fateh Squad, the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS) and the Intelligence Wing.
Operation Dara-e-Bolan commenced on the evening of 29 January 2024 at 9:00 pm local time and continued for two days. After achieving the desired results, the BLA’s Senior Command Council announced the conclusion of Operation Dara-e-Bolan on 31 January 2024 at 7:00 pm and issued instructions to all units to vacate their positions and report back to their base camps.
During the operation, BLA Sarmachars took complete control of an area within a 70 kilometre radius, including Mach city and the strategically important National Highway N-65. Over the course of Operation Dara-e-Bolan, a total of 78 enemy personnel were killed. These included 45 Frontier Corps (FC) personnel who were killed within the first three hours of the operation in Mach city; 10 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on an army camp at the Pir Ghaib Bolan location; 4 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on a military convoy at the Gokurt Mach location; 12 regular army personnel who were killed on 30 January when Majeed Brigade Fidayeen eliminated them and entered the FC headquarters; and at least 5 SSG commandos who were targeted and killed by the Fidayeen on 31 January 2024. In addition, two police personnel were also killed, including one Station House Officer (SHO).
A large number of Levies and police personnel were captured by the BLA during the operation; however, as they were Baloch, they were released. During Operation Dara-e-Bolan, 13 brave fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army attained martyrdom. Of these, 12 martyred Sarmachars belonged to the Majeed Brigade Fidayeen, while one martyred Sarmachar was from the BLA’s Fateh Squad.
The martyred Sarmachars were: Qasim Baloch, Saddam Hussain, Salal Baloch, Farooq Baloch, Atta Baloch, Hammal Momin, Zeeshan Zehri, Nadir Bangulzai, Nizam Baloch, Zeeshan Baloch, Jamal Baloch, Wadood Satakzai, and Kashif Shahwani.
Farooq Baloch, alias Chakar, son of Syed, belonged to the Absar area of Turbat. Alongside being a university graduate, he was an avid reader and intellectual companion. Farooq Baloch joined the Baloch liberation struggle in 2021 and offered his services to the Majeed Brigade. His role in Operation Dara-e-Bolan was extremely critical. He drove an explosives-laden vehicle into the gate of the FC Headquarters in Mach, which not only killed dozens of enemy personnel on the spot but also enabled the remaining fidayeen of the Majeed Brigade to enter the camp.

Shafi Bangulzai was born in 1950 into the house of Mir Shah Dad Khan Bangulzai at Chander in the district of Kachh, Balochistan. He graduated from Degree College Quetta. When Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto dismissed the National Awami Party (NAP) government in Balochistan and imposed Martial Law, Shafi Baloch, along with many other Baloch youth, joined the resistance movement. He was arrested by the Pakistani police on December 17th from a hotel on Jan Mohd Road, Quetta. On December 20, 1975, military intelligence took Shafi Baloch (Lashker Khan) with them to the mountains of Jimy in the Mastung area so that he could show them the way. Without his cooperation, they reached an abandoned camp. Shaheed Shafi Baloch’s last words, bravely spoken to his captors before they shot him, were: “If you want to kill me, I am ready to die. I am happy that I saved my comrades from your bullets. My only sorrow is that my desire to see my motherland free will not be fulfilled.”

Bohair Baloch, son of Dil Jan and a resident of Tehsil Buleda, district Kech (Turbat), was shot dead by indiscriminate firing of Pakistani forces personnel in the Gilli area of Buleda on August 20, 2025.

Bohair was returning home from his agricultural fields after cultivation when forces stationed in the area opened direct fire on him, killing him instantly.

Eyewitnesses confirmed that he was deliberately targeted by Pakistani forces, who have established checkpoints throughout the agricultural belt of Buleda.

These included 45 Frontier Corps (FC) personnel who were killed within the first three hours of the operation in Mach city; 10 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on an army camp at the Pir Ghaib Bolan location; 4 FC personnel who were killed in an attack on a military convoy at the Gokurt Mach location; 12 regular army personnel who were killed on 30 January when Majeed Brigade Fidayeen eliminated them and entered the FC headquarters; and at least 5 SSG commandos who were targeted and killed by the Fidayeen on 31 January 2024. In addition, two police personnel were also killed, including one Station House Officer (SHO).
A large number of Levies and police personnel were captured by the BLA during the operation; however, as they were Baloch, they were released. During Operation Dara-e-Bolan, 13 brave fighters of the Baloch Liberation Army attained martyrdom. Of these, 12 martyred Sarmachars belonged to the Majeed Brigade Fidayeen, while one martyred Sarmachar was from the BLA’s Fateh Squad.
The martyred Sarmachars were: Qasim Baloch, Saddam Hussain, Salal Baloch, Farooq Baloch, Atta Baloch, Hammal Momin, Zeeshan Zehri, Nadir Bangulzai, Nizam Baloch, Zeeshan Baloch, Jamal Baloch, Wadood Satakzai, and Kashif Shahwani.
Nadir Bangulzai Baloch, alias Bali, son of Abdul Rahman Bangulzai, a resident of Killi Bangulzai, Quetta, offered his services to the BLA - Majeed Brigade one year prior. Nadir Bangulzai was a politically conscious activist and a fully trained guerrilla fighter. Despite being wounded during Operation Dara-e-Bolan, he continued advancing and despite severe injuries, carried out effective attacks against the enemy for an additional twenty four hours.

Yasir Baloch, son of Mohammad Karim and a resident of Balicha, Tump, worked along the border routes that sustain families across this region. These routes exist only because the Pakistani state has offered nothing else, and this sole means of livelihood is also under their control.
On 25 September 2026, he joined a picnic in the Lutham area of Balicha, Tump district, with his friends. They informed the Pakistani army about their picnic at the mentioned location, and they were met with a rocket fired by a drone operated by Pakistani forces, which ended his life along with those of his three other friends: Sameer Baloch, son of Abdul Khaliq; Zubair Nawab, son of Nawab; and Didag Baloch, son of Mohammad Omar. Two other people were also injured in the incident.

On 3 February 2024, the Pakistani Army’s Inter-Services Public Relations (ISPR) issued a statement declaring that 24 terrorists had been neutralized in a military operation conducted in the Mach area of Bolan. The operation was launched in response to Operation Darra-e-Bolan, an operation launched by the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), a Baloch pro-independence militant group, in the Mach area of Bolan district. The group reportedly maintained control of the area for three days.

However, subsequent investigations revealed that four of the deceased individuals had previously been reported as victims of enforced disappearances, and some of their cases had been registered with Baloch human rights organizations.

The identities of the deceased individuals were confirmed as follows:

- Bashir Ahmed, son of Haji Khan Marri, a resident of Mashriqi Bypass, Quetta, who was forcibly disappeared on 2 July 2023.

- Arman Marri, son of Nihal Khan Marri, a resident of Mashriqi Bypass, Quetta, who was forcibly disappeared on 2 July 2023.

- Sobadar, son of Gulzar Khan Tengani, a resident of the Main Kor area of Harnai district, who was forcibly disappeared on 9 September 2023.

- Shakil, son of Ramzan, a resident of the Mishk area of Zehri, Khuzdar district.

The family members of Bashir and Arman were also actively participating in a sit-in protest in Islamabad. Organized by the Baloch Yakjehti Committee (BYC), the sit-in was held outside the National Press Club to protest enforced disappearances and extrajudicial killings.

The families tirelessly appealed to the government to secure the return of their forcibly disappeared loved ones, but all their pleas fell on deaf ears. Ultimately, they were devastated to receive the mutilated bodies of their young relatives, whom they believed had been victims of a staged encounter.

On 5 February 2024, when the family members went to Civil Hospital Quetta to receive the bodies, they were reportedly coerced into signing an unlawful form falsely stating that the deceased had links to militant groups and labeling them as terrorists. The family members refused to comply. Following a large demonstration, the bodies were eventually handed over to them.
Khalid Baloch, was a resident of the Pasni area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 19 August 2011 in Balochistan.

The Baloch Liberation Army’s Majeed Brigade attacked a large Pakistani army convoy at Kunchiti Cross in Dasht, Kech, on 18 September 2025. The convoy included six buses carrying army personnel and an escort squad. It had arrived in Gwadar from Karachi a day earlier and was travelling toward Turbat when the attack occurred around 1 p.m.

The operation began when Altaf alias Chakar drove a VBIED into the main bus, destroying it. After the explosion, Gwahram alias Zagrain and Khalil alias Kulmeer targeted the remaining buses and the security squad. The clash continued for over thirty minutes. According to BLA’s sources, at least 32 army personnel were killed, several wounded, and multiple buses destroyed. Reinforcements and drones arrived later, but rescue operations were delayed.

Altaf (from Alandur Buleda), Gwahram (from Paroom, Panjgur), and Khalil (from Saami, Turbat) had all joined the BLA in 2023. Each had served as an urban guerrilla before moving to the mountains and becoming part of the Majeed Brigade, where they underwent training and took on various responsibilities.

The Baloch Liberation Army’s (BLA) fighters attacked a Pakistani military post on the night of 23 July 2024 in the Sami, Gishkor area of Kech District, Balochistan. During the operation, another unit of the fighters targeted and destroyed machinery belonging to an exploitative project near the enemy army’s camp. During clashes with the Pakistani military, BLA fighter Ali Jan Baloch, alias Kareem, son of Kamal, was martyred after being hit by the blast of an enemy mortar shell. Comrade Ali Jan was from the Sami area of Turbat and was performing his duties as a patrol commander at the time. He had taken part in numerous battles against the enemy on the Zamuran, Buleda, Kulbar, Sami and Turbat fronts, where he had already established a record of bravery.
Ali Jan, alis Kareem, who had dedicated his life to the achievement of Baloch national liberation, joined a companion organization in 2018 and made the mountainous front his home. In 2020, he became affiliated with the Baloch Liberation Army. The family of the martyred Ali Jan endured oppression and violence at the hands of the occupying forces; however, the enemy army failed to force Ali Jan to abandon his stance on national freedom.

On 13th April 2026, in the Barkhan area of Balochistan, Pakistani forces shelled and bombed civilian populations, killing twelve innocent Baloch civilians, including women and children, and seriously injuring three others.

The martyrs are:

- Ali, son of Sultan Umair, aged 40
- Babul, daughter of Gulzar, aged 30
- Mir Jan, son of Ali, aged 2
- Somri, daughter of Bhangan, aged 35
- Balach, son of Sabzo, aged 70
- Shari, aged 22
- Rehman, son of Balach, aged 18
- Naikho, daughter of Jamalan, aged 17
- Allah Bakhsh, son of Balach, aged 6
- Saddo, daughter of Balach, aged 13
- Hapo, daughter of Balach, aged 8
- Mahrang, daughter of Balach, aged 2

The injured are:

- Zarbibi, daughter of Sher, aged 55
- Hazar Khan, son of Balach, aged 9
- Israr, daughter of Balach, aged 15

This is not the first time that Pakistani forces have bombed civilians in Balochistan, targeting unarmed and innocent women and children as a form of collective punishment. Nor can this be considered “collateral damage.” Rather, the Pakistani state and its forces are deliberately targeting the Baloch people to maintain an atmosphere of fear in the region, suppress internal dissent, exploit Baloch coastal resources, and continue policies of genocide against the Baloch nation.

At 5:00 AM on 31 January 2026, Jeeyand Baloch, spokesperson for the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), issued a statement announcing the commencement of the second phase of Operation Herof against the occupying state and its military and administrative structures. The operation remained active for six days, concluding at 4:00 PM on 6 February 2026.
On 6 February 2026, a concluding statement by the spokesperson declared that Operation Herof Phase 2 had concluded in a decisive victory across all fronts. It stated that Operation Herof Phase 2, carried out by the Baloch Liberation Army, was a six-day campaign of coordinated urban combat and represented the most extensive, intense, and organized military engagement in the modern history of the Baloch national resistance. The operation, which began at 5:00 AM on 31 January and ended at 4:00 PM on 6 February, successfully achieved its strategic objectives. Fourteen cities across Balochistan were targeted. Baloch fighters launched simultaneous attacks and established effective control over numerous enemy posts, military installations, and urban sectors. In several cities, BLA units maintained uninterrupted dominance over occupying forces for six consecutive days, inflicting significant political, psychological, and military damage on the enemy.
During the operation, 93 BLA fighters were martyred. These included 50 fidayeen from the Majeed Brigade, 26 fighters from the Fateh Squad, and 17 from the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS). All major BLA units participated in the operation, including Majeed Brigade, STOS, Fateh Squad, ZIRAB (intelligence wing), and Hakkal (media wing). Over 362 enemy personnel were killed, including members of the Pakistani Army, Frontier Corps, police, and state-sponsored death squads. Seventeen enemy soldiers were captured. Ten, identified as Baloch, were released with warnings, while seven remained in BLA custody and faced trial for war crimes and acts of genocide.
On 14 February 2026, another statement by the spokesperson announced that the seven occupying army personnel were in custody and that a one-week prison of war exchange had been offered. The Pakistani Army ignored the offer and intensified its military operations. On 3 March 2026, a subsequent statement declared that, due to misadventures and breaches of promises by the occupying forces, death sentences were carried out against the seven Pakistani personnel.
During Operation Herof Phase 2, dozens of Pakistani military facilities were destroyed, weapons stockpiles were seized, and the unified, disciplined resistance dealt a substantial blow to the military superiority of the occupying state.
Kabeer Sarparah, alias Ilyas, son of Pasand Khan Sarparah, joined the BLA in July 2024.
The journey of Kabeer Sarparah, known as Ilyas, began in the streets of Sariab, Quetta, and reached its destination of martyrdom in the deserts of Kharan. His choice of the path of armed struggle in July 2024 was the result of years of political consciousness nurtured in Quetta, the political heart of Balochistan. Kabeer hailed from Gurgina, a land where the soil is steeped in resistance, and through his actions, he demonstrated that the lights of the city and personal comforts hold no meaning when the motherland calls.
His personality embodied the quiet steadfastness that is the hallmark of a true Sarmachar. In a very short span of time, Kabeer Sarparah prepared himself for the harshest combat conditions. When the Kharan front intensified during "Operation Herof Phase 2," he left an indelible mark of bravery by remaining on the front lines. During a clash, he chose to stand his ground and fight rather than retreat, ultimately embracing martyrdom. His sacrifice forms part of the intellectual continuity that stretches from Sariab to Kharan.

Shahjan Baloch, son of Assa Baloch, was a resident of Balgatar, Kech. He was abducted along with his brother Adil and six other close relatives from different areas on August 22, 2023. After four months, on November 20, 2023, he was killed, along with his brother Adil and relative Nabi Dad, son of Lewari Baloch, by a Pakistan military-backed death squad in Balgatar, Kech.
Abdul Manan was a resident of the Dosay, Noshki area of Balochistan. He was martyred on 18 August 2017 in Balochistan.

Saif Jan, son of Faiz Mohammad, was a 15-year-old student from Chitkan, Panjgur. He was forcibly disappeared during the month of Ramadan. After three months, on 29 June 2026, his dead body was dumped on Airport Road, Panjgur. He was extrajudicially killed by death squads in Panjgur after three months of enforced disappearance.

Zaheer Pirkani, alias Mashyar, son of Bibi Saeeda, was a resident of the Niyam Ghundi area of Shal, Quetta. He joined the BLA in March 2024 and served in the Urban Guerrilla Front. After one year, he moved to the Mountain Front in 2025 and later joined the Majeed Brigade in April 2025. He was promoted to the rank of Patrol Commander on the Kalat front and was martyred on December 6, 2025, in Kalat, Balochistan.
The life story of Zaheer Pirkani is a reflection of the systemic oppression that compels Baloch youth to choose the path of resistance over compromise. Hailing from the Niyam Ghundi area of Shal, this courageous young man had already endured the agony of state torture cells in June 2021, when he was forcibly disappeared by the CTD. This experience only served to further ignite his national consciousness. Following his release, instead of choosing silence, he vowed to uproot the system of tyranny and formally joined the armed struggle in March 2024.
Zaheer Pirkani proved his mettle on the urban guerrilla front for a year before heading to the mountains in 2025. Due to his ideological maturity and fearlessness, he was soon inducted into the elite Majeed Brigade, where he remained active as a Patrol Commander on the Kalat front. On December 6, 2025, while on a critical mission in preparation for “Operation Herof Phase 2,” he encountered the enemy in the rugged mountains of Kalat and sacrificed his life for the sanctity of his motherland.

Operation Dara-e-Bolan, which began on 29 January 2024 continued for two days until 31 January 2024 and was successfully concluded after achieving its intended objectives. A total of 385 Sarmachars from four different units of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA) participated in Operation Dara-e-Bolan. Among them were 12 Fidayeen from the BLA’s Majeed Brigade. The other participating units included the Fateh Squad, the Special Tactical Operations Squad (STOS) and the Intelligence Wing.
Operation Dara-e-Bolan commenced on the evening of 29 January 2024 at 9:00 pm local time and continued for two days. After achieving the desired results, the BLA’s Senior Command Council announced the conclusion of Operation Dara-e-Bolan on 31 January 2024 at 7:00 pm and issued instructions to all units to vacate their positions and report back to their base camps.

Nizam Baloch, alias Sahil Baloch, son of Mohammad Jan, belonged to Pasni, Babar Shore. He offered his services to the BLA - Majeed Brigade two years prior. During Operation Dara-e-Bolan, he set an exceptional example of bravery. He encountered a group of enemy SSG commandos alone and fought dozens of them single handedly for hours, killing five commandos and forcing the remaining forces to retreat.

On 4 March 2026, a statement issued by the spokesperson of the Balochistan Liberation Front, Major Gwahram Baloch, stated that on 3 February 2026, fighters of the Balochistan Liberation Front launched a coordinated operation at four different locations in Hoshap against Pakistani forces. In this organized operation, various BLF units simultaneously targeted the enemy army at four different locations in Hoshap.
In the initial phase of the operation, one unit of fighters surrounded the police station located in Hoshap Bazaar and took control of the station, holding the personnel hostage. While this unit was seizing government weapons, ammunition, and other equipment, an enemy military convoy consisting of four vehicles approached the area, resulting in an intense face-to-face clash between BLF fighters and enemy forces. During the clash, the fighters targeted and destroyed two enemy vehicles, killing several Pakistani military personnel on board.
Meanwhile, a second unit of fighters positioned at another location attacked two armored enemy vehicles with heavy weapons. Several military personnel were killed or wounded in the clash. Witnessing the defeat and retreat of their ground forces, the enemy resorted to gunship helicopters and advanced drone technology to halt the BLF fighters’ advance.
In this prolonged clash, seven BLF fighters - Shaneed Baloch (alias Shohaz Baloch), Zabad Baloch (alias Deedag), Atta Baloch (alias Obaid), Ghaffar Baloch (alias Noroz), Abdul Samad Baloch (alias Muheem Jan), Zaheer Baloch (alias Istaal), and Nadeem (alias Sahil) - fought valiantly until their last bullet and last breath and embraced martyrdom while courageously defending their motherland.
Atta Baloch, alias Obaid Son of Shayhaq, resident of Sing Abad Tijaban, joined the armed struggle under the Balochistan Liberation Front platform in July 2022. He was an extremely brave and well-mannered comrade who proved his courage in numerous military operations. His perseverance, bravery, and sincere character will always be remembered as that of a fearless soldier.

On 29 June 2025, Masood Baloch, son of Khuda Bakhsh and a resident of Laki, Mashkay, was tortured and killed while in the custody of the Pakistani Army. He had been forcibly disappeared nearly 20 days prior, and his bullet-riddled, mutilated body bearing signs of severe torture was recovered on 29 June, 2025.
This was not the first time Masood was targeted. He had previously been subjected to enforced disappearance in 2024. Following his release, he was coerced under pressure to appear in a state-sponsored press conference intended to discredit the Baloch struggle.

data.biography:
In a face to face battle with the Pakistani military and its agents in the mountainous regions of Noshki and Kharan on 24 September 2021, more than a dozen enemy personnel were killed, whereas six freedom fighters, including five members of the Baloch Liberation Army (BLA), also embraced martyrdom.
The battle commenced early Friday morning in Siyah Lop, near Baddo Dor, when enemy forces attempted to encircle a patrolling party of Baloch freedom fighters. In the face-to-face battle that lasted for more than four hours, scores of enemy personnel were killed and injured. Five freedom fighters of the BLA and one freedom fighter of the United Baloch Army (UBA), while evacuating their comrades from the battle zone, embraced martyrdom.
The fallen comrades include Commander Ganjal alias Comrade Mazar, Nazeer alias Sangar, Faisal alias Yasir, Kaleem alias Bolani, and Rehan alias Mehrwaan, all members of the Baloch Liberation Army. A member of the United Baloch Army, Nodaan alias Hammal, bravely fought alongside BLA comrades and embraced martyrdom.
Commander Ganjal alias Comrade Mazar belonged to Lyari in Karachi and had joined the BLA four years ago. Due to his tremendous military and political skills, he quickly assumed important organisational responsibilities. Owing to his competence and sincerity toward the freedom movement, he was appointed as a regional commander of the BLA. He fulfilled his responsibilities until his last breath and rescued several of his comrades, embracing martyrdom in the process.

Martyr Razzaq Baloch was a resident of Geshkaor, in the Kolwa area of Awaran, Balochistan. He had been affiliated with the pro-independence organization Baloch Republican Army (BRA) for several years. Along with his two comrades, Siraj Baloch and Bahoot Baloch, he embraced martyrdom during a clash with the Pakistan Army in the Rekachai area between Mahra and Kolwa in Awaran on October 16, 2015.
